Gen: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth had no shape and was empty. Darkness covered the deep waters, and the Spirit of God was moving over the surface of the waters.
Then God said, "Let there be light." And light came into being.
God saw that the light was good. He separated the light from the darkness.
God named the light "day" and the darkness "night". Evening came, and then morning. That was the first day.
Then God said, "Let there be a wide space between the waters, to divide the waters into two parts."
So God made the wide space. He separated the waters below it from the waters above it. And it happened just as he said.
God named the wide space "sky". Evening came, and then morning. That was the second day.
Then God said, "Let the waters under the sky gather into one place, so that dry ground can appear." And it happened just as he said.
God named the dry ground "land", and the waters that had gathered together he named "seas". God saw that it was good.
Then God said, "Let the land grow plants: green plants that make seeds, and trees that bear fruit with seeds inside, each of its own kind." And it happened just as he said.
The land produced plants that made seeds, each of its own kind, and trees that bore fruit with seeds inside, each of its own kind. God saw that it was good.
Evening came, and then morning. That was the third day.
Then God said, "Let there be lights in the sky to separate the day from the night. Let them be signs that mark the seasons, the days and the years.
Let them shine in the sky to give light to the earth." And it happened just as he said.
God made two great lights: the bigger light to rule the day, and the smaller light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
God placed them in the sky to give light to the earth,
to rule over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. God saw that it was good.
Evening came, and then morning. That was the fourth day.
Then God said, "Let the waters be filled with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the open sky."
So God created the great sea creatures and every kind of living thing that moves in the water. He also created every kind of bird. God saw that it was good.
God blessed them and said, "Have many young and increase in number. Fill the waters of the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth."
Evening came, and then morning. That was the fifth day.
Then God said, "Let the land produce living creatures, each of its own kind: farm animals, small creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals." And it happened just as he said.
God made the wild animals, the farm animals and all the small creatures that move along the ground, each of its own kind. God saw that it was good.

Then God said, "Let us make human beings in our image, to be like us. Let them rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the farm animals, the whole earth, and all the small creatures that move along the ground."
So God created human beings in his own image. In the image of God he created them. Male and female he created them.

God blessed them and said to them, "Have children and increase in number. Fill the earth and bring it under your care and control. Rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky and every living creature that moves on the earth."
Then God said, "Look! I have given you every plant on the whole earth that makes seeds, and every tree that bears fruit with seeds. They will be your food.

And to every animal on the earth, every bird in the sky and every creature that moves along the ground, everything that has the breath of life in it, I give every green plant for food." And it happened just as he said.
God looked at everything he had made, and it was very good. Evening came, and then morning. That was the sixth day.
So the heavens and the earth were completed, with everything in them.
By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing. So on the seventh day he rested from all his work.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on that day he rested from all the work of creating that he had done.
This is the story of the heavens and the earth when they were created, at the time when the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
No bush had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant had yet sprung up in the fields. The LORD God had not yet sent rain on the earth, and there was no one to work the ground.
But a mist rose up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
Then the LORD God formed a man from the dust of the ground. He breathed the breath of life into the man's nose, and the man became a living being.
The LORD God planted a garden in the east, in Eden. There he put the man he had formed.

The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground. They were beautiful to look at and good for food. In the middle of the garden stood the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden. From there it divided into four rivers.
The first river is called the Pishon. It flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is pure. Sweet-smelling resin and precious onyx stone are also found there.
The second river is called the Gihon. It flows around the whole land of Cush.
The third river is called the Tigris. It flows east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
The LORD God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work the ground and look after it.
The LORD God gave the man this command: "You are free to eat from any tree in the garden,
but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. On the day you eat from it, you will certainly die."
Then the LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper who is just right for him."

Out of the ground the LORD God formed every wild animal and every bird in the sky. He brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called each living creature, that became its name.
So the man gave names to all the farm animals, the birds in the sky and all the wild animals. But for Adam there was no helper who was just right for him.
So the LORD God made the man fall into a deep sleep. While he was sleeping, God took one of the man's ribs and closed up the place with flesh.
Then the LORD God made a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man.
The man said, "At last! Here is someone who is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. She will be called 'woman', because she was taken out of man."
That is why a man leaves his father and his mother and is joined to his wife, and the two of them become one.
The man and his wife were both naked, but they felt no shame.
Now the snake was more cunning than any of the wild animals the LORD God had made. It said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?"
The woman answered the snake, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden.
But about the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, 'You must not eat its fruit. Do not even touch it, or you will die.'"
"You will not die!" the snake said to the woman.
"God knows that when you eat from it, your eyes will be opened. You will be like God, knowing good and evil."

The woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and lovely to look at, and that it was desirable because it could make a person wise. So she took some of the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.
Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they realised that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
In the cool part of the day, they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden. The man and his wife hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
But the LORD God called out to the man, "Where are you?"
He answered, "I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked. So I hid."
God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?"
The man said, "The woman you put here with me gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it."
Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" The woman said, "The snake tricked me, and I ate."

So the LORD God said to the snake, "Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all the farm animals and all the wild animals. You will crawl on your belly, and you will eat dust all the days of your life.
I will make you and the woman enemies of each other, and your offspring and her offspring will be enemies too. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel."
To the woman he said, "I will greatly increase your pain when you carry children. In pain you will give birth. You will long for your husband, and he will rule over you."

To Adam he said, "You listened to your wife and ate fruit from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from. So the ground is cursed because of you. All the days of your life you will have to work hard to get food from it.
It will grow thorns and weeds for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
You will sweat to earn your bread until you go back to the ground, because you were taken from it. You are dust, and to dust you will return."
Adam named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all who live.
The LORD God made clothes from animal skins for Adam and his wife, and he dressed them.

Then the LORD God said, "Look, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand, take fruit from the tree of life as well, eat it and live for ever."
So the LORD God sent him out of the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.

After he drove the man out, he placed cherubim, mighty heavenly beings, on the east side of the Garden of Eden. He also placed a flaming sword there that flashed back and forth, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam slept with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the LORD's help I have brought a man into the world."
Later she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel looked after sheep, and Cain worked the soil.
After some time, Cain brought some of the crops from the ground as an offering to the LORD.
Abel also brought an offering. He brought the best parts of some of the firstborn lambs from his flock. The LORD was pleased with Abel and his offering,
but he was not pleased with Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his face looked gloomy.
Then the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why do you look so gloomy?
If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is waiting at your door like a wild animal. It wants to control you, but you must master it."
Cain said to his brother Abel, "Let's go out to the field." While they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.
Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I don't know," he answered. "Am I supposed to look after my brother?"
The LORD said, "What have you done? Listen! Your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground.
Now you are under a curse, and you are driven from the ground, which opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
When you work the ground, it will no longer give you good crops. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."
Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is more than I can bear.
Today you are driving me away from the land, and I will be hidden from your presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
But the LORD said to him, "No. If anyone kills Cain, he will be punished seven times over." Then the LORD put a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
So Cain went away from the LORD's presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Cain slept with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was building a city at the time, and he named it Enoch, after his son.
Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad was the father of Mehujael. Mehujael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamech.
Lamech married two women. One was named Adah and the other was named Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the first of those who live in tents and keep livestock.
His brother's name was Jubal. He was the first of all who play the harp and the flute.
Zillah also had a son, Tubal-Cain. He made all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-Cain's sister was Naamah.
Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me. Wives of Lamech, hear what I say. I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for hurting me.
If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech will be avenged seventy-seven times."
Adam slept with his wife again, and she gave birth to a son. She named him Seth, because she said, "God has given me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."
Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of the LORD.
This is the written record of Adam's family line. When God created human beings, he made them to be like God.
He created them male and female, and he blessed them. On the day they were created, he called them "human beings".
When Adam was a hundred and thirty years old, he had a son who was like him, in his own image. He named him Seth.
After Seth was born, Adam lived eight hundred more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Adam lived nine hundred and thirty years in all, and then he died.
When Seth was a hundred and five years old, he became the father of Enosh.
After Enosh was born, Seth lived eight hundred and seven more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Seth lived nine hundred and twelve years in all, and then he died.
When Enosh was ninety years old, he became the father of Kenan.
After Kenan was born, Enosh lived eight hundred and fifteen more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Enosh lived nine hundred and five years in all, and then he died.
When Kenan was seventy years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
After Mahalalel was born, Kenan lived eight hundred and forty more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Kenan lived nine hundred and ten years in all, and then he died.
When Mahalalel was sixty-five years old, he became the father of Jared.
After Jared was born, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Mahalalel lived eight hundred and ninety-five years in all, and then he died.
When Jared was a hundred and sixty-two years old, he became the father of Enoch.
After Enoch was born, Jared lived eight hundred more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Jared lived nine hundred and sixty-two years in all, and then he died.
When Enoch was sixty-five years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
After Methuselah was born, Enoch walked closely with God for three hundred years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Enoch lived three hundred and sixty-five years in all.
Enoch walked closely with God. Then he was gone, because God took him away.
When Methuselah was a hundred and eighty-seven years old, he became the father of Lamech.
After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Methuselah lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years in all, and then he died.
When Lamech was a hundred and eighty-two years old, he had a son.
He named him Noah, and said, "He will bring us relief from our hard work and the painful labour of our hands, caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed."
After Noah was born, Lamech lived five hundred and ninety-five more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
Lamech lived seven hundred and seventy-seven years in all, and then he died.
After Noah was five hundred years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.
The number of people on the earth began to grow, and daughters were born to them.
The sons of God saw that these human daughters were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose.
Then the LORD said, "My Spirit will not stay in human beings for ever, because they are mortal. Their life will last no more than a hundred and twenty years."

In those days, and also later, there were giants on the earth called the Nephilim. They came from the sons of God sleeping with human daughters, who had children by them. They were the mighty heroes of long ago, famous men.
The LORD saw how wicked people on the earth had become. Everything they thought about and planned in their hearts was always evil.
The LORD was sorry that he had made human beings on the earth, and it filled his heart with pain.

So the LORD said, "I will wipe out the people I have created from the face of the earth, and the animals, the creatures that move along the ground, and the birds in the sky. I am sorry that I have made them."
But Noah pleased the LORD.
This is the story of Noah and his family. Noah was a good man who did what was right. Among the people of his time, no one could find fault with him. He walked closely with God.
Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
In God's eyes the earth was rotten with sin, and it was full of violence.
God saw how corrupt the earth had become, because all the people on earth had turned to evil ways.
So God said to Noah, "I am going to put an end to all people, because the earth is full of violence because of them. I am going to destroy them together with the earth.
Build yourself a big boat, an ark, out of cypress wood. Make rooms in it, and cover it with tar inside and out.
This is how you must build it. The ark must be a hundred and fifty metres long, twenty-five metres wide and fifteen metres high.
Make a roof for it, leaving an opening of half a metre between the roof and the sides. Put a door in the side of the ark, and build it with a lower deck, a middle deck and an upper deck.
I am going to bring a flood of water on the earth to destroy every living thing under the sky that has the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will die.
But I will make my covenant with you, my solemn promise. You will go into the ark, you and your sons, your wife and your sons' wives with you.
You must bring into the ark two of every kind of living creature, a male and a female, to keep them alive with you.
Two of every kind of bird, of every kind of animal and of every kind of creature that moves along the ground will come to you, so that they can stay alive.
Also take every kind of food that is eaten, and store it away as food for you and for them."
Noah did everything just as God commanded him.
Then the LORD said to Noah, "Go into the ark, you and your whole family, because I have seen that you are the only good person in this generation.
Take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its female, and one pair of every kind of animal that is not clean, a male and its female.
Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird, male and female, to keep every kind alive on the whole earth.
Seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe out from the face of the earth every living thing I have made."
Noah did everything the LORD commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood waters came on the earth.
Noah and his sons, his wife and his sons' wives went into the ark to escape the flood waters.
Clean and unclean animals, birds, and all the creatures that move along the ground
came to Noah in pairs, male and female, and went into the ark, just as God had commanded Noah.
After the seven days, the flood waters came on the earth.
When Noah was six hundred years old, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the sky were opened.
Rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, went into the ark, together with his wife and the wives of his three sons.
With them went every kind of wild animal, every kind of farm animal, every kind of creature that moves along the ground, and every kind of bird, everything with wings.
Pairs of every creature that has the breath of life in it came to Noah and went into the ark.
The animals going in were male and female of every living thing, just as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth. As the waters rose, they lifted the ark high above the ground.
The waters rose and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the water.
The waters rose higher and higher over the earth, until all the high mountains under the whole sky were covered.
The waters rose more than seven metres above the mountains and covered them.
Every living thing that moved on the earth died: birds, farm animals, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all human beings.
Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in it died.

Every living thing on the face of the earth was wiped out: people, animals, creatures that move along the ground, and birds in the sky. They were wiped off the earth. Only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ark.
The waters flooded the earth for a hundred and fifty days.
But God did not forget Noah and all the wild animals and farm animals that were with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to go down.
The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the sky were closed, and the rain stopped falling from the sky.
Little by little the water went down from the earth. After a hundred and fifty days the water had gone down,
and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
The waters kept going down until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains could be seen.
After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth.
Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down from the surface of the ground.

But the dove could find nowhere to land, because there was still water over the whole earth. So it came back to Noah in the ark. He reached out his hand, took the dove and brought it back into the ark.
Noah waited seven more days, and then he sent the dove out of the ark again.
In the evening the dove came back to him, and there in its beak was a freshly picked olive leaf! Then Noah knew that the water had gone down from the earth.
He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but this time it did not come back to him.

By the first day of the first month of Noah's six hundred and first year, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah took the covering off the ark and looked out. He saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
Then God said to Noah,
"Come out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and their wives.

Bring out every kind of living creature that is with you: the birds, the animals and all the creatures that move along the ground. Let them spread out over the earth, have many young and increase in number on it."
So Noah came out, together with his sons and his wife and his sons' wives.
All the animals, all the creatures that move along the ground and all the birds, everything that moves on the earth, came out of the ark, one kind after another.
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every kind of clean animal and clean bird, and he burned them on the altar as offerings to the LORD.

The LORD smelled the pleasing smell and said to himself, "I will never again curse the ground because of human beings, even though every plan of their hearts is evil from the time they are young. And I will never again destroy every living creature, as I have just done.
As long as the earth lasts, there will always be planting time and harvest time, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night."
Then God blessed Noah and his sons. He said to them, "Have many children and increase in number, and fill the earth.

All the animals on earth, all the birds in the sky, all the creatures that move along the ground and all the fish in the sea will be afraid of you and terrified of you. I am putting them into your hands.
Everything that lives and moves will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.
But you must not eat meat that still has its lifeblood in it.
And for your own lifeblood I will demand payment. I will demand it from every animal that kills a person, and I will demand it from every person who kills another person.
Whoever kills a human being will be killed by human beings, because God made human beings in his own image.
As for you, have many children and increase in number. Spread out over the earth and fill it."
Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him,
"Now I am making my covenant with you and with your children after you,
and with every living creature that was with you: the birds, the farm animals and all the wild animals, all those that came out of the ark with you, every living creature on earth.
I am making my covenant with you. Never again will all life be wiped out by the waters of a flood. Never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth."
And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come:
I have put my rainbow in the clouds. It will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
I will remember my covenant between me and you and every kind of living creature. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.
Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the covenant that will last for ever between God and every kind of living creature on the earth."
So God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I have made between me and all life on the earth."
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were the sons of Noah, and from them came all the people who spread out over the whole earth.
Noah was a farmer, and he was the first to plant a vineyard.
He drank some of its wine and became drunk, and he lay naked inside his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father naked, and he went outside and told his two brothers.

But Shem and Japheth took a cloak and laid it across their shoulders. Then they walked in backwards and covered their father's naked body. They kept their faces turned away so that they would not see their father naked.
When Noah woke up from his drunkenness, he found out what his youngest son had done to him.
He said, "May Canaan be cursed! He will be the lowest of slaves to his brothers."
He also said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be Shem's slave.
May God give Japheth more land. May Japheth live in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his slave."
After the flood Noah lived three hundred and fifty years.
Noah lived nine hundred and fifty years in all, and then he died.
This is the story of the family of Shem, Ham and Japheth, Noah's sons. They had sons of their own after the flood.
The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites and the Rodanites.
From these came the peoples who spread out to the coastlands and islands. Each group lived in its own land, with its own language, by its clans within its nations.
The sons of Ham were Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became the first mighty warrior on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter in the eyes of the LORD. That is why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter in the eyes of the LORD."
The first centres of his kingdom were Babylon, Erech, Akkad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
and Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah, the great city.
Egypt was the father of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,
Pathrusites, Casluhites and Caphtorites. The Philistines came from the Casluhites.
Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites. Later the clans of the Canaanites spread out.
The borders of Canaan reached from Sidon towards Gerar as far as Gaza, and then towards Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These were the sons of Ham, by their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.
Sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth. Shem was the ancestor of all the sons of Eber.
The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram.
The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg, which means "divided", because in his time the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
The land where they lived stretched from Mesha towards Sephar, in the hill country in the east.
These were the sons of Shem, by their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.
These were the clans of Noah's sons, listed by their family lines and nations. From them the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.
At that time the whole world spoke one language and used the same words.
As people moved towards the east, they found a flat plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
They said to each other, "Come, let's make bricks and bake them hard." They used bricks instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.
Then they said, "Come, let's build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches up to the sky. Then we will make a name for ourselves, and we will not be scattered over the face of the whole earth."
But the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the people were building.
The LORD said, "Look! They are one people, and they all speak the same language. This is only the beginning of what they will do. Soon nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.
Come, let us go down and mix up their language, so that they will not understand each other."
So the LORD scattered them from there over the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.
That is why it was called Babel, because there the LORD mixed up the language of the whole world. From there the LORD scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
This is the family line of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was a hundred years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.
After Arphaxad was born, Shem lived five hundred more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Arphaxad was thirty-five years old, he became the father of Shelah.
After Shelah was born, Arphaxad lived four hundred and three more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Shelah was thirty years old, he became the father of Eber.
After Eber was born, Shelah lived four hundred and three more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Eber was thirty-four years old, he became the father of Peleg.
After Peleg was born, Eber lived four hundred and thirty more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Peleg was thirty years old, he became the father of Reu.
After Reu was born, Peleg lived two hundred and nine more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Reu was thirty-two years old, he became the father of Serug.
After Serug was born, Reu lived two hundred and seven more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Serug was thirty years old, he became the father of Nahor.
After Nahor was born, Serug lived two hundred more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
When Nahor was twenty-nine years old, he became the father of Terah.
After Terah was born, Nahor lived a hundred and nineteen more years, and he had other sons and daughters.
After Terah was seventy years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran.
This is the family line of Terah. Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. Haran was the father of Lot.
Haran died in Ur of the Chaldeans, the land where he was born, while his father Terah was still alive.
Abram and Nahor both got married. Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah. She was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.
Sarai was not able to have children. She had no child.

Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot, who was Haran's son, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, Abram's wife. Together they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. But when they came to Haran, they settled there.
Terah lived two hundred and five years, and he died in Haran.
The LORD said to Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives and your father's family, and go to the land I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you and make your name famous, and you will be a blessing to others.
I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse anyone who treats you with contempt. All the families on earth will be blessed through you."
So Abram left, as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Haran.
He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the things they owned and the people they had gained in Haran, and they set out for the land of Canaan. And they arrived there.
Abram travelled through the land as far as the great tree of Moreh at Shechem. At that time the Canaanites were living in the land.
The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your children and their children." So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
From there he moved on to the hills east of Bethel and set up his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.
Then Abram kept moving on, travelling towards the Negev, the dry land in the south.
Now there was a famine in the land. The famine was very bad, so Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while.
As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "I know what a beautiful woman you are.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife.' Then they will kill me but let you live.
Please say that you are my sister. Then they will treat me well for your sake, and my life will be spared because of you."
When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into his palace.
Pharaoh treated Abram well for her sake. Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his household with terrible diseases because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
So Pharaoh sent for Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, 'She is my sister', so that I took her to be my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!"
Then Pharaoh gave orders to his men about Abram, and they sent him on his way with his wife and everything he had.
So Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev, with his wife and everything he had, and Lot went with him.
Abram had become very rich in livestock, silver and gold.
From the Negev he travelled from place to place until he came to Bethel, to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had been at first,
where he had built an altar before. There Abram called on the name of the LORD.
Lot, who was travelling with Abram, also had flocks, herds and tents.
But the land could not support them both while they stayed together. They had so many possessions that they were not able to live together.
Quarrels broke out between the men who looked after Abram's animals and the men who looked after Lot's animals. The Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.
So Abram said to Lot, "Let's not have any quarrelling between you and me, or between your herdsmen and mine, because we are family.
The whole land is in front of you. Let's go our separate ways. If you go to the left, I will go to the right. If you go to the right, I will go to the left."

Lot looked around and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan towards Zoar had plenty of water, like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
So Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan and set out towards the east. The two men parted company.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived among the cities of the plain and set up his tents near Sodom.
Now the people of Sodom were very wicked, and they were sinning greatly against the LORD.
After Lot had left, the LORD said to Abram, "Look around from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west.
I will give all the land that you see to you and your children after you for ever.
I will make your family as many as the dust of the earth. If anyone could count the dust, then your family could be counted.
Go and walk through the land, through all its length and width, because I am giving it to you."
So Abram moved his tents and went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron. There he built an altar to the LORD.
At this time Amraphel was king of Shinar, Arioch was king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer was king of Elam, and Tidal was king of Goiim.
These kings went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is also called Zoar.
These five kings joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, which is now the Dead Sea.
For twelve years they had been ruled by Kedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year, Kedorlaomer and the kings who were with him came and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
and the Horites in their hill country of Seir, as far as El Paran near the desert.
Then they turned back and went to En Mishpat, which is also called Kadesh. They conquered the whole land of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who were living in Hazezon Tamar.
Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela, which is Zoar, marched out and lined up for battle in the Valley of Siddim.
They fought against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar. It was four kings against five.
The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits. When the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran away, some of their men fell into the pits, and the rest escaped to the hills.
The four kings took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and then they left.
They also took Abram's nephew Lot, who was living in Sodom, along with everything he owned.
A man who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew what had happened. Abram was living near the great trees of Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshkol and Aner were Abram's allies.
When Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he called out the three hundred and eighteen trained men who had been born in his household. He chased the enemy as far as Dan.
During the night Abram divided his men into groups and attacked them. He defeated them and chased them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
He brought back all the goods, and he also brought back his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the other people.
After Abram came back from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King's Valley.
Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram and said, "May Abram be blessed by God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth.
And praise be to God Most High, who handed your enemies over to you." Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people and keep the goods for yourself."
But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand and made a solemn promise to the LORD, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth,
that I will not take anything that belongs to you, not even a thread or the strap of a sandal. Then you will never be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'
I will take nothing except what my men have eaten. But let the men who went with me, Aner, Eshkol and Mamre, have their share."
After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, and your reward will be very great."
But Abram said, "Lord GOD, what can you give me, since I still have no children? The one who will receive everything I own is Eliezer of Damascus."
Abram went on, "You have not given me any children, so a servant born in my household will be my heir."
Then the word of the LORD came to him: "This man will not be your heir. A son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir."
The LORD took Abram outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can count them." Then he said to him, "That is how many your children and their children will be."
Abram believed the LORD, and the LORD counted that faith as making him right with God.
He also said to him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to own."
But Abram said, "Lord GOD, how can I know that I will own it?"
So the LORD said to him, "Bring me a young cow, a female goat and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon."
Abram brought all these to him. He cut the animals in half and laid the halves opposite each other, but he did not cut the birds in half.
Birds of prey came down on the dead bodies, but Abram chased them away.
As the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and terrifying darkness came over him.

Then the LORD said to him, "You can be sure that your children and their children will be strangers in a country that is not theirs. They will be made slaves there and treated badly for four hundred years.
But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves, and afterwards they will come out with great wealth.
As for you, you will join your ancestors in peace. You will die at a good old age and be buried.
After four generations your people will come back here, because the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure."
When the sun had gone down and it was dark, a smoking fire pot and a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces of the animals.
On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram. He said, "I give this land to your children and their children, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.
It is the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites and the Jebusites."
Sarai, Abram's wife, had not given him any children. But she had an Egyptian slave woman named Hagar.
So Sarai said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Go and sleep with my slave. Perhaps I can have a family through her." Abram agreed to what Sarai said.
So after Abram had been living in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian slave Hagar and gave her to her husband to be his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar knew she was pregnant, she began to look down on Sarai.
Then Sarai said to Abram, "This wrong done to me is your fault. I put my slave in your arms, and now that she knows she is pregnant, she looks down on me. May the LORD judge between you and me."
Abram said to Sarai, "She is your slave, and she is in your power. Do with her whatever you think best." Then Sarai treated Hagar so badly that she ran away from her.
The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring of water in the desert. It was the spring beside the road to Shur.
He said, "Hagar, slave of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She answered, "I am running away from my mistress Sarai."
Then the angel of the LORD told her, "Go back to your mistress and obey her."
The angel of the LORD also said, "I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them."
The angel of the LORD went on, "You are pregnant, and you will have a son. You must name him Ishmael, which means 'God hears', because the LORD has heard about your suffering.
He will be like a wild donkey of a man. He will fight against everyone, and everyone will fight against him. He will live at odds with all his brothers."
Hagar gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her: "You are the God who sees me." She said, "Have I really seen the One who sees me and stayed alive?"
That is why the well was called Beer Lahai Roi, which means "the well of the Living One who sees me". It is still there, between Kadesh and Bered.
So Hagar gave Abram a son, and Abram named his son Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Live in my presence and do what is right in every way.
I will make my covenant between me and you, and I will give you a very large family."
Abram bowed down with his face to the ground, and God said to him,
"This is my covenant with you: you will be the father of many nations.
Your name will no longer be Abram. Your name will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.
I will give you many, many descendants. Nations will come from you, and kings will be among your descendants.

I will keep my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you, for all generations to come. It will be a covenant that lasts for ever. I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
I will give the whole land of Canaan, where you are now living as a stranger, to you and your descendants after you. It will be theirs for ever, and I will be their God."
Then God said to Abraham, "As for you, you must keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you, for all generations to come.
This is my covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you must keep: every male among you must be circumcised.
You must cut off the foreskin of your bodies. It will be the sign of the covenant between me and you.

For all generations to come, every male among you who is eight days old must be circumcised. This includes those born in your household and those bought with money from a foreigner, who are not your own children.
Whether they are born in your household or bought with your money, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your bodies will be a covenant that lasts for ever.
Any male who is not circumcised must be cut off from his people, because he has broken my covenant."
God also said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you must no longer call her Sarai. Her name will be Sarah.
I will bless her, and I will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her so that she will be the mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her."
Abraham bowed down with his face to the ground. But he laughed and said to himself, "Can a man who is a hundred years old have a son? Can Sarah have a baby at the age of ninety?"
And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael could live under your blessing!"

Then God said, "Yes, but your wife Sarah will have a son, and you will name him Isaac, which means 'he laughs'. I will keep my covenant with him as a covenant that lasts for ever, for his descendants after him.

And as for Ishmael, I have heard you. I will surely bless him. I will give him many children and greatly increase his numbers. He will be the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.
But I will keep my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will have by this time next year."
When God had finished speaking with Abraham, he went up from him.
On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and every male in his household, those born in his household and those he had bought, and circumcised them, just as God had told him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,
and his son Ishmael was thirteen.
Abraham and his son Ishmael were both circumcised on that same day.
And every male in Abraham's household, those born there and those bought from foreigners, was circumcised with him.
The LORD appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre. Abraham was sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them, and bowed low to the ground.
He said, "My lord, if you are pleased with me, please do not pass by your servant.
Let me have a little water brought, so that you can all wash your feet and rest under this tree.
Let me get you something to eat, so that you can be refreshed before you go on your way. You have come to your servant, after all." "Very well," they answered. "Do as you say."
So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quick," he said. "Get three large measures of the best flour, knead it and bake some bread."
Then he ran to the herd and chose a fine, tender calf. He gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
Then he brought some butter and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and set them in front of the men. While they ate, he stood near them under the tree.
"Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked him. "There, in the tent," he said.
Then the LORD said, "I will surely come back to you about this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, which was behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were already very old, and Sarah was far too old to have children.
So Sarah laughed to herself as she thought, "After I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really have this joy?"
Then the LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Will I really have a baby, now that I am old?'
Is anything too hard for the LORD? I will come back to you at the set time next year, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah was afraid, so she lied and said, "I did not laugh." But he said, "Yes, you did laugh."
Then the men got up to leave, and they looked down towards Sodom. Abraham walked along with them to see them on their way.
Then the LORD said, "Should I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and all nations on earth will be blessed through him.

I have chosen him so that he will teach his children and his family after him to live the way the LORD wants, by doing what is right and fair. Then the LORD will do for Abraham what he has promised him."
Then the LORD said, "The cry against Sodom and Gomorrah is very loud, and their sin is very serious.
I will go down and see if what they have done is as bad as the cry that has reached me. If not, I will know."
The men turned away and went towards Sodom, but Abraham stayed standing in front of the LORD.
Then Abraham came near to him and said, "Will you really destroy good people along with the wicked?
What if there are fifty good people in the city? Will you really destroy it and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty good people in it?

Surely you would never do such a thing, killing good people together with the wicked, treating the good and the wicked alike! Surely you would never do that! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?"
The LORD said, "If I find fifty good people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."
Then Abraham spoke up again: "I am nothing but dust and ashes, yet I have been bold enough to speak to the Lord.
What if there are only forty-five good people instead of fifty? Will you destroy the whole city because five are missing?" "If I find forty-five there," he said, "I will not destroy it."
Once again Abraham spoke to him: "What if only forty are found there?" He said, "For the sake of the forty, I will not do it."
Then Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, Lord, but let me speak. What if only thirty can be found there?" He answered, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."
Abraham said, "Now that I have been so bold as to speak to the Lord, what if only twenty can be found there?" He said, "For the sake of the twenty, I will not destroy it."
Then Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, Lord, but let me speak just once more. What if only ten can be found there?" He answered, "For the sake of the ten, I will not destroy it."
When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, he went on his way, and Abraham went back home.
The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When he saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground.

He said, "My lords, please come to your servant's house. You can wash your feet and spend the night, and then get up early and go on your way." "No," they answered. "We will spend the night in the town square."
But Lot kept begging them, so they went with him into his house. He made a meal for them and baked bread without yeast, and they ate.
Before they had gone to bed, all the men of the city of Sodom, both young and old, came from every part of the city and surrounded the house.
They shouted to Lot, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them."
Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him.
He said, "No, my friends. Please do not do this wicked thing.

Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you like with them. But do not do anything to these men, because they have come under the protection of my roof."

"Get out of our way," they replied. And they said, "This man came here as a stranger, and now he wants to act as our judge! We will treat you worse than them." They kept pushing hard against Lot and moved forward to break down the door.
But the two men inside reached out, pulled Lot back into the house with them and shut the door.
Then they struck the men at the door of the house with blindness, both young and old, so that they wore themselves out trying to find the door.
The two men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,
because we are going to destroy this place. The cry to the LORD against its people is so great that he has sent us to destroy it."
So Lot went out and spoke to the men who were going to marry his daughters. He said, "Hurry and get out of this place, because the LORD is about to destroy the city!" But they thought he was joking.
As dawn was breaking, the angels urged Lot, "Hurry! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away when the city is punished."
But Lot was slow to move. So the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters, and led them safely out of the city, because the LORD was being kind to them.
As soon as they had brought them out, one of them said, "Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere in the plain! Run to the mountains, or you will be swept away!"
But Lot said to them, "No, my lords, please!
You have been so kind to your servant, and you have shown me great mercy by saving my life. But I cannot run to the mountains. This disaster will catch up with me, and I will die.
Look, there is a town near enough to run to, and it is small. Let me run there. It is very small, is it not? Then my life will be saved."
He said to him, "Very well, I will grant this request too. I will not destroy the town you are talking about.
But hurry and run there, because I cannot do anything until you reach it." That is why the town was called Zoar, which means "small".
The sun had risen over the land by the time Lot reached Zoar.
Then the LORD rained down burning sulphur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. It came from the LORD out of the sky.
He destroyed those cities and the whole plain, all the people living in the cities, and everything that grew on the land.
But Lot's wife, who was behind him, looked back, and she turned into a pillar of salt.
Early the next morning Abraham got up and went back to the place where he had stood in front of the LORD.
He looked down towards Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain, and he saw thick smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace.
So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham. He brought Lot out of the disaster that destroyed the cities where Lot had lived.
Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and went to live in the mountains, because he was afraid to stay in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.
One day the older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man anywhere around here to marry us and give us children, as people do all over the world.
Come, let's get our father to drink wine, and then sleep with him, so that we can keep our family line going through our father."
That night they got their father to drink wine, and the older daughter went in and slept with him. He did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "Last night I slept with my father. Let's get him to drink wine again tonight, and you go in and sleep with him, so that we can keep our family line going through our father."
So they got their father to drink wine that night too, and the younger daughter went in and slept with him. Again he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter had a son, and she named him Moab. He is the ancestor of the Moabites of today.
The younger daughter also had a son, and she named him Ben-Ammi. He is the ancestor of the Ammonites of today.
Abraham moved on from there into the Negev and lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in Gerar.
There Abraham said about his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream one night and said to him, "You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken. She is a married woman."
Now Abimelech had not gone near her. So he said, "Lord, will you destroy a nation that has done nothing wrong?
Did Abraham not say to me, 'She is my sister'? And did she not also say, 'He is my brother'? I did this with a clear conscience and clean hands."
Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience. That is why I kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now give the man's wife back to him. He is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not give her back, you can be sure that you and all your people will die."
Early the next morning Abimelech called all his officials together. When he told them everything that had happened, they were very afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham in and said, "What have you done to us? What wrong have I done to you, that you have brought such great guilt on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should never be done."
And Abimelech asked Abraham, "What were you thinking of when you did this?"
Abraham answered, "I said to myself, 'There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'
Besides, she really is my sister. She is the daughter of my father, though not of my mother, and she became my wife.
When God sent me wandering away from my father's home, I said to her, 'This is how you can show your love for me: everywhere we go, say about me, "He is my brother."'"
Then Abimelech brought sheep and cattle and male and female slaves, and gave them to Abraham. And he gave his wife Sarah back to him.
Abimelech said, "My land is in front of you. Live wherever you like."
To Sarah he said, "I am giving your brother a thousand pieces of silver. This is to show everyone with you that you are innocent. Everyone will know that you have done nothing wrong."
Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his slave women, so that they could have children again.
The LORD had kept every woman in Abimelech's household from having children, because of Abraham's wife Sarah.
The LORD was kind to Sarah, just as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and gave Abraham a son in his old age, at the very time God had promised him.
Abraham named the son Sarah had given him Isaac.
When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."
She also said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have given him a son in his old age."
The child grew up and was weaned from his mother's milk. On the day Isaac was weaned, Abraham held a great feast.
But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had given Abraham was making fun of Isaac.
So she said to Abraham, "Get rid of that slave woman and her son. That woman's son will never share the family inheritance with my son Isaac."
This upset Abraham very much, because Ishmael was his son too.
But God said to him, "Do not be upset about the boy and your slave woman. Listen to whatever Sarah tells you, because your family line will be counted through Isaac.
I will also make the son of the slave woman into a nation, because he is your child too."

Early the next morning Abraham took some food and a skin bag of water and gave them to Hagar. He put them on her shoulders and sent her away with the boy. She went on her way and wandered in the desert of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin was gone, she put the boy under one of the bushes.
Then she went and sat down about a bowshot away, because she thought, "I cannot watch the boy die." As she sat there, she began to cry loudly.
God heard the boy crying, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. He said to her, "What is the matter, Hagar? Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy crying as he lies there.
Get up, lift the boy up and take him by the hand, because I will make him into a great nation."
Then God opened Hagar's eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the desert and became a skilled archer.
While he was living in the desert of Paran, his mother found a wife for him from Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.
So now promise me here in front of God that you will not trick me or my children or my descendants. Show me and the land where you are living the same kindness that I have shown you."
Abraham said, "I promise."
Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had taken by force.
But Abimelech said, "I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, and I heard about it only today."
So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made an agreement.
Abraham set apart seven female lambs from the flock.
Abimelech asked Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven female lambs you have set apart?"
Abraham replied, "Accept these seven lambs from me as proof that I dug this well."
So that place was called Beersheba, which means "well of the oath", because the two men made a promise there.
After they had made the agreement at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army went back to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the God who lives for ever.
And Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" "Here I am," he answered.
Then God said, "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will show you."

Early the next morning Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took two of his servants with him, and his son Isaac. When he had cut enough wood for the burnt offering, he set out for the place God had told him about.
On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
He said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey while the boy and I go over there. We will worship, and then we will come back to you."
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on his son Isaac to carry. He himself carried the fire and the knife. As the two of them walked on together,
Isaac spoke up and said to his father Abraham, "Father?" "Yes, my son?" Abraham replied. "The fire and wood are here," Isaac said, "but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
Abraham answered, "God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." And the two of them walked on together.
When they reached the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood on it. He tied up his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Then he reached out his hand and took the knife to kill his son.
But the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Here I am," he replied.
"Do not lay a hand on the boy," he said. "Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you truly respect God, because you have not held back from me your son, your only son."
Abraham looked up, and there behind him he saw a ram caught by its horns in a bush. He went over, took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son.
So Abraham called that place "The LORD Will Provide". And to this day people say, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."
The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time
and said, "The LORD says, 'I make a solemn promise by my own name. Because you have done this and have not held back your son, your only son,
I will surely bless you. I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take over the cities of their enemies,
and through your descendants all nations on earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed me.'"
Then Abraham went back to his servants, and they set off together for Beersheba. And Abraham stayed in Beersheba.
Some time later Abraham was told, "Milcah has also had children. She has given your brother Nahor sons:
Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel, who was the father of Aram,
Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel."
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah gave these eight sons to Abraham's brother Nahor.
Nahor's second wife, whose name was Reumah, also had sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maakah.
Sarah lived to be a hundred and twenty-seven years old.
She died at Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her.
Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites. He said,
"I am a foreigner and a stranger among you. Sell me some land for a burial place here, so that I can bury my dead wife."
The Hittites answered Abraham,
"Sir, listen to us. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us will refuse you his tomb for burying your dead."
Then Abraham got up and bowed down in front of the people of the land, the Hittites.
He said to them, "If you are willing to let me bury my dead, then listen to me. Ask Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf
to sell me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him and is at the end of his field. Ask him to sell it to me for the full price, so that I can own it as a burial place among you."
Ephron the Hittite was sitting among his people. He answered Abraham in front of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.
"No, sir, listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in front of my people. Bury your dead."
Again Abraham bowed down in front of the people of the land.
And he said to Ephron in front of them all, "Please listen to me. I will pay the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I can bury my dead there."
Ephron answered Abraham,
"Listen to me, sir. The land is worth four hundred pieces of silver, but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead."
Abraham agreed to Ephron's price. He weighed out for him the price he had named in front of the Hittites: four hundred pieces of silver, by the weight used by the traders of the time.
So Ephron's field in Machpelah, near Mamre, became Abraham's. This included the field and the cave in it, and all the trees within the borders of the field.
It became Abraham's property in front of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of the city.
After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which is at Hebron in the land of Canaan.
So the field and the cave in it were handed over to Abraham by the Hittites as his own burial place.
Abraham was now very old, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.
Abraham said to his oldest servant, the one in charge of everything he owned, "Put your hand under my thigh as a sign of a solemn promise.

I want you to make a promise in the name of the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth. Promise that you will not choose a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living.
Instead, go to my own country and my own relatives, and choose a wife for my son Isaac there."
The servant asked him, "What if the woman is not willing to come back with me to this land? Should I then take your son back to the country you came from?"
"Make sure that you do not take my son back there," Abraham said.

"The LORD, the God of heaven, brought me out of my father's home and my native land. He spoke to me and promised me, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send his angel ahead of you, so that you can find a wife for my son there.
If the woman is not willing to come back with you, then you will be free from this promise. But do not take my son back there."
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and made a solemn promise to him about this.
Then the servant took ten of his master's camels and set out, taking with him all kinds of good gifts from his master. He travelled to Aram Naharaim, to the town where Nahor lived.
Outside the town he made the camels kneel down near the well. It was evening, the time when the women go out to fetch water.
Then he prayed, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, give me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Look, I am standing beside this spring, and the young women of the town are coming out to fetch water.

I will say to one of them, 'Please lower your jar so that I can have a drink.' If she says, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water too', let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. That is how I will know that you have shown kindness to my master."
Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah and Nahor, Abraham's brother.
The young woman was very beautiful, and she had never slept with a man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar and came up again.
The servant hurried to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."
"Drink, sir," she said, and she quickly lowered the jar into her hands and gave him a drink.
After she had given him a drink, she said, "I will fetch water for your camels too, until they have had enough to drink."
So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to fetch more water, and fetched enough for all his camels.
Without saying a word, the man watched her closely to find out whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.
When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold nose ring weighing about six grams and two gold bracelets weighing about a hundred and ten grams.
Then he asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
She answered him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah had by Nahor."
And she added, "We have plenty of straw and food for the camels, and room for you to spend the night."
Then the man bowed down and worshipped the LORD.

He said, "Praise be to the LORD, the God of my master Abraham. He has not stopped showing his kindness and faithfulness to my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master's relatives."
The young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he hurried out to the man at the spring.

He had seen the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister's arms, and he had heard Rebekah tell what the man had said to her. So he went out to the man and found him standing by the camels near the spring.
"Come, you who are blessed by the LORD," he said. "Why are you standing out here? I have got the house ready, and a place for the camels."
So the man went to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and food were brought for the camels, and water for him and his men to wash their feet.
Then food was set in front of him, but he said, "I will not eat until I have told you what I have come to say." "Then tell us," Laban said.
So he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
The LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become very rich. The LORD has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
My master's wife Sarah gave him a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.
My master made me promise, saying, 'You must not choose a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live.
Instead, go to my father's family and to my own relatives, and choose a wife for my son.'
Then I asked my master, 'What if the woman will not come back with me?'
He replied, 'The LORD, whom I have served, will send his angel with you and make your journey a success. You will find a wife for my son from my own relatives and from my father's family.
Then, when you go to my relatives, you will be free from your promise. Even if they refuse to give her to you, you will be free from your promise.'
When I came to the spring today, I said, 'LORD, God of my master Abraham, please make my journey a success.
Look, I am standing beside this spring. If a young woman comes out to fetch water and I say to her, "Please let me drink a little water from your jar",
and if she says to me, "Drink, and I will fetch water for your camels too", let her be the one the LORD has chosen for my master's son.'
Before I had finished praying in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and fetched water, and I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water too.' So I drank, and she gave the camels water too.
I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.' Then I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
I bowed down and worshipped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right road to find the granddaughter of my master's brother for his son.
Now, if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, so that I will know which way to turn."
Laban and Bethuel answered, "This has come from the LORD. We can say nothing to you, either good or bad.
Here is Rebekah. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has said."
When Abraham's servant heard what they said, he bowed down to the ground in front of the LORD.
Then the servant brought out gold and silver jewellery and clothes, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and to her mother.
Then he and the men who were with him ate and drank, and they spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, "Send me back to my master."
But her brother and her mother replied, "Let the young woman stay with us for ten days or so. Then you may go."
But he said to them, "Do not keep me waiting, now that the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so that I can go back to my master."
Then they said, "Let's call the young woman and ask her what she wants."
So they called Rebekah and asked her, "Will you go with this man?" "I will go," she said.
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, together with her nurse, Abraham's servant and his men.
They blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your descendants take over the cities of their enemies."
Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, climbed onto the camels and went with the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Now Isaac had come from Beer Lahai Roi, because he was living in the Negev.
One evening he went out to the field to think and pray. He looked up and saw camels coming.
Rebekah also looked up, and when she saw Isaac, she got down from her camel.
She asked the servant, "Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?" "He is my master," the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.
Then the servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah, and he married her. She became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
Abraham married another wife, whose name was Keturah.
She gave him these sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.
Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. The descendants of Dedan were the Ashurites, the Letushites and the Leummites.
The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanok, Abida and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.
Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac.
But while he was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of his other wives. Then he sent them away from his son Isaac, to the land of the east.
Abraham lived a hundred and seventy-five years in all.
Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age. He was an old man who had lived a full life, and he joined his ancestors who had died before him.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.
This was the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah.
After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac, who was living near Beer Lahai Roi.
This is the family line of Abraham's son Ishmael, whom Sarah's slave, Hagar the Egyptian, had given to Abraham.
