But the people of Israel had walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
That day the LORD saved Israel from the power of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead on the seashore.
When the people of Israel saw the great power the LORD had used against the Egyptians, they feared the LORD. And they put their trust in the LORD and in his servant Moses.
Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD: "I will sing to the LORD, because he has won a glorious victory. He has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea.
The LORD is my strength and my song. He has saved me. He is my God, and I will praise him. He is my father's God, and I will lift him up high.
The LORD is a warrior. The LORD is his name.
He has thrown Pharaoh's chariots and his army into the sea. Pharaoh's best officers drowned in the Red Sea.
The deep waters covered them. They sank to the bottom like a stone.
Your right hand, LORD, is glorious in power. Your right hand, LORD, smashed the enemy to pieces.
In your great majesty you threw down those who rose up against you. You sent out your burning anger, and it burned them up like dry straw.
With a blast from your nose the waters piled up. The flowing waters stood up like a wall. The deep waters became solid in the middle of the sea.
The enemy said, 'I will chase them and catch them. I will divide what I take from them. I will take all I want. I will pull out my sword, and my hand will destroy them.'
But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Who among the gods is like you, LORD? Who is like you, glorious in holiness, amazing in praises, doing wonders?
You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.
In your faithful love you will lead the people you have set free. In your strength you will guide them to your holy home.
The nations will hear and shake with fear. Terror will grip the people of Philistia.
The leaders of Edom will be afraid. The strong men of Moab will tremble. All the people of Canaan will lose their courage.
Terror and fear will fall on them. Because of the power of your arm they will be as still as a stone, until your people pass by, LORD, until the people you bought pass by.
You will bring them in and plant them on your own mountain, the place, LORD, you made for your home, the holy place, Lord, that your hands have built.
The LORD will rule forever and ever."
When Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the people of Israel walked through the sea on dry ground.
Then Miriam the prophet, Aaron's sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her, playing tambourines and dancing.
Miriam sang to them: "Sing to the LORD, because he has won a glorious victory. He has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea."
Then Moses led Israel away from the Red Sea, and they went into the desert of Shur. For three days they travelled in the desert without finding water.
When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. That is why the place is called Marah, which means bitter.
So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What are we going to drink?"
Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD gave them a rule and a law, and there he tested them.

He said, "If you listen carefully to the LORD your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his laws, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD, who heals you."
Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there near the water.
The whole community of Israel left Elim and came to the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai. It was the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left Egypt.
In the desert the whole community grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

The people of Israel said to them, "We wish the LORD had killed us in Egypt! There we sat around pots of meat and ate all the bread we wanted. But you have brought us out into this desert to starve this whole crowd to death."

Then the LORD said to Moses, "Look, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them, to see whether they will follow my instructions.
On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days."
So Moses and Aaron said to all the people of Israel, "This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt.
And in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard you grumbling against him. Who are we, that you should grumble against us?"

Moses also said, "The LORD will give you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has heard you grumbling against him. Who are we? You are not grumbling against us, but against the LORD."
Then Moses said to Aaron, "Tell the whole community of Israel, 'Come near to the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling.'"
While Aaron was speaking to the whole community of Israel, they looked towards the desert, and there was the glory of the LORD shining in the cloud.
The LORD said to Moses,
"I have heard the grumbling of the people of Israel. Tell them, 'At sunset you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"
That evening quails came and covered the camp. And in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
When the dew was gone, there on the ground in the desert were small, round flakes, as thin as frost on the ground.
When the people of Israel saw it, they asked each other, "What is it?" because they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat.
This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Each of you is to gather as much as you need. Take an omer, about two litres, for each person living in your tent.'"
The people of Israel did this. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
When they measured it, the one who gathered a lot did not have too much, and the one who gathered a little did not have too little. Each one gathered just as much as he needed.
Then Moses said to them, "No one is to keep any of it until morning."
But some of them did not listen to Moses. They kept part of it until morning, and it was full of worms and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
Each morning everyone gathered as much as he needed. When the sun grew hot, it melted away.
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much, two omers for each person. The leaders of the community came and told Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD commanded: 'Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil. Keep whatever is left over until morning.'"
So they kept it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not smell or get worms in it.
Moses said, "Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. You will not find any of it on the ground today.
You may gather it for six days, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will not be any."
Even so, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but they found none.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to obey my commands and my teachings?
Remember that the LORD has given you the Sabbath. That is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. On the seventh day everyone is to stay where he is. No one is to go out."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The people of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed, and it tasted like thin cakes made with honey.

Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Keep an omer of manna for all time to come, so that your children can see the bread I gave you to eat in the desert when I brought you out of Egypt.'"
So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it in front of the LORD, to be kept for all time to come."
As the LORD commanded Moses, Aaron put the manna in front of the box with the Testimony, so that it would be kept.
The people of Israel ate manna for forty years, until they came to a land where people lived. They ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
An omer is one tenth of an ephah.
The whole community of Israel left the desert of Sin, travelling from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
So they argued with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink." Moses answered, "Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing the LORD?"
But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt? Was it to kill us, our children, and our animals with thirst?"
Then Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to throw stones at me."
The LORD answered Moses, "Walk on ahead of the people. Take some of the leaders of Israel with you, and take in your hand the staff you used to strike the Nile, and go.
I will stand there in front of you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." So Moses did this while the leaders of Israel watched.
He called the place Massah, which means testing, and Meribah, which means arguing, because the people of Israel argued, and because they tested the LORD by saying, "Is the LORD with us or not?"
Then the Amalekites came and attacked the people of Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Choose some men for us and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
So Joshua did what Moses told him and fought the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning. But whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.
When Moses' arms grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on each side. So his hands stayed steady until sunset.
So Joshua defeated the Amalekite army with the sword.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this in a book so that it will be remembered, and make sure Joshua hears it. I will completely wipe out the memory of the Amalekites from under heaven."
Moses built an altar and called it "The LORD is my Banner."
He said, "The LORD has made a promise: the LORD will be at war with the Amalekites in every generation."
Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard about everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
Moses had sent his wife Zipporah back home, and his father-in-law Jethro had taken her in,
along with her two sons. One son was named Gershom, because Moses had said, "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land."
The other was named Eliezer, because Moses had said, "My father's God was my helper. He saved me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to Moses in the desert, together with Moses' wife and sons. Moses was camped near the mountain of God.
Jethro sent word to Moses: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons."
So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed down and kissed him. They asked how each other was, and then they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake. He told him about all the troubles they had met on the way, and how the LORD had saved them.
Jethro was very happy to hear about all the good things the LORD had done for Israel in saving them from the Egyptians.
Jethro said, "Praise the LORD, who saved you from the Egyptians and from Pharaoh, and who saved the people from the power of the Egyptians.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, because of what he did to those who treated Israel so proudly."
Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God. Aaron came with all the leaders of Israel to eat a meal with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
The next day Moses sat down to judge the people's cases, and the people stood around him from morning until evening.

When his father-in-law saw everything Moses was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, while all these people stand around you from morning until evening?"
Moses answered him, "Because the people come to me to ask what God wants.
Whenever they have a problem, they come to me, and I decide between one person and another. I also teach them God's rules and laws."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good.
You and these people who come to you will only wear yourselves out. The work is too heavy for you. You cannot do it alone.
Now listen to me, and I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must speak for the people in front of God and bring their problems to him.
Teach them his rules and laws. Show them how they should live and what work they should do.
But choose capable men from all the people, men who fear God, who can be trusted, and who hate taking bribes. Put them in charge of the people as leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

Let them judge the people's cases at all times. They can bring the difficult cases to you, but they can decide the simple cases themselves. That will make your load lighter, because they will share it with you.
If you do this, and God commands you to, you will be able to stand the strain. And all these people will go home satisfied."
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
He chose capable men from all Israel and made them leaders of the people, leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people's cases at all times. They brought the difficult cases to Moses, but they decided the simple ones themselves.
Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro went back to his own country.
In the third month after the people of Israel left Egypt, on that very day, they came to the desert of Sinai.
After they left Rephidim, they entered the desert of Sinai, and Israel camped there in the desert in front of the mountain.
Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain. He said, "This is what you must say to the family of Jacob, and tell the people of Israel:
'You have seen what I did to Egypt. You have seen how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
Now if you truly obey me and keep my covenant, you will be my own special treasure out of all the nations. The whole earth is mine,
but you will be a kingdom of priests for me and a holy nation.' These are the words you must speak to the people of Israel."
So Moses went back and called the leaders of the people together. He told them all the words the LORD had commanded him to say.
All the people answered together, "We will do everything the LORD has said." So Moses took the people's answer back to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, "I am going to come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people will hear me speaking with you, and will always trust you." Then Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and make them holy today and tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes,
and be ready by the third day. On that day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai where all the people can see.
Put a boundary around the mountain for the people, and tell them, 'Be careful not to go up the mountain or even touch the edge of it. Anyone who touches the mountain must be put to death.

No one is to touch that person. He must be stoned or shot with arrows. Whether it is a person or an animal, it must not live.' Only when the ram's horn sounds a long blast may they come up to the mountain."
So Moses went down the mountain to the people and made them holy, and they washed their clothes.
Then he said to the people, "Be ready by the third day. Do not have sex with a woman."
On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, with a thick cloud over the mountain and a very loud trumpet blast. Everyone in the camp shook with fear.
Then Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was covered with smoke, because the LORD came down on it in fire. The smoke rose up like smoke from a furnace, and the whole mountain shook violently.
The sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice like thunder.
The LORD came down to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the top of the mountain. So Moses went up.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to force their way through to see the LORD, or many of them will die.
Even the priests, who come near to the LORD, must make themselves holy, or the LORD will break out against them."
Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, because you yourself warned us, 'Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.'"
The LORD said to him, "Go down and bring Aaron up with you. But the priests and the people must not force their way through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them."
So Moses went down to the people and told them.
Then God spoke all these words:
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, where you were slaves.
Do not have any other gods except me.
Do not make for yourselves an idol, or a statue of anything in the sky above, on the earth below, or in the water under the earth.
Do not bow down to them or worship them, because I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God. I punish the children for the sins of their parents, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
But I show faithful love to thousands of generations of those who love me and obey my commands.
Do not misuse the name of the LORD your God. The LORD will not let anyone go unpunished who misuses his name.
Remember the Sabbath day, and keep it holy.
You have six days to work and do all your jobs,
but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On that day do not do any work, not you, your son or daughter, your male or female servant, your animals, or any foreigner living in your towns.
For in six days the LORD made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, but he rested on the seventh day. That is why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
Honour your father and your mother, so that you may live a long time in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not murder.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not tell lies about your neighbour in court.
Do not long for your neighbour's house. Do not long for your neighbour's wife, his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbour."
When the people heard the thunder and the trumpet, and saw the lightning and the mountain smoking, they shook with fear and stood far away.
They said to Moses, "You speak to us yourself, and we will listen. But do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that the fear of him will be with you and keep you from sinning."
The people stayed far away, while Moses went near the thick darkness where God was.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Tell the people of Israel this: 'You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
Do not make any gods of silver or gold to worship alongside me.
Make an altar of earth for me, and offer on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. Wherever I cause my name to be honoured, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make an altar of stones for me, do not build it with cut stones, because if you use a tool on it, you will make it unholy.
And do not go up steps to my altar, so that your private parts are not shown on it.'
"These are the laws you must set before the people:
If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year he is to go free without paying anything.
If he came alone, he is to leave alone. If he had a wife when he came, she is to go with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she has sons or daughters, the woman and her children belong to her master. Only the man will go free.
But if the servant says clearly, 'I love my master, my wife, and my children. I do not want to go free,'
then his master must take him to God. He must take him to the door or the doorpost and push a sharp tool through his ear. Then he will be his servant for life.
If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free the way male servants do.
If she does not please the master who chose her for himself, he must let her be bought back. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, because he has broken his promise to her.
If he chooses her for his son, he must treat her like a daughter.
If he marries another woman, he must not take away from the first one her food, her clothing, or her rights as a wife.
If he does not give her these three things, she may go free without paying any money.
Anyone who hits a person and kills him must be put to death.
But if he did not plan it, and God let it happen, he may run away to a place I will choose for you.
But if someone plans and kills another person on purpose, take him away even from my altar and put him to death.
Anyone who attacks his father or his mother must be put to death.
Anyone who kidnaps another person must be put to death, whether he has sold the person or still has him.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death.
Suppose two men are fighting, and one hits the other with a stone or with his fist. The injured man does not die, but he has to stay in bed.

If he later gets up and walks around outside with a walking stick, the man who hit him will not be punished. But he must pay the injured man for the time he lost, and take care of him until he is completely healed.
If a man beats his male or female slave with a stick, and the slave dies on the spot, the man must be punished.
But if the slave gets up after a day or two, the owner is not to be punished, because the slave is his property.
Suppose men are fighting and hurt a pregnant woman, and she gives birth too early, but there is no serious injury. The man who hurt her must pay whatever her husband asks and the judges allow.
But if there is serious injury, you must take life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
If a man hits his male or female servant in the eye and destroys it, he must let the servant go free to pay for the eye.
If he knocks out a tooth of his male or female servant, he must let the servant go free to pay for the tooth.
If a bull kills a man or a woman with its horns, the bull must be stoned to death, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the bull will not be held responsible.

But suppose the bull has had the habit of attacking people, and the owner has been warned but has not kept it penned up. If it then kills a man or a woman, the bull must be stoned, and its owner must also be put to death.
But if the owner is allowed to pay money instead, he must pay whatever is demanded to save his life.
The same law applies if the bull attacks a son or a daughter.
If the bull attacks a male or female slave, the owner must pay the slave's master thirty pieces of silver, and the bull must be stoned.
Suppose a man uncovers a pit, or digs one and does not cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it.
The owner of the pit must pay for the loss. He must pay its owner, and the dead animal will belong to him.
If one man's bull hurts another man's bull and it dies, they must sell the live bull and share the money. They must also share the dead animal.
But if everyone knew that the bull had the habit of attacking, and its owner did not keep it penned up, the owner must pay, a live bull for the dead one, and the dead animal will be his.
"If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, he must pay back five oxen for the ox, or four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking into a house at night and is hit and killed, the person who killed him is not guilty of murder.

But if it happens after the sun has come up, the person who killed him is guilty of murder. A thief must pay back what he stole. If he has nothing, he must be sold as a slave to pay for what he stole.
If the stolen animal is found alive with him, whether it is an ox, a donkey, or a sheep, he must pay back twice as much.
If a man lets his animals graze in a field or vineyard, and lets them loose so that they eat in someone else's field, he must pay for the loss from the best of his own field or vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and spreads into thorn bushes so that it burns up bundles of grain, or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must pay for the loss.
If a man gives his neighbour money or goods to keep safe, and they are stolen from the neighbour's house, the thief, if he is caught, must pay back twice as much.
But if the thief is not found, the owner of the house must go before God, to find out whether he himself has taken his neighbour's goods.

In every case of a dispute over property, whether it is an ox, a donkey, a sheep, clothing, or anything lost, where someone says, 'This is mine,' both people must bring their case before God. The one whom God declares guilty must pay back twice as much to the other.
If a man gives his neighbour a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to look after, and it dies or is hurt or is taken away while no one is looking,
the neighbour must take an oath before the LORD that he did not take his neighbour's property. The owner must accept this, and no payment is needed.
But if the animal was stolen from the neighbour, he must pay the owner for it.
If it was torn to pieces by a wild animal, he must bring the remains as proof. He does not have to pay for what was torn to pieces.
If a man borrows an animal from his neighbour, and it is hurt or dies while the owner is not there, he must pay for it.
But if the owner was there, the borrower does not have to pay. If the animal was hired, the money paid for the hire covers the loss.
If a man talks a young woman into having sex with him, and she is a virgin who is not promised to be married, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
If her father completely refuses to let him marry her, he must still pay the full bride price that is paid for a virgin.
Do not let a woman who practises witchcraft live.
Anyone who has sex with an animal must be put to death.
Anyone who offers sacrifices to any god other than the LORD must be destroyed.
Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
Do not take advantage of a widow or an orphan.
If you do, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword. Then your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend money to one of my people who is poor, do not treat it like a business deal. Do not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbour's coat as a promise that he will pay you back, give it back to him before the sun goes down,
because that coat is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? When he cries out to me, I will hear, because I am kind.
Do not speak evil against God, and do not curse a ruler of your people.
Do not hold back the offerings from your harvest and from your wine and oil. You must give me the firstborn of your sons.
Do the same with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, and on the eighth day give them to me.
You are to be my holy people. So do not eat the meat of an animal killed by wild animals in the field. Throw it to the dogs.
"Do not spread false stories. Do not help a guilty person by telling lies in court.
Do not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you speak in court, do not side with the crowd to twist justice.
And do not favour a poor person in his case just because he is poor.
If you come across your enemy's ox or donkey wandering off, be sure to take it back to him.
If you see the donkey of someone who hates you lying under its load, do not walk away. Be sure to help him with it.
Do not deny justice to poor people in their court cases.
Stay far away from false charges. Do not put to death someone who is innocent and right, because I will not let the guilty go free.
Do not take a bribe, because a bribe blinds those who can see, and twists the words of people who are right.
Do not oppress a foreigner. You know how it feels to be a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
For six years plant your fields and gather their crops.

But in the seventh year let the land rest and do not plant it. Then the poor among your people can get food from it, and the wild animals can eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyards and your olive trees.
Do your work in six days, but on the seventh day rest. Then your ox and your donkey can rest, and your slaves and the foreigners living with you can be refreshed.
Be careful to do everything I have told you. Do not call on the names of other gods. Do not even let their names be heard on your lips.
Three times a year you must hold a feast for me.

Celebrate the Feast of Bread Without Yeast. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the set time in the month of Abib, because in that month you came out of Egypt. No one is to come before me empty-handed.

Celebrate the Feast of Harvest with the first crops from what you have planted in your fields. And celebrate the Feast of Gathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your crops from the fields.
Three times a year all your men must come before the Lord GOD.
Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me together with anything made with yeast. Do not keep the fat of my feast offerings until morning.
Bring the best of the first crops from your land to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Look, I am sending an angel ahead of you to protect you on the way and to bring you to the place I have made ready.
Pay attention to him and listen to what he says. Do not rebel against him. He will not forgive your rebellion, because my name is in him.
If you listen carefully to what he says and do everything I tell you, I will be an enemy to your enemies, and I will fight those who fight you.
My angel will go ahead of you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
Do not bow down to their gods or worship them, or follow their ways. You must completely destroy their gods and smash their sacred stones.
Worship the LORD your God, and he will bless your food and your water. I will take sickness away from among you.
No woman in your land will lose her baby or be unable to have children. I will give you a full life.
I will send my terror ahead of you, and I will throw into confusion every nation you meet. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
I will send hornets ahead of you to drive the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites out of your way.
But I will not drive them out in a single year. If I did, the land would become empty, and the wild animals would become too many for you.
I will drive them out little by little, until you have grown in number and can take over the land.

I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the River Euphrates. I will hand over to you the people who live in the land, and you will drive them out ahead of you.
Do not make any agreement with them or with their gods.
Do not let them live in your land, or they will cause you to sin against me. If you worship their gods, it will surely be a trap for you."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the leaders of Israel. Worship from a distance.
Only Moses may come near the LORD. The others must not come near, and the people must not come up with him."
Moses went and told the people all the LORD's words and laws. They all answered with one voice, "We will do everything the LORD has said."
Then Moses wrote down everything the LORD had said. Early the next morning he got up and built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Then he sent young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he sprinkled on the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, "We will do everything the LORD has said. We will obey."
Then Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people. He said, "This is the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with you, based on all these words."
Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the leaders of Israel went up the mountain.
They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a floor made of sapphire stones, as clear as the sky itself.
God did not raise his hand against these leaders of Israel. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay here. I will give you the stone tablets with the law and commands I have written for teaching the people."
So Moses set out with Joshua his helper, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the leaders, "Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you. Anyone who has a dispute can go to them."
When Moses went up the mountain, the cloud covered it.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered the mountain. On the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from inside the cloud.
To the people of Israel, the glory of the LORD looked like a burning fire on top of the mountain.
Then Moses went into the cloud as he climbed up the mountain. And he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel to bring me an offering. Receive the offering for me from everyone whose heart makes them want to give.
These are the offerings you are to receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and red yarn; fine linen; goat hair;
ram skins dyed red; fine leather; acacia wood;
olive oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet-smelling incense;
and onyx stones and other jewels to be set in the ephod and the chest piece of the high priest.
Then have them make a holy place for me, and I will live among them.
Make this holy tent and all its furniture exactly like the pattern I will show you.
Have them make a box, the ark, out of acacia wood. It is to be about one metre and ten centimetres long, and about seventy centimetres wide and seventy centimetres high.
Cover it with pure gold, inside and out, and put a gold border around it.
Make four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
Then make poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
The poles must stay in the rings of the ark. They must not be taken out.
Then put inside the ark the tablets of the covenant that I will give you.
Make a cover for the ark out of pure gold. This is the place of mercy. It is to be about one metre and ten centimetres long and seventy centimetres wide.
Make two cherubim out of hammered gold for the two ends of the cover.
Make one cherub on one end and the other cherub on the other end. Make the cherubim and the cover all one piece.
The cherubim are to have their wings spread upwards, covering the cover with their wings. They are to face each other, looking down towards the cover.
Put the cover on top of the ark, and put inside the ark the tablets of the covenant that I will give you.
There, above the cover between the two cherubim on the ark of the covenant, I will meet with you. From there I will give you all my commands for the people of Israel.
Make a table out of acacia wood. It is to be about ninety centimetres long, forty-five centimetres wide, and seventy centimetres high.
Cover it with pure gold and put a gold border around it.
Make a rim around it about as wide as a hand, and put a gold border on the rim.
Make four gold rings for the table, and fasten them to the four corners, where the four legs are.
The rings are to be close to the rim, to hold the poles used to carry the table.
Make the poles out of acacia wood and cover them with gold. The table is to be carried with them.
Make its plates, dishes, jars, and bowls out of pure gold. They are to be used for pouring out drink offerings.
Always keep the special bread on the table in front of me.
Make a lampstand out of pure gold. Hammer out its base and its stem. Its flower-shaped cups, buds, and blossoms are to be all one piece with it.
Six branches are to come out from the sides of the lampstand, three on one side and three on the other.
Each of the six branches is to have three cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and blossoms.
And on the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and blossoms.
One bud is to be under the first pair of branches, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair. All six branches come out from the lampstand.
The buds and the branches are all to be one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
Then make its seven lamps and set them up on it, so that they light the space in front of it.
Its wick cutters and trays are to be made of pure gold.
Use about thirty-four kilograms of pure gold to make the lampstand and all these tools.
Be sure to make them exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain."
"Make the holy tent with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and red yarn. Have a skilled worker sew cherubim into them.
Every curtain is to be the same size, about twelve and a half metres long and almost two metres wide.
Join five of the curtains together, and do the same with the other five.
Make loops of blue cloth along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same on the end curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain, and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, with the loops facing each other.
Then make fifty gold hooks and use them to join the two sets of curtains together, so that the holy tent is one whole.
Make curtains of goat hair to make a tent over the holy tent. Make eleven of these curtains.
All eleven curtains are to be the same size, about thirteen and a half metres long and almost two metres wide.
Join five of the curtains together into one set, and the other six into another set. Fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
Then make fifty bronze hooks and put them in the loops to join the tent together, so that it is one whole.
The extra half curtain that is left over is to hang down at the back of the holy tent.
The tent curtains will be half a metre longer on each side. What is left over will hang down over the sides of the holy tent to cover it.
Make a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
Make upright frames of acacia wood for the holy tent.
Each frame is to be about four and a half metres long and seventy centimetres wide.
Each frame is to have two pegs to fit them together. Make all the frames of the holy tent in this way.
Make twenty frames for the south side of the holy tent.
Make forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases for each frame, one under each peg.
For the other side, the north side of the holy tent, make twenty frames,
and forty silver bases, two under each frame.
Make six frames for the back of the holy tent, the west end.
Make two frames for the corners at the back of the holy tent.
At these two corners the frames are to be double from the bottom all the way to the top, held by a single ring. Make both corners like this.
So there will be eight frames and sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
Also make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the holy tent,
five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames on the west side at the back.
The middle crossbar is to go all the way from one end to the other, halfway up the frames.
Cover the frames with gold, and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Cover the crossbars with gold too.
Set up the holy tent exactly the way you were shown on the mountain.
Make a curtain of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen. Have a skilled worker sew cherubim into it.
Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood covered with gold, standing on four silver bases.
Hang the curtain from the hooks, and put the ark of the covenant behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Put the cover, the place of mercy, on the ark of the covenant in the Most Holy Place.
Put the table outside the curtain on the north side of the holy tent. Put the lampstand across from the table on the south side.
For the entrance of the tent, make a screen of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns.
Make gold hooks for this screen, and five posts of acacia wood covered with gold. Make five bronze bases for them.
"Build an altar of acacia wood. It is to be square, about two and a quarter metres long and two and a quarter metres wide, and about one and a third metres high.
Make a horn at each of its four corners, so that the horns and the altar are one piece. Cover the altar with bronze.
Make all its tools out of bronze: its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, bowls, meat forks, and fire pans.
Make a grate for it, a bronze net, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the net.
Put the grate under the ledge of the altar, so that it reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles of acacia wood for the altar and cover them with bronze.
Put the poles through the rings, so that they are on both sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make the altar hollow, out of boards. Make it just as you were shown on the mountain.
Make a courtyard for the holy tent. The south side is to be forty-five metres long, with curtains of fine twisted linen.
It is to have twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The north side is also to be forty-five metres long, with curtains, twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The west end of the courtyard is to be twenty-two metres wide, with curtains, ten posts, and ten bases.
The east end, towards the sunrise, is also to be twenty-two metres wide.
On one side of the entrance there are to be curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.
On the other side there are also to be curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.

For the entrance to the courtyard, make a screen nine metres long of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns. It is to have four posts and four bases.
All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and hooks, and bronze bases.
The courtyard is to be forty-five metres long and twenty-two metres wide, with curtains of fine twisted linen over two metres high, and with bronze bases.
All the tools used in the service of the holy tent, and all its tent pegs and the pegs of the courtyard, are to be made of bronze.
Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil from pressed olives for the lamps, so that the lamps can keep burning all the time.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain that hangs in front of the covenant box, Aaron and his sons are to keep the lamps burning in front of the LORD from evening until morning. This is a law for the people of Israel that will last forever, for all generations."
"Have your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar brought to you from among the people of Israel, so that they can serve me as priests.
Make holy clothes for your brother Aaron, to give him honour and beauty.
Speak to all the skilled workers, whom I have filled with wisdom. Tell them to make clothes for Aaron, to set him apart as holy, so that he can serve me as priest.

These are the clothes they are to make: a chest piece, an ephod, a robe, a woven shirt, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy clothes for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they can serve me as priests.
Have them use gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.
Have them make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled worker.
It is to have two shoulder pieces fastened to its two corners, so that it can be tied together.
Its skilfully woven belt must be made the same way and be one piece with it, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
Take two onyx stones and carve on them the names of the sons of Israel.
Put six names on one stone and the other six on the other stone, in the order they were born.
Carve the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a jeweller carves a seal. Then put the stones in gold settings.
Fasten the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as stones to remind God of the sons of Israel. Aaron is to carry their names on his shoulders in front of the LORD, as a reminder.
Make gold settings,
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like a rope. Fasten the chains to the settings.
Make a chest piece for making decisions, the work of a skilled worker. Make it like the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It is to be square, folded double, about twenty-three centimetres long and twenty-three centimetres wide.
Put four rows of precious stones on it. In the first row put a ruby, a topaz, and a beryl.
In the second row put a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald.
In the third row put a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
In the fourth row put a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. Set them in gold settings.
There are to be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel. Each stone is to be carved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the chest piece, make chains of pure gold, twisted like a rope.
Make two gold rings and fasten them to the two upper corners of the chest piece.
Fasten the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the chest piece.
Fasten the other ends of the chains to the two settings, and attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
Make two gold rings and fasten them to the other two corners of the chest piece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
Make two more gold rings and fasten them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above its woven belt.
Tie the rings of the chest piece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that the chest piece sits above the woven belt and does not swing out from the ephod.
Whenever Aaron goes into the Holy Place, he will carry the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the chest piece for making decisions. It will always remind the LORD of them.

Put the Urim and the Thummim in the chest piece, so that they will be over Aaron's heart whenever he goes in to the LORD. So Aaron will always carry over his heart the means of making decisions for the people of Israel in front of the LORD.
Make the robe of the ephod all of blue cloth.
It is to have an opening for the head in the middle, with a woven edge around the opening like a collar, so that it will not tear.
Around the bottom hem of the robe make pomegranates of blue, purple, and red yarn, with gold bells between them.
A gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, are to go all around the hem of the robe.
Aaron must wear it when he serves as priest. The sound of the bells will be heard when he goes into the Holy Place in front of the LORD and when he comes out, so that he will not die.
Make a plate of pure gold, and carve on it like a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
Fasten it with a blue cord to the front of the turban.

It will be on Aaron's forehead. Aaron will carry the guilt of any wrong in the holy gifts the people of Israel set apart. It will always be on his forehead, so that their gifts will be accepted by the LORD.
Weave the shirt of fine linen, and make the turban of fine linen. The sash is to be the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns.
Make shirts, sashes, and caps for Aaron's sons too, to give them honour and beauty.
Put these clothes on your brother Aaron and his sons. Then anoint them, ordain them, and set them apart as holy, so that they can serve me as priests.
Make linen underwear for them to cover their bodies, reaching from the waist to the thigh.

Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting, or come near the altar to serve in the Holy Place, so that they do not become guilty and die. This is a law that will last forever for Aaron and his descendants after him."
"This is what you must do to set Aaron and his sons apart as holy, so that they can serve me as priests. Take a young bull and two rams with nothing wrong with them.
And from fine wheat flour, without yeast, make bread, thick loaves mixed with olive oil, and thin wafers brushed with olive oil.
Put them in a basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Take the clothes and dress Aaron in the shirt, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the chest piece. Tie the woven belt of the ephod around him.
Put the turban on his head, and attach the holy crown to the turban.
Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.
Bring his sons and dress them in shirts.
Tie sashes on Aaron and his sons, and put caps on the sons. The priesthood will belong to them by a law that lasts forever. In this way you will ordain Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to put their hands on its head.
Kill the bull in front of the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.
Then take all the fat around the insides, the best part of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the bull's meat, its skin, and its dung outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons are to put their hands on its head.
Kill it, and take its blood and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, and wash its insides and its legs. Put them with the pieces and the head.
Then burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a sweet smell, an offering made to the LORD by fire.
Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons are to put their hands on its head.

Kill it, and take some of its blood and put it on the bottom of the right ears of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then sprinkle the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.

Take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. Then he and his sons and their clothes will be made holy.
Take the fat from this ram, the fat tail, the fat around the insides, the best part of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh. This is the ram for the ordination.
From the basket of bread made without yeast, which is in front of the LORD, take one loaf of bread, one thick loaf made with oil, and one thin wafer.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and have them lift them up in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering, as a sweet smell to the LORD. It is an offering made to the LORD by fire.
Take the breast of the ram for Aaron's ordination, and lift it up in front of the LORD as a wave offering. It will be your share.
Set apart as holy the parts of the ram for the ordination that belong to Aaron and his sons: the breast that was waved and the thigh that was lifted up.
This is always to be the share that Aaron and his sons receive from the people of Israel. It is the gift the people of Israel must give to the LORD from their peace offerings.
Aaron's holy clothes will belong to his descendants after him, so that they can be anointed and ordained in them.
The son who becomes priest after him, and comes into the Tent of Meeting to serve in the Holy Place, is to wear them for seven days.
Take the ram for the ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
At the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread in the basket.
They are to eat these offerings by which their sins were covered when they were ordained and made holy. No one else may eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat of the ordination or any of the bread is left until morning, burn it. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.
Do all this for Aaron and his sons, just as I have commanded you. Take seven days to ordain them.
Every day offer a bull as a sin offering to cover sin. Make the altar clean by offering a sacrifice for it, and anoint it to make it holy.
For seven days make the altar clean and set it apart as holy. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches it will be holy.
This is what you are to offer on the altar every day, without fail: two lambs a year old.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other in the evening.
With the first lamb offer about a kilogram and a half of fine flour mixed with about one litre of oil from pressed olives, and about one litre of wine as a drink offering.
Offer the other lamb in the evening, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a sweet smell, an offering made to the LORD by fire.
For all generations to come, this burnt offering is to be made every day at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting in front of the LORD. There I will meet you and speak to you.
There I will also meet with the people of Israel, and the place will be made holy by my glory.
I will make the Tent of Meeting and the altar holy. And I will set apart Aaron and his sons as holy to serve me as priests.
Then I will live among the people of Israel and be their God.
They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of Egypt so that I could live among them. I am the LORD their God."
"Make an altar of acacia wood for burning incense.
It is to be square, about forty-five centimetres long and forty-five centimetres wide, and about ninety centimetres high. Its horns are to be one piece with it.
Cover the top, all the sides, and the horns with pure gold, and put a gold border around it.
Make two gold rings for the altar below the border, on the two opposite sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
Make the poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Put the altar in front of the curtain that hangs in front of the ark of the covenant, in front of the cover over the covenant tablets. There I will meet with you.
Aaron must burn sweet-smelling incense on the altar every morning when he takes care of the lamps.
And he must burn incense again when he lights the lamps in the evening. So incense will burn in front of the LORD all the time, for all generations to come.
Do not offer any other incense on this altar, or any burnt offering or grain offering, and do not pour a drink offering on it.

Once a year Aaron must make the altar clean by putting on its horns the blood of the sin offering that covers sin. This is to be done once a year for all generations to come. The altar is most holy to the LORD."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"When you count the people of Israel, each man must pay the LORD a price for his life when he is counted. Then no plague will come on them when you count them.
Each one who is counted must give half a shekel, using the weight of the holy place, where one shekel is twenty gerahs. This half shekel is an offering to the LORD.
All who are counted, twenty years old or more, must give this offering to the LORD.
When you give the LORD this offering to pay for your lives, the rich must not give more than half a shekel, and the poor must not give less.
Take this money from the people of Israel and use it for the work of the Tent of Meeting. It will be a reminder to the LORD of the people of Israel, a payment for your lives."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Make a bronze bowl with a bronze stand for washing. Put it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and feet with water from it.
Whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting, they must wash with water so that they will not die. They must also wash whenever they come near the altar to serve by burning an offering to the LORD.
They must wash their hands and feet so that they will not die. This is a law that will last forever for Aaron and his descendants, for all generations to come."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Take the finest spices: almost six kilograms of liquid myrrh, half as much, almost three kilograms, of sweet-smelling cinnamon, almost three kilograms of sweet-smelling cane,
and almost six kilograms of cassia, all weighed by the weight of the holy place. Also take about four litres of olive oil.
Make these into a holy anointing oil, a sweet-smelling blend, the work of a perfume maker. It will be the holy anointing oil.
Use it to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the covenant,
the table and all its tools, the lampstand and its tools, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its tools, and the washing bowl with its stand.
Set them apart as holy, so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them will be holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons, and set them apart as holy so that they can serve me as priests.
Say to the people of Israel, 'This is to be my holy anointing oil for all generations to come.
Do not pour it on ordinary people, and do not make any other oil with the same recipe. It is holy, and you must treat it as holy.
Anyone who makes oil like it, or puts it on anyone who is not a priest, must be cut off from his people.'"
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Take sweet spices, gum resin, onycha, and galbanum, together with pure frankincense, all in equal amounts.
Make it into incense, a sweet-smelling blend, the work of a perfume maker. Add salt to it, to make it pure and holy.
Grind some of it into powder, and put it in front of the covenant tablets in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It will be most holy to you.
Do not make any incense with this recipe for yourselves. Treat it as holy, set apart for the LORD.
Anyone who makes incense like it to enjoy its smell must be cut off from his people."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Look, I have chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God. I have given him wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and skill in all kinds of work.
He can make beautiful designs and work with gold, silver, and bronze.
He can cut and set precious stones, carve wood, and do every kind of skilled work.
And I have chosen Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to help him. I have also given skill to all the skilled workers, so that they can make everything I have commanded you:
the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the covenant with its cover, and all the other furniture of the tent,
the table and its tools, the pure gold lampstand and all its tools, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its tools, the washing bowl and its stand,
the woven clothes, both the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons when they serve as priests,
and the anointing oil and the sweet-smelling incense for the Holy Place. They must make them just as I have commanded you."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel, 'You must keep my Sabbaths. This is a sign between me and you for all generations to come, so that you will know that I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy to you. Anyone who treats it as unholy must be put to death. Anyone who does any work on that day must be cut off from his people.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Anyone who does any work on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
The people of Israel must keep the Sabbath, celebrating it for all generations to come, as a covenant that lasts forever.
It will be a sign between me and the people of Israel forever. For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he stopped working and rested.'"
When the LORD had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the covenant, the stone tablets written by the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, "Come, make us gods who will lead us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
Aaron answered them, "Take off the gold earrings that your wives, your sons, and your daughters are wearing, and bring them to me."
So all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
He took what they gave him and shaped it with a tool into a statue of a calf. Then they said, "Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up out of Egypt!"
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, "Tomorrow there will be a feast to the LORD."
So the next day the people got up early and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Afterwards they sat down to eat and drink, and then got up to party wildly.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go down, because your people, whom you brought up out of Egypt, have become wicked.

They have quickly turned away from what I commanded them. They have made themselves a statue of a calf. They have bowed down to it and offered sacrifices to it, and they have said, 'Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up out of Egypt.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "I have seen these people, and they are stubborn people.
Now leave me alone, so that my anger can burn against them and I can destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
But Moses begged the LORD his God. He said, "LORD, why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to do them harm, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth'? Turn from your fierce anger. Change your mind, and do not bring this disaster on your people.

Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. You made a promise to them, swearing by your own name: 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. I will give your descendants all this land I promised them, and it will be theirs forever.'"
So the LORD changed his mind and did not bring on his people the disaster he had spoken of.
Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hands. They were written on both sides, front and back.
The tablets were the work of God. The writing was the writing of God, carved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "There is the sound of war in the camp."
Moses replied, "It is not the sound of people shouting because they have won, and it is not the sound of people crying because they have lost. It is the sound of singing that I hear."
When Moses came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned. He threw the tablets out of his hands and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made and burned it in the fire. Then he ground it into powder, scattered it on the water, and made the people of Israel drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people do to you, that you led them into such a great sin?"
Aaron answered, "Do not be angry, my lord. You know how these people are set on doing evil.
They said to me, 'Make us gods who will lead us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
So I told them, 'Whoever has any gold, take it off.' They gave me the gold, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!"
Moses saw that the people were out of control. Aaron had let them get out of control, so that they became a joke to their enemies.
So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, "Whoever is on the LORD's side, come to me!" And all the Levites gathered around him.

Then he said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Each man must strap a sword to his side. Go back and forth through the camp from one end to the other, and each of you kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbour.'"
The Levites did what Moses commanded, and about three thousand of the people died that day.
Then Moses said, "Today you have set yourselves apart for the LORD, because each of you was against his own son and brother. So he has given you a blessing today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a terrible sin. But now I will go up to the LORD. Maybe I can make peace with him for your sin."
So Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, these people have committed a terrible sin. They have made themselves gods of gold.
But now, please forgive their sin. If you will not, then wipe my name out of the book you have written."
The LORD answered Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, I will wipe his name out of my book.
Now go and lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go ahead of you. But when the time comes for me to punish them, I will punish them for their sin."
And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they did with the calf Aaron had made.

Then the LORD said to Moses, "Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of Egypt. Go to the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.'
I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Go up to that land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are stubborn people, and I might destroy you on the way."
When the people heard these hard words, they were very sad, and no one put on any jewellery.

For the LORD had said to Moses, "Tell the people of Israel, 'You are stubborn people. If I went with you even for a moment, I might destroy you. Now take off your jewellery, and I will decide what to do with you.'"
So from Mount Horeb onwards, the people of Israel took off their jewellery.

Moses used to take a tent and set it up outside the camp, some distance away. He called it the Tent of Meeting. Anyone who wanted to ask the LORD something would go out to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would get up and stand at the entrances to their own tents, watching Moses until he went into the tent.
As Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stay at the entrance, while the LORD spoke with Moses.
Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would all stand and worship, each at the entrance of his own tent.
The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, the way a person speaks to a friend. Then Moses would go back to the camp. But his young helper Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.
Moses said to the LORD, "You keep telling me, 'Lead these people,' but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. You have said, 'I know you by name, and you have found favour with me.'
If I have found favour with you, please teach me your ways, so that I can know you and keep finding favour with you. And remember that this nation is your people."
The LORD answered, "I myself will go with you, and I will give you rest."
Then Moses said to him, "If you do not go with us yourself, do not send us up from here.

How else will anyone know that you are pleased with me and with your people? Only if you go with us. That is what will make me and your people different from all the other people on the face of the earth."
The LORD said to Moses, "I will do what you have asked, because you have found favour with me, and I know you by name."
Then Moses said, "Please show me your glory."

The LORD said, "I will make all my goodness pass in front of you, and I will call out my name, the LORD, in front of you. I will be kind to whom I choose to be kind, and I will show mercy to whom I choose to show mercy.
But you cannot see my face, because no one can see me and live."
Then the LORD said, "There is a place near me where you can stand on a rock.
When my glory passes by, I will put you in a crack in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. But my face must not be seen."
The LORD said to Moses, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready in the morning. Then come up Mount Sinai and stand in front of me there on top of the mountain.
No one is to come with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even the flocks and herds may graze in front of the mountain."
So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hands.
Then the LORD came down in the cloud and stood there with him, and called out his name, the LORD.
The LORD passed in front of Moses, calling out, "The LORD, the LORD, the God who is merciful and kind, slow to become angry, and full of faithful love and truth.

He keeps his faithful love for thousands, and forgives wrongdoing, rebellion, and sin. But he does not let the guilty go unpunished. He punishes the children and grandchildren for the sins of their parents, to the third and fourth generation."
Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshipped.
He said, "Lord, if I have found favour with you, please go with us. Even though these people are stubborn, forgive our wrongdoing and our sin, and take us as your own people."

Then the LORD said, "Look, I am making a covenant with you. In front of all your people I will do wonders never done before in any nation in all the world. All the people around you will see the work of the LORD, because what I am going to do for you is amazing.
Obey what I command you today. Look, I will drive out ahead of you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Be careful not to make an agreement with the people who live in the land where you are going, or they will become a trap among you.
Instead, tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and cut down their Asherah poles.
Do not worship any other god, because the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

Do not make an agreement with the people who live in the land. When they chase after their gods like a prostitute and offer sacrifices to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
And you might choose some of their daughters as wives for your sons. Then those daughters would chase after their gods like prostitutes, and lead your sons to do the same.
Do not make idols out of melted metal.
Celebrate the Feast of Bread Without Yeast. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the set time in the month of Abib, because in that month you came out of Egypt.
The first male born to every mother belongs to me, including all the firstborn males of your cattle and sheep.
Buy back the firstborn donkey by giving a lamb in its place. If you do not buy it back, break its neck. Buy back all your firstborn sons. No one is to come before me empty-handed.
Work for six days, but rest on the seventh day. Even during the time of ploughing and harvest you must rest.
Celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the first crops of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Gathering at the end of the year.
Three times a year all your men must come before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
I will drive out nations ahead of you and make your land larger. No one will try to take your land while you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me together with anything made with yeast. Do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover feast be left until morning.
Bring the best of the first crops from your land to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words, because by these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant in his hands, he did not know that his face was shining because he had been talking with the LORD.
When Aaron and all the people of Israel saw Moses, his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, so Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and he spoke to them.
After that, all the people of Israel came near, and he gave them all the commands the LORD had given him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished speaking to them, he put a veil over his face.
But whenever he went in to speak with the LORD, he took the veil off until he came out. And when he came out and told the people of Israel what he had been commanded,
they saw that his face was shining. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in again to speak with the LORD.
Moses gathered the whole community of Israel together and said to them, "These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is to be your holy day, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Anyone who does any work on that day must be put to death.
Do not light a fire in any of your homes on the Sabbath day."
Moses said to the whole community of Israel, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
From what you have, bring an offering to the LORD. Everyone who is willing is to bring the LORD an offering of gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and red yarn; fine linen; goat hair;
ram skins dyed red; fine leather; acacia wood;
olive oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet-smelling incense;
and onyx stones and other jewels to be set in the ephod and the chest piece.
All the skilled workers among you are to come and make everything the LORD has commanded:
the holy tent with its tent and its covering, its hooks, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the ark with its poles, its cover, and the curtain that hides it;
the table with its poles and all its tools, and the special bread;
the lampstand for light with its tools and lamps, and oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the sweet-smelling incense, and the screen for the entrance of the holy tent;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles and all its tools, and the washing bowl with its stand;
the curtains of the courtyard with their posts and bases, and the screen for the entrance to the courtyard;
the tent pegs for the holy tent and for the courtyard, and their ropes;
and the woven clothes for serving in the Holy Place, both the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons when they serve as priests."
Then the whole community of Israel left Moses.
Everyone whose heart moved him and whose spirit made him willing came and brought an offering to the LORD for the work on the Tent of Meeting, for all its service, and for the holy clothes.
All who were willing, both men and women, came and brought gold jewellery of every kind: pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. Everyone brought their gold as a wave offering to the LORD.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or red yarn, or fine linen, or goat hair, or ram skins dyed red, or fine leather, brought them.
Everyone who could give silver or bronze brought it as an offering to the LORD. And everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
Every skilled woman spun yarn with her hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.
And all the women who were willing and had the skill spun the goat hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and other jewels to be set in the ephod and the chest piece.
They also brought spices and olive oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the sweet-smelling incense.
All the men and women of Israel who were willing brought to the LORD a gift they freely chose to give, for all the work the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Then Moses said to the people of Israel, "Look, the LORD has chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and with skill in all kinds of work.
He can make beautiful designs and work with gold, silver, and bronze,
cut and set precious stones, carve wood, and do every kind of skilled work.
And the LORD has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.

He has filled them with skill to do every kind of work as carvers, designers, and people who sew beautiful patterns in blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen, and as weavers. They can do every kind of work and make beautiful designs.

"So Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person to whom the LORD has given wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of building the holy place, are to do the work just as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the LORD had given wisdom, everyone whose heart moved him to come and do the work.
They received from Moses all the offerings the people of Israel had brought for the work of building the holy place. And the people kept bringing more gifts every morning.
So all the skilled workers who were doing the work on the holy place stopped what they were doing,
and said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the work the LORD commanded us to do."
