So Moses gave an order, and it was announced all through the camp: "No man or woman is to make anything more as an offering for the holy place." So the people were stopped from bringing more,
because what they already had was more than enough to do all the work.
All the skilled workers among them made the holy tent with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and red yarn, with cherubim sewn into them by a skilled worker.
All the curtains were the same size, about twelve and a half metres long and almost two metres wide.
They joined five of the curtains together, and did the same with the other five.
They made loops of blue cloth along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and the same on the end curtain in the second set.
They made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, with the loops facing each other.
Then they made fifty gold hooks and used them to join the two sets of curtains together, so that the holy tent was one whole.
They made curtains of goat hair to make a tent over the holy tent, eleven curtains in all.
All eleven curtains were the same size, about thirteen and a half metres long and almost two metres wide.
They joined five of the curtains together into one set, and the other six into another set.
They made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
They made fifty bronze hooks to join the tent together, so that it was one whole.
They made a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
They made upright frames of acacia wood for the holy tent.
Each frame was about four and a half metres long and seventy centimetres wide.
Each frame had two pegs to fit them together. They made all the frames of the holy tent in this way.
They made twenty frames for the south side of the holy tent.
They made forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases for each frame, one under each peg.
For the other side, the north side of the holy tent, they made twenty frames,
and forty silver bases, two under each frame.
They made six frames for the back of the holy tent, the west end.
They made two frames for the corners at the back of the holy tent.
At these two corners the frames were double from the bottom all the way to the top, held by a single ring. Both corners were made like this.
So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
They also made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the holy tent,
five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames on the west side at the back.
They made the middle crossbar so that it went all the way from one end to the other, halfway up the frames.
They covered the frames with gold, and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. They covered the crossbars with gold too.
They made the curtain of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim sewn into it by a skilled worker.
They made four posts of acacia wood for it and covered them with gold. They made gold hooks for them, and cast four silver bases for them.
For the entrance of the tent they made a screen of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns.
They made five posts with hooks for the screen. They covered the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and made their five bases of bronze.
Bezalel made the ark out of acacia wood. It was about one metre and ten centimetres long, and about seventy centimetres wide and seventy centimetres high.
He covered it with pure gold, inside and out, and put a gold border around it.
He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
Then he made poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
He made the cover, the place of mercy, out of pure gold. It was about one metre and ten centimetres long and seventy centimetres wide.
He made two cherubim out of hammered gold for the two ends of the cover,
one cherub on one end and the other cherub on the other end. He made the cherubim and the cover all one piece.
The cherubim had their wings spread upwards, covering the cover with their wings. They faced each other, looking down towards the cover.
He made the table out of acacia wood. It was about ninety centimetres long, forty-five centimetres wide, and seventy centimetres high.
He covered it with pure gold and put a gold border around it.
He made a rim around it about as wide as a hand, and put a gold border on the rim.
He cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners, where the four legs were.
The rings were close to the rim, to hold the poles used to carry the table.
He made the poles out of acacia wood and covered them with gold, to carry the table.
He made the things for the table out of pure gold: its plates, dishes, bowls, and jars for pouring out drink offerings.
He made the lampstand out of pure gold. He hammered out its base and its stem. Its flower-shaped cups, buds, and blossoms were all one piece with it.
Six branches came out from the sides of the lampstand, three on one side and three on the other.
Each of the six branches had three cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and blossoms, on one branch and on the other branch.
And on the lampstand itself there were four cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and blossoms.
One bud was under the first pair of branches, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair. All six branches came out from the lampstand.
The buds and the branches were all one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, its wick cutters, and its trays out of pure gold.
He used about thirty-four kilograms of pure gold to make the lampstand and all its tools.
He made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, about forty-five centimetres long and forty-five centimetres wide, and about ninety centimetres high. Its horns were one piece with it.
He covered the top, all the sides, and the horns with pure gold, and put a gold border around it.
He made two gold rings below the border, on the two opposite sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure, sweet-smelling incense, the work of a perfume maker.
He built the altar of burnt offering out of acacia wood. It was square, about two and a quarter metres long and two and a quarter metres wide, and about one and a third metres high.
He made a horn at each of its four corners, so that the horns and the altar were one piece. He covered the altar with bronze.
He made all the altar's tools out of bronze: its pots, shovels, bowls, meat forks, and fire pans.
He made a grate for the altar, a bronze net, and put it under the ledge of the altar, so that it reached halfway up.
He cast four bronze rings for the four corners of the bronze grate, to hold the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with bronze.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it. He made the altar hollow, out of boards.
He made the bronze washing bowl and its bronze stand from the bronze mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Then he made the courtyard. The south side was forty-five metres long, with curtains of fine twisted linen.
It had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The north side was also forty-five metres long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The west end was twenty-two metres wide, with curtains, ten posts, and ten bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The east end, towards the sunrise, was also twenty-two metres wide.
On one side of the entrance there were curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.
On the other side of the entrance to the courtyard there were also curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.
All the curtains around the courtyard were made of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were covered with silver. All the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

The screen for the entrance to the courtyard was made of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns. It was nine metres long and over two metres high, the same as the curtains of the courtyard.
It had four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks and bands were silver, and their tops were covered with silver.
All the tent pegs of the holy tent and of the courtyard around it were bronze.
These are the amounts of the materials used for the holy tent, the Tent of the Covenant. They were recorded at Moses' command by the Levites, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. He was a carver and a designer, and he sewed beautiful patterns in blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen.
All the gold given as an offering and used for the work on the holy place weighed about one thousand kilograms, by the weight of the holy place.
The silver given by those in the community who were counted weighed about three thousand four hundred kilograms, by the weight of the holy place.

This was one beka, half a shekel, for each person, by the weight of the holy place. It was given by everyone who was counted, twenty years old or more, six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men.
About three thousand four hundred kilograms of silver was used to cast the bases for the holy place and for the curtain, one hundred bases, about thirty-four kilograms for each base.
He used the remaining twenty kilograms of silver to make the hooks for the posts, to cover the tops of the posts, and to make their bands.
The bronze given as an offering weighed about two thousand four hundred kilograms.
He used it to make the bases for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grate and all its tools,
the bases for the courtyard all around and for its entrance, and all the tent pegs for the holy tent and for the courtyard around it.
From the blue, purple, and red yarn they made woven clothes for serving in the Holy Place. They also made the holy clothes for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Bezalel made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
They hammered the gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads, to weave into the blue, purple, and red yarn and the fine linen, the work of a skilled worker.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, fastened to its two corners, so that it could be tied together.
Its skilfully woven belt was made the same way and was one piece with it, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They set the onyx stones in gold settings and carved on them the names of the sons of Israel, the way a jeweller carves a seal.
Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as stones to remind God of the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the chest piece, the work of a skilled worker, like the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It was square, folded double, about twenty-three centimetres long and twenty-three centimetres wide.
They put four rows of precious stones on it. In the first row was a ruby, a topaz, and a beryl.
In the second row was a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald.
In the third row was a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
In the fourth row was a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They were set in gold settings.
There were twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel. Each stone was carved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the chest piece they made chains of pure gold, twisted like a rope.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and fastened the rings to the two upper corners of the chest piece.
They fastened the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the chest piece.
They fastened the other ends of the chains to the two settings, and attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two gold rings and fastened them to the other two corners of the chest piece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and fastened them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above its woven belt.

They tied the rings of the chest piece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that the chest piece sat above the woven belt and did not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the robe of the ephod, woven all of blue cloth.
There was an opening in the middle of the robe like a collar, with a woven edge around the opening so that it would not tear.
Around the bottom hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple, and red yarn and twisted linen.
They made bells of pure gold and put them between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe.
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, went all around the hem of the robe to be worn for serving as priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
For Aaron and his sons they made shirts woven from fine linen,
and the turban of fine linen, the linen caps, and the underwear of fine twisted linen.
The sash was made of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and red yarn, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate, the holy crown, out of pure gold, and carved on it like a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
They tied a blue cord to it to fasten it on the turban, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the work on the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting, was finished. The people of Israel did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then they brought the holy tent to Moses: the tent and all its furniture, its hooks, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the curtain that hides the ark;
the ark of the covenant with its poles and its cover;
the table with all its tools and the special bread;
the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its tools, and the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil, the sweet-smelling incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grate, its poles and all its tools, and the washing bowl with its stand;
the curtains of the courtyard with their posts and bases, the screen for the entrance to the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the tools for the work of the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting;
and the woven clothes for serving in the Holy Place, both the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons when they serve as priests.
The people of Israel had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses looked over all the work and saw that they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"On the first day of the first month, set up the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting.
Put the ark of the covenant in it, and hang the curtain in front of the ark to hide it.
Bring in the table and set out what belongs on it. Then bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
Put the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the covenant, and hang the screen at the entrance of the holy tent.
Put the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting.
Put the washing bowl between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard around it, and hang the screen at the entrance to the courtyard.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the holy tent and everything in it. Set it and all its furniture apart as holy, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its tools. Set the altar apart as holy, and it will be most holy.
Anoint the washing bowl and its stand, and set them apart as holy.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Dress Aaron in the holy clothes, anoint him, and set him apart as holy, so that he can serve me as priest.
Bring his sons and dress them in shirts.
Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they can serve me as priests. Their anointing will make them priests for all generations to come, forever."
Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
So the holy tent was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year.
Moses set up the holy tent. He put its bases in place, set up its frames, put in its crossbars, and set up its posts.
Then he spread the tent over the holy tent and put the covering over the tent, as the LORD had commanded him.
He took the tablets of the covenant and put them inside the ark. He fixed the poles to the ark and put the cover on top of it.
Then he brought the ark into the holy tent and hung the curtain to hide the ark of the covenant, as the LORD had commanded him.
Moses put the table in the Tent of Meeting on the north side of the holy tent, outside the curtain.
He set out the bread on it in front of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him.
He put the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting across from the table, on the south side of the holy tent.
He set up the lamps in front of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him.
Moses put the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting in front of the curtain,
and burned sweet-smelling incense on it, as the LORD had commanded him.
Then he hung the screen at the entrance of the holy tent.
He put the altar of burnt offering near the entrance of the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it burnt offerings and grain offerings, as the LORD had commanded him.
He put the washing bowl between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons used it to wash their hands and feet.
Whenever they went into the Tent of Meeting or came near the altar, they washed, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses set up the courtyard around the holy tent and the altar, and hung the screen at the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the holy tent.
Moses could not go into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the holy tent.
In all their travels, whenever the cloud lifted from above the holy tent, the people of Israel would set out.
But if the cloud did not lift, they did not set out until the day it lifted.
So the cloud of the LORD was over the holy tent by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, where all the people of Israel could see it, in all their travels.
Lev: The LORD called Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting. He said,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When any of you brings a gift to the LORD, bring an animal from your cattle or from your sheep and goats.
If the gift is a burnt offering from the cattle, it must be a male with nothing wrong with it. Bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting, so that the LORD will accept it.
Put your hand on the head of the animal. Then it will be accepted for you, to make you right with God.
Kill the young bull in front of the LORD. Aaron's sons, the priests, will bring the blood and splash it all around the altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Then skin the animal and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest will light a fire on the altar and lay wood neatly on the fire.
Then they will lay the pieces, the head, and the fat neatly on the wood burning on the altar.
But wash the inside parts and the legs with water. The priest will burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a gift made by fire, with a smell that pleases the LORD.
If the burnt offering is from the flock, a sheep or a goat, it must be a male with nothing wrong with it.
Kill it on the north side of the altar in front of the LORD. Aaron's sons, the priests, will splash its blood all around the altar.
Cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat. The priest will lay them neatly on the wood burning on the altar.
But wash the inside parts and the legs with water. The priest will offer all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a gift made by fire, with a smell that pleases the LORD.
If the burnt offering to the LORD is a bird, bring a dove or a young pigeon.
The priest will bring it to the altar, twist off its head, and burn it on the altar. Its blood will be drained out on the side of the altar.
He will take away its throat pouch and its feathers, and throw them beside the altar on the east side, where the ashes are.

He will tear it open by its wings, but not pull it fully apart. Then the priest will burn it on the altar, on the wood on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a gift made by fire, with a smell that pleases the LORD.
When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, it must be fine flour. Pour oil on it and put incense on it.

Bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests. The priest will take a handful of the flour and oil, with all the incense, and burn it on the altar as the part that is remembered. It is a gift made by fire, with a smell that pleases the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the gifts made by fire to the LORD.
When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be flat bread made without yeast, from fine flour mixed with oil, or thin wafers without yeast, spread with oil.
If your grain offering is cooked on a flat pan, it must be fine flour without yeast, mixed with oil.
Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
If your grain offering is cooked in a pot, it must be made of fine flour with oil.
Bring the grain offering made from these things to the LORD. Give it to the priest, and he will take it to the altar.
The priest will take the part that is remembered from the grain offering and burn it on the altar. It is a gift made by fire, with a smell that pleases the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the gifts made by fire to the LORD.
No grain offering you bring to the LORD may be made with yeast. Do not burn any yeast or any honey as a gift made by fire to the LORD.
You may bring them to the LORD as a gift of the first part of your harvest, but they must not be burned on the altar as a pleasing smell.
Put salt on every grain offering. Do not leave out the salt of your God's covenant from your grain offering. Add salt to all your offerings.
If you bring the LORD a grain offering from the first part of your harvest, bring fresh heads of grain, roasted in the fire and crushed.
Put oil on it and lay incense on it. It is a grain offering.
The priest will burn some of the crushed grain and some of the oil, with all the incense, as the part that is remembered. It is a gift made by fire to the LORD.
If someone brings a peace offering from the cattle, male or female, it must have nothing wrong with it when he offers it to the LORD.
He will put his hand on the head of the animal and kill it at the door of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron's sons, the priests, will splash the blood all around the altar.
From the peace offering he will bring a gift made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the inside parts, and all the fat on the inside parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the fatty covering of the liver. He will remove these with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons will burn it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering on the wood on the fire. It is a gift made by fire, with a smell that pleases the LORD.
If his peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, male or female, it must have nothing wrong with it.
If he brings a lamb, he will offer it in front of the LORD.
He will put his hand on its head and kill it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron's sons will splash its blood all around the altar.

From the peace offering he will bring a gift made by fire to the LORD: its fat, the whole fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the inside parts, and all the fat on the inside parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the fatty covering of the liver. He will remove these with the kidneys.
The priest will burn it on the altar. It is food, a gift made by fire to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he will offer it in front of the LORD.
He will put his hand on its head and kill it in front of the Tent of Meeting. The sons of Aaron will splash its blood all around the altar.
From it he will bring his gift made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the inside parts, and all the fat on the inside parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the fatty covering of the liver. He will remove these with the kidneys.
The priest will burn them on the altar. It is food, a gift made by fire, with a pleasing smell. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a rule forever, for all your people after you, wherever you live: Do not eat any fat or any blood."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: Someone may sin without meaning to, by doing something the LORD has commanded must not be done.
If it is the chosen high priest who sins, and so brings guilt on the people, he must bring the LORD a young bull with nothing wrong with it, as a sin offering for the sin he has done.
He will bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Meeting in front of the LORD. He will put his hand on the bull's head and kill it in front of the LORD.
The chosen priest will take some of the bull's blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times in front of the LORD, in front of the curtain of the holy place.

He will put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense, which stands before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. He will pour out the rest of the bull's blood at the bottom of the altar for burnt offerings, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He will take all the fat from the bull of the sin offering: the fat that covers the inside parts, and all the fat on the inside parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the fatty covering of the liver. He will remove these with the kidneys,
just as they are removed from the bull of the peace offering. Then the priest will burn them on the altar for burnt offerings.
But the bull's skin, all its meat, its head, its legs, its inside parts, and its dung,
all the rest of the bull, he must carry outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are thrown. He will burn it there on a wood fire, at the place where the ashes are thrown.
If the whole community of Israel sins without meaning to, and they do not notice it, they have done something the LORD has commanded must not be done, and they are guilty.
When they find out about the sin they have done, the people must bring a young bull as a sin offering, and bring it in front of the Tent of Meeting.
The leaders of the community will put their hands on the bull's head in front of the LORD, and the bull will be killed in front of the LORD.
The chosen priest will bring some of the bull's blood into the Tent of Meeting.
He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in front of the LORD, in front of the curtain.

He will put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. He will pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar for burnt offerings, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He will take all its fat and burn it on the altar.
He will do with this bull just what he did with the bull of the priest's sin offering. The priest will make the people right with God, and they will be forgiven.
Then he will carry the bull outside the camp and burn it, as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the whole community.
When a leader sins without meaning to, by doing something the LORD his God has commanded must not be done, he is guilty.
When he is told about the sin he has done, he must bring a male goat with nothing wrong with it as his offering.
He will put his hand on the goat's head and kill it in front of the LORD, in the place where burnt offerings are killed. It is a sin offering.
The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger and put it on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He will pour out the rest of its blood at the bottom of that altar.
He will burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the peace offering. In this way the priest will make the leader right with God for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
If one of the ordinary people sins without meaning to, by doing something the LORD has commanded must not be done, he is guilty.
When he is told about the sin he has done, he must bring a female goat with nothing wrong with it as his offering for that sin.
He will put his hand on the head of the sin offering and kill it in the place of the burnt offering.
The priest will take some of its blood on his finger and put it on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He will pour out the rest of its blood at the bottom of the altar.

He will remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the peace offering. The priest will burn it on the altar as a smell that pleases the LORD. In this way the priest will make him right with God, and he will be forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, it must be a female with nothing wrong with it.
He will put his hand on the head of the sin offering and kill it as a sin offering in the place where burnt offerings are killed.

The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger and put it on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He will pour out all the rest of its blood at the bottom of the altar.

He will remove all its fat, just as the lamb's fat is removed from the peace offering. The priest will burn it on the altar, on top of the gifts made by fire to the LORD. In this way the priest will make him right with God for the sin he has done, and he will be forgiven.
If someone is called in public to tell what he knows as a witness, and he saw or knew something but does not speak up, he has sinned and must carry the blame.

Or someone may touch something unclean, like the dead body of an unclean wild animal, an unclean farm animal, or an unclean crawling creature. Even if he did not notice it, he has become unclean and is guilty.
Or he may touch something unclean from a person, anything at all that makes someone unclean. Even if he did not notice it, when he finds out, he is guilty.
Or someone may carelessly make a promise to do something, bad or good, the kind of careless promise people make, and not realise it. When he finds out, he is guilty in this matter.
When someone is guilty in any of these ways, he must admit the sin he has done.
Then he must bring the LORD his offering for the sin he has done: a female lamb or goat from the flock, as a sin offering. The priest will make him right with God for his sin.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he must bring the LORD two doves or two young pigeons for the sin he has done: one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
He will bring them to the priest, who will first offer the bird for the sin offering. He will twist its neck, but not pull the head right off.
He will sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood will be drained out at the bottom of the altar. It is a sin offering.
Then he will offer the second bird as a burnt offering, in the way that has been commanded. In this way the priest will make him right with God for the sin he has done, and he will be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford two doves or two young pigeons, he must bring about one and a half kilograms of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put oil or incense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He will bring it to the priest, and the priest will take a handful of it as the part that is remembered and burn it on the altar, on top of the gifts made by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
In this way the priest will make him right with God for any of these sins he has done, and he will be forgiven. The rest of the flour will belong to the priest, just like the grain offering."
The LORD said to Moses,

"If someone is unfaithful and sins without meaning to against the LORD's holy things, he must bring the LORD a guilt offering: a ram from the flock with nothing wrong with it. Its value is set in silver, by the official weight used at the holy place.

He must pay back what he has done wrong about the holy thing, and add one fifth more, and give it to the priest. The priest will make him right with God with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If someone sins by doing something the LORD has commanded must not be done, even if he did not know it, he is still guilty and must carry the blame.

He must bring the priest a ram from the flock with nothing wrong with it, of the set value, as a guilt offering. The priest will make him right with God for the wrong he did without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering. He was truly guilty before the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Someone may sin and be unfaithful to the LORD by cheating his neighbour. He may lie about something left in his care, or about a deal, or he may steal from his neighbour or treat him unfairly,
or he may find something that was lost and lie about it, swearing a false promise. These are some of the ways people sin.
If he has sinned in this way and is guilty, he must give back what he stole, or what he took unfairly, or what was left in his care, or the lost thing he found,
or anything he lied about with a promise. He must pay it back in full and add one fifth more. He must give it to the owner on the day he is found guilty.
Then he must bring the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram from the flock with nothing wrong with it, of the set value.
The priest will make him right with God in front of the LORD, and he will be forgiven for whatever he did that made him guilty."
The LORD said to Moses,

"Give Aaron and his sons this command. This is the teaching about the burnt offering: The burnt offering must stay on the fire on the altar all night until morning, and the altar fire must be kept burning.
The priest will put on his linen robe, with linen underwear on his body. He will take up the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has burned on the altar, and put them beside the altar.
Then he will take off these clothes, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar must be kept burning. It must not go out. Every morning the priest will put more wood on it. He will lay the burnt offering neatly on it and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
The fire must burn on the altar all the time. It must never go out.
This is the teaching about the grain offering: Aaron's sons will offer it to the LORD in front of the altar.
The priest will take a handful of the fine flour and oil of the grain offering, with all the incense on it, and burn it on the altar as the part that is remembered, a smell that pleases the LORD.
Aaron and his sons will eat the rest of it. It must be eaten without yeast in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of my gifts made by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Any male among Aaron's family may eat it. It is their share forever, for all their families to come, from the gifts made by fire to the LORD. Whatever touches these offerings will become holy."
The LORD said to Moses,

"This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must bring to the LORD on the day each high priest is anointed: about one and a half kilograms of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It must be made with oil on a flat pan. Bring it well mixed with oil, and offer the grain offering in broken pieces, as a smell that pleases the LORD.
The son who is anointed priest after Aaron will offer it. It is a rule forever: it must be burned completely for the LORD.
Every grain offering of a priest must be burned completely. It must not be eaten."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the teaching about the sin offering: The sin offering must be killed in front of the LORD, in the same place where the burnt offering is killed. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin will eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Whatever touches its meat will become holy. If any of its blood is splashed on a piece of clothing, you must wash it in a holy place.
The clay pot it is cooked in must be broken. If it is cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
But if any of the blood of a sin offering is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make people right with God in the Holy Place, that offering must not be eaten. It must be burned in the fire.
This is the teaching about the guilt offering. It is most holy.
The guilt offering must be killed in the place where the burnt offering is killed. Its blood will be splashed all around the altar.
All its fat will be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the inside parts,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the fatty covering of the liver, removed with the kidneys.
The priest will burn them on the altar as a gift made by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering. The same rule is for both. It belongs to the priest who makes people right with God with it.
The priest who offers someone's burnt offering may keep the skin of that animal for himself.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, or cooked in a pot or on a flat pan, belongs to the priest who offers it.
And every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all of Aaron's sons, shared equally.
This is the teaching about the peace offering that someone brings to the LORD:
If he brings it to say thank you, he must offer with it flat bread made without yeast and mixed with oil, thin wafers without yeast spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour well mixed with oil.
Along with his thank offering, he must also bring loaves of bread made with yeast.
He must give one of each kind as a special gift to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offering.
The meat of the thank offering must be eaten on the day it is offered. None of it may be left until morning.
But if his offering is to keep a promise, or is a gift he chose freely to give, it must be eaten on the day he offers it, and what is left may be eaten the next day.
But any meat still left on the third day must be burned in the fire.

If any of the meat of the peace offering is eaten on the third day, the offering will not be accepted, and it will not count for the person who brought it. It will be disgusting, and whoever eats it will carry the blame.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten. It must be burned in the fire. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
But if someone who is unclean eats meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.

If someone touches anything unclean, whether something unclean from a person, or an unclean animal, or any unclean disgusting thing, and then eats meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: Do not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal that died by itself, or was killed by wild animals, may be used for other things, but you must never eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal that may be offered as a gift made by fire to the LORD must be cut off from his people.
Wherever you live, do not eat any blood, whether from a bird or an animal.
Anyone who eats any blood must be cut off from his people."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: Whoever brings a peace offering to the LORD must bring part of it as a special gift to the LORD.
He must bring the gifts made by fire to the LORD with his own hands. He must bring the fat together with the breast, and the breast will be waved in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
The priest will burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
Give the right thigh of your peace offerings to the priest as a special gift.
The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the peace offering will have the right thigh as his share.

From the peace offerings of the people of Israel, I have taken the breast that is waved and the thigh that is lifted up, and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. This is their share from the people of Israel forever."
This is the share set apart for Aaron and his sons from the gifts made by fire to the LORD, from the day they were brought forward to serve the LORD as priests.
On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded the people of Israel to give them this. It is their share forever, for all their families to come.
This is the teaching about the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the offering for making priests, and the peace offering.
The LORD gave these commands to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the people of Israel to bring their offerings to the LORD in the Sinai desert.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Bring Aaron and his sons, the priests' clothes, the special oil for anointing, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread made without yeast.
Then gather the whole community at the door of the Tent of Meeting."
Moses did what the LORD commanded him, and the community gathered at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Moses said to them, "This is what the LORD has commanded us to do."
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the long shirt on Aaron and tied the belt around him. He dressed him in the robe and put the ephod on him. He tied the finely woven band of the ephod around him to hold it in place.
He put the chest piece on him, and placed the Urim and Thummim in the chest piece.
He put the turban on his head, and on the front of the turban he fixed the gold plate, the holy crown, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the Holy Tent and everything in it, to make them holy.
He sprinkled some oil on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and all its tools, and the washbasin and its stand, to make them holy.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him, to make him holy.
Then Moses brought Aaron's sons forward. He dressed them in long shirts, tied belts around them, and put caps on their heads, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He brought the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.

Moses killed it and took the blood. With his finger he put it on all the horns of the altar to make the altar pure. He poured out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. In this way he made it holy and made it right with God.
He took all the fat on the inside parts, the fatty covering of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and Moses burned it on the altar.
But the rest of the bull, its skin, its meat, and its dung, he burned in a fire outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he brought the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.
Moses killed it and splashed the blood all around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the inside parts and the legs with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering with a pleasing smell, a gift made by fire to the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he brought the other ram, the ram for making them priests. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.
Moses killed it and took some of its blood. He put it on the bottom of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

Then he brought Aaron's sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on the bottom of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses splashed the blood all around the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat on the inside parts, the fatty covering of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of bread without yeast that was before the LORD, he took one flat loaf, one loaf made with oil, and one thin wafer. He put them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and waved them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. It was the offering for making them priests, with a pleasing smell, a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Moses took the breast and waved it in front of the LORD as a wave offering. It was Moses' share of the ram for making priests, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. In this way he made Aaron and his clothes holy, and his sons and their clothes too.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and eat it there with the bread in the basket for making priests, as I commanded when I said, 'Aaron and his sons will eat it.'
Burn whatever is left of the meat and the bread.
Do not leave the door of the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days for making you priests are over. It will take seven days to set you apart.
What was done today is what the LORD commanded, to make you right with God.
Stay at the door of the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days, and do what the LORD requires, so that you do not die. This is what I have been commanded."
So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the leaders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, "Take a young bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both with nothing wrong with them, and offer them to the LORD.
Then tell the people of Israel, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both one year old and with nothing wrong with them, for a burnt offering.
Also take a bull and a ram for peace offerings to offer to the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the LORD will show himself to you.'"
They brought what Moses commanded to the front of the Tent of Meeting. The whole community came near and stood in front of the LORD.
Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD will appear to you."

Moses said to Aaron, "Come to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, to make yourself and the people right with God. Then offer the people's offering to make them right with God, as the LORD has commanded."
So Aaron came to the altar and killed the calf as a sin offering for himself.
His sons brought him the blood. He dipped his finger in it and put it on the horns of the altar, and he poured out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.
He burned on the altar the fat, the kidneys, and the fatty covering of the liver from the sin offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He burned the meat and the skin in a fire outside the camp.
Then he killed the burnt offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it all around the altar.
They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, with the head, and he burned them on the altar.
He washed the inside parts and the legs, and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
Then he brought the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering, killed it, and offered it for sin, just as he did with the first one.
He brought the burnt offering and offered it in the way that had been commanded.
He brought the grain offering, took a handful of it, and burned it on the altar, along with the morning burnt offering.
He also killed the bull and the ram as peace offerings for the people. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it all around the altar.
They also handed him the fat from the bull and the ram: the fat tail, the fat covering the inside parts, the kidneys, and the fatty covering of the liver.
They put the fat on top of the breasts, and he burned the fat on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh in front of the LORD as a wave offering, as Moses had commanded.
Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. After offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, he came down.
Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from the LORD and burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and bowed down with their faces to the ground.
Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, each took his incense pan, put fire in it, and laid incense on it. They offered the LORD a fire that was not allowed, something he had not commanded them to do.
So fire came out from the LORD and burned them up, and they died in front of the LORD.

Then Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD meant when he said, 'I will show that I am holy to those who come near me, and I will be honoured in front of all the people.'" And Aaron said nothing.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. He said to them, "Come here and carry your cousins away from the front of the holy place, out of the camp."
So they came and carried them out of the camp, still in their shirts, as Moses had said.

Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose or tear your clothes to mourn, or you will die, and the LORD will be angry with the whole community. But your relatives, all the people of Israel, may weep over those the LORD has burned with fire.
Do not leave the door of the Tent of Meeting, or you will die, because the LORD's anointing oil is on you." So they did what Moses said.
Then the LORD said to Aaron,
"You and your sons must not drink wine or strong drink when you go into the Tent of Meeting, or you will die. This is a rule forever, for all your families to come.
You must know the difference between what is holy and what is ordinary, and between what is unclean and what is clean.
And you must teach the people of Israel all the rules the LORD has given them through Moses."

Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons who were still alive, "Take the grain offering that is left from the gifts made by fire to the LORD, and eat it without yeast beside the altar, because it is most holy.
Eat it in a holy place, because it is your share and your sons' share of the gifts made by fire to the LORD. This is what I have been commanded.

But you, your sons, and your daughters may eat the breast that was waved and the thigh that was lifted up, in any clean place. They are given to you and your children as your share from the peace offerings of the people of Israel.

The thigh that is lifted up and the breast that is waved must be brought with the fat for the gifts made by fire, and waved in front of the LORD as a wave offering. They will belong to you and your children as your share forever, as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses searched carefully for the goat of the sin offering, and found that it had been burned up. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons who were left, and said,
"Why didn't you eat the sin offering in the holy area? It is most holy, and God gave it to you to take away the guilt of the community, to make them right with God in front of the LORD.
Its blood was not brought inside the holy place, so you should have eaten the meat in the holy area, as I commanded."

Aaron answered Moses, "Look, today they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering to the LORD, and yet these terrible things have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would the LORD have been pleased?"
When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Tell the people of Israel: Of all the animals that live on land, these are the ones you may eat.
You may eat any animal that has a hoof split in two and also chews the cud.
But some animals only chew the cud or only have split hoofs, and you must not eat them. The camel chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The rock badger chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The rabbit chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The pig has a split hoof, divided in two, but does not chew the cud, so it is unclean for you.
Do not eat their meat or touch their dead bodies. They are unclean for you.
Of all the creatures that live in water, in the seas and the rivers, you may eat any that have fins and scales.
But anything in the seas or rivers that does not have fins and scales, whether small water creatures or any other living thing in the water, is disgusting to you.
You must think of them as disgusting. Do not eat their meat, and think of their dead bodies as disgusting.
Anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is disgusting to you.
These are the birds you must think of as disgusting. Do not eat them, because they are disgusting: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, and any kind of black kite,
any kind of raven,
the horned owl, the screech owl, the seagull, and any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All flying insects that walk on four legs are disgusting to you.
But you may eat some winged insects that walk on four legs: those with jointed legs above their feet for jumping on the ground.
Of these you may eat any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
All other winged insects with four legs are disgusting to you.
These will make you unclean: anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who picks up any part of their dead bodies must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
Every animal with a hoof that is not fully split in two, or that does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Anyone who touches them will be unclean.
Of all the animals that walk on four legs, those that walk on paws are unclean for you. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries their dead bodies must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
Of the small animals that move along the ground, these are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, any kind of large lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
Of all the creatures that move along the ground, these are unclean for you. Anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

If one of them dies and falls on something, that thing becomes unclean. Whether it is made of wood, cloth, leather, or sackcloth, whatever it is used for, it must be put in water. It will be unclean until evening, and then it will be clean.
If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in the pot becomes unclean, and you must break the pot.
Any food that could be eaten, if water from such a pot gets on it, becomes unclean. Any drink in such a pot becomes unclean.
Anything that part of their dead body falls on becomes unclean. If it is an oven or a cooking stove, it must be broken to pieces. They are unclean, and you must treat them as unclean.
But a spring or a well that holds water stays clean. Yet anyone who touches the dead body in it becomes unclean.
If part of a dead body falls on seed that is to be planted, the seed stays clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and part of a dead body falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies by itself, anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who eats some of its dead body must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries its dead body must also wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
Every small creature that moves along the ground is disgusting. Do not eat it.
Do not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it crawls on its belly, walks on four legs, or has many legs. They are disgusting.
Do not make yourselves disgusting or unclean by any of these crawling creatures. Do not let them make you unclean.
For I am the LORD your God. Make yourselves holy and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean with any creature that moves along the ground.
I am the LORD who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. So be holy, because I am holy.
This is the teaching about animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every creature that moves along the ground.
It helps you to know the difference between what is unclean and what is clean, and between the animals that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: When a woman becomes pregnant and gives birth to a boy, she will be unclean for seven days, just as she is unclean during her monthly period.
On the eighth day the boy must be circumcised.
Then she must wait thirty-three days to be made clean from her bleeding. She must not touch anything holy or go into the holy place until her days of cleansing are over.
If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for two weeks, as during her period. Then she must wait sixty-six days to be made clean from her bleeding.

When her days of cleansing are over, for a son or a daughter, she must bring the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering.
The priest will offer them to the LORD and make her right with God, and she will be clean from her bleeding. This is the teaching for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.
If she cannot afford a lamb, she may bring two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest will make her right with God, and she will be clean."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Someone may have a swelling, a scab, or a shiny spot on his skin that could become a serious skin disease. He must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

The priest will look at the sore on the skin. If the hair in the sore has turned white, and the sore looks deeper than the skin, it is a serious skin disease. After looking at him, the priest will say that he is unclean.
But if the shiny spot on the skin is white, and does not look deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest will keep the person apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest will look at him again. If he sees that the sore has not changed and has not spread on the skin, the priest will keep him apart for seven more days.

On the seventh day the priest will look at him again. If the sore has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest will say he is clean. It is only a scab. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
But if the scab spreads on the skin after he has shown himself to the priest to be declared clean, he must show himself to the priest again.
The priest will look at him, and if the scab has spread on the skin, the priest will say he is unclean. It is a serious skin disease.
When someone has a serious skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
The priest will look at him. If there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a long-lasting skin disease, and the priest will say he is unclean. He does not need to keep him apart, because he is already unclean.
If the disease breaks out all over the skin, and covers the person's whole skin from head to foot, wherever the priest looks,
the priest will look at him. If the disease has covered his whole body, the priest will say he is clean of the sore. It has all turned white, so he is clean.
But whenever raw flesh shows on him, he will be unclean.
The priest will look at the raw flesh and say he is unclean. Raw flesh is unclean. It is a serious skin disease.
But if the raw flesh changes and turns white again, he must go to the priest.
The priest will look at him, and if the sore has turned white, the priest will say he is clean of the sore. He is clean.
When someone has a boil on his skin, and it has healed,
and in the place of the boil there is a white swelling, or a shiny reddish-white spot, he must show it to the priest.

The priest will look at it. If it looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest will say he is unclean. It is a serious skin disease that has broken out where the boil was.
But if the priest looks at it and there are no white hairs in it, and it is not deeper than the skin but has faded, the priest will keep him apart for seven days.
If it spreads on the skin, the priest will say he is unclean. It is a disease.
But if the shiny spot stays where it is and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest will say he is clean.
Or someone may have a burn on his skin from fire, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a shiny spot, reddish-white or white.

The priest will look at it. If the hair in the shiny spot has turned white, and it looks deeper than the skin, it is a serious skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest will say he is unclean. It is a serious skin disease.
But if the priest looks at it and there is no white hair in the shiny spot, and it is not deeper than the skin but has faded, the priest will keep him apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest will look at him. If it has spread on the skin, the priest will say he is unclean. It is a serious skin disease.
But if the shiny spot stays where it is and has not spread on the skin but has faded, it is only swelling from the burn. The priest will say he is clean, because it is only the scar from the burn.
When a man or woman has a sore on the head or in the beard,

the priest will look at the sore. If it looks deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest will say the person is unclean. It is an itching sore, a serious skin disease of the head or beard.
But if the priest looks at the itching sore and it does not look deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest will keep the person apart for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest will look at the sore. If the itch has not spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not look deeper than the skin,
the person must shave, but not shave the sore itself. Then the priest will keep the person apart for seven more days.

On the seventh day the priest will look at the itch. If it has not spread on the skin, and it does not look deeper than the skin, the priest will say the person is clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
But if the itch spreads on the skin after he has been declared clean,
the priest will look at him again. If the itch has spread on the skin, the priest does not need to look for yellow hair. The person is unclean.
But if the priest sees that the itch has not changed and black hair has grown in it, the itch is healed. The person is clean, and the priest will say he is clean.
When a man or woman has shiny white spots on the skin,
the priest will look at them. If the spots are a dull white, it is only a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin. The person is clean.
If a man loses the hair on his head, he is bald, but he is clean.
If he loses the hair on the front of his head, he has a bald forehead, but he is clean.
But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead, it is a serious skin disease breaking out there.
The priest will look at him. If the swollen sore on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white, like a serious skin disease on the body,
the man has a serious skin disease and is unclean. The priest must say he is unclean, because of the sore on his head.
A person with a serious skin disease must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose. He must cover the lower part of his face and call out, 'Unclean! Unclean!'
As long as he has the disease, he is unclean. He must live alone, in a place outside the camp.
Clothing may also have mould on it, whether it is wool or linen clothing,
or woven or knitted material of linen or wool, or leather, or anything made of leather.
If the mark on the clothing, the leather, the woven or knitted material, or the leather item is greenish or reddish, it is spreading mould, and it must be shown to the priest.
The priest will look at the mould and put the item away for seven days.
On the seventh day he will look at it. If the mould has spread on the clothing, the woven or knitted material, or the leather, whatever it is used for, it is a harmful mould. The item is unclean.
He must burn the clothing, the woven or knitted wool or linen, or the leather item with the mould on it, because it is a harmful mould. It must be burned in the fire.
But if the priest looks at it and the mould has not spread on the clothing, the woven or knitted material, or the leather item,
the priest will order that the item with the mould be washed, and he will put it away for seven more days.

After it has been washed, the priest will look at it again. If the mould has not changed colour, even if it has not spread, the item is unclean. Burn it in the fire, whether the damage is on the inside or the outside.
If the priest looks and the mould has faded after washing, he must tear the spot out of the clothing, the leather, or the woven or knitted material.
But if it appears again on the clothing, the woven or knitted material, or the leather item, it is spreading. Burn whatever has the mould in the fire.
If you wash the clothing, the woven or knitted material, or the leather item and the mould goes away, wash it a second time, and it will be clean."
This is the teaching about mould on clothing of wool or linen, on woven or knitted material, or on anything made of leather, to know whether it is clean or unclean.
The LORD said to Moses,
"This is the teaching for a person with a serious skin disease on the day he is made clean. He must be brought to the priest,
and the priest will go outside the camp to look at him. If the person has been healed of the disease,
the priest will order that two live clean birds be brought for him, with cedar wood, red yarn, and a hyssop branch.
The priest will order that one bird be killed over fresh running water in a clay pot.
Then he will take the live bird, the cedar wood, the red yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them with the live bird in the blood of the bird killed over the running water.
He will sprinkle the blood seven times on the person being made clean of the skin disease, and say he is clean. Then he will let the live bird fly away into the open fields.

The person being made clean must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water. Then he will be clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he must stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and all the rest. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and then he will be clean.

On the eighth day he must bring two male lambs and one one-year-old female lamb, all with nothing wrong with them, about four and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and about a third of a litre of oil.
The priest who makes him clean will place the man and these offerings in front of the LORD at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, with the oil. He will wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
He will kill the lamb in the holy area, where the sin offering and the burnt offering are killed. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest. It is most holy.

The priest will take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
Then the priest will pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
He will dip a finger of his right hand into the oil in his left hand, and sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times in front of the LORD.

The priest will put some of the oil left in his hand on the bottom of the person's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
He will put the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person being made clean. In this way the priest will make him right with God in front of the LORD.
Then the priest will offer the sin offering to make the person right with God for his uncleanness. After that he will kill the burnt offering.
The priest will offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. In this way the priest will make him right with God, and he will be clean.

But if the person is poor and cannot afford all this, he may bring one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make him right with God, with about one and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and about a third of a litre of oil.
He must also bring two doves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he must bring them to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting, in front of the LORD, to be made clean.
The priest will take the lamb for the guilt offering and the oil, and wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.

He will kill the lamb for the guilt offering. Then he will take some of its blood and put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest will pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
With a finger of his right hand, he will sprinkle some of the oil from his left hand seven times in front of the LORD.

He will put some of the oil in his hand on the bottom of the person's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, in the same places as the blood of the guilt offering.
He will put the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person being made clean, to make him right with God in front of the LORD.
Then he will offer the doves or the young pigeons, whichever the person can afford,
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make the person right with God in front of the LORD."
This is the teaching for someone with a serious skin disease who cannot afford the usual offerings for being made clean.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving you to own, I may put spreading mould in a house in that land.
Then the owner of the house must go and tell the priest, 'I think I see something like mould in my house.'
Before the priest goes in to look at the mould, he must order that the house be emptied, so that nothing in it will become unclean. Then the priest will go in to look at the house.
He will look at the mould. If it is on the walls in sunken greenish or reddish patches that seem deeper than the surface of the wall,
the priest will go out to the door of the house and close it up for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest will come back and look. If the mould has spread on the walls,
the priest will order that the stones with the mould be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town.
He will have the inside walls of the house scraped all over, and the plaster that is scraped off must be dumped in an unclean place outside the town.
Then they must take other stones to replace the old ones, and use new plaster to cover the house.
If the mould comes back and breaks out in the house after the stones have been pulled out and the house scraped and plastered,
the priest will come and look. If the mould has spread in the house, it is a harmful mould, and the house is unclean.
It must be torn down, its stones, its wood, and all its plaster, and carried out of the town to an unclean place.
Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps or eats in the house must wash his clothes.
But if the priest comes and looks, and the mould has not spread after the house was plastered, he will say the house is clean, because the mould is gone.
To make the house clean, he must take two birds, cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop.
He will kill one bird over fresh running water in a clay pot.
Then he will take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the red yarn, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the dead bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He will make the house clean with the bird's blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the red yarn.
Then he will let the live bird fly away out of the town into the open fields. In this way he will make the house right, and it will be clean."
This is the teaching for every kind of serious skin disease and itching sore,
for mould on clothing or in a house,
and for a swelling, a scab, or a shiny spot.
It teaches when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the teaching about serious skin diseases and mould.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Tell the people of Israel: When a man has a flow of fluid from his body, that flow makes him unclean.
He is unclean whether the fluid keeps flowing or whether it stops. That is what makes him unclean.
Any bed he lies on is unclean, and anything he sits on is unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits on something the unclean man sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the man's body must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
If the man with the flow spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any saddle the man rides on is unclean.
Anyone who touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries those things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone the man touches without rinsing his hands in water must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
A clay pot the man touches must be broken, and any wooden bowl must be rinsed with water.
When the man is healed of his flow, he must count seven days for his cleansing. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh running water, and then he will be clean.
On the eighth day he must take two doves or two young pigeons, come to the door of the Tent of Meeting in front of the LORD, and give them to the priest.
The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make him right with God in front of the LORD for his flow.
When a man has a release of seed, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any clothing or leather that has seed on it must be washed with water, and it will be unclean until evening.
When a man and a woman have sexual relations and there is a release of seed, they must both bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
When a woman has her monthly flow of blood, she will be unclean for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
Anything she lies on during her monthly flow is unclean, and anything she sits on is unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything she sits on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whether it is her bed or something she sits on, anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.
If a man sleeps with her and her monthly flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on will be unclean.
If a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside her monthly time, or if the flow continues past her monthly time, she is unclean all the days of that flow, just as during her monthly period.
Any bed she lies on during her flow is unclean, like her bed during her monthly period. Anything she sits on is unclean, like during her monthly period.
Anyone who touches these things is unclean. He must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
When she is healed of her flow, she must count seven days, and after that she will be clean.
On the eighth day she must take two doves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make her right with God in front of the LORD for the uncleanness of her flow.
You must keep the people of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so they will not die by making my Holy Tent unclean, the Tent that is among them."
This is the teaching about a man with a flow, and about a man who becomes unclean from a release of seed,
and about a woman during her monthly period, and about a man or woman with a flow, and about a man who sleeps with a woman who is unclean.
The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who died when they came near the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron not to come whenever he likes into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, in front of the cover on the Covenant Box, or he will die. For I appear in the cloud above the cover.
This is how Aaron must come into the holy place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He must put on the holy linen shirt, with linen underwear on his body. He must tie the linen belt around him and put on the linen turban. These are holy clothes. He must bathe his body in water and then put them on.
