From the community of Israel he must take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron will offer the bull as a sin offering for himself, to make himself and his family right with God.
Then he will take the two goats and present them to the LORD at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He will cast lots for the two goats: one lot for the LORD and the other for the goat that is sent away.
Aaron will bring forward the goat chosen by lot for the LORD and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat chosen by lot to be sent away will be presented alive before the LORD. It will be used to make people right with God by sending it into the desert as the goat that carries away sin.
Aaron will bring the bull for his own sin offering, to make himself and his family right with God, and he will kill the bull for his sin offering.
He will take a pan full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground sweet incense, and bring them behind the curtain.
He will put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the cover that is above the Covenant Box. Then he will not die.

He will take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the cover, on the east side. He will also sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times in front of the cover.

Then he will kill the goat for the people's sin offering and bring its blood behind the curtain. He will do with the goat's blood as he did with the bull's blood: sprinkle it on the cover and in front of the cover.

In this way he will make the Most Holy Place right with God, because of the uncleanness of the people of Israel and because of their wrongs, all their sins. He will do the same for the Tent of Meeting, which stands among them in the middle of their uncleanness.

No one else may be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make the Most Holy Place right with God until he comes out. He must make himself, his family, and the whole community of Israel right with God.
Then he will go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make it right with God. He will take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
He will sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, to clean it and make it holy from the uncleanness of the people of Israel.
When he has finished making the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar right with God, he will bring forward the live goat.

Aaron will put both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wrongs of the people of Israel, all their sins and ways of going wrong. He will put them on the goat's head, and then send the goat away into the desert with a man who is ready to take it.
The goat will carry all their wrongs on itself to a lonely place, and the man will let the goat go in the desert.
Then Aaron will go into the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen clothes he wore when he went into the Most Holy Place, and leave them there.

He will bathe his body in water in a holy place, put on his regular clothes, and come out. Then he will offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering, to make himself and the people right with God.
He will burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The man who takes the goat away into the desert must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come back into the camp.

The bull and the goat for the sin offerings, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make people right with God, must be taken outside the camp. Their skins, their meat, and their dung must be burned in the fire.
The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come back into the camp.
This is a rule for you forever: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must go without food and do no work at all, whether you were born in the land or are a foreigner living among you.
For on this day you will be made right with God and cleaned. You will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
It is a day of complete rest for you, and you must go without food. This is a rule forever.
The priest who is anointed and set apart to take his father's place will make people right with God. He will put on the linen clothes, the holy clothes.
He will make the Most Holy Place right with God, and the Tent of Meeting and the altar. He will make the priests and all the people of the community right with God.
This is a rule forever for you: once a year make the people of Israel right with God for all their sins." And it was done as the LORD commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel. Tell them this is what the LORD has commanded:
Any Israelite who kills a bull, a lamb, or a goat, inside the camp or outside it,

and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting to offer it as a gift to the LORD in front of his Holy Tent, is guilty of shedding blood. He has shed blood, and he must be cut off from his people.

This is so that the people of Israel will bring to the LORD the animals they have been killing as offerings out in the open fields. They must bring them to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting and offer them to the LORD as peace offerings.
The priest will splash the blood on the LORD's altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and burn the fat as a smell that pleases the LORD.
They must no longer offer their animals to the goat idols, which they have chased after like an unfaithful wife. This is a rule forever for them and for all their families to come.
Tell them also: Any Israelite, or any foreigner living among them, who offers a burnt offering or any other offering
and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to the LORD, must be cut off from his people.
If any Israelite, or any foreigner living among them, eats any blood at all, I will turn against that person and cut him off from his people.
For the life of a living body is in the blood. I have given you the blood on the altar to make you right with me. It is the blood, because it is life, that makes people right with God.
That is why I have told the people of Israel, 'None of you may eat blood, and no foreigner living among you may eat blood.'
If any Israelite, or any foreigner living among them, hunts and catches an animal or bird that may be eaten, he must pour out its blood and cover it with dust.

For the life of every creature is its blood. That is why I have told the people of Israel, 'Do not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Anyone who eats it must be cut off.'

Anyone, whether born in the land or a foreigner, who eats an animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will be unclean until evening, and then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe his body, he will carry the blame."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: I am the LORD your God.
Do not live the way people do in Egypt, where you used to live. Do not live the way people do in Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their customs.
Obey my laws and carefully follow my rules. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my rules and my laws. The person who obeys them will find life through them. I am the LORD.
None of you may come near a close relative to have sexual relations. I am the LORD.
Do not dishonour your father by having sexual relations with your mother. She is your mother. Do not have sexual relations with her.
Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife. That would dishonour your father.
Do not have sexual relations with your sister, whether she is your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, and whether she was born in your home or somewhere else.
Do not have sexual relations with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter. That would dishonour you.
Do not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister.
Do not have sexual relations with your father's sister. She is your father's close relative.
Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister. She is your mother's close relative.
Do not dishonour your father's brother by going near his wife for sexual relations. She is your aunt.
Do not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife. Do not have sexual relations with her.
Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife. That would dishonour your brother.
Do not have sexual relations with both a woman and her daughter. Do not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter for sexual relations. They are her close relatives. That is evil.
Do not marry your wife's sister while your wife is still alive, to be her rival and to have sexual relations with her.
Do not go near a woman for sexual relations during her monthly period, while she is unclean.
Do not have sexual relations with your neighbour's wife and make yourself unclean with her.
Do not give any of your children to be sacrificed to the god Molech. Do not dishonour the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Do not have sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman. That is disgusting.
Do not have sexual relations with any animal and make yourself unclean with it. A woman must not give herself to an animal to have sexual relations with it. That is a terrible perversion.
Do not make yourselves unclean in any of these ways. That is how the nations I am driving out ahead of you made themselves unclean.
Even the land became unclean, so I punished it for its sin, and the land threw out the people living in it, like someone vomiting.
But you must keep my rules and laws. You must not do any of these disgusting things, whether you were born in the land or are a foreigner living among you.
The people who lived in the land before you did all these disgusting things, and the land became unclean.
If you make the land unclean, it will throw you out too, just as it threw out the nation that was there before you.
Anyone who does any of these disgusting things must be cut off from his people.
So keep my commands, and do not follow any of the disgusting customs that were practised before you came. Do not make yourselves unclean with them. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the whole community of Israel and tell them: Be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
Each of you must respect your mother and your father, and keep my Sabbath days. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols, and do not make metal statues of gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
When you offer a peace offering to the LORD, offer it in the right way, so that it will be accepted for you.
It must be eaten on the day you offer it or on the next day. Anything left over until the third day must be burned in the fire.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is disgusting and will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will carry the blame, because he has treated what is holy to the LORD as ordinary. That person must be cut off from his people.
When you gather the harvest of your land, do not harvest all the way to the edges of your field, and do not go back to pick up the grain that was dropped.
Do not strip your vineyard bare, and do not pick up the grapes that have fallen. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not cheat one another.
Do not make a false promise using my name, and so dishonour the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Do not treat your neighbour unfairly or rob him. Do not keep back a hired worker's pay overnight until morning.
Do not curse a deaf person, and do not put something in front of a blind person to make him trip. Instead, fear your God. I am the LORD.
Do not be unfair when you judge. Do not favour the poor or show special respect to the powerful. Judge your neighbour fairly.
Do not go around spreading lies about your people. Do not put your neighbour's life in danger. I am the LORD.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. Correct your neighbour openly when he is wrong, so that you do not share in his sin.
Do not take revenge or hold a grudge against anyone among your people. Instead, love your neighbour as you love yourself. I am the LORD.
Keep my rules. Do not breed two different kinds of animals together. Do not plant your field with two kinds of seed. Do not wear clothes made of two kinds of material.

If a man has sexual relations with a slave woman who is promised to marry another man, but who has not been bought back or set free, they must be punished. But they are not to be put to death, because she was not free.
The man must bring a ram to the LORD at the door of the Tent of Meeting as a guilt offering.
With the ram of the guilt offering, the priest will make him right with God in front of the LORD for the sin he has done, and his sin will be forgiven.
When you come into the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, treat its fruit as forbidden. For three years it is forbidden to you and must not be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, a gift of praise to the LORD.
In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that the tree will give you more and more. I am the LORD your God.
Do not eat any meat with the blood still in it. Do not use magic or try to tell the future.
Do not cut the hair on the sides of your head or trim the edges of your beard.
Do not cut your bodies to mourn for the dead, and do not put tattoos on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not dishonour your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with evil.
Keep my Sabbath days and respect my holy place. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to people who talk with the dead or to fortune-tellers. Do not go to them, or they will make you unclean. I am the LORD your God.
Stand up in the presence of old people, and show respect to the elderly. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not treat him badly.
Treat the foreigner living with you like someone born among you. Love him as you love yourself, because you were foreigners in Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not cheat when you measure length, weight, or amount.
Use honest scales, honest weights, and honest measures for dry and liquid things. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
Keep all my rules and all my laws, and obey them. I am the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses,

"Tell the people of Israel: Any Israelite, or any foreigner living in Israel, who gives any of his children to the god Molech must be put to death. The people of the land must kill him by throwing stones at him.
I myself will turn against that person and cut him off from his people, because by giving his children to Molech he has made my holy place unclean and dishonoured my holy name.
If the people of the land look the other way when that person gives his children to Molech, and they do not put him to death,
then I myself will turn against that man and his family. I will cut him off from his people, together with everyone who follows him in being unfaithful to me by worshipping Molech.
If anyone turns to people who talk with the dead or to fortune-tellers, and is unfaithful to me by following them, I will turn against that person and cut him off from his people.
So make yourselves holy and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
Keep my rules and obey them. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death. He has cursed his father or mother, so his death is his own fault.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, with his neighbour's wife, both the man and the woman must be put to death.
If a man has sexual relations with his father's wife, he has dishonoured his father. Both of them must be put to death. Their death is their own fault.
If a man has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have done a terrible perversion. Their death is their own fault.
If a man has sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman, both of them have done something disgusting. They must be put to death. Their death is their own fault.
If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is evil. He and both women must be burned in the fire, so that there will be no such evil among you.
If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal too.
If a woman goes to an animal to have sexual relations with it, you must kill both the woman and the animal. They must be put to death. Their death is their own fault.

If a man marries his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they have sexual relations, it is shameful. They must be cut off in front of their people. He has dishonoured his sister and must carry the blame.
If a man has sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period, he has exposed the source of her flow, and she has uncovered it too. Both of them must be cut off from their people.
Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister or your father's sister. That would dishonour a close relative. Both people must carry the blame.
If a man has sexual relations with his uncle's wife, he has dishonoured his uncle. They will carry the blame for their sin and will die without children.
If a man marries his brother's wife, it is an unclean thing. He has dishonoured his brother. They will have no children.
So keep all my rules and all my laws, and obey them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not throw you out.
Do not follow the customs of the nation I am driving out ahead of you. They did all these things, and that is why I hated them.
But I have told you, 'You will own their land. I will give it to you as your own, a land flowing with milk and honey.' I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the other nations.

So you must know the difference between clean and unclean animals, and between clean and unclean birds. Do not make yourselves disgusting by eating any animal, bird, or crawling creature that I have set apart as unclean for you.
Be holy for me, because I, the LORD, am holy. I have set you apart from the other nations to belong to me.
A man or a woman who talks with the dead or tells fortunes must be put to death. They must be killed by stoning. Their death is their own fault."
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and tell them: A priest must not make himself unclean by touching a dead body among his people,
except for a close relative: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
or an unmarried sister who depends on him because she has no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.
He must not make himself unclean for people related to him by marriage, and so make himself unfit for holy work.
Priests must not shave their heads, or shave the edges of their beards, or cut their bodies.
They must be holy to their God and not dishonour his name. They offer the gifts made by fire to the LORD, the food of their God, so they must be holy.
A priest must not marry a woman who has been a prostitute or who is not pure, or a woman divorced from her husband, because the priest is holy to his God.
Treat him as holy, because he offers the food of your God. He must be holy to you, because I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy.
If a priest's daughter dishonours herself by becoming a prostitute, she dishonours her father. She must be burned in the fire.

The high priest, the one among his brothers who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been set apart to wear the priestly clothes, must not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes to mourn.
He must not go near any dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
He must not leave the holy place to mourn, or he will dishonour the holy place of his God, because the anointing oil of his God is on him like a crown. I am the LORD.
The woman he marries must be a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who is not pure, or a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not dishonour his children among his people. I am the LORD, who makes him holy."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron: For all time to come, none of your descendants who has something wrong with his body may come near to offer the food of his God.
No man who has something wrong with his body may come near: no one who is blind or lame, or who has a damaged face or a deformed body,
no one with a crippled foot or hand,
no one who has a hunched back or is very small, no one with an eye problem, an itching skin disease, or sores, and no one whose private parts are damaged.

No descendant of Aaron the priest who has something wrong with his body may come near to offer the gifts made by fire to the LORD. Since he has something wrong with him, he must not come near to offer the food of his God.
He may still eat the food of his God, both the most holy food and the holy food.
But he must not go near the curtain or come near the altar, because he has something wrong with his body. He must not dishonour my holy places, for I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
So Moses told this to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the holy gifts that the people of Israel set apart for me, so that they do not dishonour my holy name. I am the LORD.

Tell them: For all time to come, if any of your descendants is unclean and comes near the holy gifts that the people of Israel set apart for the LORD, that person must be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.

None of Aaron's descendants who has a serious skin disease or a flow from his body may eat the holy gifts until he is clean. Anyone who touches something made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has a release of seed,
or anyone who touches a crawling creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean in any way,
will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy gifts unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down, he will be clean. After that he may eat the holy gifts, because they are his food.
He must not eat an animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals, because it would make him unclean. I am the LORD.
The priests must keep my commands, or they will become guilty and die for dishonouring them. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
No one outside a priest's family may eat the holy gifts. A guest staying with a priest, or a hired worker, must not eat them.
But if a priest buys a slave with his money, the slave may eat them, and so may slaves born in his house. They may eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries someone who is not a priest, she may no longer eat the special gifts from the holy offerings.

But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, and has no children, and comes back to live in her father's house as when she was young, she may eat her father's food. But no one outside the family may eat any of it.
If someone eats a holy gift by mistake, he must give the priest the same amount of holy food, plus one fifth more.
The priests must not dishonour the holy gifts that the people of Israel offer to the LORD
by letting the people eat them, which would bring guilt on them. For I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
The LORD said to Moses,

"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel, and tell them: Any Israelite, or any foreigner in Israel, may bring a burnt offering to the LORD, either to keep a promise or as a gift freely given.
To be accepted for you, it must be a male bull, sheep, or goat with nothing wrong with it.
Do not offer anything that has something wrong with it, because it will not be accepted for you.
When anyone brings a peace offering to the LORD from the cattle or the flock, to keep a promise or as a freely given gift, it must be perfect to be accepted. There must be nothing wrong with it.
Do not offer the LORD an animal that is blind, injured, or crippled, or that has warts, sores, or a running skin disease. Do not put any of these on the altar as a gift made by fire to the LORD.
You may offer a bull or a lamb that has a body part too long or too short as a freely given gift, but it will not be accepted to keep a promise.
Do not offer the LORD an animal whose private parts are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. Do not do this in your land.
Do not accept animals like these from a foreigner and offer them as the food of your God. They are damaged and have something wrong with them, so they will not be accepted for you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"When a calf, a lamb, or a young goat is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be accepted as a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Do not kill a cow or a sheep on the same day as its young.
When you offer a thank offering to the LORD, offer it in the right way so that it will be accepted for you.
It must be eaten on the same day. Leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.
Keep my commands and obey them. I am the LORD.
Do not dishonour my holy name. I must be honoured as holy among the people of Israel. I am the LORD, who makes you holy,
who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: These are my special feasts, the feasts of the LORD, which you must announce as holy gatherings.
You may work for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a day of complete rest and a holy gathering. Do no work at all. Wherever you live, it is a Sabbath for the LORD.
These are the special feasts of the LORD, the holy gatherings you must announce at their set times.
The LORD's Passover begins at sunset on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of that month, the Feast of Bread Without Yeast to the LORD begins. For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
For seven days, offer a gift made by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you come into the land I am giving you, and you gather its harvest, bring the priest a bundle of the first grain you harvest.
He will wave the bundle in front of the LORD so that it will be accepted for you. The priest will wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
On the day you wave the bundle, offer a one-year-old male lamb with nothing wrong with it as a burnt offering to the LORD.
With it, bring a grain offering of about three kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil, a gift made by fire to the LORD with a pleasing smell, and a drink offering of about one litre of wine.
Do not eat any bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that day, when you bring this offering to your God. This is a rule forever for all your families to come, wherever you live.
From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the bundle of grain to be waved, count seven full weeks.
Count fifty days, up to the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then bring a grain offering of new grain to the LORD.
From your homes, bring two loaves of bread to be waved, each made from about three kilograms of fine flour and baked with yeast. They are an offering to the LORD from the first part of your harvest.

With the bread, offer seven one-year-old lambs with nothing wrong with them, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old male lambs as peace offerings.
The priest will wave the two lambs with the bread from the first harvest in front of the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy to the LORD and will belong to the priest.
On that same day, announce a holy gathering and do no regular work. This is a rule forever for all your families to come, wherever you live.

When you gather the harvest of your land, do not harvest all the way to the edges of your field, and do not pick up the grain that was dropped. Leave it for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: On the first day of the seventh month, have a day of rest, a holy gathering remembered with the blowing of trumpets.
Do no regular work, and offer a gift made by fire to the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses,
"The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement, the day of being made right with God. Have a holy gathering, go without food, and offer a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Do no work at all on that day, because it is the Day of Atonement, when you are made right with the LORD your God.
Anyone who does not go without food on that day must be cut off from his people.
I will destroy from among his people anyone who does any work on that day.
Do no work at all. This is a rule forever for all your families to come, wherever you live.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must go without food. Keep this Sabbath from the evening of the ninth day of the month until the next evening."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, the Feast of Shelters to the LORD begins, and it lasts seven days.
On the first day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
For seven days, offer gifts made by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day, have a holy gathering and offer a gift made by fire to the LORD. It is a special gathering, and you must do no regular work.

These are the special feasts of the LORD that you must announce as holy gatherings. At them you bring gifts made by fire to the LORD: burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its own day.
These are added to the LORD's Sabbaths, and to your gifts, all your promised offerings, and all the freely given offerings you bring to the LORD.

So, starting on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the crops of the land, celebrate the feast of the LORD for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day is a day of rest.
On the first day, take the best fruit from the trees, palm branches, leafy branches, and willows from the stream, and celebrate with joy in front of the LORD your God for seven days.
Celebrate it as a feast to the LORD for seven days every year. This is a rule forever for all your families to come. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
Live in shelters for seven days. Everyone born in Israel must live in shelters,
so that your children after you will know that I made the people of Israel live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
So Moses told the people of Israel about the special feasts of the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil from pressed olives for the lamps, so that they can be kept burning all the time.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain in front of the Covenant Box, Aaron must keep the lamps burning before the LORD from evening until morning, always. This is a rule forever for all your families to come.
He must always look after the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD.
Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, using about three kilograms of flour for each loaf.
Put them in two rows, six in each row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
Put pure incense along each row. It will be the part that is remembered for the bread, a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day the bread must be set out before the LORD, always. It is a covenant forever for the people of Israel.
The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons, and they must eat it in a holy place. It is a most holy part of the gifts made by fire to the LORD, their share forever."
There was a man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian. He went out among the people of Israel, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite man.
The son of the Israelite woman spoke against the holy Name of the LORD and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
They kept him under guard until the LORD would make clear to them what to do.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Take the man who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him must put their hands on his head, and then the whole community must stone him.
Tell the people of Israel: Anyone who curses his God will carry the blame for his sin.

Anyone who speaks against the name of the LORD must be put to death. The whole community must stone him. Whether he is a foreigner or born in the land, if he speaks against the Name, he must be put to death.
Anyone who kills another person must be put to death.
Anyone who kills someone's animal must replace it, a life for a life.
If anyone injures his neighbour, the same must be done to him as he has done:
a broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Whatever injury he has caused must be done to him.
Whoever kills an animal must replace it, but whoever kills a person must be put to death.
You must have the same law for the foreigner and for the one born in the land. I am the LORD your God."
Moses told this to the people of Israel. They took the man who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him to death. The people of Israel did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you come into the land I am giving you, the land itself must rest and keep a Sabbath for the LORD.
For six years you may plant your fields and prune your vineyards and gather their crops.
But the seventh year must be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath for the LORD. Do not plant your fields or prune your vineyards that year.
Do not harvest what grows by itself, and do not pick the grapes from your vines that have not been pruned. It is a year of complete rest for the land.
Whatever the land grows by itself during its Sabbath year will be food for you all: for you, your male and female servants, your hired workers, and the foreigners living with you.
It will also be food for your farm animals and for the wild animals in your land. Everything it grows may be eaten.
Count seven Sabbath years, seven times seven years, which adds up to forty-nine years.
Then, on the tenth day of the seventh month, sound the loud trumpet. On the Day of Atonement, sound the trumpet through all your land.

Make the fiftieth year holy, and announce freedom everywhere in the land for everyone living there. It will be a year of Jubilee for you. Each of you must go back to your own family land and to your own family.
The fiftieth year will be your year of Jubilee. Do not plant, do not harvest what grows by itself, and do not pick the grapes from the vines that were not pruned.
It is a Jubilee, and it is holy for you. Eat only what the fields grow by themselves.
In this Year of Jubilee, each of you must go back to your own family land.
When you sell land to your neighbour or buy land from him, do not cheat each other.
When you buy from your neighbour, set the price by the number of years since the last Jubilee. He will set the price he sells for by the number of harvests left.
If there are many years left, the price goes up. If there are only a few years left, the price goes down. What he is really selling you is the number of harvests.
Do not cheat each other, but fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
Obey my rules and keep my laws carefully, and you will live safely in the land.
The land will give its fruit, and you will eat all you want and live there in safety.
You may ask, 'What will we eat in the seventh year, if we do not plant or harvest our crops?'
I will send my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that the land will give enough crops for three years.
When you plant in the eighth year, you will still be eating from the old harvest. You will keep eating the old food until the harvest of the ninth year comes in.
The land must never be sold forever, because the land belongs to me. You are only foreigners and guests living with me.
Everywhere in the land you own, you must allow the land to be bought back.
If someone among you becomes poor and sells some of his land, his closest relative must come and buy back what he sold.
If he has no one to buy it back for him, but later he does well and has enough to buy it back himself,
he must count the years since he sold it, and pay back the man he sold it to for the years that are left. Then he can go back to his land.
But if he cannot get enough to buy it back, the land will stay with the person who bought it until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it will be given back, and he can return to his land.
If someone sells a house in a walled city, he has one full year after the sale to buy it back. For one year he has the right to buy it back.
If it is not bought back within the full year, the house in the walled city will belong forever to the person who bought it and to his family after him. It will not be given back in the Jubilee.
But houses in villages without walls around them are treated like fields in the countryside. They can be bought back, and they must be given back in the Jubilee.
The Levites, however, may always buy back their houses in the towns that belong to them.
If a Levite's house in one of their towns is sold and not bought back, it must be given back in the Jubilee. For the houses in the Levites' towns are their own land among the people of Israel.
But the pasture land around their towns must not be sold, because it belongs to them forever.
If someone among you becomes poor and cannot support himself, help him. Let him live with you as you would a foreigner or a guest.
Do not charge him interest or make a profit from him. Fear your God, and let him live among you.
Do not lend him money with interest, and do not sell him food for a profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If someone among you becomes poor and sells himself to you, do not make him work like a slave.
Treat him like a hired worker or a guest living with you. He will work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
Then he and his children may leave you and go back to their own family and to the land of their fathers.
The people of Israel are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves.
Do not rule over him cruelly, but fear your God.
Your male and female slaves may come from the nations around you. You may buy slaves from them.
You may also buy some of the children of foreigners living among you, and members of their families born in your land. They may become your property.
You may leave them to your children after you as their property, and they may be your slaves for life. But you must not rule cruelly over your fellow Israelites.
A foreigner or a guest living among you may become rich, while one of your fellow Israelites becomes poor and sells himself to that foreigner or to a member of the foreigner's family.
After he has sold himself, he still has the right to be bought back. One of his brothers may buy him back,
or his uncle, or his cousin, or any close relative in his family. Or if he becomes rich, he may buy himself back.

He and the man who bought him must count the years from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price for his freedom is set by the number of years, as if he were paid like a hired worker for that time.
If many years are left, he must pay back a larger part of the price he was sold for.
If only a few years are left until the Year of Jubilee, he must count them and pay back a smaller amount, according to the years that remain.
He must be treated like a worker hired year by year. You must make sure his owner does not rule over him cruelly.
If he is not bought back in any of these ways, he and his children must be set free in the Year of Jubilee.
For the people of Israel belong to me as servants. They are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not make idols for yourselves. Do not set up carved statues or holy stone pillars, and do not put carved stones in your land to bow down to them. For I am the LORD your God.
Keep my Sabbath days and respect my holy place. I am the LORD.
If you live by my rules and carefully obey my commands,
I will send you rain at the right time. The land will give its crops, and the trees in the fields will give their fruit.

Your harvesting of grain will last until it is time to pick grapes, and your picking of grapes will last until it is time to plant. You will have all the food you want, and you will live safely in your land.
I will give peace in the land. You will lie down to sleep, and no one will make you afraid. I will remove dangerous animals from the land, and war will not pass through your country.
You will chase your enemies, and they will be killed by the sword in front of you.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will be killed by the sword in front of you.
I will look on you with kindness. I will give you many children and make you grow in number, and I will keep my covenant with you.
You will still be eating last year's harvest when you have to clear it out to make room for the new.
I will put my home among you, and I will not turn away from you.
I will walk among you. I will be your God, and you will be my people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the heavy wooden bar from your necks and let you walk with your heads held high.
But if you will not listen to me and will not obey all these commands,
if you reject my rules and hate my laws, and refuse to obey all my commands, and so break my covenant,

then this is what I will do to you: I will bring sudden terror on you, wasting diseases and fever that will make your eyes fail and your life drain away. You will plant your seed for nothing, because your enemies will eat the crops.
I will turn against you, and your enemies will defeat you. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will run away even when no one is chasing you.
If after all this you still will not listen to me, I will punish you seven times more for your sins.
I will break your proud strength. I will make the sky above you like iron, giving no rain, and the ground under you as hard as bronze.
All your hard work will be for nothing, because your land will not give its crops, and the trees will not give their fruit.
If you still go against me and refuse to listen to me, I will strike you seven times more, as your sins deserve.
I will send wild animals among you. They will take your children, destroy your cattle, and make you few. Your roads will be empty.
If even after these things you do not turn back to me, but keep going against me,
then I myself will go against you. I myself will strike you seven times for your sins.
I will bring war on you to punish you for breaking my covenant. When you gather in your cities for safety, I will send disease among you, and you will be handed over to your enemies.
When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will be able to bake all your bread in one oven, and they will hand it out by weight. You will eat, but you will not be full.
If in spite of all this you still do not listen to me, but keep going against me,
then in my anger I will go against you. I myself will punish you seven times for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters.
I will destroy your places of idol worship and cut down your incense altars. I will pile your dead bodies on the lifeless bodies of your idols, and I will turn away from you in disgust.
I will turn your cities into ruins and leave your holy places empty. I will not enjoy the pleasing smell of your offerings.
I will make your land so empty that even your enemies who come to live there will be shocked.
I will scatter you among the nations, and I will pull out my sword and chase after you. Your land will be empty, and your cities will be in ruins.
Then, all the time the land lies empty while you are in the land of your enemies, it will enjoy its Sabbath years. The land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
All the time it lies empty, it will have the rest it did not have during your Sabbath years when you lived there.

As for those of you who are left alive in the lands of your enemies, I will make them so afraid that the sound of a leaf blowing in the wind will make them run. They will run as if running from a sword, and they will fall even when no one is chasing them.
They will trip over one another as if running from a sword, even when no one is chasing them. You will not be able to stand up against your enemies.
You will die among the nations. The land of your enemies will swallow you up.
Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of your enemies because of their sins, and because of the sins of their fathers too.
But they may confess their sins and the sins of their fathers, how they were unfaithful to me and went against me,
which made me go against them and bring them into the land of their enemies. If their proud hearts are humbled and they accept the punishment for their sins,
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

For the land will be left empty by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies empty without them. They will accept the punishment for their sins, because they rejected my laws and hated my rules.

Yet in spite of all this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or hate them so much that I destroy them completely and break my covenant with them. For I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I will remember the covenant I made with their ancestors, whom I brought out of Egypt while the nations watched, to be their God. I am the LORD."
These are the rules, laws, and teachings that the LORD gave on Mount Sinai through Moses, between himself and the people of Israel.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: If someone makes a special promise to give a person to the LORD, he may pay the set value of that person instead.
The set value of a man from twenty to sixty years old is fifty pieces of silver, using the official weight of the holy place.
For a woman of that age, the set value is thirty pieces of silver.
For a person from five to twenty years old, the set value is twenty pieces of silver for a boy and ten pieces for a girl.
For a child from one month to five years old, the set value is five pieces of silver for a boy and three pieces of silver for a girl.
For a person sixty years old or more, the set value is fifteen pieces of silver for a man and ten pieces for a woman.

If someone is too poor to pay the set value, the person must be brought to the priest, and the priest will set a value. The priest will set it according to what the one who made the promise can afford.
If the promise is an animal that may be offered to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD becomes holy.
He must not swap it or change it, a good one for a bad one or a bad one for a good one. If he does swap one animal for another, both the animal and the one swapped for it become holy.
If the promise is an unclean animal, one that may not be offered to the LORD, the animal must be brought to the priest.
The priest will judge its value, whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets, that is its value.
If the owner wants to buy it back, he must pay its value plus one fifth more.
If someone gives his house as a holy gift to the LORD, the priest will judge its value, whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets, that is its value.
If the one who gave the house wants to buy it back, he must pay its value plus one fifth more, and then it will be his again.
If someone gives part of his family land to the LORD, its value will be set by the amount of seed needed to plant it: fifty pieces of silver for every two hundred kilograms of barley seed.
If he gives his field in the Year of Jubilee, the full set value stands.
But if he gives his field after the Jubilee, the priest will work out the price by the number of years left until the next Year of Jubilee, and the set value will be lowered.
If the one who gave the field wants to buy it back, he must pay its value plus one fifth more, and it will be his again.
But if he does not buy back the field, or if he has sold it to someone else, it can never be bought back.
When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD, like a field given completely to him. It will belong to the priests.
If someone gives the LORD a field he has bought, which is not part of his family land,
the priest will work out its value up to the Year of Jubilee. The man must pay that amount on that same day, as a holy gift to the LORD.
In the Year of Jubilee, the field will go back to the person he bought it from, the one whose family land it is.
All set values must use the official weight of the holy place, twenty small weights to each piece of silver.
But no one may give the firstborn of an animal as a special gift, because the firstborn already belongs to the LORD. Whether it is a calf or a lamb, it is the LORD's.
If it is an unclean animal, the owner may buy it back by paying its set value plus one fifth more. If it is not bought back, it must be sold at its set value.

But anything that someone gives completely to the LORD from what he owns, whether a person, an animal, or family land, may not be sold or bought back. Everything given completely in this way is most holy to the LORD.
No person who has been given over to be destroyed may be bought back. He must be put to death.
A tenth of everything the land produces, whether grain from the fields or fruit from the trees, belongs to the LORD. It is holy to the LORD.
If someone wants to buy back any of his tenth, he must pay its value plus one fifth more.
A tenth of the cattle and the flock, every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd's rod as they are counted, will be holy to the LORD.
The owner must not pick out the good ones from the bad, and must not swap any of them. If he does swap one, both the animal and the one swapped for it become holy. They cannot be bought back."
These are the commands the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai for the people of Israel.
Num: On the first day of the second month, in the second year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Sinai desert. He said,
"Count all the people of Israel by their clans and families. List the name of every man, one by one,
all who are twenty years old or more and able to go to war in Israel. You and Aaron must count them by their army groups.
One man from each tribe, the head of his family group, will help you.
These are the names of the men who will help you: From Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.
From Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
From Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab.
From Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar.
From Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.
From the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
From Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.
From Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
From Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran.
From Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
From Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
These were the men chosen from the community, the leaders of their fathers' tribes. They were the heads of the army groups of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named,
and on the first day of the second month they called the whole community together. The people were listed by their clans and families, and every man twenty years old or more was named, one by one.
So Moses counted them in the Sinai desert, as the LORD had commanded him.
From the descendants of Reuben, Israel's oldest son, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Reuben was forty-six thousand five hundred.
From the descendants of Simeon, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Simeon was fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
From the descendants of Gad, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Gad was forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
From the descendants of Judah, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Judah was seventy-four thousand six hundred.
From the descendants of Issachar, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Issachar was fifty-four thousand four hundred.
From the descendants of Zebulun, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Zebulun was fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
From the descendants of Ephraim, one of the sons of Joseph, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Ephraim was forty thousand five hundred.
From the descendants of Manasseh, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Manasseh was thirty-two thousand two hundred.
From the descendants of Benjamin, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Benjamin was thirty-five thousand four hundred.
From the descendants of Dan, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Dan was sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
From the descendants of Asher, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Asher was forty-one thousand five hundred.
From the descendants of Naphtali, every man twenty years old or more who could go to war was listed by name, one by one, by clans and families.
The number counted from the tribe of Naphtali was fifty-three thousand four hundred.
These are the men counted by Moses and Aaron, with the help of the twelve leaders of Israel, one for each family group.
All the men of Israel twenty years old or more who could go to war were counted by their families.
The total number was six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites were not counted with them by their fathers' tribe.
For the LORD had said to Moses,
"Do not count the tribe of Levi, and do not include them in the count of the people of Israel.

Instead, put the Levites in charge of the Holy Tent where the Covenant Law is kept, with all its furniture and everything that belongs to it. They must carry the Holy Tent and all its furniture. They will take care of it and camp around it.
When the Holy Tent is to move, the Levites will take it down, and when it is to be set up, the Levites will set it up. Anyone else who comes near it must be put to death.
The people of Israel will set up their tents, each man in his own camp and under his own flag, by their army groups.
But the Levites will camp around the Holy Tent where the Covenant Law is kept, so that my anger will not fall on the people of Israel. The Levites are responsible for the Holy Tent."
The people of Israel did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"The people of Israel must camp around the Tent of Meeting, at some distance from it. Each man must camp under his own flag, with the banners of his family group.
On the east side, toward the sunrise, the tribes under the flag of Judah's camp will set up their tents by their army groups. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His army group numbers seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The tribe of Issachar will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His army group numbers fifty-four thousand four hundred.
Then comes the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His army group numbers fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The total number in Judah's camp, by their army groups, is one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred. They will march out first.
On the south side, the tribes under the flag of Reuben's camp will camp by their army groups. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His army group numbers forty-six thousand five hundred.
The tribe of Simeon will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His army group numbers fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
Then comes the tribe of Gad. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His army group numbers forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
The total number in Reuben's camp, by their army groups, is one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty. They will march out second.
Then the Tent of Meeting will move out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the other camps. They will march out in the same order as they camp, each in his own place under his own flag.
On the west side, the tribes under the flag of Ephraim's camp will camp by their army groups. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His army group numbers forty thousand five hundred.
The tribe of Manasseh will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His army group numbers thirty-two thousand two hundred.
Then comes the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His army group numbers thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The total number in Ephraim's camp, by their army groups, is one hundred eight thousand one hundred. They will march out third.
On the north side, the tribes under the flag of Dan's camp will camp by their army groups. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His army group numbers sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The tribe of Asher will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ochran.
His army group numbers forty-one thousand five hundred.
Then comes the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His army group numbers fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The total number in Dan's camp is one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They will march out last, under their flags."
These are the people of Israel, counted by their families. The total number in all the camps, by their army groups, was six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites were not counted with the other people of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So the people of Israel did everything the LORD commanded Moses. They camped under their flags in this way, and they marched out in this way, each man with his clan and family.
This is the family history of Aaron and Moses at the time the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the oldest, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These were Aaron's sons, the priests who were anointed and set apart to serve as priests.

But Nadab and Abihu died in front of the LORD when they offered him a fire that was not allowed, in the Sinai desert. They had no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was alive.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Bring the tribe of Levi forward and put them under Aaron the priest to help him.
They will do the work for him and for the whole community at the Tent of Meeting, serving at the Holy Tent.
They will take care of all the furniture of the Tent of Meeting and do the work the people of Israel are responsible for, serving at the Holy Tent.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. From all the people of Israel, they are the ones given completely to him.
Appoint Aaron and his sons to serve as priests. Anyone else who comes near the holy things must be put to death."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Look, I have chosen the Levites from among the people of Israel to take the place of every firstborn son of Israel. The Levites belong to me,
because all the firstborn are mine. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, both people and animals. They are mine. I am the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert. He said,
"Count the Levites by their families and clans. Count every male one month old or more."
So Moses counted them, as the LORD had told him.
These were the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These were the clans from the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei.
The clans from the sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The clans from the sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites, by their families.
The clans of Libni and Shimei came from Gershon. These were the Gershonite clans.
The number of all their males one month old or more was seven thousand five hundred.
The Gershonite clans were to camp on the west side, behind the Holy Tent.
The leader of the Gershonite families was Eliasaph son of Lael.
At the Tent of Meeting, the Gershonites were in charge of the Holy Tent itself, its tent and covering, the curtain at the door of the Tent of Meeting,
the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard around the Holy Tent and the altar, and the ropes. They did all the work connected with these things.
The clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel came from Kohath. These were the Kohathite clans.
The number of all their males one month old or more was eight thousand six hundred. They were in charge of the holy place.
The Kohathite clans were to camp on the south side of the Holy Tent.
The leader of the Kohathite families was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They were in charge of the Covenant Box, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the tools used in the holy place, and the curtain. They did all the work connected with these things.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest. He was in charge of those who took care of the holy place.
The clans of Mahli and Mushi came from Merari. These were the Merarite clans.
The number of all their males one month old or more was six thousand two hundred.
The leader of the Merarite families was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the Holy Tent.
The Merarites were in charge of the frames of the Holy Tent, its crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment. They did all the work connected with these things,
and also with the posts all around the courtyard, with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes.

Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons were to camp on the east side of the Holy Tent, in front of the Tent of Meeting, toward the sunrise. They were in charge of the holy place on behalf of the people of Israel. Anyone else who came near it was to be put to death.
The total number of Levite males one month old or more, counted by Moses and Aaron by their clans at the LORD's command, was twenty-two thousand.
The LORD said to Moses, "Count all the firstborn males of Israel who are one month old or more, and make a list of their names.
Take the Levites for me in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel, and the Levites' animals in place of all the firstborn animals of the people of Israel. I am the LORD."
So Moses counted all the firstborn sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded him.
The total number of firstborn males one month old or more, listed by name, was twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel, and the Levites' animals in place of their animals. The Levites belong to me. I am the LORD.
There are two hundred seventy-three more firstborn sons of Israel than there are Levites. To buy them back,
collect five pieces of silver for each one, using the official weight of the holy place, which is twenty small weights to each piece.
Give the money paid to buy back the extra firstborn to Aaron and his sons."
So Moses collected the money from the firstborn who were more than the number of Levites who took their place.
From the firstborn of Israel he collected one thousand three hundred sixty-five pieces of silver, using the official weight of the holy place.
Moses gave the money to Aaron and his sons, as the LORD had commanded him.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Count the Kohathites among the Levites by their clans and families.
Count all the men from thirty to fifty years old who come to work at the Tent of Meeting.
This is the work of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting: they will take care of the most holy things.
When the camp is ready to move, Aaron and his sons must go in, take down the curtain that hangs in front, and cover the Covenant Box with it.
Then they must put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth of solid blue on top, and put its carrying poles in place.
Over the table for the holy bread they must spread a blue cloth, and put on it the dishes, the spoons, the bowls, and the jars for drink offerings. The bread that is always there must stay on it.
They must spread a red cloth over these, cover it with fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They must take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand, its lamps, its wick cutters, its trays, and all the jars for the oil used with it.
They must wrap it and all its tools in a covering of fine leather and put it on a carrying frame.
Over the gold altar they must spread a blue cloth, cover it with fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They must take all the tools used for serving in the holy place, wrap them in a blue cloth, cover them with fine leather, and put them on a carrying frame.
They must clear the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
Then they must put on it all the tools used at the altar: the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels, and the bowls. They must spread a covering of fine leather over it and put its poles in place.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy furniture and all the holy tools, and the camp is ready to move, the Kohathites will come to carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things from the Tent of Meeting that the Kohathites must carry.

Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, will be in charge of the oil for the lamps, the sweet incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He will be in charge of the whole Holy Tent and everything in it, the holy place and its furniture."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Do not let the Kohathite clans be destroyed from among the Levites.
Do this for them so that they will live and not die when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons must go in and give each man his job and tell him what to carry.
But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Count the Gershonites also, by their families and clans.
Count all the men from thirty to fifty years old who come to serve at the Tent of Meeting.
This is the work of the Gershonite clans, the work they do and what they carry:
They will carry the curtains of the Holy Tent, the Tent of Meeting itself, its covering and the outer covering of fine leather, the curtain at the door of the Tent of Meeting,

the curtains of the courtyard around the Holy Tent and the altar, the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard, the ropes, and all the equipment used for this work. They will do all the work connected with these things.
All the work of the Gershonites, both carrying and other work, must be done under the direction of Aaron and his sons. Tell them exactly what they are responsible to carry.
This is the work of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting. They will work under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Count the Merarites by their clans and families.
Count all the men from thirty to fifty years old who come to work at the Tent of Meeting.
This is what they must carry as part of their work at the Tent of Meeting: the frames of the Holy Tent, its crossbars, its posts, and its bases,
and the posts all around the courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, ropes, and all their equipment and everything used with them. Tell each man by name exactly what he must carry.
This is the work of the Merarite clans at the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest."
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families.
They counted all the men from thirty to fifty years old who came to work at the Tent of Meeting.
Counted by clans, they numbered two thousand seven hundred fifty.
This was the total of the Kohathite clans who served at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
The Gershonites were counted by their clans and families.
All the men from thirty to fifty years old who came to work at the Tent of Meeting
were counted by their clans and families, and they numbered two thousand six hundred thirty.
This was the total of the Gershonite clans who served at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had commanded.
The Merarites were counted by their clans and families.
All the men from thirty to fifty years old who came to work at the Tent of Meeting
were counted by their clans, and they numbered three thousand two hundred.
This was the total of the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families.
All the men from thirty to fifty years old who came to do the work of serving and carrying at the Tent of Meeting
numbered eight thousand five hundred eighty.
As the LORD had commanded through Moses, each man was counted and given his work and told what to carry. So they were counted, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Command the people of Israel to send out of the camp anyone who has a serious skin disease, anyone who has a flow from the body, and anyone who is unclean from touching a dead body.
Send out both men and women. Put them outside the camp, so that they do not make the camp unclean, because I live among my people there."
The people of Israel did this. They sent them outside the camp, just as the LORD had told Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: When a man or woman does wrong to another person in any way, they are being unfaithful to the LORD, and that person is guilty.
He must admit the sin he has done. He must pay back in full what he owes for the wrong, add one fifth more, and give it to the person he wronged.

But if that person has died and has no close relative to receive the payment, the payment belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest. This is in addition to the ram the priest offers to make the guilty person right with God.
All the special holy gifts that the people of Israel bring to the priest belong to him.
Each person's holy gifts are his own to give, but whatever is given to the priest belongs to the priest."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: A man's wife may go astray and be unfaithful to him.

She may have sexual relations with another man, and her husband does not know about it. She has made herself unclean, but it is kept secret, there is no witness against her, and she was not caught in the act.

Or a feeling of jealousy may come over her husband, and he may suspect his wife, and she really has made herself unclean. Or a feeling of jealousy may come over him and he suspects his wife, even though she has not made herself unclean.

In either case, the man must bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring an offering for her: about one and a half kilograms of barley flour. He must not pour oil or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering to bring a hidden wrong to light.
The priest will bring the woman forward and have her stand in front of the LORD.
He will put some holy water in a clay jar, and take some dust from the floor of the Holy Tent and put it into the water.

The priest will have the woman stand in front of the LORD. He will loosen her hair and put the grain offering for jealousy in her hands, the offering that brings a wrong to light. The priest himself will hold the bitter water that brings a curse.

Then the priest will make the woman take an oath. He will say to her, 'If no other man has slept with you, and you have not gone astray and made yourself unclean while married to your husband, may this bitter water that brings a curse not harm you.
But if you have gone astray while married to your husband, and made yourself unclean by sleeping with a man other than your husband...'
Here the priest will make the woman take the oath of the curse, and say to her, 'may the LORD make your people use your name in curses and oaths, by making your womb shrivel and your belly swell.
May this water that brings a curse go into your body and make your belly swell and your womb shrivel.' And the woman must say, 'Amen. So be it.'
The priest will write these curses on a scroll and then wash the words off into the bitter water.
He will make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water will go into her and cause bitter pain.
The priest will take the grain offering for jealousy from the woman's hands, wave it in front of the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
He will take a handful of the grain offering as the part that is remembered and burn it on the altar. After that he will make the woman drink the water.

If she has made herself unclean and been unfaithful to her husband, then when she drinks the water that brings a curse, it will go into her and cause bitter pain. Her belly will swell and her womb will shrivel, and her name will be used in curses among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean and is pure, she will not be harmed, and she will be able to have children.
This is the teaching about jealousy, for when a wife goes astray and makes herself unclean while married to her husband,
or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a man and he suspects his wife. He must have her stand in front of the LORD, and the priest will do all that this teaching says.
The husband will be free from blame, but the woman will carry the blame for her sin."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: A man or a woman may make a special promise to set himself apart for the LORD as a Nazirite.
Then he must stay away from wine and other strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or from other strong drink. He must not drink grape juice or eat grapes, fresh or dried.
As long as he is a Nazirite, he must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins.
As long as his promise lasts, no razor may touch his head. Until the time he set apart for the LORD is over, he is holy, and he must let the hair of his head grow long.
As long as he is set apart for the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
Even if his father, mother, brother, or sister dies, he must not make himself unclean for them, because the sign that he is set apart for God is on his head.
All the time he is a Nazirite, he is holy to the LORD.
If someone dies suddenly beside him and makes his long hair unclean, he must shave his head on the day he is made clean, the seventh day.
On the eighth day he must bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, to make him right with God, because he sinned by being near the dead body. That same day he must make his head holy again.

He must set himself apart again for the LORD for the full time of his promise, and bring a one-year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The days before do not count, because his time of being set apart was made unclean.
This is the teaching for the Nazirite when his time of being set apart is over: He must be brought to the door of the Tent of Meeting.

There he must bring his offerings to the LORD: a one-year-old male lamb with nothing wrong with it for a burnt offering, a one-year-old female lamb with nothing wrong with it for a sin offering, and a ram with nothing wrong with it for a peace offering.
He must also bring a basket of bread made without yeast: loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and thin wafers spread with oil, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
The priest will bring them before the LORD and offer the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He will offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, together with the basket of bread without yeast. The priest will also offer its grain offering and drink offering.
Then at the door of the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite must shave off the long hair that showed he was set apart. He must take the hair and put it in the fire under the peace offering.
After the Nazirite has shaved off his hair, the priest will put in his hands the boiled shoulder of the ram, one loaf without yeast from the basket, and one wafer without yeast.

The priest will wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was given. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the teaching for the Nazirite who makes a promise, and about the offering he must bring to the LORD for being set apart, besides anything else he can afford. He must do whatever he promised, following the teaching for the Nazirite."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you must bless the people of Israel. Say to them:
'May the LORD bless you and keep you safe.
May the LORD smile on you and be kind to you.
May the LORD look on you with favour and give you peace.'
In this way they will put my name on the people of Israel, and I will bless them."
Moses finished setting up the Holy Tent. He anointed it and made it holy, with all its furniture, and he anointed the altar and all its tools and made them holy.
On that day the leaders of Israel brought gifts. These were the heads of the family groups, the leaders of the tribes who had been in charge of the counting.
They brought their gifts to the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, one wagon for every two leaders and an ox from each one. They brought them in front of the Holy Tent.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Accept these gifts from them, so they can be used for the work at the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each group as their work needs."
So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
