He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work needed,
and four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work needed. They worked under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
But Moses gave none to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the holy things, which had to be carried on their shoulders.
When the altar was anointed, the leaders brought gifts to dedicate it, and they presented their gifts in front of the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, "Each day, one leader must bring his gift for the dedication of the altar."
On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah, brought his gift.

His gift was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, by the official weight of the holy place. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He also brought one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense,
one young bull, one ram, and one one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,
one male goat for a sin offering,
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his gift.

His gift was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, by the official weight of the holy place. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He also brought one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense,
one young bull, one ram, and one one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,
one male goat for a sin offering,
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day, Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the people of Zebulun, brought his gift.

His gift was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, by the official weight of the holy place. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He also brought one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense,
one young bull, one ram, and one one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,
one male goat for a sin offering,
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day, Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the people of Reuben, brought his gift.

His gift was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, by the official weight of the holy place. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.

one young bull, one ram, and one one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,

and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Elizur son of Shedeur.

He also brought one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense,
one young bull, one ram, and one one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,
one male goat for a sin offering,
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph son of Deuel, the leader of the people of Gad, brought his gift.

His gift was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, by the official weight of the holy place. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.

and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Eliasaph son of Deuel.

These were the gifts from the leaders of Israel to dedicate the altar when it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed one hundred thirty shekels, and each bowl seventy. All the silver dishes together weighed two thousand four hundred shekels, by the official weight of the holy place.
The twelve gold dishes full of incense weighed ten shekels each, by the official weight of the holy place. All the gold dishes together weighed one hundred twenty shekels.
The animals for the burnt offering were twelve young bulls, twelve rams, and twelve one-year-old male lambs, with their grain offerings. Twelve male goats were given for the sin offering.
The animals for the peace offering were twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty one-year-old male lambs. These were the gifts for dedicating the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover on the Covenant Box, from between the two winged creatures. In this way the LORD spoke to him.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron: When you set up the seven lamps, they must shine toward the area in front of the lampstand."
Aaron did this. He set up the lamps so that they lit the area in front of the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The lampstand was made of gold, hammered into shape from its base to its flower shapes. Moses had it made just like the pattern the LORD had shown him.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Take the Levites from among the people of Israel and make them clean.
This is how to make them clean: Sprinkle the water for washing away sin on them. Have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean.
Then have them take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You must take a second young bull for a sin offering.
Bring the Levites to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and gather the whole community of Israel there.
Bring the Levites before the LORD, and the people of Israel will put their hands on them.
Aaron will present the Levites to the LORD as a wave offering from the people of Israel, so that they may do the LORD's work.
The Levites will put their hands on the heads of the bulls. Offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make the Levites right with God.
Have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and present them to the LORD as a wave offering.
In this way you will set the Levites apart from the rest of the people of Israel, and the Levites will belong to me.
After you have made them clean and presented them as a wave offering, the Levites may go in to do their work at the Tent of Meeting.
They are the ones from among the people of Israel who are given completely to me. I have taken them for myself in place of every firstborn son of the people of Israel.
Every firstborn in Israel, whether person or animal, is mine. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart for myself.
And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.

From all the people of Israel, I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons. They will do the work for the people of Israel at the Tent of Meeting and help make them right with God, so that no disaster will strike the people of Israel when they come near the holy place."
Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel did with the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses about them.
The Levites made themselves clean from sin and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD, and made them right with God to make them clean.
After that, the Levites went in to do their work at the Tent of Meeting under Aaron and his sons. They did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"This is the rule for the Levites: Men twenty-five years old or more will come to take part in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
At fifty years old they must retire from their regular work and stop serving.
They may help their brothers with their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they must not do the work themselves. This is how you must arrange the duties of the Levites."
In the first month of the second year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert. He said,
"The people of Israel must celebrate the Passover at its set time.
Celebrate it at its set time, at sunset on the fourteenth day of this month. Follow all its rules and laws."
So Moses told the people of Israel to celebrate the Passover.
They celebrated it in the Sinai desert at sunset on the fourteenth day of the first month. The people of Israel did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
But some men were unclean because they had touched a dead body, so they could not celebrate the Passover on that day. They came to Moses and Aaron that same day
and said, "We are unclean because we touched a dead body. But why should we be kept from bringing the LORD's offering at the set time with the other people of Israel?"
Moses answered them, "Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands about you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: If any of you, or any of your descendants, are unclean because of a dead body, or are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate the LORD's Passover.
Celebrate it at sunset on the fourteenth day of the second month. Eat the lamb with bread made without yeast and with bitter herbs.
Do not leave any of it until morning, and do not break any of its bones. Follow all the rules for the Passover.

But if a man is clean and is not away on a journey, and still does not celebrate the Passover, he must be cut off from his people. He did not bring the LORD's offering at the set time, so he will carry the blame for his sin.
If a foreigner living among you wants to celebrate the LORD's Passover, he must follow its rules and laws. The same rule applies to the foreigner and to the person born in the land."
On the day the Holy Tent was set up, the cloud covered it, the Tent of the Covenant Law. From evening until morning the cloud over the Holy Tent looked like fire.
It was always like this. The cloud covered it by day, and at night it looked like fire.
Whenever the cloud lifted from above the Tent, the people of Israel set out. Wherever the cloud stopped, the people of Israel camped.
At the LORD's command the people of Israel set out, and at his command they camped. As long as the cloud stayed over the Holy Tent, they stayed in camp.
When the cloud stayed over the Holy Tent for a long time, the people of Israel obeyed the LORD and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud was over the Holy Tent for only a few days. At the LORD's command they stayed in camp, and at his command they set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted, they set out.
Whether the cloud stayed over the Holy Tent for two days, a month, or a year, the people of Israel stayed in camp and did not set out. But when it lifted, they set out.
At the LORD's command they camped, and at the LORD's command they set out. They obeyed the LORD's command, as he gave it through Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call the community together and to tell the camps when to move.
When both trumpets are blown, the whole community must gather in front of you at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
If only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of the army groups of Israel, must gather in front of you.
When the trumpets sound a loud alarm, the tribes camped on the east side must set out.
When the alarm sounds a second time, the tribes camped on the south side must set out. The alarm will be the signal to move.
But when you call the people together, blow the trumpets without sounding the alarm.
Aaron's sons, the priests, will blow the trumpets. This is a rule forever for you and for all your families to come.
When you go to war in your own land against an enemy who attacks you, sound the alarm on the trumpets. Then the LORD your God will remember you and save you from your enemies.

Also on your happy days, at your special feasts, and at the start of each month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. They will remind your God of you. I am the LORD your God."
On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from above the Tent of the Covenant Law.
Then the people of Israel set out from the Sinai desert and travelled from place to place, until the cloud stopped in the desert of Paran.
This was the first time they set out at the LORD's command through Moses.
First, the army groups under the flag of Judah's camp set out. Nahshon son of Amminadab was over this army.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the army of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon was over the army of the tribe of Zebulun.
Then the Holy Tent was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.
Next, the army groups under the flag of Reuben's camp set out. Elizur son of Shedeur was over this army.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the army of the tribe of Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the army of the tribe of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The Holy Tent was set up again before they arrived.
Next, the army groups under the flag of Ephraim's camp set out. Elishama son of Ammihud was over this army.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the army of the tribe of Manasseh.
Abidan son of Gideoni was over the army of the tribe of Benjamin.
Last of all, the army groups under the flag of Dan's camp set out, guarding the back of all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over this army.
Pagiel son of Ochran was over the army of the tribe of Asher.
Ahira son of Enan was over the army of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the order in which the army groups of Israel marched when they set out.

Moses said to Hobab, son of Moses' father-in-law Reuel the Midianite, "We are setting out for the place the LORD said he would give us. Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
But Hobab answered, "No, I will not go. I am going back to my own land and my own people."
Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the desert, and you can be our guide.
If you come with us, we will share with you all the good things the LORD gives us."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and travelled for three days. The Covenant Box of the LORD went ahead of them during those three days, to find them a place to rest.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the Covenant Box set out, Moses said, "Rise up, LORD! Let your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate you run away from you!"
And whenever it stopped, he said, "Come back, LORD, to the many thousands of Israel."
The people began to complain about their troubles, and the LORD heard them. When he heard it, he became angry, and fire from the LORD burned among them and destroyed some of the edges of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
So that place was called Taberah, which means burning, because fire from the LORD had burned among them.
The mixed crowd of foreigners among them began to crave other food, and the people of Israel started crying again. They said, "If only we had meat to eat!
We remember the fish we ate for free in Egypt, and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now we have lost our appetite. We never see anything but this manna!"
The manna was like small coriander seeds and looked like pale yellow resin.
The people went around gathering it. They ground it in hand mills or crushed it with stones, then boiled it in pots or made it into flat loaves. It tasted like bread baked with olive oil.
At night, when the dew fell on the camp, the manna fell with it.
Moses heard all the families crying, each man at the door of his tent. The LORD became very angry, and Moses was upset.
Moses said to the LORD, "Why have you brought this trouble on me, your servant? What have I done to displease you, that you put the burden of all these people on me?
Did I give birth to all these people? Did I bring them into the world, that you tell me to carry them in my arms, like a nurse carries a baby, to the land you promised their ancestors?
Where can I get meat for all these people? They keep crying to me, 'Give us meat to eat!'
I cannot carry all these people by myself. The load is too heavy for me.
If this is how you are going to treat me, please kill me right now, if you care for me at all. Do not let me face my own ruin."
The LORD said to Moses, "Bring me seventy of Israel's leaders, men you know to be leaders and officials among the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.

I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will help you carry the burden of the people, so that you do not have to carry it alone.

Tell the people: Make yourselves holy and get ready for tomorrow, when you will eat meat. The LORD heard you crying, 'If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt!' So now the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.
You will not eat it for just one day, or two days, or five, or ten, or twenty days,
but for a whole month, until it comes out of your noses and you hate it. This is because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried to him, saying, 'Why did we ever leave Egypt?'"
But Moses said, "Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month!'
Would there be enough even if all the flocks and herds were killed for them? Would there be enough even if all the fish in the sea were caught for them?"
The LORD answered Moses, "Is my power too small? Now you will see whether what I say comes true or not."
So Moses went out and told the people what the LORD had said. He gathered seventy of their leaders and had them stand around the Tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy leaders. When the Spirit came on them, they prophesied, but they did not do it again.
Two men, Eldad and Medad, had stayed in the camp. They were on the list of leaders, but they had not gone out to the Tent. Yet the Spirit came on them too, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"
Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' helper since he was young, spoke up. "Moses, my master, stop them!"
But Moses answered, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his Spirit on all of them!"
Then Moses and the leaders of Israel went back to the camp.
Then the LORD sent a wind that brought quails in from the sea. It brought them down all around the camp, about a day's walk in every direction, piled about a metre deep on the ground.
All that day and night, and all the next day, the people went out and gathered quails. No one gathered less than about two thousand litres. Then they spread them out all around the camp to dry.
But while the meat was still in their mouths, before they had even chewed it, the LORD became angry with the people and struck them with a terrible disease.
So that place was called Kibroth Hattaavah, which means graves of craving, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
From Kibroth Hattaavah the people travelled to Hazeroth, and they stayed there.
Miriam and Aaron began to speak against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a woman from Cush.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn't he spoken through us too?" And the LORD heard what they said.
Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, "All three of you, come out to the Tent of Meeting." So the three of them went out.
The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the door of the Tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and they both stepped forward.
He said, "Listen to what I say. When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, show myself to him in visions and speak to him in dreams.
But it is not like that with my servant Moses. He is faithful in all my house.
With him I speak face to face, clearly and not in riddles. He even sees what the LORD looks like. So why were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
The LORD was very angry with them, and he left.
When the cloud lifted from above the Tent, Miriam's skin was suddenly covered with a disease, white like snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she had the skin disease.
He said to Moses, "Please, my master, do not punish us for this sin we have so foolishly done.
Do not let her be like a baby born dead, with half its flesh eaten away."
So Moses cried out to the LORD, "O God, please heal her!"
The LORD answered Moses, "If her father had spat in her face, would she not be in disgrace for seven days? Keep her outside the camp for seven days. After that she may be brought back."
So Miriam was kept outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought back.
After that, the people left Hazeroth and camped in the desert of Paran.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Send some men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the people of Israel. Send one leader from each of the ancestral tribes."
So Moses sent them out from the desert of Paran, as the LORD had commanded. All of them were leaders among the people of Israel.
These were their names: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur.
From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.
From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph.
From the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun.
From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu.
From the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi.
From the tribe of Manasseh, one of Joseph's tribes, Gaddi son of Susi.
From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.
From the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael.
From the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi.
From the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
When Moses sent them to explore Canaan, he said, "Go up through the Negev, the dry south land, and on into the hill country.
See what the land is like. Find out whether the people who live there are strong or weak, few or many.
Is the land they live in good or bad? Are their towns open camps or protected by walls?
Is the soil rich or poor? Are there trees on it or not? Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." It was the season for the first ripe grapes.
So they went up and explored the land, from the desert of Zin as far as Rehob, near the road to Hamath.
They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai lived, the descendants of Anak. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
When they came to the Valley of Eshcol, they cut off a branch with a single bunch of grapes. Two of them carried it on a pole between them. They also brought back some pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the Valley of Eshcol, which means bunch of grapes, because of the bunch the people of Israel cut there.
After forty days of exploring the land, they came back.
They came to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel at Kadesh, in the desert of Paran. They reported to them and to the whole community and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told Moses, "We went into the land where you sent us. It really is a land flowing with milk and honey! Here is some of its fruit.
But the people who live there are strong, and their towns have walls and are very large. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the Negev. The Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live near the sea and along the Jordan River."
Then Caleb quieted the people in front of Moses and said, "Let's go up right now and take the land. We can certainly do it!"
But the men who had gone with him said, "We cannot attack those people. They are stronger than we are."

So they spread a bad report among the people of Israel about the land they had explored. They said, "The land we explored destroys the people who live in it. All the people we saw there are very tall.
We even saw the Nephilim there, the descendants of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. Next to them we felt like grasshoppers, and that is how we looked to them."
That night the whole community cried out loudly, and the people wept.
All the people of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. The whole community said to them, "We wish we had died in Egypt, or even here in this desert!
Why is the LORD bringing us to this land, only to have us killed in battle? Our wives and children will be taken captive! Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
And they said to one another, "Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt."
Then Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground in front of the whole community of Israel gathered there.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of the men who had explored the land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole community of Israel, "The land we passed through and explored is a very, very good land.
If the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not turn against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land. We will swallow them up like bread. Their protection is gone, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!"
But the whole community talked about stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the Tent of Meeting to all the people of Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people treat me with no respect? How long will they refuse to trust me, even after all the miracles I have done among them?
I will strike them with a deadly disease and destroy them. Then I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they are."
But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear about it! By your power you brought these people out from among them.

And they will tell the people who live in this land. They have already heard that you, LORD, are with these people, that you are seen face to face, that your cloud stays over them, and that you go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you kill all these people at once, the nations who have heard about you will say,
'The LORD was not able to bring these people into the land he promised them, so he killed them in the desert.'
So now, Lord, please show how great your power is, just as you have said:

'The LORD is slow to become angry and full of faithful love. He forgives sin and rebellion. Yet he does not let the guilty go unpunished. He punishes children for the sins of their parents, to the third and fourth generation.'
Please forgive the sin of these people, because your faithful love is so great, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt until now."
The LORD answered, "I have forgiven them, as you asked.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD,
not one of these men will see the land. They saw my glory and the miracles I did in Egypt and in the desert, yet they have tested me ten times and have not obeyed me.
Not one of them will see the land I promised their ancestors. None of those who treated me with no respect will see it.
But my servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed me with all his heart. So I will bring him into the land he explored, and his descendants will own it.
Since the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and set out into the desert, along the road to the Red Sea."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"How long must I put up with this evil community that complains against me? I have heard the complaints of the people of Israel against me.
So tell them: 'As surely as I live, says the LORD, I will do to you exactly what I heard you say.
Your dead bodies will fall in this desert. Every one of you twenty years old or more who was counted, who complained against me,
will never enter the land where I promised to settle you. Only Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun will enter it.
You said your children would be taken captive. But I will bring them in, and they will enjoy the land you have rejected.
But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this desert.
Your children will wander like shepherds in this desert for forty years. They will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the desert.
For forty years, one year for each of the forty days you explored the land, you will suffer for your sins. Then you will know what it is like to have me against you.'
I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do these things to this whole evil community that has joined together against me. They will come to their end in this desert, and here they will die."
The men Moses had sent to explore the land came back and made the whole community complain against him by spreading a bad report about the land.
These men who spread the bad report about the land were struck down by a disease and died before the LORD.
Of all the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh stayed alive.
When Moses told all the people of Israel what the LORD had said, they were filled with sorrow.
Early the next morning they set out for the top of the hill country. They said, "We have sinned. Now we are ready to go to the place the LORD promised."
But Moses said, "Why are you disobeying the LORD's command? This will not succeed!
Do not go up, because the LORD is not with you. You will be beaten by your enemies.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will be killed in battle. Because you have turned away from following the LORD, he will not be with you."
But they dared to go up toward the top of the hill country anyway. Neither Moses nor the Covenant Box of the LORD left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and attacked them, and beat them all the way to Hormah.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: After you come into the land I am giving you as your home,

you will bring gifts made by fire to the LORD from your cattle or your flocks. It may be a burnt offering or another sacrifice, to keep a special promise, or as a freely given gift, or at your special feasts, as a smell that pleases the LORD.
Whoever brings his offering must also bring the LORD a grain offering of about one and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with about one litre of olive oil.
With each lamb for the burnt offering or other sacrifice, also prepare about one litre of wine as a drink offering.
With a ram, prepare a grain offering of about three kilograms of fine flour mixed with about one and a third litres of oil,
and about one and a third litres of wine as a drink offering. It will be a smell that pleases the LORD.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or other sacrifice, to keep a special promise or as a peace offering to the LORD,
bring with the bull a grain offering of about four and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with about two litres of oil.
Also bring about two litres of wine as a drink offering. It will be a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
This is what must be done for each bull, each ram, and each lamb or young goat.
Do this for each animal, however many you prepare.
Everyone born in the land must do these things in this way when bringing a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
If a foreigner is living among you, or anyone else who lives with you in the years to come, and he wants to bring a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD, he must do just as you do.
The community must have one rule for you and for the foreigner living among you. It is a rule forever for all your families to come. Foreigners and you are the same before the LORD.
The same laws and rules apply to you and to the foreigner living among you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you come into the land where I am taking you,
and you eat the food of the land, set some of it aside as a special gift to the LORD.
From the first of your dough, give a loaf as a special gift. Give it just as you give a special gift from the grain at the threshing place.
For all time to come, you must give the LORD a special gift from the first of your dough.
You may make a mistake and fail to keep some of these commands the LORD gave Moses,
any of the commands the LORD gave you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave them and on through all time to come.

If the whole community did this by mistake, without knowing it, the whole community must offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a smell that pleases the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering as the rules say, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest will make the whole community of Israel right with God, and they will be forgiven, because it was a mistake. They have brought the LORD their gift made by fire and their sin offering for their mistake.
The whole community of Israel will be forgiven, and so will the foreigners living among them, because all the people were part of the mistake.
If one person sins by mistake, he must bring a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest will make that person right with God before the LORD for the sin he did by mistake. When he has been made right with God, he will be forgiven.
The same rule applies to everyone who sins by mistake, whether born in Israel or a foreigner living among them.
But anyone who sins on purpose, in open defiance, whether born in the land or a foreigner, insults the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people.
He has treated the LORD's word with contempt and broken his command. That person must surely be cut off. His guilt stays on him."
While the people of Israel were in the desert, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
They kept him under guard, because it was not yet clear what should be done to him.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole community must stone him outside the camp."
So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: For all time to come, you must make tassels on the corners of your clothes, with a blue cord on each tassel.

These tassels will help you remember. When you see them, you will remember all the commands of the LORD and obey them. Then you will not follow the desires of your own heart and eyes, which lead you to be unfaithful to me.
So you will remember and obey all my commands, and you will be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."
Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, became proud. He was joined by Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, from the tribe of Reuben.
They rose up against Moses, together with two hundred fifty men of Israel, well-known leaders who had been chosen by the community.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is with them. So why do you put yourselves above the LORD's people?"
When Moses heard this, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

Then he said to Korah and all his followers, "In the morning the LORD will show who belongs to him and who is holy. He will let that person come near him. The one he chooses, he will bring near to himself.
So this is what you must do, Korah, you and all your followers: take incense pans.
Tomorrow, put fire and incense in them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. You Levites have gone too far!"
Moses also said to Korah, "Listen, you Levites!

Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the community and brought you near to himself? He lets you work at the LORD's Holy Tent and stand before the community to serve them.
He has brought you and all your fellow Levites near to himself. Now you want to be priests too?
It is really against the LORD that you and all your followers have joined together. Who is Aaron, that you complain against him?"
Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they said, "We will not come!
Is it not enough that you brought us out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the desert? Now you also want to make yourself our ruler!
You have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, or given us fields and vineyards to own. Do you think you can fool these men? We will not come!"
Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken even one donkey from them, and I have never done wrong to any of them."
Moses said to Korah, "Tomorrow you and all your followers must stand before the LORD, you and they, and Aaron too.
Each man must take his incense pan and put incense in it. Bring them before the LORD, two hundred fifty incense pans. You and Aaron must bring your pans as well."
So each man took his incense pan, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Korah gathered all his followers against them at the door of the Tent of Meeting. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole community.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Move away from these people, so that I can destroy them at once!"
But Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground and said, "O God, the God who gives breath to all living things, will you be angry with the whole community when only one man sins?"
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the community: 'Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'"
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the leaders of Israel followed him.
He warned the community, "Get away from the tents of these evil men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be destroyed because of all their sins."

So the people moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the doors of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children.
Then Moses said, "This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, and that it was not my own idea.
If these men die a natural death, as all people die, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD does something completely new, and the ground opens up and swallows them with everything they own, and they go down alive to the place of the dead, then you will know that these men have rejected the LORD."
As soon as Moses finished saying all this, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened up and swallowed them and their families, all of Korah's men, and everything they owned.
They went down alive to the place of the dead, with everything they had. The earth closed over them, and they disappeared from the community.
All the people of Israel around them heard their screams and ran away, shouting, "The earth is going to swallow us too!"
Then fire came out from the LORD and burned up the two hundred fifty men who were offering the incense.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, to take the incense pans out of the fire and scatter the burning coals far away, because the pans are holy.

These are the pans of the men who sinned at the cost of their lives. Hammer them into thin sheets to cover the altar, because they were offered before the LORD and have become holy. They will be a warning sign to the people of Israel."
So Eleazar the priest collected the bronze incense pans brought by the men who had been burned up, and had them hammered into a covering for the altar.

This was a reminder to the people of Israel that no one except a descendant of Aaron should come to burn incense before the LORD, or he would become like Korah and his followers. This was just as the LORD had told Eleazar through Moses.
But the next day the whole community of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. They said, "You have killed the LORD's people!"
When the community gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Get away from these people, so that I can destroy them at once!" And they bowed down with their faces to the ground.

Moses said to Aaron, "Take your incense pan, put fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Hurry to the community and make them right with God. The LORD's anger has broken out, and the deadly disease has started."
Aaron did what Moses said. He ran into the middle of the crowd, where the disease had already begun among the people. He put the incense on and made the people right with God.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the disease stopped.
Fourteen thousand seven hundred people died from the disease, besides those who had died because of Korah.
Then Aaron went back to Moses at the door of the Tent of Meeting, because the disease had stopped.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and get twelve walking sticks from them, one from the leader of each ancestral tribe. Write each leader's name on his stick.
On the stick for Levi, write Aaron's name. There must be one stick for the head of each ancestral tribe.
Put them in the Tent of Meeting in front of the Covenant Box, where I meet with you.
The stick of the man I choose will sprout buds. In this way I will put a stop to the constant complaining of the people of Israel against you."
So Moses spoke to the people of Israel, and their leaders gave him twelve sticks, one for each leader of an ancestral tribe. Aaron's stick was among them.
Moses placed the sticks before the LORD in the Tent of the Covenant Law.
The next day Moses went into the Tent of the Covenant Law, and he saw that Aaron's stick, which stood for the tribe of Levi, had sprouted. It had put out buds, opened flowers, and grown ripe almonds!
Moses brought all the sticks out from before the LORD and showed them to the people of Israel. They looked, and each leader took back his own stick.
The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's stick back in front of the Covenant Box. Keep it there as a warning to those who rebel, so that their complaining against me will stop and they will not die."
Moses did just as the LORD commanded him.
The people of Israel said to Moses, "We are going to die! We are lost, all of us are lost!
Anyone who even comes near the LORD's Holy Tent will die. Are we all going to die?"

The LORD said to Aaron, "You, your sons, and your family will be responsible for any wrong done against the holy place. You and your sons alone will be responsible for any wrong done in your work as priests.
Bring your relatives, the tribe of Levi, your father's tribe, to work with you. They will join you and help you while you and your sons serve in front of the Tent of the Covenant Law.
They will work under you and take care of the whole Tent. But they must not go near the holy tools or the altar, or both they and you will die.
They will join you and be responsible for the care of the Tent of Meeting, doing all the work there. No one else may come near you.
You will be responsible for the holy place and the altar, so that my anger will not fall on the people of Israel again.
I myself have chosen your relatives the Levites from among the people of Israel. They are a gift to you, given to the LORD, to do the work at the Tent of Meeting.

But only you and your sons may serve as priests, for everything at the altar and behind the curtain. I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift. Anyone else who comes near the holy place must be put to death."

Then the LORD said to Aaron, "I myself have put you in charge of the special gifts brought to me, all the holy gifts the people of Israel give me. I give them to you and your sons as your share forever, because you have been anointed.

Of the most holy gifts that are not burned, this part is yours: every gift they bring me, whether grain offerings, sin offerings, or guilt offerings. They are most holy and belong to you and your sons.
Eat them as most holy food. Every male may eat them. Treat them as holy.

This is also yours: the special gifts set aside from all the wave offerings of the people of Israel. I give them to you and your sons and daughters as your share forever. Everyone in your family who is clean may eat them.
I also give you all the best of the olive oil, the new wine, and the grain, the first part of the harvest that they give to the LORD.
All the first ripe crops of their land that they bring to the LORD will be yours. Everyone in your family who is clean may eat them.
Everything in Israel that is given completely to the LORD will be yours.
The firstborn of every person or animal offered to the LORD will be yours. But you must accept payment to buy back every firstborn son, and every firstborn of an unclean animal.
When they are one month old, they must be bought back for the set price of five pieces of silver, using the official weight of the holy place, which is twenty small weights.
But you must not buy back the firstborn of a cow, a sheep, or a goat. They are holy. Splash their blood on the altar and burn their fat as a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
Their meat will be yours, just like the breast that is waved and the right thigh are yours.

All the special gifts from the holy offerings that the people of Israel give to the LORD, I give to you and your sons and daughters as your share forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD, an agreement that will last, for you and your descendants."
The LORD said to Aaron, "You will not own any land in Israel or have any share among the people. I am your share and your inheritance among the people of Israel.
I have given the Levites the tenth of everything in Israel as their inheritance, in return for the work they do at the Tent of Meeting.
From now on, the other people of Israel must not come near the Tent of Meeting, or they will be guilty of sin and die.

Only the Levites will do the work at the Tent of Meeting, and they will be responsible for any wrongs against it. This is a rule forever for all your families to come. The Levites will not own any land among the people of Israel.

Instead, I have given the Levites as their inheritance the tenth that the people of Israel give as a special gift to the LORD. That is why I said, 'They will not own any land among the people of Israel.'"
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you receive from the people of Israel the tenth I have given you as your inheritance, you must give a tenth of that tenth as a special gift to the LORD.
Your gift will count for you as if it were grain from the threshing place or juice from the winepress.
In this way you too will give a special gift to the LORD from all the tenths you receive from the people of Israel. Give the LORD's share to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts you receive, you must give the best and holiest part as the LORD's special gift.
Tell the Levites: When you give the best part, the rest will count for you like the produce of the threshing place or the winepress.
You and your families may eat the rest anywhere. It is your pay for your work at the Tent of Meeting.
If you give the best part, you will not be guilty of sin because of it. But do not dishonour the holy gifts of the people of Israel, or you will die."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"This is a rule the LORD has commanded: Tell the people of Israel to bring you a red young cow with no marks or anything wrong with it, one that has never worn a yoke.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. It must be taken outside the camp and killed in front of him.
Eleazar the priest will take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Then the cow must be burned while he watches: its skin, its meat, its blood, and its dung must all be burned.
The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and red yarn and throw them into the fire where the cow is burning.
After that, the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Then he may come back into the camp, but he will be unclean until evening.
The man who burns the cow must also wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.

Then a man who is clean will gather up the cow's ashes and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They will be kept for the community of Israel to use in the water for washing away uncleanness. It is a sin offering.
The man who gathers up the ashes must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is a rule forever, for the people of Israel and for the foreigners living among them.
Anyone who touches a dead body will be unclean for seven days.
He must wash himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not wash himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a dead body and does not wash himself makes the LORD's Holy Tent unclean. That person must be cut off from Israel. Because the cleansing water was not sprinkled on him, he is unclean. His uncleanness stays on him.
This is the teaching for when someone dies in a tent: Anyone who goes into the tent, and anyone who is already in it, will be unclean for seven days.
Every open jar without a lid tied on it will be unclean.
Out in the open fields, anyone who touches someone killed with a sword, or someone who died naturally, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
To make the unclean person clean, put some ashes from the burned sin offering into a jar and pour fresh running water over them.

Then a man who is clean must take a hyssop branch, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent and everything in it, and the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who has touched a human bone, a person who was killed, someone who died, or a grave.

The clean man must sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and the seventh day. On the seventh day he will make him clean. Then the person being made clean must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and that evening he will be clean.

But anyone who is unclean and does not make himself clean must be cut off from the community, because he has made the LORD's holy place unclean. The cleansing water has not been sprinkled on him, so he is unclean.
This is a rule forever for them. The man who sprinkles the cleansing water must also wash his clothes, and anyone who touches the cleansing water will be unclean until evening.
Anything an unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."
In the first month the whole community of Israel arrived in the desert of Zin, and they stayed at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
There was no water for the community, so the people gathered against Moses and Aaron.
They argued with Moses and said, "We wish we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
Why did you bring the LORD's people into this desert? So that we and our animals would die here?
Why did you make us leave Egypt and bring us to this terrible place? There is no grain, no figs, no grapevines, and no pomegranates here. There is not even water to drink!"
Moses and Aaron left the crowd and went to the door of the Tent of Meeting. They bowed down with their faces to the ground, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD said to Moses,

"Take the walking stick, and you and your brother Aaron gather the community together. While they watch, speak to that rock, and it will pour out its water. In this way you will bring water out of the rock for the community and their animals to drink."
So Moses took the stick from its place before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the people in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?"
Then Moses raised his hand and hit the rock twice with his stick. Water poured out, plenty of it, and the community and their animals drank.
But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to show my holiness in front of the people of Israel, you will not lead this community into the land I am giving them."
This was the water of Meribah, which means arguing, because there the people of Israel argued with the LORD, and he showed them that he is holy.
From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom. They said, "This is what your brother Israel says: You know about all the hardships we have been through.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived there for many years. The Egyptians treated us and our ancestors cruelly.
But when we cried out to the LORD, he heard us and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are here at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your land.

Please let us pass through your country. We will not go through your fields or vineyards, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King's Highway and not turn to the right or the left until we have passed through your land."
But Edom answered, "You may not pass through here. If you try, we will come out and attack you with our swords."
The people of Israel replied, "We will stay on the main road. If we or our animals drink any of your water, we will pay for it. We only want to pass through on foot, nothing else."
But Edom answered again, "You may not pass through." Then Edom came out against them with a large and powerful army.
Since Edom refused to let Israel pass through their land, Israel turned away from them.
The whole community of Israel set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Aaron is going to die and join his people who have died. He will not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel, because both of you rebelled against my command at the water of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.
Take off Aaron's priestly clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will die there and join his people."
Moses did what the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor while the whole community watched.
Moses took off Aaron's clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. And Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole community learned that Aaron had died, all the people of Israel mourned for him for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that the people of Israel were coming along the road to Atharim. He attacked Israel and captured some of them.
Then Israel made a special promise to the LORD: "If you will hand these people over to us, we will completely destroy their towns."
The LORD listened to Israel and handed the Canaanites over to them. They completely destroyed them and their towns, so the place was called Hormah, which means destruction.
The people of Israel set out from Mount Hor along the road to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the way.
They spoke against God and against Moses: "Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in the desert? There is no bread and no water, and we hate this awful food!"
So the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people. They bit the people, and many of the Israelites died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We sinned when we spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a model of a poisonous snake and put it on a pole. Anyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole. Whenever someone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, he lived.
The people of Israel moved on and camped at Oboth.
Then they left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, in the desert facing Moab toward the sunrise.
From there they moved on and camped in the Zered Valley.
From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon River, in the desert that reaches into Amorite land. The Arnon is the border between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why the Book of the Wars of the LORD speaks of "Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slopes of the valleys that reach to the town of Ar and lie along the border of Moab."
From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing about it!
Sing about the well that the leaders dug, that the important men of the people dug with their royal sticks and walking sticks." From the desert they went on to Mattanah,
from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
From Bamoth they went to the valley in Moab, where the top of Mount Pisgah looks out over the wasteland.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, to say:
"Let us pass through your country. We will not go into any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King's Highway until we have passed through your land."
But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his land. He gathered his whole army and marched out into the desert to fight Israel. When he reached Jahaz, he attacked Israel.
But Israel defeated him in battle and took over his land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River, as far as the land of the Ammonites, because the Ammonite border was strongly protected.
Israel took all the Amorite towns and settled in them, including Heshbon and all its villages.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites. He had fought against the earlier king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon River.
That is why the poets say: "Come to Heshbon! Let the city of Sihon be rebuilt and made strong again.
For fire came out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's city. It burned up Ar in Moab, and the rulers of the hills by the Arnon.
How terrible for you, Moab! You are destroyed, you people who worship the god Chemosh! He has let his sons run away and his daughters be captured by Sihon, king of the Amorites.
But we have shot them down. Heshbon is destroyed all the way to Dibon. We have destroyed them as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to explore the town of Jazer. The Israelites captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
Then they turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, marched out with his whole army to fight them at Edrei.

But the LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon."
So they defeated Og, his sons, and his whole army, leaving no survivors, and they took over his land.
Then the people of Israel moved on and camped in the plains of Moab, along the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
The people of Moab were terrified because there were so many Israelites. Moab was filled with dread because of the people of Israel.
So the Moabites said to the leaders of Midian, "This crowd is going to eat up everything around us, like an ox eats up the grass in a field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to call Balaam son of Beor, who lived at Pethor near the Euphrates River, in his own native land. Balak's message said, "A whole nation has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the land, and they have settled next to me.

Please come now and put a curse on these people for me, because they are too strong for me. Then perhaps I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed."
The leaders of Moab and Midian set out, taking with them the payment for a fortune-teller. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak's message.
Balaam said to them, "Stay here tonight, and I will bring you back whatever answer the LORD gives me." So the Moabite leaders stayed with him.
God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message:
'A nation has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Then perhaps I will be able to fight them and drive them away.'"
But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. You must not put a curse on these people, because they are blessed."
The next morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's leaders, "Go back to your own country, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
So the Moabite leaders went back to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
Then Balak sent other leaders, more of them and more important than the first.
They came to Balaam and said, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: 'Please do not let anything stop you from coming to me.
I will reward you very richly and do whatever you say. Please come and put a curse on these people for me.'"
But Balaam answered Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me his palace full of silver and gold, I could not do anything, big or small, that goes against the command of the LORD my God.
Now stay here tonight as the others did, so I can find out what else the LORD will tell me."
That night God came to Balaam and said, "Since these men have come to call you, go with them. But do only what I tell you."
So Balaam got up in the morning, put the saddle on his donkey, and went with the Moabite leaders.
But God was angry that he was going, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to block his way. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a sword in his hand, she turned off the road into a field. Balaam beat her to make her go back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between two vineyards, with a wall on each side.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she pressed close to the wall, crushing Balaam's foot against it. So he beat her again.
Then the angel of the LORD went ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn, either to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam. He became furious and beat her with his stick.
Then the LORD made the donkey able to speak, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have beaten me these three times?"
Balaam answered the donkey, "You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your own donkey, which you have always ridden, right up to this day? Have I ever done this to you before?" "No," he said.
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a sword in his hand. So Balaam bowed low with his face to the ground.
The angel of the LORD asked him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I came to block your way, because the path you are on is wrong in my sight.
The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, I would certainly have killed you by now, but I would have let her live."
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not know you were standing in the road to stop me. Now, if you are not pleased, I will go back home."
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but say only what I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's leaders.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite town on the Arnon River, at the edge of his land.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send you an urgent message to come? Why didn't you come to me? Do you think I am not able to reward you well?"
Balaam answered Balak, "Well, I have come to you now. But do I have the power to say just anything? I must say only what God puts in my mouth."
Then Balaam went with Balak to Kiriath Huzoth.
Balak offered cattle and sheep as sacrifices, and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the leaders who were with him.
The next morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth Baal, the high places of Baal. From there Balaam could see part of the people of Israel.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me."
Balak did what Balaam said, and the two of them offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. I will tell you whatever he shows me." Then he went off to a bare hilltop.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have prepared seven altars, and on each one I have offered a bull and a ram."
The LORD put a message in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."
So Balaam went back and found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with all the leaders of Moab.
Then Balaam spoke his message: "Balak brought me from Aram. The king of Moab brought me from the eastern mountains. 'Come,' he said, 'put a curse on Jacob for me. Come, speak against Israel.'
But how can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I speak against those whom the LORD has not spoken against?
From the tops of the rocks I see them. From the hills I watch them. They are a people who live apart. They do not think of themselves as one of the nations.
Who can count the people of Jacob? They are as many as the specks of dust. Who can count even a quarter of Israel? Let me die like those who do right. Let my end be like theirs!"
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, but you have done nothing but bless them!"
Balaam answered, "Must I not be careful to say only what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Then Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will see only part of them, not all of them. From there, curse them for me."
So Balak took him to the field of Zophim on top of Mount Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there."
The LORD met Balaam, put a message in his mouth, and said, "Go back to Balak and give him this message."
So Balaam went back and found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with the leaders of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"
Then Balaam spoke his message: "Get up, Balak, and listen. Hear me, son of Zippor.
God is not a human being, that he should lie. He is not a man, that he should change his mind. Does he promise and not do it? Does he speak and not make it happen?
Look, I have been told to bless. God has blessed, and I cannot change it.
He has not found any wrong in Jacob, or seen any trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them. They shout to welcome him as their King.
God brought them out of Egypt. He is like the strength of a wild ox for them.
No magic spell can work against Jacob, and no fortune-telling can harm Israel. Now people will say about Jacob and Israel, 'Look what God has done!'
Look! The people rise up like a lioness. They get up like a lion. They will not rest until they have eaten their prey and drunk the blood of what they have killed."
Then Balak said to Balaam, "If you won't curse them, at least don't bless them!"
But Balaam answered Balak, "Didn't I tell you that I must do whatever the LORD says?"
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps God will be pleased to let you curse them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Mount Peor, which looks out over the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me."
Balak did what Balaam said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Now Balaam saw that the LORD was pleased to bless Israel, so he did not go to look for signs as he had done before. Instead, he turned and looked toward the desert.
When Balaam looked up, he saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came on him.
Then he spoke his message: "This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
the message of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the All-Powerful, who bows down with his eyes wide open:
How beautiful are your tents, people of Jacob, your homes, people of Israel!
They spread out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloe plants planted by the LORD, like cedar trees beside the water.
Water will flow from their buckets, and their seed will have plenty of water. Their king will be greater than Agag, and their kingdom will be lifted high.
God brought them out of Egypt. He is like the strength of a wild ox for them. They will eat up the nations that are their enemies. They will break their bones in pieces and strike them with arrows.
Like a lion they lie down to rest, like a lioness. Who would dare to wake them? May everyone who blesses you be blessed, and may everyone who curses you be cursed!"
Balak became very angry with Balaam. He clapped his hands in anger and said to him, "I called you to curse my enemies, but you have blessed them these three times!
Now get out of here and go home! I said I would reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from your reward."
Balaam answered Balak, "Didn't I tell the messengers you sent me,
'Even if Balak gave me his palace full of silver and gold, I could not go against the LORD's command to do anything good or bad on my own. I must say only what the LORD says'?
Now I am going back to my people. But come, let me warn you what these people will do to your people in the days to come."
Then he spoke his message: "This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
the message of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the All-Powerful, who bows down with his eyes wide open:

I see him, but not now. I look at him, but he is not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A king's royal stick will rise out of Israel. He will crush the heads of Moab, and the skulls of all the people of Sheth.
Edom will be conquered. Seir, his enemy, will be conquered, while Israel grows strong.
A ruler will come out of Jacob, and he will destroy the survivors of the city."
Then Balaam looked at Amalek and spoke this message: "Amalek was first among the nations, but in the end it will be destroyed forever."
Then he looked at the Kenites and spoke this message: "Your home is safe, like a nest set high in the rocks.
Yet you Kenites will be burned up, when Assyria takes you away as prisoners."
Then he spoke this message: "Oh, who can live when God does this?
Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus. They will crush Assyria and Eber, but they too will be destroyed forever."
Then Balaam got up and went back home, and Balak went on his way.
While Israel was staying at Shittim, the men began to have sexual relations with Moabite women.
These women invited them to the sacrifices for their gods. The people ate the sacrifices and bowed down to these gods.
So Israel joined in worshipping Baal of Peor, and the LORD became very angry with Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and kill them, and hang them up in broad daylight before the LORD, so that the LORD's fierce anger will turn away from Israel."
So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you must kill those of your men who have joined in worshipping Baal of Peor."
Just then, while Moses and the whole community of Israel were weeping at the door of the Tent of Meeting, an Israelite man brought a Midianite woman into his family's tent, right in front of them.
When Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest, saw this, he got up from the crowd and took a spear in his hand.
He followed the Israelite man into the tent and drove the spear through both of them, through the man and into the woman's body. Then the deadly disease among the people of Israel stopped.
But twenty-four thousand people had already died from the disease.
The LORD said to Moses,

"Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest, has turned my anger away from the people of Israel. He was as eager as I am to protect my honour among them, so I did not destroy the people of Israel in my anger.
So tell him that I am making my covenant of peace with him.

It will be a covenant for him and his descendants after him, that they will be priests forever. This is because he was eager to protect the honour of his God, and he made the people of Israel right with God."
The Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a family group in the tribe of Simeon.
The Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi, daughter of Zur, who was the head of a family group in Midian.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Treat the Midianites as enemies and attack them.

They treated you as enemies when they tricked you into worshipping Baal of Peor, and through Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, their relative, who was killed on the day of the disease that came because of Peor."
After the deadly disease, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest,
"Count the whole community of Israel by their families. Count all the men twenty years old or more who are able to go to war in Israel."
So on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan River across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke to the people. They said,
"Count all the men twenty years old or more, as the LORD commanded Moses." These were the people of Israel who came out of Egypt:
Reuben was Israel's oldest son. The clans that came from Reuben were: from Hanoch, the Hanochite clan; from Pallu, the Palluite clan;
from Hezron, the Hezronite clan; and from Carmi, the Carmite clan.
These were the clans of Reuben. The number counted was forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty.
Pallu's son was Eliab,

and Eliab's sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram, leaders chosen by the community, who rebelled against Moses and Aaron. They were among Korah's followers when they rebelled against the LORD.
The earth opened up and swallowed them along with Korah, and his followers died when the fire burned up two hundred fifty men. They became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The clans that came from Simeon were: from Nemuel, the Nemuelite clan; from Jamin, the Jaminite clan; from Jachin, the Jachinite clan;
from Zerah, the Zerahite clan; and from Shaul, the Shaulite clan.
These were the clans of Simeon. The number counted was twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The clans that came from Gad were: from Zephon, the Zephonite clan; from Haggi, the Haggite clan; from Shuni, the Shunite clan;
from Ozni, the Oznite clan; from Eri, the Erite clan;
from Arod, the Arodite clan; and from Areli, the Arelite clan.
These were the clans of Gad. The number counted was forty thousand five hundred.
Two of Judah's sons, Er and Onan, died in the land of Canaan.
The clans that came from Judah were: from Shelah, the Shelanite clan; from Perez, the Perezite clan; and from Zerah, the Zerahite clan.
The clans that came from Perez were: from Hezron, the Hezronite clan; and from Hamul, the Hamulite clan.
These were the clans of Judah. The number counted was seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The clans that came from Issachar were: from Tola, the Tolaite clan; from Puvah, the Punite clan;
from Jashub, the Jashubite clan; and from Shimron, the Shimronite clan.
These were the clans of Issachar. The number counted was sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The clans that came from Zebulun were: from Sered, the Seredite clan; from Elon, the Elonite clan; and from Jahleel, the Jahleelite clan.
These were the clans of Zebulun. The number counted was sixty thousand five hundred.
The clans that came from Joseph came through his sons Manasseh and Ephraim.
The clans that came from Manasseh were: from Machir, the Machirite clan. Machir was the father of Gilead, and from Gilead came the Gileadite clan.
These were the clans that came from Gilead: from Iezer, the Iezerite clan; from Helek, the Helekite clan;
from Asriel, the Asrielite clan; from Shechem, the Shechemite clan;
from Shemida, the Shemidaite clan; and from Hepher, the Hepherite clan.
Hepher's son Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These were the clans of Manasseh. The number counted was fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
The clans that came from Ephraim were: from Shuthelah, the Shuthelahite clan; from Becher, the Becherite clan; and from Tahan, the Tahanite clan.
From Shuthelah's son Eran came the Eranite clan.
These were the clans of Ephraim. The number counted was thirty-two thousand five hundred. All these were the clans that came from Joseph.
The clans that came from Benjamin were: from Bela, the Belaite clan; from Ashbel, the Ashbelite clan; from Ahiram, the Ahiramite clan;
from Shephupham, the Shuphamite clan; and from Hupham, the Huphamite clan.
The clans that came from Bela's sons Ard and Naaman were: from Ard, the Ardite clan; and from Naaman, the Naamite clan.
These were the clans of Benjamin. The number counted was forty-five thousand six hundred.
The clan that came from Dan was: from Shuham, the Shuhamite clan. These were the clans of Dan.
All the Shuhamite clans together numbered sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The clans that came from Asher were: from Imnah, the Imnite clan; from Ishvi, the Ishvite clan; and from Beriah, the Berite clan.
The clans that came from Beriah were: from Heber, the Heberite clan; and from Malchiel, the Malchielite clan.
Asher also had a daughter named Serah.
These were the clans of Asher. The number counted was fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The clans that came from Naphtali were: from Jahzeel, the Jahzeelite clan; from Guni, the Gunite clan;
from Jezer, the Jezerite clan; and from Shillem, the Shillemite clan.
These were the clans of Naphtali. The number counted was forty-five thousand four hundred.
The total number of the men of Israel counted was six hundred one thousand seven hundred thirty.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Divide the land among these tribes as their own, according to the number of names counted.
Give a larger share of land to a larger tribe and a smaller share to a smaller tribe. Each tribe will receive land according to the number of people counted.
But the land must be divided by casting lots. Each ancestral tribe will receive its share by the names of their tribes.
