Each share will be divided by lot among the larger and smaller tribes."
These were the clans of the Levites that were counted: from Gershon, the Gershonite clan; from Kohath, the Kohathite clan; and from Merari, the Merarite clan.
These were also Levite clans: the Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, and the Korahite clan. Kohath was the father of Amram.
Amram's wife was Jochebed, a descendant of Levi, born into Levi's family in Egypt. She gave Amram two sons, Aaron and Moses, and a daughter, their sister Miriam.
Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered the LORD a fire that was not allowed.
The number of Levite males one month old or more was twenty-three thousand. They were not counted with the rest of the people of Israel, because they were not given any land among them.
These are the people counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, when they counted the people of Israel on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
Not one of them had been among those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest in the Sinai desert.
For the LORD had said about those people, "They will all die in the desert." Not one of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The daughters of Zelophehad came forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. His daughters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole community at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and they said,
"Our father died in the desert. He was not one of Korah's followers who joined together against the LORD. He died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father's name disappear from his clan just because he had no son? Give us land among our father's relatives."
So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
And the LORD said to Moses,
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right. You must give them land among their father's relatives as their own. Give them their father's share.
Tell the people of Israel: If a man dies and has no son, give his land to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, give his land to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give his land to his father's brothers.
If his father had no brothers, give his land to the closest relative in his clan, and that person will own it. This is a rule and a law for the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain in the Abarim range and look at the land I have given the people of Israel.
After you have seen it, you too will die and join your people who have died, just as your brother Aaron did.
For when the community argued with me in the desert of Zin, both of you disobeyed my command to show my holiness to them at the water." This was the water of Meribah at Kadesh, in the desert of Zin.
Moses said to the LORD,
"LORD, you are the God who gives breath to all living things. Please appoint a man over this community
who will lead them out to battle and bring them back home, so that the LORD's people will not be like sheep without a shepherd."
The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man who has the Spirit in him, and put your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole community, and appoint him as leader while they watch.
Give him some of your authority, so that the whole community of Israel will obey him.

He will stand before Eleazar the priest, who will ask for the LORD's decisions for him by using the Urim. At his command, Joshua and all the people of Israel, the whole community, will go out and come in."
Moses did what the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole community.
He put his hands on him and appointed him as leader, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Give the people of Israel this command: Make sure you bring me my offerings at their set times, my food for the gifts made by fire, as a smell that pleases me.
Tell them: This is the gift made by fire that you must bring to the LORD: two one-year-old male lambs with nothing wrong with them, every day, as a regular burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at sunset.
With each one, bring a grain offering of about one and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with about one litre of oil from pressed olives.
This is the regular burnt offering that was set up at Mount Sinai, a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD.
With each lamb, bring a drink offering of about one litre of strong drink. Pour it out to the LORD in the holy place.
Offer the second lamb at sunset, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
On the Sabbath day, offer two one-year-old male lambs with nothing wrong with them, with a grain offering of about three kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the first day of every month, bring the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With each bull, bring a grain offering of about four and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil. With the ram, bring about three kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil.
With each lamb, bring about one and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil. This is a burnt offering, a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD.

Their drink offerings must be about two litres of wine with each bull, about one and a third litres with the ram, and about one litre with each lamb. This is the burnt offering for every month of the year.
Also offer one male goat to the LORD as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
The LORD's Passover is on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of that month, a feast begins. For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
Bring the LORD a gift made by fire, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With them bring a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about four and a half kilograms with each bull and about three kilograms with the ram.
With each of the seven lambs, bring about one and a half kilograms.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering to make you right with God.
Offer these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering.
Do this every day for seven days. It is food for the gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD. Offer it in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
On the day of the first harvest, when you bring the LORD an offering of new grain at the Feast of Weeks, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
Bring a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, as a smell that pleases the LORD.
With them bring a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about four and a half kilograms with each bull, about three kilograms with the ram,
and about one and a half kilograms with each of the seven lambs.
Also bring one male goat to make you right with God.
Offer these with their drink offerings, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. Make sure the animals have nothing wrong with them.
On the first day of the seventh month, have a holy gathering and do no regular work. It is a day for you to blow the trumpets.
Bring a burnt offering as a smell that pleases the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With them bring a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about four and a half kilograms with the bull, about three kilograms with the ram,
and about one and a half kilograms with each of the seven lambs.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering to make you right with God.

These are in addition to the burnt offering for the new month with its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings, as the rules say. They are a gift made by fire, a smell that pleases the LORD.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, have a holy gathering. Go without food and do no work at all.
Bring the LORD a burnt offering as a smell that pleases him: one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With them bring a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about four and a half kilograms with the bull, about three kilograms with the ram,
and about one and a half kilograms with each of the seven lambs.

Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the sin offering for making the people right with God, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, have a holy gathering and do no regular work. Celebrate a feast to the LORD for seven days.
Bring a burnt offering, a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With them bring a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about four and a half kilograms with each of the thirteen bulls, about three kilograms with each of the two rams,
and about one and a half kilograms with each of the fourteen lambs.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the second day, offer twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the third day, offer eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the fourth day, offer ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the fifth day, offer nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the sixth day, offer eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the seventh day, offer seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bulls, rams, and lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the eighth day, have a special gathering and do no regular work.
Bring a burnt offering, a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD: one bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with nothing wrong with them.
With the bull, the ram, and the lambs, bring their grain offerings and drink offerings, the right amount for the number of animals, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

Offer these to the LORD at your special feasts. They are in addition to the offerings you bring to keep a promise and your freely given gifts, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings."
Moses told the people of Israel everything the LORD had commanded him.
Moses said to the leaders of the tribes of Israel, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
When a man makes a special promise to the LORD, or swears an oath that binds him to do something, he must not break his word. He must do everything he said.
When a young woman still living in her father's house makes a promise to the LORD or binds herself to do something,
and her father hears about her promise or her pledge but says nothing to her, then all her promises and every pledge she made must be kept.
But if her father forbids it on the day he hears about it, none of her promises or pledges have to be kept. The LORD will forgive her, because her father stopped her.
If she gets married while she is still bound by a promise, or by a careless pledge she made,
and her husband hears about it but says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her promises and pledges must be kept.
But if her husband forbids it on the day he hears about it, he cancels the promise she made and the careless pledge she spoke. The LORD will forgive her.
Any promise or pledge made by a widow or a divorced woman must be kept.
If a married woman makes a promise or binds herself with an oath while living in her husband's house,
and her husband hears about it but says nothing to her and does not forbid it, then all her promises and every pledge she made must be kept.
But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears about them, then none of the promises or pledges she spoke have to be kept. Her husband has cancelled them, and the LORD will forgive her.
Her husband may allow or cancel any promise she makes, and any pledge to go without things.
But if her husband says nothing to her about it from one day to the next, then he has allowed all her promises and pledges. He has agreed to them by saying nothing on the day he heard about them.
If he cancels them some time after he hears about them, he will carry the blame for her broken promise."
These are the rules the LORD gave Moses about a man and his wife, and about a father and his young daughter still living in his house.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Pay back the Midianites for what they did to the people of Israel. After that you will die and join your people."
So Moses said to the people, "Prepare some of your men for war, so they can go against Midian and carry out the LORD's punishment on them.
Send one thousand men from each of the tribes of Israel to fight."
So one thousand men were chosen from each tribe from the many thousands of Israel, twelve thousand men ready for battle.
Moses sent them to war, one thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas took with him things from the holy place and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every man.
Among those killed were the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The people of Israel captured the Midianite women and children, and took all their cattle, flocks, and goods as plunder.
They burned all the towns where the Midianites lived, and all their camps.
They took all the plunder and everything they had captured, both people and animals.
They brought the captives, the animals, and the plunder to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the community of Israel at their camp on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went out of the camp to meet them.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had come back from the battle.
He asked them, "Have you let all the women live?
They are the ones who followed Balaam's advice and led the people of Israel to be unfaithful to the LORD in what happened at Peor. That is why the disease struck the LORD's people.
Now kill every boy, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But save for yourselves every girl who has never slept with a man.
All of you who have killed anyone or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days you must make yourselves and your captives clean.
Also make clean every piece of clothing, and everything made of leather, goat hair, or wood."
Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, "This is the rule from the law that the LORD gave Moses:
Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, lead,

and anything else that can stand the heat, must be passed through fire, and then it will be clean. But it must also be made clean with the cleansing water. Whatever cannot stand the heat must be passed through the water.
On the seventh day, wash your clothes, and you will be clean. Then you may come into the camp."
The LORD said to Moses,
"You, Eleazar the priest, and the family leaders of the community must count all the people and animals that were captured.
Divide them into two equal parts: one for the soldiers who went into battle and one for the rest of the community.
From the soldiers' half, set apart a share for the LORD: one out of every five hundred, whether people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep and goats.
Take this from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's special gift.

From the half that belongs to the people of Israel, take one out of every fifty, whether people, cattle, donkeys, sheep and goats, or other animals. Give them to the Levites, who take care of the LORD's Holy Tent."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
The plunder left from what the soldiers had taken was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep and goats,
seventy-two thousand cattle,
sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand women who had never slept with a man.
The half that belonged to the soldiers was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep and goats,
and the LORD's share of these was six hundred seventy-five.
There were thirty-six thousand cattle, and the LORD's share was seventy-two.
There were thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, and the LORD's share was sixty-one.
There were sixteen thousand people, and the LORD's share was thirty-two.
Moses gave the LORD's share as a special gift to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The other half belonged to the people of Israel, the half that Moses had set apart from the soldiers' share.
The community's half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep and goats,
thirty-six thousand cattle,
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand people.
From the people of Israel's half, Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals, as the LORD had commanded him. He gave them to the Levites, who took care of the LORD's Holy Tent.
Then the officers over the army units, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, came to Moses.
They said to him, "We, your servants, have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one man is missing.
So we have brought the LORD a gift of the gold jewellery each of us found: arm bands, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces. We bring them to make ourselves right with the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted the gold from them, all of it made into jewellery.
All the gold that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds gave as a special gift to the LORD weighed sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting, so that the LORD would remember the people of Israel.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad had very large herds and flocks. They saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were good places for animals.
So the people of Gad and Reuben came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community, and said,
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
the land the LORD conquered for the community of Israel, is good land for animals, and we, your servants, have many animals."
They said, "If you are pleased with us, let this land be given to us, your servants, as our own. Do not make us cross the Jordan River."
Moses said to the people of Gad and Reuben, "Should your fellow Israelites go to war while you sit here?
Why are you trying to discourage the people of Israel from crossing over into the land the LORD has given them?
That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to look at the land.
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and then they discouraged the people of Israel from going into the land the LORD had given them.
The LORD was angry that day, and he made this promise:
'Because they did not follow me with all their hearts, not one of the men twenty years old or more who came out of Egypt will see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Only Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun will see it, because they followed the LORD with all their hearts.'
The LORD was angry with Israel, and he made them wander in the desert for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in his sight had died.
And now here you are, a new brood of sinners, taking your fathers' place and making the LORD even angrier with Israel!
If you turn away from following him, he will leave all these people in the desert again, and you will be the cause of their destruction."
Then they came up to Moses and said, "We want to build pens here for our animals and towns for our children.

But we ourselves will arm ourselves and lead the people of Israel into battle until we have brought them to their own land. Meanwhile our children will live in towns with strong walls, safe from the people of the land.
We will not come back to our homes until every Israelite has received his own land.
We will not take any land with them on the other side of the Jordan, because we have received our land here on the east side of the Jordan."
Moses said to them, "If you will do this, if you will arm yourselves for battle before the LORD,
and all your armed men cross the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven out his enemies ahead of him,
and the land is conquered before the LORD, then you may come back. You will have done your duty to the LORD and to Israel, and this land will be yours before the LORD.
But if you do not do this, you will be sinning against the LORD, and you can be sure your sin will catch up with you.
Build towns for your children and pens for your sheep, but do what you have promised."
The people of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "We, your servants, will do as you, our master, command.
Our children, our wives, our flocks, and all our animals will stay here in the towns of Gilead.
But all of us, your servants, every man armed for war, will cross over to fight before the LORD, just as you, our master, have said."
So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the family leaders of the tribes of Israel.

He said to them, "If the people of Gad and Reuben, every man armed for battle, cross the Jordan with you before the LORD, and the land is conquered for you, then give them the land of Gilead as their own.
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they must take their share of land with you in Canaan."
The people of Gad and Reuben answered, "We, your servants, will do what the LORD has said.
We will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the land we own will be on this side of the Jordan."

So Moses gave the people of Gad and Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan. He gave them the whole land with its towns and the land around them.
The people of Gad rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran as towns with strong walls, and they built pens for their sheep.
The people of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo, and Baal Meon, whose names were changed, and Sibmah. They gave new names to the towns they rebuilt.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
So Moses gave Gilead to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settled there.
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, captured some villages and called them Havvoth Jair, which means villages of Jair.
Nobah captured Kenath and the villages around it, and called it Nobah after his own name.
These are the stages of the journey of the people of Israel, when they came out of Egypt in their army groups, led by Moses and Aaron.
At the LORD's command, Moses wrote down the places where they started each stage of their journey. These are the stages, from one starting place to the next.
The people of Israel set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover. They marched out boldly while all the Egyptians watched,
as the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn sons, whom the LORD had struck down. The LORD had also judged their gods.
The people of Israel left Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They left Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the desert.
They left Etham, turned back to Pi Hahiroth, east of Baal Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
They left Pi Hahiroth and walked through the middle of the sea into the desert. After travelling three days in the desert of Etham, they camped at Marah.
They left Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there.
They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They left the Red Sea and camped in the desert of Sin.
They left the desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They left Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They left Rephidim and camped in the Sinai desert.
They left the Sinai desert and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
They left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez.
They left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.
They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
They left Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.
They left Bene Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.
They left Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.
They left Ezion Geber and camped at Kadesh, in the desert of Zin.
They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
At the LORD's command, Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor, and he died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt.
Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the people of Israel were coming.
They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
They left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, on the border of Moab.
They left Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad.
They left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim.
They left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the Abarim mountains, near Nebo.
They left the Abarim mountains and camped on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan River across from Jericho.
There on the plains of Moab they camped along the Jordan, from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim.
On the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you must drive out all the people who live in the land ahead of you. Destroy all their carved stone idols and their metal statues, and tear down all their places of worship on the hills.
Take over the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to own.

Divide the land among your clans by casting lots. Give a larger share to a larger clan and a smaller share to a smaller clan. Whatever land the lot falls on for each clan will be theirs. Divide it among your ancestral tribes.

But if you do not drive out the people who live in the land, those you allow to stay will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will cause you trouble in the land where you live.
And then I will do to you what I planned to do to them."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Give the people of Israel this command: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will be given to you as your own. These are its borders:
Your southern side will include part of the desert of Zin, along the border of Edom. On the east, your southern border will start at the south end of the Dead Sea.
It will turn south of Scorpion Pass, continue on to Zin, and go south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it will go on to Hazar Addar and over to Azmon.
From Azmon it will turn toward the stream on the border of Egypt and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
Your western border will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. This will be your border on the west.
For your northern border, draw a line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor,
and from Mount Hor to the road into Hamath. The border will then go on to Zedad,
continue to Ziphron, and end at Hazar Enan. This will be your border on the north.
For your eastern border, draw a line from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
The border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. From there it will go along the slopes east of Lake Galilee.
Then the border will go down along the Jordan River and end at the Dead Sea. This will be your land, with these borders all around it."
Moses gave the people of Israel this command: "This is the land you will divide among yourselves by casting lots. The LORD has commanded that it be given to the nine and a half tribes.
For the tribes of Reuben and Gad, family by family, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received their land.
These two and a half tribes have received their land on the east side of the Jordan, across from Jericho, toward the sunrise."
The LORD said to Moses,
"These are the names of the men who will divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Also choose one leader from each tribe to help divide the land.
These are their names: From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud.
From the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon.
From the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli.
From the sons of Joseph: from the tribe of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod,
and from the tribe of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
From the tribe of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach.
From the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan.
From the tribe of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi.
From the tribe of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud."
These are the men the LORD commanded to divide the land of Canaan among the people of Israel.
On the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses,
"Command the people of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from the land they will own. Also give the Levites the pasture land around these towns.
The towns will be their homes, and the pasture land will be for their cattle, their flocks, and all their other animals.
The pasture land around each town you give the Levites must reach out about four hundred fifty metres from the town wall in every direction.

Outside the town, measure about nine hundred metres on the east side, nine hundred on the south side, nine hundred on the west side, and nine hundred on the north side, with the town in the middle. This will be their pasture land.
Six of the towns you give the Levites will be towns of safety, where a person who has killed someone may run for protection. Besides these, give them forty-two other towns.
In all, give the Levites forty-eight towns, together with their pasture land.

The towns you give the Levites will come from the land of the people of Israel. Take more towns from the larger tribes and fewer from the smaller tribes. Each tribe must give some of its towns to the Levites, according to the size of its land."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
choose some towns to be your towns of safety. A person who kills someone by accident may run there for protection.
These towns will be a safe place from the relative who wants to pay back the killing, so that the person accused of killing will not die before he stands trial before the community.
The six towns you give will be your towns of safety.
Give three towns on the east side of the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. They will be towns of safety.
These six towns will be places of safety for the people of Israel and for foreigners and visitors living among them. Anyone who kills someone by accident may run there.
But if someone strikes another person with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone has a stone in his hand that could kill, and he strikes another person and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone has a wooden object in his hand that could kill, and he strikes another person and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
The relative who pays back the killing must put the murderer to death himself. When he finds him, he must put him to death.
If someone pushes another person because he hates him, or throws something at him on purpose from a hiding place, so that he dies,

or if he hits him with his fist out of hatred, so that he dies, the one who struck him must be put to death. He is a murderer. The relative who pays back the killing must put the murderer to death when he finds him.
But someone may suddenly push another person without hating him, or throw something at him without planning it,
or, without seeing him, drop a stone on him that is big enough to kill, so that he dies. He was not his enemy and did not mean to harm him.
Then the community must judge between the one who killed and the relative who wants to pay back the killing, following these rules.

The community must protect the one accused of killing from the relative who wants revenge, and send him back to the town of safety where he ran. He must stay there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the one accused of killing ever goes outside the borders of the town of safety where he ran,
and the relative finds him outside the town and kills him, the relative will not be guilty of murder.
The one accused should have stayed in his town of safety until the high priest died. Only after the high priest's death may he go back to his own land.
These are rules and laws for you and for all your families to come, wherever you live.
Anyone who kills a person must be put to death as a murderer only on the word of witnesses. No one may be put to death on the word of just one witness.
Do not accept payment to spare the life of a murderer who deserves to die. He must be put to death.
And do not accept payment to let someone who ran to a town of safety go back and live on his own land before the high priest dies.

Do not make the land where you live unclean. Killing makes the land unclean, and nothing can make the land right with God after a person has been killed, except the death of the one who did the killing.
Do not make the land where you live unclean, the land where I live, for I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel."

The family leaders of the clan of Gilead came forward. Gilead was the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from the clans of Joseph's descendants. They spoke to Moses and the leaders, the heads of the families of Israel.
They said, "Sir, the LORD commanded you to divide the land among the people of Israel by casting lots. He also commanded you to give the land of our relative Zelophehad to his daughters.
But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, their land will be taken away from our family land and added to the land of the tribe they marry into. So our share will become smaller.
And when the Year of Jubilee comes for the people of Israel, their land will be added to the tribe they married into, and it will be taken away for good from the land of our ancestral tribe."
So at the LORD's command, Moses gave the people of Israel this order: "What the tribe of Joseph's descendants is saying is right.
This is what the LORD commands about the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry anyone they like, as long as they marry within a clan of their father's tribe.
Land in Israel must not pass from one tribe to another. Every Israelite must keep the land that belongs to the tribe of his ancestors.
Every daughter who receives land in any tribe of Israel must marry someone from a clan of her father's tribe. In this way every Israelite will keep the land of his ancestors.
No land may pass from one tribe to another, for each tribe of Israel must keep its own land."
So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Zelophehad's daughters, Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, married their cousins on their father's side.
They married into the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their land stayed in their father's clan and tribe.
These are the commands and laws that the LORD gave the people of Israel through Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
Deut: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel on the east side of the Jordan River, in the desert, in the Jordan Valley across from Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It takes eleven days to travel from Mount Sinai to Kadesh Barnea by the road through the hill country of Seir.
On the first day of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year, Moses told the people of Israel everything the LORD had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
There, east of the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain God's teaching. He said:
"When we were at Mount Sinai, the LORD our God said to us, 'You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Break camp and move on. Go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all the places around it: the Jordan Valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Negev in the south, and the coast. Go into the land of the Canaanites and to Lebanon, as far as the great Euphrates River.
Look, I have given you this land. Go in and take the land the LORD promised to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.'"
At that time I said to you, "I cannot carry the load of leading you all by myself.
The LORD your God has made you grow in number, and today you are as many as the stars in the sky.
May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times more, and bless you as he promised!
But how can I carry all your problems, your burdens, and your arguments by myself?
Choose some wise men with understanding, who are respected in your tribes, and I will make them your leaders."
You answered me, "What you have said is a good idea."

So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and made them your leaders. They were put in charge of groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, and ten, and served as officials for your tribes.
At that time I commanded your judges: "Listen to the cases between your people and judge fairly, whether the case is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a foreigner living among you.

When you judge, do not take sides. Listen to the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because the judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case that is too hard for you, and I will hear it."
At that time I told you everything you should do.
Then, as the LORD our God commanded us, we left Mount Sinai and went through that huge and terrible desert you saw, along the road to the hill country of the Amorites, and we came to Kadesh Barnea.
I said to you, "You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
Look, the LORD your God has given you the land. Go up and take it, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, told you. Do not be afraid or lose heart."
Then all of you came to me and said, "Let's send men ahead of us to explore the land for us. They can tell us which road to take and which towns we will come to."
The idea seemed good to me, so I chose twelve of your men, one from each tribe.
They went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.
They took some of the fruit of the land and brought it down to us. They reported, "The land the LORD our God is giving us is a good land."
But you refused to go up. You rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
You complained in your tents and said, "The LORD must hate us. He brought us out of Egypt just to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us.

Where can we go? Our brothers have made us lose heart. They say, 'The people there are stronger and taller than we are. Their towns are large, with walls up to the sky. We even saw the Anakim there, the giants!'"
Then I said to you, "Do not be terrified or afraid of them.
The LORD your God is going ahead of you, and he will fight for you, just as you saw him do for you in Egypt.
And in the desert you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a father carries his son, all the way until you reached this place."
But even after this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
who went ahead of you on your journey to find places for you to camp. He showed you the way to go with fire by night and a cloud by day.
When the LORD heard what you said, he was angry and made this solemn promise:
"Not one of the people of this evil generation will see the good land I promised to give your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it. I will give him and his descendants the land he walked on, because he followed the LORD with all his heart."
Because of you, the LORD was angry with me too, and he said, "You will not enter the land either.
But your helper, Joshua son of Nun, will enter it. Encourage him, because he will lead Israel to take the land as their own.
And your little children, the ones you said would be taken captive, who are too young to know right from wrong, will enter the land. I will give it to them, and they will own it.
But as for you, turn around and go back into the desert, along the road to the Red Sea."

Then you said to me, "We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us." So every one of you put on his weapons, thinking it would be easy to go up into the hill country.
But the LORD said to me, "Tell them, 'Do not go up and fight, because I will not be with you. Your enemies will defeat you.'"
So I told you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the LORD's command and proudly marched up into the hill country.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you. They chased you like a swarm of bees and beat you down from Seir all the way to Hormah.
You came back and wept before the LORD, but he would not listen to you or pay attention to you.
So you stayed at Kadesh for a long time, all the time that you stayed there.
Then we turned back and set out into the desert along the road to the Red Sea, as the LORD had told me. For a long time we wandered around the hill country of Seir.
Then the LORD said to me,
"You have wandered around this hill country long enough. Now turn north.
Give the people these orders: You are about to pass through the land of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, but be very careful.
Do not start a fight with them, because I will not give you any of their land, not even enough to put your foot on. I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his own.
Pay them with money for the food you eat and for the water you drink."

The LORD your God has blessed everything you have done. He has watched over you as you travelled through this huge desert. For these forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.

So we passed by our relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. We left the Jordan Valley road that comes up from Elath and Ezion Geber, and we turned and travelled along the desert road to Moab.
The LORD said to me, "Do not trouble the Moabites or start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land, because I have given the town of Ar to the descendants of Lot as their own."
Long ago the Emim lived there. They were a strong people, many in number, and as tall as the Anakim.
Like the Anakim, they were known as Rephaim, but the Moabites called them Emim.
The Horites used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out. They destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land the LORD gave them as their own.
The LORD said, "Now get up and cross the Zered Valley." So we crossed the Zered Valley.

Thirty-eight years passed from the time we left Kadesh Barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley. By then that whole generation of fighting men had died out of the camp, as the LORD had sworn would happen.
The LORD's hand was against them until he had completely removed them from the camp.
When the last of the fighting men among the people had died,
the LORD said to me,
"Today you will pass by Ar, on the border of Moab.

When you come near the land of the Ammonites, do not trouble them or start a fight with them. I will not give you any of the Ammonites' land, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their own."
That land was also known as a land of the Rephaim, who used to live there. The Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
They were a strong people, many in number, and as tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them ahead of the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place.
The LORD had done the same for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. He destroyed the Horites ahead of them, and they drove them out and have lived in their place to this day.
And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorim, who came from Crete and settled in their place.
"Now get up and cross the Arnon Valley. Look, I am handing over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take it, and go to war against him.
Starting today, I will make all the nations under heaven terrified and afraid of you. When they hear about you, they will tremble and shake with fear because of you."
From the desert of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with an offer of peace. They said,
"Let us pass through your land. We will stay on the main road and not turn off to the right or the left.
Sell us food to eat and water to drink, and we will pay you with money. Only let us pass through on foot,
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar have done. Let us pass until we cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us."
But Sihon, king of Heshbon, would not let us pass through. The LORD your God made him stubborn and his heart hard, so that he could hand him over to you, as he has now done.
The LORD said to me, "Look, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Begin now to take over his land as your own."
Then Sihon and his whole army came out to fight us at Jahaz.
But the LORD our God handed him over to us, and we defeated him, his sons, and his whole army.
At that time we captured all his towns and completely destroyed them, the men, women, and children. We left no survivors.
We kept only the animals and the goods from the towns we had captured as plunder for ourselves.
From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the valley itself, all the way to Gilead, no town had walls too high for us. The LORD our God gave us all of them.
But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, the land along the Jabbok River, or the towns in the hill country, or any place the LORD our God had told us not to go.
Next we turned and went up the road toward Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out with his whole army to fight us at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, "Do not be afraid of him. I have handed him over to you, with his whole army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God also handed over to us Og, king of Bashan, and his whole army. We defeated them and left no survivors.
At that time we captured all his towns. There was not one of their towns that we did not take: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, Og's kingdom in Bashan.
All these towns had high walls with gates and bars, and there were also many villages without walls.
We completely destroyed them, as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon. We destroyed every town, the men, women, and children.
But we kept all the animals and the goods from the towns as plunder for ourselves.
So at that time we took from these two Amorite kings the land east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
The people of Sidon call Mount Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.
We took all the towns on the high plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns in Og's kingdom in Bashan.

Og, king of Bashan, was the last of the Rephaim, the giants. His bed was made of iron. It is still in the Ammonite city of Rabbah. It was about four metres long and nearly two metres wide, by the usual measure.
Of the land we took over at that time, I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the land north of Aroer by the Arnon Valley, with half the hill country of Gilead and its towns.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og's kingdom, to half the tribe of Manasseh. The whole region of Argob in Bashan used to be known as a land of the Rephaim.

Jair, from the tribe of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He named these villages of Bashan after himself, Havvoth Jair, and they are still called that today.
I gave Gilead to Machir.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the land from Gilead down to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
Their land also included the Jordan Valley, with the Jordan River as its border, from Lake Galilee down to the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you: "The LORD your God has given you this land to own. But all your fighting men must cross over armed, ahead of your fellow Israelites.
Your wives, your children, and your animals, and I know you have many animals, may stay in the towns I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your fellow Israelites as he has to you, and they too take over the land the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. After that, each of you may go back to the land I have given you."
At that time I commanded Joshua: "You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you will go into.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God himself will fight for you."
At that time I begged the LORD,
"Sovereign LORD, you have only begun to show me, your servant, how great and powerful you are. What god in heaven or on earth can do the great and mighty things you do?
Please let me cross over and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan, that fine hill country and Lebanon."
But because of you, the LORD was angry with me and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, "That is enough! Do not speak to me about this again.
Go up to the top of Mount Pisgah and look west, north, south, and east. Look at the land with your own eyes, because you will not cross the Jordan.
But appoint Joshua as leader. Encourage him and make him strong, because he will lead these people across, and he will help them take over the land you will see."
So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.
Now, Israel, listen to the rules and laws I am teaching you. Obey them, so that you may live and go in and take over the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Do not add anything to what I command you, and do not take anything away from it. Just obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
You saw with your own eyes what the LORD did at Baal Peor. The LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed the god Baal of Peor.
But all of you who held on to the LORD your God are still alive today.
Look, I have taught you rules and laws, just as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you will obey them in the land you are going to take over.

Obey them carefully, for this will show the nations how wise and understanding you are. When they hear about all these rules, they will say, "This great nation really is a wise and understanding people!"
What other nation, however great, has a god as near to them as the LORD our God is to us whenever we pray to him?
And what other nation, however great, has rules and laws as fair as all this teaching I am giving you today?

But be careful, and watch yourselves closely, so that you do not forget the things you have seen with your own eyes. Do not let them slip from your heart as long as you live. Teach them to your children and to your grandchildren.

Remember the day you stood before the LORD your God at Mount Sinai, when he said to me, "Gather the people before me so they can hear my words. Then they will learn to fear me as long as they live on the earth, and they will teach these things to their children."
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. It was blazing with fire that reached up to the sky, and it was covered with darkness and thick black clouds.
Then the LORD spoke to you from the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you did not see any shape. There was only a voice.
He told you about his covenant, the Ten Commandments, which he commanded you to obey. He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you the rules and laws you must obey in the land you are going to take over.
On the day the LORD spoke to you at Mount Sinai from the fire, you did not see any shape. So be very careful,
and do not ruin yourselves by making an idol in any shape at all, whether in the form of a man or a woman,
or any animal on the land, or any bird that flies in the sky,
or any creature that crawls on the ground, or any fish in the water below the land.

And when you look up at the sky and see the sun, the moon, and the stars, all the lights of heaven, do not be tempted to bow down and worship them. The LORD your God has given them to all the nations under heaven.
But the LORD took you and brought you out of Egypt, out of that furnace for melting iron, to be his very own people, as you are today.
Because of you, the LORD was angry with me. He swore that I would not cross the Jordan and enter the good land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
I will die here in this land. I will not cross the Jordan, but you are about to cross over and take that good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant the LORD your God made with you. Do not make for yourselves an idol in any shape, which the LORD your God has forbidden.
For the LORD your God is a fire that burns everything up. He is a jealous God, who will not share your love with any other.

After you have had children and grandchildren and have lived in the land a long time, you may ruin yourselves by making an idol of any shape, doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God and making him angry.

If you do, I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will quickly disappear from the land you are crossing the Jordan to take. You will not live there long, but will be completely destroyed.
The LORD will scatter you among the nations, and only a few of you will survive among the nations where the LORD sends you.
There you will worship gods made by human hands, gods of wood and stone, which cannot see, hear, eat, or smell.
But if from there you look for the LORD your God, you will find him, if you look for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in trouble and all these things have happened to you, then in the days to come you will come back to the LORD your God and obey him.
For the LORD your God is a God full of mercy. He will not leave you or destroy you, and he will not forget the covenant he swore to your ancestors.

Ask about the days long ago, before your time, from the day God created human beings on the earth. Search from one end of heaven to the other. Has anything as great as this ever happened? Has anyone ever heard of anything like it?
Has any other people heard the voice of God speaking from a fire, as you have, and lived?

Has any god ever tried to take one nation out of another nation for himself, by testing, by miraculous signs and wonders, by war, by his mighty hand and powerful arm, and by great and terrifying acts? Yet that is what the LORD your God did for you in Egypt, right before your eyes.
He showed you these things so that you would know that the LORD is God. There is no other god besides him.
He let you hear his voice from heaven to teach you. On earth he let you see his great fire, and you heard his words from the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them. He himself brought you out of Egypt by his great power,
to drive out nations greater and stronger than you, and to bring you into their land and give it to you as your own, as it is today.
So know this today and keep it in your heart: the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other.

Obey his rules and commands that I am giving you today. Then all will go well with you and your children after you, and you will live a long time in the land the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three towns on the east side of the Jordan,
where someone who killed a person by accident, without having hated him before, could run for safety. He could run to one of these towns and save his life.
The towns were Bezer in the desert high plain for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the tribe of Manasseh.
This is the teaching Moses gave the people of Israel.
These are the instructions, rules, and laws Moses gave them after they came out of Egypt,

when they were east of the Jordan in the valley near Beth Peor. This was in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Moses and the people of Israel defeated him after they came out of Egypt.
They took over his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan, the two Amorite kings who ruled east of the Jordan.
This land went from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, to Mount Siyon, which is Mount Hermon,
and included the whole Jordan Valley east of the Jordan, as far as the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
Moses called all Israel together and said to them: "Listen, Israel, to the rules and laws I am announcing to you today. Learn them and be sure to obey them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Mount Sinai.
The LORD did not make this covenant only with our ancestors, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.
The LORD spoke to you face to face from the fire on the mountain.
At that time I stood between the LORD and you to tell you what the LORD said, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, the land where you were slaves.
Do not have any other gods except me.
Do not make an idol for yourself in the shape of anything in the sky above, on the earth below, or in the water under the earth.
Do not bow down to idols or worship them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God. I punish children for the sins of their parents who hate me, to the third and fourth generation.
But I show faithful love to thousands of generations of those who love me and keep my commands.
Do not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will punish anyone who misuses his name.
Keep the Sabbath day holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
You have six days to do all your work.

But the seventh day is a Sabbath for the LORD your God. On that day no one may do any work: not you, your son or daughter, your male or female servant, your ox or donkey or any of your animals, or the foreigner living in your towns. Your male and female servants must rest just as you do.

Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with his mighty hand and powerful arm. That is why the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honour your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live long and all may go well with you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not murder.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not tell lies about your neighbour in court.
Do not want to take your neighbour's wife. Do not long for your neighbour's house, his land, his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbour.'

The LORD spoke these words in a loud voice to your whole community at the mountain, from the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness. He said nothing more. Then he wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice from the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, all the leaders of your tribes and your elders came to me.
You said, 'The LORD our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice from the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a person and that person can still live.
But now, why should we die? This great fire will burn us up. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, we will die.
What human being has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking from a fire, as we have, and lived?
You go near and listen to everything the LORD our God says. Then tell us whatever the LORD our God tells you. We will listen and obey.'
The LORD heard what you said to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard what these people said to you. Everything they said is good.
Oh, if only they would always have hearts like this, to fear me and keep all my commands! Then all would go well with them and their children forever.
Go and tell them to go back to their tents.
But you stay here with me, and I will give you all the commands, rules, and laws you must teach them. They must obey them in the land I am giving them to own.'
So be careful to do what the LORD your God has commanded you. Do not turn away from it to the right or to the left.
Walk in all the ways the LORD your God has commanded you. Then you will live, all will go well with you, and you will live long in the land you will own."
These are the commands, rules, and laws the LORD your God told me to teach you. Obey them in the land you are crossing over to take,
so that you, your children, and your grandchildren will fear the LORD your God as long as you live, and keep all his rules and commands that I give you. Then you will live a long life.

Listen, Israel, and be careful to obey. Then all will go well with you, and you will grow into a great nation in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
Listen, Israel: The LORD is our God. The LORD is the only one.
Love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
Keep these words that I am giving you today in your heart.
Teach them carefully to your children. Talk about them when you are sitting at home and when you are walking along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Tie them on your hands as a sign, and wear them on your foreheads as a reminder.
Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land he promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you. It is a land with large, fine cities that you did not build,
houses full of good things that you did not fill, wells that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant. When you have eaten and are full,
be careful that you do not forget the LORD, who brought you out of Egypt, the land where you were slaves.
Fear the LORD your God, serve him, and make your promises only in his name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the nations around you.
For the LORD your God, who is among you, is a jealous God. If you follow other gods, his anger will burn against you, and he will wipe you off the face of the earth.
Do not test the LORD your God, as you tested him at Massah.
Be sure to obey the commands of the LORD your God, and the instructions and rules he has given you.
Do what is right and good in the LORD's sight, so that all will go well with you. Then you will go in and take over the good land the LORD promised your ancestors,
and he will drive out all your enemies ahead of you, as he said.
In the future your children will ask you, "What do these instructions, rules, and laws mean that the LORD our God has commanded you?"
Then tell them, "We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand.
Right before our eyes, the LORD sent great and terrible miracles and wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on his whole family.
He brought us out of there to lead us into this land and give it to us, the land he promised our ancestors.
The LORD commanded us to obey all these rules and to fear the LORD our God, so that it would always go well with us and he would keep us alive, as he has done until today.
If we are careful to obey all these commands before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us, we will be right with him."

The LORD your God will bring you into the land you are going to take over. He will drive out many nations ahead of you: the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations bigger and stronger than you.
When the LORD your God hands them over to you and you defeat them, you must destroy them completely. Do not make any agreement with them, and do not show them mercy.
Do not marry any of them. Do not let your daughters marry their sons, and do not let your sons marry their daughters.
For they would turn your children away from following me to worship other gods. Then the LORD's anger would burn against you, and he would quickly destroy you.
This is what you must do to them: Tear down their altars, smash their holy stone pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their idols in the fire.
For you are a people set apart as holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, the LORD your God has chosen you to be his own special treasure.
The LORD did not love you and choose you because you were more in number than other peoples. In fact, you were the smallest of all peoples.

It was because the LORD loves you, and because he kept the promise he made to your ancestors. That is why he brought you out with his mighty hand and set you free from slavery, from the power of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
So know that the LORD your God is the true God. He is the faithful God who keeps his covenant of love for a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commands.
But he pays back those who hate him, to their face, by destroying them. He does not delay in paying back to their face those who hate him.
So be careful to obey the commands, rules, and laws I am giving you today.
If you listen to these laws and carefully obey them, the LORD your God will keep his covenant of faithful love with you, as he promised your ancestors.

He will love you, bless you, and make you grow in number. He will bless you with many children and with good crops: grain, new wine, and olive oil. He will bless your herds with calves and your flocks with lambs, in the land he promised your ancestors he would give you.
You will be blessed more than any other people. None of your men or women will be unable to have children, and none of your animals either.
The LORD will keep you free from all sickness. He will not bring on you any of the terrible diseases you knew in Egypt, but he will put them on all who hate you.
You must destroy all the peoples the LORD your God hands over to you. Do not feel sorry for them, and do not worship their gods, for that would be a trap for you.
You may say to yourselves, "These nations are stronger than we are. How can we drive them out?"
But do not be afraid of them. Remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all of Egypt.

You saw with your own eyes the great troubles, the miracles and wonders, and the mighty hand and powerful arm with which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you are afraid of now.
The LORD your God will also send panic among them, until even those who hide from you are destroyed.
Do not be terrified of them, for the LORD your God is with you. He is a great and awesome God.
The LORD your God will drive out those nations ahead of you little by little. You will not be allowed to destroy them all at once, or the wild animals would grow too many for you.
But the LORD your God will hand them over to you. He will throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will be able to stand against you. You will destroy them all.
Burn the idols of their gods in the fire. Do not want the silver or gold on them, and do not take it for yourselves, or it will be a trap for you. The LORD your God hates it.
Do not bring any of these hated things into your house, or you will be destroyed along with it. Hate it completely and turn away from it in disgust, because it is set apart to be destroyed.
Be careful to obey every command I am giving you today. Then you will live, grow in number, and go in and take over the land the LORD promised your ancestors.

Remember how the LORD your God led you all the way through the desert these forty years. He did it to humble you and test you, to find out what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commands or not.

He humbled you by letting you go hungry, and then he fed you with manna, food that neither you nor your ancestors had ever known. He did this to teach you that people do not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
During these forty years your clothes did not wear out, and your feet did not swell.
So understand in your heart that the LORD your God trains and corrects you, just as a father trains and corrects his son.
Obey the commands of the LORD your God. Live the way he wants, and fear him.
For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land with streams and springs, with water flowing from deep under the ground into the valleys and hills.
It is a land of wheat and barley, of grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey.
In that land you will have plenty of food to eat and will not lack anything. Its rocks have iron in them, and you can dig copper out of its hills.
When you have eaten and are full, praise the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
Be careful that you do not forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commands, laws, and rules that I am giving you today.
When you have eaten and are full, when you have built fine houses and live in them,
when your herds and flocks grow large, when your silver and gold increase, and everything you own grows,
then do not become proud and forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, the land where you were slaves.
He led you through the huge and terrible desert, with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, a dry land with no water. He made water flow for you out of hard rock.
He fed you in the desert with manna, which your ancestors had never known. He did this to humble you and test you, so that in the end it would go well with you.
Do not say to yourself, "I got all this wealth by my own power and strength."
But remember the LORD your God, for he is the one who gives you the ability to become rich. He does this to keep the covenant he promised your ancestors, as he is doing today.
If you ever forget the LORD your God and follow other gods, serving them and bowing down to them, I warn you today that you will surely be destroyed.
Just like the nations the LORD is destroying ahead of you, you too will be destroyed, because you would not obey the LORD your God.
Listen, Israel! Today you are about to cross the Jordan River to take over the land of nations bigger and stronger than you, with large cities that have walls reaching up to the sky.
The people are strong and tall. They are the Anakites. You know about them, and you have heard it said, "Who can stand up against the Anakites?"

But be sure of this today: the LORD your God is the one who goes across ahead of you like a fire that burns everything up. He will destroy them and bring them down before you. You will drive them out and wipe them out quickly, as the LORD promised you.

After the LORD your God has driven them out ahead of you, do not say to yourself, "The LORD brought me here to take this land because I am so good." No, it is because these nations are so wicked that the LORD is driving them out ahead of you.

You are not going in to take their land because you are good or because your heart is honest. It is because these nations are wicked that the LORD your God will drive them out ahead of you, and to keep the promise he made to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
So understand that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to own because you are good. In fact, you are a stubborn people.
Remember, and never forget, how you made the LORD your God angry in the desert. From the day you left Egypt until you arrived here, you have kept rebelling against the LORD.
Even at Mount Sinai you made the LORD so angry that he was ready to destroy you.

I had gone up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant the LORD had made with you. I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I did not eat any food or drink any water.
The LORD gave me two stone tablets written by the finger of God. On them were all the words the LORD spoke to you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day you were all gathered there.
At the end of the forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

Then the LORD said to me, "Get up and go down from here at once, because your people whom you brought out of Egypt have become evil. They have quickly turned away from what I commanded them and have made a metal idol for themselves!"
The LORD also said to me, "I have seen these people, and they are very stubborn.
Leave me alone so that I can destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and bigger than they are."
So I turned and went down the mountain while it was blazing with fire. The two tablets of the covenant were in my hands.
When I looked, I saw that you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made yourselves an idol shaped like a calf. You had quickly turned away from the way the LORD had commanded you.
So I took the two tablets and threw them down from my hands, breaking them in front of your eyes.

Then once again I lay face down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights. I did not eat any food or drink any water, because of all the sin you had done, doing what was evil in the LORD's sight and making him angry.
I was afraid of the LORD's terrible anger, because he was angry enough to destroy you. But again the LORD listened to me.
The LORD was also angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I prayed for Aaron too.
Then I took that sinful calf you had made and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it into powder as fine as dust, and threw the dust into the stream that flowed down the mountain.
You also made the LORD angry at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth Hattaavah.

And when the LORD sent you out from Kadesh Barnea, he said, "Go up and take over the land I have given you." But you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You did not trust him or obey him.
You have been rebelling against the LORD ever since I have known you.
So I lay face down before the LORD for those forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, do not destroy your people, your own special people, whom you rescued by your great power and brought out of Egypt with your mighty hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at how stubborn these people are, or at their wickedness and sin.

Otherwise the people of the land you brought us out of will say, 'The LORD was not able to take them into the land he promised them, and he hated them. So he brought them out to kill them in the desert.'
But they are your people, your own special people, whom you brought out by your great power and your mighty arm."
At that time the LORD said to me, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Also make a wooden chest.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Then you must put them in the chest."
So I made a chest out of acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain carrying the two tablets in my hands.

The LORD wrote on these tablets what he had written before: the Ten Commandments he had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day you were all gathered there. Then the LORD gave them to me.
