I turned and came down the mountain and put the tablets in the chest I had made. They are still there, just as the LORD commanded me.
(The Israelites travelled from the wells of the people of Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they travelled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of the LORD's Covenant, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to give blessings in his name. They still do this today.
That is why the Levites have no share of land among the other tribes. The LORD himself is their share, as the LORD your God told them.)
I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I did the first time, and once again the LORD listened to me. He chose not to destroy you.
The LORD said to me, "Get up and lead the people on their journey, so that they may go in and take over the land I promised their ancestors I would give them."

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? He asks you to fear the LORD your God, to live the way he wants, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul,
and to obey the LORD's commands and rules that I am giving you today for your own good.
Look, the heavens, even the highest heavens, belong to the LORD your God, and so does the earth and everything in it.
Yet the LORD loved your ancestors and took delight in them. He chose you, their descendants, above all other peoples, as you can see today.
So change your hearts and stop being stubborn.
For the LORD your God is God over all gods and Lord over all lords. He is the great God, mighty and awesome. He does not take sides, and he does not accept bribes.
He makes sure orphans and widows are treated fairly. He loves the foreigners living among you and gives them food and clothing.
So you too must love foreigners, because you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt.
Fear the LORD your God and serve him. Hold tightly to him, and make your promises only in his name.
He is the one you should praise. He is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that you have seen with your own eyes.
When your ancestors went down to Egypt, there were only seventy of them. But now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.
So love the LORD your God and always obey his instructions, rules, laws, and commands.

Remember today what you have learned. I am not speaking to your children, who have not known or seen how the LORD your God corrected you. They did not see his greatness, his mighty hand, his powerful arm,
or the miracles and the things he did in Egypt to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his whole land.

They did not see what he did to the Egyptian army, its horses and chariots, how he made the waters of the Red Sea flow over them as they were chasing you. The LORD destroyed them completely, and they are gone to this day.
They did not see what he did for you in the desert until you arrived here,

or what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, from the tribe of Reuben. In front of all Israel, the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, along with their families, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them.
But you have seen with your own eyes all these great things the LORD has done.
So obey every command I am giving you today, so that you will be strong enough to go in and take over the land you are crossing over to take,
and so that you may live a long time in the land the LORD promised to give your ancestors and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
The land you are going into to take over is not like Egypt, where you came from. There you planted your seed and had to water it by hand, like a vegetable garden.
But the land you are crossing over to take is a land of hills and valleys that drinks rain from the sky.
It is a land the LORD your God cares for. His eyes are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end.
If you carefully obey the commands I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and serve him with all your heart and all your soul,
then he will send rain on your land at the right time, in autumn and in spring, so that you can gather your grain, new wine, and olive oil.
He will give grass in the fields for your animals, and you will have plenty to eat.
Be careful not to be fooled into turning away to serve and worship other gods.

If you do, the LORD's anger will burn against you. He will shut up the sky so there will be no rain, and the land will not produce its crops. Then you will quickly die off the good land the LORD is giving you.
So keep these words of mine in your hearts and minds. Tie them on your hands as a sign, and wear them on your foreheads as a reminder.
Teach them to your children. Talk about them when you are sitting at home and when you are walking along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates,
so that you and your children may live long in the land the LORD promised to give your ancestors, for as long as the sky is above the earth.
If you carefully obey all these commands I am giving you, to love the LORD your God, to live the way he wants, and to hold tightly to him,
then the LORD will drive out all these nations ahead of you. You will take the land of nations bigger and stronger than you.
Every place where you set your foot will be yours. Your land will reach from the desert to Lebanon, and from the Euphrates River to the Mediterranean Sea.
No one will be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will make all the people in the land terrified of you wherever you go, just as he promised you.
Look, today I am giving you a choice between a blessing and a curse.
You will be blessed if you obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today.
You will be cursed if you do not obey the commands of the LORD your God, but turn away from the way I am commanding you today and follow other gods you have not known.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are going to take over, announce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These mountains are west of the Jordan River, toward the setting sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Jordan Valley, near Gilgal, beside the great trees of Moreh.
You are about to cross the Jordan to go in and take over the land the LORD your God is giving you. When you have taken it and are living there,
be careful to obey all the rules and laws I am giving you today.
These are the rules and laws you must be careful to obey in the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to own, for as long as you live on the earth.
Completely destroy all the places where the nations you are driving out worshipped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Tear down their altars, smash their holy stone pillars, and burn their Asherah poles in the fire. Cut down the idols of their gods and wipe out their names from those places.
Do not worship the LORD your God in the way they worship their gods.
Instead, go to the place the LORD your God will choose from among all your tribes as the place where his name will live. Look for that place where he lives, and go there.
Bring there your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tenth parts and special gifts, what you have promised, your free will offerings, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
There, in the presence of the LORD your God, you and your families will eat and be glad about everything you have worked for, because the LORD your God has blessed you.
You must not do as we are doing here today, where everyone does whatever they think is right.
For you have not yet arrived at the place of rest, the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
But you will cross the Jordan and live in the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own. He will give you rest from all the enemies around you, and you will live in safety.

Then bring everything I command you to the place the LORD your God will choose as the place where his name will live: your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tenth parts and special gifts, and all the best things you have promised to the LORD.
And be glad there in the presence of the LORD your God, you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites living in your towns, who have no share of land of their own.
Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings anywhere you like.
Offer them only at the place the LORD will choose in one of your tribes. There you must do everything I command you.

But you may kill and eat meat in any of your towns, as much as you want, according to the blessing the LORD your God gives you. Both people who are unclean and people who are clean may eat it, as they would eat gazelle or deer.
But you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

Do not eat these things in your own towns: the tenth part of your grain, new wine, or olive oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, anything you have promised to give, your free will offerings, or your special gifts.

Instead, eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose, together with your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites living in your towns. Be glad in the presence of the LORD your God about everything you have worked for.
Be careful never to forget the Levites as long as you live in your land.
When the LORD your God makes your land larger, as he promised you, and you want to eat meat and say, "I would like some meat," then you may eat as much meat as you want.

If the place the LORD your God chooses for his name is too far away from you, you may kill animals from the herds and flocks the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you. You may eat as much of it as you want in your own towns.
Eat it as you would eat gazelle or deer. Both people who are unclean and people who are clean may eat it.
But be sure you do not eat the blood, because the blood is the life. You must not eat the life with the meat.
Do not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that all will go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the LORD's eyes.
But take your holy gifts and what you have promised to give, and go to the place the LORD will choose.

Offer your burnt offerings, both the meat and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.

Be careful to obey all these words I am giving you, so that it will always go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
The LORD your God will wipe out the nations ahead of you in the land you are going in to take. When you have driven them out and are living in their land,

be careful not to be trapped into following their ways after they have been destroyed ahead of you. Do not ask about their gods and say, "How do these nations worship their gods? We will do the same."

You must not worship the LORD your God in their way, because they do for their gods every hateful thing the LORD hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods.
Be careful to do everything I command you. Do not add anything to it or take anything away from it.
A prophet, or someone who explains dreams, may appear among you and promise you a miraculous sign or wonder.
Even if the sign or wonder he spoke of happens, and he says, "Let us follow other gods," gods you have not known, "and let us worship them,"
do not listen to that prophet or dreamer. The LORD your God is testing you, to find out whether you love him with all your heart and all your soul.
Follow the LORD your God and fear him. Keep his commands and obey him. Serve him and hold tightly to him.

That prophet or dreamer must be put to death, because he has taught you to rebel against the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt and set you free from slavery. He tried to turn you away from the way the LORD your God commanded you to live. You must get rid of this evil from among you.

Your own brother, your son or daughter, the wife you love, or your closest friend may secretly try to lead you astray. They may say, "Let us go and worship other gods," gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known,
gods of the peoples around you, whether near or far, from one end of the earth to the other.
Do not give in to them or listen to them. Do not feel sorry for them. Do not spare them or protect them.
You must certainly put them to death. Your hand must be the first to strike them, and then the hands of all the people.
Stone them to death, because they tried to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, the land where you were slaves.
Then all Israel will hear about it and be afraid, and no one among you will do such an evil thing again.
You may hear that in one of the towns the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
some wicked men have appeared among you and led the people of their town astray, saying, "Let us go and worship other gods," gods you have not known.
Then you must look into it, search it out, and ask questions carefully. If it is true and it is proven that this hateful thing has been done among you,
you must kill all the people of that town with the sword. Destroy it completely, with everyone in it and its animals too.

Gather everything taken from the town into the middle of its public square, and burn the whole town and everything in it as an offering to the LORD your God. It must remain a pile of ruins forever. It must never be rebuilt.

Do not keep any of the things set apart for destruction. Then the LORD will turn away from his fierce anger. He will show you mercy and kindness, and he will make you grow in number, as he promised your ancestors.
He will do this if you obey the LORD your God, keep all his commands that I am giving you today, and do what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
You are the children of the LORD your God. When someone dies, do not cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads.
For you are a people set apart as holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, the LORD has chosen you to be his own special treasure.
Do not eat anything that is hateful to the LORD.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud.

But even among the animals that chew the cud or have a split hoof, you must not eat the camel, the hare, or the rock badger. They chew the cud but do not have a split hoof, so they are unclean for you.
The pig is also unclean for you. It has a split hoof but does not chew the cud. Do not eat their meat or touch their dead bodies.
Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat anything that has fins and scales.
But do not eat anything that does not have fins and scales. It is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these are the birds you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the osprey,
the red kite, the falcon, any kind of kite,
any kind of raven,
the ostrich, the owl, the seagull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the horned owl,
the pelican, the vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All flying insects are unclean for you. Do not eat them.
But you may eat any clean winged creature.

Do not eat anything you find already dead. You may give it to a foreigner living in your towns to eat, or you may sell it to a foreigner. But you are a people set apart as holy to the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Every year be sure to set aside a tenth of all the crops your fields produce.

Eat this tenth of your grain, new wine, and olive oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God, at the place he will choose as the place where his name will live. Then you will learn to always fear the LORD your God.
But the LORD your God may bless you so much that the place he chooses for his name is too far away, and the journey too long, for you to carry your tenth there.
Then sell it for money. Take the money with you and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
Use the money to buy whatever you want: cattle, sheep, wine, other strong drink, or anything you wish. Then you and your family will eat there in the presence of the LORD your God and be glad.
And do not forget the Levites living in your towns, because they have no share of land of their own.
At the end of every third year, bring the whole tenth of that year's crops and store it in your towns.

Then the Levites, who have no share of land of their own, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows living in your towns may come and eat and be full. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all the work you do.
At the end of every seven years, you must cancel all debts.

This is how it must be done: everyone who has lent money to a fellow Israelite must cancel the debt. He must not demand payment from his neighbour or his relative, because the LORD's time for cancelling debts has been announced.
You may demand payment from a foreigner, but you must cancel any debt your fellow Israelite owes you.
There should be no poor people among you, for the LORD will greatly bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you to own as your share,
if only you carefully obey the LORD your God and are careful to keep all these commands I am giving you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you as he promised. You will lend money to many nations, but you will not need to borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
If there is a poor person among your fellow Israelites in any of the towns of the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not be hard-hearted or tight-fisted toward that poor person.
Instead, be open-handed and freely lend them whatever they need.

Be careful not to have this wicked thought in your heart: "The seventh year, the year for cancelling debts, is near." Do not look unkindly at your poor fellow Israelite and give them nothing. They may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Give generously to them, and do not be unhappy about giving. Because of this, the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you do.
There will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you to be open-handed toward your fellow Israelites who are poor and in need in your land.
If one of your fellow Hebrews, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you for six years, you must set them free in the seventh year.
And when you set them free, do not send them away empty-handed.
Give to them generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to them as the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the LORD your God set you free. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But your servant may say to you, "I do not want to leave you," because he loves you and your family and is happy with you.
Then take a sharp tool and push it through his ear lobe into the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant.
Do not think it is hard to set your servant free, because their six years of service have been worth twice as much as a hired worker. And the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
Set apart for the LORD your God every firstborn male of your herds and flocks. Do not put the firstborn of your cattle to work, and do not cut the wool of the firstborn of your sheep.
Each year you and your family must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose.
If an animal has a defect, if it is lame or blind or has any other serious defect, do not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
Eat it in your own towns. Both people who are unclean and people who are clean may eat it, as they would eat gazelle or deer.
But you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
Celebrate the Passover of the LORD your God in the month of Abib, because it was in the month of Abib that the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
Sacrifice an animal from your flock or herd as the Passover to the LORD your God, at the place the LORD will choose as the place where his name will live.

Do not eat it with bread made with yeast. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, the bread of suffering, because you left Egypt in a hurry. Do this so that all your life you will remember the day you left Egypt.
Let no yeast be found anywhere in your land for seven days. And do not let any of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day remain until morning.
You must not sacrifice the Passover in just any of the towns the LORD your God gives you.
Sacrifice it only at the place the LORD your God will choose as the place where his name will live. Do it in the evening, when the sun goes down, at the same time of day you left Egypt.
Roast it and eat it at the place the LORD your God will choose. Then in the morning go back to your tents.
For six days eat bread made without yeast. On the seventh day hold a special meeting for the LORD your God, and do no work.
Count seven weeks from the time you begin to cut the grain in the fields.
Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God by bringing a free will offering. Give in proportion to the blessings the LORD your God has given you.

Be glad in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose as the place where his name will live. Celebrate with your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, the Levites in your towns, and the foreigners, orphans, and widows living among you.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and be careful to obey these rules.
Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days, after you have gathered in the grain from your threshing floor and the juice from your winepress.
Be glad at your festival, you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows living in your towns.

For seven days celebrate the festival to the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose. For the LORD your God will bless all your harvest and all the work of your hands, and your joy will be complete.

Three times a year all your men must come before the LORD your God at the place he will choose: at the Festival of Bread Made Without Yeast, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Shelters. No one should come before the LORD empty-handed.
Each of you must bring a gift as you are able, in proportion to the blessings the LORD your God has given you.
Appoint judges and officials for each of your tribes in every town the LORD your God is giving you. They must judge the people fairly.
Do not twist justice or take sides. Do not accept a bribe, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of those who are innocent.
Follow justice and only justice, so that you may live and take over the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not set up any wooden Asherah pole beside the altar you build for the LORD your God,
and do not set up a holy stone pillar, because the LORD your God hates them.
Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has any defect or flaw, because the LORD your God hates that.
Suppose a man or woman living in one of the towns the LORD your God gives you is found doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God by breaking his covenant.
Suppose they have gone and worshipped other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or the stars in the sky, which I have forbidden.
If you are told about this, or hear about it, look into it carefully. If it is true and it is proven that this hateful thing has been done in Israel,
then take the man or woman who has done this evil thing to your town gate, and stone that person to death.
A person may be put to death only on the word of two or three witnesses. No one may be put to death on the word of only one witness.
The witnesses must be the first to throw stones at the person, and then all the people must join in. You must get rid of this evil from among you.

Some cases that come before your local courts may be too hard for you to judge, such as cases of murder, of who has the right in a quarrel, or of injury. Then take them to the place the LORD your God will choose.
Go to the priests, who are Levites, and to the judge who is in office at that time. Ask them about the case, and they will give you their decision.
You must act on the decision they give you at the place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they tell you.
Follow the teaching they give you and the decision they announce. Do not turn away from what they tell you, to the right or to the left.
Anyone who proudly refuses to listen to the priest who stands there serving the LORD your God, or to the judge, must be put to death. You must get rid of the evil from Israel.
Then all the people will hear about it and be afraid, and they will not act proudly again.
You will enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, take it over, and settle in it. Then you may say, "Let us set a king over us, like all the nations around us."
If so, be sure to make the king the one the LORD your God chooses. He must be one of your own people. Do not put a foreigner over you, someone who is not a fellow Israelite.
The king must not gather large numbers of horses for himself, or send people back to Egypt to get more horses, for the LORD has told you, "You must never go back that way again."
He must not take many wives, or his heart will be turned away from the LORD. And he must not gather large amounts of silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on his royal throne, he must write out for himself a copy of this law in a book, taken from the copy kept by the priests, who are Levites.
He must keep it with him and read it every day of his life, so that he learns to fear the LORD his God and carefully obeys all the words of this law and these rules.

Then he will not think he is better than his fellow Israelites, and he will not turn away from the commands to the right or to the left. Then he and his descendants will rule his kingdom in Israel for a long time.
The priests, who are Levites, and in fact the whole tribe of Levi, will have no share of land in Israel. They will live on the food offerings made to the LORD by fire, which is their share.
They will have no land among the other tribes. The LORD himself is their share, as he promised them.
This is what the priests may have from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether it is a bull or a sheep: the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
Also give them the first part of your grain, new wine, and olive oil, and the first wool cut from your sheep.
For the LORD your God has chosen them and their descendants out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the LORD's name always.
A Levite may move from any town in Israel where he is living and come, because he truly wants to, to the place the LORD will choose.
There he may serve in the name of the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who serve there in the presence of the LORD.
He must receive an equal share of the food, even if he also has money from selling his family property.
When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to copy the hateful ways of the nations there.
Let no one be found among you who sacrifices their son or daughter in the fire, or who tries to tell the future, or reads signs, or uses magic, or casts spells,
or puts curses on people, or talks with spirits, or is a witch, or tries to speak with the dead.
The LORD hates anyone who does these things. It is because of these hateful practices that the LORD your God is driving out those nations ahead of you.
You must be completely faithful to the LORD your God.
The nations you will drive out listen to people who do magic and try to tell the future. But the LORD your God has not allowed you to do that.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people. You must listen to him.

This is what you asked the LORD your God for at Mount Sinai, on the day you were gathered there. You said, "Do not let us hear the voice of the LORD our God again or see this great fire any more, or we will die."
The LORD said to me, "What they have said is good.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
I myself will hold responsible anyone who does not listen to my words that the prophet speaks in my name.
But if a prophet dares to speak in my name something I have not commanded him to say, or speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die."
You may wonder, "How can we know whether a message has not come from the LORD?"
If a prophet speaks in the LORD's name and what he says does not happen or come true, then that message is not from the LORD. That prophet has spoken out of pride. Do not be afraid of him.
The LORD your God will destroy the nations whose land he is giving you. When you have driven them out and are living in their towns and houses,
set apart three cities for yourselves in the land the LORD your God is giving you to own.
Build roads to them, and divide the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own into three parts. Then anyone who kills a person can run to one of these cities.
This is the rule for someone who kills a person and runs there to save their life: they must have killed their neighbour by accident, without hating them beforehand.

For example, a man may go into the forest with his neighbour to cut wood. As he swings the axe to chop down a tree, the head may fly off the handle and hit his neighbour and kill him. That man may run to one of these cities and save his life.

Otherwise, the dead person's relative who has the duty to punish the killer might chase him in a rage. If the road is long, he might catch him and kill him, even though the man did not deserve to die, since he had not hated his neighbour before.
That is why I command you to set apart three cities for yourselves.
The LORD your God may make your land larger, as he promised your ancestors, and give you all the land he promised them.

He will do this if you carefully obey all these commands I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and always live the way he wants. Then you must set apart three more cities in addition to these three.
Do this so that innocent people will not be killed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own, and you will not be guilty of their death.
But suppose a man hates his neighbour, hides and waits for him, attacks him and kills him, and then runs to one of these cities.
The leaders of his own town must send for him, bring him back from the city, and hand him over to the relative who has the duty to punish the killer, so that he dies.
Do not feel sorry for him. You must clear Israel of the guilt of killing innocent people, so that all will go well with you.
Do not move your neighbour's boundary stone, which was set up by those who came before you, in the land you will receive as your own in the land the LORD your God is giving you to take over.
One witness is not enough to prove that a person is guilty of any crime or sin they may have done. A matter must be proven by the word of two or three witnesses.
If a lying witness stands up to accuse someone of a crime,
both people in the quarrel must stand in the presence of the LORD before the priests and the judges who are in office at that time.
The judges must look into the case carefully. If the witness is proven to be a liar who has told lies about a fellow Israelite,
then do to the lying witness what that witness wanted to do to the other person. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
The rest of the people will hear about it and be afraid, and no one will ever again do such an evil thing among you.
Do not feel sorry for them. The punishment must match the crime: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.
When you go to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army bigger than yours, do not be afraid of them. The LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, is with you.
When you are about to go into battle, the priest must come forward and speak to the army.
He will say, "Listen, Israel. Today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart! Do not be afraid or panic, and do not be terrified of them.
For the LORD your God is the one who goes with you. He will fight for you against your enemies and give you victory."
Then the officers must say to the army, "Has anyone built a new house and not yet dedicated it? He should go home, or he might die in battle and someone else will dedicate it.
Has anyone planted a vineyard and not yet enjoyed its fruit? He should go home, or he might die in battle and someone else will enjoy its fruit.
Is anyone engaged to a woman and not yet married her? He should go home, or he might die in battle and someone else will marry her."
Then the officers must add, "Is anyone afraid or losing courage? He should go home, so that his fellow soldiers will not lose courage too."
When the officers have finished speaking to the army, they must appoint commanders to lead it.
When you march up to attack a city, first offer its people peace.
If they accept and open their gates to you, all the people in it will become your forced workers and will serve you.
But if they refuse to make peace and fight against you, then surround the city and attack it.
When the LORD your God hands it over to you, kill all the men in it with the sword.
But you may take for yourselves the women, the children, the animals, and everything else in the city. You may use the goods taken from your enemies, which the LORD your God gives you.
This is how you must treat all the cities that are far away from you, the cities that do not belong to the nations near you.
But in the cities of the nations the LORD your God is giving you as your own, do not leave alive anything that breathes.
Destroy them completely: the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
Otherwise, they will teach you to follow all the hateful things they do for their gods, and you will sin against the LORD your God.

When you surround a city and attack it for a long time to capture it, do not destroy its trees by cutting them down with an axe. You can eat their fruit, so do not cut them down. Are the trees of the field people, that you should attack them?
But you may cut down trees that you know do not produce food. Use them to build siege works against the city that is at war with you, until it falls.
Suppose someone is found murdered, lying in a field in the land the LORD your God is giving you to own, and no one knows who killed them.
Your leaders and judges must go out and measure the distance from the body to the nearby towns.
Then the leaders of the town nearest the body must take a young cow that has never been worked and has never worn a yoke.
They must lead her down to a valley with a flowing stream, where the land has never been ploughed or planted. There in the valley they must break the young cow's neck.

The priests, the descendants of Levi, must come forward. The LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to give blessings in the LORD's name, and they are to decide every quarrel and every case of violence.
Then all the leaders of the town nearest the body must wash their hands over the young cow whose neck was broken in the valley.
They must say, "Our hands did not kill this person, and our eyes did not see it happen.
LORD, forgive your people Israel, whom you have set free. Do not hold your people Israel guilty of killing an innocent person." Then they will be forgiven for the killing.
In this way you will clear yourselves of the guilt of killing an innocent person, because you will have done what is right in the LORD's eyes.
When you go to war against your enemies and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take prisoners,
you may see among the prisoners a beautiful woman, be attracted to her, and want to marry her.
Bring her home to your house. She must shave her head and cut her nails,

and take off the clothes she was wearing when she was captured. She must live in your house and mourn for her father and mother for a whole month. After that you may go to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.
If you are no longer pleased with her, let her go wherever she wishes. You must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have shamed her.
Suppose a man has two wives. He loves one but not the other, and both have given him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the wife he does not love.
When he gives his property to his sons, he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves instead of to the son of the wife he does not love, who is really the firstborn.

He must accept the son of the wife he does not love as the firstborn and give him a double share of everything he owns. That son is the first sign of his father's strength, and the rights of the firstborn belong to him.
Suppose a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or his mother. Even when they correct him, he will not listen to them.
Then his father and mother must take hold of him and bring him to the leaders at the gate of his town.
They must say to the leaders of the town, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He eats too much and gets drunk."
Then all the men of his town must stone him to death. You must get rid of the evil from among you. All Israel will hear about it and be afraid.
If someone has done a crime that deserves death, and they are put to death and their body is hung on a pole,

do not leave the body hanging on the pole overnight. Be sure to bury it that same day, because anyone who is hung on a pole is under God's curse. Do not make unclean the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
If you see your fellow Israelite's ox or sheep wandering away, do not pretend you did not see it. Be sure to take it back to its owner.
If the owner does not live near you, or you do not know who owns it, take it home with you and keep it until the owner comes looking for it. Then give it back.
Do the same if you find their donkey, their cloak, or anything else they have lost. Do not pretend you did not see it.
If you see your fellow Israelite's donkey or ox fallen down on the road, do not pretend you did not see it. Be sure to help the owner get it back on its feet.
A woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing, for the LORD your God hates anyone who does this.
If you come across a bird's nest beside the road, in a tree or on the ground, and the mother is sitting on the young birds or the eggs, do not take the mother with the young.
You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go, so that all will go well with you and you will live a long life.
When you build a new house, put a low wall around the edge of the roof, so that you will not be guilty of someone's death if they fall off it.
Do not plant two kinds of seed in your vineyard. If you do, the whole harvest will be lost, both the crop you planted and the fruit of the vineyard.
Do not plough with an ox and a donkey tied together.
Do not wear clothes made of wool and linen woven together.
Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
Suppose a man marries a woman and sleeps with her, and then he turns against her.
He says shameful things about her and gives her a bad name, saying, "I married this woman, but when I slept with her I found she was not a virgin."
Then the young woman's father and mother must bring the proof that she was a virgin to the town leaders at the gate.
Her father will say to the leaders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he has turned against her.

Now he has said shameful things about her, saying, 'I found that your daughter was not a virgin.' But here is the proof that my daughter was a virgin." Then her parents must spread out the cloth in front of the town leaders.
The leaders of that town must take the man and punish him.

They must fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give the money to the young woman's father, because this man has given a bad name to a young Israelite virgin. She will remain his wife, and he must never divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true and no proof of the young woman's virginity is found,

she must be brought to the door of her father's house, and the men of her town must stone her to death. She has done a shameful thing in Israel by sleeping with someone while living in her father's house. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, both the man and the woman must die. You must get rid of the evil from Israel.
Suppose a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and engaged to someone else, in a town, and he sleeps with her.

Take them both to the gate of that town and stone them to death. Stone the young woman because she was in a town and did not scream for help, and stone the man because he shamed another man's future wife. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
But if a man meets an engaged young woman out in the country and forces her to sleep with him, only the man who did this must die.
Do nothing to the young woman. She has not committed a sin that deserves death. This case is like someone who attacks and murders their neighbour,
because the man found her out in the country. The engaged young woman screamed, but there was no one to rescue her.
Suppose a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and not engaged, takes hold of her, and sleeps with her, and they are found out.
He must pay her father fifty pieces of silver. Then he must marry her, because he shamed her. He must never divorce her as long as he lives.
A man must not marry his father's wife. He must not dishonour his father by sleeping with her.
No man whose private parts have been crushed or cut off may join the assembly of the LORD.
No one born from a forbidden marriage may join the assembly of the LORD. None of their descendants may join it, even down to the tenth generation.
No Ammonite or Moabite may join the assembly of the LORD. None of their descendants may ever join it, even down to the tenth generation.
For they did not come to meet you with food and water on your journey after you left Egypt. They also hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia to put a curse on you.
But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. Instead, the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
As long as you live, never try to help them have peace or success.
Do not hate an Edomite, because Edomites are your relatives. Do not hate an Egyptian, because you lived as foreigners in their land.
The third generation of children born to them may join the assembly of the LORD.
When you are camped to fight your enemies, keep away from anything that would make you unclean.
If one of your men becomes unclean because of something that happened to him during the night, he must go outside the camp and stay there.
But as evening comes he must wash himself with water, and at sunset he may come back into the camp.
Have a place outside the camp where you can go to the toilet.
Carry a small shovel along with your weapons. When you go to the toilet, dig a hole with it, and then cover up your waste.
For the LORD your God moves around in your camp to protect you and to hand your enemies over to you. Your camp must be holy, so that he will not see anything unclean among you and turn away from you.
If a slave runs away from his master and comes to you for safety, do not hand him back to his master.
Let him live among you in any town he chooses, wherever he likes best. Do not treat him badly.
No Israelite man or woman may become a temple prostitute.
Do not bring the money earned by a female or male prostitute into the house of the LORD your God to pay any promise, because the LORD your God hates them both.
Do not charge your fellow Israelite interest on a loan, whether it is money, food, or anything else that can earn interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but not a fellow Israelite. Then the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do in the land you are going in to take over.
If you make a promise to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it, because the LORD your God will certainly expect it from you, and you will be guilty of sin if you do not keep it.
But if you choose not to make a promise, you will not be guilty.
Be sure to do whatever you said you would do. You freely made your promise to the LORD your God with your own mouth, so you must keep it.
When you go into your neighbour's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want, but do not put any in your basket.
When you go into your neighbour's grain field, you may pick some heads of grain with your hand, but do not cut their grain with a sickle.
Suppose a man marries a woman, but she does not please him because he finds something shameful about her. He writes her a certificate of divorce, gives it to her, and sends her away from his house.
After she leaves his house, she may become another man's wife.
Then her second husband may also turn against her, write her a certificate of divorce, give it to her, and send her away from his house. Or her second husband may die.

In either case, her first husband, who divorced her, is not allowed to marry her again, because she has been made unclean. That would be hateful to the LORD. Do not bring sin on the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
If a man has just married, he must not be sent to war or given any other duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and make his new wife happy.
Do not take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper millstone, as a guarantee for a loan. That would be taking away a person's way of making a living.
If someone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating them as a slave or selling them, the kidnapper must die. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
If there is an outbreak of a serious skin disease, be very careful to do exactly what the priests, who are Levites, teach you. Be careful to do what I have commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on your journey after you left Egypt.
When you lend your neighbour anything, do not go into their house to take the thing they offer as a guarantee.
Stay outside, and let the person you are lending to bring it out to you.
If the person is poor, do not go to sleep while keeping their guarantee.
Be sure to give their cloak back by sunset so that they can sleep in it. Then they will bless you, and the LORD your God will see it as a right thing you have done.
Do not take advantage of a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether they are a fellow Israelite or a foreigner living in one of your towns.
Pay them their wages each day before sunset, because they are poor and are counting on it. Otherwise they may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Parents must not be put to death for what their children have done, and children must not be put to death for what their parents have done. Each person must die for their own sin.
Do not deny justice to foreigners or orphans, and do not take a widow's cloak as a guarantee for a loan.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the LORD your God set you free from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you are gathering your harvest in your field and you forget a bundle of grain, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows, so that the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches a second time. Leave what remains for the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows.
When you pick the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over the vines a second time. Leave what remains for the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
When people have a quarrel, they must take it to court, and the judges will decide the case. They must declare the innocent person right and the guilty person wrong.
If the guilty person deserves to be beaten, the judge must make him lie down and have him beaten in front of him, with the number of lashes his crime deserves.
The judge may not give more than forty lashes. If he gives more than that, your fellow Israelite would be shamed in front of you.
Do not cover an ox's mouth to stop it eating while it is treading out the grain.

Suppose brothers are living together, and one of them dies without a son. His widow must not marry someone outside the family. Her husband's brother must marry her and do his duty as a brother-in-law.
The first son she has will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be wiped out from Israel.

But if the man does not want to marry his brother's widow, she must go to the town leaders at the gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel. He will not do his duty as a brother-in-law to me."
Then the leaders of his town will call for him and talk to him. If he still says, "I do not want to marry her,"

his brother's widow must go up to him in front of the leaders, pull one of his sandals off his foot, and spit in his face. She will say, "This is what happens to the man who will not build up his brother's family."
From then on his family will be known in Israel as "the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off."
If two men are fighting, and the wife of one of them comes to rescue her husband from the man hitting him, and she reaches out and grabs the other man by his private parts,
you must cut off her hand. Do not feel sorry for her.
Do not carry two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
Do not keep two different measures in your house, one large and one small.
Use weights and measures that are accurate and honest, so that you will live a long time in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
For the LORD your God hates anyone who does such things, anyone who is dishonest.
Remember what the Amalekites did to you on your journey after you left Egypt.
When you were tired and worn out, they met you on the road and attacked everyone who was weak and lagging behind. They had no fear of God.
When the LORD your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you to own as your share, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
When you have entered the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own, and you have taken it over and settled in it,

take some of the first part of all the crops you harvest from the land the LORD your God is giving you. Put them in a basket, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose as the place where his name will live.
Go to the priest who is in office at that time and say to him, "I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD promised our ancestors he would give us."
The priest will take the basket from your hands and set it down in front of the altar of the LORD your God.

Then you must say in the presence of the LORD your God: "My ancestor was a wandering Aramean, close to dying. He went down to Egypt with only a few people and lived there. There he became a great nation, strong and with many people.
But the Egyptians treated us badly and made us suffer. They forced us to do hard work as slaves.
Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors. The LORD heard our voice and saw our suffering, our hard work, and how we were being crushed.
So the LORD brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand and powerful arm, with terrifying power, and with miracles and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, LORD, I have brought the first part of the crops from the land you have given me." Then set the basket down in front of the LORD your God and bow down to worship before him.
Then you, the Levites, and the foreigners living among you must celebrate all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your family.

In the third year, the year of the tenth parts, when you have finished setting aside a tenth of all your crops, give it to the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows, so that they may eat in your towns and be full.

Then say to the LORD your God: "I have taken from my house the holy portion and given it to the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows, just as you commanded me. I have not turned away from your commands or forgotten any of them.

I have not eaten any of it while I was mourning. I have not removed any of it while I was unclean, and I have not offered any of it to the dead. I have obeyed the LORD my God. I have done everything you commanded me.
Look down from heaven, your holy home, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us, as you promised our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey."
Today the LORD your God commands you to obey these rules and laws. Be careful to obey them with all your heart and all your soul.
Today you have declared that the LORD is your God, and that you will live the way he wants, keep his rules, commands, and laws, and obey him.
And today the LORD has declared that you are his people, his own special treasure, as he promised, and that you must keep all his commands.
He will set you high above all the nations he has made, and give you praise, fame, and honour. You will be a people set apart as holy to the LORD your God, as he promised.
Moses and the leaders of Israel gave the people this command: "Obey all the commands I am giving you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan River into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up some large stones and cover them with plaster.

When you have crossed over, write on them all the words of this law. Then you will go into the land the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
When you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and cover them with plaster.
Build an altar there to the LORD your God, an altar made of stones. Do not use any iron tool on them.
Build the altar of the LORD your God with stones from the field that have not been cut. Offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
Sacrifice peace offerings there and eat them, and be glad in the presence of the LORD your God.
Write all the words of this law very clearly on the stones you have set up."
Then Moses and the priests, who were Levites, said to all Israel, "Be quiet and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
So obey the LORD your God, and keep his commands and rules that I am giving you today."
That same day Moses gave the people this command:
"When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes must stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these tribes must stand on Mount Ebal to announce the curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
The Levites must shout out to all the people of Israel:
'Cursed is anyone who makes an idol, carved or made of metal, and sets it up in secret. It is the work of a craftsman's hands, and the LORD hates it.' Then all the people must answer, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who dishonours their father or mother.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who moves their neighbour's boundary stone.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person the wrong way on the road.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who denies justice to foreigners, orphans, or widows.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's wife, because he dishonours his father.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who has sex with any animal.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, whether she is his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his mother-in-law.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who secretly kills their neighbour.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who does not keep the words of this law by obeying them.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'"
If you fully obey the LORD your God and carefully keep all his commands that I am giving you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations on earth.
All these blessings will come to you and stay with you if you obey the LORD your God:
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country.
Your children will be blessed, and so will the crops of your land and the young of your animals, the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.
Your basket and your bread bowl will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out.
The LORD will make sure that the enemies who attack you are defeated in front of you. They will come at you from one direction but run from you in seven.
The LORD will send a blessing on your barns and on everything you do. The LORD your God will bless you in the land he is giving you.
The LORD will make you his holy people, as he promised you, if you keep the commands of the LORD your God and live the way he wants.
Then all the peoples on earth will see that you belong to the LORD, and they will be afraid of you.
The LORD will give you plenty of good things: many children, many young animals, and rich crops, in the land he promised your ancestors he would give you.

The LORD will open the heavens, his rich storehouse, to send rain on your land at the right time and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations but will not need to borrow from any.

The LORD will make you the head and not the tail. You will always be on top and never at the bottom, if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today and carefully obey them.
Do not turn away from any of the commands I am giving you today, to the right or to the left, to follow other gods and serve them.
But if you do not obey the LORD your God and do not carefully keep all his commands and rules that I am giving you today, all these curses will come on you and catch up with you:
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country.
Your basket and your bread bowl will be cursed.
Your children will be cursed, and so will the crops of your land, the calves of your herds, and the lambs of your flocks.
You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.
The LORD will send on you curses, confusion, and failure in everything you try to do, until you are destroyed and quickly come to ruin, because of the evil you did in turning away from me.
The LORD will make deadly diseases cling to you until he has wiped you off the land you are going in to take over.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, with fever and swelling, with burning heat and drought, and with crops ruined by disease and mould. These will chase you until you are destroyed.
The sky over your head will be like bronze, and the ground under your feet like iron.
Instead of rain, the LORD will send down powder and dust on your land from the sky until you are destroyed.
The LORD will make sure that you are defeated by your enemies. You will come at them from one direction but run from them in seven. You will become a terrible sight to all the kingdoms on earth.
Your dead bodies will be food for all the birds and wild animals, and there will be no one to scare them away.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, and with growths, sores, and itching that cannot be cured.
The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind.
At midday you will feel your way around like a blind person in the dark. You will not succeed in anything you do. Day after day you will be treated badly and robbed, and no one will rescue you.
You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will take her and sleep with her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not enjoy its fruit.

Your ox will be killed in front of you, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be taken from you by force and will not be given back. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will rescue them.
Your sons and daughters will be given to another nation, and you will wear out your eyes looking for them all day long, but you will be powerless to do anything.
A people you do not know will eat what your land produces and what you have worked hard for. All your life you will be treated badly and crushed.
The things you see will drive you mad.
The LORD will strike your knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be cured, spreading from the soles of your feet to the top of your head.
The LORD will send you and the king you set over you to a nation that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will worship other gods, gods made of wood and stone.
You will become a thing of horror, a joke, and an insult to all the nations where the LORD will send you.
You will plant much seed in the field but harvest little, because locusts will eat it.
You will plant vineyards and take care of them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees all over your land, but you will not use the oil, because the olives will drop off.
You will have sons and daughters, but you will not keep them, because they will be taken away as prisoners.
Swarms of locusts will take over all your trees and the crops of your land.
The foreigners who live among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
They will lend to you, but you will not lend to them. They will be the head, and you will be the tail.
All these curses will come on you. They will chase you and catch up with you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the LORD your God and keep the commands and rules he gave you.
These curses will be a sign and a warning to you and your descendants forever.
You did not serve the LORD your God joyfully and gladly when you had plenty of everything.
So you will serve the enemies the LORD sends against you. You will be hungry and thirsty, without clothes, and lacking everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
The LORD will bring a nation against you from far away, from the ends of the earth, swooping down like an eagle. It will be a nation whose language you do not understand,
a fierce-looking nation that has no respect for the old and no pity for the young.
They will eat the young of your animals and the crops of your land until you are destroyed. They will leave you no grain, new wine, or olive oil, and no calves or lambs, until you are ruined.

They will surround and attack all your towns throughout your land, until the high, strong walls you trusted in fall down. They will attack all the towns throughout the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Because of the terrible suffering your enemy will bring on you during the attack, you will eat your own children, the flesh of the sons and daughters the LORD your God has given you.
Even the most gentle and kind man among you will have no pity on his own brother, the wife he loves, or the children he has left.

He will not give any of them a share of the flesh of his children that he is eating, because it will be all he has left, because of the terrible suffering your enemy will bring on you in all your towns.

The most gentle and delicate woman among you, so delicate that she would not even try to touch the ground with the sole of her foot, will have no pity on the husband she loves or on her own son or daughter.

She will secretly eat the afterbirth from her own body and the children she gives birth to, because she will have nothing else to eat. This will happen because of the terrible suffering your enemy will bring on you in your towns.
If you do not carefully obey all the words of this law written in this book, and do not fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God,
then the LORD will send terrible disasters on you and your descendants: severe and lasting disasters, and terrible and lasting illnesses.
He will bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt that you were so afraid of, and they will cling to you.
The LORD will also bring on you every kind of sickness and disaster not written in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.
Though you were as many as the stars in the sky, only a few of you will be left, because you did not obey the LORD your God.
Just as it pleased the LORD to do good to you and make you grow in number, so it will please him to ruin you and destroy you. You will be pulled up out of the land you are going in to take over.

Then the LORD will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship other gods, gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your ancestors have known.
Among those nations you will find no peace and no place to rest your feet. There the LORD will give you a worried heart, eyes tired from longing, and a hopeless spirit.
Your life will always be in danger. You will be filled with fear night and day, never sure that you will live.
In the morning you will say, "If only it were evening!" and in the evening, "If only it were morning!" because of the terror that fills your heart and the things you see with your eyes.

The LORD will send you back to Egypt in ships, on a journey I said you would never make again. There you will try to sell yourselves to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.
These are the words of the covenant the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Mount Sinai.
Moses called all the Israelites together and said to them: You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials, and to his whole land.
You saw the great troubles, the miraculous signs, and the great wonders.
But to this day the LORD has not given you a heart that understands, eyes that see, or ears that hear.
For forty years I led you through the desert. During that time your clothes did not wear out, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You did not eat bread or drink wine or other strong drink. He did this so that you would know that he is the LORD your God.
When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight us, but we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as a share to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and to half the tribe of Manasseh.
So carefully obey the words of this covenant, so that you will succeed in everything you do.
Today all of you are standing in the presence of the LORD your God: your leaders and your tribes, your elders and officials, and all the other men of Israel,
together with your children and wives, and the foreigners living in your camps who cut your wood and carry your water.
You are standing here to enter into a covenant with the LORD your God, a covenant he is making with you today and sealing with a promise.
Today he is making you his people, and he will be your God, just as he promised you and as he promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
I am not making this covenant, with its promise, only with you
who are standing here with us today in the presence of the LORD our God. I am also making it with those who are not here with us today.
You yourselves know how we lived in Egypt and how we passed through the nations on our way here.
You saw their disgusting things and their idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold.

Make sure there is no man or woman, family or tribe among you today whose heart turns away from the LORD our God to go and worship the gods of those nations. Make sure there is no root among you that grows bitter poison.

When such a person hears the words of this curse, they may bless themselves in their heart and think, "I will be safe, even if I keep going my own stubborn way." This will bring disaster on the watered land and the dry land alike.

The LORD will never be willing to forgive them. His anger and jealousy will burn against that person like smoke. All the curses written in this book will fall on them, and the LORD will wipe out their name from under heaven.
The LORD will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law.
Your children who come after you, and foreigners who come from far-away lands, will see the disasters that have struck the land and the diseases the LORD has sent on it.

The whole land will be burning sulphur and salt. Nothing will be planted, nothing will grow, and not even weeds will come up. It will be like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD destroyed in his fierce anger.
All the nations will ask, "Why has the LORD done this to this land? Why is he so terribly angry?"
And the answer will be: "It is because these people abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, the covenant he made with them when he brought them out of Egypt.
They went and worshipped other gods and bowed down to them, gods they did not know, gods the LORD had not given them.
That is why the LORD's anger burned against this land, and he brought on it all the curses written in this book.
In great anger and fury the LORD pulled them up out of their land and threw them into another land, where they are today."
The secret things belong to the LORD our God. But the things he has shown us belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may obey all the words of this law.
All these blessings and curses I have set before you will come on you. Then, in the nations where the LORD your God scatters you, you will remember them.
And when you and your children return to the LORD your God and obey him with all your heart and all your soul, doing everything I am commanding you today,
then the LORD your God will bring you back from captivity. He will have mercy on you and gather you again from all the nations where he scattered you.
Even if you have been sent away to the farthest land under heaven, the LORD your God will gather you from there and bring you back.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land that belonged to your ancestors, and you will own it again. He will make you more successful and more numerous than your ancestors.
The LORD your God will change your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, so that you will love him with all your heart and all your soul, and live.
The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies, who hate you and who treated you cruelly.
You will again obey the LORD and keep all his commands that I am giving you today.

Then the LORD your God will make you successful in all the work of your hands. He will bless you with many children, many young animals, and rich crops. The LORD will again be glad to do good to you, just as he was glad to do good to your ancestors,
if you obey the LORD your God and keep his commands and rules written in this Book of the Law, and turn to the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
What I am commanding you today is not too hard for you or out of your reach.
It is not up in heaven, so that you have to ask, "Who will go up to heaven to get it and tell it to us, so that we can obey it?"
Nor is it on the other side of the sea, so that you have to ask, "Who will cross the sea to get it and tell it to us, so that we can obey it?"
No, the word is very near you. It is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can obey it.
Look, today I am setting before you a choice between life and good things, and death and disaster.

For today I command you to love the LORD your God, to live the way he wants, and to keep his commands, rules, and laws. Then you will live and grow in number, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are going in to take over.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are led astray to bow down to other gods and worship them,
I warn you today that you will certainly be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take over.
Today I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Now choose life, so that you and your children may live.

Choose to love the LORD your God, obey him, and hold tightly to him. For the LORD is your life, and he will give you many years in the land he promised to give your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them, "I am now a hundred and twenty years old, and I am no longer able to lead you. The LORD has told me, 'You will not cross the Jordan.'
The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations in front of you, and you will take over their land. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD said.
The LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, whom he destroyed along with their land.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you must do to them everything I have commanded you.
Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, for the LORD your God goes with you. He will never leave you or abandon you."

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him in front of all Israel, "Be strong and brave, for you must go with these people into the land the LORD promised their ancestors he would give them. You must divide it among them as their share.
The LORD himself goes ahead of you and will be with you. He will never leave you or abandon you. Do not be afraid, and do not lose heart."
So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the descendants of Levi, who carried the Ark of the LORD's Covenant, and to all the leaders of Israel.
Then Moses commanded them, "At the end of every seven years, in the year for cancelling debts, during the Festival of Shelters,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose, you must read this law aloud to all Israel so they can hear it.

Gather the people together, men, women, and children, and the foreigners living in your towns, so that they can listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and carefully obey all the words of this law.
Their children, who do not know this law, must also hear it and learn to fear the LORD your God for as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take over."
The LORD said to Moses, "The time of your death is near. Call Joshua and come to the Tent of Meeting, where I will give him his orders." So Moses and Joshua went and stood at the Tent of Meeting.
Then the LORD appeared at the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood over the entrance to the Tent.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are going to rest with your ancestors, and these people will soon be unfaithful to me. They will chase after the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me and break the covenant I made with them.

On that day my anger will burn against them. I will abandon them and hide my face from them, and they will be destroyed. Many disasters and troubles will come on them, and on that day they will ask, 'Have these disasters not come on us because our God is not with us?'
And I will certainly hide my face on that day because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods.
Now write down this song and teach it to the Israelites. Have them sing it, so that it may be a witness for me against them.

When I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey, the land I promised their ancestors, and when they have eaten all they want and become fat, they will turn to other gods and worship them. They will reject me and break my covenant.

And when many disasters and troubles come on them, this song will stand as a witness against them, because their descendants will not forget it. I know what they are planning even now, before I bring them into the land I promised them."
So Moses wrote down this song that same day and taught it to the Israelites.
The LORD gave this command to Joshua son of Nun: "Be strong and brave, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I promised them, and I myself will be with you."
Moses finished writing the words of this law in a book, from beginning to end.
Then he gave this command to the Levites who carried the Ark of the LORD's Covenant:
"Take this Book of the Law and put it beside the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD your God. It will stay there as a witness against you.
For I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still alive and with you, you have been rebelling against the LORD. How much more will you rebel after I die!
Gather to me all the leaders of your tribes and all your officials, so that I can speak these words to them and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after I die you are sure to become completely evil and turn away from the way I have commanded you. In days to come disaster will fall on you, because you will do what is evil in the LORD's sight and make him angry by what your hands have made."
Then Moses recited all the words of this song, from beginning to end, to the whole assembly of Israel.
Listen, heavens, and I will speak. Hear, earth, the words from my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain, and my words come down like dew, like gentle rain on new grass, like showers on young plants.
I will announce the name of the LORD. Praise the greatness of our God!
He is the Rock, and his work is perfect. Everything he does is just. He is a faithful God who does no wrong. He is fair and right.
But they have acted wickedly toward him. Because of their sin they are no longer his children. They are a twisted and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish and senseless people? Is he not your Father, who made you his own? He created you and formed you.
Remember the days of long ago. Think about the generations of the past. Ask your father, and he will tell you. Ask your elders, and they will explain it to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their lands, when he divided up the human race, he set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD's own share is his people. Jacob is the part he chose for himself.
