He found him in a desert land, in an empty land of howling winds. He surrounded him and cared for him. He protected him like the pupil of his own eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, he spread out his wings to catch them and carried them on his feathers.
The LORD alone led him. No foreign god was with him.
He let him ride over the high places of the land and eat the crops of the fields. He fed him with honey from the rock and olive oil from the hard stone,
with butter from the herd and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs and goats, with fine rams from Bashan, and with the best wheat. You drank wine made from the juice of grapes.
Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, heavy, and full of food. Then he abandoned the God who made him and rejected the Rock who saved him.
They made him jealous with foreign gods and angered him with their hateful idols.
They sacrificed to demons, which are not God, to gods they had not known, new gods that had only just appeared, gods your ancestors did not fear.
You forgot the Rock who became your father. You forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw this and rejected them, because his sons and daughters had made him angry.
He said, "I will hide my face from them and see what happens to them in the end. For they are a twisted generation, children who cannot be trusted.

They made me jealous with something that is not a god and angered me with their worthless idols. So I will make them jealous with people who are not a nation. I will make them angry with a nation that has no understanding.
For my anger has started a fire that burns down to the deepest grave. It will burn up the earth and its crops and set fire to the foundations of the mountains.
I will pile disasters on them and use up all my arrows against them.
They will waste away from hunger and be eaten up by burning fever and deadly disease. I will send wild animals with their teeth against them, and poisonous snakes that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will kill their children. Inside their homes, terror will strike. Young men and young women will die, babies and old men with grey hair.
I said I would scatter them far away and wipe out all memory of them from the earth.
But I was afraid of what their enemies would say. Their enemies might misunderstand and say, 'We won by our own power. It was not the LORD who did all this.'"
Israel is a nation without sense. There is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise and understood this! If only they would think about what will happen to them in the end!
How could one enemy chase a thousand of them, or two enemies make ten thousand run away, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?
For their rock is not like our Rock. Even our enemies agree with that.
Their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are full of poison, and their bunches are bitter.
Their wine is like the poison of snakes, the deadly venom of cobras.
"Have I not kept this in store, sealed up in my treasure rooms?
It is mine to pay back and to punish. In due time their feet will slip. Their day of disaster is near, and their ruin is rushing toward them."
The LORD will do justice for his people and have mercy on his servants, when he sees that their strength is gone and no one is left, neither slave nor free.
He will say, "Now where are their gods, the rock they ran to for safety,
the gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let those gods get up and help you! Let them protect you!
See now that I, I alone, am he. There is no other god beside me. I put to death and I bring to life. I wound and I heal. No one can rescue anyone from my hand.
I lift my hand to heaven and make this promise: As surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword and take hold of it to judge, I will pay back my enemies and punish those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will eat flesh: the blood of the killed and the captured, the heads of the enemy leaders."
Celebrate with his people, you nations, for he will pay back those who killed his servants. He will punish his enemies and make his land and his people clean again.
Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and recited all the words of this song so the people could hear.
When Moses had finished reciting all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you today. Command your children to carefully obey all the words of this law.
These are not just empty words for you. They are your life. By obeying them you will live a long time in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take over."
That same day the LORD said to Moses,
"Go up into the Abarim Mountains to Mount Nebo in Moab, across from Jericho. Look out over Canaan, the land I am giving the Israelites as their own.
There on the mountain you have climbed you will die and join your people who have died before you, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.
For both of you were unfaithful to me in front of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Desert of Zin. You did not show my holiness among the Israelites.
So you will see the land only from a distance. You will not enter the land I am giving the Israelites."
This is the blessing Moses, the man of God, gave the Israelites before he died.

He said: "The LORD came from Mount Sinai and rose like the sun over them from Seir. He shone out from Mount Paran. He came with tens of thousands of holy ones, with flaming fire at his right hand for them.
Truly he loves his people. All his holy ones are in your hand. They bow down at your feet, and each one receives your words.
Moses gave us the law, a treasure for the people of Jacob.
The LORD became king over Jeshurun when the leaders of the people gathered, all the tribes of Israel together.
Let Reuben live and not die, and let his people not be few."
This is what he said about Judah: "LORD, hear the cry of Judah, and bring him back to his people. With his own hands he fights for himself. Help him against his enemies!"
About Levi he said: "LORD, your Thummim and Urim belong to your faithful servant. You tested him at Massah and argued with him at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father and mother, 'I do not care about them.' He did not take the side of his brothers or his own children. For the Levites obeyed your word and kept your covenant.
They will teach your laws to Jacob and your teaching to Israel. They will offer incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar.
LORD, bless all his skills, and be pleased with the work of his hands. Crush the backs of those who rise against him. Strike down those who hate him, so that they never rise again."
About Benjamin he said: "Let the one the LORD loves live safely beside him. The LORD protects him all day long, and the one the LORD loves rests between his shoulders."
About Joseph he said: "May the LORD bless his land with the precious gifts of heaven above, with dew, and with the deep waters that lie below.
May it have the best crops the sun brings and the finest fruit each month can give,
with the best gifts of the ancient mountains and the riches of the everlasting hills,

with the best gifts of the earth and everything in it, and the kindness of the one who appeared in the burning bush. Let all these blessings rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the one who was a prince among his brothers.

He has the majesty of a firstborn bull. His horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will push back the nations, even those at the ends of the earth. Such are the tens of thousands of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh."
About Zebulun he said: "Be glad, Zebulun, when you go out, and you, Issachar, in your tents.
They will call the peoples to the mountain and offer right sacrifices there. They will feast on the riches of the seas and the treasures hidden in the sand."
About Gad he said: "Blessed is the one who makes Gad's land larger! Gad lives there like a lion, tearing at arm and head.
He chose the best land for himself. The share of a leader was kept for him. When the leaders of the people gathered, he carried out the LORD's justice and his laws for Israel."
About Dan he said: "Dan is a lion's cub, leaping out from Bashan."
About Naphtali he said: "Naphtali is full of the LORD's favour and filled with his blessing. He will take over the land to the west and the south."
About Asher he said: "Asher is the most blessed of the sons. May he be loved by his brothers, and may his land be rich with olive oil.
May the bars of your gates be iron and bronze, and may your strength last as long as you live.
There is no one like the God of Jeshurun, who rides across the heavens to help you, across the skies in his majesty.
The eternal God is your safe home, and his everlasting arms are under you. He drove out your enemy ahead of you, saying, 'Destroy them!'
So Israel will live in safety. Jacob's descendants will live alone in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drop dew.

How happy you are, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is your shield and helper, and your glorious sword. Your enemies will bow before you, and you will walk on their high places."
Then Moses climbed from the plains of Moab up to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. There the LORD showed him the whole land, from Gilead as far as Dan,
all of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the Mediterranean Sea,
the Negev in the south, and the whole valley of Jericho, the City of Palm Trees, as far as Zoar.

Then the LORD said to him, "This is the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it."
So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in Moab, as the LORD had said.
The LORD buried him in a valley in Moab, across from Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is.
Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died. Yet his eyesight was still good, and he was still strong.
The Israelites mourned for Moses on the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses was over.
Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had placed his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did what the LORD had commanded Moses.
Since then, no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
No one has done all the miraculous signs and wonders the LORD sent him to do in Egypt, to Pharaoh, to all his officials, and to his whole land.
No one has ever shown the mighty power or done the awesome things that Moses did in front of all Israel.
Josh: After Moses, the servant of the LORD, died, the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' helper.
He said, "My servant Moses is dead. So now get up. Cross the Jordan River, you and all these people, into the land I am giving to the people of Israel.
I have given you every place where you put your foot, just as I promised Moses.
Your land will stretch from the desert and Lebanon to the great Euphrates River, all the land of the Hittites, and west to the Great Sea.
No one will be able to stand against you all your life. I will be with you just as I was with Moses. I will never leave you or give up on you.
Be strong and brave, because you will lead these people to take the land I promised their ancestors.
Only be strong and very brave. Be careful to obey all the law my servant Moses gave you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you will do well wherever you go.
Keep this book of the law always on your lips. Think about it day and night, so that you will be careful to do everything written in it. Then you will do well and succeed.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid, and do not lose heart, because the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
Then Joshua gave orders to the leaders of the people.
He said, "Go through the camp and tell the people, 'Get food ready. In three days you will cross the Jordan to go in and take the land the LORD your God is giving you.'"
Joshua also spoke to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said, "Remember what Moses, the servant of the LORD, told you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest, and he will give you this land.'

Your wives, your children and your animals may stay in the land Moses gave you east of the Jordan. But all your strong fighting men must cross over ahead of your brothers, armed and ready, and help them,

until the LORD gives them rest as he has given you, and they also take the land the LORD your God is giving them. After that you may go back to your own land east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you."
They answered Joshua, "We will do everything you have told us, and we will go wherever you send us.
We obeyed Moses in everything, and we will obey you too. Only may the LORD your God be with you as he was with Moses.
Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words will be put to death. Only be strong and brave!"

Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim. He said, "Go and look over the land, especially Jericho." So they went and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and they stayed there.
Someone told the king of Jericho, "Look, some men of Israel came here tonight to spy out the land."
So the king of Jericho sent a message to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came into your house. They have come to spy out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
When it was getting dark, at the time to shut the city gate, the men left. I do not know where they went. Chase after them quickly. You may catch them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax she had laid out there.
So the king's men chased them along the road to the river crossings of the Jordan. As soon as they had gone out, the gate was shut.
Before the spies lay down to sleep, Rahab went up to them on the roof.
She said to them, "I know that the LORD has given you this land. We are terrified of you, and everyone who lives here is melting with fear because of you.

We have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt. We heard what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you completely destroyed.
When we heard it, our hearts melted, and everyone lost courage because of you. For the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
So now, please promise me by the LORD that you will be kind to my family, because I have been kind to you. Give me a sure sign
that you will spare the lives of my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters and all who belong to them. Save us from death."
The men said to her, "Our lives for yours! If you do not tell anyone what we are doing, we will be kind and faithful to you when the LORD gives us the land."
So she let them down by a rope through the window, because her house was built into the city wall, and she lived on the wall.
She said to them, "Go to the hills so the men chasing you will not find you. Hide there for three days until they come back. Then you can go on your way."
The men said to her, "We will be free from this promise you made us swear,
unless, when we come into the land, you tie this red cord in the window you let us down through. Bring your father, your mother, your brothers and all your family into your house.
If anyone goes out of your house into the street, their death will be their own fault, and we will not be to blame. But if anyone in the house with you is harmed, we will be to blame.
But if you tell anyone what we are doing, we will be free from the promise you made us swear."
She said, "Let it be as you say." She sent them away, and they left. Then she tied the red cord in the window.
They went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the men chasing them had gone back. The chasers searched all along the road but did not find them.
Then the two men came down from the hills, crossed the river and came to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "The LORD has surely given the whole land into our hands. Everyone who lives there is melting with fear because of us."
Early in the morning Joshua and all the people of Israel set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan. They camped there before crossing.
After three days the leaders went through the camp
and gave the people this order: "When you see the priests, the Levites, carrying the covenant box of the LORD your God, leave your places and follow it.
But keep a space of about a kilometre between you and the box. Do not go near it. Then you will know which way to go, because you have never been this way before."
Joshua told the people, "Make yourselves holy, because tomorrow the LORD will do amazing things among you."
Joshua told the priests, "Lift up the covenant box and go ahead of the people." So they lifted it up and went ahead of them.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so they will know that I am with you just as I was with Moses.
Tell the priests carrying the covenant box, 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's water, stand still in the river.'"
Joshua said to the people of Israel, "Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God."

He said, "This is how you will know that the living God is among you, and that he will surely drive out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites and Jebusites ahead of you.
Look, the covenant box of the Lord of all the earth is going ahead of you into the Jordan.
Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.
When the feet of the priests carrying the box of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, touch the water of the Jordan, the water flowing down will stop and stand up in one heap."
So the people left their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the covenant box ahead of them.
It was harvest time, when the Jordan overflows all its banks. As soon as the priests carrying the box reached the river and their feet touched the edge of the water,

the water coming down stopped flowing. It piled up in one heap far away, at the town of Adam near Zarethan. The water flowing down to the Dead Sea was completely cut off. So the people crossed over near Jericho.
The priests carrying the LORD's covenant box stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed on dry ground, until the whole nation had crossed over.
When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
"Choose twelve men from the people, one from each tribe,
and tell them, 'Take twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests stood. Carry them with you and put them down where you camp tonight.'"
So Joshua called the twelve men he had chosen from Israel, one from each tribe.
He said to them, "Go ahead of the box of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you lift a stone onto your shoulder, one for each tribe of Israel.
This will be a sign among you. In the future, when your children ask you, 'What do these stones mean?'

tell them, 'The water of the Jordan stopped flowing in front of the LORD's covenant box. When it crossed the Jordan, the water was cut off. These stones will remind the people of Israel of this forever.'"

So the people of Israel did as Joshua told them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one for each tribe, as the LORD had told Joshua. They carried them to their camp and put them down there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, where the priests carrying the covenant box had stood. They are still there today.
The priests carrying the box stayed standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything the LORD had told Joshua to do was done, just as Moses had told Joshua. The people hurried across.
When all the people had crossed, the LORD's box and the priests crossed over while the people watched.
The men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed, ahead of the people of Israel, as Moses had told them.
About forty thousand men, armed and ready for war, crossed over before the LORD to the plains of Jericho for battle.
That day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel. They respected him all his life, just as they had respected Moses.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
"Tell the priests carrying the box of the covenant law to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua told the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan!"
The priests carrying the LORD's covenant box came up out of the river. As soon as their feet touched dry ground, the water of the Jordan flowed back and overflowed its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the east side of Jericho.
At Gilgal Joshua set up the twelve stones they had taken out of the Jordan.
He said to the people of Israel, "In the future, when your children ask their parents, 'What do these stones mean?'
tell them, 'Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.'
For the LORD your God dried up the Jordan in front of you until you had crossed, just as he dried up the Red Sea in front of us until we had crossed.
He did this so that all the peoples of the earth would know that the LORD's power is great, and so that you would always honour the LORD your God."

All the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings by the sea heard how the LORD had dried up the Jordan for the people of Israel until we had crossed. Their hearts melted with fear, and they lost all courage because of Israel.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make knives out of flint stone and circumcise the men of Israel again."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the men of Israel at a place called the Hill of Foreskins.
This is why he did it: all the men who left Egypt, all the fighting men, had died in the desert on the way.
All the men who came out of Egypt had been circumcised, but the boys born in the desert on the journey from Egypt had not.

The people of Israel had walked in the desert for forty years, until all the fighting men who left Egypt had died, because they did not obey the LORD. The LORD had sworn that they would not see the land he promised their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So Joshua circumcised their sons, whom God raised up in their place. They were not circumcised, because no one had done it on the journey.
After the whole nation was circumcised, they stayed in the camp until they were healed.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the shame of Egypt from you." So that place is called Gilgal to this day.
While the people of Israel camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, they celebrated the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month.
The day after the Passover, they ate food grown in the land: bread made without yeast and roasted grain.
The manna stopped the day after they ate food from the land. The people of Israel no longer had manna. That year they ate the crops of Canaan.
When Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him holding a sword. Joshua went to him and asked, "Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?"
He answered, "Neither. I have come as the commander of the LORD's army." Joshua bowed with his face to the ground and worshipped. He asked, "What does my lord want to say to his servant?"
The commander of the LORD's army said, "Take off your sandals, because the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
The gates of Jericho were shut tight because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Look, I have given Jericho into your hands, with its king and its strong fighters.
March around the city once with all your fighting men. Do this for six days.
Have seven priests carry seven trumpets made from rams' horns ahead of the covenant box. On the seventh day, march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.
When you hear them play one long blast on the trumpets, have all the people give a loud shout. Then the city wall will fall down flat, and everyone will go straight in."
So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said, "Lift up the covenant box, and have seven priests carry trumpets ahead of the LORD's box."
He told the people, "Go forward! March around the city, with the armed men going ahead of the LORD's box."
When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests with the seven trumpets went forward before the LORD, blowing their trumpets, and the LORD's covenant box followed them.
The armed men marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the box. All this time the trumpets kept sounding.
But Joshua had told the people, "Do not shout or raise your voices. Do not say a word until the day I tell you to shout. Then shout!"
So he had the LORD's box carried around the city once. Then the people went back to camp and spent the night there.
Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests lifted up the LORD's box.

The seven priests with the seven trumpets kept marching ahead of the LORD's box, blowing the trumpets. The armed men went in front of them, and the rear guard followed the box. The trumpets kept sounding.
On the second day they marched around the city once and went back to camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they got up at dawn and marched around the city in the same way, but this time seven times. It was the only day they went around seven times.
The seventh time around, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua told the people, "Shout! The LORD has given you the city!
The city and everything in it must be set apart to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute and everyone with her in her house will be spared, because she hid the spies we sent.
But stay away from the things set apart for destruction. If you take any of them, you will bring destruction and trouble on the camp of Israel.
All the silver and gold, and everything made of bronze and iron, is holy to the LORD. It must go into the LORD's treasury."
So the priests blew the trumpets, and the people shouted. When they heard the trumpet sound and gave a loud shout, the wall fell down flat. Everyone charged straight in, and they took the city.
With their swords they destroyed everything in the city: men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep and donkeys.
Joshua told the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring her out with all her family, as you promised her."

So the young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and put them in a place outside the camp of Israel.
Then they burned the whole city and everything in it. But they put the silver, the gold, and the things made of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD's house.
Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her family and all who belonged to her. She lives among the Israelites to this day, because she hid the men Joshua sent to spy on Jericho.

At that time Joshua made the people take this oath: "May the man who tries to rebuild the city of Jericho be cursed before the LORD. His oldest son will die when he lays its foundations, and his youngest son will die when he sets up its gates."
So the LORD was with Joshua, and he became famous all through the land.

But the Israelites were unfaithful about the things set apart for destruction. Achan, son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of them. So the LORD was very angry with Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, near Beth Aven, east of Bethel. He told them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.
They came back to Joshua and said, "Not all the people need to go. Send about two or three thousand men to attack Ai. Do not tire out the whole army, because there are only a few people there."
So about three thousand men went up, but they ran away from the men of Ai.

The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them. They chased the Israelites from the city gate as far as Shebarim and struck them down on the slope. The people's hearts melted with fear and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and lay face down on the ground in front of the LORD's box until evening. The leaders of Israel did the same and threw dust on their heads.

Joshua said, "Oh, Lord GOD, why did you bring these people across the Jordan at all? Just to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been happy to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned and run from its enemies?
The Canaanites and everyone else in the land will hear about it. They will surround us and wipe our name off the earth. Then what will you do for your own great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying on your face?

Israel has sinned. They have broken my covenant that I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of the things set apart for destruction. They have stolen, they have lied, and they have hidden the things with their own belongings.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn and run, because they themselves are now set apart for destruction. I will not be with you any more unless you destroy what is set apart among you.

Get up! Make the people holy. Tell them, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow, because the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There are things set apart for destruction among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them.

In the morning, come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe the LORD chooses will come forward clan by clan. The clan the LORD chooses will come forward family by family. The family the LORD chooses will come forward man by man.
The one caught with the forbidden things will be burned with fire, along with all he has, because he broke the LORD's covenant and did a shameful thing in Israel.'"
Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was chosen.
The clans of Judah came forward, and the clan of Zerah was chosen. The clan of Zerah came forward man by man, and Zabdi's family was chosen.
Zabdi's family came forward man by man, and Achan, son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was chosen.
Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and confess to him. Tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.

Among the things we took, I saw a beautiful robe from Babylon, about two kilograms of silver, and a bar of gold weighing more than half a kilogram. I wanted them, so I took them. They are buried in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things out of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the gold bar, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent and everything he had, to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought this trouble on us? Today the LORD will bring trouble on you." Then all Israel stoned him. They stoned the rest and burned them with fire.

They piled a large heap of stones over him, which is still there today. Then the LORD turned away from his fierce anger. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Achor, which means Trouble, to this day.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or lose heart. Take the whole army with you and go up to Ai. Look, I have given you the king of Ai, his people, his city and his land.
Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho and its king. But this time you may keep its goods and animals for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
So Joshua and the whole army got ready to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand of his best fighting men and sent them out at night.
He ordered them, "Listen. Hide behind the city and wait. Do not go far from it. All of you stay ready.
I and all the people with me will come up to the city. When the men of Ai come out against us as they did before, we will run away from them.
They will chase us until we have drawn them away from the city, because they will say, 'They are running from us like last time.' While we run,
you get up from your hiding place and take the city. The LORD your God will give it into your hands.
When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do what the LORD has said. These are my orders."
Then Joshua sent them off. They went to their hiding place and waited between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night with the people.
Early the next morning Joshua gathered the army, and he and the leaders of Israel led them up to Ai.
All the fighting men with him went up close to the city and camped north of Ai, with a valley between them and the city.
Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
So the soldiers took their places: the main army north of the city and the ambush west of it. That night Joshua went down into the valley.
When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his men hurried out early in the morning to fight Israel at the place facing the Jordan valley. He did not know that men were hiding behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel pretended to be beaten, and they ran toward the desert.
All the men in Ai were called out to chase them. They chased Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
Not one man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city wide open while they chased Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out the spear in your hand toward Ai, because I will give the city to you." So Joshua held out his spear toward the city.
As soon as he did this, the men in hiding rose up quickly and ran into the city. They took it and quickly set it on fire.

The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. They had no chance to escape in any direction, because the Israelites who had been running toward the desert turned back against them.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and smoke was rising from it, they turned around and attacked the men of Ai.
The men in the city also came out against them, so the men of Ai were trapped in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. Israel struck them down until none were left alive and none escaped.
But they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

Israel finished killing all the men of Ai in the fields and the desert where they had chased them. When every one of them had fallen by the sword, all Israel went back to Ai and killed those who were in it.
Twelve thousand men and women died that day, all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not lower the hand holding out his spear until he had destroyed everyone who lived in Ai.
But Israel kept the animals and goods of the city for themselves, as the LORD had told Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai and made it a ruin forever, an empty place still today.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua ordered them to take the body down and throw it at the entrance of the city gate. They piled a large heap of stones over it, which is still there today.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. It was written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of uncut stones, which no iron tool had touched. On it they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.
There, while the Israelites watched, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law that Moses had written.

All Israel, foreigners and Israelites alike, with their leaders, officers and judges, stood on both sides of the covenant box of the LORD, facing the Levite priests who carried it. Half of them stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal. Moses, the servant of the LORD, had told them to do this when the people of Israel were first blessed.
Then Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, just as they are written in the book of the law.
He read every word Moses had commanded. He did not leave out one. He read it to the whole gathering of Israel, including the women, the children and the foreigners living among them.

All the kings west of the Jordan heard about these things: the kings in the hill country, in the western foothills, and all along the coast of the Great Sea as far as Lebanon. They were the kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
They joined together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel.
But when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
they came up with a trick. They pretended to be messengers from far away. They loaded their donkeys with worn-out sacks and old wineskins that were cracked and mended.
They wore old patched sandals and old clothes. All the bread they carried was dry and mouldy.
They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, "We have come from a country far away. Please make a peace treaty with us."
The men of Israel said to these Hivites, "But maybe you live near us. How can we make a treaty with you?"
They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua asked, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
They answered, "We, your servants, have come from a very distant country because of the fame of the LORD your God. We have heard all about him and everything he did in Egypt,
and what he did to the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
So our leaders and all the people of our country told us, 'Take food for the journey. Go and meet them and say, We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us.'
This bread was still warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But look how dry and mouldy it is now.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look how cracked they are. Our clothes and sandals are worn out from the very long journey."
The Israelites tasted some of their food, but they did not ask the LORD what to do.
So Joshua made peace with them and a treaty to let them live, and the leaders of the people swore an oath to keep it.
Three days after making the treaty, the Israelites heard that these people were their neighbours, living close by.
So the Israelites set out, and on the third day they came to their towns: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath Jearim.
But the Israelites did not attack them, because their leaders had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. All the people grumbled against the leaders.
But the leaders answered, "We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, so we cannot touch them now.
This is what we will do: we will let them live, so that God's anger does not fall on us for breaking our oath."
The leaders said, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water carriers for all the people, as the leaders had decided.
Then Joshua called the Gibeonites and said, "Why did you trick us by saying, 'We live far away from you,' when you actually live right here among us?
Now you are under a curse. Some of you will always be servants, cutting wood and carrying water for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "We were told clearly that the LORD your God commanded his servant Moses to give you this whole land and to destroy all its people as you came. We were very afraid for our lives because of you, so we did this.
Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you."
So Joshua did that. He saved them from the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
That day Joshua made the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the people and for the altar of the LORD, at the place the LORD would choose. They still do this today.

Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and completely destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king. He also heard that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them.
He and his people were very afraid, because Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal cities. It was bigger than Ai, and all its men were strong fighters.
So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent a message to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon.
He said, "Come and help me attack Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the people of Israel."
So the five Amorite kings, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon, joined forces. They marched out with all their armies, camped around Gibeon and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants! Come quickly and save us! Help us, because all the Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together against us."
So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his best fighting men.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I have given them into your hands. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."
Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and took them by surprise.
The LORD threw them into panic in front of Israel. Israel defeated them badly at Gibeon and chased them along the road up to Beth Horon, striking them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

As they ran from Israel down the road from Beth Horon, the LORD threw huge hailstones down on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hail than from the swords of the Israelites.
On the day the LORD gave the Amorites to Israel, Joshua spoke to the LORD. In front of all Israel he said, "Sun, stand still over Gibeon! Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon!"

So the sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation had beaten its enemies. This is written in the Book of Jashar. The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and waited about a whole day before going down.
There has never been a day like it, before or since, when the LORD listened to a human voice like that. Surely the LORD was fighting for Israel!
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.
Now the five kings had run away and hidden in a cave at Makkedah.
Someone told Joshua, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll large stones over the mouth of the cave, and put men there to guard it.
But do not stop! Chase your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, because the LORD your God has given them into your hands."
Joshua and the Israelites defeated them very badly, almost wiping them out. The few who survived escaped into their walled cities.
Then all the army came back safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah. After that, no one dared to say a word against the Israelites.
Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me."
So they brought the five kings out of the cave: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

When they brought the kings to Joshua, he called all the men of Israel. He said to the army commanders who had come with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or lose heart. Be strong and brave. This is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you fight."
Then Joshua struck and killed the kings and hung them on five trees. They hung there until evening.
At sunset Joshua ordered them to be taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave where they had hidden. Large stones were placed over the mouth of the cave, and they are still there today.

That day Joshua captured Makkedah. He killed its king and everyone in the city with the sword. He completely destroyed it and left no survivors. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked it.
The LORD gave Libnah and its king into Israel's hands too. Joshua killed everyone in the city with the sword and left no survivors. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel moved on from Libnah to Lachish. They camped around it and attacked it.
The LORD gave Lachish into Israel's hands, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He killed everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army, leaving no survivors.
Then Joshua and all Israel moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped around it and attacked it.
They captured it that same day and killed everyone in it with the sword. Joshua completely destroyed it, as he had done to Lachish.
Then Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.
They captured it and killed its king, everyone in it, and the people of its villages with the sword. They left no survivors. Just as at Eglon, they completely destroyed it and everyone in it.
Then Joshua and all Israel turned and attacked Debir.

They captured the city, its king and its villages, and killed everyone in it with the sword. They left no survivors. Joshua did to Debir and its king what he had done to Hebron and to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua conquered the whole region: the hill country, the Negev in the south, the western foothills and the mountain slopes, with all their kings. He left no survivors. He completely destroyed everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua conquered them from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their lands in one campaign, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.
When Jabin king of Hazor heard about this, he sent messages to Jobab king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Akshaph,
and to the kings in the northern hill country, in the Jordan valley south of the Sea of Galilee, in the western foothills, and in the hills of Dor to the west.
He also sent to the Canaanites in the east and the west, to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites and Jebusites in the hill country, and to the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the region of Mizpah.
They came out with all their armies, a huge crowd of soldiers, as many as the grains of sand on the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.
All these kings joined together and camped at the Waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Israel, dead. You must cut the leg muscles of their horses and burn their chariots."
So Joshua and his whole army came against them suddenly at the Waters of Merom and attacked them.

The LORD gave them into Israel's hands. Israel defeated them and chased them all the way to Greater Sidon, to Misrephoth Maim, and east to the Valley of Mizpah. They struck them down until no survivors were left.
Joshua did to them what the LORD had told him. He cut the leg muscles of their horses and burned their chariots.
Then Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and killed its king with the sword. Hazor had been the leader of all these kingdoms.
They killed everyone in it with the sword and completely destroyed them. Nothing that breathed was left alive, and Joshua burned Hazor.
Joshua captured all these royal cities and their kings. He killed them with the sword and completely destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
But Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds, except Hazor, which Joshua burned.
The Israelites kept for themselves all the goods and animals from these cities. But they killed all the people with the sword until they had destroyed them. They left no one alive who breathed.
The LORD had given orders to his servant Moses, and Moses gave them to Joshua, and Joshua obeyed them. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Joshua took this whole land: the hill country, the whole Negev, the whole region of Goshen, the western foothills, the Jordan valley, and the hill country of Israel with its foothills,
from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, to Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down and put them to death.
Joshua fought against all these kings for a long time.
Not one city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites living in Gibeon. Israel took all the others in battle.
The LORD himself made their hearts stubborn so that they would fight against Israel. That way they would be completely destroyed without mercy, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua went and wiped out the Anakites from the hill country: from Hebron, Debir and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and of Israel. Joshua completely destroyed them and their towns.
No Anakites were left in Israel's land. Only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod did some survive.
So Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had told Moses. He gave it to Israel as their own land, divided among their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.
These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites defeated east of the Jordan, whose land they took, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, including all the eastern side of the Jordan valley:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, from the middle of the valley, and half of Gilead, up to the Jabbok River, which is the border of the Ammonites.
He also ruled the eastern Jordan valley from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea, toward Beth Jeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.
They also took the land of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaites, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
He ruled over Mount Hermon, Salekah and all of Bashan, up to the border of the people of Geshur and Maakah, and half of Gilead, up to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites defeated them. And Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave their land to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh as their own.

These are the kings Joshua and the Israelites defeated west of the Jordan, from Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as their own, divided among them.

It included the hill country, the western foothills, the Jordan valley, the mountain slopes, the desert and the Negev, the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. These were the kings:
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, near Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron Meron, one; the king of Akshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor on the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goyim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. There were thirty-one kings in all.
When Joshua was old and had lived many years, the LORD said to him, "You are now very old, and there is still a great deal of land left to be taken.
This is the land that is left: all the regions of the Philistines and the Geshurites,

from the Shihor River on the border of Egypt north to the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite land. It includes the land of the five Philistine rulers in Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, and the land of the Avvites
in the south. It also includes all the land of the Canaanites, from Arah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and the border of the Amorites,
and the land of the people of Gebal, and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal Gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo Hamath.

As for all the people of the mountains from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, all the Sidonians, I myself will drive them out ahead of the Israelites. Be sure to give this land to Israel as their own, as I have told you.
So now divide this land among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh as their own."
The other half of Manasseh, with the tribes of Reuben and Gad, had already received the land Moses gave them east of the Jordan. Moses, the servant of the LORD, had given it to them.
It stretched from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the town in the middle of the valley, and included the whole plain of Medeba as far as Dibon,
and all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, up to the border of the Ammonites.
It also included Gilead, the land of the people of Geshur and Maakah, all of Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salekah,
the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who had ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last of the Rephaites. Moses had defeated them and driven them out.
But the Israelites did not drive out the people of Geshur and Maakah, so they still live among the Israelites today.
But Moses gave no land to the tribe of Levi. The food offerings burned to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their share, as he promised them.
This is what Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan:
Their land stretched from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the middle of the valley, and the whole plain past Medeba,
to Heshbon and all its towns on the plain, including Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar on the hill in the valley,
Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth Jeshimoth.

It included all the towns on the plain and the whole kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Moses had defeated him and the leaders of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, princes who lived in the land and served Sihon.
Among those killed, the Israelites also killed with the sword Balaam son of Beor, who practised fortune-telling.
The western border of Reuben was the Jordan River. These towns and their villages were the land given to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan.
This is what Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, clan by clan:
Their land included Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, near Rabbah.
It stretched from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir.

In the valley it included Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Sukkoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon. Its western border was the Jordan, as far as the end of the Sea of Galilee, east of the Jordan.
These towns and their villages were the land given to the tribe of Gad, clan by clan.
This is what Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, clan by clan:
Their land stretched from Mahanaim and included all of Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the settlements of Jair in Bashan, sixty towns.
Half of Gilead, with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan, was given to the descendants of Makir son of Manasseh, for half of Makir's descendants, clan by clan.
This is how Moses divided the land when he was on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan east of Jericho.
But Moses gave no land to the tribe of Levi. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their share, as he promised them.
This is how the land of Canaan was shared out among the Israelites. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the family groups of the tribes divided it among them.
The land for the nine and a half tribes was given out by drawing lots, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Moses had already given the two and a half tribes their land east of the Jordan, but he gave the Levites no land among them.
Joseph's descendants had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites received no share of the land, only towns to live in, with fields around them for their animals and belongings.
So the Israelites divided the land, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh Barnea about you and me.
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land. I brought back an honest report, just as I believed it.
But the others who went with me made the people's hearts melt with fear. I, however, followed the LORD my God with all my heart.
So on that day Moses swore to me, 'The land you walked on will belong to you and your children forever, because you followed the LORD my God with all your heart.'
Now look, the LORD has kept me alive for forty-five years, just as he promised, since the time he said this to Moses, while Israel wandered in the desert. Today I am eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. I am just as able to go out to battle now as I was then.
So give me this hill country the LORD promised me that day. You heard then that the Anakites were there, with large walled cities. But with the LORD's help I will drive them out, just as he said."
Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his own land.
So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite ever since, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakites. Then the land had rest from war.
The land given by lot to the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, reached south to the border of Edom, to the Desert of Zin at the far south.
Their southern border began at the southern tip of the Dead Sea, at the bay facing south.
It went south of Scorpion Pass, on to Zin, and up to the south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it ran past Hezron, up to Addar, and curved around to Karka.
It went on to Azmon and followed the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. This was their southern border.
The eastern border was the Dead Sea, up to the mouth of the Jordan. The northern border began at the bay of the sea where the Jordan flows in.
It went up to Beth Hoglah and passed north of Beth Arabah, up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
Then it went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor and turned north toward Gilgal, which faces the Pass of Adummim, south of the valley. It went on to the waters of En Shemesh and ended at En Rogel.

Then the border went up the Valley of Ben Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city, which is Jerusalem. From there it climbed to the top of the hill west of the Hinnom Valley, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the hilltop the border went to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, on to the towns of Mount Ephron, and down toward Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim.
Then it curved west from Baalah to Mount Seir, ran along the northern slope of Mount Jearim, which is Kesalon, went down to Beth Shemesh and crossed to Timnah.
It went on to the northern slope of Ekron, turned toward Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, reached Jabneel, and ended at the sea.
The western border was the coast of the Great Sea. These were the borders around the land of the people of Judah, clan by clan.
As the LORD had commanded Joshua, he gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a share of land among the people of Judah. It was Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron. Arba was the father of Anak.
Caleb drove out the three Anakites from Hebron: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, descendants of Anak.
From there he marched against the people living in Debir, which used to be called Kiriath Sepher.
Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Aksah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Aksah as his wife.
When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
She answered, "Do me a special favour. Since you have given me land in the dry south, give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
This is the land given to the tribe of Judah, clan by clan.
Their towns in the far south, toward the border of Edom, were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron, which is Hazor,
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,
Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim, Ezem,
Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon. In all there were twenty-nine towns and their villages.
In the western foothills were Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Sokoh, Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim and Gederah, also called Gederothaim. There were fourteen towns and their villages.
Then Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,
Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Kabbon, Lahmas, Kitlish,
Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah and Makkedah. There were sixteen towns and their villages.
Then Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Akzib and Mareshah. There were nine towns and their villages.
Then Ekron, with its towns and villages,
and everything west of Ekron near Ashdod, with their villages.
Then Ashdod with its towns and villages, and Gaza with its towns and villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt and the coast of the Great Sea.
In the hill country were Shamir, Jattir, Sokoh,
Dannah, Kiriath Sannah, which is Debir,
Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon and Giloh. There were eleven towns and their villages.
Then Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, and Zior. There were nine towns and their villages.
Then Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah and Timnah. There were ten towns and their villages.
Then Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,
Maarath, Beth Anoth and Eltekon. There were six towns and their villages.
Then Kiriath Baal, which is Kiriath Jearim, and Rabbah. There were two towns and their villages.
In the desert were Beth Arabah, Middin, Sekakah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi. There were six towns and their villages.
But the people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites still live there with the people of Judah today.
The land given by lot to Joseph's descendants began at the Jordan near Jericho, east of the springs of Jericho. It went up from Jericho through the desert and the hill country to Bethel.
From Bethel, which is Luz, it went on to the land of the Arkites at Ataroth.
Then it went down west to the land of the Japhletites, as far as Lower Beth Horon, then on to Gezer, and ended at the sea.
So Manasseh and Ephraim, the descendants of Joseph, received their land.
This was the land of Ephraim, clan by clan. Their border on the east went from Ataroth Addar to Upper Beth Horon,
and on to the sea. From Mikmethath on the north it curved east to Taanath Shiloh and passed by it to Janoah on the east.
Then it went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and came out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border went west to the Kanah Ravine and ended at the sea. This was the land of the tribe of Ephraim, clan by clan.
It also included all the towns and villages set apart for Ephraim inside the land of Manasseh.
They did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. To this day the Canaanites live among the people of Ephraim, but they are made to do forced labour.

This was the land given by lot to the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's oldest son. Makir was Manasseh's oldest son and the father of Gilead. Because Makir's family were great fighters, they had already received Gilead and Bashan.

So this land was for the rest of Manasseh's descendants, clan by clan: the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
But Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah and Tirzah.

They went to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders and said, "The LORD told Moses to give us land among our relatives." So Joshua gave them land among their father's brothers, as the LORD had commanded.
So Manasseh received ten shares of land, besides Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan,
because the daughters of Manasseh's family received land along with the sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.
Manasseh's border went from Asher to Mikmethath, east of Shechem. Then it went south to the people living at En Tappuah.
The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town of Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to Ephraim.

Then the border went down to the Kanah Ravine. South of the ravine there were towns belonging to Ephraim, though they were among Manasseh's towns. Manasseh's border ran along the north side of the ravine and ended at the sea.
The land to the south belonged to Ephraim, and the land to the north to Manasseh. The sea was Manasseh's western border. It touched Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

Inside the lands of Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had Beth Shan, Ibleam, and the people of Dor, Endor, Taanach and Megiddo, each with its villages. The third one on the list was Naphoth, meaning the hills.
But the people of Manasseh could not drive out the people of these towns, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites do forced labour, but they did not drive them out completely.
Joseph's descendants said to Joshua, "Why have you given us only one share of land? We are a large people, because the LORD has blessed us greatly."
Joshua answered, "If you are so many, and the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go up into the forest and clear land for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaites."
They replied, "The hill country is not big enough for us. And all the Canaanites living on the plains have iron chariots, both those in Beth Shan and its towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
But Joshua said to the descendants of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are many people, and you are very strong. You will not have only one share.
The forested hill country will be yours too. Clear it, and all of it will be yours. You can drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
The whole community of Israel gathered at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there. The land was now under their control.
But seven tribes of Israel had still not received their share of land.
So Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you wait before you go and take the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?
Choose three men from each tribe. I will send them out to travel through the land and write a description of it, showing how it can be shared. Then they will come back to me.
They are to divide the land into seven parts. Judah will stay in its land in the south, and Joseph's descendants in their land in the north.
Write descriptions of the seven parts and bring them here to me. Then I will draw lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God.

The Levites, however, get no share among you, because serving as priests of the LORD is their share. And Gad, Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their land east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."
As the men set out, Joshua told them, "Go through the land and write a description of it. Then come back to me, and I will draw lots for you here at Shiloh before the LORD."
So the men went through the land and wrote a description of it in a book, town by town, in seven parts. Then they came back to Joshua in the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua drew lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD, and there he shared out the land to the Israelites, tribe by tribe.
The first lot came out for the tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan. Their land lay between the land of Judah and the land of Joseph.
On the north side their border began at the Jordan, ran along the northern slope of Jericho, and went west into the hill country, coming out at the desert of Beth Aven.
From there it crossed to the southern slope of Luz, which is Bethel, and went down to Ataroth Addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth Horon.

From the hill facing Beth Horon on the south, the border turned south along the western side and ended at Kiriath Baal, which is Kiriath Jearim, a town of the people of Judah. This was the western side.
The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim on the west and went to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

The border went down to the foot of the hill facing the Valley of Ben Hinnom, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Hinnom Valley along the southern slope of the Jebusite city, and on down to En Rogel.
Then it curved north, went to En Shemesh, continued to Geliloth, which faces the Pass of Adummim, and went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
It went on to the northern slope facing the Jordan valley and down into the valley.
Then it went to the northern slope of Beth Hoglah and ended at the northern bay of the Dead Sea, where the Jordan flows in. This was the southern border.
The Jordan formed the border on the east side. These were the borders all around the land given to the clans of Benjamin.
The tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan, had these towns: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,
Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
Kephar Ammoni, Ophni and Geba. There were twelve towns and their villages.
Then Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city, which is Jerusalem, Gibeah and Kiriath. There were fourteen towns and their villages. This was the land given to the clans of Benjamin.
The second lot came out for the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan. Their land lay inside the land of Judah.
Their land included Beersheba, also called Sheba, Moladah,
Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth Markaboth, Hazar Susah,
Beth Lebaoth and Sharuhen. There were thirteen towns and their villages.
Then Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan. There were four towns and their villages,
and all the villages around these towns as far as Baalath Beer, which is Ramah in the south. This was the land of the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan.
Simeon's land was taken from Judah's share, because Judah had more land than it needed. So the people of Simeon received their land inside Judah's land.
The third lot came out for Zebulun, clan by clan. Their border went as far as Sarid.
It went west to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and reached the ravine near Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise to the land of Kisloth Tabor, went on to Daberath and up to Japhia.
From there it went east to Gath Hepher and Eth Kazin, came out at Rimmon, and turned toward Neah.
On the north the border went around to Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah El.
It included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem. There were twelve towns and their villages.
These towns and their villages were the land of Zebulun, clan by clan.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, clan by clan.
Their land included Jezreel, Kesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah and Beth Pazzez.
The border touched Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth Shemesh, and ended at the Jordan. There were sixteen towns and their villages.
These towns and their villages were the land of the tribe of Issachar, clan by clan.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
Their land included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Akshaph,
Allammelek, Amad and Mishal. On the west the border touched Carmel and Shihor Libnath.
Then it turned east toward Beth Dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah El, and went north to Beth Emek and Neiel, passing Kabul on the left.
It went to Abdon, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
Then the border turned back toward Ramah and went to the walled city of Tyre. It turned toward Hosah and ended at the sea, in the region of Akzib.
It also included Ummah, Aphek and Rehob. There were twenty-two towns and their villages.
These towns and their villages were the land of the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
The sixth lot came out for Naphtali, clan by clan.
Their border went from Heleph and the big tree in Zaanannim, past Adami Nekeb and Jabneel to Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
Then the border went west through Aznoth Tabor and on to Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
The walled towns were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,
Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath and Beth Shemesh. There were nineteen towns and their villages.
These towns and their villages were the land of the tribe of Naphtali, clan by clan.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of Dan, clan by clan.
Their land included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,
Me Jarkon and Rakkon, with the area facing Joppa.

But the people of Dan had trouble taking their land. So they went up and attacked Leshem. They captured it, killed its people with the sword, and settled there. They renamed Leshem as Dan, after their ancestor Dan.
These towns and their villages were the land of the tribe of Dan, clan by clan.
When they had finished dividing the land into its shares, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun a share among them.
As the LORD had commanded, they gave him the town he asked for, Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the town and lived there.

These are the shares of land that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the family groups of the tribes of Israel gave out by lot at Shiloh, before the LORD, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
"Tell the Israelites to choose the cities of safety that I told you about through Moses.
Anyone who kills a person by accident, without meaning to, can run to one of these cities. There they will be safe from the relative who wants to take revenge for the death.

The person must run to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate, and explain what happened to the leaders of that city. Then the leaders must take them into the city and give them a place to live among them.
If the relative seeking revenge chases them, the leaders must not hand the person over, because they killed their neighbour by accident and did not hate them before.

They must stay in that city until they have stood trial before the community, and until the death of the high priest serving at that time. Then they may go back to their own home in the town they ran from."
So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
East of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they chose Bezer in the desert plain from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the cities chosen for all the Israelites and for any foreigners living among them. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run there and not be killed by the relative seeking revenge before standing trial before the community.
Then the family leaders of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family leaders of the other tribes of Israel.
At Shiloh in the land of Canaan they said to them, "The LORD commanded through Moses that you give us towns to live in, with fields around them for our animals."
So, as the LORD had commanded, the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and fields from their own land.
The first lot came out for the Kohathite clans. The descendants of Aaron the priest, who were Levites, received thirteen towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin.
The rest of Kohath's descendants received ten towns from the clans of the tribes of Ephraim and Dan and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershon received thirteen towns from the clans of the tribes of Issachar, Asher and Naphtali and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, clan by clan, received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave these towns and their fields to the Levites by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they gave the following towns, named here.
They went to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clans of the Levites, because the first lot came out for them.
They gave them Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, with the fields around it, in the hill country of Judah. Arba was the father of Anak.
But the farmland and villages around the city had already been given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his own.
So to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, a city of safety for anyone who had killed someone, together with Libnah,
Jattir, Eshtemoa,
Holon, Debir,
Ain, Juttah and Beth Shemesh, each with its fields. That was nine towns from these two tribes.
From the tribe of Benjamin they gave them Gibeon, Geba,
Anathoth and Almon, each with its fields. That was four towns.
In all, the priests descended from Aaron received thirteen towns with their fields.
The rest of the Kohathite clans of the Levites received towns by lot from the tribe of Ephraim.
They received Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, a city of safety for anyone who had killed someone, and Gezer,
Kibzaim and Beth Horon, each with its fields. That was four towns.
From the tribe of Dan they received Eltekeh, Gibbethon,
Aijalon and Gath Rimmon, each with its fields. That was four towns.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh they received Taanach and Gath Rimmon, each with its fields. That was two towns.
In all, the rest of the Kohathite clans received ten towns with their fields.
