Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada. Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur's wife was named Abihail. She gave birth to Ahban and Molid.
Nadab's sons were Seled and Appaim. Seled died without having children.
Appaim's son was Ishi. Ishi's son was Sheshan. Sheshan's son was Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother, were Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without having children.
Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza. These were Jerahmeel's descendants.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter to his servant Jarha as his wife, and she gave birth to Attai.
Attai was the father of Nathan. Nathan was the father of Zabad.
Zabad was the father of Ephlal. Ephlal was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jehu. Jehu was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Helez. Helez was the father of Eleasah.
Eleasah was the father of Sismai. Sismai was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Jekamiah. Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and his son Mareshah, who was the father of Hebron.
Hebron's sons were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema was the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.
Shammai's son was Maon. Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
Caleb's concubine Ephah gave birth to Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.
Jahdai's sons were Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Caleb's concubine Maacah gave birth to Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also gave birth to Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and to Sheva, the father of Machbena and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
These were Caleb's descendants. The sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, were Shobal, the father of Kiriath Jearim,
Salma, the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph, the father of Beth Gader.
The descendants of Shobal, the father of Kiriath Jearim, were Haroeh and half of the Menuhoth people.
The clans of Kiriath Jearim were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The people of Zorah and Eshtaol came from these clans.
Salma's descendants were the people of Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.
The clans of scribes who lived at Jabez were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the ancestor of the family of Rechab.
These were the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. The second was Daniel, whose mother was Abigail from Carmel.
The third was Absalom, whose mother was Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. The fourth was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith.
The fifth was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital. The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was David's wife Eglah.
These six were born to David in Hebron, where he ruled for seven years and six months. Then he ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
These sons were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. Their mother was Bathshua, the daughter of Ammiel. These were four.
There were also Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. These were nine.
All these were David's sons, not counting the sons of his concubines. Their sister was Tamar.
Solomon's son was Rehoboam. Rehoboam's son was Abijah. Abijah's son was Asa. Asa's son was Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat's son was Joram. Joram's son was Ahaziah. Ahaziah's son was Joash.
Joash's son was Amaziah. Amaziah's son was Azariah. Azariah's son was Jotham.
Jotham's son was Ahaz. Ahaz's son was Hezekiah. Hezekiah's son was Manasseh.
Manasseh's son was Amon. Amon's son was Josiah.
Josiah's sons were Johanan, the firstborn; Jehoiakim, the second; Zedekiah, the third; and Shallum, the fourth.
Jehoiakim's descendants were his son Jeconiah and his son Zedekiah.
The sons of Jeconiah, who was taken prisoner, were his son Shealtiel,
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Pedaiah's sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's sons were Meshullam and Hananiah. Their sister was Shelomith.
Zerubbabel had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed.
Hananiah's descendants were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah, and the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, and the sons of Shecaniah.
Shecaniah's son was Shemaiah. Shemaiah's six descendants were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
Neariah's three sons were Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
Elioenai's seven sons were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
Judah's descendants were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Shobal's son Reaiah was the father of Jahath. Jahath was the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Zorathites.
These were the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was named Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah and the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah gave birth to Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were Naarah's sons.
Helah's sons were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz was the father of Anub and Zobebah, and the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.
Jabez was more respected than his brothers. His mother had named him Jabez, saying, "I gave birth to him in pain."
Jabez prayed to the God of Israel, "Please bless me and give me more land! Let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm, so that I will not have pain!" And God gave him what he asked for.
Chelub, Shuhah's brother, was the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton was the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, the father of Ir Nahash. These were the men of Recah.
Kenaz's sons were Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel's son was Hathath.
Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who founded Ge Harashim, the Valley of Craftsmen, because its people were skilled workers.
The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh were Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Ezrah's sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. One of Mered's wives gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.

His wife from Judah gave birth to Jered, the father of Gedor, Heber, the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel, the father of Zanoah. The others were the children of Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, whom Mered had married.
The sons of Hodiah's wife, the sister of Naham, were the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's descendants were Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
The sons of Shelah son of Judah were Er, the father of Lecah, Laadah, the father of Mareshah, and the clans of linen workers at Beth Ashbea.
There were also Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph, who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi Lehem. These records come from very ancient times.
They were the potters who lived at Netaim and Gederah. They lived there and worked for the king.
Simeon's sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shaul's son was Shallum. Shallum's son was Mibsam. Mibsam's son was Mishma.
Mishma's descendants were his son Hammuel, Hammuel's son Zaccur, and Zaccur's son Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters. But his brothers did not have many children, so their whole clan did not grow as large as the tribe of Judah.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until David became king.
Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, five towns,
along with all the villages around these towns as far as Baal. These were the places where they lived, and they kept a record of their family history.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah.
These men named here were leaders of their clans. Their families grew very large.
They went as far as the entrance to Gedor, to the east side of the valley, looking for pasture for their flocks.
They found rich, good pasture there. The land was wide open, quiet, and peaceful. Some descendants of Ham had lived there before.

These men whose names are listed came during the time of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites in their tents and the Meunites who lived there, and destroyed them completely, as can still be seen today. Then they settled in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.
Five hundred of these Simeonites went to the hill country of Seir. Their leaders were Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They killed the remaining Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

These were the sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn. He really was the firstborn, but because he slept with one of his father's wives, his rights as the firstborn son were given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. So Reuben is not listed in the family records as the firstborn.
Judah became the strongest of his brothers, and a ruler came from him. But the rights of the firstborn belonged to Joseph.
The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Joel's descendants were his son Shemaiah, Shemaiah's son Gog, Gog's son Shimei,
Shimei's son Micah, Micah's son Reaiah, Reaiah's son Baal,
and Baal's son Beerah. Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria took Beerah away as a prisoner. Beerah was a leader of the tribe of Reuben.
His relatives by clans, as listed in their family records, were Jeiel the chief, Zechariah,
and Bela son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel. They lived in the area from Aroer to Nebo and Baal Meon.
To the east they settled land as far as the edge of the desert that stretches to the Euphrates River, because their herds had grown too large for the land of Gilead.
While Saul was king, they went to war against the Hagrites and defeated them. Then they lived in the Hagrites' tents throughout the whole area east of Gilead.
The tribe of Gad lived next to them, in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah.
Joel was the chief, Shapham was second, then Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.
Their relatives, by families, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven in all.
These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, was the head of their families.
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon, as far as they reached.
All of these were recorded in the family records during the time of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.

The tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh had forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty men ready for war. They were brave men who could carry shields and swords, shoot with bows, and were trained for battle.
They went to war against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

God helped them in the fighting, and he handed the Hagrites and all their allies over to them. This was because they cried out to God during the battle, and he answered them because they trusted in him.
They captured the Hagrites' animals: fifty thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, and two thousand donkeys. They also took one hundred thousand people captive.
Many enemies were killed, because the battle was God's. And they lived in that land until they were taken away as prisoners.
The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They grew in number and spread from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
These were the heads of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were brave warriors, famous men, and heads of their families.
But they were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors. They chased after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed ahead of them.

So the God of Israel stirred up Pul king of Assyria, also called Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria. He took the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh away as prisoners. He took them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they still are today.
Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Amram's children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar was the father of Phinehas. Phinehas was the father of Abishua.
Abishua was the father of Bukki. Bukki was the father of Uzzi.
Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth.
Meraioth was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah. Azariah was the father of Johanan.
Johanan was the father of Azariah, who served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Seraiah. Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak.
Jehozadak was taken away as a prisoner when the LORD sent the people of Judah and Jerusalem into exile through Nebuchadnezzar.
Levi's sons were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of Gershom's sons: Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites, listed by their families.
Gershom's descendants were his son Libni, Libni's son Jahath, Jahath's son Zimmah,
Zimmah's son Joah, Joah's son Iddo, Iddo's son Zerah, and Zerah's son Jeatherai.
Kohath's descendants were his son Amminadab, Amminadab's son Korah, Korah's son Assir,
Assir's son Elkanah, Elkanah's son Ebiasaph, Ebiasaph's son Assir,
Assir's son Tahath, Tahath's son Uriel, Uriel's son Uzziah, and Uzziah's son Shaul.
Elkanah's sons were Amasai and Ahimoth.
The descendants of Elkanah were his son Zophai, Zophai's son Nahath,
Nahath's son Eliab, Eliab's son Jeroham, and Jeroham's son Elkanah.
Samuel's sons were Joel, his firstborn, and Abijah, his second son.
Merari's descendants were Mahli, Mahli's son Libni, Libni's son Shimei, Shimei's son Uzzah,
Uzzah's son Shimea, Shimea's son Haggiah, and Haggiah's son Asaiah.
These are the men David put in charge of the music in the LORD's temple after the ark had been given a place to rest there.
They served with music in front of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the LORD's temple in Jerusalem. They did their work by taking turns, as they had been assigned.
These are the men who served, along with their sons. From the Kohathite clan was Heman the singer. He was the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.
Heman's relative Asaph stood at his right side. Asaph was the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
At Heman's left side stood their relatives from the Merarite clan. Their leader was Ethan son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
Their fellow Levites were given all the other work in the tabernacle, the house of God.

But Aaron and his descendants offered the sacrifices on the altar of burnt offering and burned incense on the altar of incense. They did all the work in the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel, just as Moses the servant of God had commanded.
These were Aaron's descendants: his son Eleazar, Eleazar's son Phinehas, Phinehas's son Abishua,
Abishua's son Bukki, Bukki's son Uzzi, Uzzi's son Zerahiah,
Zerahiah's son Meraioth, Meraioth's son Amariah, Amariah's son Ahitub,
Ahitub's son Zadok, and Zadok's son Ahimaaz.
These are the places where Aaron's descendants lived, the settlements within their land. The first share was given by drawing lots to Aaron's descendants from the Kohathite clan.
They were given Hebron in the land of Judah, with its pasturelands around it.
But the fields and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
So Aaron's descendants were given Hebron, a city of refuge. They were also given Libnah, Jattir, and Eshtemoa, each with its pasturelands,
Hilen and Debir, each with its pasturelands,
and Ashan and Beth Shemesh, each with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Benjamin they were given Geba, Allemeth, and Anathoth, each with its pasturelands. So the Kohathite clans received thirteen towns in all.
The rest of Kohath's descendants were given ten towns by drawing lots, from the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershom, clan by clan, were given thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, and from the part of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, clan by clan, were given twelve towns by drawing lots, from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave these towns and their pasturelands to the Levites.
By drawing lots, they gave them the towns already named from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
Some of the Kohathite clans were given towns from the tribe of Ephraim.
They were given Shechem, a city of refuge in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer, each with its pasturelands,
Jokmeam and Beth Horon, each with its pasturelands,
and Aijalon and Gath Rimmon, each with its pasturelands.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh, the rest of the Kohathite clans were given Aner and Bileam, each with its pasturelands.
The descendants of Gershom were given these towns: From the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, each with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh and Daberath, each with its pasturelands,
and Ramoth and Anem, each with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Asher, Mashal and Abdon, each with its pasturelands,
and Hukok and Rehob, each with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, each with its pasturelands.
The rest of the Levites, the descendants of Merari, were given these towns: From the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono and Tabor, each with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Reuben, on the east side of the Jordan River across from Jericho, Bezer in the desert and Jahzah, each with its pasturelands,
and Kedemoth and Mephaath, each with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim, each with its pasturelands,
and Heshbon and Jazer, each with its pasturelands.
Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel. They were heads of their families in the clan of Tola, and brave warriors. In David's time, the number of their descendants listed in the records was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. All five of them were chiefs.
Their family records show that they had thirty-six thousand men ready for war, because they had many wives and children.
Their relatives among all the clans of Issachar were brave warriors. In all, eighty-seven thousand were listed in the family records.
Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
Bela had five sons: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were heads of their families and brave warriors. Their family records listed twenty-two thousand and thirty-four fighting men.
Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were Becher's sons.
Their family records listed the heads of their families and twenty thousand two hundred brave warriors.
Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these descendants of Jediael were heads of families. They had seventeen thousand two hundred brave warriors ready to go to war.
Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir, and Hushim was the son of Aher.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were descendants of Bilhah.
Manasseh's descendants were Asriel, whose mother was his Aramean concubine. She also gave birth to Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife from the families of Huppim and Shuppim. His sister was named Maacah. Another descendant was named Zelophehad, and he had only daughters.
Machir's wife Maacah gave birth to a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
Gilead's sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's descendants were his son Shuthelah, Shuthelah's son Bered, Bered's son Tahath, Tahath's son Eleadah, Eleadah's son Tahath,
Tahath's son Zabad, and Zabad's son Shuthelah. Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead were killed by the men of Gath who were born in that land, when they went down to steal the people's cattle.
Their father Ephraim mourned for them a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him.
Then he slept with his wife again, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. He named him Beriah, because trouble had come to his family.
Ephraim's daughter was Sheerah. She built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, and Uzzen Sheerah.
Beriah's descendants were his son Rephah, Rephah's son Resheph, Resheph's son Telah, Telah's son Tahan,
Tahan's son Ladan, Ladan's son Ammihud, Ammihud's son Elishama,
Elishama's son Nun, and Nun's son Joshua.
Their lands and settlements included Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages, as far as Azzah and its villages.
Along the borders of Manasseh were Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, with their villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these towns.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and of their sister Shua.
Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were Japhlet's sons.
Shomer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of his brother Helem were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were descendants of Asher. They were heads of families, the best and bravest warriors, and outstanding leaders. Their family records listed twenty-six thousand men ready for war.
Benjamin's firstborn son was Bela. His second was Ashbel, his third was Aharah,
his fourth was Nohah, and his fifth was Rapha.
Bela's sons were Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These were the descendants of Ehud, the heads of the families living in Geba, who were forced to move to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera. Gera led them when they moved, and he was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim had children in the country of Moab after he had sent away his wives Hushim and Baara.
By his wife Hodesh he had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, and they were heads of families.
By Hushim he had Abitub and Elpaal.
Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed. Shemed built Ono and Lod and their villages.
Beriah and Shema were heads of the families living in Aijalon. They drove out the people of Gath.
Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were Beriah's sons.
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were Elpaal's sons.
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were Shimei's sons.
Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
Iphdeiah, and Penuel were Shashak's sons.
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were Jeroham's sons.
All these were heads of families, as listed in their family records. They were leaders, and they lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
and Mikloth, who was the father of Shimeah. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-Baal. Merib-Baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea. Binea's son was Raphah, Raphah's son was Eleasah, and Eleasah's son was Azel.
Azel had six sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were Azel's sons.
The sons of his brother Eshek were Ulam, his firstborn, Jeush, his second, and Eliphelet, his third.
Ulam's sons were brave warriors who could shoot with bows. They had many sons and grandsons, one hundred and fifty in all. All these were descendants of Benjamin.
So all Israel was listed in family records, and these are written in the book of the kings of Israel. The people of Judah were taken away as prisoners to Babylon because they were unfaithful to God.
The first people to move back to their own land and towns were ordinary Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
Some people from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.
From Judah there was Uthai son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani. He was a descendant of Perez son of Judah.
From the Shilonites there was Asaiah, the firstborn, and his sons.
From the descendants of Zerah there was Jeuel. In all, there were six hundred and ninety people from Judah.
From the tribe of Benjamin there was Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah.
There was also Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah.
Their relatives, as listed in the family records, numbered nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were heads of their families.
From the priests there were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
There was also Azariah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub. Azariah was the official in charge of God's temple.
There was Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah. And there was Maasai son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.
There were one thousand seven hundred and sixty priests in all, heads of their families. They were very able men, responsible for the work of serving in God's temple.
From the Levites there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, a descendant of Merari.
There were also Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph.
There was Obadiah son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun. And there was Berechiah son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was their chief.
Until then they had been stationed at the King's Gate on the east side. They were the gatekeepers for the camp of the Levites.

Shallum son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his relatives from his family, the Korahites, were in charge of guarding the entrances to the tent. Their ancestors had been in charge of guarding the entrance to the LORD's camp.
In earlier times Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of the gatekeepers, and the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

In all, two hundred and twelve men were chosen to be gatekeepers at the entrances. They were listed in the family records in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had given them their positions of trust.
So they and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the LORD's house, the house that was a tent.
The gatekeepers were on all four sides: east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives in their villages had to come from time to time and share their work for seven days at a time.
But the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were given the job of trust. They were in charge of the rooms and the treasuries in God's temple.
They spent the night around God's temple, because they had to guard it. And they had to open it every morning.
Some of them were in charge of the objects used in the temple service. They counted them when they were brought in and when they were taken out.
Others were put in charge of the furniture and all the other holy objects, and of the fine flour, the wine, the olive oil, the incense, and the spices.
But some of the priests were the ones who mixed the spices.
A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was trusted with baking the bread used for offerings.
Some of their relatives from the Kohathite clan were in charge of preparing the holy bread for the table every Sabbath.
Some were musicians, heads of Levite families. They lived in the temple rooms and did not have other duties, because they were busy with their work day and night.
All these were heads of Levite families, as listed in their family records. They were leaders, and they lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-Baal. Merib-Baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jarah. Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea. Binea's son was Rephaiah, Rephaiah's son was Eleasah, and Eleasah's son was Azel.
Azel had six sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.
The Philistines fought against Israel. The men of Israel ran away from them, and many were killed on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines chased Saul and his sons closely, and they killed Saul's sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
The fighting was fierce around Saul. The archers caught up with him and wounded him.

Saul said to the young man who carried his armour, "Pull out your sword and kill me with it. If you don't, these uncircumcised men will come and make fun of me and hurt me." But the young man was too afraid to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
When the armour bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his own sword and died.
So Saul and his three sons died, and all his family died together.
When all the Israelites in the valley saw that the army had run away and that Saul and his sons were dead, they left their towns and ran away too. Then the Philistines came and lived in those towns.
The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped Saul's body and took his head and his armour. Then they sent messengers all through the land of the Philistines to spread the news to their idols and to their people.
They put his armour in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of Dagon.
When all the people of Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
all their brave men went and took the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the great tree in Jabesh, and they went without food for seven days.
Saul died because he was unfaithful to the LORD. He did not obey the LORD's word. He even asked advice from a woman who talked to the spirits of the dead,
instead of asking the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and gave the kingdom to David son of Jesse.
Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, "Look, we are your own flesh and blood.

In the past, even while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out to battle and brought them back. And the LORD your God told you, 'You will be the shepherd of my people Israel. You will be the ruler over my people Israel.'"

So all the leaders of Israel came to King David at Hebron. David made an agreement with them there before the LORD, and they anointed him king over Israel, just as the LORD had promised through Samuel.
David and all Israel marched to Jerusalem, which was also called Jebus. The Jebusites lived there.
The people of Jebus told David, "You will never get in here!" But David captured the fortress of Zion, which became the City of David.
David had said, "Whoever leads the attack on the Jebusites will become the commander of the army." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, so he became the commander.
David moved into the fortress, so it was called the City of David.
He built up the city around it, from the Millo all the way around, and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
David became more and more powerful, because the LORD of Armies was with him.
These were the leaders of David's mighty warriors. Together with all Israel, they gave strong support to his rule and helped make him king, just as the LORD had promised Israel.
This is the list of David's mighty warriors: Jashobeam, a Hachmonite, was the chief of the Thirty. He once used his spear to kill three hundred men in one battle.
Next was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty warriors.
He was with David at Pasdammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. There was a field full of barley there, and the Israelite army ran away from the Philistines.
But Eleazar and David stood in the middle of the field and defended it. They killed the Philistines, and the LORD gave them a great victory.
Once, three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock by the cave of Adullam, while the Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
At that time David was in the fortress, and a group of Philistine soldiers was in Bethlehem.
David had a strong longing and said, "If only someone would bring me a drink of water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem!"

So the three warriors broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But David refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as an offering to the LORD.

He said, "God forbid that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?" Because they had risked their lives to bring it, David would not drink it. These were the brave deeds of the three mighty warriors.
Abishai, Joab's brother, was the chief of the Three. He once used his spear to kill three hundred men, and he became as famous as the Three.
He was honoured more than the other two of the Three and became their commander, but he was not one of the Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did great deeds. He killed two of Moab's greatest warriors. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

He killed an Egyptian who was very tall, about two and a quarter metres. The Egyptian had a spear as thick as a weaver's rod, but Benaiah went against him with only a club. He snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with it.
These were the brave deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who became as famous as the three mighty warriors.
He was honoured more than the Thirty, but he was not one of the Three. David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
The mighty warriors also included Asahel, Joab's brother; Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa; Abiezer from Anathoth;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai from Netophah; Heled son of Baanah from Netophah;
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin; Benaiah from Pirathon;
Hurai from the ravines of Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;
Azmaveth the Baharumite; Eliahba the Shaalbonite;
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite; Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite;
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite; Eliphal son of Ur;
Hepher the Mecherathite; Ahijah the Pelonite;
Hezro from Carmel; Naarai son of Ezbai;
Joel, Nathan's brother; Mibhar son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai from Beeroth, who carried the armour of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai;
Adina son of Shiza from Reuben, a chief of the Reubenites, and the thirty men with him;
Hanan son of Maacah; Joshaphat the Mithnite;
Uzzia from Ashtaroth; Shama and Jeiel, the sons of Hotham from Aroer;
Jediael son of Shimri and his brother Joha the Tizite;
Eliel the Mahavite; Jeribai and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam; Ithmah the Moabite;
Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul son of Kish. They were among the warriors who helped David in battle.
They were armed with bows and could shoot arrows or sling stones with either their right or left hand. They were relatives of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.
Their chief was Ahiezer, and then Joash, both sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. There were also Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu from Anathoth;
Ishmaiah from Gibeon, a mighty warrior among the Thirty and a leader of the Thirty; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad from Gederah;
Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite;
the Korahites Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam;
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

Some men from the tribe of Gad joined David at his fortress in the desert. They were brave warriors, trained for battle, who could use shield and spear. Their faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as fast as gazelles on the mountains.
Ezer was the chief, Obadiah was second, Eliab third,
Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,
Jeremiah tenth, and Machbannai eleventh.
These men from Gad were army commanders. The weakest of them could take on a hundred men, and the strongest a thousand.
They crossed the Jordan River in the first month of the year, when it was flooding all its banks. They chased away everyone living in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Some men from Benjamin and Judah also came to David at his fortress.

David went out to meet them and said, "If you have come in peace to help me, I am ready to join with you. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, even though I have done nothing wrong, may the God of our ancestors see it and punish you."

Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and he said, "We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, because your God helps you." So David welcomed them and made them leaders of his troops.

Some men from Manasseh also joined David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But David and his men did not help the Philistines. After talking it over, the Philistine rulers sent him away. They said, "It will cost us our heads if he goes back to his master Saul."
When David went to Ziklag, these men from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai. Each was a commander of a thousand in Manasseh.
They helped David fight against the raiding bands, because they were all brave warriors and commanders in his army.
Day after day men came to help David, until he had a great army, like the army of God.
These are the numbers of armed soldiers who came to David at Hebron to hand Saul's kingdom over to him, just as the LORD had said.
From Judah came six thousand eight hundred men armed for war, carrying shields and spears.
From Simeon came seven thousand one hundred brave warriors ready for battle.
From Levi came four thousand six hundred men.
Jehoiada, the leader of Aaron's family, came with three thousand seven hundred men,
and Zadok, a brave young warrior, came with twenty-two commanders from his family.
From Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, came three thousand men. Until then, most of them had stayed loyal to Saul's family.
From Ephraim came twenty thousand eight hundred brave warriors, famous in their own clans.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh came eighteen thousand men, chosen by name to come and make David king.
From Issachar came two hundred leaders who understood the times and knew what Israel should do. All their relatives followed their orders.
From Zebulun came fifty thousand experienced soldiers, ready for battle with every kind of weapon. They were completely loyal and ready to help David.
From Naphtali came one thousand commanders, with thirty-seven thousand men carrying shields and spears.
From Dan came twenty-eight thousand six hundred men ready for battle.
From Asher came forty thousand experienced soldiers ready for battle.
From the east side of the Jordan River, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, came one hundred and twenty thousand men armed with every kind of weapon.
All these were warriors who could take their places in battle. They came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. All the rest of the Israelites also agreed to make David king.
They stayed there with David for three days, eating and drinking, because their relatives had provided food for them.

Also, their neighbours from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. There were plenty of supplies: flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, olive oil, cattle, and sheep. There was great joy in Israel.
David talked things over with his commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and with every one of his leaders.

Then he said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If you think it is good, and if it is the will of the LORD our God, let's send word to our relatives everywhere in all the land of Israel. Let's also send word to the priests and Levites in their towns with pasturelands, so they can come and join us.
Then let's bring the ark of our God back to us, because we did not care about it while Saul was king."
The whole assembly agreed to do this, because everyone thought it was the right thing to do.
So David gathered all Israel, from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo Hamath, to bring God's ark from Kiriath Jearim.

David and all Israel went up to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim in Judah. They went to bring back the ark of God the LORD, who sits on his throne between the cherubim, the ark that is called by his name.
They carried God's ark on a new cart from Abinadab's house, and Uzza and Ahio were guiding the cart.
David and all the Israelites were celebrating before God with all their strength, singing and playing harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzza reached out his hand to steady the ark.
The LORD became very angry with Uzza, and he struck him down because he had touched the ark. So Uzza died there in front of God.
David was angry because the LORD had burst out in anger against Uzza. That place is still called Perez Uzza today.
David was afraid of God that day. He asked, "How can I ever bring God's ark home with me?"
So David did not take the ark with him into the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-Edom from Gath.
God's ark stayed with Obed-Edom's family in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his family and everything he had.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar logs, stonemasons, and carpenters to build a palace for him.
Then David knew that the LORD had made him king over Israel and had made his kingdom great for the sake of his people Israel.
In Jerusalem David married more wives and had more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, their whole army went up to hunt for him. But David heard about it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God, "Should I go and attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Go, and I will hand them over to you."

So David and his men went up to Baal Perazim, and there he defeated them. David said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like water breaking through a dam." That is why that place is called Baal Perazim.
The Philistines left their gods behind there, and David gave orders to burn them.
Once again the Philistines raided the valley.
So David asked God again, and God answered, "Do not attack them from the front. Go around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, because God has gone out ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."
David did what God commanded, and they struck down the Philistine army all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
So David became famous in every land, and the LORD made all the nations afraid of him.
David built houses for himself in the City of David. He also prepared a place for God's ark and set up a tent for it.
Then David said, "No one except the Levites may carry God's ark. The LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him forever."
David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the LORD's ark up to the place he had prepared for it.
He called together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
From the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the leader and one hundred and twenty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Merari, Asaiah the leader and two hundred and twenty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Gershom, Joel the leader and one hundred and thirty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the leader and two hundred of his relatives.
From the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the leader and eighty of his relatives.
From the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the leader and one hundred and twelve of his relatives.
Then David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. You and your relatives must make yourselves holy, so you can bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, up to the place I have prepared for it.
The first time, you Levites did not carry it, and so the LORD our God burst out in anger against us. We did not ask him how to do it the right way."
So the priests and Levites made themselves holy, so they could bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The Levites carried God's ark on their shoulders with the poles, just as Moses had commanded by the LORD's word.
David told the leaders of the Levites to appoint some of their relatives as singers. They were to play musical instruments, lyres, harps, and cymbals, and sing loud, joyful songs.
So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel, his relative Asaph son of Berechiah, and from their relatives the Merarites, Ethan son of Kushaiah.
With them were their relatives next in rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to play loud bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play harps tuned to a high pitch, called Alamoth.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead with lyres tuned to a low pitch, called Sheminith.
Chenaniah, a leader of the Levites, was in charge of the singing. He taught the singers because he was skilled at it.
Berechiah and Elkanah were to guard the ark.
The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer were to blow trumpets in front of God's ark. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also to guard the ark.
So David, the leaders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with great joy to bring the ark of the LORD's covenant up from Obed-Edom's house.
Because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the LORD's covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David was wearing a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, who led the singing. David was also wearing a linen ephod.
So all Israel brought up the ark of the LORD's covenant with shouts of joy, with the sound of rams' horns and trumpets, and with loud cymbals, harps, and lyres.
As the ark of the LORD's covenant came into the City of David, Saul's daughter Michal looked out of a window. When she saw King David dancing and celebrating, she hated him in her heart.
They brought God's ark in and set it inside the tent David had set up for it. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the LORD's name.
Then he gave every Israelite, man and woman, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
He appointed some of the Levites to serve in front of the LORD's ark, to call on, thank, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was the leader, and Zechariah was second. Then came Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, who played harps and lyres. Asaph played loud cymbals.
Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets regularly in front of the ark of God's covenant.
That day David first gave Asaph and his relatives the job of giving thanks to the LORD with this song:
Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the nations what he has done.
Sing to him! Sing praises to him! Tell about all his wonderful works.
Be proud of his holy name. Let the hearts of those who look for the LORD be glad.
Look to the LORD and his strength. Always look to him.
Remember the wonderful things he has done, his miracles, and the judgments he has spoken,
you descendants of his servant Israel, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the LORD our God. His judgments are seen in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the promise he made for a thousand generations.
It is the covenant he made with Abraham, the promise he swore to Isaac.
He made it a law for Jacob, an everlasting covenant for Israel.
He said, "I will give you the land of Canaan as your share to keep."
This was when you were only a few people, very few, and strangers in the land.
They wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.
He did not let anyone harm them. He warned kings because of them:
"Do not touch my anointed ones! Do not harm my prophets!"
Sing to the LORD, all the earth! Tell about his salvation every day.
Tell the nations about his glory. Tell all peoples about his wonderful works.
The LORD is great and most worthy of praise. He is to be respected above all gods.
All the gods of the nations are only idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Honour and majesty surround him. Strength and joy fill his dwelling place.
Give to the LORD, you families of the nations, give to the LORD glory and strength!
Give to the LORD the glory his name deserves. Bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in the beauty of his holiness.
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world stands firm. It cannot be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice! Let them say among the nations, "The LORD is King!"
Let the sea and everything in it roar! Let the fields and everything in them be joyful!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, because he is coming to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the LORD, because he is good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Say, "Save us, God our Saviour! Gather us and rescue us from the nations, so we can give thanks to your holy name and be glad as we praise you."
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, forever and ever. Then all the people said, "Amen!" and praised the LORD.
David left Asaph and his relatives there in front of the ark of the LORD's covenant, to serve there regularly, as each day's work required.
He also left Obed-Edom and his sixty-eight relatives to serve with them. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests in front of the LORD's tabernacle at the high place in Gibeon.
They were to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, following everything written in the Law of the LORD, which he gave to Israel.
With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the others chosen by name to give thanks to the LORD, "because his faithful love lasts forever."
Heman and Jeduthun were in charge of the trumpets, the cymbals, and the other instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.
Then all the people went home, and David went back home to bless his family.
After David had settled into his palace, he said to the prophet Nathan, "Look, I am living in a palace made of cedar, but the ark of the LORD's covenant is in a tent."
Nathan told David, "Do whatever you have in mind, because God is with you."
But that same night God's word came to Nathan. God said,
"Go and tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: You are not the one who will build me a house to live in.
I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel out of Egypt until today. I have moved from one tent to another and from one dwelling place to another.
Wherever I have moved with all Israel, did I ever ask any of the leaders I commanded to shepherd my people, "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?"'
So now, tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be the ruler over my people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have destroyed all your enemies in front of you. Now I will make your name as famous as the names of the greatest men on earth.

I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there, so they can live in their own home and never be disturbed again. Wicked people will no longer crush them, as they did at the beginning,
and as they did from the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will defeat all your enemies. I tell you that the LORD will build a house for you, a family line of kings.
When your life is over and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up one of your descendants, one of your own sons, to take your place. I will make his kingdom strong.
He is the one who will build a house for me, and I will make his throne last forever.
I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will never take my faithful love away from him, as I took it away from the king who ruled before you.
I will put him in charge of my house and my kingdom forever. His throne will last forever.'"
Nathan told David everything the LORD had said in this vision.
Then King David went in and sat before the LORD. He said, "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?
And as if this were not enough in your eyes, God, you have also spoken about the future of your servant's family. You have treated me as if I were a very important man, LORD God.
What more can I say to you for honouring your servant like this? You know your servant.
LORD, you have done this great thing for your servant's sake and because you wanted to. You have made all these great things known.
LORD, there is no one like you. There is no God except you, as we have heard with our own ears.

Is there any other nation on earth like your people Israel? God went out to rescue them to be his own people, and to make a name for yourself by doing great and wonderful things. You drove out nations ahead of your people, whom you rescued from Egypt.
You made your people Israel your very own forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
So now, LORD, let the promise you have made about your servant and his family stand forever. Do what you have promised.

Then your name will stand firm and be honoured forever. People will say, 'The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, is truly Israel's God!' And the family of your servant David will stand firm before you.
You, my God, have shown your servant that you will build a family line of kings for him. That is why your servant has found the courage to pray to you.
LORD, you are God! You have promised this good thing to your servant.
Now you have been pleased to bless your servant's family, so that it will continue forever before you. You, LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever."
Some time later, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Gath and its villages from the Philistines.
He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became David's servants and paid him taxes.
David also defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, near Hamath, when Hadadezer went to set up his control along the Euphrates River.
David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He crippled all the chariot horses except enough for a hundred chariots.
When the Syrians from Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David killed twenty-two thousand of them.
Then David put groups of soldiers in the Syrian kingdom of Damascus, and the Syrians became David's servants and paid him taxes. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shields that Hadadezer's officers carried and brought them to Jerusalem.

From Tibhath and Cun, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, David took a great amount of bronze. Later Solomon used it to make the huge bronze tank called the Sea, the pillars, and the bronze objects for the temple.
Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah.

So he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory over Hadadezer, because Tou had often been at war with Hadadezer. Hadoram brought all kinds of objects made of gold, silver, and bronze.
King David gave these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Abishai son of Zeruiah killed eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He put groups of soldiers in Edom, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David ruled over all Israel. He did what was fair and right for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah was in charge of the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the record keeper.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Cherethites and Pelethites, the king's bodyguard. David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side.
Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king after him.

David said, "I will be kind to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father was kind to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him about his father's death. When David's officials came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to comfort him,

the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, "Do you really think David is honouring your father by sending these men to comfort you? No, his officials have come to explore the land, spy on it, and find a way to destroy it!"
So Hanun grabbed David's officials, shaved their beards, cut off their robes in the middle at the hips, and sent them away.

When someone told David what had happened to these men, he sent messengers to meet them, because they were deeply ashamed. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, and then come home."

The Ammonites realised that they had made David hate them. So Hanun and the Ammonites sent about thirty-four thousand kilograms of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, from Aram Maacah, and from Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah came with his army and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites also gathered from their towns and came out to fight.
When David heard about this, he sent Joab with the whole army of mighty warriors.
The Ammonites marched out and lined up for battle at the entrance of their city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country.
Joab saw that there were enemy lines in front of him and behind him. So he chose some of the best soldiers in Israel and lined them up against the Syrians.
He put the rest of the army under the command of his brother Abishai, and they lined up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, you must come and help me. But if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will come and help you.
Be brave! Let's be strong for our people and for the towns of our God. May the LORD do what he thinks is best."
Then Joab and the troops with him marched out to fight the Syrians, and the Syrians ran away from him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Syrians were running away, they also ran away from Joab's brother Abishai and went back into their city. Then Joab went back to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians saw that Israel had defeated them, they sent messengers to bring more Syrian troops from beyond the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
When David was told about it, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and marched toward them. He lined up his army against the Syrians, and they fought against him.
But the Syrians ran away from Israel. David killed seven thousand of their chariot drivers and forty thousand of their foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the commander of their army.
When Hadadezer's servants saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his servants. After that, the Syrians were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.

In the spring, the time of year when kings go off to war, Joab led out the army. He destroyed the land of the Ammonites and went and surrounded the city of Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and destroyed it.

David took the crown off the head of their king. It was made of about thirty-four kilograms of gold and had precious stones in it, and it was placed on David's head. David also took a great amount of goods from the city.
He brought out the people who lived there and made them work with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then David and all his army went back to Jerusalem.
Later, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, one of the descendants of the giants, and the Philistines were defeated.
In another war with the Philistines, Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath from Gath. Lahmi's spear had a shaft as thick as a weaver's rod.
In another battle at Gath, there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all. He was also a descendant of the giants.
When he made fun of Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, killed him.
These men were descendants of the giants in Gath, and they were killed by David and his soldiers.
Satan rose up against Israel and led David to count the people of Israel.
So David said to Joab and the leaders of the people, "Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north. Then report back to me, so I will know how many there are."

But Joab said, "May the LORD make his people a hundred times more than they are now! My master the king, aren't they all your servants anyway? Why do you want to do this? Why should you bring guilt on Israel?"
But the king's order won out over Joab. So Joab left and went all through Israel, and then came back to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the total number of people. In all Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men who could fight with a sword, and in Judah there were four hundred and seventy thousand.
But Joab did not count the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he found the king's order disgusting.
God was not pleased with what had been done, so he punished Israel.
Then David said to God, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now, please take away the guilt of your servant. I have acted very foolishly."
The LORD said to Gad, David's seer,
"Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three choices. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
So Gad went to David and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Choose for yourself:

three years of famine, or three months of being swept away by your enemies while their swords catch up with you, or three days of the LORD's sword, a terrible sickness in the land, with the LORD's angel bringing destruction all through Israel.' Now decide how I should answer the one who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let me fall into the LORD's hands, because his mercy is very great. Do not let me fall into human hands."
So the LORD sent a terrible sickness on Israel, and seventy thousand Israelites died.

God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But as the angel was about to destroy it, the LORD looked and felt sorry about the disaster. He said to the angel who was destroying the people, "That is enough! Stop now!" The LORD's angel was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David looked up and saw the LORD's angel standing between the earth and the sky, holding a drawn sword stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the leaders, who were wearing sackcloth, bowed down with their faces to the ground.

David said to God, "Wasn't I the one who ordered the people to be counted? I am the one who has sinned and done wrong. But these people are like sheep. What have they done? LORD my God, let your hand fall on me and my family, but do not let this sickness strike your people."
Then the LORD's angel told Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up, as Gad had told him to do in the LORD's name.
Ornan was threshing wheat. He turned and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid.
When David came near, Ornan looked and saw him. He left the threshing floor and bowed down before David with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, "Sell me this threshing floor so I can build an altar to the LORD on it. Sell it to me for the full price, so the sickness striking the people will stop."

Ornan said to David, "Take it! Let my master the king do whatever he thinks is best. Look, I will give you the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing boards for the firewood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I will give it all."
But King David said to Ornan, "No, I insist on paying the full price. I will not take what belongs to you and give it to the LORD. I will not offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
So David paid Ornan about seven kilograms of gold for the place.
David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him by sending fire from heaven onto the altar of burnt offering.
Then the LORD spoke to the angel, and the angel put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered sacrifices there.
The LORD's tabernacle, which Moses had made in the desert, and the altar of burnt offering were at the high place in Gibeon at that time.
But David could not go there to ask God for guidance, because he was terrified of the sword of the LORD's angel.
Then David said, "This is where the house of the LORD God will be, and this is where the altar of burnt offering for Israel will be."
David gave orders to gather the foreigners living in Israel. From among them he appointed stonecutters to cut blocks of stone for building God's temple.
David provided a large amount of iron for nails and fittings for the doors of the gates, and more bronze than could be weighed.
He also provided more cedar logs than could be counted, because the people of Sidon and Tyre had brought large amounts of cedar to David.

David said, "My son Solomon is young and has no experience, and the house to be built for the LORD must be very magnificent, famous and glorious in every country. So I will get things ready for it." So David made large preparations before he died.
Then he called his son Solomon and commanded him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, "My son, I wanted to build a house to honour the name of the LORD my God.
But the LORD's word came to me: 'You have spilled a lot of blood and fought many wars. You will not build a house to honour my name, because you have spilled so much blood on the earth in my sight.
But you will have a son who will be a man of peace. I will give him peace from all his enemies around him. His name will be Solomon, and I will give Israel peace and quiet while he is king.
He is the one who will build a house to honour my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I will make the throne of his kingdom over Israel last forever.'
Now, my son, may the LORD be with you and give you success. May you build the house of the LORD your God, as he said you would.
May the LORD give you wisdom and understanding when he puts you in charge of Israel, so that you will keep the law of the LORD your God.
You will be successful if you are careful to obey the laws and rules the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or lose heart.

I have worked hard to provide for the LORD's temple about three thousand four hundred tonnes of gold, thirty-four thousand tonnes of silver, and so much bronze and iron that it cannot be weighed. I have also provided wood and stone, and you may add to them.
You have many workers: stonecutters, masons, and carpenters, and every kind of skilled worker for every kind of job.
There is more gold, silver, bronze, and iron than can be counted. Now get to work, and may the LORD be with you."
Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon. He said to them,
"The LORD your God is with you, isn't he? He has given you peace on every side. He has handed the people of this land over to me, and the land is now under the control of the LORD and his people.

So now, commit your heart and soul to following the LORD your God. Get up and build the holy place of the LORD God. Then you can bring the ark of the LORD's covenant and the holy objects of God into the temple that will be built to honour the LORD's name."
When David was old and had lived a long, full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
He gathered all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites.
The Levites who were thirty years old or older were counted. One by one, there were thirty-eight thousand men.
David said, "Twenty-four thousand of them will be in charge of the work of the LORD's temple. Six thousand will be officials and judges.
Four thousand will be gatekeepers, and four thousand will praise the LORD with the musical instruments I have made for praise."
David divided the Levites into groups based on the families of Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
From the Gershonites came Ladan and Shimei.
Ladan had three sons: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel.
Shimei had three sons: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. These were the heads of Ladan's families.
Shimei's sons were Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were Shimei's sons.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah was second. But Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted together as one family group with one assignment.
Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were set apart forever to make the most holy things holy, to burn incense before the LORD, to serve him, and to bless people in his name forever.
But the sons of Moses, the man of God, were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.
Gershom's descendants were led by Shebuel.
Eliezer's descendants were led by Rehabiah. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had very many sons.
Izhar's descendants were led by Shelomith.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
Uzziel's sons were Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without having sons. He had only daughters, and they married their cousins, the sons of Kish.
Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.

These were the descendants of Levi by their families, the heads of families as they were listed by name and counted one by one. They were twenty years old or older, and they did the work of serving in the LORD's temple.
David had said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.
So the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the objects used in its service."
Following David's last instructions, the Levites twenty years old or older were counted.

Their job was to help Aaron's descendants in the service of the LORD's temple. They took care of the courtyards and the side rooms, the cleansing of all the holy things, and other work in the service of God's temple.
They were in charge of the holy bread on the table, the fine flour for the grain offerings, the thin cakes made without yeast, the baking pans, the mixing, and all the measuring of amounts and sizes.
They were also to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and to do the same every evening.
They helped whenever burnt offerings were offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, New Moon festivals, and other appointed feasts. They served before the LORD regularly, in the numbers required by the rules.
So the Levites took care of the Tent of Meeting and the holy place, and they helped their relatives, Aaron's descendants, in the service of the LORD's temple.
These were the groups of Aaron's descendants. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died before their father did, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
With the help of Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Ithamar, David divided them into groups for their duties.

There were more leaders among Eleazar's descendants than among Ithamar's, so they were divided this way: sixteen family heads from Eleazar's descendants, and eight family heads from Ithamar's descendants.
They divided them fairly by drawing lots, because there were officials of the holy place and officials of God among the descendants of both Eleazar and Ithamar.

The secretary Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite, wrote down their names in front of the king, the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priests' and Levites' families. One family was chosen by lot from Eleazar, and then one from Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
This was the order in which they served when they came into the LORD's temple. They followed the rules given to them by their ancestor Aaron, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
These were the rest of Levi's descendants: From Amram's descendants came Shubael, and from Shubael's descendants came Jehdeiah.
From Rehabiah's descendants came Isshiah, the chief.
From the Izharites came Shelomoth, and from Shelomoth's descendants came Jahath.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
Uzziel's son was Micah, and from Micah's descendants came Shamir.
Micah's brother was Isshiah, and from Isshiah's descendants came Zechariah.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Jaaziah's son was Beno.
Merari's descendants through Jaaziah were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
From Mahli came Eleazar, who had no sons.
From Kish came Kish's son Jerahmeel.
Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the Levites, listed by their families.

Like their relatives, the descendants of Aaron, they also drew lots in front of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priests' and Levites' families. The families of the oldest brother were treated the same as those of the youngest.

David and the army commanders also set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun for a special service. They were to prophesy while playing harps, lyres, and cymbals. This is the list of the men who did this work:
From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. They were under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the king's direction.

From the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six in all. They were under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
From the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were the sons of Heman, the king's seer. God had promised to make him strong, and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
