Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal records in Babylon. See if King Cyrus really gave an order to rebuild this temple of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision about this."
So King Darius gave an order, and they searched the records kept in the treasure rooms in Babylon.
A scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana in the province of Media. This is what was written in it:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, the king gave this order about God's temple in Jerusalem: Let the temple be rebuilt as a place to offer sacrifices. Let its foundations be laid firmly. It must be about twenty-seven meters high and twenty-seven meters wide.
It must have three layers of large stones and one layer of new wood. The cost will be paid from the king's treasury.

Also, the gold and silver things from God's temple, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, must be given back. Take them to the temple in Jerusalem and put each one in its place in God's temple."
Then Darius wrote: "So now, Tattenai, governor of the land west of the Euphrates River, Shethar-Bozenai, and your fellow officials west of the river, stay away from there.
Leave the work on this temple of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the Jewish leaders rebuild this temple of God on its old site.

I also order you to help these Jewish leaders build this temple of God. The full cost must be paid to these men from the king's money, from the taxes collected west of the Euphrates River, so that the work does not stop.

Whatever they need must be given to them every day without fail: young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil, as the priests in Jerusalem ask.
Then they can offer sacrifices that please the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
I also order that if anyone changes this order, a beam must be pulled from their house, and they must be lifted up and stuck on it. Their house must be made into a pile of rubble because of this.

May the God who has made his name live there destroy any king or people who tries to change this order or destroy this temple of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have given this order. Let it be done with all care."
Then Tattenai, governor of the land west of the Euphrates River, Shethar-Bozenai, and their friends did exactly what King Darius had ordered, with all care.

So the Jewish leaders kept building and did well, encouraged by the preaching of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished building the temple as the God of Israel had commanded and as Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia, had ordered.
The temple was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius's rule.
Then the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the people who had come back from being prisoners joyfully celebrated the dedication of this temple of God.

For the dedication of this temple of God they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs. As a sin offering for all Israel they offered twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.
They put the priests and the Levites in their groups to serve God in Jerusalem, as written in the book of Moses.
The people who had come back from being prisoners celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

The priests and Levites had all made themselves clean together, so they were all clean. The Levites killed the Passover lambs for all the people who had come back, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

The Israelites who had come back from being prisoners ate the Passover. So did everyone who had separated themselves from the unclean ways of the nations of the land to worship the LORD, the God of Israel.

For seven days they joyfully celebrated the Festival of Bread Without Yeast. The LORD had filled them with joy by changing the heart of the king of Assyria, so that he helped them with the work on the temple of God, the God of Israel.
After these things, while Artaxerxes was king of Persia, there was a man named Ezra. He was the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest.

This Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a teacher who knew the law of Moses very well, the law the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. The king gave him everything he asked for, because the LORD his God was helping him.
Some of the Israelites went up to Jerusalem with him in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes. With them were some priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the king's seventh year.
He had left Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, because his God's kind hand was on him.
Ezra had set his heart on studying the LORD's law, obeying it, and teaching its rules and decisions in Israel.
This is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and teacher, who studied the LORD's commands and rules for Israel:
"From Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, teacher of the law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
I order that any of the people of Israel in my kingdom, including their priests and Levites, who want to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
You are being sent by the king and his seven advisers to check on how well Judah and Jerusalem are obeying the law of your God, which you have with you.
Take with you the silver and gold that the king and his advisers have freely given to the God of Israel, whose home is in Jerusalem.
Also take all the silver and gold you receive from the province of Babylon, along with the gifts the people and priests freely give for the temple of their God in Jerusalem.
Use this money carefully to buy bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings. Offer them on the altar of the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
You and your fellow Jews may do whatever seems best with the rest of the silver and gold, as your God wants.
Give to the God of Jerusalem all the things that have been given to you for the service in the temple of your God.
If you need anything else for the temple of your God, you may pay for it from the king's treasury.
I, King Artaxerxes, order all the treasurers west of the Euphrates River to give Ezra the priest, teacher of the law of the God of heaven, whatever he asks of you, with all care,
up to about three and a half tonnes of silver, one hundred loads of wheat, about two thousand liters of wine, about two thousand liters of olive oil, and as much salt as he needs.
Whatever the God of heaven commands for his temple must be done fully and carefully. Why should his anger come on the kingdom of the king and his sons?
We also tell you that you must not make any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or other workers at this temple of God pay any taxes, payments, or fees.
And you, Ezra, use the wisdom your God has given you to choose judges and leaders to judge all the people west of the Euphrates River who know the laws of your God. Teach those who do not know them.
Anyone who does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king must be punished quickly, by death, by being sent away, by having their property taken, or by prison."
Ezra said: Praise the LORD, the God of our ancestors, who put it into the king's heart to make the LORD's temple in Jerusalem beautiful.

He has shown me his faithful love in front of the king, his advisers, and all his powerful officials. Because the LORD my God was helping me, I had courage, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
These are the family leaders and the people listed with them who went up with me from Babylon while King Artaxerxes ruled:
From the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom. From the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel. From the descendants of David, Hattush.
From the descendants of Shecaniah, from the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him one hundred fifty men listed in the family records.
From the descendants of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
From the descendants of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred men.
From the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
From the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
From the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
From the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred eighteen men.
From the descendants of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred sixty men.
From the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
From the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred ten men.
From the descendants of Adonikam, who came later: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men.
From the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy men.
I gathered them together at the river that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there for three days. When I looked over the people and the priests, I found that there were no Levites there.
So I sent for these leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were teachers.

I sent them to Iddo, the leader at the place called Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his relatives, the temple servants at Casiphia, so they would send us servants for the temple of our God.
Because our God's kind hand was on us, they brought us a wise man named Sherebiah, from the descendants of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel. He came with his sons and relatives, eighteen men.
They also brought Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his relatives and their sons, twenty men.
They also brought two hundred twenty of the temple servants, a group David and his officials had set up to help the Levites. All of them were listed by name.
There by the Ahava River, I announced that we would go without food and humble ourselves before our God. We asked him for a safe journey for us, our children, and everything we owned.

I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road. We had told the king, "Our God's kind hand is on everyone who looks to him, but his power and anger are against everyone who leaves him."
So we went without food and prayed to our God about this, and he answered our prayer.
Then I chose twelve of the leading priests, along with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their relatives.
I weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the objects that the king, his advisers, his officials, and all the Israelites there had given for the temple of our God.
I weighed out to them about twenty-two tonnes of silver, silver objects weighing about three and a half tonnes, about three and a half tonnes of gold,
twenty gold bowls weighing about eight and a half kilograms, and two fine objects of polished bronze, as valuable as gold.
I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD, and these objects are holy. The silver and gold are a gift freely given to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.
Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the rooms of the LORD's temple in Jerusalem, in front of the leading priests, the Levites, and the family leaders of Israel."
So the priests and Levites took the silver, gold, and objects that had been weighed out, to bring them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem.
On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River to go to Jerusalem. Our God's hand was on us, and he protected us from enemies and robbers along the way.
We arrived in Jerusalem and rested there for three days.

On the fourth day, in the temple of our God, we weighed out the silver, gold, and objects and gave them to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, and so were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was written down at that time.

Then the people who had come back from being prisoners offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
They also gave the king's orders to the king's officers and to the governors west of the Euphrates River. Then these officials helped the people and the temple of God.

After these things were done, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the peoples of the lands around them. They are copying their disgusting practices, the practices of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.

They have married their daughters and let their sons marry them too. So God's holy people have mixed with the peoples around them. The leaders and officials have been the first to be unfaithful in this."
When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my robe. I pulled hair from my head and beard, and I sat down, shocked.

Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the people who had returned. I sat there shocked until the time of the evening offering.
At the time of the evening offering, I got up from my sorrow, with my clothes and robe torn. I fell on my knees and lifted my hands to the LORD my God.
I prayed, "My God, I am too ashamed and embarrassed to lift my face to you, my God. Our sins are higher than our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens.

From the days of our ancestors until now, our guilt has been great. Because of our sins, we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to foreign kings, to the sword, to being taken prisoner, to being robbed, and to shame, as we are today.

But now, for a short time, the LORD our God has been kind to us. He has let some of us survive and has given us a safe place in his holy land. Our God has given light to our eyes and a little new life while we are still slaves.

We are slaves, but our God has not left us in our slavery. He has shown us his faithful love in front of the kings of Persia. He has given us new life to rebuild the temple of our God and repair its ruins. He has given us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
But now, our God, what can we say after this? We have disobeyed your commands,

the commands you gave through your servants the prophets. You said, 'The land you are going to take is unclean. The peoples living there have made it unclean with their disgusting practices. They have filled it from one end to the other with their filth.

So do not let your daughters marry their sons, and do not let your sons marry their daughters. Never try to help them have peace or success. Then you will be strong, enjoy the good things of the land, and leave it to your children as their own forever.'
After everything that has happened to us because of our evil acts and our great guilt, you, our God, have punished us less than our sins deserve, and you have let some of us survive.
Should we break your commands again and marry people who do these disgusting things? Wouldn't you be angry enough to destroy us completely, so that no one would be left to escape?
LORD, God of Israel, you are right. We are left as a group of survivors today. Look, we stand before you in our guilt. Because of it, none of us can stand in your presence."

While Ezra was praying and confessing, crying and lying face down in front of God's temple, a very large crowd of Israelites gathered around him: men, women, and children. They also were crying bitterly.
Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, from the descendants of Elam, said to Ezra, "We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the peoples around us. But there is still hope for Israel.
Let's make a covenant with our God to send away all these wives and their children, as you, my master, and those who tremble at our God's commands advise. Let it be done as the law says.
Get up! This is your job, and we are with you. Be brave and do it."
So Ezra got up and made the leading priests, the Levites, and all Israel promise to do what had been said. And they promised.

Then Ezra left the front of God's temple and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. While he was there, he did not eat any food or drink any water, because he was still mourning over the unfaithfulness of the people who had returned.
An announcement was sent all through Judah and Jerusalem, telling everyone who had come back from being prisoners to gather in Jerusalem.
Anyone who did not come within three days would lose all their property, as the leaders and elders had decided, and would be shut out of the community of those who had returned.

So within three days all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered in Jerusalem. On the twentieth day of the ninth month, all the people sat in the open square in front of God's temple. They were shaking because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.
Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, "You have been unfaithful. You have married foreign women and added to Israel's guilt.
Now confess to the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and do what he wants. Separate yourselves from the peoples around you and from your foreign wives."
The whole crowd answered with a loud voice, "You are right! We must do as you say.
But there are many people here, and it is the rainy season. We cannot stand outside. Besides, this cannot be done in a day or two, because so many of us have sinned in this way.

Let our leaders act for the whole community. Let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at a set time, together with the elders and judges of each town, until our God's fierce anger about this has turned away from us."
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were against this plan, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

So the people who had returned did as they had agreed. Ezra the priest chose family leaders, one from each family, all listed by name. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to look into each case.
By the first day of the first month, they had finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women.
Among the priests, these had married foreign women: from the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
They all promised to send their wives away. Because they were guilty, each of them offered a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.
From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah, also called Kelita, Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
From the rest of Israel: from the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
From the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth.
From the descendants of Pahath-Moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
From the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
From the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasu,
Bani, Binnui, Shimei,
Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
From the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Iddo, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these men had married foreign women, and some of them had children by these wives.
Neh: These are the words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the royal city of Susa.
Hanani, one of my brothers, came from Judah with some other men. I asked them about the Jews who had survived and were left from those taken prisoner, and about Jerusalem.
They told me, "The people who survived and are left in the province are in great trouble and shame. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned."
When I heard this, I sat down and cried. For several days I mourned, went without food, and prayed to the God of heaven.
I said, "LORD, God of heaven, please hear me. You are the great and amazing God. You keep your covenant of faithful love with those who love you and obey your commands.

Please listen and open your eyes to hear the prayer I, your servant, am praying to you day and night for the people of Israel, your servants. I confess the sins we Israelites have done against you. Yes, I and my father's family have sinned.
We have done very wrong against you. We have not obeyed the commands, rules, and laws you gave your servant Moses.
Please remember what you told your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations.

But if you come back to me and obey my commands, then even if your people have been scattered to the farthest edge of the sky, I will gather them from there. I will bring them to the place I have chosen as a home for my name.'
They are your servants and your people. You rescued them with your great power and your strong hand.

Lord, please listen to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayers of your servants who love to honor your name. Please let me succeed today, and make the king kind to me." At that time I served wine to the king.
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was brought to the king. I picked up the wine and gave it to him. I had never been sad in front of him before.
So the king asked me, "Why do you look so sad? You are not sick. This must be sadness of the heart." I was very afraid,
but I said to the king, "May the king live forever! How can I not look sad? The city where my ancestors are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire."
The king asked me, "What do you want?" Then I prayed to the God of heaven.
I answered the king, "If it pleases the king, and if I have pleased you, please send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so that I can rebuild it."
The queen was sitting beside the king. He asked me, "How long will your trip take? When will you come back?" The king was pleased to send me, so I told him how long I would be away.
I also said to the king, "If it pleases the king, please give me letters for the governors west of the Euphrates River, so they will let me travel safely until I reach Judah.

Please also give me a letter for Asaph, who is in charge of the king's forest, so he will give me wood. I need it to make beams for the gates of the fortress near the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will live in." The king gave me what I asked for, because my God's kind hand was on me.
So I went to the governors west of the Euphrates River and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were very upset that someone had come to help the Israelites.
I arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
Then I got up at night with a few men. I had not told anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one I was riding.
That night I went out through the Valley Gate toward the Jackal Well and the Garbage Gate. I looked at the walls of Jerusalem, which had been broken down, and at its gates, which had been burned.
Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was not enough room for my animal to get through.
So I went up the valley that night and looked at the wall. Then I turned back and came in again through the Valley Gate.
The city officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. I had not yet told anything to the Jews, the priests, the important men, the officials, or anyone else who would do the work.
Then I said to them, "You can see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned. Come, let's rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so we will not be ashamed any more."
I told them how my God's kind hand had been on me, and what the king had said to me. They said, "Let's start building!" So they got ready to do this good work.

But when Sanballat from Horon, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they laughed at us and looked down on us. They said, "What are you doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
I answered them, "The God of heaven will give us success. We, his servants, will start building. But you have no share, no right, and no history in Jerusalem."

Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests got to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They set it apart for God and put its doors in place. They rebuilt the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel, and set it apart for God.
The men of Jericho built the next section, and Zaccur son of Imri built the section after that.
The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They put in its beams and set up its doors, bolts, and bars.
Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired the next section. Next to him, Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs. Next to him, Zadok son of Baana made repairs.
The men of Tekoa repaired the next section, but their leaders refused to do the work their masters gave them.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate. They put in its beams and set up its doors, bolts, and bars.
Next to them, Melatiah from Gibeon and Jadon from Meronoth, men from Gibeon and Mizpah, made repairs up to the home of the governor of the land west of the Euphrates River.
Next to them, Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfume makers, made repairs. They rebuilt Jerusalem's wall as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them, Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half of the Jerusalem district, made repairs.
Next to them, Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs across from his own house. Next to him, Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to them, Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of the other half of the Jerusalem district, made repairs with the help of his daughters.

Hanun and the people of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it and set up its doors, bolts, and bars. They also repaired about four hundred fifty meters of the wall, as far as the Garbage Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth Hakkerem, repaired the Garbage Gate. He rebuilt it and set up its doors, bolts, and bars.

Shallun son of Col-Hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt it, put a roof on it, and set up its doors, bolts, and bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Siloam by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
After him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs up to the place across from David's tombs, as far as the man-made pool and the House of the Heroes.
After him, the Levites made repairs under Rehum son of Bani. Next to him, Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his own district.
After him, their fellow Levites made repairs under Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.
Next to him, Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, across from the slope up to the armory, at the corner of the wall.
After him, Baruch son of Zabbai worked hard to repair another section, from the corner to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him, Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of Eliashib's house to the end of it.
After him, the priests from the surrounding area made repairs.
After them, Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs across from their house. After them, Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs next to his own house.
After him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from Azariah's house to the bend and the corner of the wall.

Palal son of Uzai made repairs across from the bend of the wall and the tower that sticks out from the king's upper palace, near the courtyard of the guard. After him, Pedaiah son of Parosh made repairs.
The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel, as far as the place across from the Water Gate on the east and the tower that sticks out.
After them, the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from across the large tower that sticks out to the wall of Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate, the priests made repairs, each one across from his own house.
After them, Zadok son of Immer made repairs across from his house. After him, Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the guard at the East Gate, made repairs.
After him, Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After them, Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs across from where he lived.
After him, Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, across from the Inspection Gate, and as far as the room above the corner.
The goldsmiths and merchants made repairs between the room above the corner and the Sheep Gate.
When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became angry and very upset. He made fun of the Jews.

In front of his friends and the army of Samaria he said, "What are these weak Jews doing? Do they think they can rebuild the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish it in one day? Can they bring these burned stones back to life from the piles of rubble?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was standing beside him. He said, "Even if a fox climbed up on what they are building, it would knock their stone wall down!"
I prayed, "Listen, our God, because we are being looked down on. Turn their insults back on their own heads. Let them be carried off as prisoners to a foreign land.
Do not cover up their guilt or wipe out their sins from your sight, because they have insulted the builders."
So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, because the people worked with all their hearts.
But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the repairs to Jerusalem's walls were going ahead and that the gaps were being closed. They were very angry.
They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and cause trouble.
But we prayed to our God and posted guards day and night to protect ourselves from them.
Meanwhile the people of Judah said, "The workers are getting tired, and there is too much rubble. We cannot rebuild the wall."
Our enemies said, "Before they know it or see us, we will be right among them. We will kill them and stop the work."
The Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times over, "They will attack us from every direction."
So I placed people behind the lowest parts of the wall, in the open places. I placed them by families, with their swords, spears, and bows.

After I looked things over, I stood up and said to the important men, the officials, and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and amazing. Fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes."
Our enemies heard that we knew about their plot and that God had ruined their plans. So we all went back to the wall, each to our own work.
From that day on, half of my men did the work, while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officers stood behind all the people of Judah
who were building the wall. Those who carried loads did their work with one hand and held a weapon in the other.
Each of the builders wore his sword at his side while he worked. The man who blew the trumpet stayed with me.
I said to the important men, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is big and spread out, and we are far apart from each other along the wall.
Wherever you hear the trumpet, come and join us there. Our God will fight for us!"
So we kept working, with half the men holding spears, from the first light of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also told the people, "Every man and his helper should stay inside Jerusalem at night. Then they can guard us at night and work during the day."
So none of us took off our clothes, not I, my brothers, my servants, or the guards with me. Each of us kept our weapon with us, even when we went for water.
Then the men and their wives began to complain loudly against their fellow Jews.
Some said, "We have many sons and daughters. We need grain so we can eat and stay alive."
Others said, "We are giving up our fields, vineyards, and houses as security for loans so we can get grain during the famine."
Others said, "We had to borrow money to pay the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

We are the same as our fellow Jews, and our children are just as good as theirs. But we have to sell our sons and daughters as slaves. Some of our daughters have already been made slaves. We can do nothing about it, because our fields and vineyards now belong to other people."
When I heard their complaints and what they said, I was very angry.
I thought it over, and then I accused the important men and the officials. I told them, "You are charging your own relatives interest!" So I called a large meeting to deal with them.

I said to them, "As much as we could, we have bought back our fellow Jews who were sold to foreigners. Now you are selling your own relatives, so that they will have to be sold back to us!" They were silent and could not find anything to say.
I went on, "What you are doing is not right. You should live in the fear of our God, so our enemies among the nations will have no reason to insult us.
My relatives, my servants, and I are also lending the people money and grain. Please, let's stop charging interest!
Give back to them today their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses. Also give back the interest you are charging them, the one percent on the money, grain, new wine, and olive oil."

They answered, "We will give it back, and we will not ask them for anything more. We will do as you say." Then I called the priests and made the leaders promise in front of them to do what they had said.

I also shook out the folds of my robe and said, "In the same way, may God shake out of their house and property anyone who does not keep this promise. May that person be shaken out and left with nothing!" The whole crowd said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. And the people did what they had promised.

From the time I was made governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years in all, my relatives and I did not eat the food the governor was allowed.

The governors before me had put heavy loads on the people. They took food and wine from them, plus about half a kilogram of silver. Even their helpers ruled over the people harshly. But I did not act like that, because I feared God.
I also worked hard on the wall. We did not buy any land, and all my men gathered there to work.
At my table I fed one hundred fifty Jews and officials, besides the people who came to us from the nations around us.

Every day one ox, six of the best sheep, and some birds were prepared for me. Every ten days a large supply of all kinds of wine was brought. Even so, I did not ask for the food the governor was allowed, because the people already had heavy burdens.
Remember me kindly, my God, for all the good I have done for these people.
Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that there were no gaps left in it, though I had not yet put the doors in the gates.
So Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: "Come, let's meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono." But they were planning to harm me.
I sent messengers to tell them, "I am doing a great work, and I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to come down to you?"
They sent me the same message four times, and each time I gave them the same answer.
The fifth time, Sanballat sent his helper to me with the same message, and he had an open letter in his hand.

It said, "It is being said among the nations, and Geshem says it is true, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel. That is why you are rebuilding the wall. The reports say you are going to be their king.
You have even chosen prophets to announce about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now this report will get back to the king. So come, let's talk this over together."
I sent him this answer: "Nothing like what you are saying is happening. You are making it up in your own mind."
They were all trying to frighten us. They thought, "Their hands will get too weak to do the work, and it will never be finished." But I prayed, "Now, God, make my hands strong."

One day I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at home. He said, "Let's meet in God's house, inside the temple, and close the temple doors. Men are coming to kill you. They are coming tonight to kill you."
But I said, "Should a man like me run away? Should someone like me go into the temple to save his life? I will not go!"
I realized that God had not sent him. He had spoken this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him.
They had paid him to frighten me into doing this and sinning. Then they could give me a bad name and shame me.
Remember, my God, what Tobiah and Sanballat have done. Remember also the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who tried to frighten me.
So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul. It took fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard about it, all the nations around us were afraid and lost their confidence. They knew that this work had been done with the help of our God.
In those days the important men of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters were coming to them.
Many people in Judah had promised to be loyal to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah. Also, his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They kept telling me about the good things Tobiah was doing, and then they reported to him what I said. And Tobiah kept sending letters to frighten me.
After the wall had been rebuilt and I had set up the doors, the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were given their jobs.
I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, together with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress. Hananiah was a faithful man who feared God more than most people did.

I told them, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot. While the gatekeepers are still on duty, have them shut the doors and bar them. Choose people who live in Jerusalem as guards. Put some at their posts, and others near their own houses."
The city was wide and large, but there were only a few people in it, and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

Then my God put it into my heart to gather the important men, the officials, and the people, so they could be listed by families. I found the family record of those who had come back first. This is what was written in it:
These are the people of the province who came back from being prisoners. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken them away. Now they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to their own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of Israel:
The descendants of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The descendants of Shephatiah: three hundred seventy-two.
The descendants of Arah: six hundred fifty-two.
The descendants of Pahath-Moab, through Jeshua and Joab: two thousand eight hundred eighteen.
The descendants of Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The descendants of Zattu: eight hundred forty-five.
The descendants of Zaccai: seven hundred sixty.
The descendants of Binnui: six hundred forty-eight.
The descendants of Bebai: six hundred twenty-eight.
The descendants of Azgad: two thousand three hundred twenty-two.
The descendants of Adonikam: six hundred sixty-seven.
The descendants of Bigvai: two thousand sixty-seven.
The descendants of Adin: six hundred fifty-five.
The descendants of Ater, through Hezekiah: ninety-eight.
The descendants of Hashum: three hundred twenty-eight.
The descendants of Bezai: three hundred twenty-four.
The descendants of Hariph: one hundred twelve.
The people of Gibeon: ninety-five.
The men of Bethlehem and Netophah: one hundred eighty-eight.
The men of Anathoth: one hundred twenty-eight.
The men of Beth Azmaveth: forty-two.
The men of Kiriath Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: seven hundred forty-three.
The men of Ramah and Geba: six hundred twenty-one.
The men of Michmas: one hundred twenty-two.
The men of Bethel and Ai: one hundred twenty-three.
The men of the other Nebo: fifty-two.
The descendants of the other Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The descendants of Harim: three hundred twenty.
The people of Jericho: three hundred forty-five.
The people of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: seven hundred twenty-one.
The people of Senaah: three thousand nine hundred thirty.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, from the family of Jeshua: nine hundred seventy-three.
The descendants of Immer: one thousand fifty-two.
The descendants of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
The descendants of Harim: one thousand seventeen.
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, through Kadmiel, from the family of Hodevah: seventy-four.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph: one hundred forty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai: one hundred thirty-eight.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Sia, Padon,
Lebana, Hagaba, Salmai,
Hanan, Giddel, Gahar,
Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda,
Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah,
Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah, and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants were three hundred ninety-two.
Some people came up from the towns of Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not prove that their families were descended from Israel.
They were the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda: six hundred forty-two.
From the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai. This Barzillai had married a daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and took his family name.
They searched for their names in the family records, but they could not find them. So they were not allowed to serve as priests.
The governor told them not to eat the most holy food until there was a priest who could ask God using the Urim and Thummim.
The whole group together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty people,
besides their seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven male and female servants. They also had two hundred forty-five men and women singers.
They had seven hundred thirty-six horses, two hundred forty-five mules,
four hundred thirty-five camels, and six thousand seven hundred twenty donkeys.
Some of the family leaders gave gifts for the work. The governor gave the treasury about eight and a half kilograms of gold, fifty bowls, and five hundred thirty robes for the priests.
Some of the family leaders gave the building fund about one hundred seventy kilograms of gold and about one and a third tonnes of silver.
The rest of the people gave about one hundred seventy kilograms of gold, about one and a quarter tonnes of silver, and sixty-seven robes for the priests.

So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all the rest of Israel settled in their own towns. By the seventh month, the Israelites were living in their towns.
All the people gathered together as one in the open square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the teacher to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD had given to Israel.
So on the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the law out to the crowd of men and women and everyone old enough to understand.

He read it aloud from early morning until noon, as he faced the square in front of the Water Gate. He read to the men, the women, and all who could understand, and all the people listened carefully to the book of the law.

Ezra the teacher stood on a high wooden platform built for this purpose. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. On his left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book where all the people could see him, because he was standing above them. As he opened it, all the people stood up.
Ezra praised the LORD, the great God, and all the people lifted their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah helped the people understand the law while the people stood in their places.
They read from the book of God's law clearly and explained what it meant, so the people understood what was being read.

Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who were teaching the people said to them all, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not be sad or cry." They said this because all the people had been crying as they listened to the words of the law.

Nehemiah said, "Go and enjoy good food and sweet drinks. Send some to people who have nothing ready, because this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad, because the joy of the LORD is your strength."
The Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be quiet, because this is a holy day. Do not be sad."
Then all the people went away to eat and drink, to send food to others, and to celebrate with great joy, because they now understood the words that had been explained to them.
On the second day, the family leaders of all the people, along with the priests and Levites, gathered around Ezra the teacher to study the words of the law.
They found written in the law, which the LORD had given through Moses, that the Israelites were to live in shelters during the festival of the seventh month.

It also said they should announce this in all their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hills and bring back branches from olive trees, wild olive trees, myrtles, palms, and other leafy trees, to make shelters, as it is written."

So the people went out and brought back branches and made shelters for themselves. They built them on their roofs, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of God's temple, in the square by the Water Gate, and in the square by the Ephraim Gate.
Everyone who had come back from being prisoners built shelters and lived in them. The Israelites had not done this since the days of Joshua son of Nun. Everyone was full of joy.
Every day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the book of God's law. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they held a special gathering, as the law requires.
On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gathered together. They went without food, wore rough sackcloth, and put dust on their heads.
Those who were descended from Israel separated themselves from all foreigners. They stood and confessed their own sins and the sins of their ancestors.

They stood in their places and listened for a quarter of the day while the book of the law of the LORD their God was read. For another quarter of the day they confessed their sins and worshiped the LORD their God.
The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the stairs and cried out loudly to the LORD their God.

Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and praise the LORD your God, who lives forever and ever! Praise your glorious name, LORD. It is greater than all our blessing and praise!

You alone are the LORD. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens, and all the stars. You made the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You give life to everything, and the armies of heaven worship you.
You are the LORD God who chose Abram. You brought him out of Ur of the Babylonians and gave him the name Abraham.

You saw that his heart was faithful to you. You made a covenant with him to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites. You have kept your promise, because you are right and fair.
You saw how our ancestors suffered in Egypt. You heard them cry out at the Red Sea.

You did signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his officials, and all the people of his land, because you knew how proudly they treated our ancestors. You made a name for yourself that lasts to this day.
You split the sea in front of them, so they walked through the middle of it on dry ground. But you threw those chasing them into the deep water, like a stone into rough waters.
You led them with a pillar of cloud by day, and with a pillar of fire by night to light up the way they should go.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven. You gave them fair rules, true laws, and good orders and commands.
You taught them about your holy Sabbath. Through your servant Moses you gave them commands, rules, and laws.
When they were hungry, you gave them bread from heaven. When they were thirsty, you brought water out of a rock for them. You told them to go in and take the land you had promised to give them.
But our ancestors became proud and stubborn, and they did not obey your commands.

They refused to listen. They forgot the miracles you did among them. They became stubborn and, in their rebellion, chose a leader to take them back to slavery in Egypt. But you are a God who forgives. You are kind and merciful, slow to become angry, and full of faithful love. You did not leave them,
even when they made a metal statue of a calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt.' They spoke terrible insults against you,

but because of your great mercy you did not leave them in the desert. The pillar of cloud did not stop leading them on their way during the day, and the pillar of fire did not stop lighting the way for them at night.
You gave your good Spirit to teach them. You did not stop giving them manna to eat, and you gave them water when they were thirsty.
For forty years you took care of them in the desert, and they had everything they needed. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
You gave them kingdoms and nations, and you gave them land in every direction. They took over the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You made their children as many as the stars in the sky. You brought them into the land you had told their ancestors to go in and take.

So their children went in and took the land. You defeated the Canaanites who lived in the land ahead of them. You handed them over to them, with their kings and the peoples of the land, so they could do what they wanted with them.

They captured walled cities and fertile land. They took over houses full of good things, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and lots of fruit trees. They ate until they were full and grew fat. They enjoyed your great goodness.
But they disobeyed you and rebelled against you. They turned their backs on your law. They killed your prophets, who had warned them to come back to you. They spoke terrible insults against you.

So you handed them over to their enemies, who made them suffer. But when they were in trouble, they cried out to you, and you heard them from heaven. Because of your great mercy, you gave them rescuers who saved them from their enemies.

But as soon as they had peace, they did evil again in front of you. So you left them to their enemies, who ruled over them. When they cried out to you again, you heard them from heaven. Again and again you rescued them because of your mercy.

You warned them to come back to your law, but they were proud and did not obey your commands. They sinned against your rules, the rules that give life to anyone who obeys them. They stubbornly turned their backs on you and would not listen.
For many years you were patient with them. Your Spirit warned them through your prophets, but they would not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of other lands.
But because of your great mercy, you did not destroy them completely or leave them. You are a kind and merciful God.

Now, our God, you are the great, powerful, and amazing God. You keep your covenant of faithful love. Do not think lightly of all the hardship that has come on us, on our kings, leaders, priests, prophets, ancestors, and all your people, from the time of the kings of Assyria until today.
You have been fair in everything that has happened to us. You have been faithful, but we have done wrong.
Our kings, leaders, priests, and ancestors did not obey your law. They did not listen to your commands or the warnings you gave them.
Even while they had their own kingdom, enjoying all the good things you gave them in the large, fertile land you gave them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil ways.
Look, today we are slaves. We are slaves in the land you gave our ancestors so they could enjoy its fruit and its good things.
Its great harvest goes to the kings you have put over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and our animals as they please. We are in great trouble.
Because of all this, we are making a firm agreement and writing it down. Our leaders, our Levites, and our priests are putting their seals on it."
These are the people who put their seals on the agreement: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
The Levites were: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the family of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and their fellow Levites: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
The leaders of the people were: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

The rest of the people also joined in: the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who had separated themselves from the peoples around them to obey God's law, together with their wives, sons, and daughters, everyone old enough to understand.

They joined their relatives and leaders and made a promise, under a curse if they broke it, to follow God's law, which was given through God's servant Moses. They promised to carefully obey all the commands, rules, and laws of the LORD our Lord.
We promise not to let our daughters marry the peoples around us, and not to let our sons marry their daughters.

If the peoples around us bring goods or grain to sell on the Sabbath, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on any other holy day. Every seventh year we will not farm the land, and we will cancel all debts.
We also accept the duty to give about four grams of silver each year for the service of the temple of our God.

This is for the holy bread, the regular grain offerings and burnt offerings, the offerings on the Sabbaths, at the New Moon festivals, and at the set festivals, for the holy offerings, for the sin offerings to make Israel right with God, and for all the work of the temple of our God.
We, the priests, Levites, and people, have thrown lots to decide when each family will bring wood to the temple of our God each year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as written in the law.
We promise to bring to the LORD's temple every year the first part of our harvest and the first fruit of every tree.
As the law says, we will bring our firstborn sons and the firstborn of our cattle, herds, and flocks to the temple of our God, to the priests who serve there.

We will bring to the priests, to the storerooms of the temple of our God, the first of our dough, our offerings, the fruit of all our trees, and our new wine and olive oil. We will bring a tenth of our crops to the Levites, because the Levites collect the tenth in all the towns where we farm.
A priest descended from Aaron must be with the Levites when they collect the tenth. The Levites must bring a tenth of what they collect to the temple of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.

The people of Israel and the Levites must bring their gifts of grain, new wine, and olive oil to the storerooms where the temple things are kept, and where the priests on duty, the gatekeepers, and the singers stay. We will not neglect the temple of our God.

The leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem. The rest of the people threw lots to choose one out of every ten families to live in Jerusalem, the holy city. The other nine stayed in their own towns.
The people praised all the men who offered to live in Jerusalem.

These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem. Other Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah.
Some of the people of Judah and Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, a descendant of Perez;
and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-Hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah.
The descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred sixty-eight brave men.
From Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;
and after him Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred twenty-eight men in all.
Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in charge of the city.
From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib; Jachin;
Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the official in charge of God's temple;
and their fellow priests who did the work in the temple, eight hundred twenty-two men. Also Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah;
and his relatives, who were family leaders, two hundred forty-two men. Also Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer;
and his relatives, who were brave warriors, one hundred twenty-eight men. Their leader was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;
Shabbethai and Jozabad, two of the leaders of the Levites, who were in charge of the outside work of God's temple;
Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, who led the thanksgiving and prayer; Bakbukiah, who was second among his relatives; and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
There were two hundred eighty-four Levites in all in the holy city.
The gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon, and their relatives, who guarded the gates. There were one hundred seventy-two of them.
The rest of the Israelites, priests, and Levites lived in all the towns of Judah, each on their own family land.
The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel. Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of them.
The leader of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica. He was one of Asaph's descendants, the singers in charge of the service in God's temple.
The king had given orders about the singers, and they received a fixed amount every day.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the king's helper in everything that had to do with the people.
As for the villages and their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns, in Dibon and its towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
in Jeshua, Moladah, Beth Pelet,
Hazar Shual, and in Beersheba and its towns,
in Ziklag, and in Meconah and its towns,
in En Rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, in Lachish and its fields, and in Azekah and its towns. So they settled all the way from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
The people of Benjamin lived from Geba onward, in Michmash, Aija, and Bethel and its towns,
in Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod, and Ono, in the Valley of Craftsmen.
Some groups of Levites from Judah settled in the land of Benjamin.
These are the priests and Levites who came back with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their relatives in the time of Jeshua.
The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. Mattaniah and his relatives were in charge of the songs of thanks.
Bakbukiah and Unno, their relatives, stood across from them during the services.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim. Joiakim was the father of Eliashib. Eliashib was the father of Joiada.
Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
In the time of Joiakim, these priests were the family leaders: from Seraiah's family, Meraiah; from Jeremiah's, Hananiah;
from Ezra's, Meshullam; from Amariah's, Jehohanan;
from Malluchi's, Jonathan; from Shebaniah's, Joseph;
from Harim's, Adna; from Meraioth's, Helkai;
from Iddo's, Zechariah; from Ginnethon's, Meshullam;
from Abijah's, Zichri; from Miniamin's and Moadiah's, Piltai;
from Bilgah's, Shammua; from Shemaiah's, Jehonathan;
from Joiarib's, Mattenai; from Jedaiah's, Uzzi;
from Sallai's, Kallai; from Amok's, Eber;
from Hilkiah's, Hashabiah; and from Jedaiah's, Nethanel.
In the time of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the family leaders of the Levites and the priests were written down, while Darius the Persian was king.
The family leaders of the Levites were written in the book of the records up to the time of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel. Their relatives stood across from them to praise and give thanks, one group answering the other, as David the man of God had commanded.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
They served in the time of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the time of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and teacher.

When the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated, the Levites were brought in from wherever they lived to Jerusalem. They came to celebrate the dedication with joy, with songs of thanks, and with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
The singers also gathered from the area around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
from Beth Gilgal, and from the area of Geba and Azmaveth. The singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites made themselves clean, and then they made the people, the gates, and the wall clean.
I had the leaders of Judah go up on top of the wall. I also chose two large choirs to give thanks and march along the wall. One choir went to the right, toward the Garbage Gate.
Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah followed them,
along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
Some of the priests also followed with trumpets, along with Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
and his relatives Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played the musical instruments of David the man of God. Ezra the teacher led this group.
At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the steps of the City of David, on the slope of the wall, above David's palace, to the Water Gate on the east.
The second choir went the other way, to the left. I followed them on top of the wall, together with half the people. We went past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,
over the Ephraim Gate, the Old Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. We stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
Then the two choirs that gave thanks took their places in God's temple. So did I, together with half of the officials,
and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with their trumpets,
and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loudly, led by Jezrahiah.
That day they offered many sacrifices and celebrated, because God had given them great joy. The women and children also celebrated. The sound of joy in Jerusalem could be heard far away.

On that day men were chosen to be in charge of the storerooms for the gifts, the first part of the harvest, and the tenths. From the fields around the towns, they were to bring into the storerooms the shares the law required for the priests and Levites. The people of Judah were happy with the priests and Levites who served.
They did the work of their God and the work of making things clean, as did the singers and gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
Long ago, in the time of David and Asaph, there were leaders of the singers, and songs of praise and thanks to God.

So in the time of Zerubbabel and of Nehemiah, all Israel gave daily shares for the singers and gatekeepers. They also set apart a share for the other Levites, and the Levites set apart a share for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
On that day the book of Moses was read aloud to the people. They found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever be allowed into God's assembly,
because they did not meet the Israelites with food and water. Instead they paid Balaam to curse them, but our God turned the curse into a blessing.
When the people heard this law, they separated from Israel everyone of foreign descent.
Before this, Eliashib the priest had been put in charge of the storerooms of the temple of our God. He was a relative of Tobiah,

and he had given Tobiah a large room. That room had been used to store the grain offerings, the incense, the temple things, and the tenths of grain, new wine, and olive oil that the law said belonged to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the gifts for the priests.
While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem. In the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, I had gone back to the king. Some time later I asked the king for permission to leave,
and I came back to Jerusalem. Then I found out about the evil thing Eliashib had done for Tobiah by giving him a room in the courtyards of God's temple.
I was very upset, and I threw all of Tobiah's things out of the room.
I gave orders to clean the rooms, and then I put back the things from God's temple, with the grain offerings and the incense.
I also found out that the Levites had not been given their shares of food. So the Levites and singers who did the work had all gone back to their own fields.
So I scolded the officials and asked them, "Why has God's temple been neglected?" Then I called the Levites back and put them back at their posts.
Then all the people of Judah brought their tenths of grain, new wine, and olive oil to the storerooms.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher, and a Levite named Pedaiah in charge of the storerooms. Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, was their helper. These men were known to be honest, and their job was to hand out the shares to their relatives.
Remember me for this, my God. Do not forget the good things I have faithfully done for the temple of my God and its services.

In those days I saw people in Judah pressing grapes on the Sabbath. Others were bringing in bundles of grain and loading them on donkeys, together with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads. They were bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. So I warned them not to sell food on that day.
Some people from Tyre who lived in Jerusalem were bringing in fish and all kinds of goods and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
So I scolded the important men of Judah. I said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing? You are treating the Sabbath day like any other day!
Didn't your ancestors do the same thing? That is why our God brought all this trouble on us and on this city. Now you are making his anger against Israel even worse by not keeping the Sabbath holy."

So when evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut and not opened until the Sabbath was over. I put some of my own men at the gates so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.
Once or twice, the traders and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
But I warned them, "Why are you spending the night by the wall? If you do this again, I will use force against you." From then on they did not come on the Sabbath.

Then I ordered the Levites to make themselves clean and to go and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this too, my God, and have mercy on me because of your great and faithful love.
In those days I also saw Jewish men who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or the language of some other people, and they could not speak the language of Judah.

I scolded them and called down curses on them. I hit some of them and pulled out their hair. I made them promise in God's name, "You must not let your daughters marry their sons, and you must not take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves.

Wasn't it because of marriages like these that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among all the nations there was no king like him. His God loved him and made him king over all Israel. But even he was led into sin by foreign women.
Should we listen to you and do this terrible evil? Should we be unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"
One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat from Horon. So I chased him away from me.
Remember them, my God, because they have made the priesthood unclean and broken the covenant of the priests and Levites.
So I made the priests and Levites clean of everything foreign, and I gave them their duties, each one his own work.
I also arranged for the wood to be brought at set times, and for the first part of the harvest. Remember me kindly, my God.
Esth: This happened in the days of King Xerxes, also called Ahasuerus. He ruled over one hundred twenty-seven provinces, from India all the way to Ethiopia.
At that time King Xerxes ruled his kingdom from his royal throne in the fortress city of Susa.
In the third year of his rule, he gave a big feast for all his officials and servants. The army leaders of Persia and Media, the important men, and the governors of the provinces were there with him.
For a long time, one hundred eighty days, he showed off the great wealth of his kingdom and the glory and greatness of his royal power.

When those days were over, the king gave a seven-day feast for all the people in the fortress city of Susa, from the most important to the least. It was held in the garden courtyard of the king's palace.

There were curtains of white and blue cloth, tied with cords of fine white linen and purple material to silver rings on marble pillars. There were couches of gold and silver on a floor made of red, white, yellow, and black marble.
Drinks were served in gold cups, each one different from the others. There was plenty of royal wine, because the king was very generous.
By the king's order, no one was forced to drink. The king had told all the servants in his palace to give each guest whatever they wanted.
Queen Vashti also gave a feast for the women in King Xerxes' royal palace.
On the seventh day, when the king was in high spirits from the wine, he gave orders to the seven officials who served him: Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas.
He told them to bring Queen Vashti to him wearing her royal crown, so he could show off her beauty to the people and the officials, because she was very beautiful.
But when the officials gave Queen Vashti the king's order, she refused to come. Then the king became very angry. His anger burned inside him.
The king spoke with the wise men who understood the times, because it was his custom to ask advice from experts in law and justice.

The men closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media. They could meet with the king at any time and had the highest positions in the kingdom.
The king asked, "What does the law say should be done to Queen Vashti? She did not obey King Xerxes' order that the officials brought to her."

Memucan answered in front of the king and the officials, "Queen Vashti has not only done wrong to the king. She has also done wrong to all the officials and all the people in all the provinces of King Xerxes.
All the women will hear what the queen did, and they will look down on their husbands. They will say, 'King Xerxes ordered Queen Vashti to be brought to him, but she would not come.'
This very day the important women of Persia and Media who have heard what the queen did will tell all the king's officials the same thing. There will be no end of disrespect and anger.

If it pleases the king, let him give a royal order and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media, which cannot be changed. The order should say that Vashti may never again come into King Xerxes' presence. Let the king give her royal position to someone else who is better than she is.
When the king's order is announced all through his huge kingdom, all the wives will respect their husbands, from the most important to the least."
The king and his officials liked this advice, so the king did what Memucan said.

He sent letters to all the provinces of his kingdom, to each province in its own writing and to each people in their own language. The letters said that every man should be the ruler of his own home and should speak the language of his own people.
Later, when King Xerxes' anger had calmed down, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been ordered against her.
Then the king's personal servants said, "Let a search be made for beautiful young women who have never married, for the king.

Let the king choose officers in every province of his kingdom to bring all these beautiful young women to the women's house in the fortress city of Susa. Let them be put under the care of Hegai, the king's official in charge of the women, and let them be given beauty treatments.
Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen instead of Vashti." The king liked this advice, and he did it.
Now there was a Jewish man in the fortress city of Susa named Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin.
He had been taken from Jerusalem as a prisoner along with Jeconiah king of Judah, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took them away.

Mordecai had raised his cousin Hadassah, also called Esther, because she had no father or mother. This young woman had a lovely figure and was beautiful. When her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.

When the king's order was announced, many young women were brought to the fortress city of Susa and put under Hegai's care. Esther was also taken to the king's palace and put under the care of Hegai, who was in charge of the women.

Esther pleased Hegai, and he was kind to her. He quickly gave her beauty treatments and special food. He gave her seven chosen servant girls from the king's palace and moved her and her servant girls to the best place in the women's house.
Esther had not told anyone who her people or her family were, because Mordecai had told her not to.
Every day Mordecai walked back and forth near the courtyard of the women's house to find out how Esther was and what was happening to her.
Before a young woman's turn came to go to King Xerxes, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with perfumes and creams for women.
When a young woman went to the king, she was given anything she wanted to take with her from the women's house to the king's palace.

She would go to the king in the evening, and in the morning she would go back to a second women's house, under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's official in charge of the king's other wives. She would not go to the king again unless he was pleased with her and called for her by name.

Esther was the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle. Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter. When it was her turn to go to the king, she asked only for what Hegai, the king's official in charge of the women, suggested. Everyone who saw Esther liked her.
Esther was taken to King Xerxes in his royal palace in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his rule.

The king loved Esther more than all the other women. She pleased him and won his favor more than any of the other young women. So he put the royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king gave a great feast for all his officials and servants. It was Esther's feast. He announced a holiday in all the provinces and gave gifts generously, as only a king can.
When the young women were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
