With great force God grabs my clothing. He holds me by the collar of my shirt.
He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, God, but you do not answer. I stand up, but you only look at me.
You have turned cruel toward me. You attack me with all your strength.
You lift me up and let the wind carry me away. You toss me around in the storm.
I know you will bring me down to death, to the place where all living things must go.
Surely no one would strike a man who is ruined and crying for help in his trouble.
Didn't I cry for those who were in trouble? Didn't I feel sad for the poor?
But when I hoped for good, evil came. When I looked for light, darkness came.
My insides are churning and never rest. Days of suffering face me.
I walk around in darkness, without sunlight. I stand up in public and cry for help.
I have become a brother of jackals and a friend of ostriches.
My skin turns black and peels off. My body burns with fever.
My harp plays only sad songs, and my flute only the sound of crying.
I made a promise with my eyes not to look with desire at a young woman.
What would God above give me? What would the Almighty in heaven give as my share?
Isn't disaster for evil people, and trouble for those who do wrong?
Doesn't God see everything I do and count every step I take?
If I have lived a lie, or my feet have hurried to cheat others,
let God weigh me on honest scales, and he will see that I have no fault.
If my steps have turned off his path, if my heart has followed what my eyes wanted, or if my hands are dirty with sin,
then let someone else eat what I have planted, and let my crops be pulled up.
If my heart has been tempted by a woman, or if I have hidden and waited at my neighbor's door,
then let my wife grind grain for another man, and let other men sleep with her.
That would be a shameful thing to do, a sin that judges should punish.
It is a fire that burns all the way to destruction. It would burn up everything I have.
If I have refused to listen to the complaints of my male or female servants when they had something against me,
what will I do when God stands up to judge me? What will I say when he asks me to explain?
Didn't the same God who made me in my mother's womb make them too? Didn't he form all of us before we were born?
If I have refused to help the poor, or let widows lose hope,
if I have kept my food to myself and not shared it with orphans,
but from the time I was young I have raised orphans as a father would, and from my birth I have guided widows;
if I have seen anyone dying for lack of clothes, or a poor person with nothing to wear,
and they did not thank me for warming them with the wool of my sheep;
if I have raised my hand against an orphan because I knew the judges at the city gate would take my side,
then let my arm fall from my shoulder, and let it be broken off at the joint.
I have always been afraid of the disaster God would send. Because of his greatness, I could not do such things.
If I have put my hope in gold, or said to pure gold, 'You are my security,'
if I have been happy because I was very rich and had gained so much,
if I have looked at the shining sun or the bright moon moving across the sky,
and my heart was secretly tempted to worship them, and I blew them a kiss with my hand,
that would also be a sin for judges to punish. I would have been unfaithful to the God who is above.
If I have been glad when my enemy was ruined, or happy when trouble came to him,
but I have never let my mouth sin by cursing his life;
if the men of my household never said, 'Who has not been fed with Job's meat?'
but no stranger ever had to spend the night in the street, because I always opened my door to travelers;
if I have hidden my sins as others do, by hiding my guilt in my heart,
because I was afraid of the crowd, or afraid of what families would think, so that I kept quiet and stayed inside;
oh, how I wish someone would listen to me! Look, I sign my name to my defense. Let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser write down the charges against me!
I would proudly carry it on my shoulder. I would wear it like a crown.
I would tell him every step I have taken. I would come to him like a prince.
If my land cries out against me, and all its furrows are wet with tears,
if I have eaten its crops without paying, or caused the death of its owners,
then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley." This is the end of Job's words.
So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was sure he was right.
Then Elihu became very angry. He was the son of Barakel, from Buz, from the family of Ram. He was angry with Job, because Job made himself out to be right instead of God.
He was also angry with Job's three friends, because they had not found a good answer, and yet they had said Job was wrong.
Elihu had waited before speaking to Job, because the others were older than he was.
But when Elihu saw that the three men had nothing more to say, he became angry.
So Elihu son of Barakel from Buz said: "I am young, and you are old. That is why I held back and was afraid to tell you what I think.
I thought, 'Older people should speak. Those who have lived many years should teach wisdom.'
But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
It is not only the old who are wise, or only the aged who understand what is right.
So I say, 'Listen to me. I will tell you what I think too.'
I waited while you spoke. I listened to your reasons while you searched for words.
I paid close attention to you, but not one of you proved Job wrong or answered what he said.
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom. Let God answer him, not people.'
Job has not argued against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
These men are shocked and have no more answers. They have nothing left to say.
Should I keep waiting now that they are silent, now that they stand there with no answer?
No, I will give my answer too. I will tell you what I think.
I am full of words, and the spirit inside me pushes me to speak.
Inside, I am like wine sealed up in a bottle, like new wineskins ready to burst.
I must speak and get relief. I must open my mouth and answer.
I will not take anyone's side, and I will not flatter anyone.
I do not know how to flatter. If I did, my Maker would quickly take me away.
But now, Job, please listen to what I say. Pay attention to all my words.
Look, I am about to open my mouth. My words are on the tip of my tongue.
My words come from an honest heart. My lips will speak sincerely what I know.
The Spirit of God has made me. The breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can. Get your arguments ready and stand up to face me.
Look, I am just like you in God's sight. I too was made from clay.
So you do not need to be afraid of me. I will not press down hard on you.
But you have said it while I was listening. I heard your very words:
'I am pure and have done nothing wrong. I am clean and have no sin.
Yet God has found reasons to attack me. He treats me as his enemy.
He puts my feet in chains and watches every step I take.'
But I tell you, you are not right in this, because God is greater than any human.
Why do you complain to him that he does not answer people's questions?
God speaks in one way, and then in another, even though people may not notice it.
He speaks in dreams, in visions at night, when people are in a deep sleep, as they lie in their beds.
He may speak in their ears and frighten them with warnings,
to turn them away from doing wrong and keep them from pride.
He keeps them from going down to the grave, and saves their lives from being killed by the sword.
Or someone may be corrected with pain on his sickbed, with constant aching in his bones.
He cannot stand to eat. Even his favorite food disgusts him.
His body wastes away to nothing, and his bones that were hidden now stick out.
He comes close to the grave, and his life is near to those who bring death.
But if an angel is there beside him, one out of a thousand, a helper to tell him what is right,
the angel will be kind to him and say, 'Save him from going down to the grave. I have found a price to set him free.'
Then his body will become as healthy as a child's. He will be young and strong again.
He will pray to God, and God will be pleased with him. He will see God's face and shout for joy. God will make him right again.
He will sing to others, 'I sinned and twisted what was right, but I was not punished as I deserved.
God saved me from going down to the grave, and I will live to see the light.'
God does all these things for a person, again and again,
to bring him back from the grave, so that the light of life can shine on him.
Pay attention, Job, and listen to me. Be quiet, and I will speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, because I want to prove you right.
But if not, listen to me. Be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom."
Then Elihu continued:
"Listen to my words, you wise men. Pay attention to me, you who know so much.
The ear tests words, just as the tongue tastes food.
Let's decide for ourselves what is right. Let's learn together what is good.
Job says, 'I am innocent, but God has refused me justice.
Even though I am right, I am called a liar. I have a wound that will not heal, even though I have done nothing wrong.'
Is there anyone like Job? He drinks up insults like water.
He keeps company with people who do evil. He spends time with wicked people.
He says, 'It does a person no good to try to please God.'
So listen to me, you men who understand. God would never do evil. The Almighty would never do wrong.
He pays people back for what they do. He gives them what their ways deserve.
It is true that God will never do wrong. The Almighty will never twist justice.
Did someone put him in charge of the earth? Did someone make him ruler of the whole world?
If he decided to take back his spirit and his breath,
every living thing would die together, and people would go back to the dust.
If you understand, listen to this. Pay attention to what I say.
Can someone who hates justice rule? Will you condemn the one who is fair and mighty?
He is the one who says to kings, 'You are worthless,' and to important people, 'You are wicked.'
He does not favor rulers or treat the rich better than the poor, because he made them all with his own hands.
People die suddenly in the middle of the night. They are shaken and pass away. The powerful are removed without human help.
God watches how people live. He sees every step they take.
There is no darkness or deep shadow where evil people can hide.
God does not need to look at a person very long before bringing him to judgment.
He breaks the powerful without needing to ask questions, and puts others in their place.
He knows what they do. He overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.
He punishes them for their evil where everyone can see,
because they turned away from following him and paid no attention to any of his ways.
They made the poor cry out to God, and he heard the cry of those in need.
But if God stays quiet, who can blame him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Still, he watches over both nations and people,
so that godless people will not rule and trap the people.
Suppose someone says to God, 'I am guilty, but I will not sin any more.
Teach me what I cannot see. If I have done wrong, I will not do it again.'
Should God reward you on your terms, when you refuse to change? You must decide, not I. So tell me what you know.
People with understanding will agree with me, and every wise person who hears me will say,
'Job speaks without knowing what he is talking about. His words make no sense.'
I wish Job would be tested to the limit, because he answers like an evil man.
He adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands at us to mock us and keeps talking against God."
Then Elihu continued:
"Do you think it is right for you to say, 'I am more right than God'?
You ask him, 'What good does it do me? What do I gain by not sinning?'
I will answer you, and your friends with you.
Look up at the sky and see. Look at the clouds high above you.
If you sin, how does that hurt God? If you sin again and again, what does that do to him?
If you do what is right, what do you give him? What does he receive from you?
Your evil only hurts people like yourself, and your good deeds only help other humans.
People cry out when they are crushed by cruelty. They call for help against the power of the strong.
But no one says, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,
who teaches us more than he teaches the animals, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'
They cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evil people.
God does not listen to their empty cries. The Almighty pays no attention to them.
So he will surely not listen when you say you cannot see him, that your case is before him and you are waiting for him.
And now you say that he does not punish in his anger and does not pay much attention to sin.
So Job opens his mouth and says nothing worthwhile. He talks a lot without knowing anything."
Elihu went on speaking:
"Be patient with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to say for God.
I will gather my knowledge from far and wide, and I will show that my Maker is right.
Be sure that my words are not false. Someone with complete knowledge is here with you.
God is mighty, but he does not look down on anyone. He is mighty and firm in his purpose.
He does not keep evil people alive, but he gives justice to those who suffer.
He does not take his eyes off good people. He seats them on thrones with kings and lifts them up forever.
But if people are bound in chains, caught in the ropes of suffering,
he shows them what they have done, how they have sinned in their pride.
He makes them listen to his correction and commands them to turn away from evil.
If they obey and serve him, they will spend the rest of their days in wealth and their years in happiness.
But if they do not obey, they will die by the sword. They will die without knowledge.
Godless people hold on to their anger. Even when God chains them, they do not cry for help.
They die while they are young, among the shameful people at the shrines.
But God rescues those who suffer through their suffering. He speaks to them in their troubles.
He wanted to lead you out of trouble into a wide-open place, free from limits, to a table full of the best food.
But now you are full of the judgment the wicked deserve. Judgment and justice have taken hold of you.
Be careful that wealth does not lead you into anger. Do not let a large bribe turn you aside.
Will your riches or all your great strength help you when trouble comes?
Do not long for the night, when people are taken away from their homes.
Be careful not to turn to evil, because that seems to be what you would choose instead of suffering.
Look, God is great in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
Who has told him what to do? Who can say to him, 'You have done wrong'?
Remember to praise what he has done, which people have sung about.
Everyone has seen it. People look at it from far away.
Yes, God is great, beyond our understanding. No one can count the number of his years.
He draws up drops of water and turns them into rain from the mist.
The clouds pour down the rain, and it falls on people in showers.
Who can understand how he spreads out the clouds, or the thunder that comes from where he lives?
Look how he spreads his lightning around him and covers the bottom of the sea.
This is how he rules the nations and gives them plenty of food.
He fills his hands with lightning and commands it to hit its target.
His thunder tells of his coming. Even the cattle know a storm is on its way.
At this my heart pounds and jumps out of its place.
Listen! Listen to the roar of his voice, the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
He sends his lightning across the whole sky, to the ends of the earth.
After the lightning comes a roaring sound. He thunders with his majestic voice. He does not hold back the lightning when his voice is heard.
God's voice thunders in amazing ways. He does great things we cannot understand.
He says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth.' He tells the rain to pour down, and the heavy rain to fall.
He stops all people from working, so everyone he made may know his power.
The animals go into their shelters and stay in their dens.
The storm comes out of its room, and the cold comes from the north wind.
God's breath makes ice, and the wide waters freeze over.
He loads the thick clouds with water and scatters his lightning through them.
They swirl around wherever he directs them, doing whatever he commands them all over the face of the earth.
He sends the clouds to punish people, or to water his land, or to show his faithful love.
Listen to this, Job. Stop and think about God's amazing works.
Do you know how God controls the clouds and makes his lightning flash?
Do you know how the clouds hang in the sky, the amazing works of the one who knows everything?
You sweat in your clothes when the land is quiet under the hot south wind.
Can you help him spread out the skies, which are as hard as a mirror made of bronze?
Tell us what we should say to him. We cannot make our case, because we are in the dark.
Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?
No one can look at the sun when it shines brightly in the sky after the wind has cleared the clouds away.
Golden light comes from the north. God comes in amazing majesty.
We cannot reach the Almighty. He is great in power. He is fair and completely right, and he does not crush people.
That is why people respect him. He does not pay attention to those who think they are wise."
Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
"Who is this who darkens my plans with words that have no knowledge?
Get ready like a man. I will ask you questions, and you will answer me.
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you understand.
Who decided how big it would be? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it?
What were its foundations set on? Who laid its cornerstone,
while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?
Who shut the sea behind doors when it burst out from the womb,
when I made the clouds its clothing and wrapped it in thick darkness,
when I set its limits and put its bars and doors in place,
and said, 'You may come this far, but no farther. Here your proud waves must stop'?
Have you ever in your life given orders to the morning, or shown the dawn its place,
so it could take hold of the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth takes shape like clay under a seal. Its features stand out like the folds of a garment.
The light is taken away from the wicked, and the arm they raised to strike is broken.
Have you gone down to the springs at the bottom of the sea, or walked in the deepest parts of the ocean?
Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness?
Do you understand how wide the earth is? Tell me, if you know all this.
What is the way to the home of light? And where does darkness live?
Can you take them to their places? Do you know the paths to their homes?
Surely you know, because you were already born then, and you have lived so many years!
Have you gone into the storerooms of the snow, or seen the storerooms of the hail,
which I keep for times of trouble, for days of battle and war?
What is the way to the place where the lightning is spread out, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
Who cuts a channel for the floodwaters, or a path for the thunderstorm,
to bring rain on land where no one lives, on a wilderness with no people in it,
to water the empty and dry ground and make the new grass grow?
Does the rain have a father? Who is the father of the drops of dew?
Whose womb did the ice come from? Who gave birth to the frost from the sky
when the waters become as hard as stone and the surface of the deep sea freezes?
Can you tie up the star group called the Pleiades, or loosen the belt of Orion?
Can you bring out the star groups in their seasons, or guide the Bear with her cubs?
Do you know the laws of the skies? Can you make them rule over the earth?
Can you shout to the clouds and make them cover you with a flood of water?
Can you send out the lightning bolts so they go? Do they report to you, 'Here we are'?
Who gave wisdom to the heart? Who gave understanding to the mind?
Who is wise enough to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of the sky
when the dust turns hard and the clumps of earth stick together?
Can you hunt food for the lioness, or satisfy the hunger of the young lions
when they crouch in their dens or wait in the bushes?
Who gives food to the raven when its young cry out to God and wander around with nothing to eat?
Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the deer have their young?
Can you count the months until they give birth? Do you know when the time comes?
They crouch down, give birth to their young, and their labor pains end.
Their young grow strong in the open fields. They go off and do not come back.
Who set the wild donkey free? Who untied its ropes?
I gave it the wilderness as its home, and the salt flats as the place where it lives.
It laughs at the noise of the city. It does not hear a driver shouting.
It roams the hills for its pasture and looks for anything green to eat.
Will the wild ox agree to serve you? Will it stay by your feeding trough at night?
Can you tie it with a rope to plow your fields? Will it pull a plow through your valleys behind you?
Will you depend on it because it is so strong? Will you leave your heavy work to it?
Can you trust it to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
The ostrich flaps its wings proudly, but its feathers are not like the stork's that care for its young.
It lays its eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
It forgets that a foot might crush them, or that a wild animal might step on them.
It treats its young harshly, as if they were not its own. It does not worry that its work might be for nothing,
because God did not give it wisdom or a share of good sense.
Yet when it spreads its feathers to run, it laughs at the horse and its rider.
Do you give the horse its strength? Do you clothe its neck with a flowing mane?
Do you make it jump like a locust? Its proud snorting is terrifying.
It paws the ground in the valley and is glad about its strength. It charges out to meet the weapons.
It laughs at fear and is afraid of nothing. It does not run away from the sword.
The quiver of arrows rattles against its side, along with the flashing spear and javelin.
It races wildly over the ground. It cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.
When the trumpet blows, it snorts, 'Aha!' It smells the battle from far away. It hears the commanders' shouts and the battle cry.
Is it your wisdom that makes the hawk fly and spread its wings toward the south?
Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest up high?
It lives on the cliff and stays there at night, on a rocky peak where it is safe.
From there it looks for food. Its eyes see it from far away.
Its young ones feast on blood. Where there are dead bodies, the eagle is there."
The LORD said to Job:
"Will the one who argues with the Almighty correct him? Let the one who accuses God answer him!"
Then Job answered the LORD:
"I am nothing. How can I answer you? I put my hand over my mouth.
I spoke once, but I have no answer. I spoke twice, but I will say no more."
Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
"Get ready like a man. I will ask you questions, and you will answer me.
Would you say my judgment is wrong? Would you blame me to prove that you are right?
Do you have an arm as strong as God's? Can your voice thunder like his?
Then dress yourself in glory and splendor. Clothe yourself with honor and majesty.
Let loose your fierce anger. Look at everyone who is proud and bring them down.
Look at everyone who is proud and humble them. Crush the wicked where they stand.
Bury them all together in the dust. Shut them up in the grave.
Then I myself will admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
Look at Behemoth, which I made just as I made you. It eats grass like an ox.
Look at the strength in its hips, the power in the muscles of its belly.
Its tail sways like a cedar tree. The muscles of its thighs are tightly woven together.
Its bones are like tubes of bronze. Its legs are like bars of iron.
It is the greatest of the animals God made. Only its Maker can come near it with a sword.
The hills bring it food, where all the wild animals play.
It lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds in the marsh.
The lotus plants cover it with their shade. The willows by the stream surround it.
If the river rages, it is not afraid. It stays calm even if the Jordan River rushes up to its mouth.
Can anyone capture it while it is watching, or trap it and put a ring through its nose?
Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook, or tie down its tongue with a rope?
Can you put a rope through its nose, or a hook through its jaw?
Will it keep begging you for mercy? Will it speak gently to you?
Will it make an agreement with you to be your slave for life?
Can you play with it as you would with a bird? Can you put it on a leash for your girls?
Will traders bargain over it? Will they divide it up among the merchants?
Can you fill its skin with harpoons, or its head with fishing spears?
Put your hand on it once, and you will remember the fight. You will never do it again!
Any hope of beating it is useless. Just seeing it makes a person fall down in fear.
No one is fierce enough to wake it up. Then who can stand up against me?
Who has given me anything that I must pay back? Everything under the sky belongs to me.
I will not stay quiet about its legs, its great strength, and its fine body.
Who can strip off its outer coat? Who would come near its open jaws?
Who dares to open its mouth? Its teeth all around are terrifying.
Its back has rows of shields, tightly sealed together.
Each one is so close to the next that no air can pass between them.
They are joined to each other. They stick together and cannot be pulled apart.
When it sneezes, light flashes. Its eyes are like the first light of dawn.
Burning torches stream from its mouth. Sparks of fire shoot out.
Smoke pours from its nose, like steam from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
Its breath sets coals on fire. Flames shoot out of its mouth.
Its neck is very strong. Terror goes ahead of it.
The folds of its flesh are joined tightly together. They are firm and cannot be moved.
Its heart is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone.
When it rises up, the mighty are afraid. They run away from its thrashing.
A sword that strikes it does no harm. Neither does a spear, a dart, or an arrow.
It treats iron like straw and bronze like rotten wood.
Arrows do not make it run away. Stones from a sling are like bits of straw to it.
It thinks clubs are like straw. It laughs at the sound of a spear flying at it.
Its belly is covered with sharp pieces like broken pottery. It leaves a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
It makes the deep water boil like a pot. It stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment.
It leaves a shining trail behind it. You would think the deep sea had white hair.
Nothing on earth is equal to it. It was made to have no fear.
It looks down on everything that is proud. It is king over all the proud beasts."
Then Job answered the LORD:
"I know that you can do anything. No plan of yours can be stopped.
You asked, 'Who is this who hides my plans with words that have no knowledge?' I spoke about things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
You said, 'Listen now, and I will speak. I will ask you questions, and you will answer me.'
Before, I had only heard about you, but now I have seen you with my own eyes.
So I hate myself for what I said, and I turn away from my sin, sitting in dust and ashes."

After the LORD had said these things to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "I am angry with you and your two friends, because you have not spoken what is right about me, as my servant Job has.

So now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not punish you for your foolishness. You have not spoken what is right about me, as my servant Job has."
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.
After Job prayed for his friends, the LORD made him successful again. The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then all his brothers and sisters, and everyone who had known him before, came and ate a meal with him in his house. They comforted him and showed him sympathy for all the trouble the LORD had brought on him. Each of them gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
The LORD blessed the last part of Job's life even more than the first. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-Happuch.
In all the land there were no women as beautiful as Job's daughters. Their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
After this, Job lived one hundred forty years. He saw his children, his grandchildren, and four generations of his family.
Then Job died, old and having lived a long, full life.
Ps: Happy is the person who does not follow the advice of wicked people, who does not stand on the path that sinners take, and who does not sit down with people who mock.
Instead, he loves the LORD's law, and he thinks about it day and night.
He is like a tree planted beside streams of water. It gives its fruit at the right time, and its leaves never dry up. Everything he does goes well.
Wicked people are not like that. They are like chaff that the wind blows away.
So the wicked will not stand firm on judgment day. Sinners will have no place among good people.
The LORD watches over the way of good people, but the way of the wicked leads to ruin.
Why are the nations so angry? Why do the peoples make useless plans?
The kings of the earth get ready to fight, and the rulers plan together against the LORD and against his Anointed King. They say,
"Let's break their chains and throw off their ropes."
The one who sits on his throne in heaven laughs. The Lord makes fun of them.
Then he speaks to them in his anger and terrifies them in his fury.
He says, "I have put my King on Zion, my holy hill."
I will announce what the LORD has decided. He said to me, "You are my son. Today I have become your father.
Ask me, and I will give you the nations as your own, the farthest parts of the earth as your property.
You will break them with an iron rod. You will smash them to pieces like clay pots."
So now, you kings, be wise. Listen to this warning, you rulers of the earth.
Serve the LORD with respect and fear, and celebrate with trembling.
Bow down and honour the Son, or he will be angry and you will be destroyed on your way, because his anger can flare up quickly. Happy are all who go to him for safety.
A psalm of David, written when he ran away from his son Absalom. LORD, I have so many enemies! So many people are rising up against me.
Many people are saying about me, "God will not rescue him." Selah.
But you, LORD, are a shield that protects me all around. You give me honour, and you lift up my head.
I cry out loud to the LORD, and he answers me from his holy hill. Selah.
I lie down and sleep, and I wake up again, because the LORD keeps me safe.
I will not be afraid of tens of thousands of people who surround me to attack me.
Get up, LORD! Save me, my God! You have slapped all my enemies across the face. You have broken the teeth of the wicked.
Rescue comes from the LORD. May your blessing be on your people. Selah.
For the music director. To be played on stringed instruments. A psalm of David. Answer me when I call, my God who makes me right. Give me relief from my troubles. Be kind to me and hear my prayer.
You people, how long will you turn my honour into shame? How long will you love what is worthless and chase after lies? Selah.
But know this: the LORD has chosen faithful people for himself. The LORD will hear me when I call to him.
Tremble and do not sin. When you are on your bed, think deeply and be quiet. Selah.
Offer the right sacrifices, and trust in the LORD.
Many people say, "Who will show us anything good?" LORD, let the light of your face shine on us.
You have filled my heart with more joy than people have when they have plenty of grain and new wine.
I will lie down and sleep in peace, because you alone, LORD, keep me safe.
For the music director. To be played with flutes. A psalm of David. LORD, listen to my words. Think about what I am saying.
Hear my cry for help, my King and my God, because I pray to you.
LORD, in the morning you hear my voice. In the morning I bring my requests to you and wait for your answer.
You are not a God who is pleased with evil. Evil people cannot live with you.
Proud people cannot stand in front of you. You hate everyone who does evil.
You destroy those who tell lies. The LORD hates people who murder and cheat.
But because of your great and faithful love, I will come into your house. I will bow down toward your holy temple with deep respect.
LORD, lead me in your goodness, because I have enemies. Make your path straight in front of me.
Nothing they say can be trusted. Their hearts are full of destruction. Their throats are like an open grave. They use their tongues to flatter.
God, declare them guilty. Let their own plans make them fall. Throw them out because of their many sins, because they have rebelled against you.
But let everyone who goes to you for safety be glad. Let them always shout for joy, because you protect them. Let those who love your name celebrate because of you.
LORD, you bless good people. You surround them with your kindness like a shield.
For the music director. To be played on stringed instruments, on the eight-stringed lyre. A psalm of David. LORD, do not correct me when you are angry. Do not punish me when you are furious.
Be kind to me, LORD, because I am weak. LORD, heal me, because my bones are shaking.
My whole being is in deep distress. LORD, how long will this go on?
Come back, LORD, and rescue me. Save me because of your faithful love.
The dead do not remember you. Who can thank you from the grave?
I am worn out from groaning. Every night my bed is flooded with my tears. I soak my couch with my crying.
My eyes grow weak with sorrow. They are worn out because of all my enemies.
Get away from me, all you who do evil, because the LORD has heard me crying.
The LORD has heard my cry for mercy. The LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be ashamed and terrified. They will turn back and suddenly be put to shame.
A song of David, which he sang to the LORD about Cush from the tribe of Benjamin. LORD my God, I come to you for safety. Save me from everyone who is chasing me, and rescue me.
If you do not, they will tear me apart like a lion, ripping me to pieces with no one to rescue me.
LORD my God, if I have done this, if my hands have done wrong,
if I have done evil to someone who was at peace with me, or robbed my enemy for no reason,
then let my enemy chase me and catch me. Let him trample my life into the ground and leave my honour lying in the dust. Selah.
Get up, LORD, in your anger! Rise up against the fury of my enemies. Wake up and help me! You have commanded justice.
Let the people of the nations gather around you. Rule over them from on high.
The LORD judges the nations. Judge me, LORD, by how right I am and by my honesty.
Bring the evil of wicked people to an end, and make good people secure. You are the God who does right, and you test people's minds and hearts.
God is my shield. He saves those whose hearts are honest.
God is a fair judge. He is angry with evil every day.
If a person does not turn back from sin, God will sharpen his sword. He has bent and strung his bow.
He has prepared his deadly weapons. He has made his flaming arrows ready.
Look, the wicked person is pregnant with evil. He plans trouble and gives birth to lies.
He digs a hole, and then falls into the pit he made.
The trouble he causes comes back on him. His violence falls back on his own head.
I will thank the LORD because he does what is right. I will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
For the music director. On an instrument from Gath. A psalm of David. LORD, our Lord, how wonderful your name is in all the earth! You have put your glory above the skies.
From the mouths of children and babies you have built up strength because of your enemies, to silence the enemy and the one who wants revenge.
When I look at your skies, which your fingers made, the moon and the stars you put in place,
what are human beings that you think about them? What is a mere person that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels, and you crowned him with glory and honour.
You made him ruler over everything you made. You put everything under his feet:
all the sheep and cattle, and the wild animals too,
the birds in the sky, the fish in the sea, and everything that swims along the paths of the seas.
LORD, our Lord, how wonderful your name is in all the earth!
For the music director. To the tune "The Death of the Son." A psalm of David. I will thank the LORD with all my heart. I will tell about all the amazing things you have done.
I will be glad and celebrate because of you. I will sing praise to your name, Most High God.
When my enemies turn back, they trip and are destroyed in front of you.
You have defended my rights and my cause. You sit on your throne as a fair judge.
You have warned the nations and destroyed the wicked. You have wiped out their names forever and ever.
The enemy has been completely ruined forever. You tore down their cities, and even the memory of them is gone.
But the LORD rules forever. He has set up his throne to judge.
He will judge the world fairly. He will judge the peoples with honesty.
The LORD is a safe tower for those who are crushed, a safe tower in times of trouble.
Those who know your name will trust in you, because you, LORD, have never left those who look for you.
Sing praises to the LORD, who lives in Zion. Tell the nations what he has done.
The one who punishes murderers remembers those who suffer. He does not forget their cries.
Be kind to me, LORD. See how those who hate me make me suffer. Lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I can tell of all your praise. I will celebrate your rescue at the gates of the city of Zion.
The nations have fallen into the pit they dug. Their own feet are caught in the net they hid.
The LORD is known by the justice he does. The wicked are trapped by what their own hands have done. Meditation. Selah.
The wicked will go down to the grave, along with all the nations that forget God.
But people in need will not always be forgotten. The hope of the poor will never die.
Get up, LORD! Do not let mere humans win. Let the nations be judged in front of you.
Make them afraid, LORD. Let the nations know they are only human. Selah.
LORD, why do you stand so far away? Why do you hide when there is trouble?
Proud, wicked people hunt down the weak. Let them be caught in the evil plans they make.
The wicked person boasts about what his heart wants. He praises greedy people and insults the LORD.
The wicked person is so proud that he does not look for God. There is no room for God in his thoughts.
Everything he does always seems to succeed. He is proud, and your laws are far from his mind. He sneers at all his enemies.
He says to himself, "Nothing will shake me. I will never have trouble, for all generations."
His mouth is full of curses, lies, and threats. Trouble and evil are on the tip of his tongue.
He hides and waits near the villages. From his hiding places he murders innocent people. His eyes secretly watch for helpless victims.
He waits in secret like a lion in its den. He waits to catch the helpless. He catches them and drags them off in his net.
The helpless are crushed and fall down. They fall under his strength.
He says to himself, "God has forgotten. He has covered his face. He will never see."
Get up, LORD! God, raise your hand to act! Do not forget the helpless.
Why does the wicked person insult God? Why does he say to himself, "God will not make me answer for it"?
But you do see trouble and sorrow. You notice it and take it into your hands. The victim leaves himself in your care. You help children who have no father.
Break the arm of the wicked and evil person. Search out all his evil until you find no more.
The LORD is King forever and ever! The nations will disappear from his land.
LORD, you have heard what humble people want. You will encourage them, and you will listen to them,
to give justice to children with no father and to those who are crushed, so that mere humans from the earth can no longer terrify anyone.
For the music director. Of David. I go to the LORD for safety. So how can you say to me, "Fly away like a bird to your mountain"?
Look, the wicked are bending their bows. They put their arrows on the strings to shoot from the dark at people whose hearts are honest.
When the foundations are being destroyed, what can good people do?
The LORD is in his holy temple. The LORD's throne is in heaven. His eyes watch. He looks closely at all people.
The LORD tests good people, but he hates the wicked and those who love violence.
He will rain burning coals on the wicked. Fire, burning sulfur, and a scorching wind will be what they get.
The LORD always does what is right, and he loves what is right. Honest people will see his face.
For the music director. On the eight-stringed lyre. A psalm of David. Help, LORD, because there are no faithful people left. Loyal people have disappeared from among humans.
Everyone lies to their neighbour. They flatter with their lips, but they say one thing and mean another.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and every tongue that boasts.
They say, "We will win with our tongues. Our lips belong to us. Who can be our master?"
The LORD says, "Because the weak are being crushed and the needy are groaning, I will now get up and act. I will keep them safe from those who attack them."
The LORD's words are pure, like silver that has been melted in a clay furnace and refined seven times.
LORD, you will keep them safe. You will protect them from these people forever.
Wicked people strut around everywhere when what is shameful is praised by people.
For the music director. A psalm of David. How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I struggle with my thoughts, with sorrow in my heart every day? How long will my enemy win against me?
Look at me and answer me, LORD my God. Give light to my eyes, or I will sleep in death.
Then my enemy will say, "I have beaten him," and my enemies will celebrate when I fall.
But I trust in your faithful love. My heart is glad because you rescue me.
I will sing to the LORD, because he has been good to me.
For the music director. Of David. Foolish people say to themselves, "There is no God." They are rotten. They do disgusting things. No one does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven on all people to see if anyone understands, if anyone looks for God.
They have all turned away. All of them have become rotten. No one does good, not even one.
Do these evil people know nothing? They eat up my people as if they were eating bread, and they never call on the LORD.
There they are, filled with terror, because God is with those who do right.
You evil people ruin the plans of the poor, but the LORD keeps them safe.
I wish rescue for Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD makes his people successful again, Jacob will celebrate and Israel will be glad.
A psalm of David. LORD, who can stay in your sacred tent? Who can live on your holy hill?
The person who lives a blameless life, does what is right, and speaks the truth from the heart.
That person does not spread lies about others, does not harm a friend, and does not insult a neighbour.
That person looks down on those who are evil, but honours those who respect the LORD. That person keeps a promise even when it hurts, and does not change it.
That person lends money without charging interest, and does not take a bribe to hurt innocent people. Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
A poem of David. Keep me safe, God, because I come to you for safety.
I said to the LORD, "You are my Lord. Without you I have nothing good."
God's holy people in the land are wonderful. They are the ones I take delight in.
Those who run after other gods will have more and more sorrow. I will not pour out their offerings of blood, or even speak the names of their gods.
LORD, you have given me my share and my cup of blessing. You keep what is mine safe.
The land you have given me is in a pleasant place. Yes, I have a wonderful inheritance.
I will praise the LORD, who guides me. Even at night my heart teaches me.
I always keep the LORD in front of me. Because he is at my right side, nothing will shake me.
So my heart is glad, and my tongue celebrates. My body also will rest safely.
You will not leave me in the grave. You will not let your holy one rot away.
You will show me the path of life. Being with you fills me with joy. At your right hand there are pleasures that last forever.
A prayer of David. LORD, hear my fair request. Listen to my prayer, which comes from lips that do not lie.
Let my judgment come from you. Let your eyes see what is fair.
You have tested my heart. You have checked on me in the night. You have examined me and found nothing wrong. I have decided that my mouth will not sin.
As for what other people do, I have followed what you said and kept away from the ways of violent people.
My steps have stayed on your paths. My feet have not slipped.
I call to you, God, because you will answer me. Turn your ear to me and hear what I say.
Show me your amazing, faithful love. With your right hand you save those who come to you for safety from their enemies.
Protect me as you would protect your own eyes. Hide me in the shadow of your wings
from the wicked people who attack me, from my deadly enemies who surround me.
Their hearts are hard and unfeeling. Their mouths speak proud words.
They have tracked us down and surrounded us. Their eyes watch for a chance to throw us to the ground.
They are like a lion hungry for its prey, like a young lion hiding in wait.
Get up, LORD! Face them and bring them down! Use your sword to rescue me from the wicked.

LORD, use your hand to rescue me from such people, people of this world whose reward is in this life only. You fill the stomachs of those you treasure. Their children have plenty, and they store up wealth for their own children.
But because I have done what is right, I will see your face. When I wake up, I will be satisfied to see you.

For the music director. Of David, the servant of the LORD. He sang the words of this song to the LORD when the LORD rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul. He said: I love you, LORD. You are my strength.
The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and the one who rescues me. My God is my rock, where I go for safety. He is my shield, my strong saviour, and my high tower.
I call to the LORD, who deserves praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
The ropes of death were wrapped around me. Floods of evil terrified me.
The ropes of the grave were around me. Traps of death were in front of me.
In my trouble I called to the LORD. I cried to my God for help. From his temple he heard my voice. My cry reached his ears.
Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations of the mountains shook and moved, because he was angry.
Smoke came out of his nose. Burning fire came out of his mouth. Glowing coals blazed from it.
He pulled the skies apart and came down. Dark clouds were under his feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew. He soared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness his hiding place. Dark rain clouds and thick clouds in the sky were his tent around him.
Out of the brightness around him came his thick clouds, with hailstones and flashes of fire.
The LORD thundered from the sky. The voice of the Most High rang out, with hailstones and flashes of fire.
He shot his arrows and scattered his enemies. He sent great bolts of lightning and threw them into confusion.
Then the bottom of the sea could be seen. The foundations of the earth were uncovered when you warned them, LORD, with a blast of breath from your nose.
He reached down from on high and took hold of me. He pulled me out of deep waters.
He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, because they were too strong for me.
They attacked me on the day I was in trouble, but the LORD held me up.
He brought me out into a wide-open place. He rescued me because he was pleased with me.
The LORD has rewarded me because I did what is right. He has paid me back because my hands are clean.
I have kept the ways of the LORD. I have not done evil by turning away from my God.
All his laws are in front of me. I have not turned away from his rules.
I was blameless in front of him. I have kept myself from sin.
So the LORD has rewarded me because I did what is right, because my hands are clean in his eyes.
To those who are faithful, you show that you are faithful. To those who are blameless, you show that you are blameless.
To those who are pure, you show that you are pure. But to those who are crooked, you show that you are clever.
You save people who are humble, but you bring down those whose eyes are proud.
LORD, you keep my lamp burning. My God turns my darkness into light.
With your help I can attack a troop of soldiers. With my God I can jump over a wall.
God's way is perfect. The LORD's word has been tested. He is a shield to everyone who comes to him for safety.
Who is God except the LORD? Who is the rock except our God?
It is God who gives me strength and makes my way perfect.
He makes my feet as sure as the feet of a deer. He helps me stand on high places.
He trains my hands for battle, so my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You have given me your shield of rescue. Your right hand holds me up. Your gentle care has made me great.
You give me a wide path to walk on, so my feet do not slip.
I chased my enemies and caught them. I did not turn back until they were destroyed.
I struck them down so they could not get up. They fell under my feet.
You gave me strength for battle. You made those who attacked me bow down at my feet.
You made my enemies turn and run, and I destroyed those who hated me.
They cried for help, but there was no one to save them. They cried to the LORD, but he did not answer.
I crushed them as fine as dust blown by the wind. I threw them out like mud in the streets.
You rescued me from people who fought against me. You made me ruler over nations. People I did not know serve me.
As soon as they hear about me, they obey me. Foreigners bow down to me.
Foreigners lose heart and come trembling out of their strong places.
The LORD lives! Praise be to my rock! May God my saviour be honoured!
He is the God who pays back my enemies for me and brings nations under my control.
He rescues me from my enemies. You lift me high above those who attack me. You rescue me from violent people.
So I will thank you, LORD, among the nations. I will sing praises to your name.
He gives his king great victories. He shows faithful love to his anointed king, to David and his descendants forever.
For the music director. A psalm of David. The skies tell about the glory of God. The sky shows what his hands have made.
Day after day they speak. Night after night they share knowledge.
There is no language or speech anywhere where their voice is not heard.
Yet their message goes out to all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. God has set up a tent in the sky for the sun.
The sun comes out like a bridegroom leaving his room, like a strong runner who is happy to run his race.
It rises at one end of the sky and travels across to the other end. Nothing can hide from its heat.
The LORD's law is perfect. It refreshes the soul. The LORD's covenant can be trusted. It makes simple people wise.
The LORD's rules are right. They make the heart glad. The LORD's commands are pure. They give light to the eyes.
Respect for the LORD is pure. It lasts forever. The LORD's decisions are true, and all of them are fair.
They are worth more than gold, more than a lot of pure gold. They are sweeter than honey, sweeter than honey straight from the honeycomb.
They warn me, your servant. There is a great reward for those who obey them.
Who can see their own mistakes? Forgive me for the faults I cannot see.
Keep me, your servant, from sins I know are wrong. Do not let them control me. Then I will be blameless and innocent of great sin.
LORD, my rock and my saviour, may the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart please you.
For the music director. A psalm of David. May the LORD answer you when you are in trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob protect you.
May he send you help from his holy place and support you from Zion.
May he remember all your offerings and accept your burnt sacrifices. Selah.
May he give you what your heart wants and make all your plans succeed.
We will shout for joy when you win. We will raise our flags in the name of our God. May the LORD give you everything you ask for.
Now I know that the LORD saves his anointed king. He answers him from his holy heaven with the saving power of his right hand.
Some people trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
They are brought to their knees and fall, but we rise up and stand firm.
LORD, save the king! Answer us when we call!
For the music director. A psalm of David. LORD, the king is glad because of your strength. How great is his joy because you gave him victory!
You have given him what his heart wanted. You have not refused what he asked for. Selah.
You came to meet him with rich blessings. You put a crown of pure gold on his head.
He asked you for life, and you gave it to him, a long life that goes on forever and ever.
Because you gave him victory, his glory is great. You have given him honour and majesty.
You have given him blessings that last forever. You have filled him with the joy of being with you.
The king trusts in the LORD. Because of the faithful love of the Most High, nothing will shake him.
Your hand will find all your enemies. Your right hand will find those who hate you.
When you appear, you will burn them up like a fiery furnace. The LORD will swallow them up in his anger. Fire will burn them up.
You will wipe their children off the earth, their descendants from among all people.
They planned evil against you and made evil plans, but they cannot succeed.
You will make them turn and run when you aim your arrows at their faces.
LORD, be honoured in your strength. We will sing and praise your power.
For the music director. To the tune "The Deer of the Morning." A psalm of David. My God, my God, why have you left me all alone? Why are you so far from saving me, so far from my cries of pain?
My God, I cry out by day, but you do not answer. I cry out by night, and I cannot be quiet.
But you are holy. You sit on your throne, and Israel praises you.
Our ancestors trusted in you. They trusted you, and you rescued them.
They cried out to you and were saved. They trusted in you and were not disappointed.
But I am a worm, not a man. People insult me and look down on me.
Everyone who sees me makes fun of me. They insult me and shake their heads, saying,
"He trusts in the LORD. Let the LORD rescue him. Let the LORD save him, since he is so pleased with him."
But you brought me safely out of my mother's womb. You made me trust you even when I was a baby at my mother's breast.
I have depended on you since I was born. You have been my God since I came out of my mother's womb.
Do not stay far from me, because trouble is near and there is no one to help.
Many bulls surround me. Strong bulls from Bashan are all around me.
They open their mouths wide against me, like roaring lions tearing their prey.
I am poured out like water. All my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax. It has melted inside me.
My strength is dried up like a broken piece of pottery. My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You have laid me down in the dust of death.
Dogs surround me. A gang of evil people closes in on me. They have pierced my hands and my feet.
I can count all my bones. People stare at me and look down on me.
They divide my clothes among them. They throw dice for what I am wearing.
But you, LORD, do not stay far away. You are my strength. Come quickly to help me!
Rescue me from the sword. Save my precious life from the power of the dogs.
Save me from the mouth of the lion! You have rescued me from the horns of the wild oxen.
I will tell my brothers and sisters about your name. I will praise you among the gathered people.
You who respect the LORD, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, honour him! All you descendants of Israel, stand in awe of him!
He has not looked down on or turned away from the suffering of the one who suffers. He has not hidden his face from him. He listened when he cried to him for help.
You are the reason I praise you among the great crowd of people. I will keep my promises in front of those who respect him.
Poor people will eat and be full. Those who look for the LORD will praise him. May your hearts live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD. All the families of the nations will bow down in front of you.
The kingdom belongs to the LORD. He rules over the nations.
All the rich people of the earth will eat and worship. Everyone who goes down to the dust will bow down to him, those who cannot keep themselves alive.
Future generations will serve him. People will tell their children about the Lord.
They will come and tell people not yet born that he does what is right, because he has done it.
The LORD is my shepherd, so I will not be in need.
He lets me lie down and rest in green fields. He leads me beside calm, quiet waters.
He refreshes my soul. He leads me on the paths of what is right, so that his name is honoured.
Even if I walk through a valley as dark as death, I will not fear any harm, because you are with me. Your shepherd's rod and staff give me comfort.
You set a table for me while my enemies look on. You pour oil on my head as a sign of welcome. My cup is full to overflowing.
I am sure that your goodness and your faithful love will stay with me every day of my life. And I will live in the house of the LORD for ever.
A psalm of David. The earth belongs to the LORD, and everything in it. The world and all who live in it belong to him.
He built it on the seas and set it firmly on the waters.
Who may go up the LORD's hill? Who may stand in his holy place?
Those whose hands are clean and whose hearts are pure, who do not worship what is false and do not make promises they mean to break.
They will receive a blessing from the LORD. God their saviour will declare them right.
These are the people who look for him, who look for your face, God of Jacob. Selah.
Lift up your heads, you gates! Open up, you ancient doors, so the King of glory can come in.
Who is the King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, you gates! Open up, you ancient doors, so the King of glory can come in.
Who is this King of glory? The LORD of Armies is the King of glory! Selah.
Of David. LORD, I give my life to you.
My God, I trust in you. Do not let me be put to shame. Do not let my enemies win over me.
No one who waits for you will ever be put to shame. But those who betray others for no reason will be put to shame.
Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths.
Guide me in your truth and teach me, because you are God my saviour. I wait for you all day long.
LORD, remember your tender mercy and your faithful love. You have shown them from long ago.
Do not remember the sins I did when I was young, or the wrong things I did. Remember me because of your faithful love, because you are good, LORD.
The LORD is good and does what is right. So he teaches sinners the way they should go.
He guides humble people in what is right and teaches them his way.
All the LORD's ways are loving and faithful toward those who keep his covenant and his laws.
LORD, for the honour of your name, forgive my sin, because it is great.
Who are the people who respect the LORD? He will teach them the way they should choose.
They will live good lives, and their children will receive the land.
The LORD is a close friend to those who respect him. He makes his covenant known to them.
My eyes are always on the LORD, because he will free my feet from the net.
Turn to me and be kind to me, because I am lonely and suffering.
The troubles of my heart keep growing. Rescue me from my distress.
Look at my suffering and my pain, and forgive all my sins.
See how many enemies I have. They hate me with a cruel hatred.
Protect my life and rescue me. Do not let me be put to shame, because I come to you for safety.
May my innocence and honesty protect me, because I wait for you.
God, rescue Israel from all their troubles.
Of David. LORD, judge me, because I have lived an innocent life. I have trusted in the LORD without doubting.
Examine me, LORD, and test me. Look closely at my heart and mind.
I always keep your faithful love in front of my eyes. I live by your truth.
I do not sit with liars, and I do not spend time with people who pretend to be good.
I hate the meetings of evil people, and I will not sit with the wicked.
I wash my hands to show I am innocent, and I go around your altar, LORD,
singing songs of thanks out loud and telling about all the amazing things you have done.
LORD, I love the house where you live, the place where your glory stays.
Do not sweep me away with sinners. Do not take my life along with murderers,
whose hands are full of evil plans and bribes.
But I live an innocent life. Rescue me and be kind to me.
My feet stand on level ground. In the great gatherings I will praise the LORD.
Of David. The LORD is my light and the one who saves me. Who should I be afraid of? The LORD is the strong place where my life is safe. Who should I fear?
When evil people attacked me to eat me up, those enemies and attackers tripped and fell.
Even if an army surrounds me, my heart will not be afraid. Even if war breaks out against me, I will still be confident.
I have asked one thing from the LORD, and this is what I want: to live in the LORD's house all the days of my life, to look at the LORD's beauty and to seek him in his temple.
When trouble comes, he will keep me safe in his shelter. He will hide me in his holy tent. He will set me high on a rock.
Then my head will be held high above my enemies who surround me. I will offer sacrifices in his tent with shouts of joy. I will sing and make music to the LORD.
LORD, hear me when I call out loud. Be kind to me and answer me.
When you said, "Look for my face," my heart said to you, "LORD, I will look for your face."
Do not hide your face from me. Do not turn me, your servant, away in anger. You have been my helper. Do not reject me or leave me, God my saviour.
Even if my father and mother leave me, the LORD will take care of me.
LORD, teach me your way. Lead me on a straight path because of my enemies.
Do not hand me over to what my enemies want, because liars rise up against me and breathe out violence.
I am still sure of this: I will see the LORD's goodness while I am still alive.
Wait for the LORD. Be strong and brave. Yes, wait for the LORD.
Of David. LORD, I call to you. My rock, do not refuse to hear me. If you stay silent, I will be like those who go down to the grave.
Hear my voice when I beg for mercy, when I cry to you for help, when I lift up my hands toward your Most Holy Place.
Do not drag me away with the wicked, with those who do evil. They speak friendly words to their neighbours, but they have evil in their hearts.
Pay them back for what they have done, for their evil actions. Pay them back for what their hands have done. Give them what they deserve.
They do not care about what the LORD has done or what his hands have made. So he will tear them down and never build them up again.
Praise the LORD, because he has heard my voice when I begged for mercy.
The LORD is my strength and my shield. My heart trusts in him, and he helps me. My heart jumps for joy, and I will thank him with my song.
The LORD is the strength of his people. He is a fortress that saves his anointed king.
Save your people and bless those who belong to you. Be their shepherd and carry them forever.
A psalm of David. Give honour to the LORD, you heavenly beings. Give honour to the LORD for his glory and strength.
Give the LORD the glory his name deserves. Worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.
The LORD's voice is over the waters. The God of glory thunders. The LORD thunders over the mighty waters.
The LORD's voice is powerful. The LORD's voice is full of majesty.
The LORD's voice breaks the cedar trees. The LORD smashes the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes the mountains of Lebanon jump like a calf, and Mount Sirion like a young wild ox.
The LORD's voice strikes with flashes of lightning.
The LORD's voice shakes the wilderness. The LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
The LORD's voice makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare. In his temple everyone shouts, "Glory!"
The LORD sat on his throne above the flood. The LORD sits on his throne as King forever.
The LORD gives strength to his people. The LORD blesses his people with peace.
A psalm. A song for the dedication of the temple. Of David. I will praise you highly, LORD, because you lifted me up. You did not let my enemies celebrate over me.
LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you healed me.
LORD, you brought me up from the grave. You kept me alive so I did not go down into the pit.
Sing praise to the LORD, all you his faithful people. Thank him and remember his holy name.
His anger lasts only a moment, but his kindness lasts a lifetime. Crying may last through the night, but joy comes in the morning.
When things were going well for me, I said, "Nothing will ever shake me."
LORD, when you were kind to me, you made me as strong as a mountain. But when you hid your face, I was terrified.
I cried to you, LORD. I begged the Lord for mercy:
"What good will it do if I die, if I go down into the pit? Can dust praise you? Can it tell how faithful you are?
Hear me, LORD, and be kind to me. LORD, be my helper."
You turned my crying into dancing. You took off my clothes of sadness and dressed me with joy,
so that my heart may sing praises to you and not be silent. LORD my God, I will thank you forever!
For the music director. A psalm of David. LORD, I come to you for safety. Never let me be put to shame. Rescue me because you do what is right.
Turn your ear to me. Come quickly to rescue me. Be my strong rock, a fortress to save me.
You are my rock and my fortress. For the honour of your name, lead me and guide me.
Free me from the trap that is hidden for me, because you are my safe place.
I put my spirit into your hands. Rescue me, LORD, faithful God.
I hate those who worship worthless idols. But I trust in the LORD.
I will be glad and celebrate because of your faithful love. You saw my suffering. You cared about my deep troubles.
You have not handed me over to my enemy. You have set my feet in a wide-open place.
Be kind to me, LORD, because I am in trouble. My eyes, my soul, and my body are worn out with sorrow.
My life is used up by sadness and my years by groaning. My strength is failing because of my sin. My bones are wasting away.
Because of all my enemies, my neighbours look down on me completely. My friends are horrified by me. People who see me in the street run away from me.
People have forgotten me as if I were dead. I have become like a broken pot.
I hear many people whispering lies about me. There is terror all around me. They plot together against me and plan to take my life.
But I trust in you, LORD. I say, "You are my God."
My life is in your hands. Rescue me from my enemies and from those who chase me.
Let your face shine on me, your servant. Save me because of your faithful love.
LORD, do not let me be put to shame, because I have called to you. Let the wicked be put to shame. Let them lie silent in the grave.
Shut the lips of liars, who speak proudly and with hatred against good people.
How great is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who respect you! You give it to those who come to you for safety, in front of everyone.
You hide them in the safety of your presence from people who plot against them. You keep them safe in your shelter from accusing tongues.
Praise the LORD, because he showed me his amazing, faithful love when I was in a city under attack.
In my panic I said, "I have been cut off from your sight!" But you heard my cry for mercy when I called to you for help.
Love the LORD, all you his faithful people! The LORD protects those who are faithful to him, but he pays back the proud in full.
Be strong and brave, all you who put your hope in the LORD.
Of David. A thoughtful psalm. Happy is the person whose wrongdoing is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
Happy is the person whom the LORD does not count as guilty, whose spirit has no lies in it.
When I kept quiet about my sin, my body wasted away because I groaned all day long.
Day and night your hand pressed down on me. My strength dried up as in the heat of summer. Selah.
Then I admitted my sin to you. I did not hide my wrongdoing. I said, "I will confess my sins to the LORD," and you forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah.
So let all your faithful people pray to you while they can still find you. Then when the great floodwaters rise, they will not reach them.
You are my hiding place. You protect me from trouble. You surround me with songs of rescue. Selah.
I will teach you and show you the way you should go. I will guide you and keep my eye on you.
Do not be like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding. They must be controlled with bits and bridles, or they will not come to you.
Wicked people have many sorrows, but the LORD's faithful love surrounds those who trust in him.
Be glad in the LORD and celebrate, you who do what is right! Shout for joy, all you whose hearts are honest!
Shout for joy to the LORD, you who do what is right! It is right for honest people to praise him.
Thank the LORD with the lyre. Make music to him on the ten-stringed harp.
Sing a new song to him. Play skilfully and shout for joy!
The LORD's word is right and true. He is faithful in everything he does.
He loves what is right and fair. The earth is full of the LORD's faithful love.
The skies were made when the LORD spoke. All the stars were made by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea into a heap. He puts the deep waters into storerooms.
Let the whole earth respect the LORD. Let everyone in the world stand in awe of him.
He spoke, and the world came into being. He gave the command, and it stood firm.
The LORD ruins the plans of the nations. He stops what the peoples intend to do.
But the LORD's plans stand firm forever. What he intends lasts for all generations.
Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people he chose as his very own.
The LORD looks down from heaven and sees everyone.
From where he sits on his throne, he watches everyone who lives on earth.
He shapes all their hearts, and he understands everything they do.
No king is saved by the size of his army. No warrior escapes by his great strength.
A horse is no sure way to be saved. Its great strength cannot rescue anyone.
But the LORD watches over those who respect him, those who hope in his faithful love.
He rescues them from death and keeps them alive in times of famine.
We wait for the LORD. He is our help and our shield.
Our hearts are glad in him, because we trust in his holy name.
LORD, may your faithful love be with us, because we put our hope in you.
Of David, when he pretended to be insane in front of Abimelech, who drove him away, and he left. I will praise the LORD at all times. My mouth will always praise him.
I will boast about the LORD. Let humble people hear it and be glad.
Join me in telling of the LORD's greatness. Let's honour his name together.
I looked for the LORD, and he answered me. He rescued me from everything I was afraid of.
Those who look to him shine with joy. Their faces are never covered with shame.
This poor man called out, and the LORD heard him. He saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the LORD camps around those who respect him, and he rescues them.
Taste and see that the LORD is good. Happy is the person who goes to him for safety.
Respect the LORD, you his holy people, because those who respect him have everything they need.
Even young lions may be weak and hungry, but those who look to the LORD will not be without any good thing.
Come, children, listen to me. I will teach you to respect the LORD.
Do you want to enjoy life and live long enough to see good days?
Then keep your tongue from evil and your lips from telling lies.
Turn away from evil and do good. Look for peace and chase after it.
The LORD's eyes watch over those who do right. His ears listen to their cries.
But the LORD's face is against those who do evil. He will wipe out any memory of them from the earth.
Good people cry out, and the LORD hears them. He rescues them from all their troubles.
The LORD is close to those whose hearts are broken. He saves those whose spirits are crushed.
Good people may have many troubles, but the LORD rescues them from all of them.
He protects all their bones. Not one of them will be broken.
Evil will kill the wicked. Those who hate good people will be found guilty.
The LORD rescues his servants. No one who goes to him for safety will be found guilty.
Of David. LORD, argue against those who argue against me. Fight against those who fight against me.
Pick up your shields, large and small, and come to help me.
Raise your spear and block the way of those who are chasing me. Say to me, "I am the one who saves you."
Let those who are trying to kill me be put to shame and disgraced. Let those who plan to ruin me be turned back in confusion.
Let them be like chaff blown by the wind, with the angel of the LORD driving them away.
Let their path be dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD chasing them.
For no reason they hid their net for me in a pit. For no reason they dug a pit to trap me.
Let ruin come on them by surprise. Let the net they hid catch them. Let them fall into the ruin they planned.
Then I will be full of joy in the LORD. I will celebrate because he rescued me.
With my whole body I will say, "LORD, who is like you? You rescue the poor from those who are too strong for them. You rescue the poor and needy from those who rob them."
Lying witnesses rise up. They ask me about things I know nothing about.
They pay me back evil for good. I am left all alone.
But when they were sick, I wore rough clothes of sadness. I went without food to humble myself. My prayers went unanswered.
I acted as if they were my friends or brothers. I bowed my head in sadness, like someone crying for his mother.
But when I was in trouble, they gathered together and celebrated. Attackers I did not even know gathered against me. They kept tearing at me without stopping.
Like godless people mocking at a feast, they ground their teeth at me.
Lord, how long will you just watch? Rescue me from their attacks. Rescue my precious life from these lions.
Then I will thank you in front of the great crowd. I will praise you among many people.
Do not let my lying enemies celebrate over me. Do not let those who hate me for no reason wink at each other.
They do not talk about peace. Instead, they make up lies against the quiet people of the land.
They open their mouths wide against me and say, "Aha! Aha! We saw it with our own eyes!"
LORD, you have seen it. Do not stay silent. Lord, do not be far away from me.
Wake up! Get up and defend me, my God! My Lord, fight for my cause!
LORD my God, declare me innocent because you are fair. Do not let them celebrate over me.
Do not let them say to themselves, "Aha! This is just what we wanted!" Do not let them say, "We have swallowed him up!"
Let everyone who is happy about my trouble be put to shame and confused. Let those who make themselves great at my expense be covered with shame and disgrace.
Let those who want me to be proved right shout for joy and be glad. Let them always say, "The LORD is great! He is pleased when his servant does well!"
My tongue will talk about how you do what is right, and I will praise you all day long.
For the music director. Of David, the servant of the LORD. I have a message in my heart about the sin of the wicked: they have no fear of God at all.
They think so highly of themselves that they cannot see their own sin and hate it.
The words they speak are evil and full of lies. They have stopped being wise and doing good.
Even in bed they plan evil. They choose a path that is not good. They do not turn away from evil.
LORD, your faithful love reaches to the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
Your goodness is like the mighty mountains. Your fair judgments are like the deep ocean. LORD, you take care of people and animals.
God, how precious your faithful love is! People find safety in the shadow of your wings.
They eat their fill of the rich food in your house. You let them drink from your river of delights.
You are the spring of life. Your light lets us see light.
Keep showing your faithful love to those who know you, and your goodness to those whose hearts are honest.
Do not let proud people trample on me. Do not let the hands of the wicked drive me away.
Look how the evil people have fallen! They are thrown down and cannot get up.
Of David. Do not get upset because of evil people. Do not be jealous of those who do wrong.
They will soon dry up like grass. They will wither like green plants.
Trust in the LORD and do good. Live in the land and enjoy safe pasture.
Find your joy in the LORD, and he will give you what your heart wants.
Give everything you do to the LORD. Trust in him, and he will do this:
He will make your goodness shine like the dawn, and the justice of your cause like the noonday sun.
Be still in front of the LORD and wait patiently for him. Do not get upset when others succeed, or when people carry out their evil plans.
Stop being angry and turn away from rage. Do not get upset. It only leads to evil.
Evil people will be destroyed, but those who wait for the LORD will receive the land.
In a little while the wicked will be gone. You will look for them, but they will not be there.
But humble people will receive the land and enjoy great peace.
Wicked people plot against good people and grind their teeth at them.
But the Lord laughs at the wicked, because he knows their day is coming.
The wicked pull out their swords and bend their bows to bring down the poor and needy, to kill those who live honestly.
