But their swords will stab their own hearts, and their bows will be broken.
The little that good people have is better than the riches of many wicked people.
The power of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD holds up good people.
The LORD watches over the lives of blameless people. What they receive will last forever.
They will not be put to shame in bad times. Even in times of famine they will have plenty.
But wicked people will die. The LORD's enemies will be like flowers in the fields. They will disappear like smoke.
Wicked people borrow and do not pay back, but good people give generously.
Those the LORD blesses will receive the land, but those he curses will be destroyed.
The LORD makes a person's steps firm when he is pleased with the way that person lives.
Even if they trip, they will not fall down, because the LORD holds their hand.
I was young and now I am old, yet I have never seen good people abandoned, or their children begging for bread.
They are always generous and lend freely. Their children are a blessing.
Turn away from evil and do good. Then you will live safely forever.
The LORD loves justice, and he will not leave his faithful people. They will be protected forever, but the children of the wicked will be destroyed.
Good people will receive the land and live in it forever.
Good people speak words of wisdom. Their tongues speak what is fair.
The law of their God is in their hearts. Their feet do not slip.
Wicked people watch for good people, looking for a chance to kill them.
But the LORD will not leave good people in their power or let them be found guilty when they are put on trial.
Wait for the LORD and follow his way. He will honour you by giving you the land. You will see the wicked destroyed.
I have seen a wicked and powerful person spreading out like a green tree in its own soil.
But he soon passed away and was gone. I looked for him, but he could not be found.
Look at blameless people and watch honest people. There is a future for those who make peace.
But all sinners will be destroyed. The future of the wicked will be cut off.
The LORD saves good people. He is their fortress in times of trouble.
The LORD helps them and rescues them. He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they go to him for safety.
A psalm of David, to help remember. LORD, do not correct me when you are angry. Do not punish me in your burning anger.
Your arrows have pierced me. Your hand presses down hard on me.
My whole body is sick because of your anger. My bones have no health because of my sin.
My sins are like a flood over my head. They are like a load too heavy for me to carry.
My wounds stink and fill with pus because of my foolishness.
I am bent over and bowed down low. I go around crying all day long.
My back burns with pain. My whole body is sick.
I am weak and completely crushed. I groan because of the pain in my heart.
Lord, you know everything I long for. My groaning is not hidden from you.
My heart pounds. My strength is gone. Even the light has left my eyes.
My friends and companions stay away because of my sickness. My family stands far away.
Those who want to kill me set traps for me. Those who want to hurt me talk about ruining me. They plan lies all day long.
But I am like a deaf man who cannot hear, like a man who cannot speak and does not open his mouth.
I am like someone who does not hear, who has no answer to give.
LORD, I wait for you. You will answer, Lord my God.
I said, "Do not let them celebrate over me, or boast against me when my foot slips."
I am about to fall. My pain is always with me.
I admit my sin. I am troubled by what I have done wrong.
My enemies are strong and many. So many people hate me for no reason.
They pay me back evil for good. They attack me because I try to do what is good.
LORD, do not leave me. My God, do not be far from me.
Hurry to help me, Lord my saviour.

For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David. I said, "I will be careful about how I live, so I do not sin with my tongue. I will keep my mouth shut, as if with a muzzle, while wicked people are around me."
So I was silent and said nothing, not even anything good. But my pain grew worse.
My heart grew hot inside me. As I thought about it, the fire burned. Then I spoke out:
"LORD, show me when my life will end and how many days I have. Let me know how short my life is.
You have made my days only a few hands wide. My whole lifetime is like nothing to you. Every person is only a breath." Selah.
"Each person walks around like a shadow. They rush around for nothing. They pile up wealth, not knowing who will get it.
So, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
Rescue me from all my sins. Do not let foolish people make fun of me.
I was silent. I did not open my mouth, because you are the one who did this.
Stop hitting me. I am worn out by the blows from your hand.
When you correct people for their sins, you eat away their wealth like a moth. Every person is only a breath." Selah.
"LORD, hear my prayer. Listen to my cry for help. Do not ignore my tears. I am a visitor with you, a foreigner, just as all my ancestors were.
Look away from me so I can be happy again before I leave and am gone."
For the music director. A psalm of David. I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned to me and heard my cry.
He lifted me out of a terrible pit, out of the mud and clay. He set my feet on a rock and gave me a firm place to stand.
He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see it and be amazed, and they will trust in the LORD.
Happy is the person who trusts in the LORD, who does not look to proud people or to those who turn to lies.
LORD my God, you have done many wonderful things, and you have many plans for us. No one can compare with you. If I tried to tell about them all, there would be too many to count.
You did not want sacrifices and offerings. You have opened my ears to listen. You did not ask for burnt offerings and sin offerings.
Then I said, "Here I am. I have come. It is written about me in the scroll of the book.
I am happy to do what you want, my God. Your law is in my heart."
I have told the good news of your goodness to the great crowd. LORD, you know I have not closed my lips.
I have not hidden your goodness in my heart. I have talked about your faithfulness and how you save. I have not kept your faithful love and truth secret from the great crowd.
LORD, do not hold back your tender mercy from me. May your faithful love and truth always protect me.
So many troubles surround me that I cannot count them. My sins have caught up with me, so that I cannot see. They are more than the hairs on my head. I have lost all courage.
Please, LORD, rescue me. Hurry, LORD, and help me.
Let all those who are trying to kill me be put to shame and confused. Let those who want to hurt me be turned back in disgrace.
Let those who say to me, "Aha! Aha!" be shocked by their own shame.
But let all who look for you be full of joy and gladness because of you. Let those who love your saving help always say, "The LORD is great!"
But I am poor and needy. May the Lord think about me. You are my helper and my rescuer. My God, do not wait.
For the music director. A psalm of David. Happy is the person who cares about the poor. The LORD will rescue him in times of trouble.
The LORD will protect him and keep him alive. He will be blessed in the land. The LORD will not hand him over to what his enemies want.
The LORD will hold him up when he is sick in bed, and will bring him back to health.
I said, "LORD, be kind to me! Heal me, because I have sinned against you."
My enemies say evil things about me: "When will he die and his name be forgotten?"
When one of them comes to visit me, he says things he does not mean. In his heart he collects bad news, and when he leaves, he tells everyone.
All who hate me whisper together about me. They imagine the worst for me.
They say, "He has a terrible disease. He is lying down and will never get up again."
Even my close friend, someone I trusted, who ate my bread, has turned against me.
But you, LORD, be kind to me. Raise me up so I can pay them back.
I know that you are pleased with me, because my enemy does not win over me.
You hold me up because I am innocent, and you keep me with you forever.
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, forever and ever! Amen and amen.
For the music director. A thoughtful psalm of the sons of Korah. As a deer longs for streams of water, so I long for you, God.
I am thirsty for God, the living God. When can I go and stand in front of God?
My tears have been my food day and night, while people keep asking me, "Where is your God?"
I remember these things as I pour out my heart: how I used to walk with the crowd, leading them to God's house, with shouts of joy and praise among the crowd celebrating a festival.
Why are you so sad, my soul? Why are you so upset inside me? Put your hope in God! I will praise him again, because he is with me and saves me.
My God, I am so sad inside. So I will remember you from the land of the Jordan River, from the peaks of Mount Hermon, from Mount Mizar.
Deep waters call out to deep waters in the roar of your waterfalls. All your waves and breakers have rolled over me.
By day the LORD sends his faithful love. At night his song is with me, a prayer to the God who gives me life.
I say to God, my rock, "Why have you forgotten me? Why must I go around crying because my enemy is crushing me?"
My enemies insult me as if they were breaking my bones. They keep asking me, "Where is your God?"
Why are you so sad, my soul? Why are you so upset inside me? Put your hope in God! I will praise him again, my saviour and my God.
God, prove that I am innocent. Defend my cause against an ungodly nation. Rescue me from liars and evil people.
You are God, my strength. Why have you rejected me? Why must I go around crying because my enemy is crushing me?
Send out your light and your truth. Let them lead me. Let them bring me to your holy hill, to the place where you live.
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise you with the harp, God, my God.
Why are you so sad, my soul? Why are you so upset inside me? Put your hope in God! I will praise him again, my saviour, my helper, and my God.
For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A thoughtful psalm. God, we have heard it with our own ears. Our ancestors told us what you did in their days, long ago.
With your own hand you drove out the nations and planted our ancestors in the land. You crushed the peoples and made our ancestors spread out.
They did not take the land with their own swords. Their own strength did not save them. It was your right hand, your strength, and the light of your face, because you loved them.
God, you are my King. Command victories for the people of Jacob!
With your help we push back our enemies. With the power of your name we trample those who attack us.
I do not trust in my bow. My sword cannot save me.
But you save us from our enemies. You put those who hate us to shame.
We boast about God all day long. We will praise your name forever. Selah.
But now you have rejected us and disgraced us. You no longer go out with our armies.
You made us run away from our enemies. Those who hate us have robbed us.
You have let us be eaten like sheep, and you have scattered us among the nations.
You sold your people for almost nothing. You gained nothing from selling them.
You have made us a joke to our neighbours. The people around us laugh at us and make fun of us.
You have made us an insult among the nations. People shake their heads at us.
I live in disgrace all day long. My face is covered with shame
because of the insults of those who mock me, because of the enemy who wants revenge.
All this has happened to us, but we have not forgotten you. We have not been unfaithful to your covenant.
Our hearts have not turned away. Our feet have not left your path.
But you crushed us and left us where the jackals live. You covered us with deep darkness.
If we had forgotten the name of our God or lifted our hands in prayer to a foreign god,
wouldn't God have found out? He knows the secrets of every heart.
But because of you we face death all day long. We are thought of as sheep to be killed.
Wake up, Lord! Why are you sleeping? Get up! Do not reject us forever.
Why do you hide your face? Why do you forget our suffering and how we are being crushed?
We are pushed down into the dust. Our bodies cling to the ground.
Get up and help us. Rescue us because of your faithful love.

For the music director. To the tune "The Lilies." A thoughtful psalm of the sons of Korah. A wedding song. My heart is full of beautiful words as I recite my poem for the king. My tongue is like the pen of a skilled writer.
You are the most excellent of men. Your lips speak with grace, so God has blessed you forever.
Put your sword at your side, mighty warrior. Clothe yourself in splendour and majesty.
In your majesty ride out to victory for the sake of truth, humility, and what is right. Let your right hand do amazing things.
Your arrows are sharp. They pierce the hearts of the king's enemies. The nations fall at your feet.
Your throne, God, lasts forever and ever. You rule your kingdom with a fair sceptre.
You love what is right and hate what is evil. So God, your God, has chosen you above your companions by pouring on you the oil of joy.
All your robes smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia. From palaces decorated with ivory, the music of stringed instruments makes you glad.
Daughters of kings are among the women you honour. At your right hand stands the queen, wearing gold from Ophir.
Listen, daughter. Think about this and pay attention. Forget your people and your father's family.
The king will be delighted by your beauty. Honour him, because he is your lord.
The people of Tyre will come with a gift. Rich people will try to win your favour.
The princess is in her rooms, looking glorious. Her gown is woven with gold.
She is led to the king in a beautifully embroidered dress. The young women, her friends who follow her, are brought to you.
They are led in with joy and gladness. They enter the king's palace.
Your sons will take the place of your ancestors. You will make them rulers over all the earth.
I will make your name remembered for all generations. So the nations will praise you forever and ever.
For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. To the tune of Alamoth. God is our safe place and our strength. He is always there to help in times of trouble.
So we will not be afraid, even if the earth shakes and the mountains fall into the middle of the sea,
even if its waters roar and foam and the mountains shake as the waters rise. Selah.
There is a river whose streams make the city of God glad, the holy place where the Most High lives.
God is in the middle of that city. It will not fall. God will help it at the break of day.
The nations are in an uproar. Kingdoms fall. God raises his voice, and the earth melts.
The LORD of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
Come and see what the LORD has done, the ruins he has brought on the earth.
He stops wars all over the world. He breaks the bow and snaps the spear. He burns the chariots with fire.
He says, "Be still, and know that I am God. I will be honoured among the nations. I will be honoured in the earth."
The LORD of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
For the music director. A psalm of the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you nations! Shout to God with cries of joy!
The LORD Most High is amazing. He is the great King over all the earth.
He brings nations under our control and peoples under our feet.
He chose our land for us, the pride of Jacob, whom he loved. Selah.
God has gone up with shouts of joy. The LORD has gone up with the sound of a trumpet.
Sing praises to God! Sing praises! Sing praises to our King! Sing praises!
God is the King of all the earth. Sing a psalm of praise to him.
God rules over the nations. God sits on his holy throne.
The leaders of the nations gather together with the people of the God of Abraham. All the rulers of the earth belong to God. He is greatly honoured!
A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. The LORD is great and deserves great praise in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.
Mount Zion, high and beautiful, is the joy of the whole earth. It is like the highest point of the north, the city of the great King.
God is in its strong towers. He has shown that he is its fortress.
Look, kings joined forces and marched together against it.
But when they saw it, they were amazed. They were terrified and ran away.
They were seized with trembling there, with pain like a woman giving birth.
You destroyed them like ships of Tarshish wrecked by an east wind.
What we have heard, we have now seen in the city of the LORD of Armies, the city of our God. God will make it secure forever. Selah.
God, in your temple we think about your faithful love.
God, your praise reaches to the ends of the earth, just like your name. Your right hand is full of goodness.
Let Mount Zion be glad! Let the towns of Judah celebrate because of your fair judgments.
Walk around Zion. Go all the way around it. Count its towers.
Look closely at its walls. Go through its strong places, so you can tell the next generation about them.
This God is our God forever and ever. He will be our guide even to the end.
For the music director. A psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you nations. Listen, everyone who lives in the world,
both ordinary people and important people, rich and poor alike.
My mouth will speak words of wisdom. My heart will speak with understanding.
I will listen carefully to a wise saying. I will explain my riddle while playing the harp.
Why should I be afraid when trouble comes, when wicked people who want to trip me up surround me?
They trust in their wealth and boast about how rich they are.
But no one can pay to save another person's life. No one can pay God a ransom for someone.
The price to save a life is too high. No payment is ever enough
to let someone live forever and never see the grave.
Everyone can see that wise people die. Foolish and stupid people also die, and they leave their wealth to others.
They think their houses will last forever, that their homes will last for all generations. They even name their lands after themselves.
But people, even with all their riches, do not last. They are like the animals that die.
This is what happens to those who trust in themselves, and to those who agree with what they say. Selah.
Like sheep they are headed for the grave. Death will be their shepherd. In the morning honest people will rule over them. Their bodies will rot in the grave, far from their fine homes.
But God will rescue me from the power of the grave. He will surely take me to himself. Selah.
Do not be upset when someone becomes rich, when the wealth of their house grows.
When they die, they will take nothing with them. Their wealth will not go down with them.
While they lived, they thought they were blessed, and people praise you when you do well for yourself.
But they will join their ancestors, who will never see the light again.
People who have riches but no understanding are like the animals that die.
A psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks. He calls to the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets.
God shines out from Zion, the city of perfect beauty.
Our God is coming, and he will not be silent. A fire burns up everything in front of him. A great storm rages around him.
He calls to the skies above and to the earth, so he can judge his people.
He says, "Gather my faithful people to me, those who made a covenant with me by offering sacrifices."
The skies announce that he is fair, because God himself is the judge. Selah.
"Listen, my people, and I will speak. Israel, I will give evidence against you. I am God, your God.
I am not blaming you for your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are always in front of me.
I do not need a bull from your barn or goats from your pens.
Every animal in the forest is mine, and the cattle on a thousand hills.
I know every bird in the mountains. All the wild animals in the fields are mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, because the world is mine and everything in it.
Do I eat the meat of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
Bring thankfulness to God as your sacrifice. Keep the promises you made to the Most High.
Call to me when you are in trouble. I will rescue you, and you will honour me."
But God says to the wicked, "What right do you have to recite my laws or talk about my covenant?
You hate my correction and throw my words behind you.
When you see a thief, you join him. You spend time with people who are unfaithful in marriage.
Your mouth is quick to speak evil. Your tongue makes up lies.
You sit and speak against your brother. You spread lies about your own mother's son.
You did these things and I was silent, so you thought I was just like you. But now I will correct you and lay out the charges against you right in front of you.
Think about this, you who forget God, or I will tear you to pieces and no one will rescue you.
Whoever brings thankfulness as a sacrifice honours me. To the one who follows the right path, I will show God's saving help."

For the music director. A psalm of David, written when the prophet Nathan came to him after David had slept with Bathsheba. God, be kind to me because of your faithful love. Because of your great mercy, wipe out my sins.
Wash away all my guilt. Make me clean from my sin.
I know the wrong things I have done. My sin is always in front of me.
I have sinned against you, against you only, and done what is evil in your eyes. So you are right when you speak, and fair when you judge.
I was a sinner from the moment I was born, a sinner from the time my mother became pregnant with me.
You want truth deep inside me. You teach me wisdom in the secret places of my heart.
Make me pure with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness again. Let the bones you have crushed celebrate.
Turn your face away from my sins. Wipe out all my guilt.
God, create a pure heart in me. Give me a new spirit that is faithful to you.
Do not send me away from you. Do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Give me back the joy of your rescue. Give me a willing spirit to keep me going.
Then I will teach sinners your ways, and they will turn back to you.
God, the God who saves me, rescue me from the guilt of murder. Then my tongue will sing loudly about how you do what is right.
Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will praise you.
You do not take pleasure in sacrifices, or I would bring one. You are not pleased with burnt offerings.
The sacrifice God wants is a broken spirit. God, you will not turn away a heart that is broken and sorry for sin.
Be kind to Zion and make it successful. Build up the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you will be pleased with the right sacrifices, with burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings. Then bulls will be offered on your altar.

For the music director. A thoughtful psalm of David, written when Doeg the Edomite went and told Saul, "David has gone to Ahimelech's house." Why do you boast about evil, you mighty man? God's faithful love lasts all day long.
Your tongue plans destruction. It is like a sharp razor, cutting with lies.
You love evil more than good, and lying more than telling the truth. Selah.
You love words that destroy, you lying tongue.
So God will bring you down forever. He will grab you and drag you out of your tent. He will pull you up by the roots from the land of the living. Selah.
Good people will see it and be filled with awe. They will laugh at you and say,
"Look at this man who did not make God his fortress, but trusted in his great wealth and grew strong by destroying others."
But I am like an olive tree growing green in God's house. I trust in God's faithful love forever and ever.
I will always thank you for what you have done. In front of your faithful people I will hope in your name, because it is good.
For the music director. To the tune "Mahalath." A thoughtful psalm of David. Foolish people say to themselves, "There is no God." They are rotten and do disgusting evil. No one does good.
God looks down from heaven on all people to see if anyone understands, if anyone looks for God.
All of them have turned away. All of them have become rotten. No one does good, not even one.
Do these evil people know nothing? They eat up my people as if they were eating bread, and they never call on God.
There they were, filled with terror where there was nothing to fear. God scattered the bones of those who attacked you. You put them to shame, because God has rejected them.
I wish rescue for Israel would come out of Zion! When God brings his people back from captivity, Jacob will celebrate and Israel will be glad.

For the music director. To be played on stringed instruments. A thoughtful psalm of David, written when the people of Ziph went and said to Saul, "David is hiding among us." God, save me by the power of your name. Defend my cause by your strength.
God, hear my prayer. Listen to what I am saying.
Strangers are attacking me. Violent people are trying to kill me. They do not care about God. Selah.
But God is my helper. The Lord is the one who keeps me alive.
May my enemies be paid back for their evil. Destroy them, because you are faithful.
I will gladly bring you an offering. I will praise your name, LORD, because it is good.
You have rescued me from all my troubles. I have seen my enemies defeated.
For the music director. To be played on stringed instruments. A thoughtful psalm of David. God, listen to my prayer. Do not ignore my cry for mercy.
Listen to me and answer me. My troubles make me restless and I groan
because of what my enemy says and how the wicked attack me. They bring trouble on me and hate me in their anger.
My heart is in deep pain. The terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fear and trembling have come over me. Horror has overwhelmed me.
I said, "I wish I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away and be at rest.
I would fly far away and stay in the wilderness. Selah.
I would hurry to find shelter from the raging wind and storm."
Lord, confuse the wicked and mix up their words, because I see violence and fighting in the city.
Day and night they go around on its walls. Evil and trouble are inside it.
Destruction is inside the city. Threats and lies never leave its streets.
If an enemy were insulting me, I could put up with it. If someone who hated me were rising against me, I could hide from him.
But it is you, someone like me, my companion and close friend.
We used to share sweet friendship together. We walked together with the crowd at God's house.
Let death take my enemies by surprise. Let them go down alive into the grave, because evil lives in their homes and hearts.
But I call to God, and the LORD saves me.
Evening, morning, and noon I cry out in distress, and he hears my voice.
He rescues me unharmed from the battle against me, even though many people are against me.
God, who has ruled forever, will hear and bring them down. Selah. They never change their ways, and they do not respect God.
My friend attacks his friends. He breaks his promises.
His words are as smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, but they are like swords ready to strike.
Give your worries to the LORD, and he will take care of you. He will never let good people fall.
But you, God, will bring the wicked down into the pit of ruin. Murderers and liars will not live out half their lives. But I will trust in you.

For the music director. To the tune "Silent Dove in Distant Lands." A poem of David, written when the Philistines captured him in Gath. God, be kind to me, because people are trying to swallow me up. All day long they attack and crush me.
My enemies try to swallow me up all day long. So many people proudly fight against me.
When I am afraid, I will trust in you.
I praise God for what he has promised. I trust in God, so I will not be afraid. What can mere humans do to me?
All day long they twist my words. They are always planning to hurt me.
They plot together and hide. They watch my every step, eager to kill me.
Will they get away with their evil? God, bring the nations down in your anger.
You keep track of all my wandering. You have collected all my tears in your bottle. Haven't you written them in your book?
My enemies will turn back on the day I call for help. This I know: God is on my side.
I praise God for what he has promised. I praise the LORD for what he has promised.
I trust in God, so I will not be afraid. What can people do to me?
God, I will keep the promises I made to you. I will give you offerings of thanks.
You have rescued me from death and kept my feet from tripping, so I can walk with God in the light of life.

For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David, written when he ran away from Saul into the cave. Be kind to me, God, be kind to me, because I come to you for safety. I will find safety in the shadow of your wings until the disaster has passed.
I cry out to God Most High, to God who does everything he planned for me.
He sends help from heaven and saves me. He scolds those who are chasing me. Selah. God sends his faithful love and his truth.
I am surrounded by lions. I lie among people who are on fire with hatred, people whose teeth are spears and arrows and whose tongues are sharp swords.
God, be honoured above the skies! Let your glory be over all the earth!
They set a net to catch my feet. I was bowed down in distress. They dug a pit in my path, but they fell into it themselves. Selah.
My heart is steady, God. My heart is steady. I will sing and make music.
Wake up, my soul! Wake up, lute and harp! I will wake up the dawn.
Lord, I will thank you among the peoples. I will sing praises to you among the nations.
Your great and faithful love reaches to the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
God, be honoured above the skies. Let your glory be over all the earth.
For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David. You rulers, do you really speak what is right? Do you judge people fairly?
No, in your hearts you plan evil. Your hands spread violence over the earth.
Wicked people go wrong from the day they are born. From birth they wander off and tell lies.
Their poison is like the poison of a snake, like a cobra that blocks its ears
so it cannot hear the music of the snake charmer, however skilful he is.
God, break the teeth in their mouths! LORD, tear out the fangs of these lions!
Let them disappear like water that drains away. When they shoot their arrows, let them be blunt.
Let them be like a slug that melts away as it moves, like a baby born dead that never sees the sun.
Before your cooking pots feel the heat of the burning thorns, God will sweep them away, green and burning alike.
Good people will be glad when they see the wicked punished. They will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
Then people will say, "There really is a reward for good people. There really is a God who judges the earth."

For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David, written when Saul sent men to watch David's house so they could kill him. Rescue me from my enemies, my God. Protect me from those who attack me.
Rescue me from people who do evil. Save me from murderers.
Look, they are lying in wait to kill me. Powerful people gather together against me, LORD, but not because I have done wrong or sinned.
I have done nothing wrong, yet they hurry to attack me. Get up and help me! Look at what is happening!
LORD God of Armies, God of Israel, wake up and punish all the nations. Show no mercy to wicked traitors. Selah.
They come back in the evening, howling like dogs and prowling around the city.
Look at what spews from their mouths. Their words cut like swords. They say, "Who can hear us?"
But you, LORD, laugh at them. You make fun of all the nations.
You are my strength. I watch for you, because God is my high tower.
My God will come to meet me with his faithful love. God will let me look down on my defeated enemies.
Do not kill them, or my people may forget. Scatter them with your power and bring them down, Lord, our shield.
Their mouths are full of sin, and their lips speak evil words. Let them be caught in their pride, because of the curses and lies they speak.
Destroy them in your anger. Destroy them until they are gone. Then everyone to the ends of the earth will know that God rules over Jacob. Selah.
Let them come back in the evening, howling like dogs and prowling around the city.
They wander around looking for food, and growl all night if they do not get enough.
But I will sing about your strength. In the morning I will sing loudly about your faithful love. You have been my high tower, a safe place when I am in trouble.
You are my strength. I will sing praises to you. God is my high tower, the God who shows me faithful love.

For the music director. To the tune "The Lily of the Covenant." A teaching poem of David, written when he fought against Aram Naharaim and Aram Zobah, and when Joab came back and killed twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. God, you have rejected us and broken through our defences. You have been angry. Now bring us back again.
You made the land shake and split it open. Repair its cracks, because it is shaking.
You have made your people suffer hard times. You have given us wine that makes us stagger.
But you have raised a flag for those who respect you, a place to gather because of your truth. Selah.
Save us with your right hand and answer us, so the people you love may be rescued.
God has spoken from his holy place: "I will win! I will divide up Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is my helmet. Judah is my sceptre.
Moab is my washbowl. I will throw my sandal on Edom to show I own it. I shout in victory over Philistia."
Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
God, haven't you rejected us? You no longer go out with our armies, God.
Help us against our enemy, because human help is useless.
With God we will fight bravely, and he will trample down our enemies.
For the music director. To be played on a stringed instrument. Of David. God, hear my cry. Listen to my prayer.
From the ends of the earth I call to you when my heart is weak. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I am.
You have been my safe place, a strong tower against the enemy.
Let me live in your tent forever. Let me find safety in the shelter of your wings. Selah.
God, you have heard my promises. You have given me what belongs to those who respect your name.
Make the king's life long. Let his years go on for generations.
Let him sit on his throne in God's presence forever. Let your faithful love and truth protect him.
Then I will always sing praises to your name as I keep my promises every day.
For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David. I find rest in God alone. My rescue comes from him.
He alone is my rock and my saviour. He is my fortress, so I will never be badly shaken.
How long will all of you attack one man? Will all of you push him down, like a leaning wall or a broken fence?
They only plan to push him down from his high position. They love telling lies. They bless with their mouths, but in their hearts they curse. Selah.
Find rest, my soul, quietly in God alone. My hope comes from him.
He alone is my rock and my saviour. He is my fortress, so I will not be shaken.
My rescue and my honour depend on God. He is my strong rock and my safe place.
Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your hearts to him. God is our safe place. Selah.
Ordinary people are only a breath, and important people are just a lie. If you put them on a scale, together they weigh less than a breath.
Do not trust in taking things by force. Do not hope in stolen goods. Even if your riches grow, do not set your heart on them.
God has spoken one thing, and I have heard it twice: power belongs to God.
Faithful love also belongs to you, Lord. You pay back each person for what they have done.

A psalm of David, written when he was in the wilderness of Judah. God, you are my God. I search hard for you. My soul is thirsty for you. My whole body longs for you in a dry and tired land where there is no water.
I have seen you in your holy place and seen your power and glory.
Your faithful love is better than life, so my lips will praise you.
I will praise you as long as I live. I will lift up my hands in prayer to you.
I will be satisfied as if I had eaten the richest food. My mouth will sing praises to you with joyful lips.
I remember you when I lie in bed. I think about you through the night.
You have been my helper. I sing for joy in the shadow of your wings.
I hold on to you closely. Your right hand holds me up.
But those who want to kill me will go down into the depths of the earth.
They will be killed by the sword. Jackals will eat their bodies.
But the king will be glad in God. Everyone who makes promises in God's name will praise him, and the mouths of liars will be shut.
For the music director. A psalm of David. God, hear me as I tell you my complaint. Protect my life from the terror of my enemy.
Hide me from the secret plans of the wicked, from the noisy crowd of evil people.
They sharpen their tongues like swords. They aim their cruel words like deadly arrows.
They shoot from hiding places at innocent people. They shoot suddenly and are not afraid.
They encourage each other in their evil plans. They talk about setting hidden traps. They say, "Who will see them?"
They plan their crimes and say, "We have a perfect plan!" The human mind and heart are very cunning.
But God will shoot them with his arrows. Suddenly they will be struck down.
Their own words will bring them down. Everyone who sees them will shake their heads.
All people will be afraid. They will tell what God has done and think carefully about his works.
Good people will be glad in the LORD and find safety in him. All whose hearts are honest will praise him!
For the music director. A psalm of David. A song. God, praise waits for you in Zion. We will keep our promises to you.
You hear prayer. All people will come to you.
When our sins were too much for us, you forgave our wrongdoing.
Happy is the one you choose and bring near to live in your courtyards. We are filled with the good things of your house, your holy temple.
You answer us with amazing acts of goodness, God our saviour. You are the hope of everyone to the ends of the earth and of those far away across the seas.
With your power you formed the mountains. You are dressed in strength.
You calm the roaring seas and their crashing waves, and the uproar of the nations.
Those who live far away are amazed at your wonders. Where the morning dawns and where the evening fades, you make people shout for joy.
You take care of the land and water it. You make it very rich. God's streams are full of water. You give people grain, because that is how you planned it.
You soak its ploughed rows and flatten its ridges. You soften it with showers and bless its crops.
You crown the year with your goodness. Your wagons overflow with plenty.
The grasslands of the wilderness overflow. The hills are dressed with joy.
The fields are covered with flocks. The valleys are clothed with grain. They shout for joy and sing!
For the music director. A song. A psalm. Shout with joy to God, all the earth!
Sing about the glory of his name! Praise him gloriously!
Say to God, "How amazing are the things you do! Your power is so great that your enemies bow down to you.
All the earth worships you and sings to you. They sing praises to your name." Selah.
Come and see what God has done, the amazing things he has done for people.
He turned the sea into dry land. They walked through the river on foot. There we celebrated because of him.
He rules forever by his power. His eyes watch the nations. Do not let rebels rise up against him. Selah.
Praise our God, all you nations! Let the sound of his praise be heard.
He keeps us alive and does not let our feet slip.
God, you tested us. You purified us like silver.
You brought us into prison and put heavy loads on our backs.
You let people ride over our heads. We went through fire and water, but you brought us to a place of plenty.
I will come into your temple with burnt offerings. I will keep the promises I made to you,
the promises my lips made and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.
I will offer you fat animals as burnt offerings, with the smoke of rams. I will offer bulls and goats. Selah.
Come and listen, all you who respect God. I will tell you what he has done for me.
I cried out to him with my mouth. His praise was on my tongue.
If I had held on to sin in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
But God has surely listened. He has heard my prayer.
Praise God! He has not turned away my prayer or taken his faithful love away from me.
For the music director. To be played on stringed instruments. A psalm. A song. May God be kind to us and bless us. May his face shine on us. Selah.
Then your ways will be known on earth, and your saving power among all nations.
Let the nations praise you, God. Let all the nations praise you.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, because you judge the peoples fairly and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
Let the nations praise you, God. Let all the nations praise you.
The land has given its harvest. God, our God, blesses us.
God blesses us. All the ends of the earth will respect him.
For the music director. A psalm of David. A song. Let God rise up! Let his enemies be scattered! Let those who hate him run away from him.
Blow them away like smoke. As wax melts in a fire, let the wicked be destroyed in front of God.
But let good people be glad. Let them celebrate in front of God. Let them be filled with joy.
Sing to God! Sing praises to his name! Praise the one who rides on the clouds. His name is the LORD! Celebrate in front of him!
God, in his holy home, is a father to those without a father and a defender of widows.
God gives lonely people a family. He leads prisoners out with singing, but those who rebel live in a dry, sun-baked land.
God, when you went out ahead of your people, when you marched through the wilderness, Selah,
the earth shook. The skies poured down rain in front of God, the God of Sinai, in front of God, the God of Israel.
God, you sent plenty of rain. You refreshed your land when it was worn out.
Your people settled there. God, in your goodness you provided for the poor.
The Lord gave the message, and a great crowd of women spread the news:
"Kings and their armies run away! They run away!" The women at home divide the stolen goods.
Even those who stayed among the sheep pens found treasures: doves with wings covered with silver and feathers of shining gold.
When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like snow falling on Mount Zalmon.
The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan have many peaks.
You mountains with many peaks, why do you look with jealousy at the mountain where God chooses to rule? The LORD will live there forever.
The chariots of God are tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands. The Lord has come from Sinai into his holy place.
You went up on high and led captives with you. You received gifts from people, even from those who rebelled, so that the LORD God could live there.
Praise the Lord, who carries our burdens every day. He is the God who saves us. Selah.
Our God is a God who saves. The Lord GOD rescues us from death.
But God will crush the heads of his enemies, the hairy heads of those who keep on sinning.
The Lord said, "I will bring them back from Bashan. I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so you may wade in the blood of your enemies, and the tongues of your dogs may have their share."
God, your parade has been seen, the parade of my God and King into the holy place.
The singers are in front, the musicians are behind, and in between are young women playing tambourines.
Praise God in the great gatherings. Praise the Lord, you people of Israel!
There is little Benjamin leading them, the leaders of Judah with their crowd, and the leaders of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Your God has commanded you to be strong. God, show us your strength, as you have done for us before.
Because of your temple in Jerusalem, kings will bring gifts to you.
Warn the wild beast among the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations. Make them bow down with bars of silver. Scatter the nations who love war.
Leaders will come from Egypt. Ethiopia will hurry to lift up its hands to God.
Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord. Selah.
Sing to the one who rides across the highest heavens, the ancient skies. Listen! He thunders with his mighty voice.
Announce God's strength! His majesty is over Israel. His power is in the skies.
God, you are amazing in your holy place. The God of Israel gives strength and power to his people. Praise God!
For the music director. To the tune "Lilies." Of David. Save me, God, because the water has come up to my neck!
I am sinking in deep mud, and there is nowhere to stand. I have gone into deep water, and the flood is sweeping over me.
I am worn out from crying for help. My throat is dry. My eyes are tired from looking for my God.
Those who hate me for no reason are more than the hairs on my head. Many powerful enemies want to destroy me for no reason. I am forced to give back what I did not steal.
God, you know how foolish I have been. My sins are not hidden from you.
Lord GOD of Armies, do not let those who hope in you be put to shame because of me. God of Israel, do not let those who look for you be disgraced because of me.
I have been insulted because of you. Shame covers my face.
I have become a stranger to my own brothers, a foreigner to my mother's children.
My deep love for your house burns inside me like a fire. The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
When I cried and went without food, they insulted me for it.
When I wore rough clothes of sadness, people made jokes about me.
Those who sit at the city gate talk about me. Drunks make up songs about me.
But LORD, I pray to you at the time you choose to show kindness. God, because of your great and faithful love, answer me with your sure rescue.
Pull me out of the mud. Do not let me sink. Rescue me from those who hate me and from the deep waters.
Do not let the floodwaters sweep over me. Do not let the deep water swallow me up. Do not let the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, LORD, because your faithful love is good. Because of your great mercy, turn to me.
Do not hide your face from me, your servant, because I am in trouble. Answer me quickly!
Come near and rescue me. Set me free from my enemies.
You know how I am insulted, shamed, and disgraced. You see all my enemies.
Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for someone to feel sorry for me, but there was no one. I looked for someone to comfort me, but I found no one.
They put poison in my food. When I was thirsty, they gave me sour wine to drink.
Let their own table become a trap for them. Let it become their punishment and a snare.
Let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see. Let their backs always be bent with trouble.
Pour out your anger on them. Let your burning anger catch up with them.
Let their homes be left empty. Let no one live in their tents.
They attack the person you have already wounded. They talk about the pain of those you have hurt.
Add one crime after another to their record. Do not let them share in your goodness.
Let their names be wiped out of the book of life. Do not let them be listed with good people.
But I am in pain and distress. God, let your saving power protect me.
I will praise God's name with a song. I will honour him with thanks.
This will please the LORD more than offering an ox, or a bull with its horns and hoofs.
Humble people will see it and be glad. You who look for God, let your hearts be encouraged.
The LORD hears those in need. He does not look down on his people who are prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them!
God will save Zion and rebuild the towns of Judah. His people will settle there and own the land.
The children of his servants will receive it. Those who love his name will live there.
For the music director. Of David. To help remember. God, hurry to rescue me. LORD, come quickly to help me.
Let those who are trying to kill me be put to shame and confused. Let those who want to ruin me be turned back in disgrace.
Let those who say, "Aha! Aha!" turn back because of their shame.
But let all who look for you be full of joy and gladness because of you. Let those who love your saving help always say, "God is great!"
But I am poor and needy. Come quickly to me, God. You are my helper and my rescuer. LORD, do not wait.
LORD, I come to you for safety. Never let me be put to shame.
Because you do what is right, rescue me and save me. Turn your ear to me and save me.
Be my rock of safety where I can always go. Give the command to save me, because you are my rock and my fortress.
My God, rescue me from the power of the wicked, from the grip of evil and cruel people.
Lord GOD, you are my hope. I have trusted you since I was young.
I have depended on you since I was born. You brought me out of my mother's womb. I will always praise you.
My life is an example to many people, because you are my strong place of safety.
My mouth is full of your praise. I tell of your glory all day long.
Do not throw me away when I am old. Do not leave me when my strength is gone.
My enemies talk against me. Those who are waiting to kill me plot together.
They say, "God has left him. Go after him and catch him, because no one will rescue him."
God, do not stay far away from me. My God, hurry to help me.
Let those who accuse me be put to shame and destroyed. Let those who want to hurt me be covered with shame and disgrace.
But I will always have hope. I will praise you more and more.
All day long I will tell how you do what is right and how you save, even though I cannot understand it all.
I will come and tell about the mighty acts of the Lord GOD. I will remind everyone that you alone do what is right.
God, you have taught me since I was young. To this day I tell about the amazing things you do.
Even when I am old and grey, God, do not leave me. Let me tell the next generation about your strength, and everyone still to come about your power.
God, your goodness reaches to the skies. You have done great things. God, who is like you?
You have let me see many bitter troubles, but you will give me life again. You will bring me up again from the depths of the earth.
You will make me even more honoured, and you will comfort me again.
I will praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God. I will sing praises to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy as I sing praises to you. I will sing because you have rescued me.
My tongue will talk about how you do what is right all day long, because those who wanted to hurt me have been put to shame and confused.
Of Solomon. God, give the king your justice. Give the king's son your goodness.
Then he will judge your people fairly and treat your poor people with justice.
Let the mountains bring peace and plenty to the people. Let the hills bring the fruit of goodness.
He will defend the poor among the people. He will save the children of those in need, and he will crush those who treat them cruelly.
People will respect you as long as the sun shines and as long as the moon lasts, for all generations.
He will be like rain falling on a cut field, like showers that water the earth.
While he rules, good people will do well, and there will be plenty of peace until the moon is gone.
He will rule from sea to sea, from the Euphrates River to the ends of the earth.
The desert tribes will bow down in front of him. His enemies will lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and of the islands will bring him payments. The kings of Sheba and Seba will bring him gifts.
All kings will bow down to him. All nations will serve him.
He will rescue the needy when they cry out, and the poor who have no one to help them.
He will feel sorry for the weak and needy. He will save the lives of those in need.
He will rescue them from cruelty and violence. Their lives are precious to him.
Long live the king! May he be given gold from Sheba. May people always pray for him and bless him all day long.
Let there be plenty of grain all over the land, waving even on the hilltops. Let its fruit sway like the trees of Lebanon. Let the people in the cities do well, like grass in the field.
May his name last forever. May his fame continue as long as the sun shines. All nations will be blessed through him, and they will call him blessed.
Praise the LORD God, the God of Israel. He alone does amazing things.
Praise his glorious name forever! Let the whole earth be filled with his glory! Amen and amen.
This is the end of the prayers of David, the son of Jesse.
A psalm of Asaph. God really is good to Israel, to those whose hearts are pure.
But as for me, I almost lost my footing. My feet nearly slipped.
I was jealous of proud people when I saw how well the wicked were doing.
They do not struggle when they die. Their bodies are healthy and strong.
They do not have the troubles other people have. They are not struck by problems like everyone else.
So they wear pride like a necklace. They wrap themselves in violence like clothing.
Their eyes bulge out from their fat faces. Their minds are full of proud ideas.
They make fun of others and speak with hatred. In their pride they threaten to crush people.
They speak as if they rule the skies. Their tongues strut across the earth.
So people turn to them and drink in everything they say.
They say, "How would God know? Does the Most High know anything?"
Look, this is what the wicked are like. They always have an easy life, and their riches keep growing.
It seems I have kept my heart pure for nothing. I have washed my hands to show I am innocent, but for nothing.
All day long I have trouble. Every morning brings me new punishment.
If I had said, "I will talk like this," I would have betrayed your children.
When I tried to understand all this, it was too hard for me,
until I went into God's holy place. Then I understood what will happen to the wicked in the end.
You put them on slippery ground. You throw them down to ruin.
How suddenly they are destroyed! They are completely swept away by terrors.
They are like a dream that disappears when a person wakes up. Lord, when you get up, you will brush them aside like a dream.
When my heart was bitter and my feelings were hurt,
I was foolish and did not understand. I was like an animal in front of you.
Yet I am always with you. You hold my right hand.
You guide me with your advice, and afterward you will take me into glory.
Who do I have in heaven but you? There is nothing on earth I want more than you.
My body and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart. He is mine forever.
Those who are far from you will be destroyed. You destroy everyone who is unfaithful to you.
But for me, it is good to be near God. I have made the Lord GOD my safe place, so I can tell about everything you have done.
A thoughtful psalm of Asaph. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember the people you bought long ago, the tribe you rescued to be your own. Remember Mount Zion, where you live.
Walk through these endless ruins. See all the damage the enemy has done to your holy place.
Your enemies roared in the place where you met with us. They set up their flags as signs of victory.
They acted like men swinging axes to cut through a thick forest.
They smashed all the carved wood with axes and hammers.
They burned your holy place to the ground. They made the place where your name lives unclean.
They said to themselves, "We will crush them completely!" They burned down every place in the land where God was worshipped.
We no longer see miraculous signs. There are no prophets left. None of us knows how long this will last.
How long, God, will the enemy insult you? Will the enemy insult your name forever?
Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand? Take it out from your robe and destroy them!
But God has been my King from long ago. He brings rescue all over the earth.
With your power you split the sea in two. You smashed the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan and gave it as food to the creatures of the desert.
You opened up springs and streams. You dried up rivers that always flowed.
The day belongs to you, and so does the night. You set the sun and the light in their places.
You set all the borders of the earth. You made summer and winter.
Remember, LORD, how the enemy has insulted you, how foolish people have insulted your name.
Do not hand over the life of your dove to wild animals. Do not forget your suffering people forever.
Remember your covenant, because the dark places of the land are full of violence.
Do not let crushed people be turned away in shame. Let the poor and needy praise your name.
Get up, God! Defend your cause. Remember how foolish people insult you all day long.
Do not ignore the shouting of your enemies. The noise of those who rise against you keeps getting louder.
For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A psalm of Asaph. A song. We thank you, God. We thank you, because you are near. People tell about the amazing things you have done.
God says, "When the time I have chosen comes, I will judge fairly.
When the earth and everyone who lives on it shake, I am the one who holds its pillars firm. Selah.
I said to proud people, 'Do not boast.' I said to the wicked, 'Do not show off your strength.
Do not raise your horns against heaven. Do not speak so stubbornly and proudly.'"
Honour does not come from the east or the west, or from the desert in the south.
It is God who judges. He brings one person down and lifts another up.
The LORD holds a cup in his hand, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the very last drop.
But I will always tell about this. I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
God says, "I will break the strength of all the wicked, but the strength of good people will be lifted up."
For the music director. To be played on stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song. God is known in Judah. His name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem. His home is in Zion.
There he broke the flaming arrows, the shields and swords, and the weapons of war. Selah.
You shine with glory. You are more majestic than mountains full of prey.
Brave soldiers have been robbed. They lie in the sleep of death. None of the warriors can lift a hand.
When you shouted at them, God of Jacob, both horses and chariots fell into a deep sleep.
You alone are to be feared. Who can stand in front of you when you are angry?
From heaven you announced your judgment. The earth was afraid and was silent
when you, God, rose up to judge and to save all the suffering people of the earth. Selah.
Even human anger ends up praising you. Those who survive your anger are held back.
Make promises to the LORD your God and keep them. Let all the nations around bring gifts to the one who should be feared.
He breaks the pride of rulers. The kings of the earth are afraid of him.
For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph. I cry out to God. I cry out to God for help, and he listens to me.
When I was in trouble, I looked for the Lord. All night I lifted my hands in prayer without getting tired. But nothing could comfort me.
I think of God, and I groan. I think about it, and my spirit grows weak. Selah.
You keep my eyes from closing. I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
I think about the old days, the years long ago.
At night I remember my songs. I think deeply, and my spirit asks questions:
"Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he never be kind to us again?
Has his faithful love disappeared forever? Has his promise failed for all time?
Has God forgotten to be kind? Has his anger shut off his mercy?" Selah.
Then I thought, "This is what hurts me most: that the Most High no longer uses his right hand for us."
But I will remember what the LORD has done. I will remember the amazing things you did long ago.
I will think about all your works and consider all your mighty acts.
God, your ways are holy. What god is as great as our God?
You are the God who does amazing things. You show your strength among the nations.
With your strong arm you rescued your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God. The waters saw you and trembled. The deepest seas shook.
The clouds poured down rain. The skies rumbled with thunder. Your arrows of lightning flashed everywhere.
Your thunder roared in the whirlwind. Your lightning lit up the world. The earth trembled and shook.
Your path went through the sea, your way through the mighty waters, but no one saw your footprints.
You led your people like a flock of sheep, using Moses and Aaron.
A thoughtful psalm of Asaph. My people, listen to my teaching. Pay attention to what I say.
I will speak to you in stories. I will explain mysteries from long ago,
things we have heard and know, things our ancestors told us.
We will not hide them from their children. We will tell the next generation about the LORD's praiseworthy acts, his power, and the amazing things he has done.
He made a covenant with Jacob and gave his law to Israel. He commanded our ancestors to teach it to their children,
so the next generation would know it, even children not yet born, and they would get up and tell their own children.
Then they would put their hope in God and not forget what he has done, but would keep his commands.
They would not be like their ancestors, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose hearts were not loyal to God and whose spirits were not faithful to him.
The soldiers of Ephraim were armed with bows, but they turned and ran on the day of battle.
They did not keep God's covenant. They refused to live by his law.
They forgot what he had done, the amazing things he had shown them.
He did miracles in front of their ancestors in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
He split the sea and led them through. He made the water stand up like a wall.
He led them with a cloud by day and with the light of a fire all night.
He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them plenty of water, as if from the deep sea.
He made streams come out of the rock and made water flow down like rivers.
But they kept on sinning against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert.
They deliberately tested God by demanding the food they craved.
They spoke against God. They said, "Can God set a table of food in the wilderness?
It is true that he struck the rock and water gushed out and streams overflowed. But can he also give us bread? Can he supply meat for his people?"
When the LORD heard this, he was very angry. A fire broke out against Jacob, and his anger rose against Israel,
because they did not believe God or trust him to save them.
Yet he gave a command to the skies above and opened the doors of heaven.
He rained down manna for them to eat. He gave them grain from heaven.
People ate the bread of angels. He sent them all the food they could eat.
He made the east wind blow in the sky, and by his power he led out the south wind.
He rained down meat on them like dust, birds as many as the sand on the seashore.
He made them fall inside their camp, all around their tents.
So they ate until they were more than full. He gave them what they craved.
But before they had finished eating what they wanted, while the food was still in their mouths,
God's anger rose against them. He killed their strongest men and struck down the young men of Israel.
In spite of all this, they kept on sinning. They did not believe in his amazing works.
So he ended their days with nothing to show for them, and their years in terror.
Whenever God killed some of them, the rest would look for him. They would turn back and eagerly search for God.
They remembered that God was their rock, that God Most High was the one who rescued them.
But they only flattered him with their mouths and lied to him with their tongues.
Their hearts were not loyal to him. They were not faithful to his covenant.
But he was full of mercy. He forgave their sins and did not destroy them. Many times he held back his anger and did not let all his fury loose.
He remembered that they were only human, a breath of wind that passes and does not come back.
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and made him sad in the desert!
Again and again they tested God and upset the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his power or the day he rescued them from their enemy,
when he did his miraculous signs in Egypt and his wonders in the region of Zoan.
He turned their rivers into blood, so they could not drink from their streams.
He sent swarms of flies that ate them up, and frogs that ruined them.
He gave their crops to grasshoppers, and the work of their hands to locusts.
He destroyed their grapevines with hail and their fig trees with frost.
He handed their cattle over to the hail and their flocks to bolts of lightning.
He let loose on them his burning anger, his fury, rage, and trouble, a group of destroying angels.
He cleared a path for his anger. He did not spare them from death but handed their lives over to disease.
He struck down all the firstborn sons in Egypt, the first of their strength in the tents of Ham.
But he led his own people out like sheep. He guided them like a flock through the wilderness.
He led them safely, so they were not afraid. But the sea swallowed up their enemies.
He brought them to the border of his holy land, to the hill country his right hand had won.
He drove out nations in front of them. He measured out their land as an inheritance for them, and let the tribes of Israel live in their homes.
But they tested and rebelled against God Most High. They did not keep his laws.
They turned away and were unfaithful like their ancestors. They were as unreliable as a crooked bow.
They made him angry with their places of worship on the hills. They made him jealous with their idols.
When God heard them, he was very angry. He completely rejected Israel.
He left his tent at Shiloh, the tent where he had lived among people.
He let the ark of his strength be captured. He handed over his glory to the enemy.
He let his people be killed by the sword. He was very angry with the people who belonged to him.
Fire destroyed their young men, and their young women had no wedding songs.
Their priests were killed by the sword, and their widows could not even cry for them.
Then the Lord woke up as if from sleep, like a warrior shouting after drinking wine.
He beat back his enemies and put them to shame forever.
Then he rejected the family of Joseph. He did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
Instead, he chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his holy place like the high heavens, like the earth that he set firmly in place forever.
He chose his servant David and took him from the sheep pens.
He brought him from caring for the sheep and their lambs to be the shepherd of his people Jacob, of Israel, who belonged to him.
David cared for them with an honest heart and led them with skilful hands.
A psalm of Asaph. God, the nations have invaded the land that belongs to you. They have made your holy temple unclean. They have turned Jerusalem into piles of rubble.
They have left the dead bodies of your servants as food for the birds. They have given the bodies of your faithful people to the wild animals.
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one left to bury them.
Our neighbours insult us. The people around us laugh at us and make fun of us.
How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy keep burning like fire?
Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you, on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.
They have eaten up the people of Jacob and destroyed their homeland.
Do not hold the sins of our ancestors against us. Let your mercy come quickly to meet us, because we are in desperate need.
Help us, God our saviour, for the glory of your name. Rescue us and forgive our sins for the honour of your name.
Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?" Let us see you take revenge on the nations for the blood of your servants.
Listen to the groans of the prisoners. With your great power, save those who have been sentenced to death.
Lord, pay back our neighbours seven times over for the insults they have thrown at you.
Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever. We will praise you for all generations.

For the music director. To the tune "The Lilies of the Covenant." A psalm of Asaph. Listen to us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock. You sit on your throne above the cherubim. Shine out
in front of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Wake up your power! Come and save us!
God, bring us back. Let your face shine on us, and we will be saved.
LORD God of Armies, how long will you be angry with your people's prayers?
You have fed them with tears as their bread. You have made them drink bowls full of tears.
You have made us something our neighbours fight over. Our enemies laugh at us.
God of Armies, bring us back. Let your face shine on us, and we will be saved.
You brought a grapevine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground for it. It put down deep roots and filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains. Its branches were like mighty cedar trees.
It spread its branches out to the Mediterranean Sea and its shoots to the Euphrates River.
Why have you broken down its walls so that everyone who passes by picks its grapes?
Wild pigs from the forest ruin it. Wild animals from the fields feed on it.
God of Armies, please come back! Look down from heaven and see. Take care of this vine,
the root your right hand planted, the son you made strong for yourself.
It has been cut down and burned with fire. Your people are dying because of your angry warning.
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, the son of man you made strong for yourself.
Then we will not turn away from you. Give us new life, and we will call on your name.
LORD God of Armies, bring us back. Let your face shine on us, and we will be saved.
For the music director. On an instrument from Gath. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God, our strength! Shout with joy to the God of Jacob!
Start the music! Play the tambourine and the sweet lyre and harp.
Blow the ram's horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on our festival day.
This is a law for Israel, a rule from the God of Jacob.
He made it a law for the people of Joseph when he went out against the land of Egypt. I heard a voice I did not know say:
"I took the load off their shoulders. Their hands were set free from carrying baskets.
You called out in your trouble, and I rescued you. I answered you from the thundercloud. I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
Listen, my people, and I will warn you. Israel, if only you would listen to me!
You must not have any foreign god among you. You must not bow down to any strange god.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
But my people would not listen to me. Israel did not want me.
So I let them follow their own stubborn hearts and live by their own plans.
If only my people would listen to me! If only Israel would follow my ways!
I would quickly defeat their enemies and turn my hand against those who attack them.
Those who hate the LORD would bow down to him in fear, and their punishment would last forever.
But I would feed you with the finest wheat. I would satisfy you with honey from the rock."
A psalm of Asaph. God takes his place in the great meeting. He gives judgment among the "gods":
"How long will you judge unfairly and take the side of the wicked? Selah.
Defend the weak, the poor, and those with no father. Protect the rights of the poor and the crushed.
Rescue the weak and needy. Save them from the power of the wicked."
They know nothing. They understand nothing. They walk around in the dark, while all the foundations of the earth are shaking.
I said, "You are gods. All of you are sons of the Most High.
But you will die like ordinary people. You will fall like any other ruler."
Get up, God, and judge the earth, because all the nations belong to you.
A song. A psalm of Asaph. God, do not stay silent. Do not be quiet. Do not stay still, God.
Look, your enemies are in an uproar. Those who hate you are raising their heads proudly.
They make clever plans against your people. They plot against those you treasure.
They say, "Come, let's wipe them out as a nation, so the name of Israel will never be remembered again."
They have agreed on a plan together. They have joined forces against you:
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia and the people of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them to give strength to the descendants of Lot. Selah.
Do to them what you did to Midian, and to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.
They were destroyed at Endor, and their bodies became like manure on the ground.
Make their important men like Oreb and Zeeb. Make all their leaders like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, "Let's take for ourselves the pasturelands of God."
My God, make them like tumbleweeds, like chaff blown by the wind.
As fire burns a forest and as a flame sets the mountains on fire,
chase them with your storm. Terrify them with your hurricane.
Cover their faces with shame, so they will look for your name, LORD.
Let them be put to shame and terrified forever. Let them die in disgrace.
Then they will know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth.
For the music director. On an instrument from Gath. A psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely is the place where you live, LORD of Armies!
I long and even faint with longing for the courtyards of the LORD. My heart and my whole body cry out for the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow has a nest for herself where she can have her young, near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King and my God.
Happy are those who live in your house. They are always praising you. Selah.
Happy are those whose strength comes from you, whose hearts are set on travelling to your house.
As they pass through the Valley of Tears, they make it a place of springs. The autumn rains cover it with pools of blessing.
They grow stronger and stronger, and each of them appears in front of God in Zion.
LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer. Listen, God of Jacob. Selah.
God, our shield, look with kindness on the face of your anointed king.
One day in your courtyards is better than a thousand days anywhere else. I would rather stand at the door of the house of my God than live in the tents of the wicked.
The LORD God is our sun and our shield. The LORD gives kindness and honour. He does not hold back any good thing from those who live blameless lives.
LORD of Armies, happy is the person who trusts in you.
For the music director. A psalm of the sons of Korah. LORD, you were kind to your land. You made the people of Jacob successful again.
You forgave the sins of your people. You covered all their sin. Selah.
You took back all your anger. You turned away from your burning rage.
God our saviour, bring us back again. Put an end to your anger against us.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will your anger go on for all generations?
Won't you give us new life again, so your people can be glad because of you?
LORD, show us your faithful love. Give us your saving help.
I will listen to what God the LORD says. He promises peace to his people, his faithful ones. But they must not go back to their foolish ways.
His saving help is surely near those who respect him, so that his glory may live in our land.
Faithful love and truth meet together. Goodness and peace kiss each other.
Truth springs up from the earth, and goodness looks down from heaven.
The LORD will give what is good, and our land will produce its harvest.
Goodness goes ahead of him and prepares the way for his steps.
A prayer of David. LORD, listen to me and answer me, because I am poor and needy.
Protect my life, because I am faithful to you. You are my God. Save me, your servant, who trusts in you.
Be kind to me, Lord, because I call to you all day long.
Fill me, your servant, with joy, because, Lord, I give my life to you.
Lord, you are good and ready to forgive. You are full of faithful love for all who call to you.
LORD, hear my prayer. Listen to my cry for mercy.
When I am in trouble I will call to you, because you will answer me.
Lord, there is no one like you among the gods. No one can do what you do.
All the nations you have made will come and bow down in front of you, Lord. They will honour your name.
You are great and you do amazing things. You alone are God.
LORD, teach me your way, and I will live by your truth. Give me a heart that is completely devoted to respecting your name.
Lord my God, I will praise you with all my heart. I will honour your name forever.
Your faithful love for me is great. You have rescued me from the depths of the grave.
God, proud people are attacking me. A gang of violent people is trying to kill me. They do not care about you.
But you, Lord, are a God who is full of mercy and kindness. You are slow to get angry, and full of faithful love and truth.
Turn to me and be kind to me! Give your strength to me, your servant. Save me, the son of your servant.
Show me a sign of your goodness, so those who hate me will see it and be ashamed. LORD, you have helped me and comforted me.
A psalm of the sons of Korah. A song. The LORD built his city on the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the other places where the people of Jacob live.
City of God, wonderful things are said about you. Selah.
God says, "I will list Rahab and Babylon among those who know me. Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia too. People will say, 'This one was born in Zion.'"
It will be said about Zion, "This one and that one were born there." The Most High himself will make it strong.
When the LORD writes down the names of the nations, he will note, "This one was born there." Selah.
Those who sing and those who dance will say, "All my springs of joy are in you."

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the music director. To the tune "The Suffering of Affliction." A thoughtful psalm of Heman the Ezrahite. LORD, the God who saves me, I cry out to you day and night.
Let my prayer come to you. Turn your ear to my cry.
My life is full of troubles. I am close to the grave.
I am counted among those going down to the pit. I am like a man with no strength left.
I have been left among the dead, like those killed in battle who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more, who are cut off from your care.
You have put me in the deepest pit, in the darkest depths.
Your anger lies heavy on me. You have crushed me with all your waves. Selah.
