I remember the old days. I think about everything you have done. I consider what your hands have made.
I lift up my hands to you. I am thirsty for you, like dry land. Selah.
Answer me quickly, LORD. My spirit is failing. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the grave.
Let me hear about your faithful love every morning, because I trust in you. Show me the way I should go, because I give my life to you.
LORD, rescue me from my enemies. I run to you to hide me.
Teach me to do what you want, because you are my God. May your good Spirit lead me on level ground.
LORD, for the honour of your name, keep me alive. Because you do what is right, bring me out of trouble.
Because of your faithful love, silence my enemies. Destroy all those who attack me, because I am your servant.
Of David. Praise the LORD, my rock, who trains my hands for war and my fingers for battle.
He is my faithful love and my fortress, my high tower and my rescuer, my shield where I find safety. He brings people under my rule.
LORD, what are human beings that you care about them? What is a mere person that you think about them?
People are like a breath. Their days are like a passing shadow.
Open your heavens, LORD, and come down. Touch the mountains so they smoke.
Send lightning and scatter the enemy. Shoot your arrows and make them run.
Reach down your hand from above. Rescue me and save me from the deep waters, from the power of foreigners,
whose mouths tell lies and whose right hands make false promises.
God, I will sing a new song to you. I will make music to you on the ten-stringed lyre.
You are the one who gives victory to kings, who rescues your servant David from the deadly sword.
Rescue me and save me from the power of foreigners, whose mouths tell lies and whose right hands make false promises.
Then our sons will grow up like healthy young plants, and our daughters will be like beautifully carved pillars in a palace.
Our barns will be full of every kind of food. Our sheep will increase by thousands, even tens of thousands, in our fields.
Our oxen will pull heavy loads. No enemy will break through our walls. No one will be taken captive, and there will be no cries of distress in our streets.
Happy are the people who have these blessings. Happy are the people whose God is the LORD.
A psalm of praise. Of David. I will honour you, my God and King. I will praise your name forever and ever.
I will praise you every day. I will honour your name forever and ever.
The LORD is great and deserves great praise! No one can measure how great he is.
Parents will praise your works to their children. They will tell about your mighty acts.
I will think about your glorious majesty and your amazing works.
People will talk about the power of your awesome acts, and I will tell about your greatness.
They will celebrate your great goodness and sing joyfully about how you do what is right.
The LORD is kind and full of mercy. He is slow to get angry and full of faithful love.
The LORD is good to everyone. He shows mercy to everything he has made.
Everything you have made will thank you, LORD. Your faithful people will praise you.
They will talk about the glory of your kingdom and tell about your power,
so that everyone will know about your mighty acts and the glorious majesty of your kingdom.
Your kingdom lasts forever. You rule through all generations. The LORD keeps all his promises and is loving in everything he does.
The LORD holds up all who fall. He lifts up all who are bowed down.
Everyone looks to you with hope, and you give them their food at the right time.
You open your hand and satisfy the needs of every living thing.
The LORD is right in everything he does and kind in all his works.
The LORD is near to everyone who calls on him, to everyone who calls on him sincerely.
He gives those who respect him what they want. He hears their cry and saves them.
The LORD watches over everyone who loves him, but he will destroy all the wicked.
My mouth will praise the LORD. Let every living thing praise his holy name forever and ever.
Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, my soul.
I will praise the LORD all my life. I will sing praises to my God as long as I live.
Do not put your trust in rulers, in mere humans who cannot save you.
When their breath leaves them, they go back to the ground. On that very day all their plans come to nothing.
Happy are those whose helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD their God.
He made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them. He stays faithful forever.
He gives justice to those who are crushed and food to those who are hungry. The LORD sets prisoners free.
The LORD opens the eyes of blind people. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down. The LORD loves good people.
The LORD watches over foreigners. He takes care of children with no father and widows, but he ruins the plans of the wicked.
The LORD will rule forever. Your God, Zion, will rule for all generations. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! It is good to sing praises to our God. It is pleasant and right to praise him.
The LORD is rebuilding Jerusalem. He is bringing back the scattered people of Israel.
He heals those whose hearts are broken and bandages their wounds.
He counts the stars and calls each one by name.
Our Lord is great and very powerful. There is no limit to his understanding.
The LORD lifts up humble people, but he throws the wicked to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanks. Make music to our God on the harp.
He covers the sky with clouds. He sends rain to the earth and makes grass grow on the hills.
He gives food to the cattle and to the young ravens when they call.
He is not impressed by the strength of a horse or the power of a man's legs.
The LORD is pleased with those who respect him, with those who hope in his faithful love.
Praise the LORD, Jerusalem! Praise your God, Zion!
He makes the bars of your gates strong. He blesses your people inside your walls.
He brings peace to your borders. He fills you with the finest wheat.
He sends his command to the earth. His word runs quickly.
He spreads snow like wool and scatters frost like ashes.
He throws down hail like pebbles. Who can stand his freezing cold?
Then he sends his word and melts them. He makes his wind blow, and the waters flow.
He has made his word known to Jacob, his laws and rules to Israel.
He has not done this for any other nation. They do not know his rules. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from the heavens! Praise him in the heights above!
Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his armies of heaven!
Praise him, sun and moon! Praise him, all you shining stars!
Praise him, highest heavens, and you waters above the skies.
Let them praise the name of the LORD, because he gave the command and they were created.
He set them in place forever and ever. He gave a law that will never change.
Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all the deep oceans,
lightning and hail, snow and clouds, and stormy winds that do what he says,
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
wild animals and all cattle, small creatures and flying birds,
kings of the earth and all nations, rulers and all leaders of the earth,
young men and young women, old people and children.
Let them praise the name of the LORD, because his name alone is great. His glory is above the earth and the heavens.
He has made his people strong. He is praised by all his faithful people, the people of Israel, who are close to his heart. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Sing a new song to the LORD. Praise him in the gathering of his faithful people.
Let Israel be glad because of their Maker. Let the people of Zion be full of joy because of their King.
Let them praise his name with dancing. Let them make music to him with tambourine and harp.
The LORD takes delight in his people. He crowns humble people with victory.
Let his faithful people celebrate his glory. Let them sing for joy on their beds.
Let the praises of God be in their mouths and a two-edged sword in their hands,
to punish the nations and bring judgment on the peoples,
to tie up their kings with chains and their leaders with iron shackles,
to carry out the judgment written against them. This is the honour of all his faithful people. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Praise God in his holy place! Praise him in his mighty heavens!
Praise him for his mighty acts! Praise him for his amazing greatness!
Praise him with the sound of the trumpet! Praise him with harp and lyre!
Praise him with tambourine and dancing! Praise him with stringed instruments and flute!
Praise him with loud cymbals! Praise him with crashing cymbals!
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!
Prov: These are the wise sayings of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel.
They will help you gain wisdom and learn from correction. They will help you understand wise words.
They will teach you to live wisely and to do what is right, fair, and honest.
They give good sense to simple people, and knowledge and good judgment to young people.
Let wise people listen and learn even more. Let people with understanding get good advice.
Then they will understand wise sayings and stories, the words and riddles of wise people.
Respect for the LORD is where knowledge begins, but fools hate wisdom and correction.
My son, listen to your father's teaching. Do not turn away from your mother's instruction.
Their teaching will be like a beautiful crown on your head and a necklace around your neck.
My son, if sinners try to tempt you, do not give in to them.
They may say, "Come with us. Let's hide and wait to kill someone. Let's ambush some innocent person just for fun.
Let's swallow them alive, like the grave swallows people, whole, like those who go down into the pit.
We will get all kinds of valuable things. We will fill our houses with stolen goods.
Join us, and we will all share the money equally."
My son, do not go along with them. Stay far away from their paths.
Their feet run to do evil. They hurry to kill people.
It is useless to spread a net where a bird can see it,
but these people set a trap for themselves. They are waiting to take their own lives.
That is what happens to everyone who is greedy for money they did not earn. Their greed takes away their own lives.
Wisdom shouts out in the street. She raises her voice in the public squares.
She calls out on the noisy street corners. At the city gates she makes her speech:
"How long will you simple people love being simple? How long will mockers enjoy making fun of others, and fools hate knowledge?
Listen to my warning and turn back. I will pour out my thoughts to you. I will make my words known to you.
I called you, but you refused to listen. I reached out my hand, but no one paid attention.
You ignored all my advice and did not want my warnings.
So I will laugh when disaster comes to you. I will make fun of you when trouble strikes,
when trouble hits you like a storm, when disaster comes on you like a whirlwind, when distress and pain overwhelm you.
Then they will call to me, but I will not answer. They will look hard for me, but they will not find me,
because they hated knowledge and did not choose to respect the LORD.
They did not want my advice. They rejected all my warnings.
So they will eat the fruit of the way they lived. They will be filled with the results of their own plans.
Simple people turn away from wisdom, and it kills them. Fools are careless, and it destroys them.
But whoever listens to me will live in safety. They will be at ease, with no fear of harm."
My son, accept what I say, and store up my commands inside you.
Turn your ear to wisdom, and set your heart on understanding.
Call out for good judgment. Cry out loud for understanding.
Look for wisdom as you would look for silver. Search for it as you would search for hidden treasure.
Then you will understand what it means to respect the LORD, and you will find the knowledge of God.
The LORD gives wisdom. Knowledge and understanding come from his mouth.
He stores up sound wisdom for honest people. He is a shield to those who live without blame.
He guards the paths of those who are fair, and he protects the way of his faithful people.
Then you will understand what is right, fair, and honest, and every good path.
Wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to you.
Good sense will watch over you. Understanding will protect you.
Wisdom will save you from the ways of evil people, from people whose words are twisted,
who leave the straight paths to walk in dark ways,
who enjoy doing wrong and take delight in twisted evil,
whose paths are crooked and whose ways are dishonest.
Wisdom will save you from the woman who is unfaithful, from the woman who is a stranger, with her flattering words,
who has left the husband of her youth and forgotten the covenant she made before her God.
Her house leads down to death. Her paths lead to the spirits of the dead.
No one who goes to her comes back. They never reach the paths of life again.
So follow the ways of good people, and stay on the paths of those who do right.
Honest people will live in the land. Those who are blameless will stay in it.
But the wicked will be removed from the land. Those who are unfaithful will be pulled out of it.
My son, do not forget my teaching. Keep my commands in your heart,
because they will give you a long life, many years, and peace.
Never let kindness and faithfulness leave you. Tie them around your neck. Write them on your heart.
Then you will win favour and a good name with God and with people.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart. Do not depend on your own understanding.
In everything you do, remember him, and he will make your paths straight.
Do not think you are so wise. Respect the LORD and turn away from evil.
This will bring health to your body and strength to your bones.
Honour the LORD with your wealth, with the first and best part of everything you produce.
Then your barns will be full to overflowing, and your barrels will overflow with new wine.
My son, do not refuse the LORD's discipline. Do not be upset when he corrects you,
because the LORD corrects those he loves, just as a father corrects the son he delights in.
Happy is the person who finds wisdom, the person who gains understanding.
Wisdom is more valuable than silver. It pays better than gold.
She is worth more than rubies. Nothing you could want compares with her.
In her right hand she holds a long life. In her left hand she holds riches and honour.
Her ways are pleasant ways. All her paths lead to peace.
She is a tree of life to those who hold on to her. Those who hold her close will be happy.
The LORD used wisdom to lay the foundations of the earth. He used understanding to set the skies in place.
By his knowledge the deep waters burst open, and the clouds drop dew.
My son, do not let wisdom and good sense out of your sight. Hold on to them,
and they will give you life and be like a beautiful necklace around your neck.
Then you will walk safely on your way, and your foot will not trip.
When you lie down, you will not be afraid. When you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.
Do not be afraid of sudden disaster or of the ruin that comes on the wicked,
because the LORD will be your confidence. He will keep your foot from being caught in a trap.
Do not hold back good from those who deserve it when you are able to help.
Do not say to your neighbour, "Come back later. I will give it to you tomorrow," when you have it with you now.
Do not plan to harm your neighbour, who lives trustingly near you.
Do not argue with someone for no reason when they have done you no harm.
Do not be jealous of violent people, and do not copy any of their ways.
The LORD hates people who are twisted, but he is a close friend to honest people.
The LORD's curse is on the house of the wicked, but he blesses the home of good people.
He mocks those who mock, but he is kind to humble people.
Wise people will receive honour, but fools will only get shame.
Listen, my children, to your father's teaching. Pay attention and gain understanding.
I am giving you good teaching. Do not turn away from what I tell you.
When I was a boy in my father's house, still young and my mother's only child,
my father taught me. He said, "Hold on to my words with all your heart. Keep my commands, and you will live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. Do not forget my words or turn away from them.
Do not leave wisdom, and she will protect you. Love her, and she will watch over you.
Wisdom is the most important thing. So get wisdom. Even if it costs everything you have, get understanding.
Value wisdom highly, and she will lift you up. Hold her close, and she will bring you honour.
She will put a beautiful crown on your head. She will give you a glorious crown."
Listen, my son, and accept what I say. Then you will live for many years.
I have taught you the way of wisdom. I have led you along straight paths.
When you walk, nothing will hold you back. When you run, you will not trip.
Hold on tightly to what you have been taught. Do not let it go. Guard it well, because it is your life.
Do not set foot on the path of the wicked. Do not walk in the way of evil people.
Stay away from it. Do not go on it. Turn away from it and keep going.
Evil people cannot sleep until they have done something wrong. They lose sleep until they make someone fall.
They eat the bread of evil and drink the wine of violence.
The path of good people is like the first light of dawn. It shines brighter and brighter until it is full daylight.
But the way of the wicked is like deep darkness. They do not know what makes them trip.
My son, pay attention to what I say. Listen closely to my words.
Do not let them out of your sight. Keep them deep in your heart.
They are life to those who find them and health to their whole body.
Above everything else, guard your heart, because everything you do flows from it.
Keep your mouth from twisted talk. Keep lying lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead. Keep your gaze fixed on what is in front of you.
Make a level path for your feet, and all your ways will be secure.
Do not turn to the right or to the left. Keep your feet away from evil.
My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Listen carefully to what I understand,
so you will keep good judgment and your lips will hold on to knowledge.
The lips of an unfaithful woman drip with honey. Her words are smoother than oil.
But in the end she is as bitter as poison, as sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to the grave.
She does not think about the path of life. Her ways wander, and she does not even know it.
So now, my sons, listen to me. Do not turn away from what I say.
Keep far away from her. Do not go near the door of her house.
If you do, you will lose your honour to others and give the best years of your life to someone cruel.
Strangers will enjoy your wealth, and what you worked for will go to someone else's house.
At the end of your life you will groan, when your body is worn out and wasted away.
You will say, "How I hated being taught! How my heart hated being corrected!
I would not listen to my teachers or pay attention to those who taught me.
Now I am almost completely ruined, in front of the whole community."
Drink water from your own well, fresh water from your own spring.
Should your springs overflow into the streets, your streams into the public squares?
Let them belong to you alone, not shared with strangers.
May your spring be blessed. Enjoy the wife you married when you were young.
She is like a loving deer, a graceful doe. May her breasts always satisfy you. May you always be captivated by her love.
My son, why be captivated by an unfaithful woman? Why hold another man's wife in your arms?
The LORD sees everything people do. He watches all their paths.
The evil things the wicked do will trap them. The ropes of their own sin will hold them tight.
They will die because they would not be taught. Their great foolishness will lead them astray.
My son, have you promised to pay your neighbour's debt? Have you shaken hands to guarantee a stranger's loan?
Then you are trapped by what you said. You are caught by your own words.
So do this, my son, to free yourself, because you are in your neighbour's power. Go and humble yourself. Keep begging your neighbour to let you go.
Do not let your eyes sleep. Do not even let your eyelids close.
Free yourself like a deer escaping from the hunter, like a bird escaping from the trap.
Go and look at the ant, you lazy person. Watch how it lives, and become wise.
It has no leader, no boss, and no ruler,
yet it gathers its food in summer and stores it up at harvest time.
How long will you lie there, you lazy person? When will you get up from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little rest, a little folding of the hands to rest,
and poverty will come on you like a robber, and need will attack you like an armed soldier.
A worthless and evil person goes around telling lies.
He winks with his eyes, signals with his feet, and points with his fingers.
His heart is twisted, and he is always planning evil. He is always stirring up trouble.
So disaster will come on him suddenly. In a moment he will be broken, and nothing can heal him.
There are six things the LORD hates, seven things he cannot stand:
proud eyes, a lying tongue, hands that kill innocent people,
a heart that plans evil, feet that are quick to run to do wrong,
a witness who tells lies, and a person who stirs up trouble among family members.
My son, keep your father's commands. Do not turn away from your mother's teaching.
Always keep them in your heart. Tie them around your neck.
When you walk, they will guide you. When you sleep, they will watch over you. When you wake up, they will speak to you.
These commands are a lamp, and this teaching is a light. The correction they give shows you the way to live.
They will keep you away from an immoral woman, from the smooth talk of another man's wife.
Do not long in your heart for her beauty. Do not let her catch you with her eyes.
A prostitute can be had for a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts for your very life.
Can a man carry fire in his lap without burning his clothes?
Can he walk on hot coals without burning his feet?
It is the same with a man who sleeps with his neighbour's wife. No one who touches her will escape punishment.
People do not hate a thief if he steals because he is starving and needs food.
But if he is caught, he must pay back seven times what he stole, even if it costs everything in his house.
But a man who commits adultery has no sense. He destroys himself.
He will be beaten and disgraced. His shame will never be wiped away.
Jealousy makes a husband furious. He will show no mercy when he takes revenge.
He will not accept any payment. He will not be satisfied, no matter how many gifts you give him.
My son, hold on to my words. Store up my commands inside you.
Keep my commands, and you will live. Guard my teaching as you would guard your own eyes.
Tie them on your fingers. Write them on your heart.
Say to wisdom, "You are my sister." Call understanding your close relative.
They will keep you away from the unfaithful woman, from the stranger with her flattering words.
Once I was looking out through the window of my house.
Among the simple people, I noticed a young man who had no sense.
He was going down the street near the corner where she lived, walking toward her house.
It was getting dark, in the evening, as the night grew dark.
Then a woman came out to meet him. She was dressed like a prostitute and had a sly plan.
She was loud and wild. She never stayed at home.
Sometimes she was in the streets, sometimes in the squares, waiting on every corner.
She grabbed him and kissed him. With a bold face she said to him,
"I have meat from my peace offerings at home. Today I kept my promises.
So I came out to meet you. I was looking for you, and now I have found you!
I have covered my bed with coloured sheets of fine linen from Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let's make love all night until morning. Let's enjoy each other's love.
My husband is not at home. He has gone on a long trip.
He took a bag of money with him. He will not be home until the full moon."
She led him astray with her persuasive words. She tempted him with her smooth talk.
He followed her right away, like an ox going to be killed, like a fool walking into a trap,
until an arrow pierces his liver. He is like a bird rushing into a trap, not knowing it will cost him his life.
So now, my sons, listen to me. Pay attention to what I say.
Do not let your heart turn toward her ways. Do not wander onto her paths.
She has brought down many victims. A great army has been killed by her.
Her house is the road to the grave. It leads down to the rooms of death.
Wisdom is calling out! Understanding is raising her voice!
She stands on the hilltops along the road, where the paths meet.
Beside the gates leading into the city, at the entrances, she cries out:
"I am calling to you, all people! I am speaking to everyone.
You simple people, learn good sense! You fools, gain understanding!
Listen, because I have important things to say. Everything I say is right.
My mouth speaks the truth. My lips hate what is evil.
Everything I say is right. None of it is crooked or twisted.
It is all clear to those who understand, and right to those who have knowledge.
Choose my teaching instead of silver, and knowledge instead of pure gold.
Wisdom is worth more than rubies. Nothing you could want compares with her.
I, wisdom, live together with good sense. I have knowledge and good judgment.
To respect the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, boasting, evil ways, and twisted words.
Good advice and sound wisdom belong to me. I have understanding and power.
Through me kings rule, and rulers make fair laws.
Through me princes govern, and all the nobles who rule the earth fairly.
I love those who love me. Those who look for me will find me.
Riches and honour are with me, lasting wealth and success.
What I give is better than the finest gold. What I produce is better than pure silver.
I walk on the path of what is right, along the paths of justice.
I give wealth to those who love me, and I fill their storerooms.
The LORD had me at the very beginning of his work, before he did anything else long ago.
I was formed long ages ago, at the very beginning, before the earth was made.
I was born before the deep oceans existed, before there were springs full of water.
I was born before the mountains were set in place, before the hills,
before he made the earth and its fields, or even the first grains of dust in the world.
I was there when he set the skies in place, when he marked the horizon on the face of the deep sea,
when he put the clouds above and made the springs of the deep flow strongly,
when he set the limits of the sea so the waters would not go beyond his command, when he marked out the foundations of the earth.
I was the skilled worker at his side. I was his delight day after day, always happy in his presence,
happy with the whole world he made, and delighted with the human race.
So now, my children, listen to me. Happy are those who follow my ways.
Listen to my teaching and be wise. Do not ignore it.
Happy is the person who listens to me, watching every day at my gates, waiting beside my doorway.
Whoever finds me finds life and receives kindness from the LORD.
But whoever misses me harms himself. Everyone who hates me loves death."
Wisdom has built her house. She has carved its seven pillars.
She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine. She has set her table.
She has sent out her servant girls, and she calls from the highest places in the city:
"Let all who are simple come in here!" To those who have no sense she says,
"Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
Leave your simple ways and live. Walk on the path of understanding."
If you correct a mocker, you will get insulted. If you correct a wicked person, you will get hurt.
Do not correct mockers, or they will hate you. Correct wise people, and they will love you.
Teach wise people, and they will become even wiser. Teach good people, and they will learn even more.
Respect for the LORD is where wisdom begins. Knowing the Holy One is understanding.
Through wisdom you will live longer. Years will be added to your life.
If you are wise, you are the one who benefits. If you mock, you alone will suffer.
Foolishness is like a loud woman. She has no self-control and knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat at the highest point of the city,
calling out to people walking by, who are minding their own business:
"Let all who are simple come in here!" To those who have no sense she says,
"Stolen water is sweet. Food eaten in secret tastes good!"
But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are deep in the grave.
These are the wise sayings of Solomon. A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son brings sorrow to his mother.
Treasure gained by evil does no good, but doing what is right saves people from death.
The LORD does not let good people go hungry, but he refuses to give the wicked what they crave.
Lazy hands make a person poor, but hard-working hands bring wealth.
A son who gathers crops in summer is wise, but a son who sleeps during harvest brings shame.
Blessings crown the heads of good people, but the mouths of the wicked hide violence.
Good people are remembered as a blessing, but the names of the wicked will rot away.
Wise people accept instructions, but a fool who talks too much will fall.
Whoever lives honestly walks safely, but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.
Whoever winks at evil causes trouble, and a fool who talks too much will fall.
The words of good people are a fountain of life, but the mouths of the wicked hide violence.
Hatred stirs up fights, but love covers over every wrong.
Wisdom is found on the lips of people with understanding, but a rod is for the back of those who have no sense.
Wise people store up knowledge, but the mouths of fools invite ruin.
Rich people's wealth is like a strong city to them, but poverty ruins poor people.
The pay of good people leads to life, but the earnings of the wicked lead to sin.
Whoever accepts correction is on the path to life, but whoever ignores warnings leads others astray.
Whoever hides hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads lies is a fool.
When there are too many words, sin is not far away, but whoever controls their tongue is wise.
The words of good people are like pure silver, but the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The words of good people feed many, but fools die because they have no sense.
The LORD's blessing makes people rich, and he adds no trouble to it.
A fool enjoys doing evil, but a person with understanding enjoys wisdom.
What the wicked fear will happen to them, but good people will get what they want.
When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone, but good people stand firm forever.
A lazy person is to those who send him like vinegar to the teeth or smoke to the eyes.
Respect for the LORD adds years to your life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
Good people can look forward to joy, but the hopes of the wicked come to nothing.
The way of the LORD is a safe place for honest people, but it brings ruin to those who do evil.
Good people will never be moved, but the wicked will not stay in the land.
The mouths of good people speak wisdom, but a twisted tongue will be cut off.
Good people know the right thing to say, but the wicked say only twisted things.
The LORD hates dishonest scales, but he is pleased with honest weights.
When pride comes, shame follows, but wisdom comes with humility.
Honest people are guided by their honesty, but unfaithful people are destroyed by their dishonesty.
Riches are useless on the day of God's anger, but doing what is right saves people from death.
The goodness of blameless people makes their path straight, but the wicked fall because of their own evil.
The goodness of honest people saves them, but unfaithful people are trapped by their own evil desires.
When wicked people die, their hope dies with them. Everything they expected from their power comes to nothing.
Good people are rescued from trouble, and the wicked get into it instead.
Godless people destroy their neighbours with their words, but good people are rescued by their knowledge.
When things go well for good people, the city celebrates. When the wicked die, there are shouts of joy.
A city is made great by the blessing of honest people, but it is destroyed by the words of the wicked.
Whoever looks down on their neighbour has no sense, but a person with understanding keeps quiet.
A gossip tells secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps a secret.
Without wise leadership a nation falls, but with many advisers there is victory.
Whoever guarantees a stranger's debt will surely suffer, but whoever refuses to make such promises is safe.
A kind woman gains respect, but violent men gain only riches.
Kind people do themselves good, but cruel people bring trouble on themselves.
Wicked people earn wages that do not last, but those who plant goodness receive a sure reward.
Whoever is truly good finds life, but whoever chases evil finds death.
The LORD hates people with twisted hearts, but he is pleased with those who live blameless lives.
You can be sure of this: evil people will not go unpunished, but the children of good people will be rescued.
A beautiful woman who has no good sense is like a gold ring in a pig's nose.
What good people want ends only in good, but what the wicked hope for ends in anger.
One person gives freely and gets even richer. Another holds back what he should give, and ends up poor.
A generous person will do well. Whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.
People curse the person who holds back grain to sell at a higher price, but they bless the one who sells it.
Whoever looks for good finds kindness, but whoever looks for evil will find it.
Whoever trusts in riches will fall, but good people will grow like green leaves.
Whoever brings trouble on their family will inherit only wind. A fool will be a servant to the wise.
The fruit of good people is a tree of life, and whoever is wise wins people over.
If good people are paid back on earth for what they do, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but whoever hates being corrected is stupid.
The LORD is pleased with a good person, but he condemns someone who plans evil.
No one can be made secure by doing evil, but the roots of good people cannot be pulled up.
A good wife is like a crown to her husband, but a wife who brings shame is like a disease in his bones.
The plans of good people are fair, but the advice of the wicked is full of lies.
The words of the wicked are a trap to kill people, but the words of honest people rescue them.
The wicked are destroyed and gone, but the family of good people stands firm.
People are praised for their wisdom, but those with twisted minds are looked down on.
It is better to be unimportant and have a servant than to act important and have no food.
Good people take care of their animals, but even the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel.
Whoever works their land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases dreams has no sense.
The wicked want what evil people have stolen, but the roots of good people produce fruit.
Evil people are trapped by their sinful words, but good people escape from trouble.
People are filled with good things by what they say, and the work of their hands brings them a reward.
Fools think their own way is right, but wise people listen to advice.
Fools show their anger right away, but sensible people ignore an insult.
An honest witness tells the truth, but a false witness tells lies.
Careless words cut like a sword, but the words of wise people bring healing.
Truthful words last forever, but lies last only a moment.
There are lies in the hearts of those who plan evil, but those who work for peace are full of joy.
No real harm comes to good people, but the wicked are full of trouble.
The LORD hates lying lips, but he is pleased with people who are truthful.
Sensible people keep their knowledge to themselves, but fools announce their foolishness.
Hard-working people will rule, but lazy people will end up as slaves.
Worry weighs a person down, but a kind word cheers them up.
Good people are careful about choosing friends, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
Lazy people do not even cook what they have hunted, but hard-working people value what they have.
The path of goodness leads to life. On that path there is no death.
A wise son listens to his father's teaching, but a mocker will not listen to correction.
People enjoy good things because of what they say, but unfaithful people are hungry for violence.
Whoever guards their mouth protects their life, but whoever talks too much will be ruined.
Lazy people want things but get nothing, but hard-working people get everything they want.
Good people hate lies, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
Goodness protects people who live honestly, but evil brings sinners down.
Some people pretend to be rich but have nothing. Others pretend to be poor but have great wealth.
A rich person may have to pay a ransom for their life, but a poor person never even hears a threat.
The light of good people shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked goes out.
Pride only leads to arguments, but wisdom is found in those who take advice.
Money gained dishonestly disappears, but whoever earns money little by little makes it grow.
Hope that is put off makes the heart sick, but a wish that comes true is like a tree of life.
Whoever refuses to be taught will pay for it, but whoever respects a command will be rewarded.
The teaching of wise people is a fountain of life. It helps people escape the traps of death.
Good understanding wins favour, but the way of unfaithful people is hard.
Sensible people act with knowledge, but fools show off their foolishness.
A wicked messenger gets into trouble, but a trustworthy messenger brings healing.
Whoever refuses correction will end up poor and ashamed, but whoever accepts correction will be honoured.
A wish that comes true is sweet, but fools hate to turn away from evil.
Walk with wise people and you will become wise, but a friend of fools will get hurt.
Trouble chases sinners, but good things reward good people.
Good people leave an inheritance for their grandchildren, but a sinner's wealth is stored up for good people.
A poor person's field may produce plenty of food, but injustice sweeps it away.
Whoever refuses to discipline their son hates him, but whoever loves him is careful to correct him.
Good people have enough to eat, but the stomachs of the wicked stay hungry.
A wise woman builds up her home, but a foolish woman tears hers down with her own hands.
Whoever lives honestly respects the LORD, but whoever follows crooked ways looks down on him.
A fool's proud talk brings a beating on his back, but the words of wise people protect them.
Where there are no oxen, the feeding trough is empty, but a big harvest comes from the strength of an ox.
An honest witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
A mocker looks for wisdom and does not find it, but knowledge comes easily to someone with understanding.
Stay away from a foolish person, because you will not find knowledge in what they say.
Sensible people are wise because they think about where they are going, but fools are foolish because they fool themselves.
Fools laugh at making things right after they sin, but honest people want to please each other.
Each heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of honest people will do well.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
Even while laughing, a heart can be sad, and joy can end in sorrow.
Unfaithful people will be paid back for their ways, and good people will be rewarded for theirs.
Simple people believe anything, but sensible people think carefully about every step.
Wise people are careful and turn away from evil, but fools are hot-headed and careless.
People with quick tempers do foolish things, and people who plot evil are hated.
Simple people end up with foolishness, but sensible people are crowned with knowledge.
Evil people will bow down in front of good people, and the wicked at the gates of those who do right.
Poor people are avoided even by their neighbours, but rich people have many friends.
Whoever looks down on their neighbour sins, but whoever is kind to the poor is blessed.
Don't those who plan evil go astray? But those who plan good find love and faithfulness.
All hard work brings a profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
The wealth of wise people is their crown, but the foolishness of fools brings only more foolishness.
An honest witness saves lives, but a false witness tells lies.
Whoever respects the LORD has a strong fortress, and their children will have a safe place.
Respect for the LORD is a fountain of life. It turns people away from the traps of death.
A large population is a king's glory, but a ruler without people is ruined.
Whoever is slow to get angry has great understanding, but whoever has a quick temper shows how foolish they are.
A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but jealousy rots the bones.
Whoever crushes the poor insults their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honours God.
The wicked are brought down by their own evil, but good people have a safe place even in death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of a person with understanding, and even fools come to know it.
Doing what is right makes a nation great, but sin brings shame on any people.
A king is pleased with a wise servant, but he is angry with one who brings shame.
A gentle answer turns away anger, but harsh words stir it up.
The tongues of wise people make knowledge attractive, but the mouths of fools pour out foolishness.
The LORD's eyes are everywhere. He watches both the evil and the good.
Gentle words are a tree of life, but lying words crush the spirit.
A fool rejects his father's correction, but whoever accepts a warning is sensible.
There is great treasure in the house of good people, but the income of the wicked brings them trouble.
The lips of wise people spread knowledge, but the hearts of fools do not.
The LORD hates the sacrifices of the wicked, but he is pleased with the prayers of honest people.
The LORD hates the way of the wicked, but he loves those who chase after what is right.
Harsh punishment waits for those who leave the right path. Those who hate correction will die.
Even the grave and the place of destruction lie open in front of the LORD. How much more the hearts of people!
Mockers do not like to be corrected, so they will not go to wise people.
A happy heart makes a cheerful face, but a sad heart crushes the spirit.
A heart with understanding looks for knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on foolishness.
Every day is hard for those who suffer, but a cheerful heart enjoys a feast that never ends.
It is better to have a little and respect the LORD than to have great wealth with trouble.
A meal of vegetables with love is better than the finest steak with hatred.
A hot-tempered person starts fights, but a patient person calms arguments down.
The path of a lazy person is blocked with thorns, but the path of honest people is a smooth road.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish man looks down on his mother.
Foolishness makes those with no sense happy, but a person with understanding keeps walking straight.
Plans fail without advice, but with many advisers they succeed.
People enjoy giving a good answer. How good is the right word at the right time!
The path of life leads upward for wise people and keeps them from going down to the grave.
The LORD tears down the house of proud people, but he protects the property of widows.
The LORD hates the thoughts of the wicked, but kind words please him.
Greedy people bring trouble on their families, but whoever hates bribes will live.
Good people think before they answer, but the mouths of the wicked pour out evil.
The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayers of good people.
A bright, cheerful look brings joy to the heart. Good news gives health to the body.
Whoever listens to helpful correction will be at home among wise people.
Whoever refuses correction hurts themselves, but whoever listens to it gains understanding.
Respect for the LORD teaches wisdom. Humility comes before honour.
People make plans in their hearts, but the right answer comes from the LORD.
People think everything they do is right, but the LORD weighs their motives.
Give everything you do to the LORD, and your plans will succeed.
The LORD has made everything for its own purpose, even the wicked for the day of disaster.
The LORD hates everyone with a proud heart. You can be sure they will be punished.
Faithful love and truth make up for sin. Respect for the LORD keeps people away from evil.
When the LORD is pleased with how someone lives, he makes even their enemies live at peace with them.
It is better to have a little and do what is right than to have a large income and be unfair.
People plan their path in their hearts, but the LORD decides where their steps will go.
A king speaks as if his words come from God. He must not be unfair when he judges.
Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD. He made all the weights in the bag.
Kings hate it when people do wrong, because a throne is made secure by doing what is right.
Kings are pleased with honest words. They value people who speak the truth.
A king's anger can mean death, but a wise person will calm him down.
When a king is happy, it means life. His favour is like a cloud that brings spring rain.
It is much better to get wisdom than gold, and better to choose understanding than silver.
The road of honest people avoids evil. Whoever watches where they go protects their life.
Pride comes before destruction, and a proud spirit comes before a fall.
It is better to be humble and live among the poor than to share stolen goods with proud people.
Whoever pays attention to good teaching will do well. Happy is the person who trusts in the LORD.
People with wise hearts are known for their understanding, and kind words make teaching easier to accept.
Understanding is a fountain of life to those who have it, but foolishness brings punishment to fools.
The heart of a wise person guides their mouth, and makes their words more convincing.
Kind words are like honey. They are sweet to the soul and bring healing to the body.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
A worker's hunger makes him work. His empty stomach drives him on.
Worthless people plan evil. Their words are like a burning fire.
A twisted person stirs up fights, and gossip separates close friends.
A violent person tempts their neighbour and leads them down a path that is not good.
Whoever winks while plotting evil, whoever purses their lips, is already set on doing wrong.
Grey hair is a glorious crown. It is earned by living a good life.
It is better to be patient than to be a powerful warrior. It is better to control your temper than to capture a city.
People throw dice into their laps, but every decision comes from the LORD.
It is better to eat a dry crust of bread in peace than to have a house full of feasting with fighting.
A wise servant will rule over a master's son who brings shame, and will share the inheritance with the brothers.
A melting pot tests silver, and a furnace tests gold, but the LORD tests hearts.
Evil people listen to evil talk. Liars pay attention to harmful words.
Whoever makes fun of the poor insults their Maker. Whoever is happy when disaster strikes will be punished.
Grandchildren are a crown to the old, and parents are the pride of their children.
Fine words do not suit a fool, and lying words suit a ruler even less.
A bribe seems like a magic stone to the one who gives it. Wherever he turns, he thinks he will succeed.
Whoever forgives an offence builds love, but whoever keeps bringing it up separates close friends.
One warning goes deeper into a person with understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
Evil people are always looking to rebel, so a cruel messenger will be sent against them.
It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool doing something foolish.
If someone pays back evil for good, trouble will never leave their house.
Starting a fight is like letting water out of a dam, so stop before the argument breaks out.
Declaring the guilty innocent and the innocent guilty are both hated by the LORD.
Why should a fool have money to pay for wisdom when he has no desire to understand?
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born to help in times of trouble.
Only someone with no sense would shake hands to guarantee a neighbour's debt.
Whoever loves to sin loves to fight. Whoever builds a high gate is asking for disaster.
People with twisted hearts do not do well, and people who tell lies fall into trouble.
Having a foolish child brings sorrow. The father of a fool has no joy.
A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
Wicked people secretly accept bribes to twist justice.
A person with understanding keeps their eyes on wisdom, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son brings sorrow to his father and bitterness to his mother.
It is not good to punish innocent people, or to beat officials for being honest.
People with knowledge are careful with their words. People with understanding stay calm.
Even fools are thought to be wise if they keep quiet. If they keep their mouths shut, they seem to have understanding.
A person who keeps to themselves only cares about what they want. They reject all good advice.
A fool does not enjoy understanding. He only enjoys giving his own opinions.
When evil comes, contempt comes with it. Shame brings disgrace.
A person's words can be like deep waters. The fountain of wisdom is like a flowing stream.
It is not good to favour the wicked or to keep innocent people from getting justice.
A fool's words lead to arguments. His mouth asks for a beating.
A fool's mouth destroys him. His words are a trap for his own life.
The words of a gossip are like tasty snacks. They go down deep inside a person.
Whoever is lazy in their work is a brother to someone who destroys things.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower. Good people run to him and are safe.
Rich people think their wealth is a strong city, a wall too high to climb.
Before a fall, a person's heart is proud, but humility comes before honour.
Whoever answers before listening is foolish and shames themselves.
A person's spirit can help them through sickness, but who can bear a crushed spirit?
A heart with understanding gains knowledge. The ears of wise people look for knowledge.
A gift opens doors for the giver and brings them into the presence of important people.
The first person to tell their side of a case seems right, until someone else comes and asks questions.
Throwing lots settles arguments and separates powerful opponents.
A brother who has been hurt is harder to win back than a strong city. Arguments are like the locked gates of a fortress.
People's stomachs are filled by what their mouths say. They are satisfied by the harvest of their lips.
The tongue has the power of life and death. Those who love to talk will eat its fruit.
Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing and receives kindness from the LORD.
Poor people beg for mercy, but rich people answer harshly.
Someone with many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
It is better to be poor and live honestly than to be a fool whose words are twisted.
Eagerness without knowledge is not good. If you hurry too much, you will miss the way.
People ruin their lives by their own foolishness, and then their hearts rage against the LORD.
Wealth brings many friends, but poor people are left by their friends.
A false witness will not go unpunished. Whoever pours out lies will not escape.
Many people try to win the favour of a ruler. Everyone is a friend of someone who gives gifts.
All the relatives of a poor person avoid him. How much more do his friends stay away! He chases after them, begging, but they are gone.
Whoever gains wisdom loves themselves. Whoever holds on to understanding will do well.
A false witness will not go unpunished. Whoever pours out lies will be destroyed.
It is not right for a fool to live in luxury, and even worse for a slave to rule over princes.
Good sense makes a person patient. It is to their honour to overlook an offence.
A king's anger is like the roar of a lion, but his kindness is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is a disaster to his father. A quarrelling wife is like water that keeps dripping.
Houses and wealth are passed down from parents, but a sensible wife is a gift from the LORD.
Laziness makes people fall into a deep sleep. Lazy people will go hungry.
Whoever keeps the commands protects their life, but whoever does not care how they live will die.
Whoever is kind to the poor is lending to the LORD, and he will reward them.
Discipline your children while there is still hope. Do not let them destroy their lives.
A hot-tempered person must pay the price. If you rescue them, you will have to do it again.
Listen to advice and accept correction, so that in the end you will be wise.
People make many plans in their hearts, but it is the LORD's purpose that wins.
What people want in a person is kindness. It is better to be poor than to be a liar.
Respect for the LORD leads to life. Then you can rest content, untouched by trouble.
A lazy person buries his hand in the dish and will not even lift it back to his mouth.
Punish a mocker, and simple people will learn good sense. Correct someone with understanding, and they will gain knowledge.
A son who robs his father and drives out his mother brings shame and disgrace.
My son, if you stop listening to teaching, you will wander away from the words of knowledge.
A corrupt witness makes fun of justice, and the mouths of the wicked swallow up evil.
Punishment is ready for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
Wine makes people mock, and beer makes them start fights. Whoever is led astray by drink is not wise.
A king's anger is like the roar of a lion. Whoever makes him angry puts their own life at risk.
It is to a person's honour to avoid arguments, but every fool is quick to quarrel.
Lazy people do not plough in autumn, so at harvest time they look for food and find nothing.
The plans in a person's heart are like deep water, but someone with understanding can draw them out.
Many people claim to be loyal, but who can find someone who is truly faithful?
Good people live honest lives. Their children after them are blessed.
When a king sits on his throne to judge, he sees through evil and scatters it.
Who can say, "I have kept my heart pure. I am clean and free from sin"?
The LORD hates dishonest weights and dishonest measures.
Even children show what they are like by what they do, whether their actions are pure and right.
Ears that hear and eyes that see, the LORD made them both.
Do not love sleep, or you will become poor. Keep your eyes open, and you will have plenty of food.
"It's no good, it's no good!" says the buyer. Then he goes off and boasts about his bargain.
There is gold and plenty of rubies, but words of knowledge are a rare jewel.
Take the coat of someone who guarantees a stranger's debt. Hold it as security if he does it for a woman he does not know.
Food gained by cheating tastes sweet at first, but later it is like a mouth full of gravel.
Make plans by asking for advice. If you go to war, get good guidance.
A gossip tells secrets, so avoid people who talk too much.
If someone curses their father or mother, their lamp will go out in total darkness.
An inheritance gained too quickly at the start will not be blessed in the end.
Do not say, "I will pay you back for this wrong!" Wait for the LORD, and he will rescue you.
The LORD hates dishonest weights, and dishonest scales do not please him.
The LORD directs a person's steps. So how can anyone understand their own way?
It is a trap to make a promise to God too quickly and only think about it afterwards.
A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
The human spirit is the LORD's lamp. It searches out the deepest parts of a person.
Faithful love and truth keep a king safe. His throne is made secure by faithful love.
The glory of young men is their strength. The beauty of old men is their grey hair.
Blows and wounds wash away evil, and beatings clean the deepest parts of a person.
The king's heart is in the LORD's hand like streams of water. He turns it wherever he wants.
People think everything they do is right, but the LORD weighs their hearts.
Doing what is right and fair pleases the LORD more than offering sacrifices.
Proud eyes and a proud heart, which are the lamp of the wicked, are sin.
The plans of hard-working people lead to profit, but everyone who is in too much of a hurry ends up poor.
Riches gained by lying are like a mist that blows away, and they lead to death.
The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is right.
The path of guilty people is crooked, but the actions of innocent people are right.
It is better to live in a corner on the roof than to share a house with a quarrelling wife.
Wicked people long for evil. They show no mercy to their neighbours.
When a mocker is punished, simple people learn wisdom. When wise people are taught, they gain knowledge.
The Righteous One watches the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
Whoever closes their ears to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered.
A secret gift calms anger, and a bribe hidden in a coat calms great fury.
When justice is done, good people are glad, but evil people are terrified.
Whoever wanders from the path of understanding will end up resting among the dead.
Whoever loves pleasure will become poor. Whoever loves wine and rich food will never be rich.
The wicked become the price paid for good people, and the unfaithful for the honest.
It is better to live in a desert than with a quarrelling, complaining wife.
Wise people have precious treasure and oil stored in their homes, but foolish people use up everything they have.
Whoever chases after goodness and kindness will find life, goodness, and honour.
A wise person can attack a city defended by mighty warriors and pull down the fortress they trust in.
Whoever guards their mouth and tongue keeps themselves out of trouble.
A proud and arrogant person is called a mocker. They act with great pride.
A lazy person's wishes will kill him, because his hands refuse to work.
Some people are greedy all day long, but good people give without holding back.
The LORD hates the sacrifices of the wicked, especially when they bring them with evil motives.
A false witness will be destroyed, but whoever listens carefully will be heard forever.
Wicked people put on a bold face, but honest people think carefully about their ways.
No wisdom, no understanding, and no plan can succeed against the LORD.
A horse is made ready for the day of battle, but the victory belongs to the LORD.
A good name is worth more than great riches. Being respected is better than silver and gold.
Rich people and poor people have this in common: the LORD made them all.
Sensible people see danger coming and hide, but simple people keep going and suffer for it.
Humility and respect for the LORD bring wealth, honour, and life.
Thorns and traps lie on the path of crooked people. Whoever protects their life stays far away from them.
Teach children the way they should go, and when they are old they will not turn away from it.
Rich people rule over poor people. The borrower is a slave to the lender.
Whoever plants evil will harvest trouble, and the rod they used in anger will be broken.
A generous person will be blessed, because they share their food with the poor.
Drive out the mocker, and fighting will stop. Arguments and insults will end.
Whoever loves a pure heart and speaks kindly will have the king as a friend.
The LORD's eyes watch over knowledge, but he ruins the words of the unfaithful.
A lazy person says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!"
The mouth of an unfaithful woman is a deep pit. Whoever the LORD is angry with will fall into it.
Foolishness is tied up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away.
Whoever crushes the poor to get rich, or gives gifts to the rich, will end up poor.
Listen carefully to the sayings of the wise. Set your heart on what I teach.
It is good to keep these sayings in your heart and have them ready on your lips.
I am teaching you today, yes, you, so that you will put your trust in the LORD.
I have written thirty sayings for you, full of good advice and knowledge,
to teach you what is true and right, so you can give honest answers to those who sent you.
Do not take advantage of poor people just because they are poor. Do not crush the needy in court.
The LORD will take up their case and take the life of those who rob them.
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person. Do not spend time with someone who is easily angered,
or you may learn their ways and trap yourself.
Do not be one who shakes hands to guarantee someone else's debts.
If you cannot pay, they will take even the bed you are sleeping on.
Do not move the ancient boundary stone that your ancestors set up.
Do you see someone who is skilled at their work? They will serve kings, not unimportant people.
When you sit down to eat with a ruler, pay close attention to what is in front of you.
If you have a big appetite, put a knife to your throat to control it.
Do not crave his fine food, because it may be a trick.
Do not wear yourself out trying to get rich. Be wise enough to stop.
Why set your eyes on riches that are here one moment and gone the next? They suddenly grow wings and fly off into the sky like an eagle.
Do not eat the food of a stingy person. Do not crave his fine food,
because he is always thinking about how much it costs. "Eat and drink," he says, but he does not mean it.
You will throw up the little you have eaten and waste your kind words.
Do not speak to fools, because they will look down on your wise words.
Do not move the ancient boundary stone. Do not take over the fields of orphans,
because their Defender is strong. He will take up their case against you.
Set your heart on instruction and your ears on words of knowledge.
Do not hold back discipline from a child. If you punish him with a rod, he will not die.
Punish him with the rod, and you will save his life from the grave.
My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will be glad.
Deep inside, I will celebrate when your lips say what is right.
Do not let your heart be jealous of sinners. Always keep respecting the LORD.
There is surely a future for you, and your hope will not be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise. Keep your heart on the right path.
Do not join those who drink too much wine or stuff themselves with meat,
because drunks and people who overeat become poor, and too much sleep dresses them in rags.
Listen to your father, who gave you life. Do not look down on your mother when she is old.
Buy the truth and do not sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
The father of a good child has great joy. Whoever has a wise son delights in him.
Let your father and mother be glad. Let the mother who gave birth to you celebrate.
My son, give me your heart. Let your eyes follow my ways.
A prostitute is a deep pit, and an unfaithful wife is a narrow well.
She hides and waits like a robber and makes many men unfaithful.
Who has trouble? Who has sorrow? Who is always fighting? Who is always complaining? Who has bruises for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Those who stay up late drinking wine, those who go looking for bowls of mixed wine.
Do not stare at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.
In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a poisonous viper.
Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will think confused thoughts.
You will feel like someone lying in the middle of the sea, or someone lying at the top of a ship's mast.
You will say, "They hit me, but I am not hurt! They beat me, but I don't feel it! When will I wake up so I can go and get another drink?"
Do not be jealous of evil people. Do not want to spend time with them,
because their hearts plan violence and their lips talk about causing trouble.
A house is built by wisdom and made strong by understanding.
Through knowledge its rooms are filled with all kinds of rare and beautiful treasures.
A wise person is powerful. A person with knowledge grows stronger and stronger.
You need wise guidance to fight a war, and victory comes from having many advisers.
Wisdom is too high for a fool. When the leaders meet at the city gate, he has nothing to say.
Whoever plans evil will be known as a troublemaker.
Foolish plans are sin, and people hate a mocker.
If you give up when trouble comes, your strength is very small.
Rescue those who are being taken away to death. Hold back those who are stumbling toward being killed.
If you say, "But we didn't know about this," doesn't God, who weighs hearts, see it? Doesn't the one who guards your life know it? Won't he pay back each person for what they have done?
My son, eat honey, because it is good. Honey from the honeycomb is sweet to taste.
In the same way, wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will not be cut off.
Do not hide and wait like a wicked person to attack the home of a good person. Do not raid the place where they live.
Even if good people fall seven times, they get up again, but the wicked are brought down by disaster.
Do not celebrate when your enemy falls. Do not let your heart be glad when they trip,
or the LORD will see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from them.
Do not get upset because of evil people, and do not be jealous of the wicked,
because evil people have no future. The lamp of the wicked will go out.
My son, respect the LORD and the king. Do not join with those who rebel,
because disaster will suddenly come on them. Who knows what ruin both the LORD and the king can bring?
These are also sayings of wise people: It is not good to take sides when judging.
Whoever tells the guilty, "You are innocent," will be cursed by peoples and hated by nations.
But things will go well for those who find the guilty guilty, and rich blessings will come on them.
An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Finish your outdoor work and get your fields ready. After that, build your house.
Do not speak against your neighbour without a reason. Do not use your lips to deceive.
Do not say, "I will do to him what he did to me. I will pay him back for what he did."
I walked past the field of a lazy person, past the vineyard of someone who had no sense.
It was all overgrown with thorns. The ground was covered with weeds, and its stone wall had fallen down.
I looked and thought about it carefully. I saw it and learned a lesson:
A little sleep, a little rest, a little folding of the hands to rest,
and poverty will come on you like a robber, and need will attack you like an armed soldier.
These are more wise sayings of Solomon, which were copied down by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah.
It is God's glory to hide things, but it is the glory of kings to search things out.
As the sky is high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be understood.
Remove the waste from silver, and the silversmith can make something beautiful.
Remove the wicked from the king's presence, and his throne will be made secure by doing what is right.
Do not try to make yourself look important in front of the king. Do not claim a place among great people.
It is better to be told, "Come up here," than to be sent lower down in front of an important person you have seen.
Do not rush to take someone to court. What will you do in the end if your neighbour proves you wrong and puts you to shame?
If you have an argument with your neighbour, settle it between the two of you. Do not tell another person's secret,
or whoever hears it may shame you, and your bad name will never go away.
Words spoken at the right time are like golden apples in a silver setting.
Wise correction to a listening ear is like a gold earring or a necklace of fine gold.
A faithful messenger is like cool snow at harvest time to those who send him. He refreshes his masters.
Someone who boasts about gifts they never give is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
A ruler can be persuaded by patience, and gentle words can break bones.
If you find honey, eat only as much as you need, or you will eat too much and throw it up.
Do not visit your neighbour's house too often, or they will get tired of you and hate you.
A person who tells lies about their neighbour in court is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Trusting an unfaithful person in times of trouble is like having a bad tooth or a crippled foot.
Singing songs to someone with a heavy heart is like taking away their coat on a cold day, or pouring vinegar on soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
By doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
As the north wind brings rain, a gossiping tongue brings angry looks.
It is better to live in a corner on the roof than to share a house with a quarrelling wife.
Good news from a faraway land is like cold water to a thirsty person.
A good person who gives in to the wicked is like a muddy spring or a dirty well.
It is not good to eat too much honey, and it is not honourable to look for honour for yourself.
A person without self-control is like a city with broken-down walls.
Like snow in summer or rain at harvest time, honour does not suit a fool.
Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, a curse that is not deserved does not land on anyone.
A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools.
Do not answer fools in the foolish way they speak, or you will be just like them.
Answer fools as their foolishness deserves, or they will think they are wise.
Sending a message by a fool is like cutting off your own feet or drinking poison.
A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is as useless as a crippled person's legs.
Giving honour to a fool is like tying a stone into a sling.
A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is like a thorn bush in the hand of a drunk.
Hiring a fool or anyone who happens to pass by is like an archer who shoots at everyone.
A fool who repeats his foolishness is like a dog that goes back to its vomit.
Do you see someone who thinks they are wise? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
A lazy person says, "There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion is in the streets!"
As a door turns on its hinges, a lazy person turns over in bed.
A lazy person buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to lift it back to his mouth.
A lazy person thinks he is wiser than seven people who give sensible answers.
Getting involved in someone else's argument is like grabbing a stray dog by the ears.
Like a madman shooting burning arrows and deadly weapons
is someone who tricks their neighbour and then says, "I was only joking!"
Without wood a fire goes out. Without gossip an argument dies down.
As charcoal keeps embers glowing and wood keeps a fire burning, a quarrelsome person keeps arguments going.
The words of a gossip are like tasty snacks. They go down deep inside a person.
Smooth words from an evil heart are like cheap silver paint on a clay pot.
Hateful people hide their hatred with their words, but in their hearts they plan to deceive.
Even if they speak kindly, do not believe them, because their hearts are full of seven kinds of evil.
Their hatred may be hidden by lies, but their evil will be exposed in front of everyone.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone will be crushed by it when it rolls back.
A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and flattering words bring ruin.
Do not boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what a day may bring.
Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth. Let a stranger praise you, not your own lips.
A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but the trouble a fool causes is heavier than both.
Anger is cruel and rage is like a flood, but who can stand up against jealousy?
Open correction is better than hidden love.
The wounds a friend gives can be trusted, but an enemy gives many kisses.
Someone who is full refuses even honey, but to someone who is hungry, even bitter food tastes sweet.
A person who wanders from home is like a bird that wanders from its nest.
Perfume and incense make the heart glad, and so does the sincere advice of a friend.
Do not leave your friend or your father's friend. Do not go to your brother's house when disaster strikes you. A neighbour nearby is better than a brother far away.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad. Then I can answer anyone who insults me.
Sensible people see danger coming and hide, but simple people keep going and suffer for it.
Take the coat of someone who guarantees a stranger's debt. Hold it as security if he does it for a woman he does not know.
If you bless your neighbour with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse.
A quarrelling wife is like water dripping on a rainy day.
Trying to control her is like trying to control the wind or hold oil in your hand.
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
Whoever takes care of a fig tree will eat its fruit. Whoever looks after their master will be honoured.
As water reflects a face, a person's heart reflects who they really are.
Death and the grave are never satisfied, and people's eyes are never satisfied either.
A melting pot tests silver and a furnace tests gold, and people are tested by the praise they receive.
Even if you crush a fool in a bowl with grain, you will not get his foolishness out of him.
Know well how your flocks are doing. Pay close attention to your herds,
because riches do not last forever, and a crown does not last for all generations.
When the hay is cut and new grass appears, and the grass is gathered from the hills,
your lambs will give you clothes, and your goats will pay for a field.
You will have plenty of goats' milk to feed you, your family, and your servant girls.
The wicked run away even when no one is chasing them, but good people are as brave as a lion.
When a country rebels, it has many rulers, but a ruler with understanding and knowledge keeps order.
A poor person who crushes the poor is like a heavy rain that washes away all the crops.
Those who turn away from the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law fight against them.
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who look to the LORD understand it completely.
It is better to be poor and live honestly than to be rich and crooked.
A son who keeps the law is wise, but a son who spends time with people who eat and drink too much shames his father.
Whoever gets rich by charging high interest is collecting it for someone who will be kind to the poor.
If someone refuses to listen to the law, even their prayers are hated by God.
Whoever leads honest people down an evil path will fall into their own trap, but blameless people will receive good things.
Rich people think they are wise, but a poor person with understanding can see through them.
When good people win, there is great celebration, but when the wicked rise to power, people hide.
Whoever hides their sins will not do well, but whoever admits them and turns away from them will find mercy.
Happy is the person who always respects God, but whoever makes their heart hard will fall into trouble.
A wicked ruler over helpless people is like a roaring lion or a charging bear.
A ruler who crushes his people has no sense, but one who hates dishonest gain will live a long life.
Someone who is troubled by the guilt of murder will run until they die. No one should help them.
Whoever lives a blameless life will be kept safe, but whoever follows crooked ways will suddenly fall.
Whoever works their land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases dreams will have plenty of poverty.
A faithful person will be richly blessed, but someone in a hurry to get rich will not go unpunished.
It is not good to take sides, but some people will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A stingy person is in a hurry to get rich and does not know that poverty is waiting for him.
Whoever corrects someone will in the end be more appreciated than someone who flatters.
Whoever robs their father or mother and says, "That's not wrong," is no better than a destroyer.
A greedy person stirs up fights, but whoever trusts in the LORD will do well.
Whoever trusts in themselves is a fool, but whoever lives wisely will be kept safe.
Whoever gives to the poor will never be in need, but whoever closes their eyes to the poor will receive many curses.
When the wicked rise to power, people hide, but when the wicked are destroyed, good people grow in number.
Whoever stays stubborn after being corrected many times will suddenly be destroyed, and nothing can save them.
When good people do well, the people celebrate, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad, but a man who spends time with prostitutes wastes his wealth.
A king makes his country strong by being fair, but one who demands bribes tears it down.
Whoever flatters their neighbour is spreading a net for their feet.
Evil people are trapped by their own sin, but good people can sing and be glad.
Good people care about justice for the poor, but the wicked do not care at all.
Mockers stir up a city, but wise people calm down anger.
If a wise person takes a fool to court, the fool shouts and laughs, and there is no peace.
Murderers hate people who are honest and try to kill those who do right.
Fools let all their anger out, but wise people keep themselves under control.
If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.
Poor people and those who crush them have this in common: the LORD gives sight to the eyes of both.
If a king judges the poor fairly, his throne will be secure forever.
Discipline and correction bring wisdom, but a child left to do whatever he wants brings shame to his mother.
When the wicked grow in number, sin grows too, but good people will see them fall.
Discipline your children, and they will give you peace. They will bring you delight.
Where there is no message from God, people run wild, but happy are those who keep the law.
Words alone will not correct a servant. Even if he understands, he will not respond.
Do you see someone who speaks too quickly? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
If you spoil your servant from childhood, in the end he will think he is your son.
An angry person stirs up fights, and a hot-tempered person commits many sins.
Pride brings a person down, but a humble spirit gains honour.
Whoever helps a thief hurts themselves. They are put under oath, but they dare not say anything.
Fear of people is a trap, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
