Many people want the ruler's favour, but justice for people comes from the LORD.
Good people hate those who are dishonest, and the wicked hate those who live honestly.
These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh, a message. He said to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
"I am the most ignorant of people. I do not have human understanding.
I have not learned wisdom, and I do not have knowledge of the Holy One.

Who has gone up to heaven and come back down? Who has gathered the wind in his hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in his coat? Who has set all the ends of the earth in place? What is his name, and what is his son's name? Tell me, if you know!
Every word of God is perfect. He is a shield to those who go to him for safety.
Do not add to his words, or he will correct you and show that you are a liar.
LORD, I ask two things from you. Do not refuse me before I die.
Keep lies and dishonesty far from me. Do not make me poor or rich. Give me only the food I need each day.
If I have too much, I may turn away from you and say, 'Who is the LORD?' If I am poor, I may steal and bring shame on the name of my God.
Do not tell lies about a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will pay for it.
There are people who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
There are people who think they are pure, but they have not been washed clean of their filth.
There are people who are so proud. They look down on everyone.
There are people whose teeth are like swords and whose jaws are like knives. They eat up the poor from the earth and the needy from among people.
The leech has two daughters. They cry, 'Give! Give!' There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, 'Enough!':
the grave, a woman who cannot have children, land that never gets enough water, and fire that never says, 'Enough!'
Anyone who mocks their father and refuses to obey their mother will have their eyes pecked out by ravens from the valley and eaten by vultures.
There are three things too amazing for me, four that I do not understand:
the way an eagle flies in the sky, the way a snake moves on a rock, the way a ship sails on the open sea, and the way a man loves a young woman.
This is the way of an unfaithful wife: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, 'I have done nothing wrong.'
Three things make the earth shake, four things it cannot stand:
a servant who becomes king, a fool who has plenty to eat,
a woman no one loves who gets married, and a servant girl who takes the place of her mistress.
There are four things on earth that are small but very wise:
Ants are not strong creatures, yet they store up their food in summer.
Rock badgers are not powerful creatures, yet they make their homes in the rocks.
Locusts have no king, yet they all march together in rows.
A lizard can be caught in your hand, yet it is found in kings' palaces.
There are three things that walk proudly, four that move with dignity:
the lion, the mightiest of animals, which does not turn back from anything,
the strutting rooster, the male goat, and a king with his army around him.
If you have been foolish and proud, or if you have planned evil, put your hand over your mouth!
As churning milk makes butter and twisting a nose makes it bleed, stirring up anger causes fights."
These are the words of King Lemuel, a message his mother taught him:
"My son, my own son, the answer to my prayers!
Do not waste your strength on women, or on those who destroy kings.
Lemuel, it is not right for kings to drink wine. It is not right for rulers to want beer.
If they drink, they may forget what the law says and take away the rights of those who suffer.
Give beer to those who are dying and wine to those who are deeply troubled.
Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their troubles no more.
Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves. Defend the rights of all who are helpless.
Speak up and judge fairly. Defend the rights of the poor and needy."
Who can find a good wife? She is worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her completely. He has everything he needs.
She does him good and not harm all the days of her life.
She looks for wool and linen and works with eager hands.
She is like a merchant's ship, bringing her food from far away.
She gets up while it is still dark to provide food for her family and portions for her servant girls.
She looks at a field and buys it. With the money she has earned, she plants a vineyard.
She works hard and with energy. Her arms are strong for her tasks.
She sees that her business is going well. Her lamp does not go out at night.
She holds the wool in one hand and spins the thread with the other.
She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
She is not afraid of snow for her family, because all of them are dressed in warm red clothes.
She makes coverings for her bed. She dresses in fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he sits with the leaders of the land.
She makes linen clothes and sells them. She supplies belts to the merchants.
She is dressed in strength and dignity. She laughs without fear of the future.
When she speaks, her words are wise. She teaches with kindness.
She watches over everything that happens in her home. She is never lazy.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her too:
"Many women do wonderful things, but you are better than all of them."
Charm can fool you, and beauty does not last, but a woman who respects the LORD should be praised.
Give her the reward she has earned. Let her works bring her praise at the city gate.
Eccl: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
"Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless, like a breath of wind."
What do people gain from all the hard work they do under the sun?
One generation goes, and another generation comes, but the earth stays forever.
The sun rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries back to the place where it rises.
The wind blows to the south, and turns around to the north. It keeps turning around as it goes, and the wind comes back again to its paths.
All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is never full. The rivers go back to the place they flow from, and they flow again.
Everything is more tiring than words can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, and the ear is never filled with hearing.
What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done. There is nothing new under the sun.
Is there anything people can point to and say, "Look, this is new"? It was already here long ago, in the ages before us.
No one remembers the people who came before, and the people still to come will not be remembered by those who come after them.
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I set my heart to search out and explore with wisdom everything that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to people to keep them busy.
I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and look, everything is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted.
I said to myself, "Look, I have gained great wisdom, more than anyone who ruled Jerusalem before me. Yes, my heart has learned a great deal of wisdom and knowledge."
I set my heart to understand wisdom, and also madness and foolishness. I learned that this too was like chasing the wind.
For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and the more knowledge you gain, the more grief you have.
I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with fun. Enjoy pleasure." But look, this also was meaningless.
I said about laughter, "It is foolish," and about fun, "What good does it do?"

I searched in my heart how to cheer myself with wine, while my heart still guided me with wisdom, and how to take hold of foolishness, until I could see what is good for people to do under heaven all the days of their lives.
I did great works. I built houses for myself. I planted vineyards for myself.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I made pools of water for myself, to water the forest where the trees were growing.
I bought male and female servants, and I had servants born in my house. I also owned great herds and flocks, more than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasures of kings and provinces. I got men and women singers, and the pleasures people delight in: musical instruments of every kind.
So I became great, and grew richer than anyone in Jerusalem before me. And my wisdom stayed with me.
I did not keep from my eyes anything they wanted. I did not hold back my heart from any joy, for my heart was glad because of all my work, and this was my reward for all my work.
Then I looked at all the things my hands had done, and at the work I had worked so hard to do. And look, everything was meaningless, like chasing the wind. Nothing was gained under the sun.
I turned to think about wisdom, madness, and foolishness. For what can the king who comes after me do? Only what has already been done long ago.
Then I saw that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
The wise person has eyes in their head, but the fool walks in darkness. And yet I saw that the same end happens to them all.
Then I said in my heart, "What happens to the fool will happen to me too. So why was I so wise?" Then I said in my heart that this too is meaningless.
For the wise person, like the fool, will not be remembered forever. In the days to come, everyone will long be forgotten. Yes, the wise person must die just like the fool!
So I hated life, because the work done under the sun was painful to me. Everything is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
I hated all the hard work I had done under the sun, because I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will be in charge of all the work I have done with such effort and wisdom under the sun. This too is meaningless.
So my heart began to give up hope about all the hard work I had done under the sun.
For a person may work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and then have to leave everything they own to someone who never worked for it. This too is meaningless and a great evil.
For what do people get from all their hard work and from all the striving of their hearts under the sun?
All their days are full of pain, and their work is full of grief. Even at night their hearts do not rest. This too is meaningless.
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and enjoy the good in their work. I saw that this also comes from the hand of God.
For who can eat or enjoy anything more than I can?

To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy. But to the sinner he gives the work of gathering and storing up, to give it to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
There is a season for everything, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pull up what was planted;
a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to tear down, and a time to build up;
a time to cry, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
a time to throw stones away, and a time to gather stones together; a time to hug, and a time to stop hugging;
a time to search, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;
a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to be silent, and a time to speak;
a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
What do workers gain from all their hard work?
I have seen the burden God has given to people to keep them busy.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put eternity in people's hearts, yet they cannot understand the work God has done from the beginning to the end.
I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good as long as they live.
And that everyone should eat and drink and enjoy the good in all their work. This is the gift of God.
I know that whatever God does lasts forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it. God does it so that people will stand in awe of him.
What is now has already been long ago, and what is to come has already been long ago. God calls back what has passed away.
I also saw under the sun that in the place of justice, there was wickedness, and in the place of what is right, there was wickedness.
I said in my heart, "God will judge both the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every purpose and every work."
I said in my heart, "As for people, God tests them, so that they can see that they are like animals.

For what happens to people also happens to animals. The same thing happens to both. As one dies, so does the other. Yes, they all have the same breath, and people have no advantage over animals, for everything is meaningless.
All go to the same place. All come from dust, and all return to dust again.
Who knows whether the spirit of people goes up, and whether the spirit of animals goes down into the earth?"
So I saw that there is nothing better than for people to enjoy their work, because that is their reward. For who can bring them to see what will happen after they are gone?

Then I looked again and saw all the cruelty that is done under the sun. Look, I saw the tears of people who were treated cruelly, and they had no one to comfort them. Their oppressors had power, but those who suffered had no one to comfort them.
So I said the dead, who died long ago, are better off than the living who are still alive.
Yes, better than both of them is the one who has not yet been born, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
Then I saw that all hard work and success come from people being jealous of their neighbors. This too is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
The fool folds their hands and does nothing, and ruins themselves.
Better one handful with peace and quiet than two handfuls with hard work and chasing the wind.
Then I looked again and saw something else meaningless under the sun.

There is a person who is all alone, with no son or brother. There is no end to all their hard work, and their eyes are never satisfied with riches. They never ask, "Who am I working for, and why am I keeping myself from enjoying life?" This too is meaningless. Yes, it is a sad business.
Two are better than one, because they get a good reward for their work.
If one of them falls, the other can help them up. But pity the person who is alone when they fall, with no one to help them up.
Also, if two lie down together, they keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone?
Someone may overpower a person who is alone, but two can stand up against them. And a rope made of three strands is not quickly broken.
A poor but wise young person is better than an old and foolish king who no longer listens to advice.
For the young person came out of prison to become king, even though he was born poor in that kingdom.
I saw all the people who live under the sun follow the young person, the one who took the king's place.
There was no end to all the people he led. Yet those who come later will not be happy with him. Surely this too is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
Watch your steps when you go to God's house. It is better to come near and listen than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not even know they are doing wrong.
Do not speak too quickly, and do not let your heart rush to say anything before God. For God is in heaven, and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
Just as dreams come when you have too many worries, a fool's talk comes with too many words.
When you make a promise to God, do not wait to keep it, for he has no pleasure in fools. Keep what you promise.
It is better not to make a promise than to make one and not keep it.
Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not tell the temple messenger, "It was a mistake." Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?
For many dreams and many words are meaningless. Instead, have deep respect for God.

If you see the poor being treated cruelly in a district, and justice and fairness taken away by force, do not be surprised. For one official is watched by a higher official, and there are officials over them both.
The produce of the land is for everyone. Even the king gets his profit from the fields.
Whoever loves money will never have enough money, and whoever loves riches will never be satisfied with what they earn. This too is meaningless.
When good things increase, so do the people who use them up. And what does the owner gain, except to look at them with their eyes?
The sleep of a worker is sweet, whether they eat little or much. But the riches of the wealthy keep them from sleeping.
There is a terrible evil I have seen under the sun: riches that are stored up by their owner and end up hurting them.
Those riches are lost through bad luck, and when that person has a son, there is nothing left in their hand to give him.
Just as they came from their mother's womb, they will leave naked, as they came. They will take nothing from their hard work that they can carry in their hand.
This too is a terrible evil: exactly as they came, so they will go. What do they gain from working hard for the wind?
All their days they also eat in darkness. They are frustrated, sick, and angry.

Look, this is what I have seen to be good and right: for a person to eat and drink and enjoy the good in all their hard work under the sun, all the days of life God has given them. For this is their reward.
Also, when God gives a person riches and wealth, and the power to enjoy them, to accept their reward and be happy in their work, this is the gift of God.
Such a person will not often think about how short their life is, because God keeps them busy with the joy of their heart.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily on people:

God gives a person riches, wealth, and honor, so that they have everything their heart wants. But God does not give them the power to enjoy it, and a stranger enjoys it instead. This is meaningless, and it is a terrible sickness.
A man may have a hundred children and live many years. But if his heart is not filled with good things, and he does not even get a proper burial, I say a baby born dead is better off than he is.
For the baby comes for nothing and leaves in darkness, and its name is covered in darkness.
It has never seen the sun or known anything. Yet it has more rest than that man.
Even if he lives a thousand years twice over but does not enjoy good things, do not all go to the same place?
All the hard work people do is for their mouths, and yet their hunger is never satisfied.
For what advantage does a wise person have over a fool? What does a poor person gain by knowing how to live before others?
It is better to enjoy what your eyes can see than to keep wanting more. This too is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what people are. No one can argue with someone who is stronger than they are.
The more words there are, the more meaningless they become. How does that help anyone?
For who knows what is good for people in life, during the few meaningless days they pass through like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they are gone?
A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
It is better to go to a house where people are mourning than to a house where people are feasting. For death is the end of everyone, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter, because a sad face can make the heart better.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of fun.
It is better to listen to the correction of a wise person than to listen to the songs of fools.
Like the crackling of thorns burning under a pot, so is the laughter of a fool. This too is meaningless.
Surely cheating people makes a wise person foolish, and a bribe ruins the mind.
The end of a thing is better than its beginning. Being patient is better than being proud.
Do not be quick to get angry, for anger lives in the heart of fools.
Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" It is not wise to ask that.
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is even better, for all who live under the sun.
For wisdom protects, just as money protects. But the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom keeps alive the one who has it.
Think about what God has done. Who can make straight what he has made crooked?
When times are good, be happy. When times are bad, think about this: God has made the one as well as the other, so that people cannot find out what will come after them.
In my meaningless life I have seen all this: a righteous person dying even though they do right, and a wicked person living long even though they do evil.
Do not be too righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why destroy yourself?
Do not be too wicked, and do not be a fool. Why die before your time?
It is good to hold on to the one warning and not let go of the other. For whoever has respect for God will avoid all extremes.
Wisdom makes one wise person stronger than ten rulers in a city.
Surely there is no one on earth who is righteous, who always does good and never sins.
Also, do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others too.
I tested all this with wisdom. I said, "I will be wise," but it was far beyond me.
Whatever exists is far off and very deep. Who can find it out?
So I turned my heart to understand, to explore, and to search for wisdom and the meaning of things, and to understand that wickedness is stupid and that foolishness is madness.
I found something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is a trap and a net, and whose hands are chains. The one who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will be caught by her.
"Look," says the Teacher, "this is what I have found, adding one thing to another to find the answer,
which I am still searching for but have not found. I found one upright man among a thousand, but I have not found one woman among all of them.
Look, this is the only thing I have found: God made people upright, but they have gone looking for many schemes."
Who is like the wise person? Who knows the meaning of things? Wisdom makes a person's face shine, and softens its hard look.
I say, "Obey the king's command," because you made a promise before God.
Do not be in a hurry to leave the king's presence. Do not stand up for something evil, for he does whatever he pleases.
For the king's word has power. Who can say to him, "What are you doing?"
Whoever obeys his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart will know the right time and the right way.
For there is a right time and a right way for everything, even though people carry a heavy load of trouble.
For no one knows what will happen. Who can tell anyone how it will happen?
No one has power to hold back the wind or the spirit, and no one has power over the day of their death. No one is let off from the battle, and wickedness will not rescue those who do it.
I saw all this when I set my mind to everything that is done under the sun. There are times when one person rules over another and hurts them.
Then I saw the wicked being buried. They used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they did these things. This too is meaningless.
When a sentence against an evil act is not carried out quickly, people's hearts are filled with plans to do evil.
Even though a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives a long time, I know for sure that it will go better with those who have respect for God and stand in awe of him.
But it will not go well with the wicked. Their days will not grow long like a shadow, because they do not respect God.

There is something meaningless that happens on earth: there are righteous people who get what the wicked deserve, and there are wicked people who get what the righteous deserve. I say this too is meaningless.

So I praise the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for people under the sun than to eat, drink, and be happy. This joy will go with them in their work all the days of life that God gives them under the sun.
I set my heart to know wisdom and to watch the work that is done on earth, even going without sleep day and night.

Then I saw all that God has done. No one can understand the work that is done under the sun. However hard people work to search it out, they cannot find it. Even if a wise person claims to understand it, they really cannot find it.
I thought about all this and explored it all: the righteous and the wise, and what they do, are in God's hand. No one knows whether love or hate is waiting for them. Everything lies ahead of them.

The same thing comes to everyone. The same end comes to the righteous and the wicked, to the good, to the clean and the unclean, to those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good person, so it is with the sinner. As it is with those who make promises, so it is with those who are afraid to make them.

This is the evil in everything that is done under the sun: the same end comes to everyone. Also, people's hearts are full of evil, and there is madness in their hearts while they live. After that, they join the dead.
Whoever is still among the living has hope. Yes, a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no more reward, and even the memory of them is forgotten.
Their love, their hate, and their jealousy have long since disappeared. They will never again have a part in anything that happens under the sun.
Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart, for God has already approved what you do.
Always wear white clothes, and always put oil on your head.

Enjoy life with the wife you love, all the days of this meaningless life that God has given you under the sun, all your meaningless days. For this is your reward in life and in the hard work you do under the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength. For in the grave, where you are going, there is no work, no planning, no knowledge, and no wisdom.

I looked again and saw under the sun that the race is not won by the fastest, nor the battle by the strongest. Food does not always come to the wise, nor riches to the clever, nor favor to the skilled. Time and chance happen to them all.
For no one knows when their time will come. Like fish caught in a cruel net, and like birds caught in a trap, so people are caught by evil times that fall on them suddenly.
I also saw this example of wisdom under the sun, and it impressed me greatly.
There was a small city with only a few people in it. A powerful king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siege works against it.
Now a poor but wise man lived there, and by his wisdom he saved the city. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the poor man's wisdom is looked down on, and no one listens to his words.
The quiet words of the wise are better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good.
Just as dead flies make the perfumer's oil smell bad, a little foolishness outweighs wisdom and honor.
The heart of the wise leads them the right way, but the heart of a fool leads them the wrong way.
Even when the fool walks along the road, they have no sense, and they show everyone that they are a fool.
If a ruler becomes angry with you, do not leave your post. For staying calm can put great wrongs to rest.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the kind of mistake that comes from a ruler.
Fools are put in high positions, while the rich sit in low places.
I have seen servants riding on horses, while princes walk on the ground like servants.
Whoever digs a pit may fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
Whoever cuts stones may be hurt by them. Whoever splits wood may be in danger from it.
If the axe is dull and its edge is not sharpened, you must use more strength. But skill brings success.
If a snake bites before it is charmed, the snake charmer gains nothing.
The words of a wise person are kind, but a fool is destroyed by their own lips.
Their words begin with foolishness and end with wicked madness.
A fool keeps talking and talking. No one knows what is coming. Who can tell anyone what will happen after them?
The work of fools makes them tired, because they do not even know the way to town.
How sad for you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes feast in the morning!
How happy you are, land, when your king comes from a noble family, and your princes eat at the right time, for strength and not to get drunk!
Because of laziness the roof falls in, and because of idle hands the house leaks.
A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life happy, and money is the answer for everything.
Do not curse the king, not even in your thoughts, and do not curse the rich in your bedroom. For a bird in the sky may carry your words, and something with wings may tell what you said.
Throw your bread on the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
Share what you have with seven, yes, even with eight, for you do not know what trouble may come on the earth.
If the clouds are full of rain, they pour it out on the earth. If a tree falls to the south or to the north, wherever the tree falls, there it will stay.
Whoever keeps watching the wind will never plant, and whoever keeps looking at the clouds will never harvest.
Just as you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones grow in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not understand the work of God, who makes everything.
Plant your seed in the morning, and in the evening do not stop working. For you do not know which will succeed, this or that, or whether both will do equally well.
Light is truly sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun.
Yes, if a person lives many years, let them enjoy them all. But let them remember the days of darkness, for there will be many. Everything to come is meaningless.

Young person, be happy while you are young, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Follow the ways of your heart and what your eyes see. But know that God will judge you for all these things.
So put sadness out of your heart, and put away pain from your body, for youth and the dawn of life are fleeting and meaningless.
Remember your Creator while you are young, before the days of trouble come, and the years come near when you will say, "I find no pleasure in them."
Remember him before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark, and the clouds come back after the rain;
in the day when the guards of the house tremble, and the strong men bend over, and the grinders stop because they are few, and those who look through the windows see only darkness;
when the doors to the street are shut, and the sound of grinding fades; when people rise up at the sound of a bird, but all their songs grow faint;

when people are afraid of heights and of dangers on the road; when the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire is gone. For people go to their everlasting home, and the mourners walk around in the streets.
Remember him before the silver cord is cut, or the golden bowl is broken, or the jar is smashed at the spring, or the wheel is broken at the well,
and the dust goes back to the earth as it was, and the spirit goes back to God who gave it.
"Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"
Besides being wise, the Teacher also taught the people knowledge. Yes, he thought carefully, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
The Teacher searched to find pleasing words, and he wrote what was upright and true.
The words of the wise are like sharp sticks used to drive cattle, and their collected sayings are like nails driven in firmly. They are given by one Shepherd.
Beyond these, my son, be warned: there is no end to making many books, and much study makes the body tired.
This is the end of the matter. Everything has been heard. Have deep respect for God and keep his commands, for this is the whole duty of every person.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.
Song: This is Solomon's Song of Songs, the most beautiful song of all.
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your love is better than wine.
Your perfumed oils smell wonderful. Your name is like perfume poured out. That is why the young women love you.

Take me away with you. Let us hurry! The king has brought me into his rooms. The friends say: We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! She says: They are right to love you.
I am dark but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, dark like the tents of Kedar, lovely like Solomon's curtains.
Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has burned my skin. My mother's sons were angry with me. They made me take care of the vineyards, so I have not taken care of my own vineyard.
Tell me, you whom my heart loves, where do you feed your flock? Where do you let them rest at noon? Why should I be like a woman wearing a veil, wandering beside the flocks of your friends?
If you do not know, most beautiful of women, follow the tracks of the sheep, and feed your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
My love, I compare you to a fine horse pulling Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, and your neck with strings of jewels.
We will make you earrings of gold, decorated with silver.
While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its sweet smell.
My beloved is to me like a little bag of myrrh resting between my breasts.
My beloved is to me like a cluster of henna flowers from the vineyards of En Gedi.
Look, you are beautiful, my love. Look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.
Look, you are handsome, my beloved, and so pleasant! Our bed is green and fresh.
The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are fir trees.
I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among thorns, so is my love among the young women.
Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men. I sat down in his shade with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
He brought me to the banquet hall, and his banner over me is love.
Make me strong with raisins, refresh me with apples, for I am weak with love.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand holds me close.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise by the gazelles and by the deer of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until the time is right.
Listen! It is my beloved! Look, here he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young deer. Look, he is standing behind our wall! He is looking through the windows. He is peeking through the lattice.
My beloved spoke and said to me, "Get up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away with me.
For look, the winter is over. The rain has ended and gone.
Flowers are appearing on the earth. The time of singing has come, and the voice of the dove is heard in our land.
The fig tree is ripening its green figs. The vines are blossoming and giving off their sweet smell. Get up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away."
My dove, hiding in the cracks of the rock, in the hiding places on the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, for our vineyards are in bloom.
My beloved is mine, and I am his. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
Until the day cools and the shadows run away, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
At night on my bed, I looked for the one my heart loves. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
I will get up now and go around the city, through the streets and the squares. I will look for the one my heart loves. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
The watchmen who go around the city found me. I asked them, "Have you seen the one my heart loves?"
I had hardly passed them when I found the one my heart loves. I held on to him and would not let him go until I had brought him into my mother's house, into the room of the one who gave birth to me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise by the gazelles and by the deer of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until the time is right.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, smelling of myrrh and frankincense, and all the spices of the merchants?
Look, it is Solomon's carriage! Sixty strong men surround it, the strongest men of Israel.
They all carry swords and are skilled in war. Each man has his sword at his side, ready for the dangers of the night.
King Solomon made himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its posts of silver, its base of gold, and its seat of purple cloth. Its inside was lovingly decorated by the daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out, you daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon wearing the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, the day his heart was filled with joy.
Look, you are beautiful, my love. Look, you are beautiful. Your eyes behind your veil are like doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep just shorn, coming up from the washing. Each one has its twin, and not one of them is missing.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks behind your veil are like halves of a pomegranate.
Your neck is like the tower of David, built to store weapons, with a thousand shields hanging on it, all the shields of strong warriors.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.
Until the day cools and the shadows run away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
You are beautiful in every way, my love. There is no flaw in you.
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Look down from the top of Amana, from the tops of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions and the mountains of the leopards.
You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride. You have stolen my heart with one look of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is so much better than wine, and the smell of your perfume is better than any spice!
Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like honey from the comb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your clothes is like the smell of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring closed up, a sealed fountain.
Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates with the finest fruits, with henna and nard,
nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree, myrrh and aloes, and all the finest spices.
You are a fountain in the gardens, a well of fresh flowing water, streams flowing down from Lebanon.
Wake up, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden, so that its sweet smells spread. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its finest fruits.

I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb and my honey. I have drunk my wine and my milk. The friends say: Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink your fill of love.
I was asleep, but my heart was awake. Listen! My beloved is knocking: "Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one. My head is wet with dew, and my hair with the damp of the night."
I have taken off my robe. Must I put it on again? I have washed my feet. Must I get them dirty again?
My beloved put his hand through the opening of the latch, and my heart pounded for him.
I got up to open the door for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
I opened the door for my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone away. My heart sank when he spoke. I looked for him, but I did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer.
The watchmen who go around the city found me. They beat me and bruised me. The guards of the walls took away my cloak.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise: if you find my beloved, tell him that I am weak with love.
How is your beloved better than any other, most beautiful of women? How is your beloved better than any other, that you make us promise this?
My beloved is fair and glowing with health, the best among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold. His hair is wavy and black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, washed in milk, set like jewels.
His cheeks are like beds of spices, giving off sweet perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
His arms are like rods of gold set with jewels. His body is like polished ivory covered with sapphires.
His legs are like marble pillars set on bases of fine gold. He looks like Lebanon, as fine as its cedars.
His mouth is sweetness itself. Yes, he is lovely in every way. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your beloved turn, so that we can look for him with you?
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
I belong to my beloved, and my beloved belongs to me. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
You are beautiful, my love, like the city of Tirzah, lovely like Jerusalem, as stunning as an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down the slopes of Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing. Each one has its twin, and not one of them is missing.
Your cheeks behind your veil are like halves of a pomegranate.
There may be sixty queens, eighty other wives, and young women without number.

But my dove, my perfect one, is the only one. She is her mother's only daughter, the favorite of the one who gave birth to her. The young women saw her and called her blessed. The queens and the other wives saw her and praised her.
Who is this who appears like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, as stunning as an army with banners?
I went down to the grove of nut trees to look at the new growth in the valley, to see whether the vines had budded and the pomegranates were in bloom.
Before I knew it, my desire had placed me among the royal chariots of my people.
Come back, come back, Shulammite! Come back, come back, so that we may look at you! He says: Why do you want to look at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince's daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Your navel is like a round bowl that never runs out of mixed wine. Your waist is like a heap of wheat surrounded by lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like a tower of ivory. Your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath Rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon that looks toward Damascus.
Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel. Your hair is like purple cloth. The king is held captive by its locks.
How beautiful and how pleasant you are, my love, with all your delights!
Your height is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters of fruit.
I said, "I will climb the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit." May your breasts be like clusters of grapes on the vine, and the smell of your breath like apples.
Your mouth is like the best wine, flowing smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over the lips of those who sleep.
I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
Come, my beloved! Let us go out into the fields. Let us spend the night in the villages.
Let us go early to the vineyards. Let us see whether the vines have budded, whether their blossoms have opened, and whether the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.
The mandrakes give off their sweet smell. At our doors are all kinds of fine fruits, new and old, which I have saved up for you, my beloved.
Oh, I wish you were like my brother, who nursed at my mother's breasts! Then if I found you outside, I could kiss you, and no one would look down on me.
I would lead you and bring you into my mother's house, she who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranates.
His left hand would be under my head, and his right hand would hold me close.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise: do not stir up or awaken love until the time is right.

Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? She says: Under the apple tree I woke you. There your mother became pregnant with you. There she went into labor and gave birth to you.

Place me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm. For love is as strong as death, and its jealousy is as unyielding as the grave. It burns like blazing fire, like a mighty flame of the LORD.
Many waters cannot put out love, and rivers cannot wash it away. If someone offered all the riches of their house for love, they would be completely laughed at.
We have a little sister, and she is still young. What shall we do for our sister on the day someone asks to marry her?
If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver on her. If she is a door, we will cover her with boards of cedar.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So in his eyes I became like one who brings peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He rented the vineyard out to caretakers. Each one was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
But my own vineyard is mine to give. The thousand pieces of silver are for you, Solomon, and two hundred are for those who care for its fruit.
You who live in the gardens, with friends listening, let me hear your voice!
Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of spices!
Isa: This is the vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem, during the time when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
Listen, heavens! Pay attention, earth! For the LORD has spoken: "I raised children and brought them up, but they have turned against me.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey knows where its master feeds it. But Israel does not know me. My people do not understand."

How terrible for this sinful nation, a people weighed down with guilt, children of evildoers, children who do what is corrupt! They have turned away from the LORD. They have rejected the Holy One of Israel. They have turned their backs on him.
Why do you want to be beaten more? Why do you keep rebelling? Your whole head is sick, and your whole heart is weak.
From the bottom of your feet to the top of your head, there is nothing healthy. There are only wounds, bruises, and open sores. They have not been cleaned, bandaged, or soothed with oil.
Your country is ruined. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers are eating up your land right in front of you. It is ruined, as if strangers had destroyed it.
The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a melon field, like a city under attack.
If the LORD of Armies had not left us a few survivors, we would have been like Sodom. We would have been like Gomorrah.
Listen to the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

"What are all your many sacrifices to me?" says the LORD. "I have had more than enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.
When you come to meet with me, who asked you to do this, to trample through my courts?
Stop bringing meaningless offerings. Your incense is disgusting to me. New Moons, Sabbaths, and special meetings, I cannot stand your evil gatherings.
I hate your New Moon festivals and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to me. I am tired of carrying them.
When you lift up your hands to pray, I will hide my eyes from you. Even when you pray many prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves. Make yourselves clean. Take your evil deeds out of my sight. Stop doing evil.
Learn to do good. Seek justice. Help those who are treated cruelly. Defend the orphans. Stand up for the widows."
"Come now, let us talk this over," says the LORD. "Even though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow. Even though they are red like crimson, they will be like wool.
If you are willing and obey, you will eat the good things of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel, you will be destroyed by the sword. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken."
See how the faithful city has become like a prostitute! She was once full of justice. Righteousness lived in her, but now murderers live there.
Your silver has become worthless metal. Your wine is mixed with water.
Your leaders are rebels and friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chase after gifts. They do not defend the orphans, and the widows' cases never come before them.
So the Lord GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: "I will get relief from my enemies and pay back those who oppose me.
I will turn my hand against you. I will completely burn away your worthless metal and remove all your impurities.
I will give you judges again, like you had at first, and advisers like you had in the beginning. After that you will be called 'The City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.'"
Zion will be rescued by justice, and those who turn back to her by righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will be destroyed together, and those who turn away from the LORD will perish.
You will be ashamed of the sacred oak trees you loved, and you will be embarrassed because of the gardens you chose.
You will be like an oak tree with dying leaves, and like a garden that has no water.
The strong will become like dry straw, and their work like a spark. Both will burn together, and no one will put out the fire.
This is what Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the mountain of the LORD's house will be set up as the highest of the mountains. It will be raised above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.

Many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths." For the teaching will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and settle arguments for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into pruning tools. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will never train for war again.
Come, people of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
For you, LORD, have left your people, the house of Jacob, because they are full of customs from the east. They practice fortune telling like the Philistines, and they make deals with foreigners.
Their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures. Their land is full of horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
Their land is also full of idols. They worship things made with their own hands, things their own fingers have made.
So people will be brought low, and everyone will be humbled. Do not forgive them!
Go into the rocks and hide in the dust, away from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty.
The proud looks of people will be brought low, and the pride of everyone will be humbled. The LORD alone will be lifted high on that day.
For the LORD of Armies has a day set aside for all who are proud and arrogant, for all who are lifted up, and they will be brought low.
It will come against all the tall, lofty cedars of Lebanon, and all the oaks of Bashan,
against all the high mountains, against all the lofty hills,
against every tall tower, against every strong wall,
against all the ships of Tarshish, and against every beautiful thing people admire.
The pride of people will be humbled, and the arrogance of everyone will be brought low. The LORD alone will be lifted high on that day.
The idols will completely disappear.
People will run into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth powerfully.
On that day people will throw away their idols of silver and gold, which they made for themselves to worship. They will throw them to the moles and the bats.
They will run into the caves of the rocks and the cracks in the rough cliffs, away from the terror of the LORD and the glory of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth powerfully.
Stop trusting in mere humans, who have only a breath in their nostrils. What are they worth?
Look, the Lord GOD of Armies is about to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything they depend on: all their food and all their water;
the strong man and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the fortune teller and the elder,
the captain of fifty and the respected man, the adviser, the skilled craftsman, and the clever magician.
I will make boys their leaders, and children will rule over them.
The people will treat each other cruelly, each person against another, neighbor against neighbor. The young will be rude to the old, and worthless people will insult the respected.
A man will grab his brother in his father's house and say, "You have a coat, so you be our leader. Take charge of this pile of ruins!"
But on that day he will shout, "I cannot fix this! There is no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people."
For Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen, because what they say and what they do is against the LORD. They insult his glorious presence.
The look on their faces gives them away. They show off their sin like Sodom. They do not even hide it. How terrible for them! They have brought disaster on themselves.
Tell the righteous that it will go well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of what they have done.
How terrible for the wicked! Disaster is coming on them, for they will be paid back for what their hands have done.
As for my people, children treat them cruelly, and women rule over them. My people, your leaders mislead you and confuse the path you should take.
The LORD stands up to argue his case. He stands to judge the peoples.
The LORD brings his charge against the elders and leaders of his people: "You are the ones who have ruined my vineyard. What you stole from the poor is in your houses.
How dare you crush my people and grind the faces of the poor into the dust?" says the Lord GOD of Armies.
The LORD also says, "The women of Zion are proud. They walk with their heads held high and flirting eyes. They take dainty little steps with jingling ornaments on their ankles.
So the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the women of Zion, and the LORD will make their heads bald."
On that day the Lord will take away all their finery: their ankle bracelets, headbands, and moon shaped necklaces,
their earrings, bracelets, and veils,
their headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume bottles, and charms,
their signet rings and nose rings,
their fine robes, capes, cloaks, and purses,
their mirrors, fine linen clothes, crowns, and shawls.
Instead of sweet perfume, there will be a bad smell. Instead of a belt, a rope. Instead of nicely styled hair, baldness. Instead of a fine robe, rough sackcloth. Instead of beauty, burn marks.
Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
The gates of Zion will weep and mourn. She will be empty and will sit on the ground.
On that day seven women will grab hold of one man and say, "We will eat our own food and wear our own clothes. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our shame!"
On that day, the branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of those left alive in Israel.
Whoever is left in Zion and whoever remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone in Jerusalem whose name is written among the living.
This will happen when the Lord has washed away the filth of the women of Zion, and cleaned the blood from Jerusalem, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.
Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over those who gather there a cloud of smoke by day and a glow of flaming fire by night. Over all the glory there will be a covering.
It will be a shelter that gives shade from the heat of the day, and a safe place and hiding place from the storm and the rain.
Let me sing a song for the one I love, a song about his vineyard. My loved one had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

He dug it up and cleared out the stones, and planted it with the best vines. He built a watchtower in the middle of it and cut out a winepress in it. He expected it to produce good grapes, but it produced only wild, sour grapes.
"Now, people of Jerusalem and people of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard that I have not done? When I expected good grapes, why did it produce only sour ones?
Now I will tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard. I will take away its hedge, and it will be eaten up. I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland. It will not be trimmed or dug, and briers and thorns will grow there. I will also command the clouds not to send rain on it."

The vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the garden he delighted in. He looked for justice, but saw cruelty. He looked for righteousness, but heard cries of distress.
How terrible for those who keep buying house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone, and you live alone in the land!
The LORD of Armies said this in my hearing: "Surely many houses will be left empty, even great and beautiful houses, with no one living in them.
Ten acres of vineyard will produce only one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will produce only an ephah of grain."
How terrible for those who get up early in the morning to chase after strong drink, who stay up late at night until wine sets them on fire!
They have harps, lyres, tambourines, flutes, and wine at their feasts, but they do not respect what the LORD is doing. They do not think about the work of his hands.
So my people will be taken away as captives because they do not understand. Their important people will starve, and the crowds will be dried up with thirst.
So the grave has made its appetite larger and opened its mouth wide without limit. The glory of Jerusalem, its crowds, its noise, and all who party in it will go down into it.
So people will be brought low, and everyone will be humbled, and the eyes of the proud will look down.
But the LORD of Armies will be lifted high by his justice, and the holy God will show himself holy by his righteousness.
Then lambs will feed there as in their own pasture, and strangers will eat among the ruins of the rich.
How terrible for those who drag their sin along with ropes of lies, and pull wickedness behind them as if with cart ropes!
They say, "Let God hurry up and do his work quickly so we can see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and happen, so we will know it!"
How terrible for those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness light and light darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
How terrible for those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
How terrible for those who are heroes at drinking wine and champions at mixing strong drinks,
who let the guilty go free for a bribe, and take away justice from the innocent!

So, as fire eats up straw and dry grass sinks down in the flames, their roots will rot and their flowers will blow away like dust. For they have rejected the teaching of the LORD of Armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

That is why the LORD's anger burns against his people. He has raised his hand against them and struck them down. The mountains shake, and dead bodies lie like garbage in the streets. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
He will raise a flag for the nations far away. He will whistle for them from the ends of the earth. Look, they are coming quickly and swiftly!
None of them will get tired or stumble. None of them will doze or sleep. Not a belt will come loose, and not a sandal strap will break.
Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are ready. Their horses' hooves are hard as flint, and their chariot wheels spin like a whirlwind.
They roar like a lioness. They roar like young lions. They growl as they grab their prey and carry it off, and no one can rescue it.
On that day they will roar over Judah like the roaring of the sea. If anyone looks at the land, they will see only darkness and trouble. Even the light will be darkened by the clouds.
In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the edge of his robe filled the temple.
Above him stood seraphs, heavenly beings. Each one had six wings. With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They were calling to one another, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!"
At the sound of their voices, the doorposts and the thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
Then I said, "How terrible for me! I am ruined! For I am a man with unclean lips, and I live among a people with unclean lips. And my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Armies!"
Then one of the seraphs flew to me holding a burning coal, which he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He touched my mouth with it and said, "Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is taken away, and your sin is forgiven."
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?" And I said, "Here I am. Send me!"
He said, "Go and tell this people: 'You will keep hearing, but you will not understand. You will keep seeing, but you will not know what you see.'

Make the hearts of these people hard. Make their ears deaf and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back to me, and be healed."
Then I asked, "Lord, how long?" He answered, "Until the cities lie in ruins with no one living in them, until the houses are empty of people, and the land is completely ruined,
until the LORD has sent everyone far away, and the land is left completely empty.
Even if a tenth of the people remain, it will be burned again. But like a terebinth or an oak that leaves a stump when it is cut down, the holy seed will be its stump."
When Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, King Rezin of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched up to fight against Jerusalem, but they could not conquer it.
The royal family of David was told, "Syria has joined forces with Ephraim." So the hearts of Ahaz and his people shook, like trees in the forest shaking in the wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out with your son Shear Jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the water channel of the upper pool, on the road to the washerman's field.
Tell him: 'Be careful and stay calm. Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of these two burnt out stumps of smoking firewood, the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria and of the son of Remaliah.
Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have made evil plans against you. They have said,
"Let us attack Judah and tear it apart. Let us divide it among ourselves and make the son of Tabeel king over it."
But this is what the Lord GOD says: "It will not stand. It will not happen."
For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is only Rezin. Within sixty five years Ephraim will be shattered and will no longer be a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is only the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, you will not stand at all.'"
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again and said,
"Ask the LORD your God for a sign. Ask for anything, from the deepest depths or from the highest heights."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask. I will not put the LORD to the test."
Then Isaiah said, "Listen now, family of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of people? Must you also try the patience of my God?
So the Lord himself will give you a sign: Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and she will call him Immanuel.
He will eat butter and honey by the time he knows how to refuse evil and choose good.
For before the child knows how to refuse evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you are so afraid of will be left empty.
The LORD will bring on you, your people, and your father's family a time worse than any since Ephraim broke away from Judah. He will bring the king of Assyria."
On that day the LORD will whistle for the flies from the far streams of the Nile in Egypt, and for the bees from the land of Assyria.
They will come and settle in the steep valleys, in the cracks of the rocks, on all the thorn bushes, and in all the pastures.
On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates River, the king of Assyria, to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to cut off your beard too.
On that day a person will keep alive only one young cow and two sheep.
But they will give so much milk that the person will have butter to eat. Everyone left in the land will eat butter and honey.
On that day every place that once had a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be covered with briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows to hunt, because the whole land will be covered with briers and thorns.
You will no longer go to the hills that were once dug with a hoe, because you will be afraid of the briers and thorns. They will become places where cattle are let loose and where sheep walk around.
The LORD said to me, "Take a large writing tablet and write on it in plain letters: 'Maher Shalal Hash Baz.'"
"And I will call reliable witnesses to confirm it: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah."
Then I went to the prophetess, my wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. The LORD said to me, "Name him 'Maher Shalal Hash Baz.'
For before the boy knows how to say 'My father' or 'My mother,' the riches of Damascus and the treasures of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria."
The LORD spoke to me again and said,
"These people have rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, and they are glad about Rezin and the son of Remaliah.
So look, the Lord is about to bring against them the mighty flood waters of the Euphrates River, the king of Assyria with all his power. It will rise over all its channels and run over all its banks.
It will sweep on into Judah, flooding and rising up to the neck. Its spreading wings will cover the whole width of your land, Immanuel!"
Raise the battle cry, you nations, and be shattered! Listen, all you distant lands: get ready for battle and be shattered! Get ready for battle and be shattered!
Make your plans together, but they will come to nothing. Give your orders, but they will not stand, for God is with us.
The LORD spoke to me with his strong hand on me, and he warned me not to follow the ways of this people. He said,
"Do not call everything a plot that these people call a plot. Do not fear what they fear, and do not be terrified.
The LORD of Armies is the one you must treat as holy. He is the one you should fear. He is the one you should dread.

He will be a holy place of safety. But for both kingdoms of Israel he will be a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall. And for the people of Jerusalem he will be a trap and a snare.
Many of them will stumble. They will fall and be broken. They will be trapped and captured."
Wrap up this message as a witness. Seal up this teaching among my followers.
I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding his face from the people of Jacob. I will put my hope in him.
Here I am, with the children the LORD has given me. We are signs and wonders in Israel from the LORD of Armies, who lives on Mount Zion.
People will say to you, "Ask the mediums and the spiritists, who whisper and mutter." But should not a people ask their God? Why ask the dead on behalf of the living?
Go to God's teaching and his warning! If they do not speak according to this word, there is no light of dawn for them.
They will wander through the land, deeply troubled and hungry. When they are hungry, they will become angry and curse their king and their God. They will look up toward heaven,
and then look down at the earth, and they will see only trouble, darkness, and frightening gloom. They will be thrown out into deep darkness.

But there will be no more gloom for the land that was in trouble. In the past, God humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali. But in the future he will make it glorious, the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. A light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death.

You have made the nation grow larger. You have increased their joy. They are happy in your presence, like people are happy at harvest time, like soldiers are glad when they divide the treasure they captured.
For you have broken the heavy yoke on their shoulders, the rod used to beat them, and the stick of the one who treated them cruelly, just as you did on the day you defeated Midian.
Every warrior's boot used in the noisy battle, and every piece of clothing rolled in blood, will be burned. They will be fuel for the fire.

For a child has been born to us. A son has been given to us. He will carry the responsibility of ruling on his shoulders. He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

His rule and his peace will keep growing, and there will be no end to them. He will rule on the throne of David and over his kingdom. He will set it up firmly and keep it strong with justice and righteousness from that time on and forever. The burning love of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.
The Lord has sent a message against the people of Jacob, and it has fallen on Israel.
All the people will know it, Ephraim and the people living in Samaria, who say with pride and arrogant hearts,
"The bricks have fallen down, but we will rebuild with cut stone. The fig trees have been cut down, but we will plant cedars in their place."
So the LORD has made the enemies of Rezin strong against them, and he has stirred up their enemies.
The Syrians from the east and the Philistines from the west have swallowed up Israel with open mouths. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
But the people have not turned back to the one who struck them. They have not looked for the LORD of Armies.
So the LORD will cut off from Israel both head and tail, both palm branch and reed, in a single day.
The elders and important people are the head, and the prophets who teach lies are the tail.
Those who lead these people mislead them, and those who are led are swallowed up.

So the Lord will not be pleased with their young men, and he will not show pity to their orphans and widows. For everyone is godless and evil, and every mouth speaks foolishness. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
Wickedness burns like a fire. It eats up the briers and thorns. It sets the thick forest on fire, and it rises up in a column of smoke.
Because of the anger of the LORD of Armies, the land is burned up, and the people are like fuel for the fire. No one spares even their own brother.
They grab food on the right, but are still hungry. They eat on the left, but are not satisfied. Each one eats the flesh of their own arm.
Manasseh eats Ephraim, and Ephraim eats Manasseh, and together they turn against Judah. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
How terrible for those who make unfair laws, and for those who write laws that hurt people,
to take away justice from the needy and rob the poor among my people of their rights. They make widows their victims and rob orphans!
What will you do on the day of punishment, when disaster comes from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you leave your riches?
There will be nothing left to do but bow down among the prisoners or fall among the dead. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
How terrible for Assyria, the rod of my anger! The club in its hand is my fury.
I am sending Assyria against a godless nation. I am commanding it to attack the people who make me angry, to take their goods and steal their treasure, and to trample them like mud in the streets.
But that is not what Assyria intends. That is not what it has in mind. Its plan is to destroy, to wipe out many nations.
For the king of Assyria says, "Are not all my commanders kings?
Was not Calno conquered like Carchemish? Was not Hamath like Arpad? Was not Samaria like Damascus?
My hand has taken hold of kingdoms full of idols, kingdoms whose carved images were greater than those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
I have dealt with Samaria and its idols. Shall I not do the same to Jerusalem and its idols?"
When the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will say, "I will punish the king of Assyria for the proud boasting of his heart and the arrogant look in his eyes."

For the king says, "I have done this by the strength of my own hand and by my own wisdom, because I am clever. I have moved the borders of nations and stolen their treasures. Like a mighty bull, I have brought down their rulers.

My hand has taken the riches of the nations like someone reaching into a bird's nest. Like people gathering eggs that have been left behind, I have gathered up the whole earth. Not one flapped a wing, or opened its mouth, or made a sound."

Does an axe brag that it is greater than the person who swings it? Does a saw boast against the one who uses it? That would be like a rod lifting up the person who holds it, or a wooden stick lifting up someone who is not made of wood!
So the Lord GOD of Armies will send a wasting sickness on the king's strong warriors. Under his glory a fire will be lit, burning like a blazing flame.
The Light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One will become a flame. In a single day it will burn up and destroy his thorns and briers.
It will completely destroy the glory of his forests and his fertile fields, both body and soul. It will be like a sick person wasting away.
The trees left in his forests will be so few that a child could count them and write them down.
On that day the survivors of Israel, those who are left of the people of Jacob, will no longer depend on the one who struck them down. They will truly depend on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A small group will return, the survivors of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
Even though your people, Israel, are as many as the sand on the seashore, only a few will return. Destruction has been decided, and it will flood the land with righteous judgment.
For the Lord GOD of Armies will carry out the destruction he has decided on, throughout the whole land.
So this is what the Lord GOD of Armies says: "My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians, even though they beat you with a rod and raise a club against you, as Egypt did.
In a very short time my anger against you will end, and my anger will turn to destroy them."
The LORD of Armies will beat them with a whip, as he struck down Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise his staff over the waters, as he did in Egypt.
On that day their heavy load will be lifted from your shoulders, and their yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because you have grown so strong.
The enemy has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. He stores his supplies at Michmash.
They have crossed the pass and spent the night at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has run away.
Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is running away. The people of Gebim are running for safety.
This very day the enemy will stop at Nob. He shakes his fist at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord GOD of Armies will cut off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, and the proud will be brought low.
He will cut down the thick forest with an iron axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
A shoot will grow from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.
The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of good advice and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and deep respect for the LORD.
He will delight in respecting the LORD. He will not judge by what he sees with his eyes, or decide by what he hears with his ears.

Instead, he will judge the poor fairly and make right decisions for the humble people of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his words, and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
Righteousness will be like a belt around his waist, and faithfulness like a belt around his hips.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf will be together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will eat together. Their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
A baby will play near the hole of a cobra, and a young child will put their hand into the nest of a poisonous snake.
They will not hurt or destroy anything on all my holy mountain. For the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
On that day the root of Jesse will stand as a flag for the peoples. The nations will come looking for him, and the place where he rests will be glorious.
On that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to bring back the survivors of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He will raise a flag for the nations. He will gather the people of Israel who were driven out, and bring together the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's jealousy will disappear, and the enemies of Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not be hostile toward Ephraim.

They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west. Together they will take treasure from the people of the east. They will take control of Edom and Moab, and the people of Ammon will obey them.
