The LORD will completely dry up the gulf of the Egyptian sea. With his scorching wind he will sweep his hand over the Euphrates River. He will split it into seven streams, so that people can walk across in sandals.
There will be a highway for the survivors of his people coming from Assyria, just as there was for Israel when they came up out of the land of Egypt.
On that day you will say: "I will thank you, LORD. Even though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away, and you comfort me.
Look, God is my salvation. I will trust him and not be afraid. For the LORD, yes the LORD, is my strength and my song. He has become my salvation."
With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
On that day you will say: "Thank the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the nations what he has done! Announce that his name is lifted high!
Sing to the LORD, for he has done wonderful things! Let this be known in all the earth!
Shout out loud and sing for joy, people of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel among you is great!"
This is the message of judgment against Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a flag on a bare hilltop! Shout to the soldiers! Wave your hand to signal them to march through the gates of the nobles.
I have given orders to my chosen soldiers. Yes, I have called my warriors to carry out my anger, those who celebrate my victory with pride.
Listen to the noise on the mountains, like the noise of a huge crowd! Listen to the uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathering together! The LORD of Armies is gathering an army for battle.
They come from a faraway land, from the ends of the sky. The LORD and the weapons of his anger are coming to destroy the whole land.
Cry out, for the day of the LORD is near! It will come like destruction from the Almighty.
So every hand will hang down weak, and every heart will melt with fear.
They will be terrified. Pain and sorrow will grab them. They will twist in pain like a woman giving birth. They will look at each other in shock, their faces burning red.
Look, the day of the LORD is coming, a cruel day of fury and fierce anger. It will make the land a wasteland and destroy the sinners in it.
The stars of the sky and their groups will not give their light. The sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon will not shine.
I will punish the world for its evil, and the wicked for their sins. I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant and humble the pride of the cruel.
I will make people harder to find than pure gold, rarer than the gold of Ophir.
So I will make the heavens shake, and the earth will be shaken out of its place, because of the fury of the LORD of Armies on the day of his fierce anger.
Like a hunted gazelle, like sheep with no shepherd to gather them, everyone will go back to their own people and run away to their own land.
Everyone who is found will be stabbed. Everyone who is caught will die by the sword.
Their babies will be smashed to pieces before their eyes. Their houses will be robbed, and their wives will be raped.
Look, I will stir up the Medes against them, who do not care about silver and do not desire gold.
Their bows will strike down the young men. They will have no pity on babies and will not spare the children.
Babylon, the most glorious of kingdoms, the beauty and pride of the Babylonians, will be destroyed by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
No one will ever live there again, generation after generation. No Arab will set up a tent there, and no shepherds will rest their flocks there.
Instead, wild desert animals will lie down there, and its houses will be full of jackals. Owls will live there, and wild goats will leap about there.
Hyenas will howl in its towers, and jackals in its beautiful palaces. Its time is almost here, and its days will not last much longer.
The LORD will have mercy on Jacob and will choose Israel again. He will settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and unite with the people of Jacob.

The nations will take them and bring them back to their own place. Then the people of Israel will make those nations their servants in the LORD's land. They will capture those who once captured them, and they will rule over those who once treated them cruelly.
On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain, your trouble, and the hard labor you were forced to do,
you will sing this mocking song about the king of Babylon: "See how the cruel ruler has come to an end! His fury has come to an end!
The LORD has broken the rod of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers,
who struck the peoples in anger with blow after blow, who ruled the nations in fury and attacked them without stopping.
Now the whole earth is at rest and is quiet. People break out in song.
Even the cypress trees and the cedars of Lebanon celebrate over you. They say, 'Since you have been brought down, no woodcutter comes to cut us down.'

The grave below is excited to meet you when you arrive. It wakes up the spirits of the dead to greet you, all who were leaders of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
They will all say to you, 'You have become as weak as we are! You have become just like us!'
All your splendor has been brought down to the grave, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed, and worms are your blanket.
How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! You have been thrown down to the earth, you who once conquered the nations!
You said in your heart, 'I will go up to heaven! I will raise my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain where the gods gather, far away in the north!
I will go up above the tops of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!'
But you will be brought down to the grave, to the deepest part of the pit.
Those who see you will stare at you and think about you. They will say, 'Is this the man who made the earth shake, who made kingdoms tremble,
who turned the world into a wilderness, who destroyed its cities, and who would not let his prisoners go home?'
All the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own tomb.
But you are thrown out of your grave like a rejected branch. You are covered with the dead, those killed by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit, like a dead body trampled underfoot.
You will not be buried with them, because you destroyed your own land and killed your own people. The children of evildoers will never be mentioned again.
Get ready to kill his sons because of the sins of their fathers. Do not let them rise up and take over the earth, or fill the world with their cities."
"I will rise up against them," says the LORD of Armies. "I will wipe out Babylon's name and its survivors, its children and its grandchildren," says the LORD.
"I will make it a place for owls and swamps of water. I will sweep it away with the broom of destruction," says the LORD of Armies.
The LORD of Armies has made a promise: "Surely, what I have planned will happen, and what I have decided will stand.
I will crush the Assyrians in my land and trample them on my mountains. Their yoke will be taken off my people, and their heavy load will be lifted from their shoulders."
This is the plan decided for the whole earth. This is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of Armies has made his plan. Who can stop it? His hand is stretched out. Who can turn it back?
This message came in the year that King Ahaz died:
Do not celebrate, all you Philistines, because the rod that struck you is broken. For from the root of that snake a poisonous snake will grow, and its young will be a fiery flying serpent.
The poorest of the poor will find food, and the needy will lie down in safety. But I will kill your root with hunger, and it will kill your survivors.
Cry out, you gates! Weep, you city! Melt away with fear, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke is coming from the north, and not one soldier in its army falls behind.
What answer shall we give the messengers from that nation? That the LORD has built Zion, and in her his suffering people will find safety.
This is the message of judgment against Moab. In one night Ar in Moab is destroyed and ruined. In one night Kir in Moab is destroyed and ruined.
The people go up to the temple and to Dibon, to their high places, to weep. Moab cries over Nebo and Medeba. Every head is shaved bald, and every beard is cut off.
In the streets they wear sackcloth. On the rooftops and in the town squares everyone cries out, weeping bitterly.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out. Their voices are heard as far away as Jahaz. So the soldiers of Moab cry out, and their hearts tremble inside them.
My heart cries out for Moab! Its people run away to Zoar, as far as Eglath Shelishiyah. They go up the hill to Luhith, weeping as they go. On the road to Horonaim they cry out over their destruction.
The waters of Nimrim are dried up. The grass has dried up, the new grass is gone, and nothing green is left.
So they carry away the riches they have gained and stored up, across the Valley of the Willows.
Their cries are heard all around the borders of Moab. Their weeping reaches as far as Eglaim and Beer Elim.
The waters of Dimon are full of blood, but I will bring even more on Dimon: a lion to attack those of Moab who escape, and those who are left in the land.
Send lambs as a gift to the ruler of the land, from Sela across the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
Like birds that have been chased away, like a nest that has been scattered, so are the women of Moab at the crossings of the Arnon River.
"Give us advice! Make a fair decision! Cover us with your shade like night in the middle of the day! Hide those who have been driven out! Do not betray those who are running for their lives!

Let the people driven out of Moab stay with you. Be a hiding place for them from the destroyer." For the one who treats people cruelly will come to an end. Destruction will stop. The attacker will disappear from the land.
Then a throne will be set up in faithful love. Someone from the family of David will sit on it in faithfulness. He will judge fairly, seek justice, and be quick to do what is right.
We have heard about Moab's pride, how very proud it is. We have heard of its arrogance, its pride, and its anger. But its boasting is empty.
So the people of Moab will cry. Everyone will cry for Moab. You will mourn and be heartbroken for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth.

The fields of Heshbon are dying, and so are the vines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its best vines, which once reached as far as Jazer and spread out into the wilderness. Its branches spread out and went across the sea.
So I weep, as Jazer weeps, for the vines of Sibmah. I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh. For the shouts of battle have fallen on your summer fruit and your harvest.
Happiness and joy are taken away from the fruitful fields. No one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one stomps grapes in the winepresses. I have put an end to the shouting.
So my heart cries for Moab like the sad music of a harp, and my inner being aches for Kir Hareseth.
When Moab goes to its high place and wears itself out, when it goes to its temple to pray, it will do no good.
This is the message the LORD spoke about Moab in the past.

But now the LORD says, "Within three years, counted exactly as a hired worker counts the years, Moab's glory will be brought down, along with all its many people. Only a few will be left, and they will be weak."
This is the message of judgment against Damascus: "Look, Damascus will no longer be a city. It will become a heap of ruins.
The cities of Aroer will be deserted. They will become places for flocks to lie down, and no one will scare them away.
The strong cities of Ephraim will disappear, and the kingdom of Damascus will come to an end. The survivors of Syria will be like the faded glory of the people of Israel," says the LORD of Armies.
"On that day the glory of Jacob will fade, and his strong body will waste away.
It will be like a harvester gathering wheat, cutting the grain with his arm. It will be like someone picking up the leftover grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

Yet some will be left, like the olives left after an olive tree is beaten, two or three at the very top of the tree, four or five on the outer branches of a fruit tree," says the LORD, the God of Israel.
On that day people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will turn to the Holy One of Israel.
They will no longer look to the altars they made with their own hands. They will not respect what their fingers have made, the Asherah poles or the incense altars.
On that day their strong cities will be like deserted places in the forests and on the hilltops, which people left when the Israelites came. Everything will be ruined.
For you have forgotten the God who saves you. You have not remembered the Rock who makes you strong. So you plant beautiful gardens and set out vines from foreign lands.
On the day you plant them, you put a fence around them. In the morning you make your seeds sprout. But the harvest will disappear on a day of sickness and pain that cannot be cured.
Oh, the roaring of many peoples, roaring like the roaring of the seas! The rushing of nations, rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!

The nations rush like the rushing of mighty waters, but when God speaks sternly to them, they run far away. They are chased away like chaff blown by the wind on the hills, like dust whirling in a storm.
In the evening, look, there is sudden terror! By morning they are gone. This is what happens to those who rob us. This is the fate of those who steal from us.
How terrible for the land of buzzing wings, the land beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,

which sends messengers by sea in boats made of papyrus on the waters! Go, you fast messengers, to a nation of tall people with smooth skin, a people feared near and far, a strong nation that conquers others, whose land is divided by rivers.
All you people of the world, all who live on the earth: when a flag is raised on the mountains, look! When the trumpet sounds, listen!
For this is what the LORD said to me: "I will quietly watch from my home, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives. He will cut down and take away the spreading branches.
They will all be left for the birds of prey on the mountains and for the wild animals. The birds will feed on them all summer, and the wild animals all winter.

At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Armies from a people tall and smooth skinned, a people feared near and far, a strong nation that conquers others, whose land is divided by rivers. The gifts will be brought to Mount Zion, the place of the name of the LORD of Armies.
This is the message of judgment against Egypt: "Look, the LORD is riding on a fast cloud and coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt tremble before him, and the hearts of the Egyptians melt with fear.
I will turn Egyptians against Egyptians. Brother will fight brother, and neighbor will fight neighbor. City will fight city, and kingdom will fight kingdom.
The Egyptians will lose heart, and I will bring their plans to nothing. They will ask their idols, the spirits of the dead, the mediums, and the fortune tellers for help.
I will hand the Egyptians over to a cruel master, and a fierce king will rule over them," says the Lord GOD of Armies.
The waters of the river will dry up, and the Nile will become empty and dry.
The canals will stink. The streams of Egypt will shrink and dry up. The reeds and rushes will wither.
The plants along the Nile, at the edge of the river, and every field planted by the Nile, will dry up, blow away, and be gone.
The fishermen will cry and mourn. Everyone who throws a hook into the Nile will be sad, and those who spread nets on the water will lose heart.
Those who work with combed flax will be in despair, and the weavers of fine white cloth will lose hope.
The workers who weave cloth will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be sick at heart.
The officials of Zoan are complete fools. Pharaoh's wisest advisers give stupid advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am one of the wise men, a son of ancient kings"?
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and show you what the LORD of Armies has planned against Egypt.
The officials of Zoan have become fools. The leaders of Memphis are fooled. The leaders of its tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has poured into them a spirit of confusion. They make Egypt stagger in everything it does, like a drunk person staggering in their own vomit.
There is nothing Egypt can do, no one at all, head or tail, palm branch or reed.
On that day the Egyptians will be weak like frightened women. They will shake with fear when the LORD of Armies raises his hand against them.
The land of Judah will terrify the Egyptians. Everyone who hears Judah's name will be afraid, because of what the LORD of Armies has planned against them.
On that day five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and promise to be loyal to the LORD of Armies. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
On that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of Egypt, and a stone pillar to the LORD at its border.

It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Armies in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of those who treat them cruelly, he will send them a savior and defender, and he will rescue them.
The LORD will make himself known to Egypt, and on that day the Egyptians will know the LORD. They will worship him with sacrifices and offerings. They will make promises to the LORD and keep them.
The LORD will strike Egypt, but he will also heal it. They will turn to the LORD, and he will listen to their prayers and heal them.
On that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt, and the Egyptians to Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
On that day Israel will join Egypt and Assyria as the third, a blessing in the middle of the earth.
The LORD of Armies will bless them and say, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my special possession."
In the year that the army commander came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.
At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz. He said, "Go, take off the sackcloth from your body and the sandals from your feet." So Isaiah did this, walking around naked and barefoot.
Then the LORD said, "My servant Isaiah has walked around naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a warning against Egypt and Ethiopia.
In the same way the king of Assyria will lead away the prisoners from Egypt and the captives from Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their bottoms uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
Those who trusted in Ethiopia and boasted about Egypt will be terrified and ashamed.
On that day the people who live on this coast will say, 'Look what has happened to the ones we trusted, the ones we ran to for help to save us from the king of Assyria! How can we escape now?'"
This is the message of judgment against the wilderness by the sea. Like whirlwinds sweeping through the south, an enemy is coming from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
I have been shown a terrible vision: the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Attack, Media! I will put an end to all the groaning Babylon caused.
So my body is filled with pain. Pains have grabbed me, like the pains of a woman giving birth. I am so troubled that I cannot hear. I am so terrified that I cannot see.
My heart is pounding, and fear makes me shake. The evening I longed for has become a time of trembling.
They set the table. They spread out the rugs. They eat and they drink. Get up, you commanders! Oil your shields!
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Go, post a watchman and have him report what he sees.
When he sees chariots with pairs of horsemen, riders on donkeys, or riders on camels, let him listen carefully, very carefully."
Then the watchman shouted like a lion: "Lord, I stand on the watchtower every day, and I stay at my post every night.
Look, here comes a chariot with a pair of horsemen!" Then he answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the carved images of its gods lie broken on the ground!"
My people, crushed like grain on the threshing floor, I have told you what I heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel.
This is the message of judgment against Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, how much of the night is left? Watchman, how much of the night is left?"
The watchman answers, "Morning is coming, but night is coming too. If you want to ask, then ask. Come back again."
This is the message of judgment against Arabia. You traveling groups of Dedanites, who camp in the thick bushes of Arabia,
bring water for the thirsty. You people of Tema, bring food for those running away.
For they are running from swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one year, counted exactly as a hired worker counts the years, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
Only a few of the archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be left. The LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken."
This is the message of judgment against the Valley of Vision. What is wrong with you, that you have all gone up on the rooftops?
You city full of noise and shouting, you town full of partying! Your dead were not killed by the sword, and they did not die in battle.
All your leaders ran away together. They were captured without anyone using a bow. All of you who were found were captured together, even though you had run far away.
So I said, "Turn away from me. Let me weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me about the destruction of my people."
For the Lord GOD of Armies has brought a day of panic, of trampling, and of confusion in the Valley of Vision. It is a day of walls being broken down and of crying out to the mountains.
Elam picks up its arrows, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir takes the cover off its shield.
Your best valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen take their positions at the city gates.
God has taken away Judah's protection. On that day you looked to the weapons in the Palace of the Forest.
You saw that there were many cracks in the walls of the City of David. You stored up water in the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you tore houses down to make the wall stronger.
You built a pool between the two walls for the water from the old pool. But you did not look to the one who made it all happen. You did not respect the one who planned it long ago.
On that day the Lord GOD of Armies called you to weep and to mourn, to shave your heads and to wear sackcloth.
But look, instead there is joy and celebration, killing cattle and sheep, eating meat and drinking wine. You say, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The LORD of Armies has told me this: "Surely this sin will not be forgiven you until the day you die," says the Lord GOD of Armies.
This is what the Lord GOD of Armies says: "Go to this official, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace, and say to him:
'What are you doing here? Who gave you permission to cut out a tomb for yourself here, carving your grave up high, chiseling a resting place for yourself in the rock?'
Look, the LORD is about to grab you firmly and throw you away, you mighty man.
He will roll you up tightly like a ball and throw you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your fine chariots will stay. You are a disgrace to your master's house!
I will remove you from your office, and you will be pulled down from your position.
On that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
I will dress him in your robe and put your belt around him. I will give him your authority. He will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the people of Judah.
I will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder. What he opens, no one can shut, and what he shuts, no one can open.
I will fix him firmly like a peg in a solid wall. He will be a place of honor for his father's family.
All the glory of his father's family will hang on him, their children and grandchildren, like all the small dishes, from bowls to jars."
"On that day," says the LORD of Armies, "the peg fixed in the solid wall will give way. It will break off and fall, and the load hanging on it will crash down. The LORD has spoken."
This is the message of judgment against Tyre. Cry out, you ships of Tarshish! For Tyre is destroyed, with no house left and no harbor to enter. The news has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
Be silent, you people who live on the coast, you traders of Sidon, who grew rich from those who sail the sea.
On the great waters came the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile. That was Tyre's income. She was the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the strong fortress of the sea says, "I have never been in labor or given birth. I have never raised sons or brought up daughters."
When the news reaches Egypt, they will be in great pain over the report about Tyre.
Sail across to Tarshish! Cry out, you people who live on the coast!
Is this your city of celebration, the ancient city, whose people traveled to settle in faraway lands?
Who planned this against Tyre, the city that gave out crowns, whose traders were princes, whose merchants were honored all over the earth?
The LORD of Armies planned it, to bring down the pride of all its glory and to humble all who were honored on earth.
Go through your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. There is no harbor anymore.
The LORD has stretched out his hand over the sea and made kingdoms shake. He has given orders to destroy the strong cities of Canaan.
He said, "You will celebrate no more, crushed virgin daughter of Sidon. Get up, cross over to Cyprus. Even there you will find no rest."
Look at the land of the Babylonians. That people is no more. The Assyrians made it a place for desert creatures. They built their siege towers, tore down its palaces, and made it a ruin.
Cry out, you ships of Tarshish, for your fortress is destroyed!
On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the length of a king's life. At the end of seventy years, Tyre will be like the prostitute in the song:
"Pick up a harp and walk around the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play sweetly, sing many songs, so that you will be remembered."
At the end of seventy years, the LORD will deal with Tyre. She will go back to earning her pay and will sell herself to all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

But her profits and her pay will be set apart for the LORD. They will not be stored up or saved. Her profits will go to those who live in the presence of the LORD, so they will have plenty of food and fine clothes.
Look, the LORD is about to empty the earth and ruin it. He will turn it upside down and scatter the people who live on it.

It will be the same for everyone: for the people and the priest, for the servant and the master, for the maid and her mistress, for the buyer and the seller, for the lender and the borrower, for the one who collects interest and the one who pays it.
The earth will be completely emptied and completely ruined, for the LORD has spoken this word.
The earth dries up and withers. The world fades away and withers. The great people of the earth grow weak.
The earth is made unclean by the people who live on it, because they have disobeyed the laws, broken the rules, and broken the everlasting covenant.
So a curse eats up the earth, and its people must pay for their guilt. So the people of the earth are burned up, and only a few are left.
The new wine dries up, and the vine withers. All who were happy now groan.
The happy sound of tambourines is silent. The noise of those who celebrate has stopped. The joyful harp is quiet.
People no longer drink wine with a song. Strong drink tastes bitter to those who drink it.
The city of chaos is broken down. Every house is shut up so no one can enter.
People cry out in the streets for wine. All joy has turned to gloom. All happiness has left the land.
The city is left in ruins, and its gate is smashed to pieces.
This is how it will be on the earth among the nations: like an olive tree after it has been beaten, like the few grapes left after the harvest.
But those who are left raise their voices and shout for joy. They shout from the west about the majesty of the LORD.
So give glory to the LORD in the east. Praise the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, in the islands of the sea!

From the ends of the earth we hear songs: "Glory to the Righteous One!" But I said, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! How terrible for me!" Traitors betray. Yes, traitors betray with great treachery.
Terror, a pit, and a trap are waiting for you, people of the earth.

Whoever runs away from the sound of terror will fall into the pit. Whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For the floodgates of the heavens are opened, and the foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is completely broken. The earth is split apart. The earth is shaken violently.
The earth staggers like a drunk person. It sways back and forth like a hut in the wind. Its sin is so heavy on it that it falls and will never rise again.
On that day the LORD will punish the powers in the heavens above and the kings on the earth below.
They will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit. They will be shut up in prison, and after many days they will be punished.
Then the moon will be embarrassed and the sun will be ashamed. For the LORD of Armies will rule as king on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and he will show his glory in front of his elders.
LORD, you are my God. I will lift you high and praise your name, for you have done wonderful things. You planned them long ago, and you have carried them out faithfully and truly.
You have turned the city into a heap of rubble, the strong city into a ruin. The palace of foreigners is no longer a city. It will never be rebuilt.
So strong peoples will honor you. Cities of cruel nations will respect you.

You have been a safe place for the poor, a safe place for the needy in their trouble, a shelter from the storm, and shade from the heat. For the breath of the cruel is like a storm beating against a wall.
Like heat in a dry land, you silence the noise of foreigners. Like heat cooled by the shade of a cloud, the song of the cruel is silenced.
On this mountain the LORD of Armies will prepare a feast for all peoples, a feast of the richest food and the finest wine, the best meat and the purest wine.
On this mountain he will destroy the covering that is over all peoples, the veil that is spread over all nations.
He will swallow up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face. He will take away the shame of his people from all the earth. The LORD has spoken.
On that day people will say, "Look, this is our God! We waited for him, and he saved us! This is the LORD! We waited for him. Let us be glad and celebrate because he has saved us!"
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled down where it stands, like straw trampled into a manure pile.
Moab will stretch out its hands in it, like a swimmer stretching out their hands to swim. But God will bring down its pride, along with all the clever things its hands have done.
He will bring down your high, strong walls. He will tear them down and throw them to the ground, into the dust.
On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city. God makes salvation its walls and its defenses.
Open the gates, so that the righteous nation may enter, the nation that stays faithful.
You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds stay fixed on you, because they trust in you.
Trust in the LORD forever, for the LORD, the LORD himself, is the Rock that lasts forever.
He brings down those who live up high. He brings down the proud city. He brings it down to the ground. He throws it into the dust.
Feet trample it down, the feet of the poor and the steps of the needy."
The path of the righteous is level. You, the Upright One, make the way of the righteous smooth.
Yes, LORD, we wait for you as we walk in the way of your laws. Your name and your fame are what our hearts desire.
My soul longs for you in the night. Yes, my spirit inside me looks for you eagerly. For when your judgments come on the earth, the people of the world learn what is right.
Even when kindness is shown to the wicked, they do not learn what is right. Even in a land of honest people they keep doing evil, and they do not see the majesty of the LORD.
LORD, your hand is raised, but they do not see it. Let them see your burning love for your people and be ashamed. Let the fire saved for your enemies burn them up.
LORD, you give us peace. Everything we have done, you have done for us.
LORD our God, other masters besides you have ruled over us, but your name alone is the one we honor.
Those masters are dead. They will not live again. Their spirits will not rise. You punished them and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
You have made the nation grow, LORD. You have made the nation grow! You have shown your glory. You have pushed back all the borders of the land.
LORD, they came to you in their trouble. When you disciplined them, they could only whisper a prayer.
Like a pregnant woman about to give birth, who twists in pain and cries out, so were we because of you, LORD.
We were pregnant. We twisted in pain, but we gave birth only to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth, and no new people have been born into the world.
But your dead will live. Their bodies will rise again. You who live in the dust, wake up and shout for joy! For your dew is like the morning dew, and the earth will give birth to its dead.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut the doors behind you. Hide yourselves for a little while, until God's anger has passed.
For look, the LORD is coming out of his place to punish the people of the earth for their sins. The earth will uncover the blood spilled on it. It will no longer hide those who were killed.
On that day the LORD will punish Leviathan, the gliding serpent, Leviathan, the twisting serpent, with his fierce, great, and powerful sword. He will kill the dragon of the sea.
On that day, sing about a fruitful vineyard:
"I, the LORD, take care of it. I water it all the time. I guard it day and night so that no one can harm it.
I am not angry anymore. But if I find briers and thorns, I will go to battle against them. I will march out and burn them all up together.
Or else let them come to me for safety. Let them make peace with me. Yes, let them make peace with me."
In the days to come Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
Has the LORD struck Israel as hard as he struck those who struck Israel? Has Israel been killed like those who killed them?
No, he punished them by sending them away into exile. He drove them out with his fierce wind, like the east wind.

In this way Jacob's guilt will be forgiven, and this is how his sin will be taken away: he will crush all the stones of the pagan altars like chalk, so that no Asherah poles or incense altars will be left standing.
The strong city is deserted, an empty place left behind like the wilderness. Calves feed there and lie down there. They strip its branches bare.

When its branches dry up, they are broken off, and women come and use them to make fires. For these are people without understanding. So the one who made them will not have pity on them. The one who formed them will show them no kindness.
On that day the LORD will thresh like a farmer, from the Euphrates River to the brook of Egypt. And you, people of Israel, will be gathered up one by one.

On that day a great trumpet will sound. Those who were dying in the land of Assyria, and those who were driven out to the land of Egypt, will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
How terrible for the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, and for the fading flower of its glorious beauty, set on the head of the fertile valley, the city of those overcome by wine!
Look, the Lord has someone who is mighty and strong. Like a hailstorm, a destroying storm, like a flood of powerful overflowing waters, he will throw that crown down to the ground with his hand.
The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.
The fading flower of its glorious beauty, set on the head of the fertile valley, will be like a fig that ripens before the summer harvest. As soon as someone sees it, they pick it and eat it.
On that day the LORD of Armies will be a glorious crown and a beautiful wreath for those of his people who are left.
He will give a spirit of justice to the one who sits as judge, and strength to those who turn back the enemy at the gate.

But these also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink. Priests and prophets stagger from strong drink. They are confused by wine. They stumble from strong drink. They make mistakes when they see visions. They stumble when they make decisions.
All their tables are covered with vomit and filth. There is no clean place left.
They say, "Who does he think he is teaching? Who is he explaining his message to? Babies who have just stopped drinking milk, who have just been taken from the breast?
For he says: rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there."
So God will speak to this people through strange lips and a foreign language.
He told them, "This is the place of rest. Let the tired rest. This is the place of peace." But they would not listen.

So the word of the LORD to them will become: rule on rule, rule on rule, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there. Then they will go, fall backward, and be broken. They will be trapped and captured.
So listen to the word of the LORD, you mockers who rule these people in Jerusalem.

You say, "We have made a covenant with death. We have made a deal with the grave. When the overwhelming flood sweeps by, it cannot touch us, for we have made lies our hiding place, and we have hidden ourselves behind falsehood."
So this is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, I am laying a stone in Zion as a foundation, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a firm foundation. Whoever believes will never panic.
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail will sweep away your hiding place of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be canceled. Your deal with the grave will not stand. When the overwhelming flood sweeps by, you will be beaten down by it.
Every time it comes, it will carry you away. It will come morning after morning, by day and by night. Understanding this message will bring nothing but terror."
The bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap yourself in.
For the LORD will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim. He will be angry as he was in the Valley of Gibeon. He will do his work, his strange work, and carry out his task, his unusual task.
So now, stop mocking, or your chains will become heavier. For I have heard from the Lord GOD of Armies that destruction has been decided against the whole land.
Listen and hear my voice! Pay attention and hear what I say!
Does a farmer keep plowing all the time to plant? Does he keep breaking up and turning over the soil?
When he has made the ground level, does he not scatter dill and sow cumin? Does he not plant wheat in rows, barley in its proper place, and spelt along the edges?
His God teaches him and shows him the right way.
Dill is not threshed with a heavy sledge, and a cart wheel is not rolled over cumin. Instead, dill is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread must be crushed, but he does not keep threshing it forever. He drives the wheels of his cart over it, but his horses do not crush it to powder.
This also comes from the LORD of Armies, whose plans are wonderful and whose wisdom is great.
How terrible for Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Add year to year, and let your festivals go on.
Then I will bring trouble on Ariel. There will be mourning and weeping. The city will become to me like an altar hearth, burning with fire.
I will set up camp all around you. I will surround you with towers and build siege works against you.

You will be brought low. You will speak from the ground. Your words will come mumbling out of the dust. Your voice will sound like a ghost coming up from the ground. Your words will whisper out of the dust.
But your many enemies will become like fine dust, and the crowds of cruel attackers like chaff blowing away. It will happen suddenly, in an instant.
The LORD of Armies will come against them with thunder, earthquake, and loud noise, with windstorm and storm, and with flames of a fire that burns everything up.
Then the crowds of all the nations that fight against Ariel, that attack her and her fortress and bring trouble on her, will be like a dream, like a vision in the night.

It will be like a hungry person who dreams they are eating, but wakes up still hungry. It will be like a thirsty person who dreams they are drinking, but wakes up weak and still thirsty. That is how it will be for the crowds of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
Be shocked and amazed! Blind yourselves and stay blind! They are drunk, but not from wine. They stagger, but not from strong drink.
For the LORD has poured on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has closed your eyes, you prophets. He has covered your heads, you seers.
This whole vision is like the words of a sealed book to you. If you give it to someone who can read and say, "Please read this," they will answer, "I cannot, because it is sealed."
If you give the book to someone who cannot read and say, "Please read this," they will answer, "I do not know how to read."
The Lord says, "These people come near to me with their mouths and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me. Their worship of me is made up only of rules taught by people.
So once again I will do amazing things among these people, wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of their wise people will disappear, and the understanding of their clever people will vanish."
How terrible for those who try hard to hide their plans from the LORD, who do their work in the dark and say, "Who sees us? Who will know?"

You turn everything upside down! Is the potter the same as the clay? Can something that was made say about the one who made it, "He did not make me"? Can a pot say about the potter, "He knows nothing"?
In a very short time, Lebanon will be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will seem like a forest.
On that day the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of gloom and darkness.
The humble will be filled with fresh joy in the LORD, and the poorest people will celebrate in the Holy One of Israel.
For the cruel will come to nothing, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for chances to do evil will be cut off,
those who make someone guilty with a word, who set traps for the one who defends justice in court, and who use lies to take away justice from the innocent.
So this is what the LORD, who rescued Abraham, says to the people of Jacob: "Jacob will no longer be ashamed. Their faces will no longer turn pale.
When they see their children, the work of my hands, among them, they will honor my name as holy. They will honor the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Those who are confused in spirit will gain understanding, and those who complain will accept teaching."
"How terrible for the rebellious children," says the LORD, "who carry out plans that are not mine, who make agreements without my Spirit, adding sin to sin.
They go down to Egypt without asking me. They look for help from Pharaoh's strength and hide in Egypt's shadow.
But Pharaoh's strength will bring you shame, and hiding in Egypt's shadow will bring you disgrace.
Though Judah's officials are in Zoan and their messengers have arrived in Hanes,
everyone will be put to shame because of a people who cannot help them. Egypt brings no help and no benefit, only shame and disgrace."

This is the message of judgment about the animals of the Negev. Through a land of trouble and danger, of lionesses and lions, of poisonous snakes and fiery flying serpents, the messengers carry their riches on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people who cannot help them.
Egypt's help is useless and empty. So I call her Rahab the Do Nothing.
Now go, write this on a tablet in front of them, and write it in a book, so that it will be a witness for the days to come, forever and ever.
For these are rebellious people, lying children, children who refuse to listen to the LORD's teaching.
They say to the seers, "Stop seeing visions!" and to the prophets, "Do not tell us what is right. Tell us nice things. Prophesy lies.
Get out of our way. Leave the path. Stop telling us about the Holy One of Israel!"
So this is what the Holy One of Israel says: "You have rejected this message. You trust in cruelty and lies, and you depend on them.
So this sin will be like a crack in a high wall, bulging out and about to fall. It will crash down suddenly, in an instant.
It will be smashed like a clay pot, broken so completely that not one piece is left big enough to carry coals from a fire or to scoop water from a well."
This is what the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says: "You will be saved by turning back to me and resting in me. Your strength will come from being calm and trusting me." But you would not do it.
You said, "No, we will run away on horses." So you will run away! You said, "We will ride on fast horses." So those who chase you will be fast!
A thousand of you will run away from the threat of one enemy. At the threat of five, you will all run away, until you are left like a flagpole on a mountaintop, like a flag on a hill.
Yet the LORD is waiting to be kind to you. He rises up to show you mercy. For the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all who wait for him.
You people of Zion who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be kind to you when you cry for help. As soon as he hears you, he will answer you.
Though the Lord gives you the bread of trouble and the water of suffering, your teacher will not hide anymore. You will see your teacher with your own eyes.
Whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the way. Walk in it."
Then you will treat your silver covered idols and your gold covered images as unclean. You will throw them away like dirty rags and say to them, "Go away!"
He will send rain for the seed you plant in the ground, and the food that comes from the land will be rich and plenty. On that day your cattle will graze in wide pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat good feed, spread out with fork and shovel.
On the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall, streams of water will flow on every high mountain and every tall hill.

The moon will shine as brightly as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter, like the light of seven full days, on the day the LORD bandages his people's injuries and heals the wounds he gave them.
Look, the name of the LORD is coming from far away, burning with anger, in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is like a fire that burns everything.
His breath is like a rushing flood that rises up to the neck. He will shake the nations in the sieve of destruction. He will put a bit in the mouths of the peoples that leads them to ruin.
But you will sing as on the night of a holy festival. Your hearts will be glad, like people walking to the music of flutes on their way to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The LORD will make people hear his majestic voice. He will show his arm coming down in raging anger, with flames of fire that burn everything, with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
The voice of the LORD will shatter Assyria. He will strike them with his rod.
Every blow the LORD strikes on them with his punishing rod will be to the music of tambourines and harps, as he fights them in battle with his raised arm.

For a burning place has long been ready. Yes, it has been prepared for the king. Its fire pit has been made deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, sets it on fire.

How terrible for those who go down to Egypt for help, who depend on horses, who trust in their many chariots and in their very strong horsemen, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel or ask the LORD for help!
Yet he too is wise. He can bring disaster, and he does not take back his words. He will rise up against the family of evildoers and against those who help people who do wrong.

The Egyptians are only humans, not God. Their horses are only flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble, and the one being helped will fall. They will all die together.

For this is what the LORD says to me: "When a lion, a young lion, growls over the animal it has caught, and a whole crowd of shepherds is called out against it, it is not frightened by their shouts or troubled by their noise. In the same way the LORD of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill.
Like birds flying over their nests, the LORD of Armies will protect Jerusalem. He will shield it and rescue it. He will pass over it and save it."
People of Israel, turn back to the one you have rebelled against so terribly.
For on that day every one of you will throw away your idols of silver and gold, the sinful idols your hands have made.
"Assyria will fall by a sword, but not a human sword. A sword not made by people will destroy them. They will run from the sword, and their young men will be made to do forced labor.
Their stronghold will fall because of terror, and their commanders will panic at the sight of the battle flag," says the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, a king will rule with righteousness, and leaders will rule with justice.
Each one will be like a shelter from the wind and a hiding place from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shade of a large rock in a tired, thirsty land.
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
The minds of those who act too quickly will understand and know. Those who stutter will speak clearly and easily.
Fools will no longer be called noble, and cheats will no longer be highly respected.
For fools speak foolishness, and their minds plan evil. They do godless things and spread lies about the LORD. They leave the hungry empty and keep water from the thirsty.
The ways of cheats are evil. They make wicked plans to destroy the poor with lies, even when the needy are in the right.
But noble people make noble plans, and by noble deeds they stand.
Get up, you women who are so comfortable, and listen to me! You daughters who feel so secure, hear what I say!
In a little more than a year, you who feel so secure will tremble. For the grape harvest will fail, and the fruit harvest will not come.
Tremble, you women who are so comfortable! Shake with fear, you who feel so secure! Take off your fine clothes and put sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts in sorrow for the pleasant fields and the fruitful vines,
and for the land of my people, where thorns and briers will grow. Yes, mourn for all the happy homes in this joyful city.
For the palace will be deserted, and the busy city will be empty. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever, a joy for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
until the Spirit is poured out on us from heaven. Then the wilderness will become a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will seem like a forest.
Justice will live in the wilderness, and righteousness will stay in the fruitful field.
The result of righteousness will be peace. Its effect will be quietness and confidence forever.
My people will live in peaceful homes, in safe houses, in quiet places of rest,
even if hail flattens the forest and the city is completely torn down.
How blessed you will be, sowing your seed by every stream, and letting your oxen and donkeys roam freely.

How terrible for you, destroyer, who has never been destroyed! How terrible for you, traitor, who has never been betrayed! When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed. When you finish betraying, you will be betrayed.
LORD, be kind to us. We wait for you. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in times of trouble.
At the sound of your thunder, the peoples run away. When you rise up, the nations scatter.
Your enemies' goods will be gathered up as caterpillars strip a field. People will rush on them like a swarm of locusts.
The LORD is lifted high, for he lives in heaven. He will fill Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the firm foundation of your times, a rich store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Deep respect for the LORD is your treasure.
Look, their brave men cry out in the streets. The messengers who hoped for peace weep bitterly.
The highways are empty. No one travels on the roads. The covenant has been broken. Its witnesses are rejected. No one is respected.
The land mourns and dries up. Lebanon is ashamed and withers. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.
"Now I will rise up," says the LORD. "Now I will show my power. Now I will be lifted high.
Your plans are like dry grass, and what you produce is like straw. Your own breath is a fire that will burn you up.
The peoples will be burned to powder like lime, like thorn bushes cut down and thrown into the fire.
You who are far away, listen to what I have done! You who are near, see how powerful I am!"
The sinners in Zion are terrified. The godless are shaking with fear. They ask, "Who of us can live with this consuming fire? Who of us can live with this fire that burns forever?"

The one who lives right and speaks the truth, who refuses to get rich by cheating others, who keeps their hands from taking bribes, who closes their ears to plans of murder, and shuts their eyes so as not to look at evil,
that person will live on the heights. Their safe place will be a fortress of rock. They will be given food, and their water will never run out.
Your eyes will see the King in his beauty. You will see a land that stretches far away.
You will think back on the time of terror and say, "Where is the official who counted? Where is the one who weighed the tribute money? Where is the officer who counted the towers?"
You will no longer see those proud and fierce people, those people with a strange language you could not understand, with their stammering speech that made no sense.

Look at Zion, the city where we celebrate our festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful place to live, a tent that will never be moved. Its tent pegs will never be pulled up, and none of its ropes will be broken.
There the LORD will be our Mighty One. It will be like a place of wide rivers and streams, but no enemy ship with oars will row there, and no mighty warship will sail there.
For the LORD is our judge. The LORD is our lawgiver. The LORD is our king. He is the one who will save us.
Your ship's ropes hang loose. They cannot hold the mast steady or spread out the sail. Then a huge amount of treasure will be divided up. Even the lame will carry off their share.
No one living in Zion will say, "I am sick." The people who live there will have their sins forgiven.
Come near, you nations, and listen! Pay attention, you peoples! Let the earth and everything in it hear, the world and everything that comes from it.
For the LORD is angry with all the nations, and furious with all their armies. He will completely destroy them. He will hand them over to be killed.
Their dead will be thrown out, and the smell of their bodies will rise. The mountains will be soaked with their blood.
All the stars in the sky will melt away, and the sky will be rolled up like a scroll. All its stars will fall like withered leaves from a vine, like shriveled figs from a fig tree.
My sword has finished its work in the heavens. Look, now it will come down on Edom, the people I have set apart for destruction, to judge them.

The sword of the LORD is covered with blood. It is covered with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat from the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Wild oxen will fall with them, young bulls along with strong bulls. Their land will be soaked with blood, and their dust will be greasy with fat.
For the LORD has a day of paying back, a year of repaying the wrongs done to Zion.
Edom's streams will be turned into tar, its dust into burning sulfur. Its land will become burning tar.
It will not be put out, day or night. Its smoke will rise forever. From generation to generation it will lie in ruins. No one will ever travel through it again.
Desert owls and porcupines will take it over. Great owls and ravens will live there. God will measure it out for confusion and emptiness, like a builder using a measuring line and a level.
Its nobles will have nothing left there to call a kingdom. All its leaders will be gone.
Thorns will grow over its palaces, and nettles and thistles over its forts. It will become a home for jackals, a place for owls.
Desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and wild goats will call to one another. The night creatures will rest there and find themselves a place to stay.
Owls will make their nests there. They will lay eggs, hatch them, and gather their young under their wings. Falcons will gather there too, each with its mate.

Look in the book of the LORD and read it: not one of these creatures will be missing. Not one will be without its mate. For the LORD has commanded it with his mouth, and his Spirit will gather them together.
He has divided the land among them. He has measured out their portions with his hand. They will own it forever and live there from generation to generation.
The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will celebrate and bloom like a flower.
It will burst into bloom and shout for joy and sing. It will be given the glory of Lebanon and the beauty of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the beauty of our God.
Make the weak hands strong, and make the shaking knees firm.
Say to those who are afraid, "Be strong! Do not be afraid! Look, your God is coming to pay back your enemies. He is coming to repay them, and to save you."
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unblocked.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and those who cannot speak will shout for joy. For water will burst out in the wilderness, and streams will flow in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground will become springs of water. Where jackals once lived, grass, reeds, and rushes will grow.
A highway will be there, a road called "The Holy Way." The unclean will not travel on it. It will be for those who walk in God's way. Fools will not wander onto it.
No lion will be there, and no wild animal will go on it. They will not be found there. Only those God has rescued will walk on it.

Those the LORD has set free will come back. They will enter Zion singing, and everlasting joy will be on their heads like a crown. Gladness and joy will fill them, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah's rule, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the walled cities of Judah and captured them.

Then the king of Assyria sent his field commander from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem with a large army. The commander stood by the water channel of the upper pool, on the road to the washerman's field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went out to meet him.
The field commander said to them, "Tell Hezekiah: 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What are you trusting in that makes you so confident?
You say you have a plan and strength for war, but those are only empty words. Who are you depending on, that you dare to rebel against me?

Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that broken reed of a walking stick. If a man leans on it, it will cut into his hand and pierce it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like to all who trust in him.
But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed? Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this one altar."
Now make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses, if you can find enough riders to put on them!
How can you turn back even the weakest officer among my master's servants? Yet you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
Do you think I have come to attack and destroy this land without the LORD? The LORD himself told me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"

Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the field commander, "Please speak to us, your servants, in Aramaic, because we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew where the people on the wall can hear."

But the commander said, "Did my master send me to say these things only to your master and to you? Did he not also send me to the men sitting on the wall, who will have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine along with you?"
Then the commander stood and shouted loudly in Hebrew, "Listen to the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: 'Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He cannot rescue you.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, "The LORD will surely rescue us. This city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."

Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from your own vine and your own fig tree, and drink water from your own well,
until I come and take you away to a land like your own, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, "The LORD will rescue us." Have the gods of any nation ever rescued their land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
Which of all the gods of these lands has ever rescued their land from me? So how can the LORD rescue Jerusalem from my hand?'"
But the people stayed silent and did not answer a word, because the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him what the field commander had said.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'Today is a day of trouble, of punishment, and of shame. We are like a woman ready to give birth, but with no strength to deliver the baby.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the field commander, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to insult the living God. Perhaps the LORD your God will punish him for the words he has heard. So pray for the people who are still left.'"
When King Hezekiah's officials came to Isaiah,
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of what you have heard, the words with which the servants of the king of Assyria have insulted me.
Listen, I will put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will go back to his own land. And there I will have him killed by the sword.'"
The field commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish. So he went back and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Then the king of Assyria received a report that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was marching out to fight against him. When he heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this message:
"Tell Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let the God you trust fool you when he says, "Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."
Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other lands, destroying them completely. Do you think you will be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed rescue them? The gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, or the kings of Hena and Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
"LORD of Armies, God of Israel, you sit on your throne between the cherubim. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
Turn your ear, LORD, and listen. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Listen to all the words Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all these nations and their lands.
They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, because they were not gods at all. They were only wood and stone, made by human hands.
So now, LORD our God, save us from his power, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone are the LORD."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word the LORD has spoken against him: 'The virgin daughter of Zion looks down on you and laughs at you. The daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you as you run away.
Who have you insulted and spoken against? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your proud eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your servants you have insulted the Lord. You have said, "With my many chariots I have climbed up the highest mountains, the farthest parts of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars and its best cypress trees. I have reached its highest peaks and its finest forests.
I have dug wells and drunk water in foreign lands. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the rivers of Egypt."
Have you not heard? Long ago I planned it. In days of old I designed it. Now I have made it happen, so that you have turned walled cities into piles of rubble.

That is why their people had no strength. They were terrified and ashamed. They were like grass in the field, like tender green plants, like grass growing on a rooftop that dries up before it can grow.
But I know where you sit, when you come and go, and how you rage against me.
Because you rage against me, and because your pride has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth. I will make you go back the same way you came.'

This will be the sign for you, Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the second year what grows from that. But in the third year you will plant and harvest, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Once again the survivors of Judah, those who are left, will put down roots below and bear fruit above.
For a group of people will come out of Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The burning love of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.
So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: 'He will not come into this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with a shield or build a ramp against it.
He will go back the same way he came. He will not enter this city,' says the LORD.
'I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.'"
Then the angel of the LORD went out and killed one hundred eighty five thousand soldiers in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up early the next morning, there were dead bodies everywhere!
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and left. He went back to Nineveh and stayed there.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon became king after him.

In those days Hezekiah became sick and was about to die. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Put your house in order, because you are going to die. You will not get better.'"
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
He said, "LORD, please remember how I have walked before you faithfully and with all my heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
"Go and tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I will add fifteen years to your life.
I will rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.
This is the sign from the LORD to show you that he will do what he has promised:
Look, I will make the shadow cast by the sun go back ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.'" So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had gone down.
This is what Hezekiah king of Judah wrote after he had been sick and had gotten better:
I said, "In the prime of my life must I go through the gates of the grave? Am I robbed of the rest of my years?"
I said, "I will never again see the LORD, the LORD, in the land of the living. I will no longer look on people or be with those who live in this world.
My home has been pulled down and taken from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver rolls up cloth. He cuts me off from the loom. From day to night you make an end of me.
I waited patiently until morning, but like a lion he broke all my bones. From day to night you make an end of me.
I cried like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes grew tired from looking up to heaven. Lord, I am in trouble. Come and help me!"
But what can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done this. I will walk humbly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, by such things people live, and my spirit finds life in them too. You have healed me and let me live.
Surely it was for my good that I went through such bitter pain. In your love you kept me from the pit of destruction. You have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For the grave cannot praise you. Death cannot sing your praise. Those who go down to the pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.
The living, only the living, can praise you, as I am doing today. Parents tell their children about your faithfulness.
The LORD will save me. So we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
Isaiah had said, "Prepare a paste of figs and put it on the boil, and he will get better."
Hezekiah had asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
At that time Merodach Baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent Hezekiah letters and a gift, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had gotten better.

Hezekiah was happy to see the messengers. He showed them everything in his storehouses: the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine olive oil, his whole armory, and everything in his treasuries. There was nothing in his palace or in his whole kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them.
Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, "What did those men say? Where did they come from?" Hezekiah answered, "They came to me from a faraway country, from Babylon."
Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah answered, "They saw everything in my palace. There is nothing in my treasuries that I did not show them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Listen to the word of the LORD of Armies:
'Look, the time is surely coming when everything in your palace, and everything your ancestors have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left,' says the LORD.
'Some of your own descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away. They will become officials serving in the palace of the king of Babylon.'"
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD you have spoken is good." For he thought, "At least there will be peace and safety while I live."
"Comfort, comfort my people," says your God.
"Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and tell her that her hard service is over, that her sin has been paid for, that she has received from the LORD's hand double for all her sins."
A voice is calling out, "Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness! Make a straight highway in the desert for our God.
Every valley will be raised up, and every mountain and hill will be made low. The uneven ground will become level, and the rough places will become smooth.
The glory of the LORD will be shown, and all people will see it together. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken."
A voice says, "Call out!" And I asked, "What shall I call out?" "All people are like grass, and all their beauty is like the flowers of the field.
The grass dries up and the flowers fade when the breath of the LORD blows on them. Surely the people are grass.
The grass dries up and the flowers fade, but the word of our God lasts forever."
You who bring good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who bring good news to Jerusalem, shout it out loud! Shout it! Do not be afraid! Say to the towns of Judah, "Here is your God!"
Look, the Lord GOD is coming with power, and he will rule with his strong arm. Look, he brings his reward with him, and his payment comes with him.
He takes care of his flock like a shepherd. He gathers the lambs in his arms and carries them close to his heart. He gently leads the mother sheep that have young.

Who has measured the oceans in the palm of his hand, or measured the sky with the width of his hand? Who has held all the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on scales and the hills in a balance?
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or taught him as his adviser?
Whom did the LORD ask for advice? Who taught him the right way to judge? Who taught him knowledge or showed him the way of understanding?
Look, the nations are like a drop in a bucket. They are like a speck of dust on the scales. Look, he lifts up the islands as if they were fine dust.
All the trees of Lebanon would not be enough wood for the altar fire, and all its animals would not be enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing before him. He counts them as less than nothing, as empty and meaningless.
So who can you compare God to? What image can you compare him with?
An idol is cast by a craftsman, and a goldsmith covers it with gold and makes silver chains for it.
A person too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot. They look for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not fall over.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Have you not been told from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
God sits on his throne above the circle of the earth, and its people look like grasshoppers to him. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He brings rulers down to nothing and makes the judges of this world meaningless.
They have hardly been planted. They have hardly been sown. They have hardly put down roots in the ground, when he blows on them and they dry up, and the wind sweeps them away like straw.
"So who will you compare me to? Who is equal to me?" says the Holy One.

Look up at the sky and see. Who created all these stars? He leads them out like an army, one by one, and calls each one by name. Because of his great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.
Jacob, why do you say, Israel, why do you complain, "The LORD does not see my troubles. My God ignores my rights"?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He never grows weak or tired. No one can measure how deep his understanding is.
He gives strength to the tired and increases the power of the weak.
Even young people grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
But those who wait for the LORD will find new strength. They will rise up on wings like eagles. They will run and not grow weary. They will walk and not grow tired.
"Be silent before me, you islands! Let the nations find new strength. Let them come near and speak. Let us meet together in court.

Who has stirred up a ruler from the east and called him in righteousness to serve him? God hands nations over to him and lets him conquer kings. His sword turns them to dust. His bow scatters them like straw in the wind.
He chases them and moves on safely, on a road his feet have never traveled.
Who has done this and made it happen? Who has called each generation from the beginning? I, the LORD, am the first, and I will be with the last. I am he."
The islands have seen it and are afraid. The ends of the earth tremble. They come near and gather together.
Each one helps the other and says to their friend, "Be strong!"

The craftsman encourages the goldsmith. The one who smooths metal with a hammer encourages the one who strikes the anvil. He says of the welding, "It is good." Then he fastens the idol with nails so that it will not fall over.
"But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, you descendants of my friend Abraham,
I took you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I said, 'You are my servant. I have chosen you and have not rejected you.'
So do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not be discouraged, for I am your God. I will make you strong and help you. I will hold you up with my victorious right hand.
Look, all who are angry with you will be ashamed and disgraced. Those who fight against you will become nothing and will die.
You will look for your enemies, but you will not find them. Those who make war against you will be as nothing at all.
For I am the LORD your God, who holds your right hand and says to you, 'Do not be afraid. I will help you.'
Do not be afraid, Jacob, you little worm, you people of Israel. I myself will help you," says the LORD. "Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I will make you like a new, sharp threshing sledge with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and make the hills like chaff.
You will toss them into the air, and the wind will carry them away. The storm will scatter them. But you will be glad in the LORD and boast in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy look for water, but there is none. Their tongues are dry with thirst. But I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not leave them.
