I will make rivers flow on the bare hills, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into pools of water, and the dry ground into springs.
I will plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive trees in the wilderness. I will put cypress, fir, and pine trees together in the desert,
so that people will see and know, and think about it and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Present your case," says the LORD. "Bring your best arguments," says the King of Jacob.
"Let your idols come and tell us what is going to happen. Tell us what happened in the past, so we can think about it and know how it turned out. Or tell us what is coming in the future.
Tell us what will happen later, so that we will know you are gods. Do something, good or bad, so that we will be amazed and afraid together.
But look, you are less than nothing, and your works are worthless. Whoever chooses you is disgusting.
I have stirred up a ruler from the north, and he has come, a ruler from the east who calls on my name. He tramples rulers like mud, like a potter stomping clay.
Who told about this from the beginning, so we could know? Who told us before, so we could say, 'He was right'? No one told about it. No one announced it. No one heard any words from you.
I was the first to tell Zion, 'Look, here they are!' I sent a messenger to Jerusalem with good news.
When I look among the idols, there is no one, no adviser among them who can give an answer when I ask.
Look, they are all false! Their works are nothing. Their metal images are only wind and confusion."
"Here is my servant, whom I support, my chosen one, in whom I delight. I have put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations.
He will not shout or raise his voice. He will not make his voice heard in the streets.
He will not break a bent reed, and he will not put out a flickering lamp. He will faithfully bring justice.
He will not grow weak or lose heart until he has set up justice on the earth. The islands will wait hopefully for his teaching."

This is what God the LORD says, the one who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and everything that grows on it, who gives breath to its people and life to those who walk on it:
"I, the LORD, have called you to do what is right. I will take hold of your hand and keep you safe. I will make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to set prisoners free from the dungeon, and to bring those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
I am the LORD. That is my name. I will not give my glory to anyone else, or my praise to carved idols.
Look, the things I said before have happened, and now I tell you about new things. I tell you about them before they begin to happen."
Sing a new song to the LORD! Sing his praise from the ends of the earth, you who sail on the sea and everything in it, you islands and all who live on them.
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, the villages where the people of Kedar live. Let the people of Sela sing for joy. Let them shout from the tops of the mountains!
Let them give glory to the LORD and announce his praise in the islands.
The LORD will march out like a mighty warrior. He will stir up his anger like a soldier. He will shout a battle cry. Yes, he will shout out loud, and he will defeat his enemies.
"I have kept quiet for a long time. I have been silent and held myself back. But now, like a woman giving birth, I will cry out. I will gasp and pant.
I will flatten the mountains and hills and dry up all their plants. I will turn rivers into dry land and dry up the pools.

I will lead the blind along a road they do not know. I will guide them on paths they have never known. I will turn the darkness in front of them into light and make the rough places smooth. These are the things I will do. I will not leave them.
But those who trust in idols, who say to metal images, 'You are our gods,' will be turned back in shame."
"Listen, you who are deaf! Look, you who are blind, so that you can see!
Who is blind like my servant, or deaf like the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one I made peace with, blind like the servant of the LORD?
You see many things, but you do not pay attention. Your ears are open, but you do not listen."
Because the LORD is righteous, he was pleased to make his teaching great and glorious.

But these people have been robbed and looted. All of them are trapped in pits and hidden away in prisons. They have become victims with no one to rescue them, stolen goods with no one to say, "Give them back!"
Which of you will listen to this? Who will pay close attention from now on?
Who handed Jacob over to be looted, and Israel to robbers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? For they would not follow his ways or obey his teaching.
So he poured out his burning anger on them, and the violence of war. It surrounded them with flames, yet they did not understand. It burned them, but they did not take it to heart.
But now, this is what the LORD says, the one who created you, Jacob, the one who formed you, Israel: "Do not be afraid, for I have rescued you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.

When you pass through the waters, I will be with you. When you pass through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned. The flames will not set you on fire.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I gave Egypt as the price to set you free. I gave Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
Because you are precious and honored in my eyes, and because I love you, I will give people in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your children from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, 'Give them up!' and to the south, 'Do not hold them back!' Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth,
everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made."
Bring out the people who have eyes but are blind, who have ears but are deaf.

Let all the nations gather together, and let the peoples come together. Which of their gods could have told us this, or announced what happened in the past? Let them bring their witnesses to prove they were right, so that others will hear and say, "It is true."

"You are my witnesses," says the LORD, "and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you will know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, and there will be none after me.
I, yes I, am the LORD. Apart from me there is no savior.
I told you what would happen, then I saved you and made it known. It was not some foreign god among you. You are my witnesses," says the LORD, "that I am God.
Yes, from the beginning of time, I am he. No one can rescue anyone from my hand. When I act, who can undo it?"

This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: "For your sake I will send an army to Babylon. I will bring all the Babylonians down as people running away, in the ships they were so proud of.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King."
This is what the LORD says, the one who made a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,
who led out chariots and horses, the army and its strong soldiers together. They lay down and never got up again. They were put out like a wick that has burned out:
"Do not keep thinking about what happened before. Do not dwell on the past.
Look, I am doing something new! It is springing up now. Do you not see it? I am making a road in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
The wild animals will honor me, the jackals and the owls, because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen ones,
the people I formed for myself, so that they will tell of my praise.
Yet you have not called on me, Jacob. You have grown tired of me, Israel.
You have not brought me sheep for burnt offerings, or honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you by demanding offerings, or tired you out by asking for incense.
You have not bought sweet smelling cane for me with your money, or filled me with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead, you have burdened me with your sins and tired me out with your wrongdoing.
I, yes I, am the one who wipes away your sins for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins anymore.
Remind me of the past. Let us argue the matter together. State your case and prove that you are right.
Your first father sinned, and your spokesmen rebelled against me.
So I will disgrace the leaders of the temple. I will hand Jacob over to destruction and Israel to insult."
"But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
This is what the LORD says, the one who made you, who formed you in the womb, and who will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your children and my blessing on your descendants.
They will spring up like grass in a meadow, like willow trees by flowing streams.
One will say, 'I belong to the LORD.' Another will call himself by the name of Jacob. Another will write on his hand, 'The LORD's,' and take the name of Israel."
This is what the LORD says, Israel's King and Redeemer, the LORD of Armies: "I am the first and I am the last. Apart from me there is no God.
Who is like me? Let him say so. Let him tell it and explain it to me, what has happened since I set up my ancient people. Let them tell what is coming and what will happen.
Do not tremble. Do not be afraid. Did I not tell you this long ago and announce it? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? No, there is no other Rock. I know of none."
All who make idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Those who speak for idols are blind and know nothing, so they will be put to shame.
Who would shape a god or cast an idol that cannot help anyone?
Look, all who worship it will be put to shame. The craftsmen are only human. Let them all gather together and take their stand. They will be terrified and put to shame together.

The blacksmith takes a tool and works with it over the coals. He shapes the idol with hammers, working it with his strong arm. He gets hungry and loses his strength. He drinks no water and grows tired.
The woodworker measures with a line and marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with chisels and marks it with a compass. He shapes it like a man, a handsome human figure, to live in a shrine.
He cuts down cedars, or he picks a cypress or an oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a pine tree, and the rain makes it grow.
Then people use it as fuel. They take some of it to warm themselves. They light a fire and bake bread. But they also make a god from it and worship it. They make an idol and bow down to it.
Half of the wood they burn in the fire. Over it they cook their meat. They roast it and eat until they are full. They also warm themselves and say, "Ah! I am warm. I can see the fire."
From the rest of the wood they make a god, their idol. They bow down to it and worship it. They pray to it and say, "Save me, for you are my god!"
They do not know or understand anything. Their eyes are closed so they cannot see, and their minds are closed so they cannot understand.

No one stops to think. No one has the knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire. I even baked bread on its coals. I roasted meat and ate it. Should I make something disgusting from the rest of it? Should I bow down to a block of wood?"
Such a person feeds on ashes. A deceived heart leads them astray. They cannot save themselves or say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
"Remember these things, Jacob, for you, Israel, are my servant. I formed you. You are my servant. Israel, I will never forget you.
I have wiped away your sins like a thick cloud, your wrongdoing like the morning mist. Come back to me, for I have rescued you."

Sing for joy, you heavens, for the LORD has done this! Shout out loud, you depths of the earth! Burst into song, you mountains, you forests and all your trees! For the LORD has rescued Jacob, and he shows his glory in Israel.
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, who formed you in the womb: "I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by myself.
I make the signs of false prophets fail and make fools of fortune tellers. I turn back the wise and make their knowledge foolish.

I make the words of my servant come true and carry out the plans of my messengers. I say of Jerusalem, 'People will live there again,' and of the towns of Judah, 'They will be rebuilt. I will restore their ruins.'
I say to the deep waters, 'Dry up! I will dry up your rivers.'
I say of Cyrus, 'He is my shepherd, and he will do everything I want.' He will say of Jerusalem, 'Let it be rebuilt,' and of the temple, 'Let its foundations be laid.'"

This is what the LORD says to his chosen one, to Cyrus, whose right hand I hold, to conquer nations before him and to take away the power of kings, to open doors before him so that no gates will be shut:
"I will go ahead of you and make the rough places smooth. I will break down gates of bronze and cut through bars of iron.
I will give you treasures hidden in the dark, riches stored in secret places, so that you will know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.
For the sake of Jacob my servant, and Israel my chosen one, I call you by your name. I give you a title of honor, even though you do not know me.
I am the LORD, and there is no other. Apart from me there is no God. I will make you strong, even though you do not know me,
so that from the rising of the sun to its setting, people will know that there is no one besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I make the light and create the darkness. I bring peace and create disaster. I, the LORD, do all these things.
You heavens above, rain down righteousness. Let the clouds pour it down. Let the earth open wide, let salvation spring up, and let righteousness grow with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
How terrible for anyone who argues with their Maker, a clay pot among other clay pots on the ground! Does the clay say to the potter, 'What are you making?' Does your work say, 'He has no hands'?
How terrible for anyone who says to a father, 'What have you fathered?' or to a mother, 'What have you given birth to?'"
This is what the LORD says, the Holy One of Israel, its Maker: "Do you question me about what will happen to my children? Do you give me orders about the work of my hands?
I made the earth and created people on it. My own hands stretched out the heavens. I command all the stars.
I will raise up Cyrus to do what is right, and I will make all his paths straight. He will rebuild my city and set my exiles free, without asking for any price or reward," says the LORD of Armies.

This is what the LORD says: "The riches of Egypt, the goods of Ethiopia, and the tall people of Seba will come over to you and belong to you. They will follow behind you, coming in chains. They will bow down before you and beg you, saying, 'Surely God is with you, and there is no other. There is no other god.'"
Truly you are a God who hides himself, God of Israel, the Savior.
All the makers of idols will be put to shame and disgraced. They will all go away in disgrace together.
But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. You will never be put to shame or disgraced, forever and ever.

For this is what the LORD says, the one who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it. He set it firmly in place. He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be lived in. He says: "I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I have not spoken in secret, from somewhere in a land of darkness. I did not say to the descendants of Jacob, 'Look for me for nothing.' I, the LORD, speak the truth. I say what is right.
Gather together and come. Come near together, you survivors from the nations. Those who carry around their wooden idols know nothing. They pray to gods that cannot save.

Tell them to come and present their case. Let them talk it over together. Who told about this long ago? Who announced it in the distant past? Was it not I, the LORD? There is no God apart from me, a righteous God and a Savior. There is no one besides me.
Turn to me and be saved, all you ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
I have made a promise by my own name. My mouth has spoken what is right, and it will not be taken back: every knee will bow before me, and every tongue will swear loyalty to me.
They will say of me, 'Only in the LORD are righteousness and strength.'" All who have been angry with him will come to him and be put to shame.
But all the descendants of Israel will be made right with the LORD, and they will celebrate.
The idols Bel and Nebo bow down low. They are carried away by animals and cattle. The idols you used to carry around are now heavy loads, a burden for tired animals.
Together they bend low and bow down. They cannot save the load. Instead, they themselves are carried off into captivity.
"Listen to me, people of Jacob, all you who are left of the people of Israel. I have carried you since you were born. I have taken care of you since you were in the womb.
Even when you are old, I will be the same. Even when your hair is gray, I will carry you. I made you, and I will carry you. I will hold you up and rescue you.
Who will you compare me to? Who will you say is my equal? Who will you compare me with, as if we were the same?
Some people pour gold out of their bags and weigh out silver on scales. They hire a goldsmith to make it into a god. Then they bow down and worship it!

They lift it onto their shoulders and carry it. They set it in its place, and there it stands. It cannot move from its spot. Even when someone cries out to it, it cannot answer. It cannot save them from their trouble.
Remember this and stand firm. Think about it again, you rebels.
Remember the things I did long ago. For I am God, and there is no other. I am God, and there is no one like me.
I tell the end from the beginning, and from long ago I tell what is still to come. I say, 'My plan will stand, and I will do everything I want.'
I call a bird of prey from the east, a man from a faraway land to carry out my plan. What I have said, I will make happen. What I have planned, I will do.
Listen to me, you stubborn people, you who are far from doing what is right.
I am bringing my righteousness near. It is not far away, and my salvation will not be late. I will give salvation to Zion and my glory to Israel."
"Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground with no throne, daughter of the Babylonians. You will no longer be called tender and delicate.
Take the millstones and grind flour. Take off your veil. Lift up your skirt and uncover your legs, and wade through the rivers.
Your nakedness will be uncovered, and your shame will be seen. I will take revenge, and I will spare no one."
Our Redeemer, whose name is the LORD of Armies, is the Holy One of Israel.
"Sit in silence and go into darkness, daughter of the Babylonians. You will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people. I let my own people be disgraced, and I handed them over to you. But you showed them no mercy. Even on the old you put a very heavy yoke.
You said, 'I will be queen forever!' But you did not think about these things or consider how they would end.
So now listen, you lover of pleasure, who sits safely and says to herself, 'I am the only one, and there is no one else. I will never be a widow or lose my children.'
Both of these things will come on you suddenly, in a single day: the loss of your children and becoming a widow. They will come on you in full, despite all your magic and all your powerful spells.
You have trusted in your wickedness and said, 'No one sees me.' Your wisdom and your knowledge have led you astray. You have said to yourself, 'I am the only one, and there is no one else.'
So disaster will come on you, and you will not know how to charm it away. Trouble will fall on you, and you will not be able to pay it off. Ruin you never expected will come on you suddenly.
Keep going, then, with your spells and your many magic tricks, which you have worked at since you were young. Maybe they will help you. Maybe you will scare someone.
All the advice you have received has only worn you out. Let your astrologers come forward, those who study the stars and make predictions month by month. Let them save you from what is coming on you.
Look, they are like straw. The fire will burn them up. They cannot even save themselves from the power of the flames. This is not a fire of coals to warm yourself, or a fire to sit beside.
That is all they can do for you, the ones you have worked with and traded with since you were young. Each of them will go their own way. There will be no one to save you."

"Listen to this, people of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and come from the family line of Judah. You make promises in the name of the LORD and call on the God of Israel, but not in truth or in righteousness.
You call yourselves citizens of the holy city and claim to depend on the God of Israel, whose name is the LORD of Armies.
I told you long ago what would happen. My mouth announced it, and I made it known. Then suddenly I acted, and it happened.
For I knew how stubborn you are. Your neck is as stiff as iron, and your forehead as hard as bronze.
So I told you these things long ago. Before they happened I announced them to you, so that you could not say, 'My idol did them. My carved image and my metal god commanded them.'
You have heard these things. Now look at them all. Will you not admit it? From now on I will tell you about new things, hidden things you have not known.
They are created now, not long ago. You have not heard about them before today, so you cannot say, 'Yes, I knew about them.'
You have not heard or understood. Your ears have been closed since long ago. For I knew how unfaithful you are. You have been called a rebel since you were born.
For the sake of my name I hold back my anger. For the sake of my praise I hold it back from you, so that I do not cut you off.
Look, I have refined you, but not like silver. I have tested you in the furnace of suffering.
For my own sake, for my own sake, I do this. How can I let my name be disgraced? I will not give my glory to anyone else.
Listen to me, Jacob, Israel whom I have called: I am he. I am the first, and I am the last.
My own hand laid the foundations of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens. When I call them, they all stand up together.
Gather together, all of you, and listen! Which of the idols has told about these things? The one the LORD loves will carry out his plan against Babylon. His arm will be against the Babylonians.
I, yes I, have spoken. I have called him. I will bring him, and he will succeed in his mission.
Come near to me and listen to this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret. When it happens, I am there." And now the Lord GOD has sent me with his Spirit.
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: "I am the LORD your God, who teaches you what is good for you, who leads you in the way you should go.
Oh, if only you had listened to my commands! Then your peace would have flowed like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would have been as many as the sand, and your children as many as its grains. Their name would never be cut off or wiped out from before me."
Leave Babylon! Run away from the Babylonians! Announce this with shouts of joy and make it known. Send it out to the ends of the earth. Say, "The LORD has rescued his servant Jacob!"
They were not thirsty when he led them through the deserts. He made water flow for them from the rock. He split the rock, and water gushed out.
"There is no peace for the wicked," says the LORD.
Listen to me, you islands. Pay attention, you nations far away. The LORD called me before I was born. While I was still in my mother's womb, he spoke my name.
He made my words like a sharp sword. He hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me like a polished arrow and hid me in his quiver.
He said to me, "You are my servant, Israel, through whom I will show my glory."
But I said, "I have worked for nothing. I have used up my strength for nothing and with no result. Yet what is due to me is in the LORD's hand, and my reward is with my God."

And now the LORD speaks, the one who formed me in the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him and gather Israel to himself. For I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has been my strength.

He says, "It is too small a thing for you to be my servant only to bring back the tribes of Jacob and restore the survivors of Israel. I will also make you a light for the nations, so that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth."

This is what the LORD says, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to the one who was hated by people and rejected by the nation, to the servant of rulers: "Kings will see you and stand up. Princes will see you and bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you."

This is what the LORD says: "At the right time I answered you. On the day of salvation I helped you. I will keep you safe and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and to give out again the land that was left empty.
You will say to the prisoners, 'Come out!' and to those in darkness, 'Come into the light!' They will feed beside the roads and find pasture on every bare hill.
They will not be hungry or thirsty. The desert heat and the sun will not hurt them. For the one who has mercy on them will lead them, and guide them to springs of water.
I will turn all my mountains into roads, and my highways will be raised up.
Look, they will come from far away, some from the north, some from the west, and some from the land of Aswan."
Shout for joy, you heavens! Celebrate, you earth! Burst into song, you mountains! For the LORD comforts his people and has mercy on his suffering ones.
But Zion said, "The LORD has left me. The Lord has forgotten me."
"Can a mother forget the baby at her breast and have no love for the child she gave birth to? Even if she could forget, I will never forget you!
Look, I have written your name on the palms of my hands. Your walls are always in front of me.
Your children are hurrying back, and those who destroyed you and ruined you are leaving.
Look up and see all around you. All your children are gathering and coming to you. As surely as I live," says the LORD, "you will wear them all like jewels. You will put them on like a bride.
Your land was ruined, empty, and destroyed. But now it will be too small for all your people, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children born during your time of sorrow will say to you, 'This place is too small for us. Give us more room to live.'

Then you will say to yourself, 'Who gave birth to all these for me? I had lost my children and could have no more. I was sent away into exile and wandered about. Who raised these children? I was left all alone. Where did they come from?'"

This is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, I will lift my hand to signal the nations. I will raise my flag for the peoples. They will carry your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will take care of your children, and their queens will nurse them. They will bow down before you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD. Those who hope in me will never be disappointed."
Can the prey be taken away from warriors, or captives be rescued from a fierce ruler?
But this is what the LORD says: "Yes, captives will be taken away from warriors, and prey will be rescued from the fierce. I will fight those who fight you, and I will save your children.

I will make those who treat you cruelly eat their own flesh. They will be drunk on their own blood, as if it were wine. Then all people will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."

This is what the LORD says: "Where is the certificate of divorce I gave your mother when I sent her away? Or to which of my creditors did I sell you? Look, you were sold because of your sins. Your mother was sent away because of your rebellion.

Why was there no one here when I came? Why did no one answer when I called? Is my arm too short to rescue you? Do I not have the power to save you? Look, with one stern word I dry up the sea. I turn rivers into a desert. Their fish rot because there is no water, and they die of thirst.
I dress the sky in darkness and cover it with sackcloth."

The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of one who is taught, so that I know how to encourage the tired with a word. Morning after morning he wakes me up. He opens my ears to listen like one being taught.
The Lord GOD has opened my ears, and I have not rebelled. I have not turned away.
I offered my back to those who beat me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard. I did not hide my face from insults and spitting.
Because the Lord GOD helps me, I will not be disgraced. So I have set my face like a stone, and I know I will not be put to shame.
The one who proves me innocent is near. Who will bring charges against me? Let us face each other! Who is my accuser? Let him come near me!
Look, the Lord GOD helps me. Who will say I am guilty? Look, they will all wear out like old clothes. The moths will eat them up.
Who among you respects the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Whoever walks in darkness and has no light, let them trust in the name of the LORD and depend on their God.

But look, all of you who light fires and arm yourselves with burning torches, go ahead and walk in the light of your own fires and the torches you have lit. This is what you will receive from my hand: you will lie down in great pain.
"Listen to me, you who chase after righteousness, you who look for the LORD. Look to the rock you were cut from, and to the stone quarry you were dug out of.
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave birth to you. When I called him, he was only one man. But I blessed him and made him many.

For the LORD will comfort Zion. He will comfort all her ruins. He will make her deserts like Eden, and her dry lands like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found there, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.
Listen to me, my people. Hear me, my nation. For my teaching will go out from me, and my justice will become a light to the nations.
My righteousness is coming near. My salvation is on its way, and my arm will bring justice to the nations. The islands will look to me and wait with hope for my arm.

Look up at the heavens, and look down at the earth below. The heavens will disappear like smoke, and the earth will wear out like old clothes. Its people will die like flies. But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will never fail.
Listen to me, you who know what is right, you people who have my teaching in your hearts. Do not be afraid of people's insults, and do not be frightened when they mock you.
For moths will eat them up like clothes, and worms will eat them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation from generation to generation."
Wake up, wake up, arm of the LORD, and clothe yourself with strength! Wake up as in the days of old, as in generations long ago. Was it not you who cut Rahab to pieces, who stabbed that sea monster?
Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, and made a road in the depths of the sea for the people you rescued to cross over?

Those the LORD has set free will come back. They will enter Zion singing, and everlasting joy will be on their heads like a crown. Gladness and joy will fill them, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
"I, yes I, am the one who comforts you. Why are you afraid of mere humans who die, of people who are only grass?

Why have you forgotten the LORD your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth? Why do you live in constant fear every day of the anger of the one who treats you cruelly, who is ready to destroy? Where is the anger of that cruel one now?
The prisoners bent low in chains will soon be set free. They will not die in their dungeon, and they will not go without food.
For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is my name.
I have put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand. I set the heavens in place and laid the foundations of the earth, and I say to Zion, 'You are my people.'"
Wake up, wake up! Stand up, Jerusalem! You have drunk from the LORD's hand the cup of his anger. You have drunk to the bottom of the bowl that makes people stagger.
Of all the sons she gave birth to, there is no one to guide her. Of all the sons she raised, there is no one to take her by the hand.
These two disasters have come on you. Who will comfort you? Ruin and destruction, hunger and the sword. Who will comfort you?
Your sons have fainted. They lie at the corner of every street, like an antelope caught in a net. They are filled with the anger of the LORD and the stern warning of your God.
So listen to this, you who are suffering, who are drunk, but not with wine.
This is what your Lord GOD says, your God who defends his people: "Look, I have taken out of your hand the cup that made you stagger. You will never again drink from the bowl of my anger.
I will put it into the hands of those who tormented you, who said to you, 'Lie down so we can walk on you.' You made your back like the ground, like a street for them to walk on."
Wake up, wake up, Zion! Clothe yourself with strength. Put on your beautiful clothes, Jerusalem, the holy city. For those who are uncircumcised and unclean will never enter you again.
Shake off the dust! Get up and sit on your throne, Jerusalem! Take off the chains from your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For this is what the LORD says: "You were sold for nothing, and you will be rescued without money."
For this is what the Lord GOD says: "Long ago my people went down to live in Egypt. Later Assyria treated them cruelly for no reason.
And now, what do I have here?" says the LORD. "My people have been taken away for nothing. Those who rule over them mock them," says the LORD. "And all day long my name is insulted.
So my people will know my name. On that day they will know that I am the one who speaks. Yes, it is I."
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who announce peace, who bring good news of good things, who announce salvation, who say to Zion, "Your God is King!"
Listen! Your watchmen raise their voices. Together they shout for joy. For with their own eyes they will see the LORD return to Zion.
Burst into songs of joy together, you ruins of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted his people. He has rescued Jerusalem.
The LORD will show his holy power in front of all the nations. All the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Leave, leave, go out from there! Do not touch anything unclean! Come out from it and make yourselves pure, you who carry the holy objects of the LORD's house.
But you will not leave in a hurry. You will not go running away. For the LORD will go ahead of you, and the God of Israel will guard you from behind.
Look, my servant will act wisely. He will be raised and lifted up and highly honored.
Many people were shocked when they saw him. His face was so damaged that he hardly looked human. His body was so disfigured that he no longer looked like a man.
But he will sprinkle many nations, and kings will shut their mouths because of him. For they will see what they had never been told, and they will understand what they had never heard.
Who has believed our message? To whom has the power of the LORD been shown?

He grew up before the LORD like a tender young plant, like a root coming up out of dry ground. He was not handsome or majestic. There was nothing beautiful about his appearance that would draw us to him.
He was hated and rejected by people. He was a man of suffering who knew what sickness was. He was like someone people turn their faces away from. He was hated, and we did not think much of him.
Yet surely he took up our sickness and carried our pain. But we thought he was being punished by God, struck down by him, and made to suffer.
But he was pierced because of our rebellion. He was crushed because of our sins. He was punished so that we could have peace, and by his wounds we are healed.
All of us, like sheep, have wandered away. Each of us has turned to go our own way. And the LORD has laid on him the sins of us all.
He was treated cruelly, yet when he suffered, he did not open his mouth. He was led like a lamb to be killed. And as a sheep is silent before those who cut off its wool, he did not open his mouth.
He was arrested and judged unfairly, and taken away. Who among the people of his time cared? He was cut off from the land of the living. He was struck down for the rebellion of my people.
He was given a grave with the wicked, and he was with a rich man in his death, even though he had done nothing violent and had never spoken a lie.
Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him and make him suffer. When his life is made an offering for sin, he will see his children and live a long life. And the LORD's plan will succeed through him.
After he has suffered, he will see the light of life and be satisfied. By what he knows, my righteous servant will make many people right with God, and he will carry their sins.

So I will give him a share among the great, and he will divide the prize with the strong. For he poured out his life to death, and he was counted among the rebels. He carried the sins of many and prayed for the rebels.

"Sing, you woman who could not have children, you who never gave birth! Burst into song and shout for joy, you who were never in labor! For the woman who was left alone will have more children than the woman who has a husband," says the LORD.
"Make your tent bigger. Stretch out your tent curtains wide, and do not hold back. Make your ropes longer, and make your tent pegs strong.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left. Your descendants will take over the nations and fill the empty cities with people.

Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame. Do not be embarrassed, for you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth and will no longer remember the disgrace of being a widow.
For your Maker is your husband. The LORD of Armies is his name. The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer. He is called the God of the whole earth.
The LORD has called you back like a wife who was left alone and deeply hurt, like a wife who married young and was then rejected," says your God.
"For a short moment I left you, but with great mercy I will bring you back.
In a flood of anger I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have mercy on you," says the LORD your Redeemer.
"To me this is like the days of Noah. Just as I promised that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth, so now I promise that I will not be angry with you or scold you again.
Even if the mountains are shaken and the hills are removed, my faithful love for you will never be shaken, and my covenant of peace will never be removed," says the LORD, who has mercy on you.
"You poor city, battered by storms and not comforted, look, I will rebuild you with stones set in beautiful colors. I will lay your foundations with sapphires.
I will make your towers of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
All your children will be taught by the LORD, and their peace will be great.
You will be firmly set up in righteousness. You will be far from cruelty and will have nothing to fear. Terror will be far away and will not come near you.
If anyone attacks you, it will not be my doing. Whoever attacks you will fall because of you.
Look, I created the blacksmith who blows on the coals to make a fire and forges a weapon for its purpose. I have also created the destroyer to destroy.
No weapon made to attack you will succeed, and you will prove wrong every tongue that accuses you. This is what the servants of the LORD will receive. Their victory comes from me," says the LORD.
"Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters! You who have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost.
Why spend your money on what is not food, and your hard work on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good. Then you will enjoy the richest food.
Listen and come to me. Hear me, so that you may live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, my faithful love promised to David.
Look, I made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples.
Look, you will call nations you do not know, and nations that do not know you will come running to you, because of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has given you glory."
Look for the LORD while he can be found. Call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked leave their ways, and the evil leave their thoughts. Let them turn to the LORD, and he will have mercy on them. Let them turn to our God, for he will freely forgive.
"For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways," says the LORD.
"Just as the heavens are higher than the earth, so my ways are higher than your ways, and my thoughts higher than your thoughts.
The rain and snow come down from the sky and do not go back up without watering the earth. They make it grow and sprout, giving seed to the farmer and bread for people to eat.
In the same way, the word that comes from my mouth will not come back to me empty. It will do what I want, and it will succeed in the purpose for which I sent it.
You will go out with joy and be led out in peace. The mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees in the fields will clap their hands.
Instead of thorn bushes, cypress trees will grow. Instead of briers, myrtle trees will grow. This will bring honor to the LORD's name. It will be an everlasting sign that will never be destroyed."
This is what the LORD says: "Be fair to everyone and do what is right, for my salvation is coming soon, and my righteousness will soon be shown.
Blessed is the person who does this, the one who holds on to it, who keeps the Sabbath without making it unholy, and keeps their hand from doing any evil."
Do not let the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will surely keep me apart from his people." And do not let the eunuch say, "I am only a dry tree."
For this is what the LORD says: "To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose what pleases me and hold on to my covenant,
I will give them a monument and a name inside my house and within my walls, better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will never be cut off.

And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him, to love the name of the LORD, and to be his servants, all who keep the Sabbath without making it unholy and who hold on to my covenant,

I will bring them to my holy mountain and give them joy in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar. For my house will be called a house of prayer for all nations."
The Lord GOD, who gathers the scattered people of Israel, says: "I will gather still others to them, besides those already gathered."
Come, all you wild animals of the field! Come and eat, all you animals of the forest!
Israel's watchmen are blind. None of them know anything. They are all like dogs that cannot bark. They lie around dreaming, and they love to sleep.
These dogs are greedy. They never have enough. They are shepherds who understand nothing. They have all turned to their own way, each one looking for their own gain.
"Come," each one says, "let me get wine! Let us drink our fill of strong drink! Tomorrow will be like today, or even much better!"
Righteous people die, and no one cares. Faithful people are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous are taken away to be spared from evil.
They enter into peace. Those who walk uprightly find rest as they lie in death.
"But you, come here, you children of a sorceress, you children of people who cheat on their marriage and sell themselves!
Who are you making fun of? Who are you sneering at and sticking your tongue out at? Are you not children of rebels, children of liars?
You burn with desire among the oak trees and under every green tree. You kill your children as sacrifices in the valleys and under the overhanging rocks.
Your gods are the smooth stones of the valley. They are what you have chosen. You have poured out drink offerings to them and brought them grain offerings. Should these things make me calm?
You have made your bed on a high and lofty hill. You went up there to offer sacrifices.

Behind your doors and doorposts you have put your pagan symbols. You left me and uncovered your bed. You climbed into it and opened it wide. You made a deal with those whose beds you love, and you looked at their nakedness.
You went to the god Molech with olive oil and plenty of perfumes. You sent your messengers far away. You even went down to the grave itself.
You wore yourself out with all your traveling, but you never said, 'It is hopeless.' You found new strength, so you did not give up.
Who were you so afraid of that you lied to me? You did not remember me or think about me. Is it because I have been silent for so long that you do not fear me?
I will expose your so called righteousness and your works, and they will not help you.

When you cry out for help, let your collection of idols save you! The wind will carry them all away. A single breath will blow them away. But whoever takes shelter in me will receive the land and own my holy mountain."
And it will be said: "Build up, build up the road! Prepare the way! Remove the obstacles from the road of my people."

For this is what the high and lifted up One says, who lives forever, whose name is Holy: "I live in a high and holy place, but also with those who are sorry for their sins and humble in spirit. I bring new life to the spirit of the humble and new life to the hearts of those who are sorry.
I will not keep accusing forever, and I will not always be angry. Otherwise the spirit of the people I have created would grow faint before me.
I was angry because of their sinful greed. I punished them and hid my face in anger. Yet they kept on going their own stubborn way.
I have seen their ways, but I will heal them. I will lead them and comfort them again, and comfort those who mourn among them.
I will put praise on their lips. Peace, peace, to those far away and to those near," says the LORD. "I will heal them."
But the wicked are like the tossing sea, which cannot rest. Its waves throw up mud and dirt.
"There is no peace for the wicked," says my God.
"Shout it out loud! Do not hold back! Raise your voice like a trumpet! Tell my people about their rebellion, and the people of Jacob about their sins.

Every day they come looking for me and seem eager to learn my ways, as if they were a nation that does what is right and has not turned away from the commands of its God. They ask me for fair decisions and seem eager for God to come near them.

They say, 'Why have we fasted, and you have not seen it? Why have we humbled ourselves, and you have not noticed?' Look, on the day you fast, you do whatever you want, and you treat all your workers cruelly.
Look, your fasting ends in arguing and fighting, and in hitting each other with wicked fists. The way you fast today will not make your voice heard in heaven.

Is this the kind of fast I have chosen, only a day for people to humble themselves? Is it only to bow your head like a reed and lie on sackcloth and ashes? Is that what you call a fast, a day pleasing to the LORD?
No, this is the kind of fast I have chosen: to break the chains of injustice, to untie the ropes of the yoke, to set free those who are treated cruelly, and to break every yoke.
It is to share your food with the hungry, and to bring the poor and homeless into your house. When you see someone with no clothes, give them clothes. Do not turn away from your own family.
Then your light will break out like the dawn, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and the glory of the LORD will guard you from behind.
Then you will call, and the LORD will answer. You will cry for help, and he will say, 'Here I am.' If you get rid of the yoke of cruelty, stop pointing your finger, and stop speaking evil,
and if you give yourself to help the hungry and meet the needs of those who are suffering, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will become like the noonday sun.
The LORD will always guide you. He will satisfy your needs in a dry land and make your body strong. You will be like a garden that is well watered, like a spring whose water never runs dry.
Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins. You will build again on the old foundations. You will be called the Repairer of Broken Walls, the Restorer of Streets to Live In.

If you stop breaking the Sabbath, and stop doing as you please on my holy day, if you call the Sabbath a delight and the LORD's holy day honorable, and if you honor it by not going your own way, not doing as you please, and not speaking idle words,
then you will find your joy in the LORD. I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the inheritance of your father Jacob." For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
Look, the LORD's arm is not too short to save, and his ear is not too dull to hear.
But your sins have separated you from your God. Your sins have made him hide his face from you, so that he does not hear.
Your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with guilt. Your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue whispers evil.
No one goes to court honestly. No one argues their case truthfully. They trust in empty arguments and tell lies. They plan trouble and give birth to evil.
They hatch the eggs of poisonous snakes and weave spider webs. Whoever eats their eggs will die, and when one is broken, a snake comes out.
Their webs cannot be made into clothes. They cannot cover themselves with what they make. Their works are evil, and their hands are full of violence.
Their feet run to do evil. They hurry to kill innocent people. Their thoughts are evil thoughts. Ruin and destruction mark their roads.
They do not know the way of peace. There is no justice in their paths. They have made their roads crooked. No one who walks on them will know peace.
So justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We look for light, but there is only darkness. We look for brightness, but we walk in deep shadows.
We feel our way along the wall like the blind, feeling our way like people without eyes. At noon we stumble as if it were dusk. Among the strong, we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears. We moan sadly like doves. We look for justice, but there is none. We look for salvation, but it is far away.
For our rebellions against you are many, and our sins speak against us. Our rebellions are always with us, and we know our sins well:
we have rebelled against the LORD and denied him. We have turned our backs on our God. We have talked about cruelty and rebellion. We have planned lies in our hearts and spoken them.
So justice is pushed back, and righteousness stands far away. Truth has stumbled in the streets, and honesty cannot enter.
Truth is nowhere to be found, and whoever turns away from evil becomes a victim. The LORD saw this, and he was displeased that there was no justice.
He saw that there was no one to help, and he was shocked that no one stepped in. So his own arm brought salvation, and his righteousness held him up.
He put on righteousness like armor on his chest, and the helmet of salvation on his head. He put on the clothes of revenge and wrapped himself in burning love like a cloak.
He will repay them for what they have done: anger for his enemies and payback for those who oppose him. He will repay the islands what they deserve.
From the west, people will respect the name of the LORD. From the rising of the sun, they will honor his glory. For he will come like a rushing river, driven by the breath of the LORD.
"The Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn away from their sins," says the LORD.

"As for me, this is my covenant with them," says the LORD. "My Spirit, who is on you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, will never leave your mouth, or the mouths of your children, or the mouths of their descendants, from now on and forever," says the LORD.
"Get up and shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen on you!
Look, darkness covers the earth, and deep darkness covers the peoples. But the LORD rises on you, and his glory appears over you.
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
Look up and see all around you! They are all gathering and coming to you. Your sons are coming from far away, and your daughters are being carried in arms.
Then you will see and shine with joy. Your heart will pound and overflow with joy, because the riches of the sea will be brought to you. The wealth of the nations will come to you.
Herds of camels will cover your land, young camels from Midian and Ephah. All the people of Sheba will come, bringing gold and frankincense and announcing the praises of the LORD.
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you. The rams of Nebaioth will serve you. They will be accepted as offerings on my altar, and I will make my glorious house beautiful.
Who are these that fly along like clouds, like doves flying back to their nests?

Surely the islands are waiting for me. The ships of Tarshish lead the way, bringing your children from far away, with their silver and gold, to honor the name of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has made you glorious.
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. Though I struck you in my anger, in my kindness I will show you mercy.
Your gates will always stand open. They will never be shut, day or night, so that people can bring you the wealth of the nations, with their kings leading the way.
For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will be destroyed. Those nations will be completely ruined.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the cypress, the fir, and the pine together, to make my holy place beautiful. I will make the place where my feet rest glorious.

The children of those who treated you cruelly will come bowing before you. All who looked down on you will bow down at your feet. They will call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
You were once left alone and hated, with no one traveling through you. But I will make you the everlasting pride and joy of all generations.
You will drink the milk of nations and be nursed at the breasts of kings. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

Instead of bronze I will bring you gold. Instead of iron I will bring you silver. Instead of wood I will bring you bronze, and instead of stones, iron. I will make peace your governor and righteousness your ruler.
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, and there will be no ruin or destruction within your borders. You will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, and the moon will no longer shine on you. For the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun will never set again, and your moon will no longer fade. For the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your days of sorrow will end.
Then all your people will be righteous. They will own the land forever. They are the young plant I have planted, the work of my hands, to show my glory.
The smallest family will become a thousand people, and the least important group a strong nation. I am the LORD. When the time is right, I will make it happen quickly."

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to announce freedom to the captives, and to set the prisoners free,
to announce the year of the LORD's favor and the day when our God will pay back his enemies, to comfort all who mourn,

and to provide for those who grieve in Zion. He will give them a crown of beauty instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and clothes of praise instead of a spirit of despair. They will be called oaks of righteousness, planted by the LORD to show his glory.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and restore the places that were destroyed long ago. They will repair the ruined cities that have been empty for many generations.
Strangers will come and take care of your flocks. Foreigners will work in your fields and vineyards.
But you will be called priests of the LORD. People will call you servants of our God. You will enjoy the wealth of the nations and boast in their riches.

Instead of shame, my people will receive a double portion. Instead of disgrace, they will celebrate their inheritance. So they will receive a double share in their land, and everlasting joy will be theirs.
"For I, the LORD, love justice. I hate robbery and wrongdoing. I will faithfully reward my people and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their children among the peoples. All who see them will recognize that they are a people the LORD has blessed."

I am overjoyed in the LORD! My whole being celebrates in my God. For he has dressed me in clothes of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom wearing a priest's headdress, like a bride decorated with her jewels.
For as the soil makes the young plant come up, and a garden makes its seeds grow, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
For the sake of Zion I will not keep silent. For the sake of Jerusalem I will not rest until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a blazing torch.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings will see your glory. You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give you.
You will be a beautiful crown in the LORD's hand, a royal crown in the hand of your God.

You will no longer be called Abandoned, and your land will no longer be called Empty. Instead, you will be called Hephzibah, which means My Delight Is in Her, and your land Beulah, which means Married. For the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
As a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will marry you. As a bridegroom celebrates over his bride, so your God will celebrate over you.
I have posted watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem. They will never be silent, day or night. You who remind the LORD of his promises, do not rest,
and do not let him rest until he sets up Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.

The LORD has made a promise by his right hand and by his mighty arm: "I will never again give your grain as food to your enemies. Foreigners will never again drink the new wine you worked so hard for.
But those who harvest the grain will eat it and praise the LORD. Those who gather the grapes will drink the wine in the courts of my holy place."
Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way for the people! Build up, build up the highway! Clear away the stones! Raise a flag for the nations!
Look, the LORD has announced to the ends of the earth: "Tell the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your Savior is coming! Look, his reward is with him, and his payment comes with him.'"
They will be called The Holy People, The People Rescued by the LORD. And you will be called The City People Look For, The City No Longer Abandoned.

Who is this coming from Edom, from the city of Bozrah, with clothes stained red? Who is this, dressed in splendor, marching forward in his great strength? "It is I, the one who speaks what is right, mighty to save."
Why are your clothes red, like those of someone who stomps grapes in a winepress?
"I have stomped the winepress alone. No one from the nations was with me. I stomped on them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their blood splashed on my clothes and stained all my clothing.
For the day of paying back was in my heart, and the year for rescuing my people had come.
I looked, but there was no one to help. I was shocked that no one gave support. So my own arm brought salvation, and my own fury held me up.
I trampled the nations in my anger. I made them drunk in my fury and poured their blood out on the ground."

I will tell of the LORD's faithful love. I will praise the LORD for all he has done for us, for the many good things he has done for the people of Israel, because of his mercy and his great faithful love.
He said, "Surely they are my people, children who will not betray me." So he became their Savior.
In all their suffering, he suffered too, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and mercy he rescued them. He lifted them up and carried them all the days of long ago.
But they rebelled and made his Holy Spirit sad. So he turned and became their enemy, and he himself fought against them.

Then his people remembered the days of long ago, the days of Moses. They asked, "Where is the one who brought them through the sea, with the shepherd of his flock? Where is the one who put his Holy Spirit among them,
who sent his glorious power to be at the right hand of Moses, who divided the waters before them to make an everlasting name for himself,
who led them through the depths? Like a horse in open country, they did not stumble.
Like cattle going down into a valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest." This is how you led your people to make a glorious name for yourself.
Look down from heaven and see, from your holy and glorious home. Where is your burning love and your mighty power? Your tender love and mercy are being held back from us.
But you are our Father, even if Abraham does not know us and Israel does not recognize us. You, LORD, are our Father. Your name from long ago is Our Redeemer.
LORD, why do you let us wander from your ways and let our hearts become so hard that we do not respect you? Come back for the sake of your servants, the tribes that belong to you.
Your holy people owned your holy place for only a little while. Now our enemies have trampled it down.
We have become like people you never ruled, like those who were never called by your name.
Oh, if only you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains would shake before you,
like fire that sets twigs burning and makes water boil! Come down to make your name known to your enemies, so that the nations will tremble before you!
Long ago you did amazing things we did not expect. You came down, and the mountains shook before you.
Since the world began, no one has heard, no ear has noticed, and no eye has seen any God besides you, who acts on behalf of those who wait for him.
You come to help those who gladly do what is right, who remember your ways. But look, you were angry because we kept on sinning. We have been sinning for so long. How can we be saved?
All of us have become like someone who is unclean. All our good deeds are like dirty rags. We all wither like leaves, and our sins sweep us away like the wind.
No one calls on your name or makes an effort to hold on to you. For you have hidden your face from us and let us waste away because of our sins.
Yet, LORD, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you are the potter. We are all the work of your hand.
Do not be so very angry, LORD. Do not remember our sins forever. Please, look at us. We are all your people.
Your holy cities have become a wilderness. Zion has become a wilderness, and Jerusalem a ruin.
Our holy and beautiful temple, where our ancestors praised you, has been burned with fire. All the places we treasured are in ruins.
After all this, LORD, will you still hold back? Will you stay silent and punish us so severely?
"I was ready to be found by those who did not ask for me. I was found by those who did not look for me. To a nation that did not call on my name, I said, 'Here I am, here I am.'
All day long I held out my hands to a stubborn people, who walk in ways that are not good, following their own ideas.
They are a people who keep insulting me to my face, offering sacrifices in gardens and burning incense on altars of brick.
They sit among the graves and spend the night in secret places. They eat pork, and their pots are full of soup made from unclean meat.
They say, 'Stay away! Do not come near me, for I am too holy for you!' These people are like smoke in my nose, a fire that keeps burning all day long.
Look, it is written down before me: I will not keep silent. I will pay them back in full. I will pour it into their laps,

both for your sins and the sins of your ancestors," says the LORD. "Because they burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills, I will measure out into their laps the full payment for what they have done."

This is what the LORD says: "When juice is still found in a cluster of grapes, people say, 'Do not destroy it, there is still something good in it.' In the same way, I will act for the sake of my servants. I will not destroy them all.
I will bring out descendants from Jacob, and from Judah those who will own my mountains. My chosen people will receive the land, and my servants will live there.
Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for my people who look for me.
But you who turn away from the LORD and forget my holy mountain, who set a table for the god called Luck and fill bowls of mixed wine for the god called Fate,

I will choose you for the sword, and all of you will bow down to be killed. For I called, but you did not answer. I spoke, but you did not listen. You did what is evil in my eyes and chose what does not please me."
So this is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, my servants will eat, but you will go hungry. My servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. My servants will celebrate, but you will be put to shame.
My servants will sing from the joy of their hearts, but you will cry out from the pain in your hearts and wail with a broken spirit.
Your name will be used as a curse by my chosen people. The Lord GOD will put you to death, but he will give his servants a different name.

Whoever asks for a blessing in the land will ask it by the God of truth. Whoever makes a promise in the land will promise by the God of truth. For the troubles of the past will be forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
Look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The things of the past will not be remembered or come to mind.
But be glad and celebrate forever in what I am creating. For look, I am creating Jerusalem to be a delight, and its people to be a joy.
I will celebrate over Jerusalem and take delight in my people. The sound of weeping and crying will never be heard in it again.

Never again will a baby live only a few days, or an old person die before living a full life. Anyone who dies at a hundred will be thought of as young, and anyone who does not reach a hundred will be thought of as cursed.
They will build houses and live in them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They will not build houses for others to live in, or plant for others to eat. For my people will live as long as trees, and my chosen ones will enjoy the work of their hands for a long time.
They will not work hard for nothing, or have children who meet with disaster. For they will be a people blessed by the LORD, they and their children with them.
Before they call, I will answer. While they are still speaking, I will hear.
The wolf and the lamb will eat together. The lion will eat straw like the ox, and dust will be the snake's food. They will not hurt or destroy anything on all my holy mountain," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. So what kind of house could you build for me? Where would my resting place be?

My hand made all these things, and that is how they all came to be," says the LORD. "But this is the one I look to with favor: the one who is humble and sorry for their sins, and who trembles at my word.

But whoever sacrifices a bull is like one who kills a person. Whoever offers a lamb is like one who breaks a dog's neck. Whoever brings a grain offering is like one who offers pig's blood. Whoever burns incense is like one who worships an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and they delight in their disgusting practices.

So I will choose harsh treatment for them and bring on them what they fear most. For when I called, no one answered. When I spoke, no one listened. They did what is evil in my eyes and chose what does not please me."

Listen to the word of the LORD, you who tremble at his word: "Your own people hate you and throw you out because of my name. They have said, 'Let the LORD be glorified, so we can see your joy!' But they are the ones who will be put to shame.
Listen! There is an uproar in the city! There is a noise from the temple! It is the sound of the LORD paying back his enemies what they deserve.
Before she went into labor, she gave birth. Before the pains came, she delivered a son.

Who has ever heard of such a thing? Who has ever seen anything like this? Can a country be born in one day? Can a nation be born in a moment? Yet as soon as Zion went into labor, she gave birth to her children.
Would I bring a baby to the moment of birth and not let it be born?" says the LORD. "Would I, who let mothers give birth, close up the womb?" says your God.
"Celebrate with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her. Rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her.
For you will nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts. You will drink deeply and enjoy her overflowing glory."
For this is what the LORD says: "I will make peace flow to her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like a flooding stream. You will nurse and be carried on her hip and bounced on her knees.
As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem."
When you see this, your heart will be glad, and your body will grow strong like new grass. The power of the LORD will be shown to his servants, but his anger will be shown to his enemies.
Look, the LORD is coming with fire, and his chariots are like a whirlwind. He will bring his anger with fury, and his warning with flames of fire.
For with fire and with his sword the LORD will judge all people, and many will be killed by the LORD.

"Those who make themselves holy and pure to go into the gardens, following one who leads them in the middle, who eat pork, rats, and other disgusting things, will all come to an end together," says the LORD.
"For I know what they do and what they think. The time is coming when I will gather all nations and languages, and they will come and see my glory.

I will set a sign among them. I will send some of those who survive to the nations: to Tarshish, to Pul, and to Lud, famous for their archers, to Tubal and Greece, and to the faraway islands that have not heard of my fame or seen my glory. They will announce my glory among the nations.

They will bring all your brothers and sisters from all the nations to my holy mountain in Jerusalem as an offering to the LORD. They will come on horses, in chariots and wagons, and on mules and camels," says the LORD. "They will come just as the Israelites bring their grain offerings to the house of the LORD in clean containers.
And I will choose some of them to be priests and Levites," says the LORD.
"Just as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will last before me," says the LORD, "so your descendants and your name will last.
From one New Moon to the next, and from one Sabbath to the next, all people will come and bow down before me," says the LORD.

"They will go out and look at the dead bodies of those who rebelled against me. The worms that eat them will never die, and the fire that burns them will never go out. All people will be disgusted by them."
Jer: These are the words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests from the town of Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the LORD came to him in the thirteenth year that Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah.

It also came during the time Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, when the people of Jerusalem were taken away as captives in the fifth month.
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I set you apart. I chose you to be a prophet to the nations."
Then I said, "Oh, Lord GOD! Look, I do not know how to speak. I am too young."
But the LORD said to me, "Do not say, 'I am too young.' You must go to everyone I send you to, and say whatever I command you.
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to rescue you," says the LORD.
Then the LORD reached out his hand and touched my mouth. He said to me, "Look, I have put my words in your mouth.
Look, today I have put you in charge of nations and kingdoms, to pull up and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant."
The word of the LORD came to me again: "Jeremiah, what do you see?" I answered, "I see a branch of an almond tree."
The LORD said to me, "You have seen correctly, for I am watching to make sure my word comes true."
The word of the LORD came to me a second time: "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a boiling pot, tipping over from the north."
The LORD said to me, "From the north disaster will pour out on everyone who lives in this land.

Look, I am calling all the peoples of the northern kingdoms," says the LORD. "They will come, and each king will set up his throne at the entrance of Jerusalem's gates. They will attack all its surrounding walls and all the towns of Judah.
I will announce my judgments against my people because of all their evil. They have left me, burned incense to other gods, and worshiped idols they made with their own hands.
So get ready! Stand up and tell them everything I command you. Do not be terrified of them, or I will terrify you in front of them.
Look, today I have made you like a strong city, an iron pillar, and a bronze wall against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not defeat you, for I am with you to rescue you," says the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Go and announce this so that Jerusalem hears it: This is what the LORD says: 'I remember how faithful you were when you were young, how you loved me like a bride. You followed me through the wilderness, through a land where nothing was planted.
Israel was holy to the LORD, the first part of his harvest. All who tried to eat it up were found guilty, and disaster came on them,'" says the LORD.
Listen to the word of the LORD, people of Jacob, all you families of Israel!
This is what the LORD says: "What wrong did your ancestors find in me, that they went so far away from me? They followed worthless idols and became worthless themselves.

They did not ask, 'Where is the LORD, who brought us up out of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, a land of drought and deep darkness, a land no one travels through and where no one lives?'
I brought you into a fertile land to eat its fruit and its good things. But when you came in, you made my land unclean, and you made my inheritance disgusting.
The priests did not ask, 'Where is the LORD?' Those who taught the law did not know me. The leaders rebelled against me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed worthless idols.
So I will bring charges against you again," says the LORD. "And I will bring charges against your children's children.
Go across to the coasts of Cyprus and look. Send someone to Kedar and look carefully. See if anything like this has ever happened.
Has any nation ever changed its gods, even though they are not really gods? But my people have traded their glorious God for worthless idols.
Be shocked at this, you heavens! Shake with horror and be completely dismayed," says the LORD.
"For my people have done two evil things: they have left me, the spring of living water, and they have dug their own wells, broken wells that cannot hold water.
Is Israel a slave? Was he born a servant? Then why has he been taken as plunder?
Lions have roared at him. They have growled loudly. They have ruined his land. His towns are burned and empty, with no one living in them.
Even the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved your head in shame.
Have you not brought this on yourself by leaving the LORD your God when he led you on the way?
Now why go to Egypt to drink water from the Nile? Why go to Assyria to drink water from the Euphrates River?

Your own evil will punish you, and your turning away will correct you. So understand and see how evil and bitter it is to leave the LORD your God and to have no respect for me," says the Lord GOD of Armies.
"Long ago you broke your yoke and tore off your chains. You said, 'I will not serve you!' Instead, on every high hill and under every green tree, you lay down like a prostitute.
I planted you like a choice vine, from the very best seed. How then did you turn against me and become a wild, worthless vine?
Even if you wash yourself with strong soap and use lots of cleaning powder, the stain of your sin is still before me," says the Lord GOD.
"How can you say, 'I am not unclean. I have not followed the Baals'? Look at what you did in the valley. Think about what you have done. You are like a young female camel running here and there,

like a wild donkey used to the wilderness, sniffing the wind in her desire. Who can hold her back when she is in heat? The males that look for her do not need to tire themselves out. At mating time they will find her.
Do not run until your feet are bare and your throat is dry. But you said, 'It is no use! I love foreign gods, and I will follow them.'
As a thief is ashamed when he is caught, so the people of Israel are ashamed, they, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets.

They say to a piece of wood, 'You are my father,' and to a stone, 'You gave birth to me.' They have turned their backs to me and not their faces. Yet when they are in trouble, they say, 'Come and save us!'
But where are the gods you made for yourselves? Let them come and save you when you are in trouble! For you have as many gods as you have towns, Judah.
Why do you bring charges against me? All of you have rebelled against me," says the LORD.
