"I punished your children, but it did no good. They would not accept correction. Your own sword has killed your prophets like a hungry lion.

You people of this generation, pay attention to the word of the LORD: Have I been like a wilderness to Israel, or a land of deep darkness? Why do my people say, 'We are free to wander. We will not come to you anymore'?
Does a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding dress? Yet my people have forgotten me for more days than can be counted.
How skilled you are at chasing after love! Even the worst women could learn from your ways.
On your clothes is found the blood of innocent poor people, though you did not catch them breaking in. Yet in spite of all this,
you say, 'I am innocent. Surely he is not angry with me.' But I will judge you, because you say, 'I have not sinned.'
Why do you keep changing your mind so easily? You will be let down by Egypt, just as you were let down by Assyria.
You will also leave that place with your hands on your head in shame. For the LORD has rejected those you trust, and you will not succeed with their help."

"People say, 'If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and marries another man, should he go back to her again?' Would that not make the land completely unclean? But you have lived like a prostitute with many lovers. Yet come back to me," says the LORD.

"Look up at the bare hilltops and see. Is there any place where you have not slept with your lovers? You sat by the roadside waiting for them, like a nomad in the desert. You have made the land unclean with your prostitution and your wickedness.
That is why the showers have been held back and the spring rains have not come. Yet you have the bold face of a prostitute. You refuse to be ashamed.
Have you not just now called to me, 'My Father, you have been my friend since I was young!
Will you always be angry? Will you stay angry forever?' That is what you say, but you do all the evil you can."

During the time King Josiah ruled, the LORD said to me, "Have you seen what unfaithful Israel has done? She has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree, and lived like a prostitute there.
I thought that after she had done all this, she would come back to me. But she did not come back, and her unfaithful sister Judah saw it.
I gave unfaithful Israel her certificate of divorce and sent her away because of all her adultery. Yet her unfaithful sister Judah was not afraid. She also went and lived like a prostitute.
Israel did not take her prostitution seriously, so she made the land unclean by committing adultery with idols of stone and wood.
In spite of all this, her unfaithful sister Judah did not come back to me with all her heart. She only pretended," says the LORD.
The LORD said to me, "Unfaithful Israel is more righteous than unfaithful Judah.

Go and announce this message toward the north: 'Come back, unfaithful Israel,' says the LORD. 'I will no longer look at you in anger, for I am merciful,' says the LORD. 'I will not stay angry forever.
Only admit your guilt, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God. You have given your love to foreign gods under every green tree, and you have not obeyed my voice,' says the LORD.
Come back, unfaithful children," says the LORD, "for I am your husband. I will choose you, one from a town and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.
Then I will give you shepherds who follow my heart, who will lead you with knowledge and understanding.

In those days, when your numbers have greatly increased in the land," says the LORD, "people will no longer talk about 'the ark of the covenant of the LORD.' It will never come to mind. They will not remember it or miss it, and another one will not be made.
At that time Jerusalem will be called the Throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD. They will no longer follow their stubborn, evil hearts.
In those days the people of Judah will join the people of Israel. Together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.

I said to myself, 'How gladly I would treat you like my children and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance of any nation.' I thought you would call me 'My Father' and not turn away from following me.
But like an unfaithful wife who leaves her husband, you have been unfaithful to me, people of Israel," says the LORD.
A cry is heard on the bare hilltops, the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel. For they have chosen a crooked path and have forgotten the LORD their God.
"Come back, unfaithful children, and I will heal you of your unfaithfulness." "Yes, we are coming to you, for you are the LORD our God.
Surely the noisy worship on the hills and the mountains is a lie. Surely the salvation of Israel is found in the LORD our God.
From the time we were young, shameful idols have eaten up everything our ancestors worked for, their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us. For we have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our ancestors. From our youth until today we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."
"If you will come back, Israel," says the LORD, "if you will come back to me, and if you will get rid of your disgusting idols and stop wandering away,
and if you will make your promises by saying, 'As surely as the LORD lives,' in a way that is truthful, fair, and right, then the nations will be blessed by him, and they will boast in him."
This is what the LORD says to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: "Plow up your hard ground, and do not plant among thorns.

Make yourselves pure for the LORD. Remove the hardness from your hearts, you people of Judah and you who live in Jerusalem. Otherwise my anger will break out and burn like fire because of the evil you have done, and no one will be able to put it out.
Announce this in Judah and tell it in Jerusalem: 'Blow the trumpet throughout the land!' Shout out loud and say, 'Gather together! Let us run to the walled cities!'
Raise the flag toward Zion! Run for safety! Do not wait! For I am bringing disaster from the north, a terrible destruction."
A lion has come out of his hiding place. A destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his home to make your land a wasteland. Your towns will be ruined and left with no one living in them.
So put on sackcloth. Mourn and cry out, for the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.
"On that day," says the LORD, "the king and his officials will lose heart. The priests will be shocked, and the prophets will be amazed."
Then I said, "Oh, Lord GOD! You have completely fooled this people and Jerusalem by saying, 'You will have peace,' when the sword is at our throats."

At that time this people and Jerusalem will be told: "A scorching wind from the bare hills of the desert is blowing toward my people. It is not a gentle wind to separate grain from chaff or to clean it.
It is a wind too strong for that, and it comes at my command. Now I will announce my judgments against them."
Look! The enemy comes up like the clouds. His chariots are like a whirlwind. His horses are faster than eagles. How terrible for us! We are ruined!
Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart so that you may be saved. How long will you keep your wicked thoughts inside you?
A voice is announcing from Dan, announcing disaster from the hills of Ephraim.
"Tell this to the nations. Announce it to Jerusalem: 'An army is coming from a faraway land. They raise a battle cry against the towns of Judah.
They surround Jerusalem like men guarding a field, because she has rebelled against me,'" says the LORD.
"Your own ways and your own actions have brought this on you. This is your punishment. How bitter it is! It pierces you to the heart!"
Oh, my pain, my pain! I twist in agony! Oh, my aching heart! My heart is pounding inside me. I cannot keep silent. For I have heard the sound of the trumpet, the battle cry of war.
Disaster follows disaster. The whole land lies in ruins. Suddenly my tents are destroyed, my shelters in a moment.
How long must I see the battle flag and hear the sound of the trumpet?
"My people are foolish. They do not know me. They are foolish children who have no understanding. They are experts at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good."
I looked at the earth, and it was empty and without form. I looked at the heavens, and their light was gone.
I looked at the mountains, and they were shaking. All the hills were swaying back and forth.
I looked, and there were no people. All the birds of the sky had flown away.
I looked, and the fruitful land had become a wilderness. All its towns lay in ruins before the LORD, before his fierce anger.
This is what the LORD says: "The whole land will be ruined, but I will not destroy it completely.
So the earth will mourn and the heavens above will grow dark, because I have spoken and I have planned it. I will not change my mind or turn back."
At the sound of horsemen and archers every town runs away. Some go into the bushes. Some climb up among the rocks. All the towns are deserted. No one lives in them.

And you, ruined one, what are you doing? Why dress yourself in red and put on gold jewelry? Why paint your eyes with makeup? You make yourself beautiful for nothing. Your lovers hate you. They want to kill you.

I hear a cry like a woman in labor, a groan like a woman giving birth to her first child. It is the cry of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands and saying, "How terrible for me! I am fainting before the murderers!"

"Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem. Look around and think about it. Search through its town squares. If you can find even one person who acts fairly and looks for the truth, I will forgive this city.
Even when they say, 'As surely as the LORD lives,' they are still making false promises."

LORD, do your eyes not look for truth? You struck them, but they felt no pain. You crushed them, but they refused to accept correction. They made their faces harder than rock. They refused to turn back.
I thought, "These are only the poor. They are foolish, for they do not know the way of the LORD or the law of their God.
I will go to the leaders and speak to them. Surely they know the way of the LORD and the law of their God." But all of them together had broken the yoke and torn off the chains.

So a lion from the forest will attack them. A wolf from the desert will destroy them. A leopard will wait outside their towns to tear to pieces anyone who comes out. For their rebellions are many, and they have turned away from God again and again.

"Why should I forgive you? Your children have left me and made promises by gods that are not gods at all. I gave them all they needed, yet they committed adultery and crowded into the houses of prostitutes.
They are like well fed stallions, full of desire. Each one neighs for his neighbor's wife.
Should I not punish them for this?" says the LORD. "Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?
Go through her vineyards and destroy them, but do not destroy them completely. Strip off her branches, for these people do not belong to the LORD.
For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have been completely unfaithful to me," says the LORD.
They have lied about the LORD and said, "He will do nothing! No harm will come to us. We will never see war or hunger.
The prophets are just wind. The word of God is not in them. Let what they say happen to them!"
So this is what the LORD God of Armies says: "Because the people have said this, I will make my words in your mouth a fire, and these people the wood, and the fire will burn them up.
People of Israel," says the LORD, "I am bringing a nation from far away against you, a strong and ancient nation, a people whose language you do not know, whose words you cannot understand.
Their arrows bring death like an open grave. All of them are mighty warriors.

They will eat up your harvest and your food. They will eat up your sons and daughters. They will eat up your flocks and herds. They will eat up your vines and fig trees. With the sword they will destroy the walled cities you trust in.
Yet even in those days," says the LORD, "I will not destroy you completely.

When the people ask, 'Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?' you will tell them, 'As you have left me and served foreign gods in your own land, so now you will serve foreigners in a land that is not yours.'
Announce this to the people of Jacob and tell it in Judah:
Listen to this, you foolish people who have no sense, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.

Should you not fear me?" says the LORD. "Should you not tremble before me? I made the sand a border for the sea, a boundary that lasts forever, which it cannot cross. The waves may toss, but they cannot win. They may roar, but they cannot cross it.
But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts. They have turned aside and gone away.
They do not say to themselves, 'Let us respect the LORD our God, who gives the autumn and spring rains at the right time, and who makes sure we have the weeks of harvest.'
Your sins have kept these good things away. Your wrongdoing has kept you from having good things.
Among my people are wicked people who lie in wait like hunters hiding to catch birds. They set traps to catch people.
Like cages full of birds, their houses are full of things they got by lying. That is how they have become powerful and rich.
They have grown fat and sleek. There is no limit to their evil deeds. They do not defend the cause of the orphan so that it may succeed. They do not stand up for the rights of the poor.
Should I not punish them for this?" says the LORD. "Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?
A shocking and horrible thing has happened in the land.
The prophets tell lies, and the priests rule by their own power. And my people love it this way! But what will you do when the end comes?"
"Run for safety, people of Benjamin! Get out of Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa! Raise a signal over Beth Hakkerem! For disaster is coming from the north, a terrible destruction.
I will destroy the daughter of Zion, so beautiful and delicate.
Shepherds with their flocks will come against her. They will set up their tents all around her, each one grazing in his own spot."
"Get ready to fight against her! Get up, let us attack at noon! But how terrible for us, the day is ending, and the evening shadows are growing long.
So get up, let us attack at night and destroy her strong towers!"
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Cut down the trees and build a ramp against Jerusalem. This city must be punished. It is full of cruelty.
As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps pouring out her wickedness. Violence and destruction echo in her streets. I always see her sickness and her wounds.
Listen to this warning, Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you in disgust and make your land a wasteland where no one can live."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Let them pick clean the survivors of Israel, as one picks the last grapes from a vine. Pass your hand over the branches again, like someone gathering grapes."
Who can I speak to and warn? Who will listen to me? Look, their ears are closed, so they cannot hear. Look, the word of the LORD is a joke to them. They find no pleasure in it.

But I am full of the anger of the LORD, and I am tired of holding it in. "Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the young men gathered together. Husbands and wives will be taken, and the old and those who are very old.
Their houses will be given to others, along with their fields and their wives. For I will raise my hand against those who live in the land," says the LORD.
"From the least to the greatest, all of them are greedy for money. From prophets to priests, they all lie and cheat.
They treat the wounds of my people as if they were not serious. They say, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.

Are they ashamed of their disgusting actions? No, they have no shame at all. They do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among those who fall. When I punish them, they will be brought down," says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: "Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask for the ancient paths, ask where the good way is, and walk in it. Then you will find rest for your souls. But you said, 'We will not walk in it.'
I put watchmen over you and said, 'Listen to the sound of the trumpet!' But you said, 'We will not listen.'
So listen, you nations! Pay attention, you witnesses, to what will happen to them.
Listen, earth! I am bringing disaster on this people, the result of their own plans. For they have not listened to my words, and they have rejected my teaching.
What good to me is incense from Sheba or sweet smelling cane from a faraway land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable. Your sacrifices do not please me."
So this is what the LORD says: "I will put obstacles in front of this people. Fathers and sons alike will trip over them. Neighbors and friends will die."
This is what the LORD says: "Look, an army is coming from the land of the north. A great nation is being stirred up from the ends of the earth.
They carry bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy. They sound like the roaring sea as they ride on their horses. They come lined up for battle to attack you, daughter of Zion."
We have heard reports about them, and our hands hang limp with fear. Pain has gripped us, pain like a woman giving birth.
Do not go out into the fields or walk on the roads, for the enemy has a sword, and there is terror on every side.
My people, put on sackcloth and roll in the ashes. Mourn with bitter crying as for an only son, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
"I have made you a tester of my people, like someone who tests metals, so that you can watch and test their ways.
They are all stubborn rebels who go around spreading lies. They are like bronze and iron. They are all corrupt.
The bellows blow fiercely to burn away the lead with fire, but the refining is useless. The wicked are not removed.
They will be called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them."
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Stand at the gate of the LORD's house and announce this message there: 'Listen to the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who come through these gates to worship the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Change your ways and your actions, and I will let you live in this place.
Do not trust in lies that say, "This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD!"
If you truly change your ways and your actions, and treat each other fairly,
if you do not treat foreigners, orphans, and widows cruelly, if you do not kill innocent people in this place, and if you do not follow other gods and hurt yourselves,
then I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave your ancestors forever and ever.
But look, you are trusting in lies that are worthless.
You steal, murder, commit adultery, make false promises, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods you have not known.
Then you come and stand before me in this house that is called by my name, and say, "We are safe!" just so you can keep doing all these disgusting things.
Has this house that is called by my name become a hiding place for robbers in your eyes? Look, I have seen it myself,' says the LORD.
'Go now to the place in Shiloh where I first made a home for my name. See what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
You have done all these things,' says the LORD. 'I spoke to you again and again, but you did not listen. I called you, but you did not answer.
So what I did to Shiloh I will now do to this house that is called by my name, the temple you trust in, the place I gave to you and your ancestors.
I will throw you out of my sight, just as I threw out all your relatives, the people of Ephraim.'
So do not pray for these people, Jeremiah. Do not cry out or pray for them. Do not beg me, for I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven. They pour out drink offerings to other gods to make me angry.
But am I the one they are hurting?" says the LORD. "Are they not hurting themselves, to their own shame?"

So this is what the Lord GOD says: "Look, my anger and fury will be poured out on this place, on people and animals, on the trees of the field and the crops of the land. It will burn and not be put out."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Go ahead, add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves!
For when I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I did not just give them commands about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
This is what I commanded them: 'Obey me, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Walk in all the ways I command you, so that it will go well with you.'
But they did not listen or pay attention. They followed their own plans and their stubborn, evil hearts. They went backward and not forward.
From the day your ancestors left Egypt until today, I have sent you my servants the prophets, again and again, day after day.
But they did not listen to me or pay attention. They were stubborn and did even worse than their ancestors.
When you tell them all this, they will not listen to you. When you call to them, they will not answer.
So say to them, 'This is the nation that has not obeyed the LORD its God or accepted correction. Truth has disappeared. It is no longer heard from their lips.'
Cut off your hair and throw it away. Sing a sad song on the bare hilltops. For the LORD has rejected and left this generation that has made him angry.
The people of Judah have done evil in my eyes," says the LORD. "They have set up their disgusting idols in the house that is called by my name and made it unclean.
They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire. I never commanded this, and it never even entered my mind.

So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when people will no longer call it Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom. They will call it the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room.
Then the dead bodies of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the wild animals, and no one will scare them away.
I will put an end to the sounds of joy and gladness in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, the voices of the bride and bridegroom. For the land will become a wasteland."
"At that time," says the LORD, "the bones of the kings of Judah and its officials, the bones of the priests and prophets, and the bones of the people of Jerusalem will be taken out of their graves.

They will be spread out under the sun, the moon, and all the stars of the sky, which they loved and served, followed and asked for help, and worshiped. Their bones will not be gathered up or buried. They will be like manure lying on the ground.
All the survivors of this evil nation, in all the places where I have driven them, will choose death rather than life," says the LORD of Armies.
"Say to them, 'This is what the LORD says: When people fall down, do they not get up again? When someone turns away, do they not come back?
Then why have these people of Jerusalem turned away and kept on turning away? They hold on to lies. They refuse to come back.

I have listened carefully, but they do not say what is right. No one is sorry for their wickedness and says, "What have I done?" Each one keeps running their own way, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork in the sky knows her seasons. The dove, the swift, and the thrush know when it is time to move. But my people do not know what the LORD requires.
How can you say, "We are wise, for we have the law of the LORD," when the lying pens of the teachers of the law have turned it into a lie?
The wise will be put to shame. They will be shocked and trapped. Since they have rejected the word of the LORD, what kind of wisdom do they really have?
So I will give their wives to other men and their fields to new owners. From the least to the greatest, all are greedy for money. Prophets and priests alike, they all lie and cheat.
They treat the wounds of my people as if they were not serious. They say, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.

Are they ashamed of their disgusting actions? No, they have no shame at all. They do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among those who fall. When I punish them, they will be brought down, says the LORD.
I will take away their harvest, says the LORD. There will be no grapes on the vine and no figs on the tree. Even the leaves will dry up. What I gave them will be taken from them.'"

"Why are we sitting here? Let us gather together! Let us run to the walled cities and die there! For the LORD our God has sentenced us to die. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for a time of healing, but there was only terror.

The snorting of the enemy's horses is heard all the way from Dan. The whole land trembles at the neighing of their stallions. They have come to destroy the land and everything in it, the city and all who live there."
"Look, I am sending poisonous snakes among you, snakes that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you," says the LORD.
My sorrow is beyond healing. My heart is sick inside me.
Listen to the cry of my people from a land far away: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King no longer there?" "Why have they made me angry with their idols, their worthless foreign gods?"
"The harvest is over, the summer has ended, and we are not saved."
Because my people are crushed, I am crushed. I mourn, and horror grips me.
Is there no healing ointment in Gilead? Is there no doctor there? Then why has my people's wound not been healed?
Oh, I wish my head were a spring of water and my eyes a fountain of tears! Then I would weep day and night for my people who have been killed.
Oh, I wish I had a travelers' shelter in the desert! Then I could leave my people and go away from them. For they are all unfaithful, a crowd of traitors.
"They bend their tongues like bows to shoot out lies. They have grown strong in the land, but not by truth. They go from one evil to another, and they do not know me," says the LORD.
"Be careful of your friends. Do not trust even your brother. For every brother cheats, and every friend spreads lies.
Friends deceive each other, and no one speaks the truth. They have trained their tongues to lie. They wear themselves out doing wrong.
You live in the middle of lies. In their lies they refuse to know me," says the LORD.
So this is what the LORD of Armies says: "Look, I will melt them down and test them like metal. What else can I do because of the sin of my people?
Their tongue is a deadly arrow. It speaks lies. With their mouths they speak kindly to their neighbors, but in their hearts they set traps for them.
Should I not punish them for this?" says the LORD. "Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?"

I will weep and cry for the mountains and sing a sad song for the pastures in the wilderness. They are burned and empty, and no one travels through them. The sound of cattle is no longer heard. The birds and the animals have all run away.
"I will make Jerusalem a pile of ruins, a home for jackals. I will make the towns of Judah a wasteland where no one lives."
Who is wise enough to understand this? Who has the LORD spoken to, who can explain it? Why has the land been ruined and burned like a wilderness that no one travels through?
The LORD said, "It is because they have abandoned my law that I gave them. They have not obeyed me or followed my law.
Instead, they have followed their stubborn hearts and the Baals, as their ancestors taught them."
So this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will make this people eat bitter food and drink poisoned water.
I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known. I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Think about this! Call for the women who are paid to mourn. Send for the most skilled of them.
Let them come quickly and cry out for us, until our eyes overflow with tears and water streams from our eyelids.
For the sound of crying is heard from Zion: 'How we are ruined! How deeply we are ashamed! We must leave our land, because our homes have been torn down.'"
Now, you women, listen to the word of the LORD. Open your ears to what he says. Teach your daughters how to mourn. Teach one another a song of sorrow.
For death has climbed in through our windows and entered our strong houses. It has taken away the children from the streets and the young men from the town squares.
Say this: "This is what the LORD says: 'Dead bodies will lie like manure in the open field, like grain cut down behind the harvester, with no one to gather them.'"
This is what the LORD says: "Do not let the wise boast about their wisdom, or the strong boast about their strength, or the rich boast about their riches.

But let the one who boasts boast about this: that they understand and know me, that I am the LORD, who shows faithful love, justice, and righteousness on the earth. For these are the things I delight in," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will punish all who are circumcised only in their bodies:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and all who live in the desert and cut the hair at the sides of their heads. For all these nations are really uncircumcised, and all the people of Israel are uncircumcised in heart."
Listen to the word the LORD speaks to you, people of Israel!
This is what the LORD says: "Do not learn the ways of the nations, and do not be terrified by signs in the sky, even though the nations are terrified by them.
For the customs of these peoples are worthless. They cut down a tree in the forest, and a craftsman shapes it with his tools.
They decorate it with silver and gold. They fasten it with hammer and nails so that it will not fall over.

Their idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber field. They cannot speak. They must be carried, because they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them. They can do no harm, and they cannot do any good either."
There is no one like you, LORD. You are great, and your name is mighty in power.
Who would not respect you, King of the nations? You deserve it. Among all the wise people of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is no one like you.
They are all senseless and foolish. They are taught by worthless idols made of wood.
Beaten silver is brought from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz. Craftsmen and goldsmiths make the idols. Then they dress them in blue and purple clothes, all made by skilled workers.
But the LORD is the true God. He is the living God and the everlasting King. When he is angry, the earth shakes. The nations cannot stand up to his fury.
"Tell them this: 'These gods, who did not make the heavens and the earth, will disappear from the earth and from under the heavens.'"
But God made the earth by his power. He set up the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
When he speaks, the waters in the heavens roar. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Everyone is senseless and without knowledge. Every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. His images are fake. They have no breath in them.
They are worthless, objects to be laughed at. When the time comes to judge them, they will be destroyed.
But the God of Jacob is not like these idols. He made everything, including Israel, the tribe that belongs to him. The LORD of Armies is his name.
Pick up your belongings and leave the land, you who are surrounded by the enemy.
For this is what the LORD says: "Look, this time I will throw out those who live in this land. I will bring trouble on them so that they will feel it."
How terrible for me because of my injury! My wound is very serious. But I said to myself, "This is my sickness, and I must put up with it."
My tent is destroyed, and all its ropes are broken. My children have left me and are gone. There is no one left to set up my tent again or hang its curtains.
For the shepherds are senseless and do not ask the LORD for guidance. So they do not succeed, and all their flocks are scattered.
Listen! The news is coming, a great noise from the land of the north. It will make the towns of Judah a wasteland, a home for jackals.
LORD, I know that people's lives are not their own. No one is able to direct their own steps.
Correct me, LORD, but only with fairness, not in your anger, or you will crush me to nothing.
Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you, on the peoples who do not call on your name. For they have eaten up Jacob. They have eaten him up completely and destroyed his homeland.
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Listen to the terms of this covenant, and tell them to the people of Judah and to those who live in Jerusalem.
Tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Cursed is anyone who does not obey the terms of this covenant,
the terms I commanded your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, "Obey me and do everything I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God.
Then I will keep the promise I made to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey," the land you live in today.'" I answered, "Amen, LORD. Let it be so."
The LORD said to me, "Announce all these words in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: 'Listen to the terms of this covenant and obey them.
From the time I brought your ancestors out of Egypt until today, I have warned them again and again, saying, "Obey me."

But they did not listen or pay attention. Each of them followed their own stubborn, evil heart. So I brought on them all the punishments written in this covenant, which I had commanded them to obey but they did not.'"
Then the LORD said to me, "There is a plot among the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem.

They have gone back to the sins of their ancestors, who refused to listen to my words. They have followed other gods to serve them. Both Israel and Judah have broken the covenant I made with their ancestors.
So this is what the LORD says: 'Look, I will bring a disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
Then the people of the towns of Judah and Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn incense to, but those gods will not save them at all when disaster strikes.
Judah, you have as many gods as you have towns. And you have set up as many altars to burn incense to that shameful god Baal as there are streets in Jerusalem.'
So do not pray for these people, Jeremiah. Do not cry out or pray for them, because I will not listen when they call to me in their time of trouble.
What right does my beloved people have to be in my house, when she has done so many evil things? Can holy sacrifices take away your punishment? When you do evil, you are happy."
The LORD once called you a green olive tree, beautiful with good fruit. But with the roar of a great storm he will set it on fire, and its branches will be broken.
The LORD of Armies, who planted you, has announced disaster against you. For the people of Israel and Judah have done evil and made him angry by burning incense to Baal.
The LORD showed me their plot, so I knew about it. He showed me what they were doing.

I was like a gentle lamb being led to be killed. I did not know they were making plans against me. They said, "Let us destroy the tree and its fruit. Let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more."
But you, LORD of Armies, judge fairly. You test the heart and the mind. Let me see you pay them back, for I have placed my case in your hands.
So this is what the LORD says about the men of Anathoth who want to kill you, who say, "Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or we will kill you."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Look, I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will die of hunger.
Not one of them will be left alive. For I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year they are punished."
LORD, you are always right when I bring a complaint to you. Yet I want to talk to you about justice. Why do the wicked succeed? Why do all the unfaithful live such easy lives?
You planted them, and they have put down roots. They grow and bear fruit. You are always on their lips, but far from their hearts.
But you know me, LORD. You see me and test my heart toward you. Drag them away like sheep to be killed. Set them apart for the day of slaughter.

How long will the land be dry, and the grass in every field wither? Because the people who live there are wicked, the animals and birds have died. For the people said, "He will not see what happens to us."
"If you have raced with people on foot and they have worn you out, how can you race against horses? If you stumble in a safe land, what will you do in the thick bushes along the Jordan?
Even your own brothers, your own family, have betrayed you. They have shouted loudly against you. Do not trust them, even when they say nice things to you.
I have left my house. I have abandoned my inheritance. I have handed over the people I dearly love to their enemies.
My people have become to me like a lion in the forest. They roar at me, so I hate them.
My people have become like a speckled bird of prey, attacked by other birds of prey on all sides. Go and gather all the wild animals. Bring them to eat.
Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard. They have trampled down my field. They have turned my pleasant field into an empty wilderness.
They have made it a wasteland. It mourns before me, empty and ruined. The whole land is ruined, because no one cares.
Destroyers have come over all the bare hills in the desert. For the sword of the LORD destroys from one end of the land to the other. No one is safe.
They planted wheat but harvested thorns. They wore themselves out but gained nothing. They will be ashamed of their harvest because of the fierce anger of the LORD."

This is what the LORD says about all the evil nations around Israel, who take the land I gave my people Israel as their inheritance: "Look, I will pull them up from their land, and I will pull up the people of Judah from among them.
But after I have pulled them up, I will again have mercy on them. I will bring each of them back to their own inheritance and their own land.

And if they will carefully learn the ways of my people, and make their promises in my name, saying, 'As surely as the LORD lives,' just as they once taught my people to make promises by Baal, then they will be built up among my people.
But if any nation will not listen, I will completely pull it up and destroy it," says the LORD.
The LORD said to me, "Go and buy a linen belt and put it around your waist, but do not let it touch water."
So I bought a belt, as the LORD told me, and put it around my waist.
Then the word of the LORD came to me a second time:
"Take the belt you bought, the one you are wearing, and go now to the Euphrates River. Hide it there in a crack in the rocks."
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the LORD commanded me.
Many days later the LORD said to me, "Go now to the Euphrates and get the belt I told you to hide there."
So I went to the Euphrates and dug up the belt from the place where I had hidden it. But look, the belt was ruined. It was good for nothing.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"This is what the LORD says: 'In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
These evil people refuse to listen to my words. They follow their stubborn hearts and go after other gods to serve and worship them. They will be like this belt, good for nothing.

For just as a belt is wrapped tightly around a person's waist, so I wrapped all the people of Israel and Judah around me,' says the LORD, 'so that they would be my people, bringing me fame, praise, and honor. But they would not listen.'

So tell them this: 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every wine jar should be filled with wine.' And they will say to you, 'Do we not already know that every wine jar should be filled with wine?'

Then tell them, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am going to fill everyone who lives in this land with drunkenness, the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem.
I will smash them against each other, parents and children alike,' says the LORD. 'I will not show pity, or spare them, or have mercy. Nothing will stop me from destroying them.'"
Listen and pay attention. Do not be proud, for the LORD has spoken.
Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the dark mountains. You hope for light, but he will turn it into deep darkness and thick gloom.
But if you will not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride. My eyes will cry bitterly and overflow with tears, because the LORD's flock will be taken away as captives.
Say to the king and the queen mother, "Come down from your thrones and sit in the dust, for your glorious crowns will fall from your heads."
The towns in the south of Judah will be shut tight, and no one will be able to open them. All Judah will be taken away as captives, every one of them.
Look up and see the enemy coming from the north. Where is the flock you were given to care for, your beautiful flock?
What will you say when the LORD puts over you as rulers those you once made your allies? Will pain not grip you like a woman giving birth?
And if you ask yourself, "Why has this happened to me?" It is because of your many sins that your skirts have been torn off and your body has been treated so cruelly.
Can an Ethiopian change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Neither can you do good, you who are used to doing evil.
"I will scatter them like straw blown away by the desert wind.
This is your share, the portion I have measured out for you," says the LORD, "because you have forgotten me and trusted in lies.
So I will pull your skirts up over your face, and your shame will be seen.

I have seen your disgusting acts, your adulteries and your lustful neighing, your shameless prostitution on the hills and in the fields. How terrible for you, Jerusalem! How long will you go on being unclean?"
This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah about the drought:
"Judah mourns. Its towns are dying. Its people sit on the ground in mourning. A cry goes up from Jerusalem.
The nobles send their servants for water. They go to the wells but find no water. They come back with empty jars. Ashamed and confused, they cover their heads.
The ground is cracked because there has been no rain in the land. The farmers are upset and cover their heads.
Even the deer in the field leaves her newborn fawn, because there is no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare hills, panting like jackals. Their eyes grow dim because there is no food to eat."
Even though our sins accuse us, LORD, do something for the sake of your name. We have turned away from you many times. We have sinned against you.
You are the hope of Israel, its Savior in times of trouble. Why are you like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stays only one night?
Why are you like someone who is confused, like a warrior who cannot save anyone? You are among us, LORD, and we are called by your name. Do not leave us!

This is what the LORD says about this people: "They love to wander. They do not hold back their feet. So the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish them for their sins."
Then the LORD said to me, "Do not pray for good things for these people.
When they fast, I will not listen to their cry. When they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will destroy them with war, hunger, and disease."
But I said, "Oh, Lord GOD! Look, the prophets keep telling them, 'You will not see war or hunger. I will give you lasting peace in this place.'"

Then the LORD said to me, "The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them or command them or speak to them. They are prophesying to you false visions, fortune telling, worthless ideas, and lies from their own minds.

So this is what the LORD says about the prophets who are prophesying in my name, though I did not send them, who say, 'No war or hunger will touch this land.' Those same prophets will die by war and hunger.

And the people they are prophesying to will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem, killed by hunger and war. There will be no one to bury them, or their wives, sons, or daughters. I will pour out on them the punishment their wickedness deserves.
Speak this word to them: 'Let my eyes overflow with tears night and day without stopping. For my people, my virgin daughter, have been struck with a crushing blow, a terrible wound.
If I go out into the countryside, I see those killed by the sword. If I go into the city, I see those dying of hunger. Both prophets and priests wander through a land they do not know.'"

Have you completely rejected Judah? Do you hate Zion? Why have you struck us so badly that we cannot be healed? We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for a time of healing, but there was only terror.
LORD, we admit our wickedness and the sins of our ancestors. We have sinned against you.
For the sake of your name, do not reject us. Do not disgrace your glorious throne. Remember your covenant with us and do not break it.
Can any of the worthless idols of the nations bring rain? Can the sky send showers by itself? No, it is you, LORD our God! So we put our hope in you, for you are the one who does all these things.
Then the LORD said to me, "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me pleading for these people, I would not change my mind toward them. Send them away from me! Let them go!

And if they ask you, 'Where should we go?' tell them, 'This is what the LORD says: Those meant for death, to death. Those meant for the sword, to the sword. Those meant for hunger, to hunger. Those meant for captivity, to captivity.'
I will send four kinds of destroyers against them," says the LORD. "The sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the wild animals to eat and destroy.
I will make them something that horrifies all the kingdoms of the earth, because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem.
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will stop to ask how you are doing?
You have rejected me," says the LORD. "You keep turning your back on me. So I will reach out my hand and destroy you. I am tired of holding back.
I will separate them like chaff with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I will take away their children and destroy my people, for they have not changed their ways.
I will make their widows more numerous than the sand of the sea. At noon I will bring a destroyer against the mothers of young men. I will suddenly bring on them pain and terror.

The mother of seven will grow weak and breathe her last. Her sun will set while it is still day. She will be shamed and disgraced. I will hand over those who survive to the sword in front of their enemies," says the LORD.
How terrible for me, my mother, that you gave birth to me! Everyone in the land argues and fights with me. I have never lent money or borrowed it, yet everyone curses me.
The LORD said, "Surely I will rescue you for a good purpose. Surely I will make your enemies beg you for help in times of disaster and trouble.
Can anyone break iron, the iron from the north, or bronze?
I will give away your riches and your treasures as plunder, free of charge, because of all your sins throughout your land.
I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for my anger has started a fire that will burn against you."
LORD, you understand. Remember me and take care of me. Pay back those who chase after me. You are patient, so do not let me be taken away. Think of how I suffer insults for your sake.
When your words came, I ate them up. They became my joy and the delight of my heart, for I am called by your name, LORD God of Armies.
I never sat with the crowds who laugh and party. I sat alone because your hand was on me, and you filled me with anger at their sin.
Why does my pain never end? Why is my wound so serious that it cannot be healed? Will you be to me like a stream that runs dry, like a spring that fails?

So this is what the LORD says: "If you come back to me, I will take you back, and you will serve me again. If you speak words that are worthy and not worthless, you will be my spokesman. Let these people turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
I will make you a strong bronze wall against these people. They will fight against you, but they will not defeat you, for I am with you to save you and rescue you," says the LORD.
"I will rescue you from the hands of the wicked and save you from the grip of the cruel."
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"You must not marry or have sons or daughters in this place."
For this is what the LORD says about the sons and daughters born in this place, and about the mothers and fathers who gave birth to them in this land:

"They will die of terrible diseases. No one will mourn for them or bury them. They will be like manure lying on the ground. They will die by the sword and by hunger, and their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and the wild animals."

This is what the LORD says: "Do not enter a house where there is a funeral meal. Do not go to mourn or show sympathy for them, because I have taken away my peace from this people," says the LORD, "my faithful love and my mercy.
Both the important and the unimportant will die in this land. They will not be buried or mourned. No one will cut themselves or shave their heads for them.
No one will bring food to comfort those who mourn for the dead. No one will give them a cup to drink to comfort them for their father or mother.
And do not go into a house where there is feasting, to sit with them to eat and drink.

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Look, in this place, before your eyes and in your lifetime, I will put an end to the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom.
When you tell these people all this, they will ask you, 'Why has the LORD announced such a great disaster against us? What wrong have we done? What sin have we committed against the LORD our God?'
Then you will tell them, 'It is because your ancestors left me,' says the LORD. 'They followed other gods and served and worshiped them. They left me and did not keep my law.
But you have done even worse than your ancestors. Look, each of you is following your own stubborn, evil heart instead of listening to me.
So I will throw you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.'
But look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when people will no longer say, 'As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up out of Egypt.'

Instead they will say, 'As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up out of the land of the north and out of all the countries where he had driven them.' For I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors.

But now I am sending for many fishermen," says the LORD, "and they will catch them. After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and hill and in the cracks of the rocks.
My eyes are watching all their ways. They are not hidden from me, and their sin is not hidden from my eyes.

I will first pay them back double for their wrongdoing and their sin, because they have made my land unclean with the lifeless forms of their hateful idols and filled my inheritance with their disgusting things."

LORD, my strength and my fortress, my safe place in times of trouble, the nations will come to you from the ends of the earth and say, "Our ancestors had nothing but false gods, worthless idols that did them no good.
Can people make their own gods? Those are not gods at all!"
"So look, I will teach them. This time I will teach them about my power and my might. Then they will know that my name is the LORD."
"The sin of Judah is written with an iron pen, carved with a diamond point on the tablets of their hearts and on the horns of their altars.
Even their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside the green trees on the high hills.
My mountain in the countryside, I will give away your riches and all your treasures as plunder, along with your high places, because of the sin throughout your land.
Through your own fault you will lose the inheritance I gave you. I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have started a fire in my anger that will burn forever."
This is what the LORD says: "Cursed is the person who trusts in mere humans, who depends on human strength and whose heart turns away from the LORD.
That person will be like a bush in the desert. They will not see good things when they come. They will live in the dry places of the wilderness, in a salty land where no one lives.
But blessed is the person who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in the LORD.

They will be like a tree planted by the water that sends out its roots by the stream. It is not afraid when the heat comes. Its leaves stay green. It does not worry in a year of drought, and it never stops producing fruit."
The heart is more deceitful than anything else, and it is very sick. Who can understand it?
"I, the LORD, search the heart and test the mind, to reward each person according to their ways, according to what their actions deserve."

Like a partridge that sits on eggs it did not lay, so is the person who gets rich in unfair ways. In the middle of their life their riches will leave them, and in the end they will prove to be a fool.
A glorious throne, lifted high from the beginning, is the place of our holy temple.
LORD, you are the hope of Israel. All who leave you will be put to shame. Those who turn away from you will be written in the dust, because they have left the LORD, the spring of living water.
Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved, for you are the one I praise.
They keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come true now!"
But I have not run away from being your shepherd. I have not wished for the day of disaster. You know what I have said. It is all open before you.
Do not be a terror to me. You are my safe place in the day of disaster.
Let those who chase after me be put to shame, but keep me from shame. Let them be terrified, but keep me from terror. Bring on them the day of disaster. Destroy them with double destruction.
This is what the LORD said to me: "Go and stand at the People's Gate, where the kings of Judah go in and out. Then stand at all the other gates of Jerusalem.
Say to them, 'Listen to the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah, all you people of Judah, and everyone living in Jerusalem who comes through these gates.
This is what the LORD says: Be careful not to carry any load on the Sabbath day or bring it in through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath or do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.
But they did not listen or pay attention. They were stubborn and would not listen or accept correction.
But if you carefully obey me, says the LORD, and do not bring a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath, but keep the Sabbath day holy by not doing any work on it,

then kings who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this city with their officials. They will ride in chariots and on horses, along with the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem. And this city will be lived in forever.

People will come from the towns of Judah and the villages around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the western foothills, from the hill country, and from the south. They will bring burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, incense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

But if you do not obey me and keep the Sabbath day holy, if you carry a load as you come through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will set fire to its gates. The fire will burn up the strong buildings of Jerusalem, and it will not be put out.'"
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Get up and go down to the potter's house, and there I will give you my message."
So I went down to the potter's house, and I saw him working at his wheel.
But the pot he was shaping from the clay was ruined in his hands. So the potter made it into another pot, shaping it as he thought best.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"People of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does?" says the LORD. "Look, like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, people of Israel.
If at any time I announce that a nation or kingdom is to be pulled up, torn down, and destroyed,
and if that nation I warned turns from its evil, then I will change my mind and not bring on it the disaster I had planned.
And if at another time I announce that a nation or kingdom is to be built up and planted,
and if it does evil in my eyes and does not obey me, then I will change my mind about the good I had planned to do for it.

So now tell the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am preparing a disaster for you and making a plan against you. So turn from your evil ways, each one of you, and change your ways and your actions.'
But they will reply, 'It is no use. We will continue with our own plans. Each of us will follow our own stubborn, evil heart.'"
So this is what the LORD says: "Ask among the nations: Who has ever heard anything like this? The virgin Israel has done a most horrible thing.
Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave its rocky slopes? Do its cool waters from far away ever stop flowing?
Yet my people have forgotten me. They burn incense to worthless idols. They have stumbled off the ancient paths and walk on side roads that are not built up.
Their land will become a horror, something people hiss at forever. All who pass by will be shocked and shake their heads.
Like a wind from the east, I will scatter them before their enemies. I will show them my back and not my face on the day of their disaster."

Then the people said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah. We will still have priests to teach the law, wise people to give advice, and prophets to give us the word. Come, let us attack him with our words and pay no attention to anything he says."
Listen to me, LORD. Hear what my accusers are saying!
Should good be repaid with evil? Yet they have dug a pit to trap me. Remember how I stood before you and spoke on their behalf, to turn your anger away from them.
So let their children starve, and hand them over to the sword. Let their wives become widows with no children. Let their men be put to death, and their young men killed by the sword in battle.
Let screams be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring raiders against them. For they have dug a pit to capture me and hidden traps for my feet.
But you, LORD, know all their plans to kill me. Do not forgive their wrongdoing or wipe away their sins from your sight. Let them fall down before you. Deal with them when you are angry.
This is what the LORD said: "Go and buy a clay jar from a potter. Take some of the elders of the people and some of the leading priests with you,
and go out to the Valley of Ben Hinnom, near the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. Announce there the words I tell you.

Say, 'Listen to the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am going to bring such a disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears about it will ring.

For they have left me and turned this place into a place for foreign gods. They have burned incense here to gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah ever knew, and they have filled this place with the blood of innocent people.
They have built high places for Baal to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal. I never commanded this or spoke of it, and it never even entered my mind.
So look, the days are coming, says the LORD, when people will no longer call this place Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

In this place I will ruin the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, at the hands of those who want to kill them. I will give their dead bodies as food to the birds of the sky and the wild animals.
I will make this city a horror and something people hiss at. All who pass by will be shocked and will hiss because of all its wounds.
I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and they will eat each other's flesh, during the terrible siege when their enemies who want to kill them surround them.'
Then break the jar while the men who went with you are watching,

and say to them, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: I will smash this nation and this city just as this potter's jar is smashed, so that it cannot be repaired. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room.
This is what I will do to this place and to the people who live here, says the LORD. I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the palaces of the kings of Judah will be made unclean like Topheth, all the houses where they burned incense on the roofs to all the stars of the sky and poured out drink offerings to other gods.'"
Then Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy. He stood in the courtyard of the LORD's house and said to all the people,

"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Look, I am going to bring on this city and all the towns around it every disaster I announced against them, because they were stubborn and refused to listen to my words.'"
Now the priest Pashhur son of Immer, the chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
So Pashhur had the prophet Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, at the house of the LORD.
The next day, when Pashhur released him from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, "The LORD does not call you Pashhur anymore. Your new name is Terror All Around.

For this is what the LORD says: 'I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. With your own eyes you will see them die by the swords of their enemies. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon. He will carry them away to Babylon or kill them with the sword.

I will hand over all the riches of this city to their enemies, all its products, all its valuable things, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah. They will take them as plunder and carry them off to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, and everyone who lives in your house will go into exile in Babylon. There you will die and be buried, you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied lies.'"
LORD, you persuaded me, and I let myself be persuaded. You were stronger than I was, and you won. Now I am laughed at all day long. Everyone makes fun of me.
Whenever I speak, I cry out and shout, "Violence and destruction!" So the word of the LORD has brought me insults and mockery all day long.
But if I say, "I will not mention him or speak anymore in his name," his word is like a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones. I am worn out from holding it in. I cannot do it.

I hear many people whispering, "Terror all around! Report him! Let us report him!" All my friends are waiting for me to slip. They say, "Maybe he can be tricked. Then we will defeat him and get our revenge on him."
But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior. So those who chase after me will stumble and will not win. They will fail and be completely disgraced. Their shame will never be forgotten.
LORD of Armies, you test the righteous and see the heart and the mind. Let me see you pay them back, for I have placed my case in your hands.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For he rescues the needy from the hands of the wicked.
Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother gave birth to me never be blessed!
Cursed be the man who brought my father the news and made him very glad, saying, "A son has been born to you!"
May that man be like the towns the LORD destroyed without pity. May he hear cries of pain in the morning and the battle cry at noon,
because he did not kill me in the womb. Then my mother would have been my grave, and her womb would have stayed pregnant forever.
Why did I ever come out of the womb to see trouble and sorrow, and to end my days in shame?
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malkijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to him. They said,
"Please ask the LORD for us, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is attacking us. Perhaps the LORD will do wonders for us as he has done in the past, and make him leave us."
But Jeremiah answered them, "Tell Zedekiah,

'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am going to turn against you the weapons in your hands, which you are using to fight the king of Babylon and the Babylonians who are surrounding you outside the walls. I will gather them into the middle of this city.
I myself will fight against you with my outstretched hand and my mighty arm, in anger, in fury, and in great rage.
I will strike down those who live in this city, both people and animals. They will die of a terrible disease.

After that, says the LORD, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the people in this city who survive the disease, the sword, and the hunger. I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to their enemies who want to kill them. He will kill them with the sword. He will show them no mercy, pity, or compassion.'
And tell this people, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, hunger, or disease. But whoever goes out and surrenders to the Babylonians who are surrounding you will live. They will escape with their lives.
For I have decided to bring disaster on this city and not good, says the LORD. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.'
And say to the royal family of Judah, 'Listen to the word of the LORD.

Family of David, this is what the LORD says: Do justice every morning. Rescue the person who has been robbed from the one who treats them cruelly. Otherwise my anger will break out and burn like fire because of the evil you have done, and no one will be able to put it out.
Look, I am against you, Jerusalem, you who live above the valley on the rocky plateau, says the LORD. You say, "Who can come down against us? Who can enter our homes?"
But I will punish you as your actions deserve, says the LORD. I will set fire to your forests, and it will burn up everything around you.'"
This is what the LORD says: "Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and announce this message there:
'Listen to the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne, you and your officials and your people who come through these gates.

This is what the LORD says: Do what is fair and right. Rescue the person who has been robbed from the one who treats them cruelly. Do not mistreat or harm the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow. Do not kill innocent people in this place.
For if you truly obey these commands, then kings who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, with their officials and their people.
But if you do not obey these words, I promise by my own name, says the LORD, that this palace will become a ruin.'"
For this is what the LORD says about the palace of the king of Judah: "You are like Gilead to me, like the top of Lebanon. But I will surely make you like a wilderness, like towns where no one lives.
I will send destroyers against you, each with his weapons. They will cut down your finest cedar beams and throw them into the fire.
People from many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?'
And the answer will be, 'Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God. They worshiped and served other gods.'"
Do not weep for the dead king or mourn for him. Instead, weep bitterly for the one who is being taken away, for he will never come back to see his homeland again.
For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, who became king of Judah after his father but has left this place: "He will never come back.
He will die in the place where they have taken him as a captive. He will never see this land again."
"How terrible for the king who builds his palace by doing wrong, and its upper rooms by injustice, who makes his own people work for nothing and does not pay them for their work!
He says, 'I will build myself a great palace with large upper rooms.' He cuts out windows for it, covers it with cedar, and paints it red.
Does having more cedar make you a king? Your father had enough to eat and drink. He did what was fair and right, so everything went well for him.
He defended the cause of the poor and needy, so everything went well. Is that not what it means to know me?" says the LORD.
"But your eyes and your heart are set only on dishonest gain, on killing innocent people, and on cruelty and violence."

So this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: "People will not mourn for him, saying, 'Oh, my brother! Oh, my sister!' They will not mourn for him, saying, 'Oh, my master! Oh, his glory!'
He will be buried like a dead donkey, dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem."
"Go up to Lebanon and cry out. Let your voice be heard in Bashan. Cry out from Abarim, for all your allies have been crushed.
I warned you when you felt safe, but you said, 'I will not listen!' This has been your way since you were young. You have never obeyed me.
The wind will drive all your leaders away, and your allies will go into exile. Then you will be ashamed and disgraced because of all your wickedness.
You who live in Lebanon, who nest among the cedars, how you will groan when pain comes on you, pain like a woman giving birth!
As surely as I live," says the LORD, "even if you, Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would still pull you off.
I will hand you over to those who want to kill you, those you are afraid of, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Babylonians.
I will throw you and the mother who gave birth to you into another country, where neither of you was born, and there you will both die.
You will never come back to the land you long to return to."
Is this man Coniah a hated, broken pot, something no one wants? Why will he and his children be thrown out and sent to a land they do not know?
O land, land, land, listen to the word of the LORD!

This is what the LORD says: "Write this man down as if he had no children, a man who will not succeed in his lifetime. None of his descendants will succeed in sitting on David's throne or ruling in Judah again."
"How terrible for the shepherds who are destroying and scattering the sheep of my pasture!" says the LORD.

So this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to the shepherds who take care of my people: "You have scattered my flock and driven them away. You have not taken care of them. So I will punish you for the evil you have done," says the LORD.
"I myself will gather the survivors of my flock from all the countries where I have driven them. I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will have many children and grow in number.
I will place shepherds over them who will take care of them. They will no longer be afraid or terrified, and none of them will be missing," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will rule as king and act wisely. He will do what is fair and right in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will live in safety. This is the name he will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when people will no longer say, 'As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up out of Egypt.'

Instead they will say, 'As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the descendants of Israel up out of the land of the north and out of all the countries where he had driven them.' Then they will live in their own land."
About the prophets: My heart is broken inside me. All my bones tremble. I am like a drunk man, like someone overcome by wine, because of the LORD and his holy words.

"The land is full of people who are unfaithful in marriage. Because of the curse, the land mourns, and the pastures in the wilderness are dried up. The prophets follow an evil path and use their power in the wrong way.
Both prophets and priests are godless. Even in my temple I find their wickedness," says the LORD.
"So their path will become slippery, and they will be driven into darkness and fall there. For I will bring disaster on them in the year they are punished," says the LORD.
"Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something disgusting. They prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible. They commit adultery and live a lie. They encourage those who do evil, so that no one turns away from their wickedness. To me they are all like Sodom, and the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah."

So this is what the LORD of Armies says about the prophets: "Look, I will make them eat bitter food and drink poisoned water, because from the prophets of Jerusalem godlessness has spread throughout the land."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Do not listen to what the prophets are telling you. They fill you with false hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
They keep saying to those who hate me, 'The LORD says you will have peace.' And to all who follow their stubborn hearts they say, 'No harm will come to you.'
But which of them has stood in the council of the LORD to see and hear his word? Who has listened and heard his message?
Look, the storm of the LORD will burst out in fury, a whirlwind swirling down on the heads of the wicked.
The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has fully carried out the plans of his heart. In the days to come you will understand this clearly.
I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message. I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied.
But if they had stood in my council, they would have announced my words to my people. They would have turned them from their evil ways and their evil actions.
Am I only a God who is nearby," says the LORD, "and not a God who is far away?
Can anyone hide in secret places so that I cannot see them?" says the LORD. "Do I not fill heaven and earth?" says the LORD.
"I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in my name. They say, 'I had a dream! I had a dream!'
How long will this go on in the hearts of these lying prophets, who prophesy the deceitful ideas of their own minds?
They think the dreams they tell one another will make my people forget my name, just as their ancestors forgot my name by worshiping Baal.
Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let the one who has my word speak my word faithfully. What does straw have to do with grain?" says the LORD.
"Is not my word like fire," says the LORD, "and like a hammer that breaks a rock into pieces?
So look, I am against the prophets," says the LORD, "who steal my words from one another.
Look, I am against the prophets," says the LORD, "who use their own tongues and then say, 'The LORD says.'

Look, I am against those who prophesy false dreams," says the LORD. "They tell them and lead my people astray with their reckless lies. I did not send them or appoint them. They do not help these people at all," says the LORD.
"When these people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, 'What is the burden, the message from the LORD?' say to them, 'What burden? I will throw you away, says the LORD.'
If a prophet or a priest or anyone else says, 'This is the burden from the LORD,' I will punish that person and their household.
This is what each of you should keep saying to your friends and relatives: 'What answer has the LORD given?' or 'What has the LORD spoken?'
But you must no longer mention 'the burden from the LORD,' for each person's own words become their burden. You twist the words of the living God, the LORD of Armies, our God.
This is what you should say to a prophet: 'What answer has the LORD given you?' or 'What has the LORD spoken?'

But if you say, 'This is the burden from the LORD,' then this is what the LORD says: 'You used the words, "This is the burden from the LORD," even though I told you not to say, "This is the burden from the LORD."
So I will surely forget you and throw you out of my presence, along with the city I gave to you and your ancestors.
I will bring on you everlasting disgrace, everlasting shame that will never be forgotten.'"

After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with the officials of Judah and the craftsmen and metalworkers, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs placed in front of the LORD's temple.
One basket had very good figs, like figs that ripen early. The other basket had very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
Then the LORD asked me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten."
Then the LORD's message came to me:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Like these good figs, I will regard as good the exiles from Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Babylonians.
I will watch over them for their good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down. I will plant them and not pull them up.
I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the LORD. They will be my people, and I will be their God, because they will return to me with all their heart.

"'But like the bad figs, which are so bad they cannot be eaten,' says the LORD, 'so I will treat Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the survivors in Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who live in Egypt.
