I will make them something terrible to all the kingdoms of the earth, tossed back and forth. They will be a disgrace, a byword, a mockery, and a curse everywhere I drive them.
I will send war, famine, and disease against them until they are wiped out from the land I gave to them and their ancestors.'"
This message came to Jeremiah about all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah. That was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
Jeremiah the prophet spoke it to all the people of Judah and to everyone living in Jerusalem:
For twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until today, the LORD's word has come to me. I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.
The LORD has sent all his servants the prophets to you again and again, but you have not listened or paid attention.
They said, "Turn back, each of you, from your evil ways and evil deeds. Then you can live in the land the LORD gave to you and your ancestors forever and ever.
Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them. Do not make me angry with the idols you make with your hands. Then I will not harm you."
"But you did not listen to me," says the LORD. "You made me angry with the idols you made with your hands, and you brought harm on yourselves."
So this is what the LORD of Armies says: "Because you have not listened to my words,

I will send for all the peoples of the north," says the LORD, "and for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will bring them against this land, against its people, and against all the surrounding nations. I will completely destroy them and make them an object of horror and mockery, a ruin forever.
I will take away from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bride and groom, the sound of millstones, and the light of the lamp.
This whole land will become a horrifying ruin, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
"But when the seventy years are over, I will punish the king of Babylon and his nation for their sin," says the LORD. "I will make the land of the Babylonians a ruin forever.
I will bring on that land everything I have said against it, everything written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
Many nations and great kings will make slaves of them too. I will pay them back for what they have done and for the work of their hands."
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: "Take this cup filled with the wine of my anger from my hand. Make all the nations I send you to drink it.
When they drink it, they will stagger and go mad because of the war I will send among them."
So I took the cup from the LORD's hand and made all the nations he sent me to drink it:
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and officials, to make them a ruin, an object of horror, mockery, and cursing, as they are today;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, and all his people;
all the foreign people there; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the Philistines, of Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what is left of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites;
all the kings of Tyre and Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who cut the corners of their hair;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the foreign peoples who live in the desert;
all the kings of Zimri, Elam, and the Medes;
and all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, all the kingdoms on the face of the earth. And after them, the king of Sheshach will drink it too.
"Then tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk, and vomit. Fall down and never get up again, because of the war I will send among you.'
If they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: You must drink it!

Look, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that is called by my name. Do you really think you will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, because I am calling for war against everyone on earth, says the LORD of Armies.'

"So prophesy all these words against them. Tell them: 'The LORD will roar from on high. He will thunder from his holy dwelling. He will roar mightily against his land. He will shout like those who stomp grapes, against everyone on earth.
The noise will reach the ends of the earth, because the LORD has a case against the nations. He will judge all people, and he will hand the wicked over to the sword,' says the LORD."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Look, disaster is spreading from nation to nation. A great storm is rising from the farthest parts of the earth."
On that day those killed by the LORD will lie everywhere, from one end of the earth to the other. No one will mourn them, gather them, or bury them. They will lie like manure on the ground.
Cry and wail, you shepherds! Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock! The time has come for you to be slaughtered and scattered. You will fall and shatter like fine pottery.
The shepherds will have nowhere to run. The leaders of the flock will have no escape.
Listen to the cry of the shepherds and the wailing of the leaders of the flock, because the LORD is destroying their pasture.
The peaceful meadows are silenced because of the LORD's fierce anger.
Like a lion he has left his den. Their land has become a ruin because of the cruel sword and because of his fierce anger.
Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came from the LORD:

"This is what the LORD says: 'Stand in the courtyard of the LORD's temple and speak to the people of all the towns of Judah who come to worship in the LORD's temple. Tell them everything I command you. Do not leave out a single word.
Maybe they will listen, and each one will turn from their evil ways. Then I may change my mind about the disaster I plan to bring on them because of the evil they have done.'
Tell them, 'This is what the LORD says: If you will not listen to me and follow my law, which I have set before you,
and if you will not listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you again and again, though you have not listened,
then I will make this temple like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.'"
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the LORD's temple.
As soon as Jeremiah finished telling all the people everything the LORD had commanded him to say, the priests, the prophets, and all the people grabbed him and said, "You must die!
Why do you prophesy in the LORD's name that this temple will be like Shiloh and this city will be a ruin with no one living in it?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the LORD's temple.
When the officials of Judah heard about this, they went up from the king's palace to the LORD's temple and sat down at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's temple.
Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man deserves to die, because he has prophesied against this city. You have heard it with your own ears."
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this temple and this city all the words you have heard.
So now change your ways and your actions, and obey the LORD your God. Then the LORD will change his mind about the disaster he has announced against you.
As for me, I am in your hands. Do with me whatever you think is good and right.

But know this for certain: if you put me to death, you will bring the guilt of innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on the people who live here. For it is true that the LORD sent me to you to speak all these words for you to hear."
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve to die. He has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."
Some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole assembly of people,

"Micah from Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He told all the people of Judah, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: Zion will be plowed like a field. Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple hill will become a hill covered with forest.'

Did Hezekiah king of Judah or anyone in Judah put him to death? Didn't Hezekiah fear the LORD and ask for the LORD's favor? And didn't the LORD change his mind about the disaster he had announced against them? We are about to bring terrible harm on ourselves!"
There was another man who prophesied in the LORD's name, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath Jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land the same things Jeremiah did.
When King Jehoiakim, all his soldiers, and all the officials heard what he said, the king tried to have him killed. But Uriah heard about it and was afraid, so he ran away to Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men to Egypt.
They brought Uriah back from Egypt to King Jehoiakim, who had him killed with a sword. His body was thrown into the burial place of the common people.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, so he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD.
This is what the LORD said to me: "Make a yoke out of straps and wooden bars, and put it on your neck.
Then send messages to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon through the messengers who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Give them a message for their masters: 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Tell your masters this:
By my great power and my outstretched arm I made the earth, and the people and animals on it. I give it to anyone I choose.
Now I have handed all these lands over to my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I have even made the wild animals serve him.
All nations will serve him, his son, and his grandson, until the time comes for his own land to fall. Then many nations and great kings will make him their slave.

If any nation or kingdom will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon or put its neck under his yoke, I will punish that nation with war, famine, and disease, says the LORD, until I have destroyed it by his hand.
So do not listen to your prophets, your fortune-tellers, your dreams, your mediums, or your sorcerers who tell you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon."
They are prophesying lies to you. They will only cause you to be taken far from your land. I will drive you out, and you will die.
But if any nation puts its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will let that nation stay in its own land to farm it and live there, says the LORD.'"
I gave the same message to Zedekiah king of Judah. I said, "Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon. Serve him and his people, and you will live.
Why should you and your people die by war, famine, and disease, as the LORD has said will happen to any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the prophets who tell you, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon,' because they are prophesying lies to you.
'I did not send them,' says the LORD. 'They are prophesying lies in my name. So I will drive you out, and you will die, both you and the prophets who prophesy to you.'"

Then I said to the priests and to all these people, "This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to your prophets who say, 'Look, the things from the LORD's temple will soon be brought back from Babylon.' They are prophesying lies to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and you will live. Why should this city become a ruin?

If they really are prophets and have the LORD's word, let them pray to the LORD of Armies that the things still left in the LORD's temple, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem will not be taken to Babylon.
For this is what the LORD of Armies says about the pillars, the large bronze basin called the Sea, the stands, and the other things left in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he took Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
Yes, this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about the things left in the LORD's temple, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
'They will be taken to Babylon, and they will stay there until the day I come for them,' says the LORD. 'Then I will bring them back and return them to this place.'"

In the fifth month of that same year, the fourth year of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon, spoke to me in the LORD's temple in front of the priests and all the people. He said,
"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I will bring back to this place all the things from the LORD's temple that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from here and carried to Babylon.

I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles from Judah who went to Babylon,' says the LORD, 'because I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah answered the prophet Hananiah in front of the priests and all the people standing in the LORD's temple.
The prophet Jeremiah said, "Amen! May the LORD do this! May the LORD make your prophecy come true and bring back the things from the LORD's temple and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
But listen to what I have to say to you and to all the people.
The prophets who came before you and me, long ago, prophesied war, disaster, and disease against many countries and great kingdoms.
But a prophet who prophesies peace will be recognized as truly sent by the LORD only when his message comes true."
Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke off the prophet Jeremiah's neck and broke it.

Hananiah said in front of all the people, "This is what the LORD says: 'In the same way, within two years I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon off the necks of all the nations.'" Then the prophet Jeremiah went on his way.
After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke off the prophet Jeremiah's neck, the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Go and tell Hananiah, 'This is what the LORD says: You have broken a wooden yoke, but in its place you have made a yoke of iron.

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I have put an iron yoke on the necks of all these nations to make them serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him. I have even given him the wild animals.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, but you have made these people trust in a lie.
So this is what the LORD says: 'Look, I am going to remove you from the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have preached rebellion against the LORD.'"
And the prophet Hananiah died in the seventh month of that same year.

This is the letter that the prophet Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the elders who were left among the exiles, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had taken into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem.
He sent it with Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The letter said:
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon:
"Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat what they grow.
Get married and have sons and daughters. Find wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they also have sons and daughters. Grow in number there. Do not decrease.
Work for the peace and well-being of the city where I sent you into exile. Pray to the LORD for it, because if it has peace, you will have peace."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Do not let the prophets and fortune-tellers among you deceive you. Do not listen to the dreams you encourage them to have.
They are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "When seventy years are over for Babylon, I will come to you and keep my good promise to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you," says the LORD, "plans for peace and not for disaster, to give you hope and a future.
Then you will call on me, and you will come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will look for me and find me when you search for me with all your heart.

I will let you find me," says the LORD, "and I will bring you back from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you," says the LORD. "I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile."
You may say, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon."
But this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people who live in this city, your relatives who did not go with you into exile.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Look, I will send war, famine, and disease against them. I will make them like rotten figs, so bad they cannot be eaten.

I will chase them with war, famine, and disease. I will make them something terrible to all the kingdoms of the earth, an object of horror, shock, mockery, and disgrace among all the nations where I drive them.
This is because they have not listened to my words," says the LORD, "which I sent to them again and again through my servants the prophets. And you exiles have not listened either," says the LORD.
So listen to the LORD's message, all you exiles whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: "Look, I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them right before your eyes.
Because of them, all the exiles from Judah in Babylon will use this curse: 'May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire.'

For they have done disgraceful things in Israel. They committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and spoke lies in my name, things I did not command them. I know it, and I am a witness to it," says the LORD.
Tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite:

"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests. You wrote,
'The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be in charge of the LORD's temple. You should put any madman who acts like a prophet in the stocks and in chains.
So why have you not stopped Jeremiah from Anathoth, who acts like a prophet among you?
He has sent a message to us in Babylon saying, The exile will be long. Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat what they grow.'"
Zephaniah the priest read this letter to Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Send this message to all the exiles: 'This is what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Shemaiah has prophesied to you, even though I did not send him, and he has made you trust in a lie.

So this is what the LORD says: I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. None of his family will be left among these people, and he will not see the good things I will do for my people, says the LORD, because he has preached rebellion against the LORD.'"
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

For look, the days are coming,' says the LORD, 'when I will bring my people Israel and Judah back from captivity,' says the LORD. 'I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will own it.'"
These are the words the LORD spoke about Israel and Judah.
This is what the LORD says: "We hear cries of terror, of fear, not of peace.
Ask and see: can a man give birth to a child? Then why do I see every strong man holding his stomach like a woman in labor? Why has every face turned pale?
How terrible that day will be! There will be no other like it. It will be a time of trouble for Jacob, but he will be rescued from it.
On that day," says the LORD of Armies, "I will break the yoke off their necks and tear off their chains. Foreigners will no longer make them slaves.
Instead they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

So do not be afraid, Jacob my servant," says the LORD. "Do not be discouraged, Israel. For look, I will rescue you from far away, and your descendants from the land where they are captives. Jacob will come back and have peace and quiet. No one will make him afraid.

For I am with you to save you," says the LORD. "I will completely destroy all the nations where I scattered you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will correct you fairly, but I will not let you go unpunished."
This is what the LORD says: "Your injury cannot be healed. Your wound is very serious.
There is no one to plead your case, no bandage for your wound. You have no medicine to heal you.
All your lovers have forgotten you. They do not care about you. I have struck you as an enemy would, and punished you cruelly, because your guilt is so great and your sins so many.
Why do you cry out about your injury? Your pain cannot be healed. I have done these things to you because your guilt is so great and your sins so many.
But all who devour you will be devoured. All your enemies, every one of them, will go into exile. Those who rob you will be robbed. All who attack you will be attacked.
For I will make you healthy again and heal your wounds," says the LORD, "because they have called you an outcast, saying, 'This is Zion, whom no one cares about.'"

This is what the LORD says: "Look, I will bring Jacob's people back from captivity and have compassion on their homes. The city will be rebuilt on its ruins, and the palace will stand in its proper place.
Songs of thanks and the sound of celebration will come from them. I will make them grow in number, and they will not be few. I will honor them, and they will not be looked down on.
Their children will be as they were long ago. Their community will be established before me, and I will punish all who oppress them.
Their leader will be one of their own. Their ruler will come from among them. I will bring him near, and he will come close to me. For who would dare come close to me on his own?" says the LORD.
"So you will be my people, and I will be your God."
Look, the storm of the LORD will burst out in fury, a sweeping storm swirling down on the heads of the wicked.
The LORD's fierce anger will not turn back until he has fully carried out the plans of his heart. In the days to come you will understand this.
"At that time," says the LORD, "I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people."
This is what the LORD says: "The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness. I will come to give Israel rest."
Long ago the LORD appeared to us and said: "I have loved you with a love that lasts forever. That is why I have kept drawing you to me with faithful love.
I will build you up again, and you will be rebuilt, young Israel. Once more you will pick up your tambourines and go out dancing with joy.
Once more you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria. The farmers will plant them and enjoy their fruit.
A day will come when watchmen on the hills of Ephraim will shout, 'Come, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!'"
This is what the LORD says: "Sing with joy for Jacob. Shout for the greatest of the nations. Make it known, praise, and say, 'LORD, save your people, the survivors of Israel!'

Look, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the ends of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, pregnant women and women in labor. A huge crowd will come back.

They will come weeping, and I will lead them as they pray. I will guide them beside streams of water, on a smooth path where they will not stumble. For I am Israel's father, and Ephraim is my firstborn son.
Listen to the LORD's message, you nations. Announce it in the faraway coastlands. Say, 'The one who scattered Israel will gather them and watch over them like a shepherd watches his flock.'
For the LORD has rescued Jacob and set him free from someone too strong for him.

They will come and sing for joy on the heights of Zion. They will be radiant over the LORD's good gifts: the grain, the new wine, the olive oil, the young sheep and cattle. Their lives will be like a well-watered garden, and they will never be sad again.
Then young women will dance for joy, and young men and old men too. I will turn their mourning into joy. I will comfort them and give them gladness instead of sorrow.
I will give the priests more than enough, and my people will be filled with my good gifts," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted, because her children are gone."
This is what the LORD says: "Stop your crying and wipe away your tears, for your work will be rewarded," says the LORD. "Your children will come back from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future," says the LORD. "Your children will come back to their own land.
I have clearly heard Ephraim mourning: 'You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will come back, for you are the LORD my God.
After I turned away, I was sorry. After I understood, I beat my chest in sorrow. I was ashamed and humiliated, because I carried the disgrace of my youth.'
Is Ephraim not my dear son, the child I delight in? Even though I often speak against him, I still remember him with love. So my heart longs for him. I will surely have mercy on him," says the LORD.
"Set up road signs. Put up guideposts. Pay attention to the highway, the road you traveled. Come back, young Israel. Come back to these towns of yours.
How long will you wander, unfaithful daughter? For the LORD has created something new on earth: a woman will protect a man."

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "When I bring them back from captivity, the people in the land of Judah and its towns will once again say: 'May the LORD bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain.'
Judah and all its towns will live there together, the farmers and those who move about with their flocks.
For I will refresh the weary and satisfy everyone who is weak with sorrow."
At this I woke up and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will fill the land of Israel and Judah with people and animals.
Just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant," says the LORD.
"In those days people will no longer say, 'The parents have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'
Instead, each person will die for their own sin. Whoever eats sour grapes, their own teeth will be set on edge.
Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. They broke that covenant, even though I was like a husband to them," says the LORD.

"But this is the covenant I will make with the people of Israel after those days," says the LORD: "I will put my law inside them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

No longer will they need to teach their neighbors or their relatives, saying, 'Know the LORD,' because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest," says the LORD. "For I will forgive their sin, and I will never again remember their wrongs."
This is what the LORD says, he who gives the sun to light the day and sets the moon and stars to light the night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is his name:
"If these laws of nature ever disappear from my sight," says the LORD, "then Israel's descendants will stop being a nation before me forever."

This is what the LORD says: "If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I will reject all of Israel's descendants for everything they have done," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when this city will be rebuilt for the LORD, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will stretch from there straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn toward Goah.

The whole valley where dead bodies and ashes are thrown, and all the fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the LORD. The city will never again be uprooted or torn down."
This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was surrounding Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was locked up in the courtyard of the guard at the palace of the king of Judah.

Zedekiah king of Judah had locked him up there. He said, "Why do you prophesy like this? You say, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Babylonians. He will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will speak to him face to face and see him with his own eyes.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and Zedekiah will stay there until I deal with him, says the LORD. If you fight against the Babylonians, you will not win.'"
Jeremiah said, "The LORD's message came to me:
'Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is going to come to you and say, "Buy my field in Anathoth, because as my nearest relative you have the right to buy it."'

Then, just as the LORD had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said, 'Please buy my field in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin. You have the right to own it and to buy it back for the family. Buy it for yourself.' Then I knew this was the LORD's message.
So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out seventeen pieces of silver for him.
I signed the deed and sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed out the silver on the scales.
Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy containing the terms and conditions and the open copy.
I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah. I did this in front of my cousin Hanamel, the witnesses who had signed the deed, and all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
In front of them all I gave Baruch these instructions:
'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds, both the sealed copy and the open copy, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields, and vineyards will once again be bought in this land.'
After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
"Oh, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and your outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.
You show faithful love to thousands, but you also bring the consequences of the parents' sins on their children after them. You are the great and mighty God. The LORD of Armies is your name.
Your plans are great, and your deeds are mighty. Your eyes see everything people do, and you reward each person for how they live and for what they do.
You did miraculous signs and wonders in Egypt, and you still do them today, both in Israel and among all people. You have made a name for yourself that lasts to this day.
You brought your people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land that you promised their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They came in and took it over, but they did not obey you or follow your law. They did nothing you commanded them to do. So you brought all this disaster on them.

Look, siege ramps have been built against the city to capture it. Because of war, famine, and disease, the city will be handed over to the Babylonians who are attacking it. What you said has happened, as you can see.
And yet, Lord GOD, you have told me, 'Buy the field with silver and call witnesses,' even though the city will be handed over to the Babylonians."
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Look, I am the LORD, the God of all people. Is anything too hard for me?
So this is what the LORD says: I am going to hand this city over to the Babylonians and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Babylonians attacking this city will come in and set it on fire. They will burn it down, along with the houses where people made me angry by burning incense to Baal on the roofs and pouring out drink offerings to other gods.

The people of Israel and Judah have done nothing but evil in my sight since they were young. The people of Israel have done nothing but make me angry with the idols they made with their hands, says the LORD.
From the day this city was built until now, it has stirred up my anger and fury, so I must remove it from my sight.

This is because of all the evil the people of Israel and Judah have done to make me angry: they, their kings, their officials, their priests, their prophets, the people of Judah, and those living in Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me, not their faces. I taught them again and again, but they would not listen or accept correction.
They set up their disgusting idols in the temple that is called by my name, and made it unclean.

They built high places for Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, to sacrifice their sons and daughters in the fire to Molech. I never commanded them to do this. It never even entered my mind that they would do something so disgusting and make Judah sin."
"Now this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about this city. You are saying, 'It will be handed over to the king of Babylon through war, famine, and disease.'
But look, I will gather them from all the countries where I drove them in my anger, fury, and great rage. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.
They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way of life, so that they will always respect me, for their own good and for the good of their children after them.
I will make a covenant with them that will last forever. I will never stop doing good to them. I will put respect for me in their hearts, so that they will never turn away from me.
I will enjoy doing good to them. I will faithfully plant them in this land with all my heart and all my soul."
This is what the LORD says: "Just as I have brought all this great disaster on these people, so I will bring them all the good things I have promised them.
Fields will be bought again in this land. You now say, 'It is a wasteland with no people or animals. It has been handed over to the Babylonians.'

But people will buy fields with silver, sign deeds, seal them, and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, in the villages around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, in the towns of the hill country, the western foothills, and the Negev, because I will bring them back from captivity," says the LORD.
While Jeremiah was still locked up in the courtyard of the guard, the LORD's message came to him a second time:
"This is what the LORD says, the LORD who made the earth, who formed it and set it in place. The LORD is his name:
'Call to me, and I will answer you. I will tell you great and hidden things that you do not know.'
For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Judah, which have been torn down to defend against the siege ramps and the sword:

'People are coming to fight the Babylonians, but the houses will be filled with the dead bodies of those I will kill in my anger and fury. I have turned my face away from this city because of all its wickedness.
But look, I will bring health and healing to it. I will heal my people and let them enjoy great peace and security.
I will bring Judah and Israel back from captivity and rebuild them as they were before.
I will make them clean from all the sin they have committed against me. I will forgive all their sins and their rebellion against me.

Then this city will bring me joy, praise, and honor before all the nations of the earth. They will hear about all the good things I do for it, and they will tremble in awe at all the good and the peace I give it.'"

This is what the LORD says: "You say about this place, 'It is a ruin, with no people or animals.' The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are empty, with no people or animals living there. But in this place you will hear once again

the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bride and groom, and the voices of people bringing thank offerings to the LORD's temple, saying, 'Give thanks to the LORD of Armies, for the LORD is good. His faithful love lasts forever.' For I will bring the land back from captivity as it was before," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "In this place, now a ruin with no people or animals, and in all its towns, there will again be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, the western foothills, and the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, in the villages around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will keep the good promise I made to the people of Israel and the people of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will make a righteous Branch grow from David's family. He will do what is fair and right in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will live in safety. This is the name it will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness."
For this is what the LORD says: "David will never fail to have a descendant sitting on the throne of Israel.
And the Levitical priests will never fail to have someone standing before me to offer burnt offerings, burn grain offerings, and make sacrifices every day."
The LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"This is what the LORD says: 'If you could break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer came at their set times,
then my covenant with my servant David could be broken, and he would have no descendant to rule on his throne. So could my covenant with the Levitical priests who serve me.
Just as the stars in the sky cannot be counted and the sand on the seashore cannot be measured, so I will make the descendants of my servant David and the Levites who serve me too many to count.'"
The LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Have you noticed what these people are saying? 'The LORD has rejected the two families he chose.' So they look down on my people and no longer think of them as a nation."
This is what the LORD says: "If I had not made my covenant with day and night, and set the laws of heaven and earth,

then I would reject the descendants of Jacob and of my servant David, and not choose any of David's descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But I will bring them back from captivity and have mercy on them."

This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and all its towns, with his whole army and all the kingdoms and peoples of the earth under his rule:

"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah. Tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.

You will not escape from him. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. You will see the king of Babylon with your own eyes, and he will speak to you face to face. And you will go to Babylon.'
But listen to the LORD's message, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the LORD says about you: 'You will not die by the sword.

You will die in peace. As people burned spices in honor of your ancestors, the kings who came before you, so they will burn spices in your honor and mourn for you, saying, "Oh no, master!" I myself have promised this,' says the LORD."
Then Jeremiah the prophet told all this to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.
At the time, the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and the remaining towns of Judah, Lachish and Azekah. These were the only fortified towns left in Judah.
The LORD's message came to Jeremiah after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to announce freedom for the slaves.
Everyone was to set free their Hebrew slaves, both men and women. No one was to keep a fellow Jew as a slave.
All the officials and people who made this covenant agreed to set their male and female slaves free and not keep them as slaves any longer. They obeyed and let them go.
But later they changed their minds. They took back the slaves they had freed and forced them to become slaves again.
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, the land where they were slaves. I said,

'At the end of every seven years, each of you must free any fellow Hebrew who has sold himself to you. After he has served you six years, you must let him go free.' But your ancestors did not listen to me or pay attention.
Recently you turned back and did what is right in my eyes. Each of you announced freedom for your fellow Hebrews. You even made a covenant before me in the temple that is called by my name.
But then you turned around and dishonored my name. Each of you took back the male and female slaves you had set free to go wherever they wanted. You forced them to become your slaves again."

"So this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed me by announcing freedom for your fellow Hebrews and neighbors. So look, I am announcing freedom for you," says the LORD, "freedom to die by war, disease, and famine. I will make you something terrible to all the kingdoms of the earth.
I will hand over the people who broke my covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before me. They cut a calf in two and walked between its pieces.
The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land walked between the pieces of the calf.
I will hand them over to their enemies who want to kill them. Their dead bodies will become food for the birds and the wild animals.
I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials to their enemies who want to kill them, to the army of the king of Babylon, which has pulled back from you for now.

Look, I will give the order," says the LORD, "and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it down. I will make the towns of Judah a ruin where no one lives."
This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
"Go to the Rechabite family and speak to them. Bring them into one of the rooms of the LORD's temple and give them wine to drink."
So I went and got Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, along with his brothers and all his sons, the whole Rechabite family.

I brought them into the LORD's temple, into the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. It was next to the officials' room, above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the doorkeeper.
I set bowls full of wine and some cups in front of the Rechabites and said to them, "Drink some wine."
But they answered, "We do not drink wine, because our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us: 'You and your descendants must never drink wine.
Do not build houses, plant seeds, or plant vineyards. Do not own any of these things. Instead, always live in tents. Then you will live a long time in the land where you are wanderers.'
We have obeyed everything our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us. We have never drunk wine, nor have our wives, sons, or daughters.
We have not built houses to live in. We have no vineyards, fields, or crops.
We have lived in tents and fully obeyed everything our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.
But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded the land, we said, 'Come, let us go to Jerusalem to escape the Babylonian and Aramean armies.' That is why we are living in Jerusalem."
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Go and tell the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem, 'Will you not learn a lesson and obey my words?' says the LORD.

'Jonadab son of Rechab ordered his descendants not to drink wine, and they have obeyed him. To this day they do not drink wine, because they obey their ancestor's command. But I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not obeyed me.

Again and again I sent you all my servants the prophets. They said, "Each of you must turn from your evil ways and change what you do. Do not follow other gods to serve them. Then you will live in the land I gave to you and your ancestors." But you did not pay attention or listen to me.
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their ancestor gave them, but these people have not obeyed me.'

So this is what the LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Look, I am going to bring on Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem all the disaster I announced against them. I spoke to them, but they did not listen. I called to them, but they did not answer.'"

Then Jeremiah said to the Rechabite family, "This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'You have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jonadab. You have kept all his instructions and done everything he commanded you.'
So this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a descendant who serves me.'"
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you about Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the time I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until today.
Maybe when the people of Judah hear about all the disaster I plan to bring on them, each of them will turn from their evil ways. Then I will forgive their wickedness and their sin."
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on a scroll all the words the LORD had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah told Baruch, "I am restricted. I cannot go into the LORD's temple.

So you go to the LORD's temple on a day of fasting and read the LORD's words from the scroll you wrote as I dictated. Read them to the people there, and to all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.
Maybe they will bring their prayers to the LORD and each turn from their evil ways, because the anger and fury the LORD has announced against these people are great."
Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet told him. He read the LORD's words from the scroll in the LORD's temple.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a time of fasting before the LORD was announced for all the people in Jerusalem and all who came to Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.

Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll to all the people in the LORD's temple. He read them from the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the temple.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the LORD's words from the scroll,

he went down to the secretary's room in the king's palace. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah told them everything he had heard Baruch read to the people from the scroll.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch with this message: "Bring the scroll you read to the people and come here." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and went to them.
They said to him, "Please sit down and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they looked at each other in fear and said to Baruch, "We must tell the king everything."
Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you write all this? Did Jeremiah dictate it?"
Baruch answered, "Yes, he dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."
Then the officials told Baruch, "You and Jeremiah must go and hide. Do not let anyone know where you are."
They left the scroll in the room of Elishama the secretary and went to the king in the courtyard. They told him everything.
The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi brought it from the room of Elishama the secretary. He read it to the king and to all the officials standing beside him.
It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in his winter house, with a fire burning in a fire pot in front of him.
Each time Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut them off with a knife and threw them into the fire, until the whole scroll was burned up in the fire pot.
The king and his servants heard all these words, but they were not afraid. They did not tear their clothes in sorrow.
Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah even begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
Instead the king ordered Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.
After the king had burned the scroll with the words Baruch had written as Jeremiah dictated, the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Take another scroll and write on it everything that was on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And tell Jehoiakim king of Judah, 'This is what the LORD says: You burned that scroll and said, "Why did you write that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and wipe out both people and animals?"
So this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no descendant to sit on David's throne. His dead body will be thrown out, left in the heat by day and the frost by night.

I will punish him, his children, and his servants for their wickedness. I will bring on them, on the people living in Jerusalem, and on the people of Judah all the disaster I announced against them, because they did not listen.'"

So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it everything that had been on the scroll Jehoiakim king of Judah burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to it.
Zedekiah son of Josiah became king of Judah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made him king of the land of Judah.
But neither he, nor his officials, nor the people of the land listened to the words the LORD spoke through the prophet Jeremiah.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to the prophet Jeremiah with this request: "Please pray to the LORD our God for us."
At this time Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, because he had not yet been put in prison.
Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt. When the Babylonians who were surrounding Jerusalem heard the news, they pulled back from Jerusalem.
Then the LORD's message came to the prophet Jeremiah:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to ask me, 'Look, Pharaoh's army, which has come out to help you, will go back to its own land, Egypt.
Then the Babylonians will come back and attack this city. They will capture it and burn it down.'
This is what the LORD says: Do not fool yourselves by thinking, 'The Babylonians will surely leave us.' They will not leave.
Even if you defeated the whole Babylonian army attacking you, and only wounded men were left in their tents, they would get up and burn this city down."
After the Babylonian army had pulled back from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to claim his share of property among the people there.
But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the captain of the guard there, Irijah son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah, arrested the prophet Jeremiah and said, "You are deserting to the Babylonians!"
Jeremiah said, "That is not true! I am not deserting to the Babylonians." But Irijah would not listen. He arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were furious with Jeremiah. They beat him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had turned into a prison.
Jeremiah was put into a cell in an underground dungeon, and he stayed there a long time.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he asked him privately, "Is there any message from the LORD?" Jeremiah answered, "Yes, there is. You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."
Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What crime have I committed against you, your officials, or these people that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not attack you or this land'?
Now please listen, my lord the king. Please let me bring my request to you. Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."

So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was placed in the courtyard of the guard. Every day he was given a loaf of bread from the street of the bakers, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.
Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah heard what Jeremiah was telling all the people:

"This is what the LORD says: 'Whoever stays in this city will die by war, famine, or disease. But whoever goes out and surrenders to the Babylonians will live. They will escape with their life and survive.'
This is what the LORD says: 'This city will certainly be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.'"

Then the officials said to the king, "This man must be put to death. He is discouraging the soldiers who are left in this city, and all the people too, by the things he is saying. This man is not looking out for the good of these people, but for their harm."
King Zedekiah said, "He is in your hands. The king cannot do anything to stop you."

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the well of Malchijah, the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes. There was no water in the well, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
But Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a court official in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the well. At that time the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
Ebedmelech left the palace and said to the king,

"My lord the king, these men have done a wicked thing in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into a well, and he will starve to death there, because there is no more bread in the city."
Then the king commanded Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, "Take thirty men from here with you and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the well before he dies."
So Ebedmelech took the men with him and went to a room under the treasury in the palace. He took some old rags and worn-out clothes from there and lowered them with ropes into the well to Jeremiah.
Ebedmelech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah, "Put these old rags and worn-out clothes under your arms to pad the ropes." Jeremiah did so.
Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and lifted him out of the well. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

Then King Zedekiah sent for the prophet Jeremiah and had him brought to the third entrance of the LORD's temple. The king said to Jeremiah, "I am going to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me."
Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, won't you surely put me to death? And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me."
But King Zedekiah made a secret promise to Jeremiah: "As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us breath, I will not put you to death or hand you over to these men who want to kill you."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared and this city will not be burned down. You and your family will live.
But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Babylonians. They will burn it down, and you will not escape from them.'"
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have deserted to the Babylonians. They may hand me over to them, and they will treat me cruelly."
But Jeremiah said, "They will not hand you over. Please obey the LORD by doing what I tell you. Then things will go well for you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:

Look, all the women left in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officers of the king of Babylon. Those women will say to you: 'Your close friends misled you and overpowered you. Now that your feet are stuck in the mud, they have deserted you.'

All your wives and children will be brought out to the Babylonians. You yourself will not escape from them. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down because of you."
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you will die.
If the officials hear that I talked with you, they may come and say to you, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide anything from us, or we will kill you.'
If they do, tell them, 'I was begging the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"
All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them exactly what the king had told him to say. So they said no more to him, because no one had overheard the conversation.
And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.
In the tenth month of the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his whole army and surrounded Jerusalem.
On the ninth day of the fourth month, in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the city wall was broken through.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came in and sat at the Middle Gate: Nergal Sharezer, Samgar Nebo, Sarsechim the chief official, Nergal Sharezer the chief adviser, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they ran away. They left the city at night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Jordan Valley.

But the Babylonian army chased them and caught up with Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and took him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where the king passed sentence on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons while Zedekiah watched. He also killed all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
The Babylonians burned down the king's palace and the people's houses, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took into exile in Babylon the people who were left in the city, along with those who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people.
But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left behind in the land of Judah some of the poorest people, who owned nothing. At that time he gave them vineyards and fields.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders about Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard:
"Take him and look after him. Do not harm him in any way. Do for him whatever he asks."
So Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, Nebushazban the chief official, Nergal Sharezer the chief adviser, and all the other officers of the king of Babylon
sent for Jeremiah and had him brought out of the courtyard of the guard. They put him in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him home. So Jeremiah stayed among the people.
While Jeremiah was still locked up in the courtyard of the guard, the LORD's message had come to him:

"Go and tell Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am going to carry out my words against this city, bringing disaster and not good. You will see it happen on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, says the LORD. You will not be handed over to the men you are afraid of.
I will certainly save you. You will not die by the sword. You will escape with your life, because you trusted in me, says the LORD.'"

This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, had set him free at Ramah. He had found Jeremiah bound in chains among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile to Babylon.
The commander of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said to him, "The LORD your God announced this disaster against this place.
Now the LORD has brought it about, just as he said he would. All this has happened because you people sinned against the LORD and did not obey him.

But today I am freeing you from the chains on your wrists. If you want to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if you do not want to come with me to Babylon, then do not come. Look, the whole land is in front of you. Go wherever you think is good and right."

Before Jeremiah turned to go, Nebuzaradan added, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has made governor over the towns of Judah. Live with him among the people. Or go anywhere else you think is right." Then the commander of the guard gave him food and a gift and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived with him among the people left in the land.

Some army officers and their men were still out in the countryside. They heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor of the land, and had put him in charge of the men, women, and children, the poorest people of the land, who had not been taken into exile to Babylon.

So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite, along with their men.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, made a promise to them and their men: "Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians. Settle down in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.

As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Babylonians who come to us. But you go ahead and harvest the wine, summer fruit, and olive oil. Store them in your jars and live in the towns you have taken over."

The Jews who were in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and all the other countries also heard that the king of Babylon had left some survivors in Judah and had made Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor over them.
So all these Jews came back to the land of Judah from all the places where they had been scattered. They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and harvested a great amount of wine and summer fruit.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers who had been out in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They said to him, "Don't you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah: "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he kill you? Then all the Jews who have gathered around you would be scattered, and the survivors of Judah would be lost."
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do such a thing! What you are saying about Ishmael is not true."

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. Ishmael was from the royal family and had been one of the king's chief officers. While they were eating a meal together at Mizpah,

Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him got up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword. They killed the man the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
The day after Gedaliah was murdered, before anyone knew about it,
eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They had shaved their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves. They were bringing grain offerings and incense to the LORD's temple.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he met them, he said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
But as soon as they were inside the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men with him killed them and threw their bodies into a well.
But ten of them said to Ishmael, "Don't kill us! We have wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey hidden in a field." So he left them alone and did not kill them with the others.

The well where Ishmael threw all the bodies of the men he had killed along with Gedaliah was the one King Asa had dug when he was afraid of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the dead.

Then Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people in Mizpah, including the king's daughters and everyone else left there, whom Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had put in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
When Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers with him heard about all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
they took all their men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They caught up with him near the great pool at Gibeon.
When all the people Ishmael had with him saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army officers with him, they were glad.
All the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and went over to Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan and fled to the Ammonites.

Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers with him took all the survivors from Mizpah whom he had rescued from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after Ishmael had murdered Gedaliah son of Ahikam. These were the soldiers, women, children, and court officials he had brought back from Gibeon.
They went on and stopped at Geruth Kimham near Bethlehem, on their way to Egypt.
They wanted to escape the Babylonians, because they were afraid of them. Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
Then all the army officers, including Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, came

to Jeremiah the prophet and said, "Please listen to our request and pray to the LORD your God for us, for all of us who are left. Once we were many, but now, as you can see, only a few of us are left.
Pray that the LORD your God will tell us where we should go and what we should do."
Jeremiah the prophet answered them, "I have heard you. I will pray to the LORD your God as you have asked. I will tell you everything the LORD answers. I will not hold anything back from you."
Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not do everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
Whether it is pleasant or unpleasant, we will obey the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you. Then things will go well for us, because we will obey the LORD our God."
Ten days later the LORD's message came to Jeremiah.
So he called together Johanan son of Kareah, all the army officers with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, the one you sent me to with your request:
'If you stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down. I will plant you and not pull you up, because I am sorry about the disaster I have brought on you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you fear now. Do not be afraid of him,' says the LORD, 'because I am with you to save you and rescue you from his power.
I will show you mercy, so that he will have mercy on you and let you go back to your own land.'
But suppose you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the LORD your God.
Suppose you say, 'No, we will go to Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the trumpet call to battle or go hungry. We will live there.'
Then listen to the LORD's message, you survivors of Judah. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'If you are determined to go to Egypt and live there,
then the war you fear will catch up with you there in Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow you there to Egypt, and you will die there.
All who are determined to go to Egypt to live there will die by war, famine, and disease. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I will bring on them.'

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Just as my anger and fury were poured out on the people of Jerusalem, so my fury will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become an object of cursing and horror, of mockery and disgrace. You will never see this place again.'
Survivors of Judah, the LORD has told you, 'Do not go to Egypt!' Be sure of this: I warn you today
that you have made a deadly mistake. You sent me to the LORD your God and said, 'Pray to the LORD our God for us. Tell us everything he says, and we will do it.'
Today I have told you, but you still have not obeyed the LORD your God in anything he sent me to tell you.
So now be sure of this: you will die by war, famine, and disease in the place where you want to go and live."
Jeremiah finished telling all the people everything the LORD their God had sent him to tell them.
Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to live there.'
Baruch son of Neriah is turning you against us, so that we will be handed over to the Babylonians. Then they can kill us or take us into exile in Babylon."
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the army officers, and all the people disobeyed the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah.
Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers took all the survivors of Judah who had come back to live in the land of Judah from all the nations where they had been scattered.

They took the men, women, and children, the king's daughters, and everyone Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan. They also took Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to Egypt, because they did not obey the LORD, and they arrived at Tahpanhes.
At Tahpanhes the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"While the people of Judah are watching, take some large stones and bury them in the clay of the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes.

Then tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I will send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will set his throne over these stones I have buried here, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
He will come and attack Egypt. Those meant for death will die. Those meant for captivity will be taken captive. Those meant for the sword will be killed by the sword.

I will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt. He will burn the temples and carry off their gods as captives. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there unharmed.
He will smash the sacred pillars at Beth Shemesh in Egypt and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt.'"
This message came to Jeremiah about all the Jews living in Egypt, in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the region of Pathros:
"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Today they are in ruins, and no one lives in them.
This happened because of the evil they did. They made me angry by burning incense and worshiping other gods that neither they nor you nor your ancestors had ever known.
Again and again I sent you my servants the prophets to say, 'Please do not do this disgusting thing that I hate!'
But they did not listen or pay attention. They did not turn from their wickedness or stop burning incense to other gods.
So my fury and anger were poured out. They burned like fire through the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and made them the ruined wasteland they are today."

"So now this is what the LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Why are you bringing such great disaster on yourselves? You are cutting off from Judah men and women, children and babies, so that no one will be left.

Why do you make me angry with the idols you make with your hands, burning incense to other gods here in Egypt where you have come to live? You will destroy yourselves and become a curse and a disgrace among all the nations of the earth.
Have you forgotten the wickedness done by your ancestors, by the kings of Judah and their wives, and by you and your wives, in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have not humbled themselves or shown respect. They have not followed my law or the rules I set before you and your ancestors."
"So this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Look, I have decided to bring disaster on you and to destroy all Judah.

I will take the survivors of Judah who were determined to go to Egypt and live there, and they will all die. They will fall in Egypt, killed by war and famine. From the least to the greatest, they will die by war and famine. They will become an object of cursing and horror, of mockery and disgrace.
I will punish those who live in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem, with war, famine, and disease.

None of the survivors of Judah who have gone to live in Egypt will escape or survive to go back to the land of Judah. They long to go back and live there, but no one will go back except a few who escape."
Then all the men who knew their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women standing there, a large crowd, and all the people living in Pathros in Egypt, answered Jeremiah,
"We will not listen to the message you have spoken to us in the LORD's name!

We will certainly do everything we have said we would. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our officials did in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. At that time we had plenty of food. We were well off and had no trouble.
But ever since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have had nothing, and we have been dying by war and famine."

And the women said, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes in her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands knowing and agreeing?"
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, both men and women, who had answered him,

"Do you think the LORD did not remember the incense you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, you and your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land? Do you think it did not come to his mind?

The LORD could not put up with it any longer, because of your evil actions and the disgusting things you did. That is why your land became a ruin, an object of horror and cursing, with no one living in it, as it is today.
This disaster has come on you, as you see today, because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD. You did not obey him or follow his law, his rules, and his instructions."
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women, "Listen to the LORD's message, all you people of Judah who are in Egypt.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have said with your mouths and shown with your actions, 'We will certainly keep the vows we made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.' Go ahead, then. Keep your promises and carry out your vows!

But listen to the LORD's message, all you people of Judah living in Egypt: 'I have sworn by my great name,' says the LORD, 'that no one from Judah living anywhere in Egypt will ever again use my name in an oath, saying, "As surely as the Lord GOD lives."
For I am watching over them to bring disaster, not good. All the people of Judah in Egypt will die by war and famine until they are all gone.
Only a few will escape the sword and come back from Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the survivors of Judah who came to live in Egypt will know whose word comes true, mine or theirs.
This will be the sign to you,' says the LORD, 'that I will punish you in this place, so that you will know my threats of disaster against you will certainly come true.'

This is what the LORD says: 'Look, I will hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to his enemy Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who wanted to kill him.'"
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, Baruch son of Neriah wrote on a scroll the words Jeremiah the prophet dictated. Then Jeremiah gave Baruch this message:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
You said, 'How terrible for me! The LORD has added sorrow to my pain. I am worn out from groaning, and I cannot find rest.'
Tell Baruch, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am about to tear down what I have built and pull up what I have planted, throughout the whole land.
