Are you looking for great things for yourself? Do not look for them. For I am going to bring disaster on all people, says the LORD. But wherever you go, I will let you escape with your life.'"
This is the LORD's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the nations.

About Egypt: This is about the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was at Carchemish by the Euphrates River. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated it in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
"Get your shields ready, large and small, and march out to battle!
Harness the horses! Mount up, you riders! Take your places with your helmets on! Sharpen your spears! Put on your armor!
But what do I see? They are terrified and running away. Their soldiers are defeated. They run in a hurry and do not look back. There is terror on every side," says the LORD.
"The fastest cannot run away, and the strongest cannot escape. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.
Who is this rising like the Nile, like rivers with surging waters?
Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers with surging waters. Egypt says, 'I will rise and cover the earth. I will destroy cities and the people in them.'
Charge, you horses! Race wildly, you chariots! Let the soldiers march out: men from Cush and Put who carry shields, and men from Lud who use the bow.

But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies. It is a day of revenge, when he will pay back his enemies. The sword will eat until it is full and drink their blood until it is satisfied. For the Lord GOD of Armies will offer a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get healing balm, young woman of Egypt. You try many medicines, but they do no good. There is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame. Your cries fill the earth. One soldier stumbles over another, and they both fall down together."
This is the message the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon coming to attack Egypt:
"Announce it in Egypt. Proclaim it in Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes: 'Take your positions and get ready, because the sword is devouring everything around you.'
Why have your strong soldiers been swept away? They cannot stand, because the LORD has pushed them down.
He makes many stumble. They fall over one another. They say, 'Get up! Let us go back to our own people, to the land where we were born, away from the cruel sword.'
There they shout, 'Pharaoh king of Egypt is nothing but noise. He has missed his chance.'
As surely as I live," says the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies, "someone is coming who is like Mount Tabor among the mountains, like Mount Carmel by the sea.
Pack your bags for exile, you people living in Egypt. For Memphis will become a ruin, burned down, with no one living there.
Egypt is a beautiful young cow, but a horsefly is coming from the north to attack her. It is coming.

Even the hired soldiers in her army are like fattened calves. They too will turn and run away together. They will not stand their ground, because the day of disaster is coming on them, the time for them to be punished.
Egypt will hiss like a snake slithering away as the enemy army marches in. They will come against her with axes, like men cutting down trees.
They will cut down her forest," says the LORD, "even though it is so thick no one can get through it. They are more numerous than locusts. No one can count them.
The people of Egypt will be put to shame. They will be handed over to the people of the north."
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I am going to punish Amon, the god of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and her kings, Pharaoh and all who trust in him.
I will hand them over to those who want to kill them, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But later Egypt will be lived in again, as in the past," says the LORD.

"But do not be afraid, Jacob my servant. Do not be discouraged, Israel. For look, I will rescue you from far away, and your descendants from the land where they are captives. Jacob will come back and have peace and quiet. No one will make him afraid.

Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant," says the LORD, "for I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will correct you fairly, but I will not let you go unpunished."
This is the LORD's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines, before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.

This is what the LORD says: "Look, waters are rising in the north. They will become a flooding river. They will flood the land and everything in it, the towns and the people who live there. People will cry out, and everyone living in the land will wail.
When they hear the pounding hooves of the warhorses, the rumbling of the chariots, and the noise of their wheels, fathers will not even turn back for their children. Their hands will hang limp,
because the day has come to destroy all the Philistines and to cut off every ally left to help Tyre and Sidon. The LORD is going to destroy the Philistines, the survivors from the island of Caphtor.
Gaza will shave its head in mourning. Ashkelon will be silenced. You survivors of their valley, how long will you cut yourselves in grief?
You cry, 'Oh, sword of the LORD, how long until you rest? Go back into your sheath. Rest and be still.'
But how can it rest when the LORD has given it orders? He has sent it against Ashkelon and the seacoast."

About Moab. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "How terrible for Nebo, because it will be destroyed! Kiriathaim will be put to shame and captured. The fortress will be put to shame and torn down.
No one will praise Moab anymore. In Heshbon people plot her downfall: 'Come, let us put an end to her as a nation.' You too, town of Madmen, will be silenced. The sword will chase you.
Listen to the cries from Horonaim: ruin and great destruction!
Moab is crushed. Her little ones cry out.
People climb the road up to Luhith, weeping bitterly as they go. On the road down to Horonaim they hear cries of anguish over the destruction.
Run! Save your lives! Be like a bush in the desert.
Because you trusted in what you made and in your riches, you too will be captured. Your god Chemosh will go into exile, along with his priests and officials.
The destroyer will come against every town, and not one town will escape. The valley will be ruined and the plain destroyed, as the LORD has said.
Give wings to Moab so she can fly away, because her towns will become ruins with no one living in them.
A curse on anyone who is lazy in doing the LORD's work! A curse on anyone who holds back their sword from bloodshed!

Moab has been at ease since its youth, like wine left to settle on its dregs. It has never been poured from one jar to another. It has never gone into exile. So its flavor has stayed the same, and its smell has not changed.
But look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will send people to pour it out. They will empty its jars and smash them to pieces.
Then Moab will be ashamed of its god Chemosh, just as the people of Israel were ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.
How can you say, 'We are warriors, strong men ready for battle'?
Moab will be destroyed, and its towns invaded. Its finest young men will go down to be slaughtered," says the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.
"Moab's disaster is close at hand. Its downfall is coming quickly.
Mourn for Moab, all you who live around it, all who know its fame. Say, 'How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff!'
Come down from your place of honor and sit on the dry ground, you people living in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come against you and torn down your fortresses.
You who live in Aroer, stand by the road and watch. Ask those who are running away, the man fleeing and the woman escaping, 'What has happened?'
Moab is put to shame, because it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Announce by the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.
Judgment has come on the plateau: on Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
on Dibon, Nebo, and Beth Diblathaim,
on Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul, and Beth Meon,
on Kerioth and Bozrah, and on all the towns of Moab, far and near.
Moab's strength is cut off. Its arm is broken," says the LORD.
"Make Moab drunk, because it has been arrogant toward the LORD. Let Moab roll around in its vomit and become a joke.
Didn't you make fun of Israel? Was Israel caught among thieves, that you shake your head in scorn every time you speak of them?
Leave your towns and live among the rocks, you people of Moab. Be like a dove that makes its nest at the mouth of a cave.
We have heard about Moab's pride. It is very proud, so high and mighty, so arrogant and full of itself.
I know how insolent it is," says the LORD, "but it means nothing. Its boasting accomplishes nothing.
So I will wail for Moab. I will cry out for all of Moab. I will mourn for the people of Kir Hareseth.

I will weep for you, vines of Sibmah, even more than the people of Jazer weep. Your branches reached as far as the sea. They reached the sea of Jazer. But the destroyer has attacked your summer fruit and your grape harvest.
Joy and gladness are gone from the fruitful fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the winepresses. No one stomps the grapes with shouts of joy. There are shouts, but not shouts of joy.
Their cries can be heard from Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath Shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim have dried up.
In Moab I will put an end," says the LORD, "to those who make offerings at the high places and burn incense to their gods.
So my heart moans for Moab like the sad music of a flute. My heart moans like a flute for the people of Kir Hareseth. The wealth they gained is gone.
Every head is shaved and every beard cut off. Every hand is gashed, and every waist is wrapped in sackcloth.
On all the roofs of Moab and in its streets there is nothing but mourning, because I have smashed Moab like a jar no one wants," says the LORD.
"How shattered it is! How they wail! How Moab turns its back in shame! Moab has become a joke and a horror to all its neighbors."
For this is what the LORD says: "Look, an enemy swoops down like an eagle, spreading its wings over Moab.
Kerioth will be captured, and its fortresses taken. On that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Moab will be destroyed as a nation, because it was arrogant toward the LORD.
Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you, people of Moab," says the LORD.
"Whoever runs from the terror will fall into a pit. Whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in a trap. For I will bring on Moab the year of its punishment," says the LORD.

"In the shadow of Heshbon, those running away stand without strength. For a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from the house of Sihon. It burns the foreheads of Moab, the skulls of those noisy boasters.
How terrible for you, Moab! The people of Chemosh are destroyed. Your sons are taken into exile, and your daughters into captivity.
But in the days to come I will bring Moab back from captivity," says the LORD. This is the end of the judgment on Moab.
About the Ammonites. This is what the LORD says: "Does Israel have no sons? Does it have no heir? Then why has Molech taken over the land of Gad, and why do his people live in its towns?

So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a heap of ruins, and its surrounding villages will be burned down. Then Israel will drive out those who drove them out," says the LORD.

"Wail, Heshbon, because Ai is destroyed! Cry out, you people of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn. Run here and there inside the walls, because Molech will go into exile, along with his priests and officials.
Why do you boast about your valleys, your fruitful valleys, you unfaithful daughter? You trusted in your riches and said, 'Who would dare attack me?'
Look, I will bring terror on you from everyone around you," says the Lord GOD of Armies. "Each of you will be driven away, and no one will gather those who run away.
But later I will bring the Ammonites back from captivity," says the LORD.
About Edom. This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Is there no more wisdom in Teman? Have the wise run out of good advice? Has their wisdom disappeared?
Turn and run! Hide in deep caves, you people of Dedan! For I will bring disaster on Esau's descendants when I come to punish them.
If grape pickers came to you, wouldn't they leave a few grapes behind? If thieves came at night, wouldn't they steal only as much as they wanted?
But I will strip Esau's descendants bare. I will uncover their hiding places, and they will not be able to hide. Their children, relatives, and neighbors will be destroyed, and they will be no more.
Leave your orphans behind, and I will keep them alive. Your widows can trust in me."
This is what the LORD says: "If those who did not deserve to drink from the cup of punishment must drink it, why should you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished. You must drink it.
For I have sworn by myself," says the LORD, "that Bozrah will become an object of horror, disgrace, ruin, and cursing. All its towns will be ruins forever."
I have heard a message from the LORD. A messenger has been sent to the nations to say: "Gather together and attack her! Get ready for battle!"
"Look, I will make you small among the nations, looked down on by everyone.

The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have fooled you. You live in the clefts of the rocks and hold the high places of the hills. But even if you build your nest as high as an eagle's, I will bring you down from there," says the LORD.
"Edom will become an object of horror. Everyone who passes by will be shocked and will gasp at all its wounds.
Like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring towns when they were destroyed," says the LORD, "no one will live there. No human being will stay there.

Look, like a lion coming up from the thick bushes along the Jordan to a rich pasture, I will suddenly chase Edom from its land. I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me?"
So listen to the plan the LORD has made against Edom, and what he intends to do to the people of Teman: Even the youngest of the flock will be dragged away. He will completely destroy their pasture.
At the sound of their fall the earth will shake. Their cries will be heard as far as the Red Sea.
Look, an enemy will rise up and swoop down like an eagle, spreading its wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
About Damascus. "Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, because they have heard bad news. They melt with fear, troubled like the restless sea that cannot be calm.
Damascus has become weak. She turns to run away, and panic grips her. Pain and suffering have seized her like a woman in labor.
How sad that the famous city has not been abandoned, the town that gave me joy!
So her young men will fall in her streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day," says the LORD of Armies.
"I will set fire to the walls of Damascus, and it will burn down the palaces of Ben-Hadad."
About Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked. This is what the LORD says: "Get up and attack Kedar! Destroy the people of the east!
Their tents and flocks will be taken. Their tent curtains, all their goods, and their camels will be carried off. People will shout to them, 'Terror on every side!'
Run away! Escape far away! Hide in deep caves, you people of Hazor," says the LORD. "For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you. He has decided to attack you.
Get up and attack a nation that is at ease and feels secure," says the LORD. "It has no gates or bars. Its people live alone.

Their camels will be taken as loot, and their many cattle as plunder. I will scatter to every wind those who cut the corners of their hair, and I will bring disaster on them from every side," says the LORD.
"Hazor will become a home for jackals, a ruin forever. No one will live there. No human being will stay there."
This is the LORD's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about Elam, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
"This is what the LORD of Armies says: Look, I will break the bow of Elam, the source of their strength.
I will bring the four winds from the four corners of the sky against Elam. I will scatter its people to all these winds. There will not be a nation where Elam's exiles do not go.

I will make Elam terrified before their enemies, before those who want to kill them. I will bring disaster on them, my fierce anger," says the LORD. "I will chase them with the sword until I have destroyed them.
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy its king and officials," says the LORD.
"But in the days to come I will bring Elam back from captivity," says the LORD.
This is the message the LORD spoke through Jeremiah the prophet about Babylon and the land of the Babylonians.

"Announce it among the nations and proclaim it. Raise a flag and proclaim it. Do not hide anything. Say, 'Babylon has been captured! Bel is put to shame. Marduk is terrified. Her images are put to shame, and her idols are terrified.'
For a nation from the north will attack her and turn her land into a wasteland. No one will live in it. Both people and animals will run away.
In those days and at that time," says the LORD, "the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together. They will come weeping as they look for the LORD their God.
They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will say, 'Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in a covenant that will last forever and never be forgotten.'
My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and made them wander on the mountains. They roamed from mountain to hill and forgot their own resting place.
Everyone who found them devoured them. Their enemies said, 'We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, their true home of righteousness, the LORD, the hope of their ancestors.'
Run away from Babylon! Leave the land of the Babylonians! Be like the goats that lead the flock.

For look, I am stirring up a group of great nations from the land of the north to attack Babylon. They will line up for battle against her and capture her. Their arrows are like skilled warriors who never come back empty-handed.
Babylon will be robbed, and all who rob her will have plenty," says the LORD.
"You people of Babylon are glad and celebrate, you who robbed my people. You frolic like a young cow in the grain, and you neigh like strong horses.
But your mother city will be deeply ashamed. She who gave you birth will be disgraced. She will become the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, a desert.
Because of the LORD's anger, no one will live there. She will be completely deserted. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be shocked and will gasp at all her wounds.
Line up for battle all around Babylon, all you archers. Shoot at her! Do not hold back your arrows, because she has sinned against the LORD.
Shout the battle cry against her from every side! She surrenders. Her towers fall. Her walls are torn down. This is the LORD's revenge. Take revenge on her! Do to her what she has done to others.
Cut off from Babylon those who plant the seed and those who swing the sickle at harvest time. Because of the cruel sword, everyone will go back to their own people and run to their own land.
Israel is like scattered sheep chased by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured them. Last of all, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon crushed their bones."
So this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to its own pasture. They will graze on Carmel and Bashan. They will eat their fill on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

In those days and at that time," says the LORD, "people will search for Israel's guilt, but there will be none. They will look for Judah's sins, but none will be found, because I will forgive the survivors I leave behind.
Attack the land of Merathaim and the people living in Pekod. Kill them and completely destroy them," says the LORD. "Do everything I have commanded you.
The noise of battle fills the land, the noise of great destruction.
How broken and shattered is the hammer of the whole earth! How Babylon has become a ruin among the nations!
I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and captured, because you fought against the LORD.
The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his anger. For the Lord GOD of Armies has work to do in the land of the Babylonians.
Come against her from far away. Break open her storehouses. Pile her up like heaps of grain. Destroy her completely. Leave nothing of her.
Kill all her young bulls. Let them go down to the slaughter. How terrible for them! Their day has come, the time for them to be punished.
Listen to those who run away and escape from the land of Babylon. They come to announce in Zion how the LORD our God has taken revenge, revenge for his temple.

Call together the archers against Babylon, all who use the bow. Camp all around her. Let no one escape. Pay her back for what she has done. Do to her as she has done to others. For she was arrogant toward the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
So her young men will fall in her streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day," says the LORD.
"Look, I am against you, you proud one," says the Lord GOD of Armies. "Your day has come, the time for me to punish you.
The proud one will stumble and fall, and no one will help him up. I will set fire to his towns, and it will burn up everything around him."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah too. All their captors hold them tightly and refuse to let them go.
But their Redeemer is strong. The LORD of Armies is his name. He will strongly defend their case so that he can bring rest to the earth and unrest to the people of Babylon.
A sword against the Babylonians!" says the LORD. "A sword against the people of Babylon, against her officials and her wise men!
A sword against her false prophets, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be terrified!
A sword against her horses and chariots, and against all the foreign soldiers among her, and they will become as weak as women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be looted!
A drought on her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of idols, and the people are crazy about their idols.
So desert creatures and hyenas will live there, and ostriches will live there too. No one will ever live there again. No one will settle there for all generations.
As when God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring towns," says the LORD, "no one will live there. No human being will stay there.
Look, an army is coming from the north. A great nation and many kings are being stirred up from the far ends of the earth.

They are armed with bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy. They sound like the roaring sea as they ride on their horses. They come lined up like soldiers for battle to attack you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard reports about them, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like a woman in labor.

Look, like a lion coming up from the thick bushes along the Jordan to a rich pasture, I will suddenly chase Babylon from its land. I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me?"

So listen to the plan the LORD has made against Babylon, and what he intends to do to the land of the Babylonians: Even the youngest of the flock will be dragged away. He will completely destroy their pasture.
At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will shake. Its cry will be heard among the nations.
This is what the LORD says: "Look, I am going to stir up a destroying wind against Babylon and against the people of Leb Kamai.
I will send foreigners to Babylon to scatter her like chaff in the wind. They will strip her land bare. They will attack her from every side on her day of disaster.
Do not let her archers string their bows or put on their armor. Do not spare her young men. Completely destroy her army.
They will fall dead in the land of the Babylonians, stabbed through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Armies, even though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.
Run away from Babylon! Run for your lives! Do not be destroyed because of her sins. It is time for the LORD's revenge. He will pay her back for what she has done.
Babylon was a gold cup in the LORD's hand. She made the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine, and so they have gone mad.
Babylon has suddenly fallen and been shattered. Wail for her! Get healing balm for her pain. Maybe she can be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Let us leave her and each go back to our own land. For her judgment reaches up to the heavens. It rises as high as the clouds.
The LORD has shown that we are in the right. Come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.
Sharpen the arrows! Pick up the shields! The LORD has stirred up the kings of the Medes, because he plans to destroy Babylon. This is the LORD's revenge, revenge for his temple.

Raise a flag against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the guard! Post the watchmen! Set up an ambush! For the LORD will do what he planned. He will carry out what he said he would do to the people of Babylon.
You who live beside many waters and are rich with treasures, your end has come. Your life is cut off like a thread.
The LORD of Armies has sworn by himself: 'I will surely fill you with soldiers like a swarm of locusts, and they will shout in victory over you.'
God made the earth by his power. He set the world in place by his wisdom. By his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
When he speaks, the waters in the heavens roar. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Everyone is foolish and without knowledge. Every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. His metal images are a lie. There is no breath in them.
They are worthless, objects of mockery. When the time comes to punish them, they will be destroyed.
But God, who is Jacob's portion, is not like them. He made everything, including Israel, the people who belong to him. The LORD of Armies is his name.
You are my war club, my weapon for battle. With you I smash nations. With you I destroy kingdoms.
With you I smash the horse and its rider.
With you I smash the chariot and its driver. With you I smash men and women. With you I smash the old and the young. With you I smash young men and young women.
With you I smash the shepherd and his flock. With you I smash the farmer and his oxen. With you I smash governors and officials.
Before your eyes I will pay back Babylon and all who live in Babylonia for all the evil they have done in Zion," says the LORD.

"Look, I am against you, you destroying mountain, you who destroy the whole earth," says the LORD. "I will stretch out my hand against you. I will roll you off the cliffs and make you a burned-out mountain.
No one will take even a stone from you for a cornerstone or a foundation. You will be a ruin forever," says the LORD.

"Raise a flag in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Get the nations ready to fight against her. Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz to attack her. Appoint a commander against her. Send the horses like a swarm of locusts.
Get the nations ready to fight against her: the kings of the Medes, their governors and officials, and all the lands they rule.
The land shakes and twists in pain, because the LORD's plans against Babylon stand firm. He will make the land of Babylon a ruin where no one lives.
Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting. They stay in their fortresses. Their strength is gone. They have become as weak as women. Her homes are set on fire. The bars of her gates are broken.
One runner after another, one messenger after another, comes to tell the king of Babylon that his whole city has been captured.
The river crossings have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. Soon the time of harvest will come for her."
"Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us and crushed us. He has emptied us like a jar. Like a monster he has swallowed us. He has filled his stomach with our best things, and then spit us out.
May Babylon pay for the violence done to us and to our families," say the people of Zion. "May the people of Babylonia pay for the blood they shed," says Jerusalem.
So this is what the LORD says: "Look, I will defend your case and take revenge for you. I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry.
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a home for jackals, an object of horror and mockery, a place where no one lives.
Her people will roar together like young lions. They will growl like lion cubs.
While they are excited, I will set out a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they shout with laughter. Then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up," says the LORD.
"I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats.
How Sheshach has been captured, the pride of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a ruin among the nations!
The sea has risen over Babylon. Its roaring waves have covered her.
Her towns have become ruins, a dry land and a desert, a land where no one lives and no one travels through.
I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him. Even the wall of Babylon will fall.
Come out of her, my people! Run for your lives! Run from the LORD's fierce anger.
Do not lose heart or be afraid when you hear rumors in the land. One rumor comes this year, another the next. There will be rumors of violence in the land, of one ruler fighting another.
For look, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her dead will lie in the middle of her.
Then heaven and earth and everything in them will shout for joy over Babylon, because destroyers will attack her from the north," says the LORD.
"Babylon must fall because of the people of Israel she killed, just as the dead all over the earth fell because of Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go! Do not wait! Remember the LORD in a faraway land, and think about Jerusalem."
"We are ashamed because we have been insulted. Our faces are covered with disgrace, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD's temple."
"So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will punish her idols. Throughout her land the wounded will groan.
Even if Babylon climbs up to the heavens and builds her fortress high and strong, I will still send destroyers against her," says the LORD.
"Listen! A cry comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Babylonians.
For the LORD is destroying Babylon and silencing her loud noise. The enemy comes like roaring waves, like crashing waters. Their battle cry rings out.
The destroyer has come against Babylon. Her warriors are captured, and their bows are broken. For the LORD is a God who pays people back. He will pay back in full.
I will make her officials and wise men, her governors, officials, and warriors drunk. They will fall asleep forever and never wake up," says the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down, and her high gates will be burned. The nations wear themselves out for nothing. Their hard work only feeds the fire."

This is the message Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when Seraiah went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the officer in charge of the king's travel arrangements.
Jeremiah had written on a scroll all the disasters that would come on Babylon, all these words written about Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, make sure you read all these words out loud.
Then say, 'LORD, you have said you will destroy this place so that no one will live in it, neither people nor animals. It will be a ruin forever.'
When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates River.
Then say, 'In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I will bring on her. Her people will wear themselves out.'" This is the end of Jeremiah's words.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, just as Jehoiakim had done.
It was because of the LORD's anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until he finally removed them from his presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

So on the tenth day of the tenth month of Zedekiah's ninth year as king, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped outside the city and built siege works all around it.
The city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city was so bad that there was no food for the people.

Then the city wall was broken through, and all the soldiers ran away. They left the city at night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, even though the Babylonians surrounded the city. They headed toward the Jordan Valley,
but the Babylonian army chased the king and caught up with Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. His whole army had deserted him.
They captured the king and took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he passed sentence on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons while Zedekiah watched. He also killed all the officials of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him in bronze chains, and took him to Babylon. He kept him in prison until the day he died.
On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He set fire to the LORD's temple, the king's palace, and all the houses in Jerusalem. Every important building he burned down.
The whole Babylonian army under the commander of the guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took into exile some of the poorest people, the rest of the people left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.
But Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, left behind some of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and fields.
The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands, and the large bronze basin called the Sea that were in the LORD's temple. They carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the bronze objects used in the temple service.
The commander of the guard took away the basins, fire pans, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes, and bowls used for drink offerings, everything made of pure gold or silver.
The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands, which King Solomon had made for the LORD's temple, was too heavy to weigh.
Each pillar was twenty-seven feet tall and eighteen feet around. Each was hollow, and its metal was four fingers thick.
On top of each pillar was a bronze capital seven and a half feet high, decorated all around with a network of bronze pomegranates. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was just like the first.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides. In all, there were one hundred pomegranates above the network around the capital.
The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank, and the three doorkeepers.

From the city he also took the officer in charge of the soldiers, seven of the king's advisers who were found in the city, the secretary of the army commander who called up the people of the land for the army, and sixty of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon had them executed. So the people of Judah were taken into exile, away from their land.
This is the number of people Nebuchadnezzar took into exile: in his seventh year, three thousand twenty-three Jews;
in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year, eight hundred thirty-two people from Jerusalem;
in Nebuchadnezzar's twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took seven hundred forty-five Jews into exile. In all, four thousand six hundred people were taken.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evil-Merodach became king of Babylon. In the first year of his reign he showed kindness to Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison.
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he ate regularly at the king's table.
Every day the king of Babylon gave him an allowance, as long as he lived, until the day he died.
Lam: How lonely the city sits, the city once so full of people! She who was great among the nations has become like a widow. She who was a princess among the provinces has become a slave.
She weeps bitterly at night, with tears on her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her. They have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile after suffering and hard slavery. She lives among the nations but finds no rest. All who chased her caught her in her distress.
The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the festivals. All her gates are deserted. Her priests groan. Her young women grieve, and she herself is in bitter pain.
Her enemies have become her masters. Her enemies are doing well, because the LORD has made her suffer for her many sins. Her children have been taken captive by the enemy.
All the splendor has left the daughter of Zion. Her leaders have become like deer that find no pasture. They have run away without strength in front of the hunter.

In the days of her suffering and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the treasures she had in days gone by. When her people fell into enemy hands, no one helped her. Her enemies looked at her and laughed at her ruin.
Jerusalem has sinned terribly, so she has become unclean. All who once honored her now look down on her, because they have seen her naked. She herself groans and turns away.
Her filth clung to her skirts. She did not think about her future. Her fall was shocking, and no one is there to comfort her. "LORD, look at my suffering, for the enemy has won!"
The enemy has laid his hands on all her treasures. She watched as the nations entered her holy place, the very people you commanded not to enter your assembly.
All her people groan as they search for bread. They trade their treasures for food to stay alive. "LORD, look and see how I am despised."
"Does this mean nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look and see if there is any pain like the pain brought on me, which the LORD made me suffer on the day of his fierce anger.
From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it overpowered them. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He has left me ruined and faint all day long.
My sins have been tied into a yoke by his hand. They are woven together and put on my neck. He has taken away my strength. The Lord has handed me over to those I cannot fight.
The Lord has rejected all the warriors among me. He has called an army against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trampled young Judah as grapes are trampled in a winepress.
This is why I weep. My eyes overflow with tears, because the one who could comfort me and give me strength is far away. My children are ruined, because the enemy has won."
Zion reaches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has ordered that Jacob's neighbors become his enemies. Jerusalem has become something unclean among them.
"The LORD is right, because I rebelled against his command. Listen, all you peoples, and look at my pain. My young women and young men have gone into exile.
I called to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and elders died in the city while searching for food to stay alive.
LORD, look how distressed I am! My stomach is in knots. My heart is broken inside me, because I have been so rebellious. Out in the street the sword kills. Inside the house there is only death.

People have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard about my trouble, and they are glad that you have done this. Bring the day you have announced, so that they will become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before you. Deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my sins. For my groans are many, and my heart is weak."

How the Lord in his anger has covered the daughter of Zion with a dark cloud! He has thrown the glory of Israel down from heaven to earth. In the day of his anger he did not remember his footstool, his temple.

Without pity the Lord has swallowed up all the homes of Jacob. In his fury he has torn down the fortresses of the daughter of Judah. He has brought them crashing to the ground. He has dishonored the kingdom and its leaders.

In fierce anger he has cut off all of Israel's strength. He has pulled back his protecting right hand as the enemy came. He has burned against Jacob like a blazing fire that consumes everything around it.

He has drawn his bow like an enemy. His right hand is raised like a foe's. He has killed everyone who was precious to look at. He has poured out his fury like fire on the tent of the daughter of Zion.

The Lord has become like an enemy. He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her fortresses. He has made mourning and crying grow and grow in the daughter of Judah.

He has torn down his temple as easily as a garden shelter. He has destroyed his meeting place. The LORD has made Zion forget her festivals and Sabbaths. In his fierce anger he has rejected both king and priest.
The Lord has rejected his altar and abandoned his holy place. He has handed the walls of her palaces over to the enemy. They shouted in the LORD's temple as if it were a festival day.
The LORD decided to tear down the wall of the daughter of Zion. He measured it out and did not hold back his hand from destroying it. He made the walls and ramparts mourn. Together they crumble away.
Her gates have sunk into the ground. He has broken and destroyed their bars. Her king and leaders are exiled among the nations. The law is no more, and her prophets receive no vision from the LORD.
The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem bow their heads to the ground.
My eyes are worn out from weeping. My stomach is in knots. My heart is poured out on the ground because my people are destroyed, because children and babies are fainting in the streets of the city.
They cry to their mothers, "Where is the bread and wine?" as they faint like wounded soldiers in the city streets, as their lives slip away in their mothers' arms.

What can I say for you? What can I compare you to, daughter of Jerusalem? What can I liken you to, so that I can comfort you, young daughter of Zion? Your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can heal you?
Your prophets saw visions for you that were false and worthless. They did not expose your sin to save you from captivity. Instead they gave you false and misleading messages.
All who pass by clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called 'the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth'?"
All your enemies open their mouths wide against you. They hiss and grind their teeth and say, "We have swallowed her up! This is the day we have waited for. We have lived to see it!"
The LORD has done what he planned. He has carried out the warning he gave long ago. He has torn you down without pity. He has let the enemy gloat over you and made your foes strong.
The people's hearts cry out to the Lord. Wall of the daughter of Zion, let your tears flow like a river day and night. Give yourself no rest. Do not let your eyes stop weeping.

Get up and cry out in the night, at the start of every night watch. Pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the lives of your children, who are fainting from hunger at the corner of every street.
"LORD, look and see! Who have you ever treated like this? Should women eat their own children, the babies they have cared for? Should priests and prophets be killed in the Lord's holy place?
Young and old lie together in the dust of the streets. My young women and young men have been killed by the sword. You killed them in the day of your anger. You slaughtered them without pity.

As if calling people to a festival, you called terrors against me from every side. On the day of the LORD's anger, no one escaped or survived. My enemy has destroyed the children I cared for and raised."
I am the man who has seen suffering under the rod of God's anger.
He has led me and made me walk in darkness instead of light.
Again and again, all day long, he has turned his hand against me.
He has made my flesh and skin waste away. He has broken my bones.
He has surrounded me with bitterness and hardship, like a city under attack.
He has made me live in darkness, like those who have been dead a long time.
He has walled me in so I cannot get out. He has weighed me down with heavy chains.
Even when I cry out and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has blocked my way with walls of cut stone. He has made my paths crooked.
He is like a bear waiting to attack me, like a lion in hiding.
He dragged me off the path and tore me to pieces. He has left me helpless.
He drew his bow and made me the target for his arrows.
He shot his arrows deep into my heart.
All my people laugh at me. They make fun of me in their songs all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness and made me drink bitter poison.
He has broken my teeth with gravel and trampled me in the dust.
Peace has been taken from me. I have forgotten what it is like to be happy.
So I said, "My strength is gone, and so is my hope in the LORD."
Remember my suffering and my wandering, the bitterness and the poison.
I remember them all the time, and my spirit sinks within me.
Yet this I call to mind, and so I have hope:
Because of the LORD's faithful love we are not destroyed, for his compassion never fails.
It is new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
I say to myself, "The LORD is all I have, so I will put my hope in him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to anyone who seeks him.
It is good to wait quietly and hope for the LORD to save us.
It is good for a person to carry the yoke while they are young.
Let them sit alone in silence, because the LORD has put it on them.
Let them bow their face to the dust. There may still be hope.
Let them offer their cheek to the one who hits them, and let them be filled with disgrace.
For the Lord will not reject us forever.
Even though he brings grief, he will show compassion, because his faithful love is so great.
For he does not like to bring suffering or grief to anyone.
Crushing all the prisoners of the earth under foot,
denying people their rights in front of the Most High,
or cheating someone in court: the Lord does not approve of these things.
Who can speak and make something happen unless the Lord has commanded it?
Don't both disaster and good things come from the mouth of the Most High?
Why should any living person complain when they are punished for their sins?
Let us examine our ways and test them, and let us return to the LORD.
Let us lift up our hearts and our hands to God in heaven and say:
"We have sinned and rebelled, and you have not forgiven.
You have covered yourself with anger and chased us. You have killed without pity.
You have covered yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can get through.
You have made us like trash and garbage among the nations.
All our enemies open their mouths wide against us.
Terror and traps have come on us, ruin and destruction."
Streams of tears flow from my eyes because my people are destroyed.
My eyes will keep pouring out tears without stopping, without rest,
until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
What I see brings me grief because of all the women of my city.
Those who were my enemies for no reason hunted me down like a bird.
They tried to end my life in a pit and threw stones at me.
Water flowed over my head, and I said, "This is the end."
I called on your name, LORD, from the bottom of the pit.
You heard my plea: "Do not close your ears to my cry for help and relief."
You came near when I called you. You said, "Do not be afraid."
Lord, you took up my case. You rescued my life.
LORD, you have seen the wrong done to me. Judge my case.
You have seen all their revenge, all their plots against me.
LORD, you have heard their insults, all their plots against me,
what my enemies whisper and say against me all day long.
Look at them! Whether they sit or stand, they make fun of me in their songs.
Pay them back, LORD, for what they have done.
Make them stubborn, and put your curse on them.
Chase them in your anger and destroy them from under the LORD's heavens.
How the gold has lost its shine! How the pure gold has changed! The sacred stones lie scattered at the corner of every street.
The precious people of Zion were once worth their weight in fine gold. Now they are treated like clay pots made by a potter's hands.
Even jackals nurse their young, but my people have become cruel, like ostriches in the desert.
The nursing baby's tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth from thirst. Children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.
Those who once ate fine food now starve in the streets. Those who were raised wearing royal purple now lie on garbage heaps.
The punishment of my people is greater than the punishment of Sodom, which was destroyed in a moment without anyone lifting a hand against it.
Her princes were brighter than snow and whiter than milk. Their bodies were more glowing than rubies, their appearance like sapphire.
But now they are blacker than soot. No one recognizes them in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones. It has become as dry as wood.
Those killed by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger. The hungry waste away, struck down by the lack of food from the fields.
With their own hands, loving mothers have cooked their own children. Their children became their food when my people were destroyed.
The LORD has unleashed all his anger. He has poured out his fierce anger. He has lit a fire in Zion that burned down its foundations.
The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did anyone in the world, that enemies and foes could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
But it happened because of the sins of her prophets and the wrongs of her priests, who spilled the blood of innocent people inside the city.
Now they wander through the streets like blind men. They are so stained with blood that no one dares to touch their clothes.
People shout at them, "Go away! You are unclean! Go away! Go away! Do not touch us!" So they ran away and wandered. Among the nations people said, "They cannot stay here any longer."
The LORD himself has scattered them. He no longer watches over them. No one respects the priests or shows kindness to the elders.
Our eyes are worn out from looking for help that never came. From our watchtowers we watched for a nation that could not save us.
Our enemies tracked our steps, so we could not walk in our streets. Our end was near. Our days were over. Our end had come.
Those who chased us were faster than eagles in the sky. They hunted us on the mountains and set ambushes for us in the desert.
The LORD's anointed king, the very breath of our life, was caught in their traps. We had thought that under his protection we would live among the nations.
Celebrate and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who live in the land of Uz. But the cup of punishment will come to you too. You will get drunk and strip yourself naked.
Your punishment is complete, daughter of Zion. He will not keep you in exile any longer. But he will punish your sin, daughter of Edom. He will expose your sins.
LORD, remember what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace.
Our land has been handed over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We have become orphans without fathers. Our mothers are like widows.
We have to pay for the water we drink. We have to buy our own firewood.
Our enemies are right on our heels. We are worn out and have no rest.
We made deals with Egypt and Assyria to get enough bread to eat.
Our ancestors sinned and are gone, and we are paying for their sins.
Slaves rule over us, and no one can rescue us from their power.
We risk our lives to get bread, because of the sword in the desert.
Our skin is as hot as an oven from the fever of hunger.
Women were raped in Zion, young women in the towns of Judah.
Leaders were hung up by their hands. Elders were shown no respect.
Young men are forced to grind grain at the mill. Boys stagger under loads of wood.
The elders no longer sit at the city gate. The young men have stopped their music.
The joy has gone from our hearts. Our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. How terrible for us, because we have sinned!
Because of this our hearts are sick. Because of these things our eyes grow dim,
because Mount Zion lies empty, and jackals roam over it.
But you, LORD, rule forever. Your throne lasts from generation to generation.
Why do you keep forgetting us? Why have you abandoned us for so long?
Bring us back to you, LORD, so that we can return. Make our lives new again, as they were long ago.
Unless you have completely rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.
Ezek: Now in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
In the fifth of the month, which was the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s captivity,
the LORD’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the LORD’s hand was there on him.

I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came out of the north: a great cloud, with flashing lightning, and a brightness around it, and out of the middle of it as it were glowing metal, out of the middle of the fire.
Out of its center came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: They had the likeness of a man.
Everyone had four faces, and each one of them had four wings.
Their feet were straight feet. The sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot; and they sparkled like burnished bronze.
They had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides. The four of them had their faces and their wings like this:
Their wings were joined to one another. They didn’t turn when they went. Each one went straight forward.

As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man. The four of them had the face of a lion on the right side. The four of them had the face of an ox on the left side. The four of them also had the face of an eagle.
Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above. Two wings of each one touched another, and two covered their bodies.
Each one went straight forward. Where the spirit was to go, they went. They didn’t turn when they went.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. The fire went up and down among the living creatures. The fire was bright, and lightning went out of the fire.
The living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.
Now as I saw the living creatures, behold, there was one wheel on the earth beside the living creatures, for each of the four faces of it.
The appearance of the wheels and their work was like a beryl. The four of them had one likeness. Their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel within a wheel.
When they went, they went in their four directions. They didn’t turn when they went.
As for their rims, they were high and dreadful; and the four of them had their rims full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them. When the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
Wherever the spirit was to go, they went. The spirit was to go there. The wheels were lifted up beside them; for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
When those went, these went. When those stood, these stood. When those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up beside them; for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
Over the head of the living creature there was the likeness of an expanse, like an awesome crystal to look at, stretched out over their heads above.
Under the expanse, their wings were straight, one toward the other. Each one had two which covered on this side, and each one had two which covered their bodies on that side.

When they went, I heard the noise of their wings like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a noise of tumult like the noise of an army. When they stood, they let down their wings.
There was a voice above the expanse that was over their heads. When they stood, they let down their wings.
Above the expanse that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone. On the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man on it above.

I saw as it were glowing metal, as the appearance of fire within it all around, from the appearance of his waist and upward; and from the appearance of his waist and downward I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him.

As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the LORD’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke.
He said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you.”
The Spirit entered into me when he spoke to me, and set me on my feet; and I heard him who spoke to me.
He said to me, “Son of man, I send you to the children of Israel, to a nation of rebels who have rebelled against me. They and their fathers have transgressed against me even to this very day.
The children are impudent and stiff-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’
They, whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that there has been a prophet among them.

You, son of man, don’t be afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you, and you dwell among scorpions. Don’t be afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.
You shall speak my words to them, whether they will hear or whether they will refuse; for they are most rebellious.
But you, son of man, hear what I tell you. Don’t be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth, and eat that which I give you.”
When I looked, behold, a hand was stretched out to me; and behold, a scroll of a book was in it.
He spread it before me. It was written within and without; and lamentations, mourning, and woe were written in it.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel.”
So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat the scroll.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll that I give you and fill your belly and your bowels with it.” Then I ate it. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
He said to me, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel, and speak my words to them.
For you are not sent to a people of a strange speech and of a hard language, but to the house of Israel—
not to many peoples of a strange speech and of a hard language, whose words you can’t understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel will not listen to you, for they will not listen to me; for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted.
Behold, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads.
I have made your forehead as a diamond, harder than flint. Don’t be afraid of them, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.”
Moreover he said to me, “Son of man, receive in your heart and hear with your ears all my words that I speak to you.
Go to them of the captivity, to the children of your people, and speak to them, and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse.”
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing, saying, “Blessed be the LORD’s glory from his place.”
I heard the noise of the wings of the living creatures as they touched one another, and the noise of the wheels beside them, even the noise of a great rushing.
So the Spirit lifted me up, and took me away; and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit; and the LORD’s hand was strong on me.
Then I came to them of the captivity at Tel Aviv who lived by the river Chebar, and to where they lived; and I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days.
At the end of seven days, the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel. Therefore hear the word from my mouth, and warn them from me.

When I tell the wicked, ‘You will surely die;’ and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity; but I will require his blood at your hand.
Yet if you warn the wicked, and he doesn’t turn from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.”

“Again, when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you have not given him warning, he will die in his sin, and his righteous deeds which he has done will not be remembered; but I will require his blood at your hand.
Nevertheless if you warn the righteous man, that the righteous not sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live, because he took warning; and you have delivered your soul.”
The LORD’s hand was there on me; and he said to me, “Arise, go out into the plain, and I will talk with you there.”
Then I arose, and went out into the plain, and behold, the LORD’s glory stood there, like the glory which I saw by the river Chebar. Then I fell on my face.
Then the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me, and said to me, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
But you, son of man, behold, they will put ropes on you, and will bind you with them, and you will not go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you will be mute and will not be able to correct them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house.”
“You also, son of man, take a tile, and lay it before yourself, and portray on it a city, even Jerusalem.
Lay siege against it, build forts against it, and cast up a mound against it. Also set camps against it and plant battering rams against it all around.

Take for yourself an iron pan and set it for a wall of iron between you and the city. Then set your face toward it. It will be besieged, and you shall lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
“Moreover lie on your left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel on it. According to the number of the days that you shall lie on it, you shall bear their iniquity.
For I have appointed the years of their iniquity to be to you a number of days, even three hundred ninety days. So you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
“Again, when you have accomplished these, you shall lie on your right side, and shall bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. I have appointed forty days, each day for a year, to you.
You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm uncovered; and you shall prophesy against it.
Behold, I put ropes on you, and you shall not turn yourself from one side to the other, until you have accomplished the days of your siege.

“Take for yourself also wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and put them in one vessel. Make bread of it. According to the number of the days that you will lie on your side, even three hundred ninety days, you shall eat of it.
Your food which you shall eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day. From time to time you shall eat it.
You shall drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin. From time to time you shall drink.
You shall eat it as barley cakes, and you shall bake it in their sight with dung that comes out of man.”
The LORD said, “Even thus will the children of Israel eat their bread unclean, among the nations where I will drive them.”

Then I said, “Ah Lord GOD! Behold, my soul has not been polluted; for from my youth up even until now I have not eaten of that which dies of itself, or is torn of animals. No abominable meat has come into my mouth!”
Then he said to me, “Behold, I have given you cow’s dung for man’s dung, and you shall prepare your bread on it.”
Moreover he said to me, “Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight, and with fearfulness. They will drink water by measure, and in dismay;
that they may lack bread and water, be dismayed one with another, and pine away in their iniquity.

“You, son of man, take a sharp sword. You shall take it as a barber’s razor to yourself, and shall cause it to pass over your head and over your beard. Then take balances to weigh and divide the hair.

A third part you shall burn in the fire in the middle of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled. You shall take a third part, and strike with the sword around it. A third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
You shall take a small number of these and bind them in the folds of your robe.
Of these again you shall take, and cast them into the middle of the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it a fire will come out into all the house of Israel.
“The Lord GOD says: ‘This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the middle of the nations, and countries are around her.

She has rebelled against my ordinances in doing wickedness more than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries that are around her; for they have rejected my ordinances, and as for my statutes, they have not walked in them.’

“Therefore the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you are more turbulent than the nations that are around you, and have not walked in my statutes, neither have kept my ordinances, neither have followed the ordinances of the nations that are around you;
therefore the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I, even I, am against you; and I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations.
I will do in you that which I have not done, and which I will not do anything like it any more, because of all your abominations.
Therefore the fathers will eat the sons within you, and the sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments on you; and I will scatter the whole remnant of you to all the winds.

Therefore as I live,’ says the Lord GOD, ‘surely, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things, and with all your abominations, therefore I will also diminish you. My eye won’t spare, and I will have no pity.

A third part of you will die with the pestilence, and they will be consumed with famine within you. A third part will fall by the sword around you. A third part I will scatter to all the winds, and will draw out a sword after them.

“‘Thus my anger will be accomplished, and I will cause my wrath toward them to rest, and I will be comforted. They will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my zeal, when I have accomplished my wrath on them.
“‘Moreover I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of all that pass by.

So it will be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment, to the nations that are around you, when I execute judgments on you in anger and in wrath, and in wrathful rebukes—I, the LORD, have spoken it—
when I send on them the evil arrows of famine that are for destruction, which I will send to destroy you. I will increase the famine on you and will break your staff of bread.
I will send on you famine and evil animals, and they will bereave you. Pestilence and blood will pass through you. I will bring the sword on you. I, the LORD, have spoken it.’”
The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy to them,

and say, ‘You mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! The Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the watercourses and to the valleys: “Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword on you, and I will destroy your high places.
Your altars will become desolate, and your incense altars will be broken. I will cast down your slain men before your idols.
I will lay the dead bodies of the children of Israel before their idols. I will scatter your bones around your altars.

In all your dwelling places, the cities will be laid waste and the high places will be desolate, so that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your incense altars may be cut down, and your works may be abolished.
The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
“‘“Yet I will leave a remnant, in that you will have some that escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the countries.

Those of you that escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their lewd heart, which has departed from me, and with their eyes, which play the prostitute after their idols. Then they will loathe themselves in their own sight for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.
They will know that I am the LORD. I have not said in vain that I would do this evil to them.”’

“The Lord GOD says: ‘Strike with your hand, and stamp with your foot, and say, “Alas!”, because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel; for they will fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.
He who is far off will die of the pestilence. He who is near will fall by the sword. He who remains and is besieged will die by the famine. Thus I will accomplish my wrath on them.

You will know that I am the LORD when their slain men are among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, under every green tree, and under every thick oak—the places where they offered pleasant aroma to all their idols.
I will stretch out my hand on them and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness toward Diblah, throughout all their habitations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
Moreover the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
“You, son of man, the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel, ‘An end! The end has come on the four corners of the land.
Now the end is on you, and I will send my anger on you, and will judge you according to your ways. I will bring on you all your abominations.
My eye will not spare you, neither will I have pity; but I will bring your ways on you, and your abominations will be among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’
“The Lord GOD says: ‘A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.
An end has come. The end has come! It awakes against you. Behold, it comes.
Your doom has come to you, inhabitant of the land! The time has come! The day is near, a day of tumult, and not of joyful shouting, on the mountains.
Now I will shortly pour out my wrath on you, and accomplish my anger against you, and will judge you according to your ways. I will bring on you all your abominations.
My eye won’t spare, neither will I have pity. I will punish you according to your ways. Your abominations will be among you. Then you will know that I, the LORD, strike.
“‘Behold, the day! Behold, it comes! Your doom has gone out. The rod has blossomed. Pride has budded.
Violence has risen up into a rod of wickedness. None of them will remain, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth. There will be nothing of value among them.
The time has come! The day draws near. Don’t let the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn; for wrath is on all its multitude.

For the seller won’t return to that which is sold, although they are still alive; for the vision concerns the whole multitude of it. None will return. None will strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.
They have blown the trumpet, and have made all ready; but no one goes to the battle, for my wrath is on all its multitude.
“‘The sword is outside, and the pestilence and the famine within. He who is in the field will die by the sword. He who is in the city will be devoured by famine and pestilence.
But of those who escape, they will escape and will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, everyone in his iniquity.
All hands will be feeble, and all knees will be weak as water.
They will also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and horror will cover them. Shame will be on all faces, and baldness on all their heads.

They will cast their silver in the streets, and their gold will be as an unclean thing. Their silver and their gold won’t be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD’s wrath. They won’t satisfy their souls or fill their bellies; because it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.
As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty; but they made the images of their abominations and their detestable things therein. Therefore I have made it to them as an unclean thing.
I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a plunder; and they will profane it.
I will also turn my face from them, and they will profane my secret place. Robbers will enter into it, and profane it.
“‘Make chains, for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.
Therefore I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will possess their houses. I will also make the pride of the strong to cease. Their holy places will be profaned.
Destruction comes! They will seek peace, and there will be none.
Mischief will come on mischief, and rumor will be on rumor. They will seek a vision of the prophet; but the law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, and the prince will be clothed with desolation. The hands of the people of the land will be troubled. I will do to them after their way, and according to their own judgments I will judge them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
In the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in my house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, the Lord GOD’s hand fell on me there.

Then I saw, and behold, a likeness as the appearance of fire—from the appearance of his waist and downward, fire, and from his waist and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as it were glowing metal.

He stretched out the form of a hand, and took me by a lock of my head; and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and the sky, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the gate of the inner court that looks toward the north, where there was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy.
Behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the appearance that I saw in the plain.

Then he said to me, “Son of man, lift up your eyes now the way toward the north.” So I lifted up my eyes the way toward the north, and saw, northward of the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.

He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they do? Even the great abominations that the house of Israel commit here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? But you will again see yet other great abominations.”
He brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold, a hole in the wall.
Then he said to me, “Son of man, dig now in the wall.” When I had dug in the wall, I saw a door.
He said to me, “Go in, and see the wicked abominations that they do here.”
So I went in and looked, and saw every form of creeping things, abominable animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed around on the wall.

Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel stood before them. In the middle of them Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan stood, every man with his censer in his hand; and the smell of the cloud of incense went up.

Then he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in his rooms of imagery? For they say, ‘The LORD doesn’t see us. The LORD has forsaken the land.’”
He said also to me, “You will again see more of the great abominations which they do.”
Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the LORD’s house which was toward the north; and I saw the women sit there weeping for Tammuz.
Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? You will again see yet greater abominations than these.”

He brought me into the inner court of the LORD’s house; and I saw at the door of the LORD’s temple, between the porch and the altar, there were about twenty-five men with their backs toward the LORD’s temple and their faces toward the east. They were worshiping the sun toward the east.

Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? For they have filled the land with violence, and have turned again to provoke me to anger. Behold, they put the branch to their nose.
