But I tell you, do not fight back against an evil person. If someone slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other cheek to them as well.
If someone takes you to court to get your shirt, let them have your coat as well.
If someone forces you to carry their things for one mile, go two miles with them.
Give to anyone who asks you, and do not turn away anyone who wants to borrow from you.
"You have heard that it was said, 'Love your neighbour and hate your enemy.'
But I tell you, love your enemies. Bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who hurt you and treat you badly.
Then you will be children of your Father in heaven. He makes his sun rise on bad people and good people, and he sends rain on those who do right and those who do wrong.
If you love only those who love you, what reward will you get? Even the tax collectors do that.
And if you greet only your friends, what are you doing more than others? Even people who do not know God do that.
So be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
"Be careful not to do your good deeds in front of other people just so they will see you. If you do, you will get no reward from your Father in heaven.

"So when you give to people in need, do not blow a trumpet to announce it. That is what the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, so that people will praise them. I tell you for certain, they have already received their full reward.
But when you give to people in need, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.
Then your giving will be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

"When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, so that people will see them. I tell you for certain, they have already received their full reward.
But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who cannot be seen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
When you pray, do not keep saying the same words over and over, like people who do not know God. They think God will hear them because they use so many words.
Do not be like them. Your Father knows what you need even before you ask him.
"This is how you should pray: 'Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
May your kingdom come. May what you want be done on earth, as it is done in heaven.
Give us today the food we need.
Forgive us the wrong things we have done, as we also forgive those who have done wrong to us.
Do not lead us into temptation, but save us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power and the glory are yours for ever. Amen.'
If you forgive other people when they sin against you, your Father in heaven will also forgive you.
But if you do not forgive others their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.

"When you fast, do not look sad like the hypocrites do. They make their faces look miserable so that people will see they are fasting. I tell you for certain, they have already received their full reward.
But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face.
Then people will not know that you are fasting, but only your Father, who cannot be seen, will know. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
"Do not store up treasures for yourselves here on earth, where moths and rust destroy them, and where thieves break in and steal them.
Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where moths and rust cannot destroy them, and where thieves cannot break in and steal them.
Where your treasure is, that is where your heart will be too.
"The eye is like a lamp for the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If the light inside you is really darkness, how dark that darkness is!
"No one can serve two masters. They will hate one and love the other, or they will be loyal to one and look down on the other. You cannot serve both God and money.

"So I tell you, do not worry about your life, about what you will eat or drink. And do not worry about your body, about what you will wear. Life is more important than food, and the body is more important than clothes.
Look at the birds in the sky. They do not plant seeds or gather a harvest or store food in barns, but your Father in heaven feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they are?
Can any of you add even one hour to your life by worrying?
"And why do you worry about clothes? Look at how the wild flowers grow. They do not work or make clothes for themselves.
But I tell you that not even King Solomon in all his splendour was dressed as beautifully as one of these flowers.
God dresses the grass in the fields like this, even though it is here today and thrown into the fire tomorrow. So he will certainly take even better care of you. Your faith is so small!
So do not worry and say, 'What will we eat?' or 'What will we drink?' or 'What will we wear?'
People who do not know God run after all these things. But your Father in heaven knows that you need them.
Put God's kingdom first, and do what he says is right. Then all these things will be given to you as well.
So do not worry about tomorrow. Tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own."
"Do not judge other people, and you will not be judged.
You will be judged in the same way that you judge others. And the amount you give to others is the amount you will be given.
"Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye, but do not notice the plank of wood in your own eye?
How can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when there is a plank in your own eye all the time?
You hypocrite! First take the plank out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly enough to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
"Do not give holy things to dogs, and do not throw your pearls to pigs. If you do, the pigs may trample them under their feet, and the dogs may turn and attack you.
"Ask, and it will be given to you. Search, and you will find. Knock, and the door will be opened to you.
Everyone who asks receives. The one who searches finds. And the door will be opened to the one who knocks.
"If your son asks for bread, which of you would give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, would you give him a snake?
Even though you are evil, you know how to give good gifts to your children. So your Father in heaven will be even more ready to give good things to those who ask him!
So in everything, treat other people the way you want them to treat you. This is what the Law and the Prophets are all about.
"Go in through the narrow gate. The gate is wide and the road is easy that leads to destruction, and many people go in that way.
But the gate is small and the road is narrow that leads to life, and only a few people find it.
"Watch out for false prophets. They come to you dressed like sheep, but inside they are hungry wolves.
You will know them by the fruit they produce. People do not pick grapes from thorn bushes, or figs from weeds.
In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit.
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot produce good fruit.
Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So you will know them by their fruit.
"Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven. Only those who do what my Father in heaven wants will enter.
On that day many will say to me, 'Lord, Lord, did we not speak God's message in your name? Did we not drive out demons in your name and do many miracles in your name?'
Then I will tell them clearly, 'I never knew you. Get away from me, you who do evil!'
"So everyone who hears these words of mine and obeys them is like a wise man who built his house on rock.
The rain came down, the rivers flooded and the winds blew and beat against that house. But it did not fall, because it was built on rock.
But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not obey them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
The rain came down, the rivers flooded and the winds blew and beat against that house. And it fell down with a great crash."
When Jesus finished saying these things, the crowds were amazed at his teaching,
because he taught them like someone who had authority, and not like their teachers of the law.
When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
A man with a skin disease came and knelt in front of him. He said, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus reached out his hand and touched the man. "I am willing," he said. "Be clean!" Straight away the man was healed of his skin disease.
Then Jesus said to him, "Make sure you do not tell anyone. But go and show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded. This will show them that you are healed."
When Jesus went into Capernaum, a Roman army officer came to him and asked him for help.
"Lord," he said, "my servant is lying at home and cannot move. He is suffering terribly."
Jesus said to him, "I will come and heal him."
The officer replied, "Lord, I am not good enough for you to come into my house. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I am a man who is under authority myself, and I have soldiers under me. I tell this one, 'Go,' and he goes. I tell that one, 'Come,' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this, he was amazed. He said to the people following him, "I tell you for certain, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.
I tell you that many people will come from the east and the west. They will sit down to eat with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
But those who should have belonged to the kingdom will be thrown outside into the darkness. There people will cry and grind their teeth."
Then Jesus said to the officer, "Go! What you believed will happen." And his servant was healed at that very moment.
When Jesus came into Peter's house, he saw Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. Then she got up and began to serve him.
When evening came, many people who had demons were brought to Jesus. He drove out the spirits with a word and healed everyone who was ill.
This made come true what the prophet Isaiah had said: "He took away our weaknesses and carried our diseases."
When Jesus saw the crowd around him, he told his followers to cross to the other side of the lake.
Then a teacher of the law came to him and said, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
Jesus replied, "Foxes have holes and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to rest his head."
Another follower said to him, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
But Jesus told him, "Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead."
Then Jesus got into a boat, and his followers went with him.
Suddenly a terrible storm came up on the lake, so that the waves were covering the boat. But Jesus was sleeping.
The followers went and woke him up. They said, "Lord, save us! We are going to drown!"
He replied, "Why are you so afraid? Your faith is so small!" Then he got up and ordered the winds and the waves to stop, and everything became completely calm.
The men were amazed. They asked, "What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the waves obey him!"
When Jesus arrived on the other side, in the country of the Gergesenes, two men who had demons met him. They came out of the tombs, and they were so violent that no one could use that road.
They shouted, "What do you want with us, Son of God? Have you come here to punish us before the right time?"
Some distance away a large herd of pigs was feeding.
The demons begged Jesus, "If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
He said to them, "Go!" So they came out and went into the pigs. Then the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned in the water.
The men looking after the pigs ran off into the town. They told everything that had happened, including what had happened to the men who had demons.
Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their area.
Jesus got into a boat, crossed over the lake and came to his own town.
Some people brought to him a man who could not move, lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man, "Cheer up, son! Your sins are forgiven."
Some of the teachers of the law said to themselves, "This man is insulting God!"
Jesus knew what they were thinking. So he said, "Why are you thinking evil things in your hearts?
Which is easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." Then he said to the man who could not move, "Get up, pick up your mat and go home."
And the man got up and went home.
When the crowd saw this, they were filled with wonder. They praised God for giving such authority to human beings.
As Jesus went on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax collector's booth. "Follow me," he told him. And Matthew got up and followed him.
Later Jesus was having a meal at Matthew's house. Many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Jesus and his followers.
When the Pharisees saw this, they asked his followers, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus heard this and said, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people do.
Go and learn what this means: 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' I have not come to call good people, but sinners, to turn away from their sins."
Then John's followers came and asked Jesus, "We and the Pharisees often go without food. Why do your followers not fast?"
Jesus answered, "How can the guests of the bridegroom be sad while he is with them? But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast.
"No one sews a patch of new cloth on old clothes. The new patch will shrink and pull away from the clothes, and the tear will get worse.

And people do not pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst. The wine will run out and the wineskins will be ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are kept safe."
While Jesus was saying this, a synagogue leader came and knelt in front of him. He said, "My daughter has just died. But come and put your hand on her, and she will live."
Jesus got up and went with him, and so did his followers.
Just then a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind Jesus. She touched the edge of his clothes.
She said to herself, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Jesus turned and saw her. "Cheer up, daughter," he said. "Your faith has healed you." And the woman was healed from that moment.
When Jesus arrived at the leader's house, he saw people playing flutes and a noisy crowd.
He said, "Go away. The girl is not dead. She is asleep." But they laughed at him.
After the crowd had been sent outside, Jesus went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
News about this spread all over that area.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him. They shouted, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
When he went indoors, the blind men came to him. Jesus asked them, "Do you believe that I can do this?" "Yes, Lord," they replied.
Then he touched their eyes and said, "Because of your faith, it will happen to you."
And they could see again. Jesus warned them strongly, "Make sure that no one knows about this."
But they went out and spread the news about him all over that area.
While they were going out, some people brought to Jesus a man who could not talk because he had a demon.
When the demon was driven out, the man began to speak. The crowd was amazed and said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!"
But the Pharisees said, "It is by the ruler of demons that he drives out demons."
Jesus went through all the towns and villages. He taught in their synagogues and preached the good news about the kingdom. And he healed every kind of disease and illness.
When he saw the crowds, he felt sorry for them, because they were worried and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then he said to his followers, "The harvest is huge, but there are only a few workers.
So ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest field."
Jesus called his twelve followers to him. He gave them authority to drive out evil spirits and to heal every kind of disease and illness.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus;
Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who later handed Jesus over to his enemies.
Jesus sent out these twelve with these instructions: "Do not go to the people who are not Jews, and do not go into any town of the Samaritans.
Instead, go to the people of Israel, who are like lost sheep.
As you go, preach this message: 'The kingdom of heaven is near.'
Heal the sick, make people with skin diseases clean, and drive out demons. You received freely, so give freely.
Do not take any gold, silver or copper money in your belts.
Do not take a bag for the journey, or a spare shirt, or sandals, or a walking stick. Workers deserve to be given their food.
"Whatever town or village you go into, look for someone who is worthy and stay at their house until you leave.
As you go into the home, greet the family.
If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it. If it is not worthy, let your peace come back to you.
If anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that home or town.
I tell you for certain, it will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgement than for that town.
"I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be as wise as snakes and as harmless as doves.
Be careful of people. They will hand you over to the courts and whip you in their synagogues.
Because of me you will be brought in front of governors and kings. You will tell them and the other nations about me.
But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given the words to say.
It will not really be you speaking. The Spirit of your Father will be speaking through you.
"Brothers will hand each other over to be killed, and fathers will hand over their children. Children will turn against their parents and have them put to death.
Everyone will hate you because of me. But whoever keeps going until the end will be saved.
When people treat you badly in one town, escape to the next. I tell you for certain, you will not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
"A student is not greater than his teacher, and a servant is not greater than his master.
It is enough for the student to be like his teacher, and the servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, the members of his family will be called even worse names!
"So do not be afraid of them. Everything that is covered up will be uncovered, and every secret will be made known.
What I tell you in the dark, say in the daylight. What is whispered in your ear, shout from the rooftops.
Do not be afraid of people who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, be afraid of God, who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Are two sparrows not sold for a small coin? Yet not one of them falls to the ground without your Father knowing.
Even the hairs on your head have all been counted.
So do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
"Whoever says in front of others that they belong to me, I will say in front of my Father in heaven that they belong to me.
But whoever says in front of others that they do not know me, I will say in front of my Father in heaven that I do not know them.
"Do not think that I came to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
I have come to turn a son against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
A person's enemies will be the members of their own family.
"Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. Anyone who loves their son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
Anyone who does not pick up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it, and whoever gives up their life for me will find it.
"Anyone who welcomes you welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
Anyone who welcomes a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet's reward. And anyone who welcomes a good person because they are good will receive a good person's reward.
And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because they are my follower, I tell you for certain, that person will never lose their reward."
When Jesus had finished giving instructions to his twelve followers, he left there to teach and preach in the towns of Galilee.
John was in prison. When he heard about the things the Christ was doing, he sent his followers to Jesus.
They asked him, "Are you the one who was to come, or should we wait for someone else?"
Jesus answered, "Go back and tell John what you hear and see.

Blind people can see. People who could not walk are walking. People with skin diseases are made clean. Deaf people can hear. Dead people are raised to life. And the good news is preached to poor people.
Blessed is anyone who does not give up their faith because of me."
As John's followers were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John. "What did you go out into the desert to see? Tall grass blowing in the wind?
If not, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? No, people who wear fine clothes live in kings' palaces.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and he is more than a prophet.
He is the one the Scriptures talk about: 'I will send my messenger ahead of you. He will prepare your way for you.'
I tell you for certain, no one born of a woman has ever been greater than John the Baptist. But even the least important person in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is.
From the time John the Baptist began preaching until now, the kingdom of heaven has been under violent attack, and violent people are trying to take it by force.
All the Prophets and the Law spoke about what would happen, until John came.
If you are willing to accept it, John is the Elijah who was to come.
Whoever has ears should listen.
"What can I compare the people of today with? They are like children sitting in the market places and calling out to other children:
'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance. We sang a sad song, and you did not cry.'
John came and did not eat or drink wine, and people say, 'He has a demon.'

The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look at him! He eats too much and drinks too much wine. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners.' But wisdom is shown to be right by what it does."
Then Jesus began to speak strongly against the towns where he had done most of his miracles, because the people had not turned away from their sins.

"How terrible it will be for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the miracles done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned away from their sins long ago. They would have dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes to show they were sorry.
But I tell you, it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgement than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will go down to the place of the dead. If the miracles done in you had been done in Sodom, it would still be here today.
But I tell you, it will be easier for Sodom on the day of judgement than for you."
At that time Jesus said, "I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth. You have hidden these things from people who are wise and clever, and shown them to little children.
Yes, Father, this is what you were pleased to do.
"My Father has given me everything. No one knows the Son except the Father. And no one knows the Father except the Son, and those to whom the Son chooses to show him.
"Come to me, all of you who are tired and carrying heavy loads, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke on you and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart. Then you will find rest for your souls.
My yoke is easy to wear, and the load I give you is light."
At that time Jesus walked through the grain fields on a Sabbath day. His followers were hungry, so they began to pick some heads of grain and eat them.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, "Look! Your followers are doing something that is against the law on the Sabbath."
He answered, "Have you not read what David did when he and his men were hungry?
He went into the house of God, and he and his men ate the holy bread. That was against the law for them. Only the priests were allowed to eat it.
And have you not read in the Law that the priests in the temple break the Sabbath rules, but they are not guilty?
I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
The Scriptures say, 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' If you had known what this means, you would not have judged people who are not guilty.
The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
Jesus went on from there and went into their synagogue.
A man with a shrivelled hand was there. Some people were looking for a reason to accuse Jesus. So they asked him, "Is it against the law to heal on the Sabbath?"
He said to them, "If any of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will you not take hold of it and lift it out?
A person is worth much more than a sheep! So it is right to do good on the Sabbath."
Then he said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and it was healed, as healthy as the other one.
But the Pharisees went out and made plans to kill Jesus.
Jesus knew about this, so he left that place. Large crowds followed him, and he healed all who were ill.
But he warned them not to tell other people about him.
This made come true what the prophet Isaiah had said:
"Here is my servant whom I have chosen, the one I love, who makes me very happy. I will put my Spirit on him, and he will announce justice to the nations.
He will not argue or shout. No one will hear his voice in the streets.
He will not break a bent reed, and he will not put out a flickering lamp, until he makes justice win.
The nations will put their hope in him."
Then some people brought Jesus a man who was blind and could not talk because he had a demon. Jesus healed him, so that he could both talk and see.
All the people were amazed. They asked, "Could this be the Son of David?"
But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, "This man drives out demons only by the power of Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons."
Jesus knew what they were thinking, and he said to them, "Every kingdom that fights against itself will be destroyed. Every town or family that fights against itself will not last.
If Satan drives out Satan, he is fighting against himself. So how can his kingdom last?
And if I drive out demons by the power of Beelzebul, by whose power do your own people drive them out? So they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come to you.
"How can anyone go into a strong man's house and steal his things, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can rob his house.
"Whoever is not with me is against me. And whoever does not help me gather is scattering.
So I tell you, people will be forgiven for every sin and every insult against God. But anyone who insults the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this world or in the world to come.
"If you make a tree good, its fruit will be good. If you make a tree bad, its fruit will be bad. A tree is known by its fruit.
You family of snakes! You are evil, so how can you say anything good? The mouth speaks what fills the heart.
A good person brings good things out of the good stored up inside them. An evil person brings evil things out of the evil stored up inside them.
But I tell you that on the day of judgement, people will have to explain every careless word they have spoken.
By your words you will be found not guilty, and by your words you will be found guilty."
Then some of the Pharisees and teachers of the law said to him, "Teacher, we want to see a miraculous sign from you."
He answered, "Evil and unfaithful people ask for a sign! But no sign will be given to them except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
Jonah was in the belly of a huge fish for three days and three nights. In the same way, the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.

The people of Nineveh will stand up on the day of judgement with the people of today and show that they are guilty. The people of Nineveh turned away from their sins when Jonah preached to them. And now someone greater than Jonah is here.

The Queen of the South will stand up on the day of judgement with the people of today and show that they are guilty. She came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom. And now someone greater than Solomon is here.
"When an evil spirit comes out of a person, it goes through dry places looking for rest, but it does not find any.
Then it says, 'I will go back to the house I left.' When it arrives, it finds the house empty, swept clean and tidy.

Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself. They go in and live there. And in the end that person is worse off than before. That is how it will be for these evil people of today."
While Jesus was still talking to the crowd, his mother and brothers were standing outside. They wanted to speak to him.
Someone told him, "Your mother and brothers are standing outside. They want to speak to you."
Jesus replied to him, "Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?"
He pointed to his followers and said, "Here are my mother and my brothers!
Anyone who does what my Father in heaven wants is my brother and sister and mother."
That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat down by the lake.
Such large crowds gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat in it. All the people stood on the shore.
Then he told them many things using stories. He said, "A farmer went out to plant his seed.
As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the path, and birds came and ate it up.
Some fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. It grew up quickly, because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched. They dried up because they had no roots.
Other seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked the plants.
But other seed fell on good soil, and it produced a crop. Some produced a hundred times as much as was planted, some sixty times and some thirty times.
Whoever has ears should listen."
The followers came to him and asked, "Why do you use stories when you speak to the people?"
He answered, "You have been given the gift of knowing the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not.
Whoever has something will be given more, and they will have plenty. But whoever does not have anything, even what they have will be taken away from them.
This is why I use stories when I speak to them: 'They look, but they do not really see. They listen, but they do not really hear or understand.'
In them the words of the prophet Isaiah come true: 'You will keep on hearing, but you will never understand. You will keep on looking, but you will never really see.

The hearts of these people have become hard. Their ears can hardly hear, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears and understand with their hearts. Then they would turn back to me, and I would heal them.'
But your eyes are blessed because they see, and your ears are blessed because they hear.
I tell you for certain, many prophets and good people wanted to see what you see, but they did not see it. They wanted to hear what you hear, but they did not hear it.
"So listen to what the story of the farmer means.
When anyone hears the message about the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was planted in their heart. This is the seed that fell along the path.
The seed that fell on rocky ground is the person who hears the message and accepts it with joy straight away.
But they have no roots, so they last only a short time. When trouble or hard times come because of the message, they quickly give up.
The seed that fell among the thorns is the person who hears the message, but the worries of this life and the lie that money brings happiness choke the message. So it produces nothing.
But the seed that fell on good soil is the person who hears the message and understands it. They produce a crop of a hundred, sixty or thirty times as much as was planted."
Jesus told them another story. "The kingdom of heaven is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
But while everyone was sleeping, his enemy came and planted weeds among the wheat, and then went away.
When the wheat came up and formed heads of grain, the weeds also appeared.
"The owner's servants came to him and said, 'Sir, did you not plant good seed in your field? So where did the weeds come from?'
"'An enemy did this,' he replied. "The servants asked him, 'Do you want us to go and pull the weeds up?'
"'No,' he answered. 'While you are pulling up the weeds, you might pull up the wheat with them.
Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the workers, "First gather the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned. Then gather the wheat and bring it into my barn."'"
Jesus told them another story. "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.
It is the smallest of all seeds. But when it grows, it is the biggest of all garden plants. It becomes a tree, and the birds come and make nests in its branches."
He told them another story. "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman mixed into a large amount of flour, until the yeast worked its way all through the dough."
Jesus used stories to tell the crowd all these things. He did not say anything to them without using a story.
This made come true what the prophet had said: "I will speak using stories. I will tell things that have been hidden since the world was made."
Then Jesus left the crowd and went into the house. His followers came to him and said, "Explain to us the story of the weeds in the field."
He answered, "The one who planted the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world. The good seed stands for the people who belong to the kingdom. The weeds are the people who belong to the evil one.
The enemy who plants the weeds is the devil. The harvest is the end of the world, and the workers are angels.
"The weeds are pulled up and burned in the fire. That is how it will be at the end of the world.
The Son of Man will send out his angels. They will remove from his kingdom everything that causes sin, and all who do evil.
They will throw them into the blazing furnace. There people will cry and grind their teeth.
Then the people who do what is right will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever has ears should listen.
"The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again. Then, full of joy, he went and sold everything he had and bought that field.
"Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a trader who was looking for fine pearls.
When he found one pearl that was worth a great deal, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
"Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was thrown into the lake and caught all kinds of fish.
When it was full, the fishermen pulled it up on the shore. Then they sat down and put the good fish in baskets, but threw the bad ones away.
That is how it will be at the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the evil people from the people who do what is right.
They will throw the evil ones into the blazing furnace. There people will cry and grind their teeth."
Jesus asked, "Have you understood all these things?" "Yes, Lord," they replied.
He said to them, "So every teacher of the law who has become a follower in the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house. He brings new treasures and old treasures out of his storeroom."
When Jesus had finished telling these stories, he left that place.
He went to his home town and began teaching the people in their synagogue. They were amazed and asked, "Where did this man get this wisdom and these miraculous powers?
Is he not the carpenter's son? Is his mother's name not Mary? Are his brothers not James, Joses, Simon and Judas?
Are all his sisters not here with us? So where did this man get all these things?"
And they refused to accept him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is honoured everywhere except in his own town and in his own home."
And he did not do many miracles there, because they did not believe in him.
At that time Herod, the ruler of Galilee, heard the reports about Jesus.
He said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has come back from the dead! That is why he has the power to do miracles."
Herod had arrested John, tied him up and put him in prison. He did this because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
John had been telling Herod, "It is against the law for you to have her as your wife."
Herod wanted to kill John, but he was afraid of the people, because they believed John was a prophet.
On Herod's birthday the daughter of Herodias danced for the guests, and Herod was very pleased with her.
So he promised with an oath to give her anything she asked for.
Her mother told her what to say. So she said, "Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a plate."
The king was very sad. But he had made a promise in front of his guests, so he ordered that her request be granted.
He had John's head cut off in the prison.
John's head was brought in on a plate and given to the girl, and she took it to her mother.
John's followers came and took his body and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard what had happened, he left in a boat and went by himself to a quiet place. But the crowds heard about it, and they followed him on foot from the towns.
When Jesus came ashore, he saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them and healed those who were ill.
When evening came, his followers came to him and said, "This is a lonely place, and it is already getting late. Send the crowds away, so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food."
Jesus replied, "They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat."
They answered, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish here."
"Bring them here to me," he said.

Then he told the people to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven and gave thanks. Then he broke the loaves and gave them to his followers, and the followers gave them to the people.
They all ate and had enough. Then the followers picked up twelve baskets full of the pieces that were left over.
About five thousand men ate, as well as women and children.
Straight away Jesus made his followers get into the boat and go on ahead of him to the other side of the lake, while he sent the crowd away.
After he had sent them away, he went up on a mountainside by himself to pray. When evening came, he was there alone.
By this time the boat was far out on the lake. It was being battered by the waves, because the wind was blowing against it.
Shortly before dawn, Jesus came out to them, walking on the lake.
When the followers saw him walking on the water, they were terrified. "It's a ghost!" they said, and they cried out in fear.
But straight away Jesus spoke to them. He said, "Cheer up! It is I. Do not be afraid."
"Lord, if it is you," Peter replied, "tell me to come to you on the water."
"Come," Jesus said. So Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water towards Jesus.
But when he saw how strong the wind was, he was afraid and began to sink. He cried out, "Lord, save me!"
Straight away Jesus reached out his hand and caught him. "Your faith is so small!" he said. "Why did you doubt?"
When they climbed back into the boat, the wind stopped.
Then those in the boat worshipped Jesus and said, "You really are the Son of God!"
After they had crossed the lake, they landed at Gennesaret.
When the people there recognised Jesus, they sent the news all around that area. People brought to him everyone who was ill.
They begged him to let them touch just the edge of his clothes, and all who touched it were healed.
Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came to Jesus from Jerusalem. They asked,
"Why do your followers break the old rules handed down by our leaders? They do not wash their hands before they eat!"
Jesus replied, "And why do you break God's command for the sake of your own rules?
God said, 'Honour your father and mother,' and 'Anyone who speaks evil of their father or mother must be put to death.'
But you say that people can tell their father or mother, 'The help you might have received from me is a gift set aside for God.'
Then they do not need to honour their father or mother. In this way you cancel God's word for the sake of your own rules.
You hypocrites! Isaiah was right when he spoke God's message about you:
'These people honour me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me.
Their worship of me is worthless. They teach rules that were made up by human beings.'"
Jesus called the crowd to him and said, "Listen and understand.
What goes into a person's mouth does not make them unclean. It is what comes out of their mouth that makes them unclean."
Then the followers came to him and asked, "Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?"
He replied, "Every plant that my Father in heaven did not plant will be pulled up by the roots.
Leave them alone. They are blind guides. If a blind person leads a blind person, both of them will fall into a pit."
Peter said, "Explain this saying to us."
"Do you still not understand?" Jesus asked them.
"Do you not see that whatever goes into the mouth goes into the stomach and then out of the body?
But the things that come out of a person's mouth come from the heart, and these make a person unclean.
Out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual sin, stealing, lying and insults.
These are what make a person unclean. But eating without washing your hands does not make you unclean."
Jesus left that place and went to the area of Tyre and Sidon.
A Canaanite woman from that area came to him, crying out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter has a demon and is suffering terribly."
But Jesus did not say a word to her. So his followers came to him and begged him, "Send her away. She keeps shouting after us."
He answered, "I was sent only to the people of Israel, who are like lost sheep."
But the woman came and knelt in front of him. "Lord, help me!" she said.
He replied, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
"Yes, Lord," she said, "but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master's table."
Then Jesus said to her, "Woman, you have great faith! What you have asked for will be done." And her daughter was healed at that moment.
Jesus left there and went along the Sea of Galilee. Then he went up on a mountainside and sat down.
Large crowds came to him. They brought people who could not walk, people who were blind or disabled, people who could not talk, and many others. They laid them at his feet, and he healed them.

The people were amazed when they saw that those who could not talk were speaking, the disabled were made well, those who could not walk were walking and the blind could see. And they praised the God of Israel.

Jesus called his followers to him and said, "I feel sorry for these people. They have been with me for three days now and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint on the way."
His followers said, "Where could we get enough bread in this lonely place to feed such a big crowd?"
"How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Seven," they replied, "and a few small fish."
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
Then he took the seven loaves and the fish, and he gave thanks. He broke them and gave them to the followers, and they gave them to the people.
They all ate and had enough. Afterwards the followers picked up seven baskets full of the pieces that were left over.
Four thousand men ate, as well as women and children.
After Jesus had sent the crowd away, he got into the boat and went to the area of Magdala.
The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus to test him. They asked him to show them a miraculous sign from heaven.
He replied, "In the evening you say, 'There will be good weather, because the sky is red.'
And in the morning you say, 'There will be a storm today, because the sky is red and cloudy.' You hypocrites! You know how to read the signs in the sky, but you cannot read the signs of the times.
Evil and unfaithful people ask for a sign, but no sign will be given to them except the sign of Jonah." Then Jesus left them and went away.
When the followers crossed to the other side of the lake, they had forgotten to take any bread.
Jesus said to them, "Be careful! Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
They talked about this among themselves and said, "He is saying this because we did not bring any bread."
Jesus knew what they were saying, so he asked, "Your faith is so small! Why are you talking among yourselves about having no bread?
Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you picked up?
Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you picked up?
How can you not understand that I was not talking to you about bread? But watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
Then they understood that he was not telling them to watch out for the yeast used in bread. He was warning them about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus came to the area of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his followers, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"
They replied, "Some say John the Baptist. Others say Elijah, and others say Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
"But what about you?" he asked. "Who do you say I am?"
Simon Peter answered, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Jesus replied, "Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! No human being showed this to you. My Father in heaven showed it to you.
And I tell you that you are Peter, which means rock. On this rock I will build my church, and even the power of death will not be able to defeat it.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you forbid on earth will be forbidden in heaven, and whatever you allow on earth will be allowed in heaven."
Then he ordered his followers not to tell anyone that he was the Christ.

From that time on Jesus began to explain to his followers that he must go to Jerusalem. He would suffer many things from the elders, the chief priests and the teachers of the law. He must be killed and then be raised to life on the third day.
Peter took him aside and began to tell him off. "Never, Lord!" he said. "This will never happen to you!"
Jesus turned and said to Peter, "Get away from me, Satan! You are standing in my way. You are not thinking about the things of God, but only about human things."
Then Jesus said to his followers, "Whoever wants to follow me must say no to themselves. They must pick up their cross and follow me.
Whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it.
What good is it if someone gains the whole world but loses their life? What can anyone give in exchange for their life?
The Son of Man is going to come in the glory of his Father with his angels. Then he will reward each person for what they have done.
I tell you for certain, some who are standing here will not die before they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom."
Six days later Jesus took Peter, James and James's brother John with him. He led them up a high mountain, where they were alone.
There his appearance was changed in front of them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as light.
Then Moses and Elijah appeared in front of them, talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, I will put up three shelters here, one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah."
While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them. A voice from the cloud said, "This is my Son, whom I love. I am very pleased with him. Listen to him!"
When the followers heard this, they fell face down on the ground, terrified.
But Jesus came and touched them. "Get up," he said. "Do not be afraid."
When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus ordered them, "Do not tell anyone what you have seen until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead."
The followers asked him, "Then why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?"
Jesus replied, "It is true that Elijah comes first and will put everything right again.
But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and people did not recognise him. Instead, they did whatever they wanted to him. In the same way the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands."
Then the followers understood that he was talking to them about John the Baptist.
When they came back to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt in front of him.
"Lord, have mercy on my son," he said. "He has seizures and suffers terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
I brought him to your followers, but they could not heal him."
Jesus replied, "You people have no faith, and you have turned away from God! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me."
Jesus ordered the demon to leave, and it came out of the boy. He was healed from that moment.
Then the followers came to Jesus in private and asked, "Why could we not drive it out?"

He replied, "Because you have so little faith. I tell you for certain, if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.
But this kind of demon does not go out except by prayer and fasting."
While they were together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be handed over to people.
They will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised to life." And the followers were filled with great sadness.
When Jesus and his followers arrived in Capernaum, the men who collected the temple tax came to Peter. They asked, "Does your teacher not pay the temple tax?"

"Yes, he does," Peter replied. When Peter came into the house, Jesus spoke first. "What do you think, Simon?" he asked. "Who do the kings of the earth collect taxes and duties from? From their own children or from others?"
"From others," Peter answered. "Then the children do not have to pay," Jesus said to him.

"But we do not want to offend them. So go to the lake and throw out your fishing line. Take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a coin. Take it and give it to them to pay the tax for you and me."
At that time the followers came to Jesus and asked, "Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
Jesus called a little child to him and made the child stand among them.
Then he said, "I tell you for certain, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
So whoever makes themselves humble like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever welcomes a little child like this in my name welcomes me.
"But suppose someone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin. It would be better for that person to have a large millstone hung around their neck and be drowned in the deep sea.
How terrible it will be for the world because of the things that cause people to sin! Such things will certainly come, but how terrible it will be for the person who causes them!

If your hand or your foot makes you sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with a hand or foot missing than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the fire that burns for ever.
And if your eye makes you sin, pull it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
"Make sure you do not look down on one of these little ones. I tell you that their angels in heaven are always with my Father in heaven.
The Son of Man came to save what was lost.
"What do you think? If a man owns a hundred sheep and one of them wanders away, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go to look for the one that wandered off?
And if he finds it, I tell you for certain, he is happier about that one sheep than about the ninety-nine that did not wander away.
In the same way, your Father in heaven does not want any of these little ones to be lost.
"If your brother or sister sins against you, go and talk to them about it, just between the two of you. If they listen to you, you have won them back.
But if they will not listen, take one or two others with you. Then everything that is said can be confirmed by two or three witnesses.
If they still refuse to listen, tell it to the church. And if they refuse to listen even to the church, treat them as you would treat someone who does not know God, or a tax collector.
"I tell you for certain, whatever you forbid on earth will be forbidden in heaven, and whatever you allow on earth will be allowed in heaven.
"Again, I tell you for certain that if two of you on earth agree about anything you ask for, my Father in heaven will do it for you.
Where two or three people come together in my name, I am there with them."
Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, "Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother or sister when they sin against me? Up to seven times?"
Jesus answered, "I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy times seven.
"So the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
As he began to do this, a man was brought to him who owed him ten thousand bags of gold.
The man was not able to pay. So his master ordered that he, his wife, his children and everything he owned be sold to pay back the debt.
"The servant fell on his knees in front of him. 'Be patient with me,' he begged, 'and I will pay back everything.'
The master felt sorry for him. He let him go and cancelled the whole debt.
"But when that servant went out, he found one of the other servants who owed him a hundred silver coins. He grabbed him and began to choke him. 'Pay back what you owe me!' he said.
"The other servant fell on his knees and begged him, 'Be patient with me, and I will pay it back.'
"But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay back the debt.
When the other servants saw what had happened, they were very upset. They went and told their master everything that had happened.
"Then the master called the servant in. 'You wicked servant,' he said. 'I cancelled all that debt of yours because you begged me to.
Should you not have had mercy on the other servant, just as I had mercy on you?'
The master was very angry. He handed him over to the jailers to be punished until he could pay back everything he owed.
"This is how my Father in heaven will treat each of you, unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart."
When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee. He went to the area of Judea on the other side of the Jordan River.
Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
Some Pharisees came to him to test him. They asked, "Is it right for a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?"
Jesus replied, "Have you not read that in the beginning the Creator made them male and female?
He said, 'That is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one.'
So they are no longer two, but one. What God has joined together, no one should separate."
They asked him, "Then why did Moses command that a man can give his wife a written notice of divorce and send her away?"
Jesus replied, "Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard. But it was not like this from the beginning.
I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, unless his wife has been unfaithful. And anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
The followers said to him, "If this is how it is between a husband and wife, it is better not to marry."
Jesus replied, "Not everyone can accept this teaching. Only those whom God helps can accept it.

Some people cannot marry because they were born that way. Others were made that way by other people. And others choose not to marry for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Whoever can accept this teaching should accept it."
Then people brought little children to Jesus so that he could put his hands on them and pray for them. But the followers told them off.
Jesus said, "Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them. The kingdom of heaven belongs to people like them."
He put his hands on them, and then he went on from there.
Just then a man came up to Jesus and asked, "Good teacher, what good thing must I do to get eternal life?"
Jesus replied, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, and that is God. If you want to enter life, obey the commandments."
"Which ones?" the man asked. Jesus replied, "'Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others.
Honour your father and mother.' And, 'Love your neighbour as you love yourself.'"
"I have obeyed all these since I was young," the young man said. "What do I still need to do?"
Jesus answered, "If you want to be perfect, go and sell everything you own and give the money to poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me."
When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he was very rich.
Then Jesus said to his followers, "I tell you for certain, it is hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
When the followers heard this, they were completely amazed. They asked, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said, "For people this is impossible. But for God everything is possible."
Then Peter said to him, "We have left everything to follow you! What will we get?"

Jesus said to them, "I tell you for certain, when everything is made new, the Son of Man will sit on his glorious throne. Then you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children or fields for me will receive a hundred times as much, and they will receive eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first."
"The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed to pay them one silver coin for the day, and he sent them into his vineyard.
"About nine o'clock in the morning he went out again. He saw others standing in the market place doing nothing.
He told them, 'You also go and work in my vineyard, and I will pay you whatever is fair.' So they went.
"He went out again about twelve o'clock and about three o'clock in the afternoon and did the same thing.
About five o'clock in the afternoon he went out and found still others standing around. He asked them, 'Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?'
"'Because no one has hired us,' they answered. "He said to them, 'You also go and work in my vineyard, and you will get whatever is fair.'
"When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager, 'Call the workers and pay them their wages. Begin with the last ones hired and go on to the first.'
"The workers who were hired about five o'clock came, and each of them received one silver coin.
So when the first workers came, they expected to receive more. But each of them also received one silver coin.
When they received it, they began to complain about the landowner.
They said, 'These men who were hired last worked only one hour. But you have paid them the same as us, and we have done most of the work in the heat of the day.'
"But he answered one of them, 'Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree to work for one silver coin?
Take your pay and go. I want to give the man who was hired last the same as I gave you.
Do I not have the right to do what I want with my own money? Or are you jealous because I am generous?'
"So the last will be first, and the first will be last. Many are invited, but few are chosen."
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve followers aside on the way and talked to them.
"We are going up to Jerusalem," he said. "The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will sentence him to death.
Then they will hand him over to people who are not Jews. They will make fun of him, whip him and nail him to a cross. But on the third day he will be raised to life."
Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came to Jesus with her sons. She knelt down and asked him for a favour.
"What do you want?" Jesus asked. She said, "Promise that one of my two sons may sit at your right side and the other at your left side in your kingdom."
Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup of suffering that I am going to drink, and be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with?" "We can," they answered.

Jesus said to them, "You will certainly drink from my cup, and be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with. But it is not for me to say who will sit at my right side or my left side. These places belong to those my Father has prepared them for."
When the other ten followers heard about this, they were angry with the two brothers.
Jesus called them together and said, "You know that the rulers of the nations like to show their power over their people. Their important leaders order them around.
It must not be like that with you. Instead, anyone who wants to be important among you must be your servant.
And anyone who wants to be first must be your slave.
In the same way, the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve others, and to give his life to set many people free."
As Jesus and his followers were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
Two blind men were sitting by the side of the road. When they heard that Jesus was going by, they shouted, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!"
The crowd told them off and told them to be quiet. But they shouted even louder, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!"
Jesus stopped and called them. "What do you want me to do for you?" he asked.
"Lord," they answered, "we want to be able to see."
Jesus felt sorry for them and touched their eyes. Straight away they could see, and they followed him.
As Jesus and his followers came near Jerusalem, they arrived at Bethphage on the Mount of Olives. Jesus sent two of his followers ahead.
He said to them, "Go to the village ahead of you. As soon as you get there, you will find a donkey tied up, with her colt next to her. Untie them and bring them to me.
If anyone says anything to you, tell them, 'The Lord needs them.' Then he will send them straight away."
This happened to make come true what the prophet had said:
"Say to the people of Zion, 'Look, your king is coming to you. He is humble, and he is riding on a donkey, on a colt, the young of a donkey.'"
The followers went and did what Jesus had told them.
They brought the donkey and the colt and put their coats on them, and Jesus sat on them.
A very large crowd spread their coats on the road. Others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds that went ahead of him and those that followed shouted, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heaven!"
When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was excited. People asked, "Who is this?"
The crowds answered, "This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee."
Jesus went into the temple of God and drove out all the people who were buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves.
He said to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are making it a hideout for robbers!"
People who were blind and people who could not walk came to him at the temple, and he healed them.
The chief priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things he did. They also saw the children shouting in the temple, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" And they were angry.
"Do you hear what these children are saying?" they asked him. "Yes," replied Jesus. "Have you never read, 'You have taught children and babies to praise you perfectly'?"
Then he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where he spent the night.
Early in the morning, as Jesus was on his way back to the city, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree by the road. He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. Then he said to it, "May you never produce fruit again!" Straight away the tree dried up.
When the followers saw this, they were amazed. "How did the fig tree dry up so quickly?" they asked.

Jesus replied, "I tell you for certain, if you have faith and do not doubt, you can do what was done to the fig tree. And you can do even more. You can say to this mountain, 'Go and throw yourself into the sea,' and it will happen.
If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer."

Jesus went into the temple. While he was teaching there, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him. "By what authority are you doing these things?" they asked. "And who gave you this authority?"
Jesus replied, "I will also ask you one question. If you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
Where did John's baptism come from? Was it from heaven, or from people?" They talked about it among themselves. They said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'From people,' we are afraid of the crowd, because they all believe that John was a prophet."
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." Then he said, "Then I will not tell you by what authority I am doing these things either.
"What do you think about this? A man had two sons. He went to the first one and said, 'Son, go and work in the vineyard today.'
"'I will not,' the son answered. But later he changed his mind and went.
"Then the father went to the other son and said the same thing. He answered, 'I will, sir,' but he did not go.

"Which of the two sons did what his father wanted?" "The first," they answered. Jesus said to them, "I tell you for certain, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God ahead of you.

John came to show you the right way to live, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and the prostitutes did believe him. Even after you saw this, you did not change your minds and believe him.

"Listen to another story. There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it and built a lookout tower. Then he rented the vineyard to some farmers and went away on a journey.
When harvest time came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit.
"But the farmers grabbed his servants. They beat one, killed another and threw stones at a third.
Then he sent other servants to them, more than the first time. The farmers treated them the same way.
Last of all, he sent his son to them. 'They will respect my son,' he said.
"But when the farmers saw the son, they said to each other, 'This is the one who will own the vineyard one day. Come, let's kill him and take what he would have owned.'
So they took him, threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
"So when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?"
They answered, "He will put those evil men to a terrible death. Then he will rent the vineyard to other farmers, who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time."
Jesus said to them, "Have you never read this in the Scriptures: 'The stone the builders rejected has become the most important stone of all. The Lord has done this, and it is wonderful to see'?
"So I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you. It will be given to a people who will produce its fruit.
Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces. And anyone it falls on will be crushed to dust."
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard Jesus' stories, they knew he was talking about them.
They looked for a way to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowds, because the people believed that Jesus was a prophet.
Jesus spoke to them again using stories. He said,
"The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his servants to the people who had been invited, to tell them to come to the feast. But they refused to come.

"Then he sent some more servants. He said, 'Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My bulls and fattened calves have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast!'
"But they paid no attention and went off, one to his field and another to his business.
The rest grabbed his servants, treated them badly and killed them.
The king was furious. He sent his army to destroy those murderers and burn their city.
"Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding feast is ready, but the people I invited did not deserve to come.
So go to the street corners and invite everyone you find to the feast.'
So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both bad and good. And the wedding hall was filled with guests.
"But when the king came in to see the guests, he noticed a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.
He asked him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?' The man had nothing to say.
"Then the king told the servants, 'Tie him up hand and foot, and throw him outside into the darkness. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'
"Many are invited, but few are chosen."
Then the Pharisees went out and made plans to trap Jesus with his own words.

They sent their followers to him, along with some supporters of Herod. They said, "Teacher, we know that you are honest. You teach the way of God truthfully. You do not let others change your mind, because you pay no attention to how important people are.
So tell us what you think. Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
But Jesus knew their evil plans. He said, "You hypocrites! Why are you trying to trap me?
Show me the coin used for paying the tax." They brought him a silver coin.
He asked them, "Whose picture and name are on this coin?"
"Caesar's," they replied. Then he said to them, "So give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to God what belongs to God."
When they heard this, they were amazed. So they left him and went away.
That same day some Sadducees came to Jesus. They say that people do not rise from the dead. They asked him a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses told us that if a man dies without having children, his brother must marry the widow and have children for him.
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died. Since he had no children, he left his wife to his brother.
The same thing happened to the second brother and the third, all the way to the seventh.
Last of all, the woman died.
So when the dead rise, whose wife will she be of the seven? All of them were married to her."
Jesus replied, "You are wrong because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
When the dead rise, they will not marry, and they will not be given in marriage. They will be like the angels in heaven.
But about the dead rising, have you not read what God said to you?
He said, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.' He is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had left the Sadducees with nothing to say, they got together.
One of them, an expert in the law, tested him with a question.
"Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?"
Jesus replied, "'Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul and with all your mind.'
This is the first and greatest commandment.
And the second is like it: 'Love your neighbour as you love yourself.'
All the Law and the Prophets are based on these two commandments."
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question.
"What do you think about the Christ?" he asked. "Whose son is he?" "The son of David," they replied.
He said to them, "Then why does David, speaking by the Holy Spirit, call him 'Lord'? David says,
'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right side until I put your enemies under your feet."'
If David calls him 'Lord', how can he be David's son?"
No one could say a word in reply. And from that day on, no one dared to ask him any more questions.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his followers.
He said, "The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. They have the job of explaining Moses' Law.
So be careful to do everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, because they do not practise what they teach.
They tie up heavy loads that are hard to carry and put them on other people's shoulders. But they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to help carry them.
"Everything they do is done for people to see. They make the little boxes of Scripture they wear on their foreheads and arms extra wide, and they make the tassels on their clothes extra long.
They love to have the place of honour at dinners and the most important seats in the synagogues.
They love to be greeted with respect in the market places, and to have people call them 'Rabbi'.
"But you should not be called 'Rabbi'. You have only one Teacher, the Christ, and you are all brothers and sisters.
And do not call anyone on earth 'father', because you have one Father, and he is in heaven.
And you should not be called 'master', because you have one Master, the Christ.
The greatest among you will be your servant.
Whoever lifts themselves up will be made humble, and whoever makes themselves humble will be lifted up.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You take away widows' houses, and then you say long prayers to make yourselves look good. So you will be punished even more.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the door of the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. You yourselves do not go in, and you will not let those who are trying to go in enter.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel over land and sea to win a single follower. And when you have won them, you make them twice as fit for hell as you are.
"How terrible it will be for you, blind guides! You say, 'If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing. But anyone who swears by the gold of the temple must keep their promise.'
You blind fools! Which is more important, the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy?
You also say, 'If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing. But anyone who swears by the gift on the altar must keep their promise.'
You blind people! Which is more important, the gift, or the altar that makes the gift holy?
So anyone who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
And anyone who swears by the temple swears by it and by God, who lives in it.
And anyone who swears by heaven swears by God's throne and by God, who sits on it.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give God a tenth of your spices, like mint, dill and cumin. But you have ignored the more important things in the Law, which are justice, mercy and faithfulness. You should have done these things, without ignoring the others.
You blind guides! You strain a tiny fly out of your drink, but you swallow a whole camel!
"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of a cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and selfishness.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, and then the outside will also be clean.

"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like tombs that have been painted white. They look beautiful on the outside, but inside they are full of dead people's bones and everything that is unclean.
In the same way, on the outside you seem to be good people. But on the inside you are full of pretending and evil.
"How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets, and you decorate the graves of good people.
And you say, 'If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have helped them kill the prophets.'
So you are admitting that you are the children of the people who murdered the prophets.
Go on, then, and finish what your ancestors started!
"You snakes! You family of snakes! How will you escape being sentenced to hell?
So I am sending you prophets, wise men and teachers. You will kill some of them and nail some to crosses. You will whip others in your synagogues and chase them from town to town.

And so you will be guilty of the blood of all the good people that has been spilled on earth. This goes from the blood of good Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berekiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
I tell you for certain, all this will come on the people of today.

"Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and throw stones at those God sends to you. Many times I have wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you were not willing!
Look, your house is left empty.
I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
Jesus left the temple and was walking away when his followers came up to him. They wanted to point out to him the buildings of the temple.
"Do you see all these things?" Jesus asked. "I tell you for certain, not one stone here will be left on top of another. Every one of them will be thrown down."

Later, Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives. The followers came to him in private and said, "Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the world?"
Jesus answered, "Be careful that no one fools you.
