Many will come using my name and saying, 'I am the Christ.' They will fool many people.
You will hear about wars, and stories about wars. Make sure you are not alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.
Nation will fight against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be times when there is no food, and there will be diseases and earthquakes in many places.
All these are the beginning of the pains, like the first pains of a woman giving birth.
"Then you will be handed over to be treated badly and put to death. All nations will hate you because of me.
At that time many will give up their faith. They will hand each other over to their enemies and hate each other.
Many false prophets will appear and fool many people.
Because evil will spread more and more, the love of most people will grow cold.
But whoever keeps going until the end will be saved.
And this good news about the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a witness to all nations. Then the end will come.
"The prophet Daniel spoke about 'the hateful thing that causes ruin'. One day you will see it standing in the holy place. Let the reader understand this.
When that happens, those who are in Judea must escape to the mountains.
No one on the roof of their house should go down to take anything out of the house.
No one in the field should go back to get their coat.
How terrible it will be in those days for women who are pregnant or feeding their babies!
Pray that you will not have to escape in winter or on a Sabbath.
At that time there will be terrible suffering. It will be worse than anything that has happened from the beginning of the world until now, and nothing like it will ever happen again.
If those days had not been cut short, no one would survive. But for the sake of God's chosen people, those days will be cut short.
"At that time if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ!' or, 'There he is!' do not believe it.
False christs and false prophets will appear. They will do great signs and wonders to fool even God's chosen people, if that were possible.
Remember, I have told you ahead of time.
"So if anyone tells you, 'He is out in the desert,' do not go out there. Or if they say, 'He is here, in the inner rooms,' do not believe it.
Lightning flashes in the east and can be seen all the way to the west. That is how it will be when the Son of Man comes.
Wherever there is a dead body, the vultures will gather.
"Straight after the suffering of those days, 'the sun will be made dark, and the moon will not give its light. The stars will fall from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.'
"Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. All the peoples of the earth will be very sad. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky, with power and great glory.
He will send out his angels with a loud trumpet call. They will gather his chosen people from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
"Learn this lesson from the fig tree. When its branches become soft and its leaves come out, you know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see all these things, you will know that he is near, right at the door.
I tell you for certain, the people of this time will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
"But no one knows the day or the hour when it will happen. Not even the angels in heaven know. Only the Father knows.
"When the Son of Man comes, it will be like it was in the days of Noah.
In the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, and marrying and giving their daughters in marriage, right up to the day Noah went into the ark.
They knew nothing about what would happen until the flood came and took them all away. That is how it will be when the Son of Man comes.
Two men will be working in a field. One will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding grain. One will be taken and the other left.
"So keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord will come.
But understand this. If the owner of the house had known at what time of night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch. He would not have let his house be broken into.
So you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at a time when you do not expect him.
"Who then is the faithful and wise servant? He is the one the master has put in charge of the servants in his house, to give them their food at the right time.
That servant will be blessed if his master finds him doing his job when he comes back.
I tell you for certain, the master will put him in charge of everything he owns.
But suppose that servant is evil. He says to himself, 'My master is staying away a long time.'
Then he begins to beat the other servants, and to eat and drink with people who get drunk.
The master of that servant will come back on a day when he does not expect him, and at a time he does not know.
The master will cut him to pieces and send him to the place where the hypocrites go. There people will cry and grind their teeth."
"At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young bridesmaids. They took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
The foolish ones took their lamps, but they did not take any extra oil with them.
The wise ones took oil in jars along with their lamps.
The bridegroom was a long time in coming, and they all became sleepy and fell asleep.
"At midnight someone shouted, 'Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!'
"Then all the bridesmaids woke up and got their lamps ready.
The foolish ones said to the wise ones, 'Give us some of your oil. Our lamps are going out.'
"'No,' they replied. 'There may not be enough for both us and you. Go to the people who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.'
"So they went to buy the oil. But while they were away, the bridegroom arrived. The bridesmaids who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
"Later the other bridesmaids also came. 'Lord, Lord,' they said, 'open the door for us!'
"But he replied, 'I tell you for certain, I do not know you.'
"So keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour when the Son of Man will come.
"It will also be like a man who was going on a journey. He called his servants and put them in charge of his money.
He gave five bags of gold to one, two bags of gold to another, and one bag of gold to another. He gave each of them as much as he knew they could handle. Then he went on his journey.
The servant who had received five bags of gold went straight away and used the money to trade. He earned five more bags.
In the same way, the one with two bags of gold earned two more.
But the servant who had received one bag went and dug a hole in the ground and hid his master's money.
"After a long time the master of those servants came back, and he settled accounts with them.
The servant who had received five bags of gold brought the other five. 'Master,' he said, 'you trusted me with five bags of gold. Look, I have earned five more.'
"His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things. I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!'
"The servant with two bags of gold also came. 'Master,' he said, 'you trusted me with two bags of gold. Look, I have earned two more.'
"His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things. I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!'

"Then the servant who had received one bag of gold came. 'Master,' he said, 'I knew that you are a hard man. You harvest where you have not planted, and you gather crops where you have not scattered seed.
So I was afraid. I went out and hid your gold in the ground. Here is what belongs to you.'
"His master replied, 'You evil, lazy servant! So you knew that I harvest where I have not planted and gather crops where I have not scattered seed?
Then you should have put my money in the bank. When I came back, I would have received it back with interest.
"'Take the bag of gold from him, and give it to the one who has ten bags.
Everyone who has something will be given more, and they will have plenty. But whoever does not have anything, even what they have will be taken away from them.
Throw that useless servant outside into the darkness. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'
"When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, he will sit on his glorious throne.
All the nations will be gathered in front of him. He will separate the people into two groups, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
"Then the King will say to those on his right, 'Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you since the world was made.
I was hungry, and you gave me something to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger, and you invited me in.
I needed clothes, and you gave them to me. I was ill, and you took care of me. I was in prison, and you came to visit me.'
"Then the people who did what was right will answer him, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?
When did we see you as a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and give them to you?
When did we see you ill or in prison and go to visit you?'
"The King will reply, 'I tell you for certain, whatever you did for one of the least important of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.'
"Then he will say to those on his left, 'Get away from me, you who are cursed! Go into the fire that burns for ever, which has been prepared for the devil and his angels.
I was hungry, and you gave me nothing to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not invite me in. I needed clothes, and you did not give me any. I was ill and in prison, and you did not take care of me.'
"They also will answer, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or needing clothes, or ill, or in prison, and did not help you?'
"He will reply, 'I tell you for certain, whatever you did not do for one of the least important of these, you did not do for me.'
"Then they will go away to be punished for ever, but the people who did what was right will go to eternal life."
When Jesus had finished saying all these things, he said to his followers,
"As you know, the Passover festival is two days away. The Son of Man will be handed over to be nailed to a cross."
Then the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders of the people met in the palace of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas.
They made a plan to arrest Jesus in a secret way and kill him.
"But not during the festival," they said, "or the people may start a riot."
Jesus was in Bethany, in the home of a man known as Simon the leper.
A woman came to him with a beautiful jar of very expensive perfume. She poured it on his head while he was sitting at the table.
When the followers saw this, they were angry. "Why this waste?" they asked.
"This perfume could have been sold for a lot of money, and the money given to poor people."
Jesus knew what they were saying, and he said to them, "Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
You will always have poor people with you, but you will not always have me.
When she poured this perfume on my body, she did it to prepare me for my burial.
I tell you for certain, wherever this good news is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, so that people will remember her."
Then one of the twelve followers, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests.
He asked, "What will you give me if I hand him over to you?" So they counted out for him thirty silver coins.
From then on, Judas watched for a chance to hand Jesus over to them.
On the first day of the Festival of Bread Made Without Yeast, the followers came to Jesus. They asked, "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?"
He replied, "Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, 'The Teacher says: My time is near. I am going to celebrate the Passover with my followers at your house.'"
So the followers did what Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, Jesus was at the table with the twelve followers.
While they were eating, he said, "I tell you for certain, one of you will hand me over to my enemies."
They were very sad. One after the other they began to say to him, "Surely you do not mean me, Lord?"
Jesus replied, "The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with me will hand me over.
The Son of Man will go, just as it is written about him. But how terrible it will be for the man who hands over the Son of Man! It would be better for him if he had never been born."
Then Judas, the one who would hand him over, said, "Surely you do not mean me, Rabbi?" Jesus answered, "You have said so."
While they were eating, Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke it and gave it to his followers. He said, "Take this and eat it. This is my body."
Then he took the cup and gave thanks, and he gave it to them. He said, "All of you drink from it.
This is my blood of the new covenant. It is poured out for many people so that their sins can be forgiven.
I tell you, I will not drink wine again from now on until the day I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom."
When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus told them, "This very night you will all run away and leave me. It is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
But after I have been raised to life, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Peter replied, "Even if all the others run away because of you, I never will."
"I tell you for certain," Jesus answered, "this very night, before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know me."
But Peter said, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I do not know you." And all the other followers said the same.
Then Jesus went with his followers to a place called Gethsemane. He said to them, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him. He began to feel very sad and troubled.
Then he said to them, "My soul is so full of sadness that I feel close to death. Stay here and keep watch with me."
He went a little further and fell with his face to the ground. He prayed, "My Father, if it is possible, take this cup of suffering away from me. But let what you want be done, not what I want."
Then he went back to his followers and found them sleeping. "Could you not keep watch with me for one hour?" he asked Peter.
"Keep watch and pray, so that you will not give in to temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak."
He went away a second time and prayed, "My Father, if this cup cannot be taken away unless I drink it, may what you want be done."
When he came back, he again found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy.
So he left them and went away once more. He prayed the third time, saying the same thing.
Then he came back to the followers and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the time has come. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.
Get up! Let's go! Here comes the man who is handing me over!"
While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived. With him was a large crowd carrying swords and clubs. They had been sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
The man who was handing Jesus over had arranged a signal with them. "The one I kiss is the man," he had said. "Arrest him."
Going straight to Jesus, Judas said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed him.
Jesus replied, "Friend, do what you came for." Then the men stepped forward, grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
At that moment one of Jesus' companions reached for his sword and pulled it out. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
"Put your sword back in its place," Jesus said to him. "All who use the sword will die by the sword.
Do you think I cannot ask my Father for help? He would send me more than twelve armies of angels straight away.
But then how would the Scriptures come true that say it must happen this way?"
At that time Jesus said to the crowd, "Am I leading a rebellion, that you have come out with swords and clubs to capture me? Every day I sat in the temple courts teaching, and you did not arrest me.
But all this has happened so that the words of the prophets in the Scriptures would come true." Then all the followers left him and ran away.
The men who had arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest. The teachers of the law and the elders had gathered there.
But Peter followed him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. He went in and sat down with the guards to see what would happen.
The chief priests and the whole council were looking for false evidence against Jesus, so that they could put him to death.
But they did not find any, even though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two men came forward.
They said, "This man said, 'I can destroy the temple of God and build it again in three days.'"
Then the high priest stood up and said to Jesus, "Are you not going to answer? What is this these men are saying against you?"
But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest said to him, "I order you to swear by the living God and tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God."
"You have said so," Jesus replied. "But I tell all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven."
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, "He has insulted God! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard him insult God.
What do you think?" "He deserves to die!" they answered.
Then they spat in his face and hit him with their fists. Others slapped him
and said, "Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit you?"
Peter was sitting out in the courtyard. A servant girl came to him. "You also were with Jesus of Galilee," she said.
But he denied it in front of all of them. "I do not know what you are talking about," he said.
Then he went out to the gateway, where another servant girl saw him. She said to the people there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."
He denied it again and swore, "I do not know the man!"
After a little while, those standing there went up to Peter. "You must be one of them," they said. "The way you talk gives you away."
Then he began to call down curses on himself, and he swore to them, "I do not know the man!" Straight away a rooster crowed.
Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said: "Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know me." And he went outside and cried bitterly.
Early in the morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the people made their plans to have Jesus put to death.
They tied him up, led him away and handed him over to Pilate, the governor.
Judas, who had handed Jesus over, saw that Jesus had been sentenced to death. He was filled with regret, and he brought the thirty silver coins back to the chief priests and the elders.
He said, "I have sinned. I have handed over an innocent man to be killed." "What do we care?" they replied. "That is your problem."
So Judas threw the money into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests picked up the coins. They said, "It is against the law to put this money into the temple treasury, because it is money paid for blood."
So they decided to use the money to buy the potter's field, as a place to bury people who were not from there.
That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
Then what the prophet Jeremiah had said came true: "They took the thirty silver coins, the price the people of Israel had set on him.
And they used them to buy the potter's field, as the Lord had commanded me."
Meanwhile Jesus stood in front of the governor. The governor asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" "You have said so," Jesus replied.
When the chief priests and the elders accused him, he did not answer.
Then Pilate asked him, "Do you not hear all the things they are accusing you of?"
But Jesus did not answer even one question, and the governor was very amazed.
It was the governor's custom at the festival to set free one prisoner chosen by the crowd.
At that time they had a well-known prisoner named Barabbas.
So when the crowd had gathered, Pilate asked them, "Which one do you want me to set free for you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called the Christ?"
He knew it was because they were jealous that the leaders had handed Jesus over to him.
While Pilate was sitting in the judge's seat, his wife sent him a message. It said, "Do not have anything to do with that innocent man. I have suffered a great deal today in a dream because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders talked the crowd into asking for Barabbas and having Jesus put to death.
"Which of the two do you want me to set free for you?" asked the governor. "Barabbas," they answered.
"Then what should I do with Jesus who is called the Christ?" Pilate asked. They all answered, "Nail him to a cross!"
"Why? What wrong has he done?" asked Pilate. But they shouted even louder, "Nail him to a cross!"

Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere, and that a riot was starting. So he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. "I am not guilty of this man's death," he said. "It is your responsibility!"
All the people answered, "Let the blame for his death be on us and on our children!"
Then Pilate set Barabbas free for them. He had Jesus whipped, and then he handed him over to be nailed to a cross.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the governor's palace. The whole company of soldiers gathered around him.
They took off his clothes and put a red robe on him.
Then they twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head. They put a stick in his right hand. Then they knelt in front of him and made fun of him. "Hail, king of the Jews!" they said.
They spat on him. They took the stick and hit him on the head again and again.
After they had made fun of him, they took off the robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him away to nail him to a cross.
As they were going out, they met a man from Cyrene named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which means the Place of the Skull.
There they offered Jesus wine to drink, mixed with a bitter liquid. But after tasting it, he refused to drink it.
When they had nailed him to the cross, they divided up his clothes by throwing dice.
Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.
Above his head they put up the written charge against him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Two robbers were nailed to crosses with him, one on his right and one on his left.
People who passed by shouted insults at him, shaking their heads.
They said, "You were going to destroy the temple and build it again in three days. So save yourself! Come down from the cross, if you are the Son of God!"
In the same way the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders made fun of him.
"He saved others," they said, "but he cannot save himself! He is the king of Israel! Let him come down now from the cross, and then we will believe in him.
He trusts in God. Let God rescue him now if he wants him. After all, he said, 'I am the Son of God.'"
In the same way, the robbers who were on crosses next to him also insulted him.
From twelve o'clock until three o'clock in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
At about three o'clock Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?" This means, "My God, my God, why have you left me all alone?"
Some of the people standing there heard this. They said, "He is calling for Elijah."
Straight away one of them ran and got a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a stick and offered it to Jesus to drink.
The rest said, "Leave him alone. Let's see if Elijah comes to save him."
Jesus cried out again in a loud voice, and he gave up his spirit.
At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.
Tombs broke open, and the bodies of many of God's people who had died were raised to life.
They came out of the tombs after Jesus rose from the dead. They went into the holy city and appeared to many people.
The Roman officer and the soldiers who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and everything that had happened. They were terrified and said, "He really was the Son of God!"
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to take care of his needs.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
As evening came, a rich man from Arimathea arrived. His name was Joseph, and he had also become a follower of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out of the rock. He rolled a big stone in front of the entrance to the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there across from the tomb.
The next day, the day after Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees went to Pilate.
"Sir," they said, "we remember that while that liar was still alive he said, 'After three days I will rise again.'

So give the order to make the tomb secure until the third day. If you do not, his followers may come and steal the body. Then they will tell the people that he has been raised from the dead. This last lie will be worse than the first."
"Take some guards," Pilate answered. "Go and make the tomb as secure as you know how."
So they went and made the tomb secure. They put a seal on the stone and placed guards there.
After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb.
Suddenly there was a powerful earthquake. An angel of the Lord came down from heaven, went to the tomb, rolled back the stone and sat on it.
He shone like lightning, and his clothes were as white as snow.
The guards were so afraid of him that they shook and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was nailed to the cross.
He is not here! He has risen, just as he said he would. Come and see the place where the Lord lay.
Then go quickly and tell his followers, 'He has risen from the dead. He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him.' Now I have told you."
So the women hurried away from the tomb. They were afraid, but they were filled with great joy. They ran to tell his followers.
Suddenly Jesus met them. "Greetings," he said. They came to him, took hold of his feet and worshipped him.
Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee. There they will see me."
While the women were on their way, some of the guards went into the city. They told the chief priests everything that had happened.
The chief priests met with the elders and made a plan. They gave the soldiers a large amount of money.
They told them, "You must say, 'His followers came during the night and stole his body while we were sleeping.'
If the governor hears about this, we will talk to him and keep you out of trouble."
So the soldiers took the money and did as they were told. And this story has been spread among the Jewish people to this very day.
Then the eleven followers went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
When they saw him, they worshipped him, but some still had doubts.
Then Jesus came to them and said, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
So go and make followers of all nations. Baptise them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
Teach them to obey everything I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the very end of the world." Amen.
Mark: This is the beginning of the good news about Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
It began just as the prophet Isaiah wrote: "Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you. He will get your road ready.
He is the voice of someone shouting in the desert, 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make straight paths for him!'"
And so John came, baptising people in the desert. He preached that people should be baptised to show they had turned away from their sins, so that God would forgive them.
People from the whole area of Judea and everyone from Jerusalem went out to him. They told about their sins, and John baptised them in the Jordan River.
John wore clothes made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
He preached, "Someone more powerful than I am is coming after me. I am not good enough even to bend down and untie his sandals.
I baptise you with water, but he will baptise you with the Holy Spirit."
At that time Jesus came from the town of Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptised him in the Jordan River.
As Jesus was coming up out of the water, he saw heaven open, and the Spirit coming down on him like a dove.
A voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, and I love you. I am very pleased with you."
Straight away the Spirit sent Jesus out into the desert.
He was in the desert for forty days, and Satan tempted him. He was with the wild animals, and angels took care of him.
After John was put in prison, Jesus went into Galilee and preached the good news from God.
He said, "The time has come. The kingdom of God is near! Turn away from your sins and believe the good news!"
As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the lake, because they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, "Come, follow me, and I will teach you to fish for people."
Straight away they left their nets and followed him.
He went on a little further and saw James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John. They were in their boat, fixing their nets.
Straight away Jesus called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, and they followed Jesus.
They went to the town of Capernaum. When the Sabbath day came, Jesus went into the synagogue and began to teach.
The people were amazed at his teaching, because he taught them like someone who had authority, not like the teachers of the law.
Just then a man with an evil spirit was in their synagogue. He shouted,
"What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the Holy One of God!"
Jesus spoke firmly to the spirit. "Be quiet!" he said. "Come out of him!"
The evil spirit shook the man hard and came out of him with a loud scream.
All the people were so amazed that they asked each other, "What is this? It is a new teaching, and he teaches with authority! He even gives orders to evil spirits, and they obey him!"
News about Jesus quickly spread everywhere in the whole area around Galilee.
As soon as they left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
Simon's mother-in-law was lying in bed with a fever, and they told Jesus about her straight away.
He went to her, took her hand and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began to serve them.
That evening, after the sun went down, people brought to Jesus all who were sick and all who had demons in them.
The whole town gathered at the door.
Jesus healed many people who had all kinds of sicknesses. He also drove out many demons. But he did not let the demons speak, because they knew who he was.
Very early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and left the house. He went to a quiet place, and there he prayed.
Simon and his friends went to look for him.
When they found him, they said, "Everyone is looking for you!"
Jesus answered, "Let us go somewhere else, to the nearby towns, so that I can preach there too. That is why I have come."
So he travelled all over Galilee. He preached in their synagogues and drove out demons.
A man with a skin disease came to Jesus. He knelt down and begged him, "If you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus felt sorry for the man. He reached out his hand and touched him. "I am willing," he said. "Be clean!"
Straight away the skin disease left the man, and he was clean.
Jesus sent him away at once with a strong warning.
He said, "Do not tell anyone about this. But go and show yourself to the priest. Offer the gifts that Moses commanded for people who are made clean. This will show everyone that you are healed."

But the man went out and began to talk freely, spreading the news everywhere. Because of this, Jesus could no longer go into a town openly. He stayed outside in quiet places. But people still came to him from everywhere.
A few days later, Jesus went back to Capernaum. People heard that he had come home.
So many people gathered that there was no room left, not even outside the door. And Jesus taught them God's message.
Then four men came, carrying a man who could not move his body.
They could not get him close to Jesus because of the crowd. So they made a hole in the roof above Jesus. Then they let the man down through the hole, lying on his mat.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man, "Son, your sins are forgiven."
Some teachers of the law were sitting there. They thought to themselves,
"Why does this man talk like that? He is insulting God! Only God can forgive sins!"
Straight away Jesus knew in his spirit what they were thinking. He said to them, "Why are you thinking these things?
Which is easier to say to this man? Is it easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven'? Or to say, 'Get up, pick up your mat and walk'?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." So he said to the man,
"I tell you, get up, pick up your mat and go home."
The man got up, picked up his mat straight away and walked out while everyone watched. They were all amazed, and they praised God. They said, "We have never seen anything like this!"
Jesus went out beside the lake again. A large crowd came to him, and he began to teach them.
As he walked along, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office. "Follow me," Jesus said to him. Levi got up and followed him.
Later, Jesus was having a meal at Levi's house. Many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and his followers, because many of them followed him.
Some teachers of the law who were Pharisees saw him eating with sinners and tax collectors. They asked his followers, "Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"

Jesus heard this and said to them, "People who are healthy do not need a doctor. Sick people do. I have not come to call people who think they are good. I have come to call sinners to turn away from their sins."
John's followers and the Pharisees were fasting. Some people came and asked Jesus, "John's followers and the followers of the Pharisees are fasting. Why are your followers not fasting?"
Jesus answered, "How can the guests at a wedding fast while the bridegroom is with them? They cannot fast while he is still with them.
But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast.
"No one sews a patch of new cloth on old clothes. If they do, the new patch will shrink and pull away from the old cloth. Then the hole will be worse.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the skins will be ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins."
One Sabbath day Jesus was walking through the grain fields. As his followers walked along, they began to pick some ears of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, "Look! Why are they doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered, "Have you never read what David did when he and his men were hungry and needed food?
When Abiathar was the high priest, David went into the house of God and ate the holy bread. Only priests were allowed to eat it. And he also gave some to his men."
Then Jesus said to them, "The Sabbath was made for people. People were not made for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
Another time Jesus went into the synagogue. A man with a shrivelled hand was there.
Some people were watching Jesus closely to see if he would heal the man on the Sabbath. They wanted a reason to accuse him.
Jesus said to the man with the shrivelled hand, "Stand up here in front of everyone."
Then he asked them, "Which is allowed on the Sabbath, to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?" But they said nothing.

Jesus looked around at them in anger. He was very sad because their hearts were so hard. He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man stretched it out, and his hand was healed and made as good as the other.
Then the Pharisees went out and straight away began to make plans with Herod's supporters about how they could kill Jesus.
Jesus went away with his followers to the lake, and a large crowd from Galilee followed. People also came from Judea,
from Jerusalem, from Idumea, from the other side of the Jordan River and from around Tyre and Sidon. A large crowd came to him because they heard about all the things he was doing.
Because of the crowd, Jesus told his followers to have a small boat ready for him, so that the people would not crush him.
He had healed many people, so all who were sick kept pushing forward to touch him.
Whenever evil spirits saw him, they fell down in front of him and shouted, "You are the Son of God!"
But Jesus gave them strict orders not to tell anyone who he was.
Jesus went up on a mountain and called to him the men he wanted, and they came to him.
He chose twelve of them to be with him, so that he could send them out to preach.
He also gave them authority to heal sicknesses and to drive out demons.
These are the twelve he chose: Simon, whom he gave the name Peter,
James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John. Jesus gave these two the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder".
Then there were Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James, the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
and Judas Iscariot, who later handed Jesus over to his enemies. Then Jesus went into a house.
Again a crowd gathered, so that Jesus and his followers could not even eat.
When his family heard about this, they went to take charge of him. They said, "He has gone mad."
The teachers of the law who came down from Jerusalem said, "He has Beelzebul in him! He drives out demons by the power of the ruler of the demons."
So Jesus called them to him and spoke to them using stories. "How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom fights against itself, that kingdom cannot last.
If a family fights against itself, that family cannot last.
And if Satan fights against himself and is divided, he cannot last. His end has come.
No one can go into a strong man's house and steal his things unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can rob his house.
I tell you for certain, people will be forgiven all their sins and all the evil things they say against God.
But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven. They are guilty of a sin that lasts for ever."
Jesus said this because they were saying, "He has an evil spirit."
Then Jesus' mother and brothers came. They stood outside and sent someone in to call him.
A crowd was sitting around Jesus. They told him, "Your mother and brothers and sisters are outside looking for you."
"Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?" Jesus asked.
Then he looked at the people sitting in a circle around him. He said, "Here are my mother and my brothers!
Anyone who does what God wants is my brother and sister and mother."
Again Jesus began to teach by the lake. The crowd around him was so large that he got into a boat on the lake and sat down. All the people stayed on the shore.
He taught them many things by using stories. In his teaching he said,
"Listen! A farmer went out to plant his seed.
As he was scattering the seed, some fell on the path, and the birds came and ate it up.
Some fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. It grew up quickly, because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun came up, the plants dried up. They withered because they had no roots.
Some seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked the plants, so they did not produce any grain.
But some seed fell on good soil. It grew up and produced a crop. Some plants produced thirty times more than was planted, some sixty times and some a hundred times."
Then Jesus said, "Whoever has ears should listen."
Later, when Jesus was alone, the twelve and the others around him asked him about the stories.
He told them, "You have been given the secret of the kingdom of God. But to people outside, everything is said in stories.
This is so that, 'They will look and look, but never see. They will listen and listen, but never understand. If they did, they might turn to God and be forgiven.'"
Then Jesus said to them, "Do you not understand this story? Then how will you understand any of the stories?
The farmer plants God's message.
Some people are like the seed on the path, where the message is planted. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the message that was planted in them.
Others are like the seed planted on rocky ground. They hear the message and straight away accept it with joy.
But they have no roots, so they last only a short time. When trouble or hard times come because of the message, they quickly give up.
Others are like the seed planted among thorns. They hear the message,
but the worries of this life, the false promise of riches and the wish for other things come in and choke the message. So it produces no fruit.
Others are like the seed planted on good soil. They hear the message, accept it and produce a crop. Some produce thirty times more than was planted, some sixty times and some a hundred times."
Jesus said to them, "Do you bring in a lamp to put it under a bowl or under a bed? No, you put it on a stand.
Whatever is hidden is meant to be shown. Whatever is secret is meant to be brought out into the open.
Whoever has ears should listen."
He went on, "Think carefully about what you hear. The same amount you give to others will be given back to you, and even more.
Whoever has something will be given more. But whoever does not have anything, even what they have will be taken away from them."
Jesus also said, "The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
Night and day, while he sleeps and while he is awake, the seed comes up and grows. But he does not know how it happens.
The soil makes the grain grow all by itself. First the stalk comes up, then the head, and then the full grain in the head.
As soon as the grain is ripe, he cuts it with his sickle, because the time to harvest has come."
Jesus said again, "What can we say the kingdom of God is like? What story can we use to explain it?
It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all the seeds planted in the ground.
But when it is planted, it grows and becomes the largest of all garden plants. It grows such big branches that the birds can rest in its shade."
Jesus used many stories like these to teach the people God's message, as much as they could understand.
He did not say anything to them without using a story. But when he was alone with his own followers, he explained everything to them.
That day, when evening came, Jesus said to his followers, "Let us go over to the other side of the lake."
They left the crowd behind and took Jesus along in the boat he was already in. There were also other boats with him.
A very strong wind came up. The waves crashed over the boat, so that it was nearly filled with water.
Jesus was in the back of the boat, sleeping on a cushion. The followers woke him up and said, "Teacher, do you not care if we drown?"
Jesus got up and gave orders to the wind. He said to the waves, "Quiet! Be still!" Then the wind stopped, and it was completely calm.
He said to his followers, "Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?"
They were terrified and asked each other, "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!"
Jesus and his followers went across the lake to the area of the Gadarenes.
When Jesus got out of the boat, a man with an evil spirit came out from the tombs straight away to meet him.
This man lived among the tombs. No one could keep him tied up any more, not even with a chain.
People had often tied his hands and feet with chains, but he tore the chains apart and broke the irons on his feet. No one was strong enough to control him.
All night and all day he stayed among the tombs and in the hills. He kept screaming and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus far away, he ran and fell on his knees in front of him.
He shouted with a loud voice, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? In God's name, I beg you, do not hurt me!"
He said this because Jesus had said to him, "Come out of this man, you evil spirit!"
Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "My name is Legion," he answered, "because there are many of us."
And he begged Jesus again and again not to send them out of that area.
A large herd of pigs was feeding on the nearby hillside.
The demons begged Jesus, "Send us among the pigs. Let us go into them."
Jesus let them do it. The evil spirits came out of the man and went into the pigs. There were about two thousand pigs in the herd. The whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
The men looking after the pigs ran off. They told the news in the town and in the countryside. The people went out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been controlled by the many demons. He was sitting there, wearing clothes and thinking clearly. And the people were afraid.
Those who had seen it told the people what had happened to the man with the demons, and about the pigs.
Then the people began to beg Jesus to leave their area.
As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had had the demons begged to go with him.
But Jesus did not let him. He said, "Go home to your family and friends. Tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has been kind to you."
So the man went away and began to tell people in the Ten Towns how much Jesus had done for him. And all the people were amazed.
Jesus crossed over by boat to the other side of the lake again. A large crowd gathered around him while he was by the lake.
Then a man named Jairus came there. He was one of the leaders of the synagogue. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet.
He begged Jesus again and again, "My little daughter is dying. Please come and put your hands on her so that she will be healed and live."
So Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed and pushed against him from every side.
A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered a great deal, even though many doctors had treated her. She had spent all the money she had, but she was getting worse instead of better.
She had heard about Jesus. So she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
She thought, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Straight away her bleeding stopped. She felt in her body that she was free from her suffering.
At once Jesus knew that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"
His followers answered, "You see how the people are crowding against you. So how can you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
But Jesus kept looking around to see who had done it.
Then the woman came and fell at his feet. She was shaking with fear, because she knew what had happened to her. She told him the whole truth.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace. You are free from your suffering."
While Jesus was still speaking, some men came from the house of Jairus, the synagogue leader. "Your daughter is dead," they said. "Why bother the Teacher any more?"
Jesus heard what they said. He told the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid. Just believe."
He did not let anyone follow him except Peter, James and John, the brother of James.
They came to the home of the synagogue leader. There Jesus saw a lot of noise and confusion. People were crying and wailing loudly.
He went inside and said to them, "Why all this noise and crying? The child is not dead. She is only sleeping."
But they laughed at him. He sent them all outside. Then he took the child's father and mother and the followers who were with him, and he went in where the child was.
He took her by the hand and said to her, "Talitha koum!" This means, "Little girl, I tell you, get up!"
Straight away the girl stood up and began to walk around. She was twelve years old. When this happened, everyone was completely amazed.
Jesus gave strict orders not to let anyone know about this. And he told them to give her something to eat.
Jesus left there and went to his home town, and his followers went with him.

When the Sabbath day came, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many people who heard him were amazed. "Where did this man get these things?" they asked. "What is this wisdom he has been given? How can he do such powerful miracles?
Is he not the carpenter, the son of Mary? Is he not the brother of James, Joses, Judas and Simon? Are his sisters not here with us?" And they would not accept him.
Jesus said to them, "A prophet is respected everywhere except in his own town, among his own relatives and in his own home."
He could not do any powerful miracles there. He only put his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He was amazed that they had no faith. Then Jesus went around teaching from village to village.
He called the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two. He gave them authority over evil spirits.
He told them, "Take nothing for the journey except a walking stick. Take no bread, no bag and no money in your belts.
Wear sandals, but do not take an extra shirt."
He told them, "When you go into a house, stay there until you leave that town.

If any place will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave. This will be a warning to them. I tell you for certain, on the day of judgement it will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah than for that town."
So they went out and preached that people should turn away from their sins.
They drove out many demons. They poured olive oil on many sick people and healed them.
King Herod heard about this, because Jesus' name had become well known. Some people were saying, "John the Baptist has been raised from the dead! That is why he has the power to do these miracles."
Others said, "He is Elijah." Still others said, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of long ago."
But when Herod heard this, he said, "It is John, the man I had beheaded. He has been raised from the dead!"
Herod himself had given orders to have John arrested. He had him tied up and put in prison. He did this because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip. Herod had married her.
John had been saying to Herod, "It is against the law for you to have your brother's wife."
So Herodias hated John and wanted to kill him. But she could not,
because Herod was afraid of John. He knew that John was a good and holy man, so he kept him safe. When Herod heard John speak, he was very troubled, but he still liked to listen to him.
Finally the right time came for Herodias. On Herod's birthday he gave a big dinner for his high officials, his army leaders and the most important men in Galilee.
The daughter of Herodias came in and danced. She pleased Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl, "Ask me for anything you want, and I will give it to you."
He made a promise to her with an oath: "Anything you ask for I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."
She went out and said to her mother, "What should I ask for?" "The head of John the Baptist," her mother answered.
Straight away the girl hurried back to the king. She said, "I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a plate right now."
The king was very upset. But because of his oath and his dinner guests, he did not want to say no to her.
So straight away he sent a soldier with orders to bring John's head. The soldier went to the prison and cut off John's head.
He brought it back on a plate and gave it to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.
When John's followers heard about this, they came and took his body and put it in a tomb.
The apostles came back to Jesus. They told him all they had done and taught.
So many people were coming and going that they did not even have a chance to eat. So Jesus said to them, "Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest."
So they went away by themselves in a boat to a quiet place.
But many people saw them leaving and recognised them. They ran there on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.
When Jesus got out of the boat, he saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he began to teach them many things.
By that time it was late in the day. His followers came to him and said, "There is nothing here, and it is already very late.
Send the people away so that they can go to the nearby farms and villages and buy something to eat."
But Jesus answered, "You give them something to eat." They said to him, "That would take more than half a year's wages! Should we go and spend that much on bread and give it to them to eat?"
"How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Go and see." When they found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."
Then Jesus told them to make all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.
So they sat down in groups of a hundred and groups of fifty.

Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up to heaven and gave thanks, and he broke the loaves. Then he gave them to his followers to hand out to the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
The followers picked up twelve baskets full of pieces of bread and fish that were left over.
The number of men who had eaten was five thousand.
Straight away Jesus made his followers get into the boat and go on ahead of him to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.
After saying goodbye to them, he went up on a mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the lake, and Jesus was alone on land.
He saw his followers working hard at rowing, because the wind was blowing against them. Shortly before dawn he went out to them, walking on the lake. He was about to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the lake, they thought he was a ghost, and they screamed.
They all saw him and were terrified. Straight away he spoke to them and said, "Be brave! It is I. Do not be afraid."
Then he climbed into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were completely amazed.
They had not understood what the loaves meant. Their hearts were still hard.
They crossed over the lake and landed at Gennesaret. There they tied up the boat.
As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognised Jesus.
They ran through that whole area and began carrying sick people on mats to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went, into villages, towns or the countryside, they put the sick in the marketplaces. They begged him to let them touch just the edge of his clothes. And all who touched him were healed.
The Pharisees and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus.
They saw some of his followers eating food with hands that were "unclean", which means they had not washed them.
The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands in a special way. They do this to keep the old rules handed down by their leaders.
When they come from the market, they do not eat unless they wash first. And they keep many other rules too, such as washing cups, jugs, copper pots and couches.
So the Pharisees and the teachers of the law asked Jesus, "Why do your followers not live by the rules handed down by our leaders? Why do they eat their food with unclean hands?"
He answered them, "Isaiah was right when he spoke about you hypocrites. He wrote, 'These people honour me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me.
Their worship of me is worthless. Their teachings are only rules made up by people.'
You have let go of the commands of God, and you are holding on to rules made up by people. You wash jugs and cups, and you do many other things like that."
He said to them, "You are very good at setting aside the commands of God so that you can keep your own rules!
For Moses said, 'Honour your father and your mother.' He also said, 'Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death.'
But you say that a man can tell his father or mother, 'Whatever help you might have received from me is Corban.'" Corban means a gift set apart for God.
"Then you no longer let him do anything for his father or mother.
In this way you cancel the word of God by your own rules that you hand down. And you do many other things like that."
Again Jesus called the crowd to him. He said, "Listen to me, all of you, and understand this.
Nothing that goes into a person from the outside can make them unclean. It is what comes out of a person that makes them unclean.
Whoever has ears should listen."
Then he left the crowd and went into a house. His followers asked him about this saying.
"Do you not understand either?" he asked. "Do you not see that nothing going into a person from the outside can make them unclean?
It does not go into their heart. It goes into their stomach and then out of their body." When Jesus said this, he was showing that all foods are clean.
He went on, "What comes out of a person is what makes them unclean.
Evil thoughts come from the inside, from a person's heart. So do sexual sins, stealing, murder,
adultery, greed, evil acts, lying, wild living, jealousy, insulting others, pride and foolishness.
All these evil things come from the inside, and they make a person unclean."
Jesus left that place and went to the area of Tyre and Sidon. He went into a house and did not want anyone to know he was there. But he could not keep it a secret.
Soon a woman heard about him. Her little daughter had an evil spirit. She came and fell at his feet.
The woman was not Jewish. She was born in Syrian Phoenicia. She begged Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
Jesus said to her, "First let the children eat all they want. It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
"Yes, Lord," she replied. "But even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
Then he told her, "Because you said this, you may go home. The demon has left your daughter."
So she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.
Then Jesus left the area of Tyre and went through Sidon. He went down to the Sea of Galilee and into the area of the Ten Towns.
There some people brought a man to him who was deaf and could hardly talk. They begged Jesus to put his hand on the man.
Jesus took him away from the crowd, to be alone with him. He put his fingers into the man's ears. Then he spat and touched the man's tongue.
He looked up to heaven and took a deep breath. He said to the man, "Ephphatha!" This means, "Be opened!"
Straight away the man's ears were opened, his tongue was set free, and he began to speak clearly.
Jesus ordered the people not to tell anyone. But the more he told them not to, the more they kept talking about it.
People were completely amazed. "He has done everything well," they said. "He even makes deaf people hear, and people who cannot speak talk!"
During those days another large crowd gathered. They had nothing to eat. So Jesus called his followers to him and said,
"I feel sorry for these people. They have already been with me for three days, and they have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they will become weak on the way. Some of them have come from far away."
His followers answered him, "There is nothing here. Where can anyone get enough bread to feed them?"
"How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Seven," they replied.
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves and gave thanks. Then he broke them and gave them to his followers to hand out to the people, and they did so.
They also had a few small fish. Jesus gave thanks for them too, and told his followers to hand them out.
The people ate and were satisfied. Afterwards the followers picked up seven baskets of pieces that were left over.
About four thousand people were there. After Jesus sent them away,
he got into the boat with his followers straight away. He went to the area of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus. They wanted to test him, so they asked him for a sign from heaven.
He sighed deeply and said, "Why do the people of today ask for a sign? I tell you for certain, no sign will be given to them."
Then he left them, got back into the boat and crossed to the other side of the lake.
The followers had forgotten to bring bread. They had only one loaf with them in the boat.
Jesus warned them, "Be careful! Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod."
They talked about this with each other. They said, "He is saying this because we have no bread."
Jesus knew what they were saying. So he asked them, "Why are you talking about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Are your hearts still hard?
You have eyes, but can you not see? You have ears, but can you not hear? Do you not remember?
When I broke five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets of pieces did you pick up?" "Twelve," they answered.
"And when I broke seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets of pieces did you pick up?" "Seven," they answered.
He said to them, "Do you still not understand?"
They came to Bethsaida. Some people brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch the man.
Jesus took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spat on the man's eyes and put his hands on him. "Do you see anything?" Jesus asked.
The man looked up. He said, "I see people. They look like trees walking around."
Once more Jesus put his hands on the man's eyes. Then the man's eyes were opened, his sight came back, and he could see everything clearly.
Jesus sent him home and said, "Do not even go into the village."
Jesus and his followers went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked them, "Who do people say I am?"
They replied, "Some say John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. And still others say one of the prophets."
"But what about you?" he asked. "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ."
Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about him.

Then he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things. He said the elders, the chief priests and the teachers of the law would reject him. He must be killed, and after three days rise again.
He spoke about this plainly. Then Peter took him to one side and began to scold him.

But Jesus turned and looked at his followers. Then he scolded Peter. "Get behind me, Satan!" he said. "You are not thinking about the things God cares about. You are only thinking about the things people care about."
Jesus called the crowd to him along with his followers. He said, "Whoever wants to follow me must say no to themselves. They must pick up their cross and follow me.
Whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for me and for the good news will save it.
What good is it for someone to gain the whole world, but lose their own life?
What can anyone give in exchange for their life?

If anyone is ashamed of me and my words among these unfaithful and sinful people, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them. He will be ashamed of them when he comes in his Father's glory with the holy angels."
Jesus said to them, "I tell you for certain, some people standing here will not die before they see the kingdom of God come with power."
Six days later Jesus took Peter, James and John with him and led them up a high mountain, where they were all alone. There his appearance was changed in front of them.
His clothes became shining white, whiter than anyone in the world could ever wash them.
Then Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters, one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah."
Peter did not really know what to say, because they were all so afraid.
Then a cloud came and covered them. A voice came from the cloud: "This is my Son, and I love him. Listen to him!"
Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus gave them orders not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
So they kept the matter to themselves. But they asked each other what "rising from the dead" meant.
They asked him, "Why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?"
Jesus answered, "It is true that Elijah does come first, and he puts everything right again. Then why is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be treated as nothing?
But I tell you, Elijah has already come. And people did to him everything they wanted, just as it is written about him."
When they came back to the other followers, they saw a large crowd around them. Some teachers of the law were arguing with them.
As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with wonder, and they ran to greet him.
"What are you arguing with them about?" Jesus asked.
A man in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has an evil spirit that makes him unable to speak.

Whenever the spirit takes hold of him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth and becomes stiff. I asked your followers to drive out the spirit, but they could not do it."
Jesus answered, "You people who have no faith! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to me."
So they brought him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it straight away threw the boy into a fit. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy's father, "How long has this been happening to him?" "Since he was a child," he answered.
"It has often thrown him into fire or water to kill him. But if you can do anything, please feel sorry for us and help us."
Jesus said to him, "'If you can'? Everything is possible for the one who believes."
Straight away the boy's father cried out with tears, "I do believe! Help me to believe more!"

Jesus saw that a crowd was running to see what was happening. So he gave a strict order to the evil spirit. "You spirit that makes him deaf and unable to speak," he said, "I command you, come out of him and never go into him again!"
The spirit screamed and shook the boy violently. Then it came out of him. The boy looked so much like a dead body that many people said, "He is dead."
But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and the boy stood up.
After Jesus had gone indoors, his followers asked him in private, "Why could we not drive out the spirit?"
He replied, "This kind can only come out by prayer and fasting."
They left that place and passed through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,
because he was teaching his followers. He said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be handed over to people who will kill him. Three days after he is killed, he will rise again."
But they did not understand what he meant, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
They came to Capernaum. When Jesus was in the house, he asked them, "What were you arguing about on the road?"
But they kept quiet, because on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the most important.
Jesus sat down and called the twelve to him. He said, "Anyone who wants to be first must be the last of all, and the servant of all."
He took a little child and had the child stand among them. Then he took the child in his arms and said to them,
"Anyone who welcomes one of these little children in my name welcomes me. And anyone who welcomes me does not welcome only me. They also welcome the one who sent me."
John said to him, "Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name. We told him to stop, because he was not one of us."
"Do not stop him," Jesus said. "No one who does a miracle in my name can soon after say anything bad about me.
Anyone who is not against us is for us.
I tell you for certain, anyone who gives you a cup of water in my name because you belong to the Christ will certainly be rewarded.
"If anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for them to be thrown into the sea with a large millstone tied around their neck.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life with one hand than to go into hell with two hands, where the fire never goes out.
In hell 'the worms that eat them do not die, and the fire is never put out.'
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life with one foot than to have two feet and be thrown into hell, where the fire never goes out.
In hell 'the worms that eat them do not die, and the fire is never put out.'
If your eye causes you to sin, pull it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
In hell 'the worms that eat them do not die, and the fire is never put out.'
Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is good. But if it loses its saltiness, how can you make it salty again? Have salt among yourselves, and live in peace with each other."
Jesus left that place and went into the area of Judea and across the Jordan River. Again crowds of people came to him. As usual, he taught them.
Some Pharisees came to test him. They asked, "Is it right for a man to divorce his wife?"
"What did Moses command you?" he replied.
They said, "Moses allowed a man to write a paper of divorce and send her away."
Jesus said to them, "Moses wrote you that law because your hearts were so hard.
But at the beginning of creation, God made them male and female.
That is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife.
The two will become one body. So they are no longer two, but one.
So no one should separate what God has joined together."
When they were in the house again, the followers asked Jesus about this.
He answered, "Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery."
People were bringing little children to Jesus so that he would touch them. But the followers told the people to stop.
When Jesus saw this, he was angry. He said to them, "Let the little children come to me. Do not stop them, because the kingdom of God belongs to people like them.
I tell you for certain, anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it."
Then he took the children in his arms. He put his hands on them and blessed them.
As Jesus was starting on his way, a man ran up to him and fell on his knees in front of him. "Good Teacher," he asked, "what must I do to receive eternal life?"
"Why do you call me good?" Jesus answered. "No one is good except God alone.
You know the commands: 'Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others. Do not cheat. Honour your father and mother.'"
"Teacher," he said, "I have obeyed all these since I was a boy."

Jesus looked at him and loved him. "You still need to do one thing," he said. "Go and sell everything you have and give the money to poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come, pick up your cross and follow me."
When the man heard this, his face fell. He went away sad, because he was very rich.
Jesus looked around and said to his followers, "How hard it is for rich people to enter the kingdom of God!"
The followers were amazed at his words. But Jesus said again, "Children, how hard it is for people who trust in riches to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
The followers were even more amazed. They said to each other, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said, "With people, this is impossible. But not with God. All things are possible with God."
Then Peter spoke up. "Look, we have left everything to follow you!"
"I tell you for certain," Jesus replied, "anyone who has left their home, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children or fields for me and for the good news

will receive a hundred times as much in this world. They will receive homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and fields, along with hard times. And in the world to come they will receive eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first."

They were on their way up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was leading the way. The followers were amazed, and those who followed behind were afraid. Again Jesus took the twelve to one side and told them what was going to happen to him.

"Listen," he said, "we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will sentence him to death and hand him over to people who are not Jews.
They will make fun of him, spit on him, whip him and kill him. Three days later he will rise again."
Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him. "Teacher," they said, "we want you to do for us whatever we ask."
"What do you want me to do for you?" he asked.
They replied, "Let one of us sit at your right side and the other at your left side when you are in your glory."
"You do not know what you are asking," Jesus said. "Can you drink the cup of suffering I am going to drink? Can you be baptised with the baptism I am going to be baptised with?"
"We can," they answered. Jesus said to them, "You will drink the cup I drink, and you will be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with.
But it is not for me to say who will sit at my right or left. Those places belong to the ones they have been prepared for."
When the other ten followers heard about this, they became angry with James and John.
Jesus called them all together. He said, "You know that those who are seen as rulers of the nations order their people around. Their important leaders use their power over them.
It must not be like that with you. Instead, anyone who wants to be important among you must be your servant.
And anyone who wants to be first must be the slave of everyone.
Even the Son of Man did not come to be served. He came to serve others, and to give his life to set many people free."
Then they came to Jericho. As Jesus and his followers were leaving the town with a large crowd, a blind man named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road begging.
When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Many people scolded him and told him to be quiet. But he shouted even louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." So they called the blind man. "Cheer up!" they said. "Get up! He is calling you."
He threw his coat to one side, jumped up and came to Jesus.
"What do you want me to do for you?" Jesus asked him. The blind man said, "Rabbi, I want to be able to see."
"Go," said Jesus. "Your faith has healed you." Straight away he could see, and he followed Jesus along the road.
As they came near Jerusalem, they came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives. Jesus sent two of his followers ahead.
He said to them, "Go to the village in front of you. As soon as you go into it, you will find a young donkey tied there. No one has ever ridden it. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord needs it, and he will send it back here soon.'"
So they went and found a young donkey tied at a door, outside in the street. As they untied it,
some people standing there asked, "What are you doing, untying that donkey?"
They answered as Jesus had told them to, and the people let them go.
They brought the young donkey to Jesus and put their coats over it. Then he sat on it.
Many people spread their coats on the road. Others spread branches they had cut in the fields.
The people who went ahead and those who followed shouted, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest heaven!"
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. He looked around at everything. But it was already late, so he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
Far away he saw a fig tree with leaves. He went to see if it had any fruit. When he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, because it was not the season for figs.
Then he said to the tree, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again!" And his followers heard him say it.

When they reached Jerusalem, Jesus went into the temple. He began to drive out the people who were buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the benches of the people selling doves.
He would not let anyone carry things through the temple courtyard.
Then he taught them. He said, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations'? But you have made it a hiding place for robbers!"
The chief priests and the teachers of the law heard this. They began looking for a way to kill him. They were afraid of him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
When evening came, Jesus and his followers left the city.
In the morning, as they walked along, they saw the fig tree. It had dried up from the roots.
Peter remembered what had happened. He said to Jesus, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has dried up!"
"Have faith in God," Jesus answered.

"I tell you for certain, if anyone says to this mountain, 'Go and throw yourself into the sea,' and does not doubt in their heart, but believes that what they say will happen, it will be done for them.
So I tell you, when you pray for anything, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
And when you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive them. Then your Father in heaven will also forgive your sins.
But if you do not forgive, your Father in heaven will not forgive your sins either."
They came again to Jerusalem. While Jesus was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders came to him.
"By what authority are you doing these things?" they asked. "And who gave you the authority to do them?"
Jesus replied, "I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
John's baptism, did it come from heaven, or did it come from people? Tell me!"
They talked about it among themselves. They said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
