But if we say, 'From people'..." They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone believed that John really was a prophet.
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you by what authority I am doing these things either."

Then Jesus began to speak to them using stories. He said, "A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it and dug a pit for a winepress. He also built a watchtower. Then he rented the vineyard out to some farmers and went away on a journey.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit from the vineyard.
But they grabbed the servant and beat him. Then they sent him away with nothing.
Then the man sent another servant to them. They hit this one on the head and treated him shamefully.
He sent still another servant, and they killed him. He sent many others. They beat some of them, and they killed others.
The man had one more person to send. It was his son, whom he loved. Last of all, he sent his son to them. He said, 'They will respect my son.'
But the farmers said to each other, 'This is the one who will receive everything one day. Come, let us kill him, and everything will be ours.'
So they took him and killed him. Then they threw him out of the vineyard.
"What will the owner of the vineyard do then? He will come and kill those farmers. Then he will give the vineyard to other people.
Have you never read this Scripture? 'The stone the builders rejected has become the most important stone of all.
The Lord has done this, and it is wonderful to see.'"
Then the leaders looked for a way to arrest Jesus, because they knew he had told the story against them. But they were afraid of the crowd. So they left him and went away.
Later they sent some Pharisees and some of Herod's supporters to Jesus. They wanted to trap him with his own words.

They came to him and said, "Teacher, we know that you are honest. You do not let others tell you what to do, and you treat everyone the same. You teach the way of God truthfully. Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
Should we pay them or not?" But Jesus knew they were being hypocrites. "Why are you trying to trap me?" he asked. "Bring me a silver coin. Let me look at it."
They brought the coin. He asked them, "Whose picture is this? And whose words?" "Caesar's," they replied.
Then Jesus said to them, "Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to God what belongs to God." And they were amazed at him.
Then some Sadducees came to Jesus. They do not believe that people rise from the dead. They asked him a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses wrote for us that if a man dies and leaves a wife but no children, his brother must marry the widow. Then he must have children for the brother who died.
There were seven brothers. The first one married and died without having any children.
The second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. It was the same with the third one.
In fact, none of the seven left any children. Last of all, the woman died too.
When the dead rise, whose wife will she be? All seven of them were married to her."
Jesus replied, "You are wrong, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
When the dead rise, they will not marry, and they will not be given in marriage. They will be like the angels in heaven.
Now, about the dead rising, have you not read in the book of Moses the story about the bush? God said to Moses, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.'
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!"
One of the teachers of the law came and heard them arguing. He saw that Jesus had given them a good answer. So he asked him, "Which is the most important of all the commands?"
Jesus answered, "The most important one is this: 'Listen, Israel. The Lord our God is the one and only Lord.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind and with all your strength.' This is the first command.
The second is this: 'Love your neighbour as you love yourself.' No other command is greater than these."
"Well said, Teacher," the man replied. "You are right in saying that God is one, and that there is no other god but him.

To love him with all your heart, with all your understanding, with all your soul and with all your strength is very important. So is loving your neighbour as you love yourself. These things are more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices."
Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely. He said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." From then on, no one dared to ask Jesus any more questions.
While Jesus was teaching in the temple, he asked, "Why do the teachers of the law say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself, speaking by the Holy Spirit, said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right side until I put your enemies under your feet."'
David himself calls him 'Lord'. So how can he be David's son?" The large crowd listened to him with joy.
As he taught, Jesus said, "Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in long robes. They like to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces.
They love to have the most important seats in the synagogues and the best places at dinners.
They take away the houses of widows, and they make long prayers to show off. These men will be punished more than others."
Jesus sat down across from the place where people put their offerings. He watched the crowd putting their money into the offering boxes. Many rich people put in large amounts.
But a poor widow came and put in two very small copper coins. Together they were worth almost nothing.
Jesus called his followers to him. He said, "I tell you for certain, this poor widow has put more into the offering box than all the others.
They all gave out of their riches. But she gave out of her poverty. She put in everything she had to live on."
As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of his followers said to him, "Look, Teacher! What huge stones! What wonderful buildings!"
"Do you see all these great buildings?" Jesus replied. "Not one stone here will be left on top of another. Every one of them will be thrown down."
Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, across from the temple. Peter, James, John and Andrew asked him in private,
"Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are all about to come true?"
Jesus began to tell them, "Be careful that no one fools you.
Many will come in my name, saying, 'I am he.' They will fool many people.
When you hear about wars and stories of wars, do not be afraid. These things must happen, but the end has not yet come.
Nation will fight against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in many places, and there will be times of hunger. These are only the beginning of the birth pains.
"Be on your guard. You will be handed over to the local courts and beaten in the synagogues. Because of me, you will stand in front of rulers and kings as witnesses to them.
And the good news must first be preached to all nations.
When you are arrested and brought to trial, do not worry beforehand about what to say. Just say whatever is given to you at that time. It will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
"Brothers will hand each other over to be killed, and fathers will hand over their children. Children will turn against their parents and have them put to death.
Everyone will hate you because of me. But whoever stays strong to the end will be saved.

"You will see 'the terrible thing that destroys' standing where it does not belong, as the prophet Daniel said." Let the reader understand this. "Then those who are in Judea must run away to the mountains.
Anyone on the roof of their house must not go down or go inside to take anything out.
Anyone in the field must not go back to get their coat.
How terrible it will be in those days for women who are pregnant, and for mothers who are feeding their babies!
Pray that this will not happen in winter.
Those days will be a time of terrible suffering. Nothing like it has ever happened from the beginning, when God created the world, until now. And nothing like it will ever happen again.
If the Lord had not made that time shorter, no one would survive. But because of the people he has chosen, he has made it shorter.
At that time, if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ!' or, 'Look, there he is!' do not believe it.
False Christs and false prophets will appear. They will do signs and wonders to fool even God's chosen people, if that were possible.
So be on your guard. I have told you everything ahead of time.
"But in those days, after that time of suffering, 'the sun will grow dark, and the moon will not give its light.
The stars will fall from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.'
Then people will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
He will send out his angels. They will gather his chosen people from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the heavens.
"Learn a lesson from the fig tree. When its branches become soft and its leaves come out, you know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, you know that the time is near. It is right at the door.
I tell you for certain, the people living now will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will disappear, but my words will never disappear.
"No one knows the day or the hour when these things will happen. Not even the angels in heaven know, and not even the Son. Only the Father knows.
Be on your guard! Stay awake and pray! You do not know when that time will come.
It is like a man who goes away on a journey. He leaves his house and puts his servants in charge, and he gives each one a job to do. He tells the one at the door to keep watch.
So keep watch! You do not know when the owner of the house will come back. It might be in the evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or at dawn.
If he comes suddenly, do not let him find you sleeping.
What I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!"
It was now two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for a sly way to arrest Jesus and kill him.
"But not during the feast," they said, "or the people may start a riot."

Jesus was in Bethany, eating at the house of a man known as Simon the Leper. A woman came with a jar made of white stone. It was full of very expensive perfume made from pure nard. She broke the jar open and poured the perfume on his head.
Some of the people there were angry. They said to each other, "Why waste this perfume?
It could have been sold for more than a year's wages, and the money given to poor people." And they spoke harshly to her.
"Leave her alone," said Jesus. "Why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
You will always have poor people with you, and you can help them any time you want. But you will not always have me.
She did what she could. She poured perfume on my body ahead of time to get it ready to be buried.
I tell you for certain, wherever the good news is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, so that people will remember her."
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them.
They were happy to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas watched for a good time to hand Jesus over.
On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the day when the Passover lamb was killed, Jesus' followers asked him, "Where do you want us to go and prepare the Passover meal for you?"
So he sent two of his followers and told them, "Go into the city. A man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
Say to the owner of the house he goes into, 'The Teacher asks, "Where is my guest room, where I can eat the Passover with my followers?"'
He will show you a large upstairs room, with everything ready. Prepare for us there."
The followers left and went into the city. They found things just as Jesus had told them. So they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, Jesus arrived with the twelve.
While they were at the table eating, Jesus said, "I tell you for certain, one of you will hand me over to my enemies. He is eating with me."
They became very sad. One by one they said to him, "Surely you do not mean me?"
"It is one of the twelve," Jesus replied. "It is the one who dips bread into the bowl with me.
The Son of Man will go just as it is written about him. But how terrible it will be for the one who hands over the Son of Man! It would be better for him if he had never been born."
While they were eating, Jesus took bread. He gave thanks and broke it. He gave it to his followers and said, "Take it. This is my body."
Then he took the cup. He gave thanks and handed it to them, and they all drank from it.
"This is my blood of the new covenant," he said to them. "It is poured out for many people.
I tell you for certain, I will not drink wine again until the day I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus told them, "All of you will turn away from me tonight. It is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Peter said, "Even if all the others turn away, I will not."
"I tell you for certain," Jesus answered, "today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you yourself will say three times that you do not know me."
But Peter kept saying firmly, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I do not know you." And all the others said the same.
They went to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to his followers, "Sit here while I pray."
He took Peter, James and John along with him. He began to be very upset and troubled.
"My soul is so full of sorrow that I feel as if I am dying," he said to them. "Stay here and keep watch."
He went a little further. Then he fell to the ground and prayed that, if possible, this time of suffering might pass him by.
"Abba, Father," he said, "everything is possible for you. Take this cup of suffering away from me. But let what you want be done, not what I want."
Then he came back to his followers and found them sleeping. "Simon," he said to Peter, "are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?
Watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak."
Once more Jesus went away and prayed the same thing.
Then he came back and again found them sleeping, because their eyes were very heavy. They did not know what to say to him.
He came back the third time and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The time has come. Look, the Son of Man is about to be handed over to sinners.
Get up! Let us go! Here comes the one who is handing me over!"
Just as Jesus was speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, appeared. With him was a crowd carrying swords and clubs. The chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders had sent them.
Judas, the one who was handing Jesus over, had given them a signal. "The one I kiss is the man," he had said. "Arrest him and take him away under guard."
So Judas went to Jesus straight away. "Rabbi!" he said, and kissed him.
The men grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
Then one of the people standing nearby pulled out his sword. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
"Am I leading a revolt against you," said Jesus, "that you have come out with swords and clubs to capture me?
Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But the Scriptures must come true."
Then all his followers left him and ran away.
A young man was following Jesus. He was wearing nothing but a linen cloth. When the crowd grabbed him,
he ran away naked, leaving the linen cloth behind.
They took Jesus to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders and the teachers of the law gathered there.
Peter followed Jesus from a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. There he sat with the guards and warmed himself at the fire.
The chief priests and the whole Council were looking for something to use against Jesus so that they could put him to death. But they did not find anything.
Many people told lies about him, but their stories did not agree.
Then some stood up and told this lie about him:
"We heard him say, 'I will destroy this temple made by people. In three days I will build another temple, not made by people.'"
But even then their stories did not agree.
Then the high priest stood up in front of them all. He asked Jesus, "Are you not going to answer? What are these charges that these men are bringing against you?"
But Jesus stayed silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest asked him, "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
"I am," said Jesus. "And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of the Mighty One. You will see him coming on the clouds of heaven."
The high priest tore his clothes. "Why do we need any more witnesses?" he asked.
"You have heard him insult God. What do you think?" They all said he was guilty and should be put to death.
Then some of them began to spit at him. They covered his face and hit him with their fists. They said, "Prophesy!" And the guards took him and beat him.
Peter was below in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls came by.
When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked closely at him. "You also were with that man from Nazareth, Jesus," she said.
But Peter said it was not true. "I do not know or understand what you are talking about," he said. Then he went out into the entrance, and a rooster crowed.
The servant girl saw him there. She said again to the people standing around, "This man is one of them."
Again he said it was not true. A little later, the people standing near Peter said to him, "You must be one of them. You are from Galilee."
Then Peter began to call down curses on himself, and he swore to them, "I do not know this man you are talking about!"

Straight away the rooster crowed the second time. Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: "Before the rooster crows twice, you will say three times that you do not know me." And he broke down and cried.
Very early in the morning, the chief priests, the elders, the teachers of the law and the whole Council made their plans. They tied up Jesus, led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
"Are you the king of the Jews?" asked Pilate. "You have said so," Jesus replied.
The chief priests accused him of many things.
So Pilate asked him again, "Are you not going to answer? Look how many things they are accusing you of."
But Jesus still did not answer, and Pilate was amazed.
It was the custom at the feast to set free one prisoner, whoever the people asked for.
A man called Barabbas was in prison with some others who had fought against the rulers. They had committed murder during the fighting.
The crowd came up and asked Pilate to do for them what he usually did.
"Do you want me to set the king of the Jews free for you?" asked Pilate.
He knew that the chief priests had handed Jesus over to him because they were jealous.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to ask Pilate to set Barabbas free instead.
"Then what should I do with the one you call the king of the Jews?" Pilate asked them.
"Nail him to a cross!" they shouted.
"Why? What wrong has he done?" asked Pilate. But they shouted even louder, "Nail him to a cross!"
Pilate wanted to please the crowd. So he set Barabbas free for them. He had Jesus whipped, and then he handed him over to be nailed to a cross.
The soldiers led Jesus away into the courtyard of the palace, called the Praetorium. They called together the whole company of soldiers.
They put a purple robe on him. Then they twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head.
And they began to call out to him, "Hail, king of the Jews!"
Again and again they hit him on the head with a stick and spat on him. They fell on their knees and pretended to worship him.
After they had made fun of him, they took off the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to nail him to a cross.
A man named Simon, from Cyrene, was passing by on his way in from the country. He was the father of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers forced him to carry the cross.
They brought Jesus to the place called Golgotha, which means the Place of the Skull.
Then they offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not drink it.
They nailed him to the cross. They divided up his clothes by throwing dice to see what each one would get.
It was nine o'clock in the morning when they nailed him to the cross.
A notice was put up saying why he was being punished. It read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
They nailed two robbers to crosses with him, one on his right and one on his left.
So the Scripture came true that says, "He was counted among the people who broke the law."
People who passed by shouted insults at him. They shook their heads and said, "So! You who are going to destroy the temple and build it again in three days,
come down from the cross and save yourself!"
In the same way, the chief priests and the teachers of the law made fun of him among themselves. "He saved others," they said, "but he cannot save himself!
Let this Christ, this king of Israel, come down now from the cross! When we see that, we will believe." Those who were nailed to crosses with him also insulted him.
At twelve o'clock, darkness covered the whole land until three o'clock in the afternoon.
At three o'clock Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" This means, "My God, my God, why have you left me all alone?"
Some of the people standing nearby heard this. They said, "Listen! He is calling for Elijah."
Someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a stick and offered it to Jesus to drink. "Leave him alone," he said. "Let us see if Elijah comes to take him down."
Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice and took his last breath.
The curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
A Roman officer was standing there in front of Jesus. He heard his cry and saw how he died. Then he said, "This man really was the Son of God!"
Some women were watching from far away. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
In Galilee these women had followed Jesus and taken care of him. Many other women were there too. They had come up with him to Jerusalem.
It was the day of preparation, the day before the Sabbath. So as evening came,
Joseph from Arimathea went boldly to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. Joseph was an important member of the Council, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead. He called the Roman officer and asked him if Jesus had already died.
When the officer told him it was true, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
So Joseph bought some linen cloth. He took down the body and wrapped it in the linen. Then he placed it in a tomb cut out of rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where Jesus was laid.
When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices. They were going to put them on Jesus' body.
Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
They asked each other, "Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?"
It was a very large stone. But when they looked up, they saw that it had already been rolled away.
As they went into the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side. They were alarmed.
"Do not be alarmed," he said. "You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was nailed to a cross. He has risen! He is not here. See the place where they laid him.
But go and tell his followers and Peter, 'He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.'"
The women went out and ran away from the tomb. They were shaking and confused. They said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.
Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus rose from the dead, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene. He had driven seven demons out of her.
She went and told those who had been with him. They were sad and crying.
When they heard that Jesus was alive and that she had seen him, they did not believe it.
After that, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them while they were walking out into the country.
They went back and told the others. But the others did not believe them either.
Later Jesus appeared to the eleven while they were eating. He scolded them because they had no faith. Their hearts were hard, because they did not believe those who had seen him after he had risen.
He said to them, "Go into all the world and preach the good news to everyone.
Whoever believes and is baptised will be saved. But whoever does not believe will be judged guilty.
These signs will go with those who believe. In my name they will drive out demons. They will speak in new languages.
They will pick up snakes with their hands. When they drink deadly poison, it will not hurt them at all. They will put their hands on sick people, and the sick people will get well."
After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, he was taken up into heaven. He sat down at the right side of God.
Then the followers went out and preached everywhere. The Lord worked with them, and he showed that their message was true by the signs that went with it. Amen.
Luke: Many people have tried to write an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us.
They wrote what we were told by people who saw these things from the start, and who served the word.
I have carefully looked into everything from the beginning. So I too thought it was good to write it down in order for you, most excellent Theophilus.
I have done this so that you can know for certain that the things you were taught are true.
In the time of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zacharias. He belonged to the priest group of Abijah. His wife was one of Aaron's descendants, and her name was Elizabeth.
They were both right with God. They kept all the Lord's commands and rules without blame.
But they had no child, because Elizabeth could not have children, and they were both very old.
One day Zacharias was serving as a priest before God, when his group's turn came.
As was the custom of the priests, he was chosen by lot to go into the Lord's temple and burn incense.
All the crowd of people were praying outside at the time when the incense was burned.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
When Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and he was filled with fear.
But the angel said to him, "Do not be afraid, Zacharias. Your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will give birth to a son, and you are to name him John.
You will be full of joy and gladness, and many people will rejoice because he is born.
He will be great in the Lord's sight. He must never drink wine or any other strong drink. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother's womb.
He will turn many of the people of Israel back to the Lord their God.

He will go ahead of the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah. He will turn the hearts of fathers back to their children, and he will turn those who disobey to the wisdom of those who do what is right. He will get a people ready for the Lord."
Zacharias said to the angel, "How can I be sure of this? I am an old man, and my wife is very old too."
The angel answered, "I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
Listen! You will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen. This is because you did not believe my words. They will come true at the right time."
The people were waiting for Zacharias, and they were amazed that he stayed so long in the temple.
When he came out, he could not speak to them. They realised that he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them, and he stayed unable to speak.
When his days of service were over, he went home.
After this, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant. She stayed hidden for five months.
She said, "The Lord has done this for me. In these days he has looked on me with kindness, and he has taken away my shame among the people."
In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth.
He went to a virgin who was promised in marriage to a man named Joseph, from the family of David. The virgin's name was Mary.
The angel came to her and said, "Greetings, you who are highly favoured! The Lord is with you. You are blessed among women!"
But when she saw him, she was very troubled by what he said, and she wondered what kind of greeting this could be.
The angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary. God has shown you his favour.
Listen! You will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus.
He will be great, and he will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.
He will rule over the family of Jacob for ever, and his kingdom will never end."
Mary said to the angel, "How can this happen? I am a virgin."
The angel answered, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will cover you. So the holy one who is born will be called the Son of God.
Listen! Your relative Elizabeth is also going to have a son, even though she is old. The one who was said to be unable to have children is now in her sixth month.
Nothing God says is impossible."
Mary said, "I am the Lord's servant. Let it happen to me just as you have said." Then the angel left her.
Soon after this, Mary got ready and hurried to a town in the hill country of Judea.
She went into Zacharias's house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby jumped inside her, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She called out with a loud voice, "You are blessed among women, and blessed is the child you will give birth to!
Why am I so favoured, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
Listen! As soon as I heard your greeting, the baby inside me jumped for joy.
Blessed is she who believed, because what the Lord has said to her will come true!"
Mary said, "My soul praises the Lord.
My spirit rejoices in God my Saviour,
because he has looked with care on me, his humble servant. Listen! From now on, all people will call me blessed.
The Mighty One has done great things for me. His name is holy.
He shows mercy to those who fear him, from one generation to the next.
He has shown the strength of his arm. He has scattered those who are proud in their hearts.
He has brought rulers down from their thrones, and he has lifted up those who are humble.
He has filled the hungry with good things, and he has sent the rich away with nothing.
He has helped Israel, his servant, because he remembered to show mercy,
just as he promised our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants for ever."
Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months, and then she went back home.
When the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, she had a son.
Her neighbours and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child. They were going to name him Zacharias, after his father.
But his mother said, "No. He is to be called John."
They said to her, "None of your relatives has that name."
Then they made signs to his father, to ask what he wanted the child to be called.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, "His name is John." They were all amazed.
Straight away his mouth was opened and his tongue was set free, and he began to speak, praising God.
All their neighbours were filled with fear, and people talked about all these things throughout the hill country of Judea.
Everyone who heard kept these things in their hearts. They said, "What will this child turn out to be?" The Lord's hand was with him.
His father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God's message. He said,
"Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, because he has come to his people and set them free.
He has raised up a mighty Saviour for us from the family of his servant David,
just as he promised long ago through his holy prophets.
He promised to save us from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us.
He promised to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,
the promise he made with an oath to our father Abraham.
He promised to save us from the hand of our enemies, so that we could serve him without fear,
in holiness and in what is right before him, all the days of our life.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High. You will go ahead of the Lord to prepare his ways.
You will tell his people how they can be saved, through the forgiveness of their sins.
This is because of the tender mercy of our God. Because of that mercy, the dawn from heaven will come to us,
to shine on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and to guide our feet into the way of peace."
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the desert until the day he was shown to Israel.
In those days Caesar Augustus sent out an order that everyone in the world should be registered.
This was the first registration, and it happened while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
So everyone went to be registered, each person to their own town.
Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem, the town of David, because he belonged to the house and family of David.
He went to be registered with Mary, who was promised to him in marriage and was expecting a child.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
She gave birth to her first son. She wrapped him in strips of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the guest room.
There were shepherds in that area, staying out in the fields and watching their flock at night.
An angel of the Lord stood near them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, "Do not be afraid. Listen! I bring you good news of great joy for all the people.
Today, in David's town, a Saviour has been born for you. He is the Christ, the Lord.
This is how you will know him. You will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a feeding trough."
Suddenly a great crowd of heaven's army was with the angel, praising God and saying,
"Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to people, because he is pleased with them."
When the angels had left them and gone into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, "Let us go to Bethlehem now and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about."
They hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough.
When they had seen him, they told everyone what had been said to them about this child.
All who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these things in her heart and thought about them.
The shepherds went back, giving glory and praise to God for everything they had heard and seen. It was just as they had been told.
When the child was eight days old and was circumcised, he was named Jesus. That was the name the angel had given him before he was conceived.
When the time of their purification was finished, as the law of Moses required, they took him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord.
This is what is written in the law of the Lord: "Every firstborn son is to be set apart as holy to the Lord."
They also went to offer a sacrifice, as the law of the Lord says: "a pair of turtle doves, or two young pigeons."
There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was right with God and devoted to him. He was waiting for God to comfort Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
The Holy Spirit had shown him that he would not die before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple. When the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him what the Law required,
Simeon took him in his arms and praised God. He said,
"Now, Master, you can let your servant go in peace, just as you promised.
My eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared in the sight of all people.
He is a light to show the truth to the nations, and he is the glory of your people Israel."
Joseph and the child's mother were amazed at the things said about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, his mother, "Listen! This child is chosen to cause many in Israel to fall and many to rise. He will be a sign that people will speak against.
And a sword will pierce your own soul too. In this way the thoughts of many hearts will be shown."
There was also a prophet named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She was very old. She had lived with her husband for seven years after she was married,
and then she had been a widow for about eighty-four years. She never left the temple, but worshipped night and day, fasting and praying.
She came up at that very moment, gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke about the child to everyone who was waiting for God to set Jerusalem free.
When they had done everything the law of the Lord required, they went back to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He was filled with wisdom, and God's grace was on him.
Every year his parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover feast.
When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem as usual for the feast.
When the feast days were over and they started for home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother did not know it.
They thought he was with the group of travellers, so they went a day's journey. Then they began looking for him among their relatives and friends.
When they did not find him, they went back to Jerusalem to look for him.
After three days they found him in the temple. He was sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at his understanding and his answers.
When his parents saw him, they were astonished. His mother said to him, "Son, why have you treated us like this? Your father and I have been very worried, looking for you."
He said to them, "Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?"
They did not understand what he said to them.
Then he went down to Nazareth with them and obeyed them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
Jesus grew in wisdom and in height, and in favour with God and with people.

It was the fifteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar. Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea. Herod was ruler of Galilee, and his brother Philip was ruler of the area of Ituraea and Trachonitis. Lysanias was ruler of Abilene.
Annas and Caiaphas were high priests. At that time the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the desert.
He went through all the area around the Jordan River. He preached that people should be baptised to show they had turned away from their sins, so that God would forgive them.
This is what is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah: "A voice of someone shouting in the desert, 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled in. Every mountain and hill will be made low. The crooked roads will be made straight, and the rough ways will be made smooth.
And all people will see God's salvation.'"
John said to the crowds who came out to be baptised by him, "You family of snakes! Who warned you to run away from God's anger that is coming?
Do the things that show you have turned from your sins. Do not start saying to yourselves, 'Abraham is our father.' I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
The axe is already at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire."
The crowds asked him, "What should we do, then?"
He answered, "Whoever has two coats should give one to someone who has none. And whoever has food should do the same."
Tax collectors also came to be baptised. They asked him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
He said to them, "Do not collect more than you are ordered to collect."
Soldiers also asked him, "And what about us? What should we do?" He said to them, "Do not take money from anyone by force, and do not accuse anyone falsely. Be content with your pay."
The people were waiting, and they were all wondering in their hearts whether John might be the Christ.

John answered them all, "I baptise you with water. But someone more powerful than I am is coming. I am not good enough even to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptise you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
He has his tool in his hand to clear the grain. He will clean his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his barn. But he will burn the husks with a fire that never goes out."
With many other words he encouraged the people and preached the good news to them.
But John spoke against Herod the ruler because of Herodias, his brother's wife, and because of all the evil things Herod had done.
Then Herod added this to all the rest: he locked John up in prison.
When all the people were being baptised, Jesus was baptised too. And while he was praying, heaven was opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down on him in a body like a dove. A voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, and I love you. I am very pleased with you."
Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his work. People thought he was the son of Joseph. Joseph was the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph.
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai.
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah.
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri.
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, the son of Er.
the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi.
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim.
the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David.
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon.
the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah.
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor.
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah.
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech.
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan.
the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan River. The Spirit led him into the desert
for forty days, and the devil tempted him. He ate nothing during those days. When they were over, he was hungry.
The devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
Jesus answered, "It is written, 'People do not live on bread alone, but on every word of God.'"
The devil led him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment.
The devil said to him, "I will give you all this power and all their glory. It has been handed over to me, and I can give it to anyone I want.
So if you will worship me, it will all be yours."
Jesus answered, "Get behind me, Satan! It is written, 'You must worship the Lord your God, and you must serve only him.'"
Then the devil led him to Jerusalem and set him on the highest point of the temple. He said, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
It is written, 'He will command his angels to take care of you and guard you,'
and, 'They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus answered, "It is said, 'You must not test the Lord your God.'"
When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Jesus until another time.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread through the whole area.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
He came to Nazareth, where he had grown up. As he usually did, he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and he stood up to read.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He unrolled it and found the place where it is written,

"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has chosen me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal those with broken hearts, to announce freedom to the prisoners, to give sight back to the blind, and to set free those who are crushed.
He has sent me to announce the year of the Lord's favour."
Then he rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
He began to say to them, "Today this Scripture has come true, as you heard it."
Everyone spoke well of him and was amazed at the kind words that came from his mouth. They said, "Is this not Joseph's son?"
Jesus said to them, "Surely you will quote this saying to me: 'Doctor, heal yourself! Do here in your home town the things we heard you did in Capernaum.'"
Then he said, "I tell you for certain, no prophet is accepted in his home town.
But I tell you the truth. There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, except to a widow in Zarephath, in the land of Sidon.
And there were many people with skin diseases in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha. Yet not one of them was made clean, except Naaman the Syrian."
When they heard this, everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger.
They got up, drove him out of the town, and took him to the edge of the hill on which the town was built, so that they could throw him off the cliff.
But he walked right through the crowd and went on his way.
Then he went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee. On the Sabbath day he taught the people,
and they were astonished at his teaching, because his word had authority.
In the synagogue there was a man with an evil demon spirit. He cried out with a loud voice,
"Leave us alone! What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the Holy One of God!"
Jesus spoke firmly to him. "Be quiet!" he said. "Come out of him!" The demon threw the man down in front of everyone and came out of him without hurting him.
All the people were amazed and said to one another, "What kind of word is this? With authority and power he gives orders to evil spirits, and they come out!"
And the news about him spread to every place in the area.
Jesus left the synagogue and went to Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they begged Jesus to help her.
He stood over her and spoke firmly to the fever, and it left her. Straight away she got up and began to serve them.
When the sun was setting, all who had people sick with all kinds of diseases brought them to Jesus. He laid his hands on every one of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many people, shouting, "You are the Christ, the Son of God!" But he spoke firmly to them and would not let them speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
At daybreak he left and went to a quiet place. The crowds looked for him, and when they found him they tried to stop him from leaving them.
But he said, "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God in the other towns as well. That is why I was sent."
And he kept preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
One day the crowd was pressing in on Jesus to hear the word of God. He was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats by the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
Jesus got into one of the boats, the one that belonged to Simon, and asked him to push out a little from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Push out into deep water, and let down your nets for a catch."
Simon answered, "Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because you say so, I will let down the nets."
When they did this, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break.
They signalled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell down at Jesus's knees and said, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man."
He and everyone with him were amazed at the catch of fish they had taken.
So were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid. From now on you will catch people."
When they had brought the boats to land, they left everything and followed him.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man covered with a skin disease saw him. He fell on his face and begged him, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus reached out his hand and touched him. "I am willing," he said. "Be clean!" Straight away the skin disease left him.
Jesus ordered him, "Do not tell anyone. But go and show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift Moses commanded for your cleansing. This will show everyone that you are healed."
But the news about Jesus spread even more, and large crowds gathered to hear him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
But Jesus often went away to quiet places and prayed.

One day, while he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was with Jesus to heal the sick.
Some men came carrying a man who could not walk, on a mat. They tried to bring him in and lay him in front of Jesus.
They could not find a way through the crowd, so they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles, right into the middle of the crowd in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said, "Friend, your sins are forgiven."
The teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to think, "Who is this man who speaks such insults against God? Who can forgive sins except God alone?"
Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." Then he said to the man who could not walk, "I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home."
Straight away the man stood up in front of them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home, praising God.
Everyone was amazed and gave glory to God. They were filled with fear and said, "We have seen amazing things today."
After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office. "Follow me," Jesus said to him.
Levi got up, left everything, and followed him.
Then Levi held a great feast for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others were eating with them.
The Pharisees and their teachers of the law complained to his followers. They said, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered, "Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do.
I have not come to call those who think they are right with God, but sinners, so that they will turn from their sins."
They said to him, "John's followers often fast and pray, and so do the followers of the Pharisees. But your followers eat and drink."
Jesus answered, "Can you make the friends of the groom fast while the groom is still with them?
But the time will come when the groom will be taken away from them. In those days they will fast."
Then he told them a story. "No one tears a piece from a new coat and sews it onto an old coat. If they do, they will tear the new coat, and the new piece will not match the old one.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the new wine will burst the skins. The wine will spill, and the skins will be ruined.
New wine must be poured into new wineskins, so that both are kept safe.
And no one who has drunk old wine wants new wine straight away. They say, 'The old is better.'"
One Sabbath day Jesus was going through the grain fields. His followers picked some heads of grain, rubbed them in their hands, and ate them.
Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what is against the law on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered, "Have you not read what David did when he and his men were hungry?
He went into the house of God, took the holy bread and ate it, and gave some to his men. That was against the law. Only the priests are allowed to eat that bread."
Then Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
On another Sabbath he went into the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was shrivelled.
The teachers of the law and the Pharisees watched Jesus, to see if he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they could find a reason to accuse him.
But Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said to the man with the shrivelled hand, "Get up and stand in the middle." So the man got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, "I ask you, which is right on the Sabbath: to do good or to do harm? To save life or to destroy it?"
He looked around at them all and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He did so, and his hand was made as well as the other.
But they were filled with anger and talked together about what they might do to Jesus.
In those days Jesus went out to a mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night praying to God.
When morning came, he called his followers to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles.
They were Simon, whom he also named Peter, Andrew his brother, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon who was called the Zealot,
Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of his followers was there, and a great number of people from all Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the coast of Tyre and Sidon.
They had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. Those who were troubled by evil spirits were also healed.
Everyone in the crowd tried to touch him, because power was coming from him and healing them all.
Jesus looked at his followers and said, "Blessed are you who are poor, because the kingdom of God is yours.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, because you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, because you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, shut you out, mock you, and say your name is evil, because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and jump for joy, because your reward in heaven is great. Their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
But how terrible for you who are rich! You have already received your comfort.
How terrible for you who are well fed now, because you will be hungry. How terrible for you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.
How terrible for you when everyone speaks well of you. Their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
But I say to you who are listening: love your enemies, and do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who treat you badly.
If someone hits you on one cheek, offer the other cheek as well. If someone takes your coat, do not stop them from taking your shirt too.
Give to everyone who asks you, and if someone takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back.
Do to others just what you would like them to do to you.
If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do that.
And if you lend to those you expect to pay you back, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be paid back in full.
But love your enemies, do good, and lend without expecting anything back. Then your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and the evil.
So be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you. A good amount, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be poured into your lap. The measure you use for others will be the measure used for you."
He also told them this story. "Can a blind person lead a blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A follower is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye, but do not notice the plank of wood in your own eye?

How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,' when you do not see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the plank out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
A good tree does not produce bad fruit, and a bad tree does not produce good fruit.
Each tree is known by its own fruit. People do not pick figs from thorn bushes, or grapes from a bramble bush.
A good person brings good things out of the good stored in their heart. An evil person brings evil things out of the evil stored in their heart. The mouth speaks what fills the heart.
Why do you call me, 'Lord, Lord,' and do not do what I say?
I will show you what the person is like who comes to me, hears my words, and does them.

That person is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on rock. When a flood came, the stream crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was built on rock.

But the person who hears and does not do what I say is like a man who built a house on the ground with no foundation. The stream crashed against it, and straight away it fell. And the ruin of that house was great."
When Jesus had finished saying all this to the people, he went into Capernaum.
A Roman army officer had a servant who was very dear to him. The servant was sick and about to die.
When the officer heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to him, asking him to come and heal his servant.
They came to Jesus and begged him earnestly. "This man deserves your help," they said,
"because he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us."
So Jesus went with them. When he was not far from the house, the officer sent friends to say to him, "Lord, do not trouble yourself. I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.
That is why I did not even think I was worthy to come to you. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I too am a man under authority, and I have soldiers under me. I tell this one, 'Go,' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come,' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this, he was amazed at the man. He turned to the crowd following him and said, "I tell you, I have not found faith like this anywhere in Israel."
When the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant well.
Soon after this, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His followers and a large crowd went with him.
As he came near the town gate, a dead man was being carried out. He was his mother's only son, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he felt deep pity for her and said, "Do not cry."
He went up and touched the stretcher, and the people carrying it stood still. He said, "Young man, I tell you, get up!"
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.
Everyone was filled with fear and gave glory to God. They said, "A great prophet has appeared among us!" and, "God has come to help his people!"
This news about Jesus spread through the whole of Judea and all the area around it.
John's followers told him about all these things.
John called two of his followers and sent them to the Lord to ask, "Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for someone else?"
When the men came to Jesus, they said, "John the Baptist sent us to ask you, 'Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for someone else?'"
At that very time Jesus healed many people of diseases, sicknesses, and evil spirits, and he gave sight to many who were blind.

Then he answered, "Go and tell John what you have seen and heard. The blind see, those who could not walk now walk, people with skin diseases are made clean, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
Blessed is anyone who does not turn away because of me."
When John's messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John. "What did you go out into the desert to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
If not, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? No. Those who wear splendid clothes and live in luxury are in kings' palaces.
What did you go out to see, then? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written, 'Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you. He will get your road ready before you.'
I tell you, among everyone born of women there is no greater prophet than John the Baptist. Yet the least person in the kingdom of God is greater than he is."
All the people who heard this, including the tax collectors, agreed that God's way was right, because they had been baptised by John.
But the Pharisees and the experts in the law rejected God's plan for them, because they had not been baptised by John.
"What can I compare the people of today with? What are they like?
They are like children sitting in the market place and calling to each other, 'We played music for you, and you did not dance. We sang a sad song, and you did not cry.'
John the Baptist came, not eating bread and not drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look at this man! He eats too much and drinks too much, and he is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
But wisdom is proved right by all her children."
One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him. Jesus went into the Pharisee's house and sat down at the table.
A woman in that town who was a sinner heard that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house. She brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
She stood behind him at his feet, crying. She began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with her hair. She kissed his feet and poured the perfume on them.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, "If this man were a prophet, he would know who is touching him and what kind of woman she is. She is a sinner."
Jesus said to him, "Simon, I have something to tell you." "Teacher, say it," he replied.
"Two people owed money to a lender. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other owed fifty.
Neither of them could pay him back, so he forgave both debts. Which of them will love him more?"
Simon answered, "I suppose the one who was forgiven more." Jesus said, "You have judged correctly."

Then he turned towards the woman and said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I came into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet. But she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not put oil on my head, but she has poured perfume on my feet.
So I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, because she loved much. But whoever has been forgiven little loves little."
Then Jesus said to her, "Your sins are forgiven."
The other guests began to say among themselves, "Who is this who even forgives sins?"
Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace."
Soon after this, Jesus travelled through towns and villages, preaching and telling the good news of the kingdom of God. The twelve were with him,
and so were some women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses. One was Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.
Another was Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod's manager. There was also Susanna, and many others. These women used their own money to support Jesus and his followers.
A large crowd gathered, and people came to him from every town. Then he told this story.
"A farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the path. It was trampled on, and the birds of the sky ate it up.
Some fell on rock. As soon as it grew, it dried up, because it had no moisture.
Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew up with it and choked it.
And some fell on good soil. It grew and produced a crop a hundred times as much." When he had said this, he called out, "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!"
His followers asked him, "What does this story mean?"
He said, "You have been given the chance to know the secrets of the kingdom of God. But to others I speak in stories, so that, 'They may look but not see, and hear but not understand.'
This is what the story means. The seed is the word of God.
The seed along the path stands for people who hear, but then the devil comes and takes the word from their hearts, so that they will not believe and be saved.
The seed on the rock stands for people who hear the word and receive it with joy. But they have no root. They believe for a while, and when testing comes they fall away.
The seed that fell among thorns stands for people who hear, but as they go on their way they are choked by worries, riches, and the pleasures of life. Their fruit never grows ripe.
But the seed on good soil stands for people with an honest and good heart. They hear the word, hold it tight, and by keeping on they produce a crop.
No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a bowl or puts it under a bed. They put it on a stand, so that people who come in can see the light.
Nothing is hidden that will not be shown, and nothing is secret that will not be known and come into the light.
So be careful how you listen. Whoever has will be given more. Whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away."
Jesus's mother and brothers came to him, but they could not get near him because of the crowd.
Someone told him, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you."
He answered, "My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it."
One day Jesus got into a boat with his followers and said to them, "Let us go over to the other side of the lake." So they set out.
As they sailed, he fell asleep. A storm of wind came down on the lake, and the boat was filling with water, and they were in danger.
The followers went and woke him. "Master, Master, we are going to die!" they said. He woke up and spoke firmly to the wind and the raging water. They stopped, and it was calm.
"Where is your faith?" he asked them. Afraid and amazed, they said to one another, "Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him!"
They sailed to the area of the Gadarenes, which is across the lake from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped ashore, a man from the town met him. This man had been controlled by demons for a long time. He wore no clothes and did not live in a house, but in the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before him, and shouted, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!"

Jesus had commanded the evil spirit to come out of the man. Many times the spirit had seized him. He was kept under guard and bound with chains and shackles, but he broke the chains, and the demon drove him into the desert.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "Legion," he replied, because many demons had gone into him.
They begged Jesus not to order them to go into the deep pit.
A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside. The demons begged Jesus to let them go into the pigs, and he let them.
The demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
When the men who looked after the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and told it in the town and in the countryside.
People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone, sitting at Jesus's feet, dressed and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the man who had been controlled by demons was healed.
Then all the people of the area of the Gadarenes asked Jesus to leave them, because they were very afraid. So he got into the boat and went back.
The man from whom the demons had gone begged to go with him. But Jesus sent him away and said,
"Go back home and tell what great things God has done for you." So the man went through the whole town, telling what great things Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, because they were all waiting for him.
Then a man named Jairus came. He was a leader of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus's feet and begged him to come to his house,
because his only daughter, about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed around him.
A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all she had on doctors, and no one could heal her.
She came up behind Jesus and touched the edge of his coat. Straight away her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, "Who touched me?" Everyone denied it. Peter and those with him said, "Master, the crowds are crowding and pushing against you, and you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
But Jesus said, "Someone did touch me. I know that power has gone out from me."
When the woman saw that she could not hide, she came trembling and fell down before him. In front of all the people she told why she had touched him, and how she had been healed straight away.
He said to her, "Daughter, take heart. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace."
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader's house and said, "Your daughter is dead. Do not bother the Teacher any more."
But Jesus heard it and said, "Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed."
When he arrived at the house, he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter, John, James, and the child's father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But he said, "Do not weep. She is not dead. She is sleeping."
They laughed at him, because they knew she was dead.
But he sent them all outside. He took her by the hand and called, "Child, get up!"
Her spirit returned, and she got up straight away. He told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were amazed, but he ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
Jesus called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to heal diseases.
He sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, "Take nothing for the journey. Do not take a stick, a bag, bread, or money. Do not take two shirts.
When you go into a house, stay there until you leave that place.
If people do not welcome you, leave that town and shake the dust off your feet as a warning against them."
So they left and went through the villages, preaching the good news and healing people everywhere.
Herod the ruler heard about everything that was happening, and he was very puzzled. Some people were saying that John had been raised from the dead.
Others said that Elijah had appeared, and still others that one of the prophets of long ago had risen.
Herod said, "I cut off John's head. So who is this man I hear such things about?" And he tried to see him.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus what they had done. Then he took them with him and they went away privately to a quiet place near a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds found out and followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who needed healing.
Late in the day the twelve came to him and said, "Send the crowd away, so they can go to the villages and farms around here to find a place to stay and get food. We are in a lonely place."
But he said, "You give them something to eat." They answered, "We have only five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people."
There were about five thousand men. Jesus said to his followers, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty."
They did so, and everyone sat down.
Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up to heaven, gave thanks, and broke them. Then he gave them to the followers to set before the crowd.
They all ate and were filled. The followers picked up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
Once, when Jesus was praying alone and his followers were with him, he asked them, "Who do the crowds say I am?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. And others say that one of the prophets of long ago has risen."
"But who do you say I am?" he asked. Peter answered, "The Christ of God."
Jesus warned them not to tell this to anyone.
He said, "The Son of Man must suffer many things. The elders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law will reject him. He must be killed, and on the third day he will be raised."
Then he said to them all, "Whoever wants to follow me must say no to themselves, pick up their cross every day, and follow me.
Whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for me will save it.
What good is it if someone gains the whole world but loses or gives up their own self?
Whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
But I tell you the truth. Some who are standing here will not die before they see the kingdom of God."
About eight days after Jesus said these things, he took Peter, John, and James with him and went up onto a mountain to pray.
As he was praying, the look of his face changed, and his clothes became shining white.
And two men were talking with him. They were Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and spoke about his departure, which he was about to bring to completion in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were very sleepy. But when they were fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

As the men were leaving Jesus, Peter said to him, "Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He did not know what he was saying.
While he was speaking, a cloud came and covered them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud: "This is my Son, and I love him. Listen to him!"
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was there alone. They kept quiet, and in those days they told no one anything of what they had seen.
The next day, when they came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
A man in the crowd called out, "Teacher, I beg you to look at my son. He is my only child.
A spirit takes hold of him, and he suddenly cries out. It throws him into fits so that he foams at the mouth. It hardly ever leaves him, and it bruises him badly.
I begged your followers to drive it out, but they could not."
Jesus answered, "You people of today have no faith, and you are twisted! How long must I stay with you and put up with you? Bring your son here."
Even while the boy was coming, the demon threw him down and shook him violently. But Jesus spoke firmly to the evil spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
They were all amazed at the greatness of God. While everyone was wondering at all that Jesus did, he said to his followers,
"Let these words sink into your ears. The Son of Man is going to be handed over to men."
But they did not understand what this meant. It was hidden from them, so they did not grasp it, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
An argument started among them about which of them was the greatest.
Jesus knew what they were thinking in their hearts. He took a little child and had the child stand beside him.
Then he said, "Whoever welcomes this little child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. The one who is least among you all is the one who is great."
John said, "Master, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us."
Jesus said, "Do not stop him. Whoever is not against you is for you."
As the time came near for Jesus to be taken up to heaven, he set out firmly to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him. They went into a Samaritan village to get things ready for him.
But the people there did not welcome him, because he was heading for Jerusalem.
When his followers James and John saw this, they said, "Lord, do you want us to call fire down from heaven to destroy them, just as Elijah did?"
But he turned and spoke firmly to them. "You do not know what kind of spirit you belong to.
The Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives, but to save them." Then they went to another village.
As they were walking along the road, someone said to him, "I will follow you wherever you go, Lord."
Jesus said, "Foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
He said to another man, "Follow me." But the man said, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
Jesus said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead. You go and tell about the kingdom of God."
Another said, "I will follow you, Lord, but first let me say goodbye to those at my home."
Jesus said to him, "No one who puts a hand to the plough and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
After this, the Lord appointed seventy others and sent them out two by two ahead of him, to every town and place he was about to go.
He said to them, "The harvest is large, but the workers are few. So pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
Go. I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a money bag, a bag, or sandals. Do not stop to greet anyone on the road.
When you enter a house, first say, 'Peace to this house.'
If someone who wants peace is there, your peace will rest on them. If not, it will come back to you.
Stay in that same house. Eat and drink what they give you, because a worker deserves to be paid. Do not move from house to house.
When you enter a town and the people welcome you, eat what is set before you.
Heal the sick who are there, and tell them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
But when you enter a town and the people do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
'We wipe off even the dust of your town that sticks to our feet, as a warning against you. But know this: the kingdom of God has come near to you.'
I tell you, on that day it will be easier for Sodom than for that town.

How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the powerful works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned from their sins long ago, sitting in rough cloth and ashes.
