But at the judgement it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to the place of the dead.
Whoever listens to you listens to me. Whoever rejects you rejects me. And whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me."
The seventy returned with joy. They said, "Lord, even the demons obey us in your name!"
He said to them, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Listen! I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and authority over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you at all.
But do not rejoice that the spirits obey you. Rejoice that your names are written in heaven."

At that same time Jesus was filled with joy through the Holy Spirit, and he said, "I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and clever, and shown them to little children. Yes, Father, this pleased you.

Then he turned to his followers and said, "Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son, and those to whom the Son chooses to show him."
Then he turned to his followers and said privately, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, but they did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but they did not hear it."
An expert in the law stood up to test Jesus. "Teacher," he asked, "what must I do to receive eternal life?"
Jesus said, "What is written in the Law? How do you read it?"
He answered, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and love your neighbour as yourself."
"You have answered correctly," Jesus said. "Do this and you will live."
But the man wanted to show that he was in the right, so he asked Jesus, "And who is my neighbour?"
Jesus replied, "A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho. He fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
By chance a priest was going down the same road. When he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.
In the same way a Levite came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the other side.
But a Samaritan who was travelling came to where the man was. When he saw him, he felt deep pity.
He went to him, bandaged his wounds, and poured on oil and wine. Then he put the man on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, 'Look after him. When I come back, I will pay you for anything extra you spend.'
Which of these three do you think was a neighbour to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?"
The expert in the law replied, "The one who showed him mercy." Jesus said, "Go and do the same."
As they travelled on, Jesus came to a village where a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to his word.
But Martha was distracted by all the work she had to do. She came to him and said, "Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me."
The Lord answered, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things.
But only one thing is needed. Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her."
One day Jesus was praying in a certain place. When he finished, one of his followers said to him, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his followers."
He said to them, "When you pray, say, 'Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us each day our daily bread.
Forgive us our sins, because we also forgive everyone who owes us. And do not lead us into testing, but save us from the evil one.'"
Then he said to them, "Suppose one of you has a friend, and you go to him at midnight and say, 'Friend, lend me three loaves of bread.
A friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to give him.'
And suppose he answers from inside, 'Do not bother me. The door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything.'
I tell you, even if he will not get up and give you the bread because he is your friend, he will get up because you keep asking, and he will give you as much as you need.
So I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given to you. Keep looking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and the door will be opened to you.
Everyone who asks receives. The one who looks finds. And the door will be opened to the one who knocks.
Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?"
Jesus was driving out a demon that could not speak. When the demon had gone out, the man who had been unable to speak began to speak, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said, "He drives out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons."
Others tested him by asking for a sign from heaven.
Jesus knew their thoughts and said, "Every kingdom that fights against itself is ruined, and a house that is divided against itself falls.
If Satan also fights against himself, how can his kingdom stand? You say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
But if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your followers drive them out? So they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come to you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own house, his things are safe.
But when someone stronger attacks him and wins, he takes away the armour the man trusted in, and he divides up what he stole.
Whoever is not with me is against me. And whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When an evil spirit comes out of a person, it goes through dry places looking for rest, and it does not find any. Then it says, 'I will go back to the house I left.'
When it returns, it finds the house swept and tidy.
Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and live there. So that person's last state is worse than the first."
As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out, "Blessed is the womb that carried you, and the breasts that nursed you!"
But he said, "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it."
As the crowds grew larger, Jesus said, "The people of today are evil. They ask for a sign, but none will be given to them except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
Just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be a sign to the people of today.

The Queen of the South will rise up at the judgement with the people of today and condemn them. She came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, and look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
The people of Nineveh will stand up at the judgement with this generation and condemn it, because they turned from their sins when Jonah preached. And look, someone greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. They put it on a stand, so that people who come in can see the light.
Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light. But when it is bad, your body is full of darkness.
So make sure that the light in you is not darkness.
If your whole body is full of light, with no dark part, it will be completely bright, as when a lamp shines on you with its light."
When Jesus had finished speaking, a Pharisee invited him to eat with him. So he went in and sat down at the table.
The Pharisee was surprised that Jesus did not wash before the meal.
The Lord said to him, "You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but inside you are full of greed and evil.
You foolish people! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
So give what is inside to the poor, and then everything will be clean for you.

But how terrible for you Pharisees! You give a tenth of your mint, rue, and every herb, but you neglect justice and the love of God. You should have done these things, without leaving the others undone.
How terrible for you Pharisees! You love the best seats in the synagogues and to be greeted in the market places.
How terrible for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like unmarked graves that people walk over without knowing it."
One of the experts in the law answered, "Teacher, when you say these things you insult us too."
Jesus said, "How terrible for you experts in the law as well! You load people with burdens that are hard to carry, and you yourselves will not lift even one finger to help them.
How terrible for you! You build tombs for the prophets, and it was your fathers who killed them.
So you show that you agree with what your fathers did. They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
Because of this, the wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles. They will kill some of them and hunt down others,
so that the people of today will be held responsible for the blood of all the prophets shed since the world was made,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who was killed between the altar and the holy place.' Yes, I tell you, the people of today will be held responsible.
How terrible for you experts in the law! You have taken away the key of knowledge. You did not go in yourselves, and you stopped those who were trying to go in."
When Jesus left there, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to oppose him fiercely and to question him about many things.
They were waiting to trap him in something he might say, so that they could accuse him.

Meanwhile, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so many that they were trampling on one another. Jesus began to speak first to his followers. "Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees," he said. "That yeast is pretending to be good.
Nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered, and nothing is hidden that will not be made known.
So whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light. And what you have whispered in inner rooms will be shouted from the rooftops.
I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
But I will show you the one you should fear. Fear the one who, after killing you, has power to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet God does not forget even one of them.
Even the hairs of your head are all counted. So do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you, whoever says in front of people that they belong to me, the Son of Man will also say that they belong to him in front of the angels of God.
But whoever denies me in front of people will be denied in front of the angels of God.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks evil against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say.
The Holy Spirit will teach you at that time what you should say."
Someone in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
Jesus replied, "Friend, who made me a judge or a divider over you?"
Then he said to them, "Watch out! Guard yourselves against every kind of greed. Life is not made up of how many things you own."
And he told them this story. "The ground of a rich man produced a very large crop.
He thought to himself, 'What shall I do? I do not have anywhere to store my crops.'
Then he said, 'This is what I will do. I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to myself, "You have plenty of good things stored up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and enjoy yourself."'
But God said to him, 'You fool! This very night your life will be demanded from you. Then who will get the things you have prepared?'
This is how it will be for anyone who stores up things for themselves but is not rich towards God."
Then Jesus said to his followers, "So I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothes.
Think about the ravens. They do not sow or reap. They have no storeroom or barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than birds!
Which of you, by worrying, can add even a little to your height?
If you cannot do even that small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
Think about the lilies, how they grow. They do not work or spin cloth. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.
If that is how God clothes the grass in the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, how much more will he clothe you, you who have so little faith!
Do not keep looking for what you will eat or drink, and do not worry.
The nations of the world run after all these things, but your Father knows that you need them.
Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well.
Do not be afraid, little flock, because your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell what you have and give to the poor. Make purses for yourselves that will not wear out, a treasure in heaven that will never fail, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Be dressed and ready, and keep your lamps burning.
Be like servants waiting for their master to come back from a wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they can open the door for him at once.
Blessed are those servants whose master finds them watching when he comes. I tell you for certain, he will dress himself to serve, have them sit down to eat, and he will come and serve them.
They will be blessed if he comes in the middle of the night, or near morning, and finds them ready.
But understand this. If the owner of the house had known what time the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and not let his house be broken into.
You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him."
Peter asked, "Lord, are you telling this story to us, or to everyone?"
The Lord answered, "Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their food at the right time?
Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing this when he comes.
I tell you the truth, he will put him in charge of everything he owns.
But suppose that servant says to himself, 'My master is taking a long time to come,' and he begins to beat the men and women servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know. He will cut him in pieces and give him a place with those who are unfaithful.
The servant who knew his master's will but did not get ready or do what the master wanted will be beaten with many blows.

But the one who did not know, and did things that deserved a beating, will be beaten with few blows. Much will be required from everyone who has been given much. And even more will be asked from the one who was trusted with much.
I have come to bring fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already burning!
But I have a baptism to go through, and how hard it is for me until it is finished!
Do you think I came to bring peace on earth? No, I tell you, I came to bring division.
From now on there will be five people in one house, divided, three against two and two against three.
They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
He also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, 'A shower is coming,' and it does.
And when the south wind blows, you say, 'It will be scorching hot,' and it is.
You hypocrites! You know how to read the look of the earth and the sky. Why can you not read this present time?
Why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

When you are on the way to court with someone who has a claim against you, try hard to settle with them before you get there. Otherwise they may drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny."
At that time some people told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus answered, "Do you think those Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered like that?
I tell you, no. But unless you turn from your sins, you will all die in the same way.
Or those eighteen people who were killed when the tower in Siloam fell on them. Do you think they were worse offenders than everyone else living in Jerusalem?
I tell you, no. But unless you turn from your sins, you will all die in the same way."
Then he told this story. "A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
So he said to the man who looked after the vines, 'Look, for three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and found none. Cut it down! Why should it waste the soil?'
The man answered, 'Sir, leave it for one more year. I will dig around it and put manure on it.
If it bears fruit next year, good. If not, then you can cut it down.'"
Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
A woman was there who had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not stand up straight at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said, "Woman, you are set free from your sickness."
He laid his hands on her, and straight away she stood up straight and gave glory to God.
The synagogue leader was angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. He said to the crowd, "There are six days for work. So come and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath."
The Lord answered him, "You hypocrites! Does not each of you untie your ox or donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead it out to drink?
Then should not this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be set free on the Sabbath?"
When he said this, all who opposed him were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the wonderful things he was doing.
Then Jesus said, "What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it with?
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky made their nests in its branches."
Again he said, "What shall I compare the kingdom of God with?
It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until it worked through all the dough."
Jesus went through towns and villages, teaching as he travelled on towards Jerusalem.
Someone asked him, "Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?" He said to them,
"Try hard to enter through the narrow door. I tell you, many will try to enter and will not be able to.
Once the owner of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, 'Lord, Lord, open the door for us.' But he will answer, 'I do not know you or where you come from.'
Then you will say, 'We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.'
But he will reply, 'I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Go away from me, all you who do evil.'
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrown outside.
People will come from east and west, and from north and south, and will sit down at the feast in the kingdom of God.
And look, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last."
At that time some Pharisees came to Jesus and said, "Leave this place and go somewhere else. Herod wants to kill you."
He replied, "Go and tell that fox, 'I drive out demons and heal people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I finish my work.
But I must keep going today, tomorrow, and the next day, because it cannot be that a prophet dies outside Jerusalem.'

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I have wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not let me!
Look, your house is left empty. I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!'"
One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat at the house of a leading Pharisee, and they were watching him closely.
In front of him was a man whose body was swollen with fluid.
Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, "Is it right to heal on the Sabbath, or not?"
But they stayed silent. So he took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
Then he asked them, "If your son, or your ox, falls into a well on the Sabbath, would you not pull him out at once?"
And they could not answer him.
Jesus noticed how the guests chose the best seats, so he told them this story.
"When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not sit in the best seat. Someone more honoured than you may have been invited.
Then the one who invited you both will come and say to you, 'Give this person your seat.' And you will be ashamed and have to take the lowest place.

Instead, when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place. Then, when your host comes, he will say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will be honoured in front of everyone at the table with you.
Everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up."

Then Jesus said to his host, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or your rich neighbours. They might invite you back, and that would be your repayment.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, those who cannot walk well, those who cannot walk, and those who are blind.
Then you will be blessed, because they cannot pay you back. You will be paid back when those who are right with God rise from the dead."
When one of the guests heard this, he said to Jesus, "Blessed is the person who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God!"
Jesus replied, "A man prepared a great feast and invited many people.
When it was time, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, 'Come, everything is ready now.'
But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said, 'I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please excuse me.'
Another said, 'I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am on my way to try them out. Please excuse me.'
Still another said, 'I have just got married, so I cannot come.'

The servant came back and reported this to his master. Then the owner of the house was angry and said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town, and bring in the poor, those who cannot walk well, those who are blind, and those who cannot walk.'
The servant said, 'Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.'
Then the master told the servant, 'Go out to the roads and the country lanes and urge people to come in, so that my house will be full.
I tell you, not one of those who were invited will taste my feast. Many are invited, but few are chosen.'"
Large crowds were travelling with Jesus. He turned and said to them,
"If anyone comes to me and does not love me more than father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, even their own life, that person cannot be my follower.
Whoever does not carry their own cross and follow me cannot be my follower.
Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Will you not first sit down and work out the cost, to see if you have enough to finish it?
Otherwise, if you lay the foundation and cannot finish, everyone who sees it will mock you,
saying, 'This person began to build and was not able to finish.'
Or suppose a king is going to war against another king. Will he not first sit down and consider whether he can face, with ten thousand men, the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If he cannot, he will send messengers while the other is still far away and ask for terms of peace.
In the same way, any of you who does not give up everything you have cannot be my follower.
Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, how can it be made salty again?
It is no good for the soil or for the manure heap. It is thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
Tax collectors and sinners were all crowding close to Jesus to hear him.
The Pharisees and the teachers of the law muttered, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
So Jesus told them this story.
"Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Will you not leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost one until you find it?
And when you find it, you carry it on your shoulders, full of joy.
Then you go home and call your friends and neighbours together and say, 'Rejoice with me. I have found my lost sheep!'
I tell you, in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who turns from their sins than over ninety-nine people who are right with God and do not need to turn.
Or suppose a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. Will she not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbours together and says, 'Rejoice with me. I have found the coin I lost!'
In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who turns from their sins."
Then he said, "A man had two sons.
The younger one said to his father, 'Father, give me my share of the property.' So the father divided his wealth between them.
Not long after that, the younger son got everything together and went to a country far away. There he wasted his wealth in wild living.
When he had spent everything, a severe famine came on that country, and he began to be in need.
He went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into the fields to feed pigs.
He was so hungry that he wanted to fill his stomach with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
Then he came to his senses and said, 'How many of my father's hired workers have more than enough bread, and here I am dying of hunger!
I will get up and go to my father, and I will say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers."'
So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt deep pity. He ran to his son, threw his arms around him, and kissed him.
The son said, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
But the father said to his servants, 'Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us eat and celebrate.
This son of mine was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.' And they began to celebrate.
Meanwhile, the older son was in the field. As he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
The servant said, 'Your brother has come home, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and well.'
The older brother was angry and would not go in. So his father went out and begged him.
But he answered his father, 'Look! All these years I have served you and never disobeyed your command. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came home, after wasting your wealth with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him!'
The father said, 'Son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.'"
Jesus also said to his followers, "There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
So he called him in and asked, 'What is this I hear about you? Give me an account of your management, because you cannot be manager any longer.'
The manager said to himself, 'What shall I do now? My master is taking the manager's job away from me. I am not strong enough to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do, so that when I lose my job people will welcome me into their homes.'
So he called in each of his master's debtors. He asked the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
'A hundred measures of olive oil,' he replied. The manager told him, 'Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.'
Then he asked another, 'And how much do you owe?' 'A hundred measures of wheat,' he replied. He told him, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
The master praised the dishonest manager because he had acted cleverly. The people of this world are more clever in dealing with their own kind than the people of the light are.
I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone they will welcome you into eternal homes.
Whoever is faithful with very little is also faithful with much. And whoever is dishonest with very little is also dishonest with much.
So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate one and love the other, or he will be loyal to one and look down on the other. You cannot serve God and money."
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and sneered at Jesus.
He said to them, "You are the ones who make yourselves look right in people's eyes, but God knows your hearts. What people value highly is hated in God's sight.
The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since then, the good news of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is trying hard to enter it.
But it is easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for the smallest mark of a pen to drop out of the Law.
Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. And the man who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.
At his gate lay a beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores.
He longed to eat what fell from the rich man's table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
The beggar died, and the angels carried him to Abraham's side. The rich man also died and was buried.
In the place of the dead, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus at his side.
So he called out, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in agony in this fire.'
But Abraham replied, 'Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, and you are in agony.
And besides all this, a great gap has been set between us and you, so that those who want to go from here to you cannot, and no one can cross from there to us.'
He answered, 'Then I beg you, father, send him to my father's house,
for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also come to this place of torment.'
Abraham said, 'They have Moses and the Prophets. Let them listen to them.'
He said, 'No, father Abraham. But if someone from the dead goes to them, they will turn from their sins.'
Abraham said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.'"
Jesus said to his followers, "Things that make people fall into sin are sure to come, but how terrible for the person through whom they come!
It would be better for them if a millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the sea, than for them to cause one of these little ones to fall into sin.
Be careful. If your brother sins against you, tell him he is wrong. If he turns from it, forgive him.
If he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times comes back and says, 'I am sorry,' you must forgive him."
The apostles said to the Lord, "Give us more faith."
The Lord said, "If you had faith as small as a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, 'Be pulled up by the roots and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Suppose one of you has a servant who is ploughing or looking after sheep. When he comes in from the field, will you say to him, 'Come at once and sit down to eat'?
Will you not rather say, 'Prepare my supper, get yourself ready, and serve me while I eat and drink. After that you can eat and drink'?
Will you thank the servant because he did what he was told? I do not think so.
So you also, when you have done everything you were told to do, should say, 'We are servants who deserve nothing. We have only done our duty.'"
On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus travelled along the border between Samaria and Galilee.
As he entered a village, ten men with skin diseases met him. They stood at a distance
and called out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
When he saw them, he said, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And as they went, they were made clean.
One of them, when he saw that he was healed, came back, praising God with a loud voice.
He threw himself at Jesus's feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus asked, "Were not all ten made clean? Where are the other nine?
Was no one found to come back and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
Then he said to the man, "Get up and go. Your faith has healed you."
Once the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come. He answered, "The kingdom of God does not come in a way you can see it coming.
People will not say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'Look, there it is!' Because the kingdom of God is among you."
Then he said to his followers, "The time will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
People will tell you, 'Look, there he is!' or 'Look, here he is!' Do not go running after them.
For the Son of Man in his day will be like the lightning, which flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by the people of today.
Just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
People were eating, drinking, marrying, and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
It was the same in the days of Lot. People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulphur rained down from the sky and destroyed them all.
It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is shown.
On that day, anyone on the roof, with their belongings in the house, must not go down to get them. Anyone in the field must not turn back.
Remember Lot's wife!
Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life will keep it.
I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed. One will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other left."
They asked him, "Where, Lord?" He said, "Where there is a dead body, there the vultures will gather."
Then Jesus told them a story to show that they should always pray and not give up.
He said, "In a certain town there was a judge who did not fear God and did not care about people.
A widow in that town kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against the person who is against me!'
For a while he refused. But finally he said to himself, 'Even though I do not fear God or care about people,
yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice. Otherwise she will wear me out by coming again and again.'"
The Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says.
Will God not give justice to his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night? Will he keep putting them off?
I tell you, he will give them justice quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He also told this story to some who were sure they were right with God and looked down on everyone else.
"Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other was a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, 'God, I thank you that I am not like other people: robbers, evildoers, those who are unfaithful in marriage, or even like this tax collector.
I go without food twice a week, and I give a tenth of all I get.'
But the tax collector stood far off. He would not even look up to heaven. He beat his chest and said, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'
I tell you, this man, and not the other, went home right with God. Everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up."
People were also bringing babies to Jesus so that he would touch them. When the followers saw this, they told the people off.
But Jesus called the children to him and said, "Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them, because the kingdom of God belongs to people like these.
I tell you for certain, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it."
A certain ruler asked him, "Good Teacher, what must I do to receive eternal life?"
Jesus asked him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about anyone. Honour your father and your mother.'"
He said, "I have kept all these since I was young."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "You still lack one thing. Sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
When the man heard this, he became very sad, because he was very rich.
Jesus saw how sad he was and said, "How hard it is for rich people to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
Those who heard this asked, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus replied, "What is impossible with people is possible with God."
Peter said, "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
Jesus said, "I tell you for certain, no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
will fail to receive many times as much in this life, and in the age to come, eternal life."
Jesus took the twelve aside and said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will come true.
He will be handed over to the Gentiles. They will mock him, treat him shamefully, and spit on him.
They will whip him and kill him. On the third day he will rise again."
The followers did not understand any of this. Its meaning was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what he said.
As Jesus came near Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road, begging.
When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
They told him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by."
He called out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Those in front told him off and said he should be quiet, but he shouted even louder, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered the man to be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
"What do you want me to do for you?" "Lord, I want to see again," he replied.
Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you."
Straight away he could see, and he followed Jesus, giving glory to God. When all the people saw it, they praised God.
Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through it.
A man there was named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he could not, because of the crowd, and because he was short.
So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see him, since Jesus was coming that way.
When Jesus reached the spot, he looked up and said, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down. I must stay at your house today."
Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed him with joy.
All the people who saw this muttered, "He has gone to be the guest of a sinner."
But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor. And if I have cheated anyone, I will pay back four times as much."
Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
The Son of Man came to look for and to save what was lost."
While the people were listening to this, Jesus went on to tell a story. He was near Jerusalem, and they thought the kingdom of God was going to appear at once.
He said, "A man of noble birth went to a country far away to be made king and then return.
He called ten of his servants and gave them ten mina coins. 'Do business with this until I come back,' he said.
But his people hated him and sent a group after him to say, 'We do not want this man to be our king.'
He was made king and came back. Then he sent for the servants he had given the money to, so that he could find out what they had gained by doing business.
The first came and said, 'Sir, your mina has earned ten more minas.'
'Well done, good servant!' he said. 'Because you have been faithful with a very small thing, you will be in charge of ten towns.'
The second came and said, 'Sir, your mina has earned five minas.'
He said, 'You will be in charge of five towns.'
Then another servant came and said, 'Sir, here is your mina. I kept it wrapped in a cloth,
because I was afraid of you. You are a hard man. You take what you did not put in, and you reap what you did not sow.'
His master replied, 'I will judge you by your own words, you wicked servant! You knew, did you, that I am a hard man, taking what I did not put in and reaping what I did not sow?
Then why did you not put my money in the bank, so that when I came back I could have collected it with interest?'
Then he said to those standing by, 'Take the mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.'
They said, 'Sir, he already has ten minas!'
He replied, 'I tell you, everyone who has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away.
But those enemies of mine who did not want me to be their king, bring them here and kill them in front of me.'"
After Jesus had said this, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
As he came near Bethsphage and Bethany, at the hill called Olivet, he sent two of his followers,
saying, "Go into the village ahead of you. As you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' say, 'The Lord needs it.'"
Those who were sent went and found it just as he had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners asked, "Why are you untying the colt?"
They replied, "The Lord needs it."
They brought it to Jesus, threw their coats on the colt, and put Jesus on it.
As he went along, people spread their coats on the road.
When he came near the place where the road goes down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of his followers began to praise God joyfully with loud voices for all the powerful works they had seen.
They shouted, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, "Teacher, tell your followers to be quiet!"
He answered, "I tell you, if they keep quiet, the stones will cry out."
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it
and said, "If you, even you, had known today what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
The days will come when your enemies will build a wall against you, surround you, and close you in on every side.
They will throw you and your children to the ground. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognise the time when God came to you."
Then Jesus entered the temple and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there.
He said, "It is written, 'My house will be a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
Every day he was teaching in the temple. But the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the leaders of the people were trying to kill him.
Yet they could not find a way to do it, because all the people were hanging on his words.
One day, as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the good news, the chief priests and the teachers of the law came up with the elders.
They said, "Tell us, by what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you this authority?"
He answered, "I will also ask you one question. Tell me:
John's baptism, was it from heaven, or from people?"
They talked it over among themselves. "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'From people,' all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John was a prophet."
So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you by what authority I do these things."
Then he told the people this story. "A man planted a vineyard, rented it to some farmers, and went away to another country for a long time.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit. But the farmers beat him and sent him away with nothing.
He sent another servant, and they beat him too, treated him shamefully, and sent him away with nothing.
He sent a third, and they wounded him and threw him out.
Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my son, whom I love. Maybe they will respect him.'
But when the farmers saw him, they talked it over. 'This is the heir,' they said. 'Let us kill him, so that the inheritance will be ours.'
So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and kill those farmers and give the vineyard to others." When the people heard this, they said, "May that never happen!"
Jesus looked straight at them and said, "Then what does this writing mean: 'The stone the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and anyone it falls on will be crushed."
The chief priests and the teachers of the law wanted to arrest him right then, but they were afraid of the people. They knew he had told this story against them.
So they watched him and sent spies who pretended to be honest. They hoped to catch Jesus in something he said, so they could hand him over to the power and authority of the governor.
The spies asked him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach what is right. You do not favour anyone, but teach the way of God truly.
Is it right for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?"
He saw through their trick and said, "Why are you testing me?
Show me a denarius. Whose image and name are on it?" "Caesar's," they replied.
He said, "Then give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to God what belongs to God."
They could not trap him in what he said in front of the people. Amazed at his answer, they became silent.
Some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, the man must marry the widow and raise up children for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died childless.
The second married her, and he also died childless.
Then the third married her, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
Finally the woman also died.
So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven were married to her."
Jesus replied, "The people of this age marry and are given in marriage.
But those who are counted worthy to share in the age to come, and in the resurrection from the dead, will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
They cannot die any more, because they are like the angels. They are God's children, because they are children of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, because all are alive to him."
Some of the teachers of the law said, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
And they did not dare to ask him any more questions.
Then Jesus said to them, "Why do people say that the Christ is David's son?
David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
David calls him Lord. So how can he be his son?"
While all the people were listening, Jesus said to his followers,

"Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love to be greeted in the market places, and to have the best seats in the synagogues and the places of honour at feasts.
They take over widows' houses, and for a pretence they make long prayers. These men will be punished most severely."
Jesus looked up and saw rich people putting their gifts into the temple offering box.
He also saw a poor widow put in two small brass coins.
He said, "I tell you the truth, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.
They all gave gifts out of what they had to spare. But she, out of her poverty, put in all she had to live on."
Some of his followers were talking about the temple, how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts offered to God. Jesus said,
"As for what you see here, the days will come when not one stone will be left on another. Every one of them will be thrown down."
They asked him, "Teacher, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?"
He replied, "Watch out that you are not led astray. Many will come in my name, saying, 'I am he,' and, 'The time is near.' Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and riots, do not be terrified. These things must happen first, but the end will not come at once."
Then he said, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in many places. There will be fearful events and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, people will arrest you and persecute you. They will hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and bring you before kings and governors because of my name.
This will be your chance to speak for me.
So make up your minds not to worry beforehand about how you will defend yourselves.
I will give you words and wisdom that none of your enemies will be able to resist or contradict.
You will even be handed over by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
Everyone will hate you because of my name.
But not a hair of your head will be lost.
By standing firm you will gain your lives.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its destruction is near.
Then those in Judea must run to the mountains. Those inside the city must leave. Those in the country must not enter the city.
These are days of punishment, so that everything that is written will come true.
How terrible for women who are pregnant and for those nursing babies in those days! There will be great distress in the land and anger against this people.
They will fall by the sword and be taken as prisoners to all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are finished.
There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars. On the earth, nations will be in anguish and confusion at the roaring of the sea and the waves.
People will faint from fear and from dread of what is coming on the world, because the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift your heads, because the time when you will be set free is near."
Then he told them this story. "Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
When they sprout leaves, you see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
I tell you for certain, the people of today will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
Be careful, or your hearts will be weighed down with wild living, drunkenness, and the worries of life, and that day will close on you suddenly like a trap.
It will come on everyone who lives on the face of the whole earth.
So stay awake at all times, and pray that you may be counted worthy to escape all that is about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
Each day Jesus taught in the temple, and each evening he went out and spent the night on the hill called Olivet.
And all the people came early in the morning to the temple to hear him.
The feast of bread made without yeast, which is called the Passover, was near.
The chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for a way to kill Jesus, because they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, called Iscariot, who was one of the twelve.
Judas went and discussed with the chief priests and the temple officers how he could hand Jesus over to them.
They were glad and agreed to give him money.
He agreed, and he looked for a chance to hand Jesus over when the crowd was not there.
Then the day of bread made without yeast came, the day the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, "Go and prepare the Passover meal for us, so that we can eat it."
They asked, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"
He said, "Listen. When you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters.
Tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher asks you, "Where is the guest room, where I can eat the Passover with my followers?"'
He will show you a large upstairs room, already furnished. Prepare the meal there."
They went and found things just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, he sat down at the table with the twelve apostles.
He said to them, "I have very much wanted to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
Then he took a cup, and when he had given thanks he said, "Take this and share it among yourselves.
I tell you, I will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in memory of me."
In the same way, after supper he took the cup, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
But look, the hand of the one who is betraying me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man will go as it has been decided, but how terrible for the man who betrays him!"
They began to ask one another which of them would do this.
They also began to argue about which of them was thought to be the greatest.
Jesus said, "The kings of the nations rule over them, and those who have power over them call themselves friends of the people.
But you must not be like that. Instead, the greatest among you should become like the youngest, and the leader should become like the one who serves.
Who is greater, the one who sits at the table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stayed with me in my trials.
And I give you a kingdom, just as my Father gave one to me,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom. And you will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel."
The Lord said, "Simon, Simon, listen! Satan has asked to have all of you, so that he can shake you like wheat.
But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."
Peter said, "Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death!"
Jesus answered, "I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today before you have said three times that you do not know me."
Then he said to them, "When I sent you out without a money bag, a bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?" "Nothing," they answered.
He said, "But now, if you have a money bag, take it, and also a bag. And if you do not have a sword, sell your coat and buy one.
I tell you, this writing must still come true in me: 'He was counted with the lawbreakers.' Yes, what is written about me is coming true."
They said, "Lord, look, here are two swords." He replied, "That is enough."
Jesus went out and made his way, as usual, to the Mount of Olives, and his followers followed him.
When he reached the place, he said to them, "Pray that you will not fall into temptation."
He withdrew from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and prayed,
"Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me. Yet not my will, but yours, be done."
An angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him.
Being in agony, he prayed even harder, and his sweat became like great drops of blood falling to the ground.
When he rose from prayer and went back to the followers, he found them asleep, worn out by sadness.
"Why are you sleeping?" he asked. "Get up and pray, so that you will not fall into temptation."
While he was still speaking, a crowd came up, and the man called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came close to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus asked, "Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?"
When those around Jesus saw what was about to happen, they said, "Lord, shall we strike with our swords?"
And one of them struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus said, "No more of this!" And he touched the man's ear and healed him.
Then Jesus said to the chief priests, the temple officers, and the elders who had come for him, "Have you come out with swords and clubs, as if I were a robber?
Every day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lay a hand on me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness."
They seized him, led him away, and took him into the high priest's house. Peter followed at a distance.
They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, and Peter sat among them.
A servant girl saw him sitting there in the firelight. She looked closely at him and said, "This man was also with him."
But he denied it. "Woman, I do not know him," he said.
A little later someone else saw him and said, "You also are one of them." "Man, I am not!" Peter replied.
About an hour later, another man insisted, "Certainly this man was with him, because he is a Galilean."
Peter replied, "Man, I do not know what you are talking about!" Just as he was speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord's word, how he had said, "Before the rooster crows today, you will deny me three times."
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who were guarding Jesus mocked him and beat him.
They blindfolded him and kept asking, "Prophesy! Who hit you?"
And they said many other insulting things to him.
At daybreak the elders of the people met together, both chief priests and teachers of the law. They led Jesus into their council
and said, "If you are the Christ, tell us." He replied, "If I tell you, you will not believe me.
And if I asked you, you would not answer.
But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
They all asked, "Are you then the Son of God?" He replied, "You say that I am."
Then they said, "Why do we need any more witnesses? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth!"
The whole group of them got up and brought Jesus before Pilate.
They began to accuse him. "We found this man misleading our nation," they said. "He tells people not to pay taxes to Caesar, and he says that he himself is the Christ, a king."
Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" Jesus replied, "You say so."
Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no reason to charge this man."
But they kept insisting, "He stirs up the people, teaching all through Judea, from Galilee all the way to here."
When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
When he learned that Jesus was under Herod's authority, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at that time.
Herod was very glad to see Jesus. He had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard about him and hoped to see him do some miracle.
He asked Jesus many questions, but Jesus gave him no answer.
The chief priests and the teachers of the law stood there, accusing him fiercely.
Then Herod and his soldiers treated Jesus with contempt and mocked him. They dressed him in fine clothes and sent him back to Pilate.
That day Herod and Pilate became friends. Before this they had been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
and said to them, "You brought this man to me as one who turns the people against the law. I have examined him in front of you and found no reason for the charges you bring against him.
Neither did Herod, because he sent him back to us. Look, he has done nothing that deserves death.
So I will punish him and then let him go."
Now he was required to release one prisoner to them at the feast.
But they all shouted together, "Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!"
Barabbas had been thrown into prison for a revolt in the city, and for murder.
Pilate spoke to them again, because he wanted to release Jesus.
But they kept shouting, "Crucify him! Crucify him!"
He said to them a third time, "Why? What crime has this man committed? I have found no reason to put him to death. So I will punish him and let him go."
But they kept shouting at the top of their voices, demanding that he be crucified, and their voices won.
So Pilate decided to give them what they asked.
He released the man who had been thrown into prison for revolt and murder, the one they asked for, and he handed Jesus over to do what they wanted.
As they led Jesus away, they seized Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, and they put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A large crowd of people followed, including women who mourned and cried for him.
Jesus turned to them and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me. Weep for yourselves and for your children.
Look, the days are coming when people will say, 'Blessed are the women who could not have children, the wombs that never gave birth, and the breasts that never nursed.'
Then they will say to the mountains, 'Fall on us!' and to the hills, 'Cover us!'
If they do these things when the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?"
Two other men, both criminals, were also led out with him to be put to death.
When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified him there, with the criminals, one on his right and one on his left.
Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they are doing." And they divided up his clothes by throwing dice.
The people stood watching. The rulers sneered at him and said, "He saved others. Let him save himself, if he is the Christ of God, the Chosen One!"
The soldiers also mocked him. They came up and offered him sour wine,
and said, "If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!"
There was a notice above him, written in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: "THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS."
One of the criminals hanging there insulted him. "Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us!"
But the other criminal spoke firmly to him. "Do you not even fear God?" he said. "You are under the same sentence.
We are punished justly. We are getting what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong."
Then he said, "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
Jesus answered, "I tell you for certain, today you will be with me in Paradise."
It was now about noon, and darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon.
The sun stopped shining, and the curtain of the temple was torn in two.
Jesus called out with a loud voice, "Father, into your hands I place my spirit." When he had said this, he breathed his last.
When the Roman officer saw what had happened, he praised God and said, "Certainly this was a good man."
When all the crowds who had gathered to see this saw what happened, they went home beating their chests.
All those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed him from Galilee, stood at a distance, watching these things.
There was a man named Joseph, a member of the council. He was a good and upright man.
He had not agreed with their decision or their action. He came from Arimathaea, a Jewish town, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus's body.
Then he took it down, wrapped it in linen cloth, and laid it in a tomb cut in the rock, where no one had ever been laid.
It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph. They saw the tomb and how his body was laid in it.
Then they went home and prepared spices and perfumes. But they rested on the Sabbath, as the commandment said.
On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women went to the tomb, taking the spices they had prepared. Some other women went with them.
They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
When they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
While they were wondering about this, suddenly two men in clothes that shone like lightning stood beside them.
The women were terrified and bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, "Why do you look for the living among the dead?
He is not here. He has risen. Remember what he told you while he was still in Galilee.
He said the Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men, be crucified, and on the third day rise again."
Then they remembered his words.
They returned from the tomb and told all this to the eleven and to all the others.
It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.
But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and saw the strips of linen lying by themselves. Then he went home, wondering what had happened.
That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
As they talked and discussed, Jesus himself came near and walked along with them.
But they were kept from recognising him.
He asked them, "What are you discussing as you walk along, looking so sad?"
One of them, named Cleopas, answered, "Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there these days?"
"What things?" he asked. "The things about Jesus of Nazareth," they replied. "He was a prophet, powerful in what he did and said before God and all the people.
The chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they crucified him.
But we had hoped that he was the one who would set Israel free. And what is more, it is now the third day since all this happened.
Then some women from our group amazed us. They went to the tomb early this morning
and did not find his body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said he was alive.
Some of our friends went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him."
He said to them, "How foolish you are, and how slow to believe everything the prophets have said!
Did the Christ not have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?"
And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he explained to them what was said in all the Scriptures about himself.
As they came near the village they were going to, Jesus acted as if he were going further.
But they urged him, "Stay with us. It is nearly evening, and the day is almost over." So he went in to stay with them.
When he was at the table with them, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and began to give it to them.
Then their eyes were opened and they recognised him, and he disappeared from their sight.
They said to each other, "Were not our hearts burning inside us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?"
They got up at once and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the eleven and those with them, gathered together
and saying, "The Lord has indeed risen, and he has appeared to Simon!"
Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognised him when he broke the bread.
While they were still talking about this, Jesus himself stood among them and said, "Peace to you."
They were startled and frightened, thinking they were seeing a ghost.
He said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts rise in your minds?
Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself. Touch me and see. A ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have."
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
They still did not believe it, because of joy and amazement. So he asked them, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
They gave him a piece of cooked fish and some honeycomb.
He took it and ate it in front of them.
He said to them, "This is what I told you while I was still with you. Everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must come true."
Then he opened their minds so they could understand the Scriptures.
He told them, "This is what is written: the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and turning from sins and the forgiveness of sins will be preached in his name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
Listen! I am sending you what my Father promised. But stay in the city until you are clothed with power from above."
Then he led them out as far as Bethany, lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven.
They worshipped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they stayed continually at the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
John: In the beginning the Word already existed. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
God made everything through him. Nothing that exists was made without him.
Life was in him, and that life was the light for all people.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has never overcome it.
God sent a man whose name was John.
He came to tell people about the light, so that everyone could believe because of what he said.
John himself was not the light. He came to tell people about the light.
The true light, who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, but the world did not recognise him.
He came to his own people, but his own people did not welcome him.
But to all who did welcome him, those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God.
They became God's children, not by being born in the normal human way, not because of human desire or a husband's choice, but because God gave them new birth.
The Word became a human being and lived among us. We saw his glory, the glory of the only Son, who came from the Father. He was full of grace and truth.
John told people about him. He called out, "This is the one I was talking about when I said, 'The one who comes after me is greater than I am, because he existed before I was born.'"
From all that he has in full, we have all received one gift of grace after another.
The law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God. But the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, has shown us what God is like.
This is what John said when the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, "Who are you?"
He did not refuse to answer. He told them plainly, "I am not the Christ, the Messiah."
They asked him, "Then who are you? Are you Elijah?" He said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet we are expecting?" He answered, "No."
Then they said, "Tell us who you are, so that we can give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
John answered in the words of the prophet Isaiah: "I am the voice of someone shouting in the desert, 'Make a straight road for the Lord.'"
Some of the people who had been sent were Pharisees.
They asked him, "If you are not the Christ, or Elijah, or the Prophet, why are you baptising people?"
John answered, "I baptise with water. But someone is standing among you whom you do not know.
He is the one who comes after me, and he is greater than I am. I am not good enough even to untie the straps of his sandals."
All this happened at Bethany, on the other side of the Jordan River, where John was baptising.
The next day John saw Jesus coming towards him. He said, "Look! There is the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
This is the one I meant when I said, 'A man who comes after me is greater than I am, because he existed before I was born.'
I did not know who he was. But I came baptising with water so that he could be made known to the people of Israel."
Then John said, "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and stay on him.
I still did not know who he was. But God, who sent me to baptise with water, told me, 'You will see the Spirit come down and stay on someone. He is the one who will baptise with the Holy Spirit.'
I have seen this happen, and I tell you that he is the Son of God."
The next day John was there again with two of his followers.
When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, "Look! There is the Lamb of God!"
When the two followers heard him say this, they went after Jesus.
Jesus turned round and saw them following him. He asked them, "What are you looking for?" They said, "Rabbi (which means Teacher), where are you staying?"
He replied, "Come and you will see." So they went and saw where he was staying, and they spent the rest of that day with him. It was about four o'clock in the afternoon.
One of the two men who heard what John said and then followed Jesus was Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter.
The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, "We have found the Messiah" (which means the Christ).
Then Andrew brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon, the son of Jonah. But you will be called Cephas" (which means Peter, or "rock").
The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, "Follow me."
Philip came from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, and the prophets also wrote about him. He is Jesus from Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
Nathanael asked, "Nazareth! Can anything good come from there?" Philip said, "Come and see."
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming towards him, he said about him, "Here is a true man of Israel. There is nothing false in him."
Nathanael asked, "How do you know me?" Jesus answered, "I saw you under the fig tree before Philip called you."
Then Nathanael said, "Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"
Jesus said to him, "Do you believe just because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see much greater things than that."
Then he said, "I tell you for certain, you will see heaven open, and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man."
Two days later there was a wedding in the town of Cana in Galilee. The mother of Jesus was there,
and Jesus and his followers had also been invited to the wedding.
When the wine ran out, Jesus' mother said to him, "They have no more wine."
Jesus replied, "Dear woman, why do you involve me? My time has not yet come."
His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."
Six stone water jars were standing there. The Jewish people used them for their washing ceremonies. Each jar could hold between eighty and a hundred and twenty litres.
Jesus told the servants, "Fill the jars with water." So they filled them right to the top.
Then he told them, "Now pour some out and take it to the man in charge of the feast." So they did.
The man in charge tasted the water that had now become wine. He did not know where it had come from, but the servants who had poured the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside
and said to him, "Everyone serves the best wine first. Then, when the guests have had plenty to drink, they bring out the cheaper wine. But you have kept the best wine until now!"
This was the first of the miraculous signs that Jesus did. It happened in Cana in Galilee. In this way he showed his glory, and his followers believed in him.
After this, Jesus went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers and his followers. They stayed there for a few days.
It was nearly time for the Jewish Passover festival, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep and doves. Others were sitting at tables, exchanging money.
So Jesus made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple, together with the sheep and cattle. He scattered the coins of the money changers and turned over their tables.
He told those who were selling doves, "Get these things out of here! Stop turning my Father's house into a market!"
His followers remembered that the Scriptures say, "My love for your house burns in me like a fire."
Then the Jewish leaders asked him, "What miraculous sign can you show us to prove that you have the right to do this?"
Jesus answered, "Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up again in three days."
The leaders replied, "It has taken forty-six years to build this temple. Are you going to raise it up in three days?"
But the temple Jesus was speaking about was his own body.
After he was raised from the dead, his followers remembered that he had said this. Then they believed the Scriptures and the words that Jesus had spoken.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem for the Passover festival, many people saw the miraculous signs he was doing and believed in him.
But Jesus did not trust himself to them, because he knew what all people are like.
No one needed to tell him about anyone, because he knew what was really in each person's heart.
There was a man named Nicodemus. He was a Pharisee and a leader of the Jewish people.
He came to Jesus at night and said, "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God. No one could do the miraculous signs you are doing unless God were with him."
Jesus replied, "I tell you for certain, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again."
Nicodemus asked, "How can someone be born when they are old? Surely they cannot go back into their mother's womb and be born a second time!"
