Jesus answered, "I tell you for certain, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit.
Human parents give birth to human life, but the Spirit gives birth to spiritual life.
So do not be surprised when I say, 'You must be born again.'
The wind blows wherever it wants to. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. It is the same with everyone who is born of the Spirit."
Nicodemus asked, "How can this be?"
Jesus said, "You are an important teacher in Israel, and you do not understand these things?
I tell you for certain, we speak about what we know, and we tell you what we have seen. But you people do not accept what we say.
I have told you about things that happen here on earth, and you do not believe me. So how will you believe if I tell you about things in heaven?
No one has ever gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
Moses lifted up the bronze snake on a pole in the desert. In the same way, the Son of Man must be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes in him will not be lost, but will have eternal life.
God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that no one who believes in him will be lost. Instead, they will have eternal life.
God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world. He sent him to save the world.
Whoever believes in him is not condemned. But whoever does not believe is condemned already, because they have not believed in the name of God's only Son.
This is how people are judged: the light has come into the world, but people loved the darkness more than the light, because the things they did were evil.
Everyone who does evil hates the light. They will not come into the light, because they are afraid that their deeds will be exposed.
But whoever lives by the truth comes into the light. Then everyone can clearly see that what they have done was done with God's help."
After this, Jesus and his followers went out into the countryside of Judea. He spent some time there with them, and they baptised people.
John was also baptising at Aenon, near Salim, because there was plenty of water there. People kept coming to him to be baptised.
This was before John was put in prison.
An argument started between some of John's followers and a certain Jewish man about the washing ceremonies.
So they came to John and said, "Rabbi, the man who was with you on the other side of the Jordan, the one you told us about, is baptising people. Everyone is going to him!"
John answered, "A person can only receive what God gives them from heaven.
You yourselves heard me say, 'I am not the Christ. I have been sent ahead of him.'
The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The bridegroom's friend waits and listens for him, and he is full of joy when he hears the bridegroom's voice. That is the joy I have, and now it is complete.
He must become more and more important, and I must become less important.
The one who comes from above is greater than all. Someone who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is greater than all.
He tells what he has seen and heard, but hardly anyone accepts what he says.
Whoever does accept what he says has put their stamp on this truth: God is true.
The one whom God has sent speaks the words of God, because God gives him the Spirit without limit.
The Father loves the Son and has put everything into his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. But whoever refuses to obey the Son will not see that life. Instead, God's anger stays on them."
The Pharisees heard that Jesus was making and baptising more followers than John. When Jesus learned about this,
(although in fact it was not Jesus himself who baptised, but his followers),
he left Judea and went back to Galilee.
On the way he had to pass through Samaria.
So he came to a town in Samaria called Sychar. It was near the field that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
Jacob's well was there. Jesus was tired from the long journey, so he sat down beside the well. It was about twelve o'clock, midday.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Please give me a drink."
His followers had gone into the town to buy food.
The Samaritan woman said to him, "You are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink?" (She said this because Jews do not usually have anything to do with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered, "If you knew the gift God gives, and who it is that is asking you for a drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
"Sir," the woman said, "you have nothing to draw water with, and the well is deep. Where can you get this living water?
Are you greater than our ancestor Jacob? He gave us this well. He drank from it himself, and so did his sons and his animals."
Jesus replied, "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water I give them will never be thirsty again. The water I give will become a spring inside them, bubbling up and giving them eternal life."
The woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water! Then I will not get thirsty, and I will not have to keep coming here to draw water."
Jesus told her, "Go and call your husband, and then come back."
"I do not have a husband," the woman replied. Jesus said to her, "You are right when you say you have no husband.
The truth is, you have had five husbands, and the man you are living with now is not your husband. What you have said is quite true."
"Sir," the woman said, "I can see that you are a prophet.
Our ancestors worshipped God on this mountain. But you Jews say that Jerusalem is the place where people must worship."
Jesus said, "Believe me, dear woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You Samaritans worship what you do not really know. We Jews worship what we do know, because salvation comes through the Jewish people.
But a time is coming, and it has already come, when true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth. These are the kind of worshippers the Father is looking for.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth."
The woman said, "I know that the Messiah, the one called Christ, is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us."
Then Jesus told her, "I am he, the one speaking to you now."
Just then his followers came back. They were surprised to find him talking with a woman. But none of them asked, "What do you want?" or "Why are you talking with her?"
Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town and said to the people,
"Come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done! Could he be the Christ?"
So the people came out of the town and went towards Jesus.
Meanwhile his followers were urging him, "Rabbi, eat something."
But he said to them, "I have food to eat that you know nothing about."
So his followers asked each other, "Did someone bring him food?"
Jesus said, "My food is to do what God, who sent me, wants, and to finish the work he gave me.
You have a saying: 'Four more months, and then it is harvest time.' But I tell you, open your eyes and look at the fields! They are ripe and ready for harvest.
Even now the person who harvests the crop is being paid. He is gathering a harvest of people for eternal life. So the one who plants and the one who harvests can celebrate together.
This proves the saying true: 'One person plants, and another harvests.'
I sent you to harvest a crop that you did not work for. Others did the hard work, and you have come in to gather the results of their work."
Many Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of what the woman said: "He told me everything I have ever done."
So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them, and he stayed there for two days.
Many more people believed because of what Jesus himself said.
They said to the woman, "Now we believe, not just because of what you told us. We have heard him ourselves, and we know that this man really is the Christ, the Saviour of the world."
After the two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
Jesus himself had said that a prophet is not honoured in his own home town.
When he arrived in Galilee, the people there welcomed him. They had seen everything he had done in Jerusalem during the Passover festival, because they had also been there.
Jesus came once more to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. A royal official was there whose son was sick in Capernaum.
This man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee. So he went to him and begged him to come and heal his son, because his son was close to death.
Jesus said to him, "Unless you people see miraculous signs and wonders, you will never believe."
The official said, "Sir, please come down before my child dies."
Jesus told him, "Go home. Your son will live." The man believed what Jesus said, and he went on his way.
While he was still on his way home, his servants met him with the news that his son was alive and well.
He asked them what time his son had started to get better. They said, "The fever left him yesterday at one o'clock in the afternoon."
Then the father realised that this was the exact time when Jesus had said to him, "Your son will live." So he and everyone in his household believed in Jesus.
This was the second miraculous sign that Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.
Some time later, Jesus went up to Jerusalem for one of the Jewish festivals.
In Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate, there is a pool which in the Hebrew language is called Bethesda. It is surrounded by five covered porches.
A large number of sick people used to lie in these porches: people who were blind, people who could not walk well, and people who were paralysed. They were waiting for the water to move.
From time to time an angel would come down into the pool and stir up the water. The first person to step into the pool after the water was stirred was healed of whatever disease they had.
One man lying there had been ill for thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been in this condition for a long time. So he asked him, "Do you want to get well?"
The sick man answered, "Sir, I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am trying to get in, someone else always goes down ahead of me."
Jesus said to him, "Get up! Pick up your mat and walk."
At once the man was healed. He picked up his mat and began to walk. This happened on a Sabbath day.
So the Jewish leaders said to the man who had been healed, "It is the Sabbath. The law does not allow you to carry your mat."
But he answered, "The man who healed me told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
They asked him, "Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?"
But the man who had been healed did not know who it was. Jesus had slipped away into the crowd that was there.
Later Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Look, you are well now. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you."
The man went away and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had healed him.
So the Jewish leaders began to persecute Jesus and looked for a way to kill him, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus said to them, "My Father is always at work, even to this day, and so I am working too."
Because of this, the leaders tried even harder to kill him. Not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was even calling God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
Jesus answered them, "I tell you for certain, the Son can do nothing by himself. He can only do what he sees his Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does too.
The Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. Yes, and he will show him even greater works than these, and you will be amazed.
Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son gives life to anyone he chooses.
The Father does not judge anyone. He has given the Son the task of judging,
so that everyone will honour the Son just as they honour the Father. Whoever does not honour the Son does not honour the Father who sent him.
I tell you for certain, whoever hears my message and believes the one who sent me has eternal life. They will not be condemned. They have already crossed over from death to life.
I tell you for certain, a time is coming, and has now come, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
The Father has life in himself, and he has also given the Son the power to have life in himself.
He has given him authority to judge, because he is the Son of Man.
Do not be amazed at this. A time is coming when all who are in their graves will hear his voice
and come out. Those who have done good will rise to live, and those who have done evil will rise to be judged and condemned.
I can do nothing on my own. I judge only as the Father tells me, and my judgement is fair, because I do not try to please myself. I want to please the one who sent me.
If I were the only one speaking for myself, what I say would not count as proof.
But there is someone else who speaks for me, and I know that what he says about me is true.
You sent messengers to John, and he spoke up for the truth.
I do not need anyone's human support, but I am telling you this so that you can be saved.
John was like a lamp that burned and gave light, and for a while you were glad to enjoy his light.
But I have proof that is greater than what John said. The work the Father has given me to finish, the very things I am doing, prove that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me has himself spoken for me. You have never heard his voice or seen what he looks like,
and his message does not live in you, because you do not believe the one he sent.
You study the Scriptures carefully, because you think that by them you will have eternal life. Yet these same Scriptures point to me!
But you refuse to come to me to receive life.
I am not looking for praise from people.
But I know you. I know that you do not have God's love in your hearts.
I have come in my Father's name, and you do not accept me. But if someone else comes in his own name, you will accept him.
How can you believe? You enjoy receiving praise from one another, but you make no effort to receive the praise that comes from the only God.
But do not think that I will accuse you in front of the Father. The one who accuses you is Moses, the one you have put your hope in.
If you really believed Moses, you would believe me, because he wrote about me.
But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?"
Some time after this, Jesus crossed to the far side of the Sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
A huge crowd kept following him, because they had seen the miraculous signs he did by healing the sick.
Then Jesus went up a hill and sat down there with his followers.
The Jewish Passover festival was coming soon.
Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming towards him. He said to Philip, "Where can we buy bread to feed all these people?"
He asked this only to test Philip, because he already knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered, "Even if we had more than half a year's wages, it would not buy enough bread for each person to have just a little!"
Another of his followers, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, spoke up.
"There is a boy here who has five small barley loaves and two small fish. But what good is that for so many people?"
Jesus said, "Tell the people to sit down." There was plenty of grass in that place, so they sat down. There were about five thousand men.

Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks to God and handed them to his followers, and they gave them out to the people who were sitting there. He did the same with the fish. Everyone had as much as they wanted.
When they had all eaten enough, he told his followers, "Gather the pieces that are left over. Let nothing be wasted."
So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves that were left over by the people who had eaten.
When the people saw the miraculous sign that Jesus had done, they began to say, "Surely this is the Prophet who was to come into the world!"
Jesus knew that they were about to come and take him by force to make him king. So he went away again to the hills by himself.
When evening came, his followers went down to the lake.
They got into a boat and started to cross the lake towards Capernaum. By now it was dark, and Jesus had not yet joined them.
A strong wind was blowing, and the water became rough.
They had rowed about five or six kilometres when they saw Jesus walking on the water and coming near the boat. They were terrified.
But he said to them, "It is I. Do not be afraid."
Then they were glad to take him into the boat, and straight away the boat reached the shore where they were heading.

The next day the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the lake realised something. Only one boat had been there, and Jesus had not got into it with his followers. They had gone away on their own.
Then some other boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
When the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor his followers were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Jesus.
They found him on the other side of the lake and asked him, "Rabbi, when did you get here?"
Jesus answered, "I tell you for certain, you are not looking for me because you saw miraculous signs. You are looking for me because you ate the loaves and had a full stomach.
Do not work for food that spoils. Work for the food that lasts for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. God the Father has put his seal of approval on him."
Then they asked him, "What must we do to do the work God wants?"
Jesus answered, "This is the work God wants: believe in the one he has sent."
So they asked him, "What miraculous sign will you do, so that we can see it and believe you? What will you do?
Our ancestors ate manna in the desert. As the Scriptures say, 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
Jesus said to them, "I tell you for certain, it was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven. It is my Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
The bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world."
"Sir," they said, "always give us this bread."
Then Jesus said, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
But as I told you, you have seen me, and still you do not believe.
Everyone the Father gives me will come to me, and I will never turn away anyone who comes to me.
I have come down from heaven, not to do what I want, but to do what the one who sent me wants.
And this is what he wants: that I should not lose even one of all those he has given me, but raise them up on the last day.
My Father wants everyone who looks to the Son and believes in him to have eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day."
Then the Jewish leaders began to grumble about him because he said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven."
They said, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph? We know his father and mother. How can he now say, 'I came down from heaven'?"
Jesus answered, "Stop grumbling among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them to me, and I will raise them up on the last day.
It is written in the Prophets: 'They will all be taught by God.' Everyone who has listened to the Father and learned from him comes to me.
No one has seen the Father except the one who has come from God. Only he has seen the Father.
I tell you for certain, whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your ancestors ate manna in the desert, and yet they died.
But here is the bread that comes down from heaven. Whoever eats it will not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live for ever. This bread is my body, which I will give so that the world may live."
Then the Jewish leaders began to argue sharply among themselves. "How can this man give us his body to eat?" they asked.
Jesus said to them, "I tell you for certain, unless you eat the body of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever eats my body and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day.
My body is real food, and my blood is real drink.
Whoever eats my body and drinks my blood remains in me, and I remain in them.
The living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father. In the same way, whoever feeds on me will live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like the manna your ancestors ate. They died, but whoever eats this bread will live for ever."
Jesus said these things while he was teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
When many of his followers heard this, they said, "This teaching is hard. Who can accept it?"
Jesus knew that his followers were grumbling about this. So he said to them, "Does this upset you?
Then what if you see the Son of Man going back up to where he was before?
The Spirit gives life. Human effort achieves nothing. The words I have spoken to you are full of the Spirit and of life.
Yet some of you do not believe." Jesus knew from the beginning which of them did not believe, and who would betray him.
He went on, "This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless the Father makes it possible for them."
From that time many of his followers turned back and no longer went with him.
So Jesus asked the twelve apostles, "You do not want to leave too, do you?"
Simon Peter answered him, "Lord, who would we go to? You have the words that give eternal life.
We believe, and we know for sure, that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Then Jesus replied, "Did I not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!"
He was talking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. Although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later going to betray Jesus.
After this, Jesus travelled around in Galilee. He did not want to go about in Judea, because the Jewish leaders there were looking for a way to kill him.
But the Jewish Festival of Shelters was coming near.
So Jesus' brothers said to him, "You should leave here and go to Judea, so that your followers there can see the things you do.
No one who wants to be famous does things in secret. Since you are doing these things, show yourself to the world!"
Even his own brothers did not believe in him.
Jesus told them, "The right time for me has not yet come. But for you any time is right.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I tell it that what it does is evil.
You go up to the festival. I am not going up to this festival yet, because my time has not yet fully come."
After saying this, he stayed on in Galilee.
But after his brothers had gone up to the festival, he went up too. He did not go publicly, but in secret.
At the festival the Jewish leaders were watching for him and asking, "Where is that man?"
Many people in the crowd were whispering about him. Some said, "He is a good man." Others said, "No, he is misleading the people."
But no one would speak about him openly, because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders.
When the festival was half over, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
The Jewish leaders were amazed and asked, "How does this man know so much when he has never been taught?"
Jesus answered, "What I teach is not my own. It comes from the one who sent me.
Anyone who chooses to do what God wants will find out whether my teaching comes from God or whether I am speaking on my own.
Whoever speaks on their own does it to win honour for themselves. But the one who works for the honour of the one who sent him is truthful. There is nothing false about him.
Did Moses not give you the law? Yet not one of you keeps the law. Why are you trying to kill me?"
The crowd answered, "You have a demon! Who is trying to kill you?"
Jesus said to them, "I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
Moses gave you circumcision (although it really came from your ancestors, not from Moses), and so you circumcise a boy even on the Sabbath.
If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken, why are you angry with me for making a whole person well on the Sabbath?
Stop judging by what you see on the outside. Judge fairly and rightly."
Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to ask, "Is this not the man they are trying to kill?
Here he is, speaking openly, and they are not saying a word to him. Have the leaders really decided that he is the Christ?
But we know where this man comes from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from."

Then Jesus, who was still teaching in the temple courts, called out, "Yes, you know me, and you know where I come from. But I have not come on my own. The one who sent me is true. You do not know him,
but I know him, because I come from him and he sent me."
At this they tried to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his time had not yet come.
Still, many people in the crowd believed in him. They said, "When the Christ comes, will he do more miraculous signs than this man has done?"
The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about him. So the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple guards to arrest him.
Jesus said, "I will be with you only a little longer, and then I am going back to the one who sent me.
You will look for me, but you will not find me. You cannot come where I am going."
The Jewish leaders said to one another, "Where does this man plan to go that we cannot find him? Will he go to our people who are scattered among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
What does he mean when he says, 'You will look for me, but you will not find me,' and 'You cannot come where I am going'?"
On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, "If anyone is thirsty, let them come to me and drink.
Whoever believes in me, as the Scriptures say, rivers of living water will flow from deep inside them."
By this he meant the Spirit, whom those who believed in him would receive later. Up to that time the Spirit had not been given, because Jesus had not yet been raised to glory.
When they heard his words, some of the people said, "This man really is the Prophet."
Others said, "He is the Christ." But others asked, "How can the Christ come from Galilee?
Do the Scriptures not say that the Christ will come from the family of David, and from Bethlehem, the town where David lived?"
So the people were divided because of Jesus.
Some wanted to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him.
Finally the temple guards went back to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, "Why did you not bring him in?"
The guards answered, "No one ever spoke the way this man does!"
"Has he fooled you too?" the Pharisees asked.
"Have any of the leaders or any of the Pharisees believed in him?
No! But this crowd, who know nothing about the law, are under a curse."
Nicodemus, the man who had gone to Jesus earlier and who was one of the Pharisees, spoke up.
He asked, "Does our law condemn a man without first hearing him to find out what he has done?"
They replied, "Are you from Galilee too? Study the Scriptures and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee."
Then they all went home.
But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
Early the next morning he came back to the temple courts. All the people gathered round him, and he sat down to teach them.
The teachers of the law and the Pharisees brought in a woman who had been caught in adultery. They made her stand in front of everyone
and said to Jesus, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of adultery.
In the law, Moses commanded us to stone women like this. Now what do you say?"
They were using this question as a trap, so that they would have a reason to accuse him. But Jesus bent down and started to write on the ground with his finger, as if he had not heard them.
When they kept on asking him, he stood up and said to them, "Let any one of you who has never sinned be the first to throw a stone at her."
Then he bent down again and wrote on the ground.

When they heard this, their own consciences troubled them, and they began to go away one at a time, the older ones first, until the last one had gone. Jesus was left alone with the woman still standing there.
Jesus stood up and saw no one but the woman. He asked her, "Woman, where are the people who accused you? Has no one condemned you?"
"No one, Lord," she said. Then Jesus said, "I do not condemn you either. Go now, and do not sin any more."
Jesus spoke to the people again. He said, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light that gives life."
The Pharisees said to him, "Here you are, speaking as your own witness. What you say about yourself does not prove anything."
Jesus answered, "Even if I speak as my own witness, what I say is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you have no idea where I come from or where I am going.
You judge by human standards. I do not judge anyone.
But even if I do judge, my judgement is true, because I am not alone. The Father who sent me is with me.
Your own law says that when two witnesses agree, their evidence is true.
I am one witness for myself, and my other witness is the Father, who sent me."
Then they asked him, "Where is your father?" Jesus answered, "You do not know me or my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father too."
Jesus said these things while he was teaching in the temple courts, near the place where the offerings were put. But no one arrested him, because his time had not yet come.
Once more Jesus said to them, "I am going away. You will look for me, but you will die in your sin. You cannot come where I am going."
This made the Jewish leaders ask, "Is he going to kill himself? Is that why he says, 'You cannot come where I am going'?"
He went on, "You are from below, but I am from above. You belong to this world, but I do not belong to this world.
That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. If you do not believe that I am who I say I am, you will indeed die in your sins."
"Who are you?" they asked. Jesus replied, "I am exactly who I have been telling you from the beginning.
I have much to say about you, and much to judge. But the one who sent me is true, and I tell the world only what I have heard from him."
They did not understand that he was talking to them about the Father.
So Jesus said, "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am who I say I am. You will know that I do nothing on my own, but say only what the Father has taught me.
The one who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him."
While he was saying these things, many people believed in him.
Jesus said to the Jewish people who had believed in him, "If you keep obeying my teaching, you are truly my followers.
Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
They answered him, "We are descendants of Abraham, and we have never been anyone's slaves. How can you say that we will be set free?"
Jesus replied, "I tell you for certain, everyone who keeps on sinning is a slave to sin.
A slave does not have a lasting place in the family, but a son belongs to it for ever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be truly free.
I know that you are Abraham's descendants. Yet you are looking for a way to kill me, because there is no room in your hearts for my message.
I am telling you what I have seen with my Father, and you are doing what you have heard from your father."
"Abraham is our father," they answered. Jesus said, "If you were really Abraham's children, you would do what Abraham did.
Instead, you are trying to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did nothing like that.
You are doing what your own father does." "We are not children born from sexual sin," they protested. "The only Father we have is God himself."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love me, because I came from God and now I am here. I did not come on my own. He sent me.
Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are not able to listen to my message.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to do what your father wants. He was a murderer from the beginning. He has never stood on the side of truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he is speaking his own language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me!
Can any of you prove that I am guilty of sin? If I am telling the truth, why do you not believe me?
Whoever belongs to God listens to what God says. The reason you do not listen is that you do not belong to God."
The Jewish leaders answered him, "Were we not right when we said that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
"I do not have a demon," said Jesus. "I honour my Father, but you dishonour me.
I am not looking for glory for myself. But there is one who is looking for it, and he is the judge.
I tell you for certain, whoever obeys my teaching will never see death."
At this the leaders said, "Now we know that you have a demon! Abraham died, and so did the prophets. Yet you say that whoever obeys your teaching will never taste death.
Are you greater than our father Abraham? He died, and so did the prophets. Who do you think you are?"
Jesus replied, "If I gave glory to myself, my glory would mean nothing. It is my Father who gives me glory, the one you claim is your God.
You do not know him, but I know him. If I said I did not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I obey his word.
Your father Abraham was full of joy at the thought of seeing my day. He saw it and was glad."
The leaders said to him, "You are not even fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?"
Jesus answered, "I tell you for certain, before Abraham was born, I AM!"
At this they picked up stones to throw at him. But Jesus hid himself and slipped away out of the temple, going right through the crowd.
As Jesus was walking along, he saw a man who had been blind since he was born.
His followers asked him, "Rabbi, why was this man born blind? Was it because he sinned, or because his parents sinned?"
Jesus answered, "It was not because this man sinned, or his parents. It happened so that the power of God could be seen at work in his life.
While it is still day, we must do the work of the one who sent me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
While I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
After saying this, Jesus spat on the ground and made some mud with the spit. He spread the mud on the man's eyes
and told him, "Go and wash in the Pool of Siloam" (the name means "Sent"). So the man went and washed, and when he came back, he could see.
His neighbours, and others who had seen him begging before, asked, "Is this not the man who used to sit and beg?"
Some said, "Yes, it is him." Others said, "No, he only looks like him." But the man himself kept saying, "I am the man."
So they asked him, "Then how were your eyes opened?"
He replied, "The man they call Jesus made some mud and spread it on my eyes. He told me, 'Go to Siloam and wash.' So I went and washed, and then I could see."
They asked him, "Where is this man?" "I do not know," he said.
They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees.
Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened the man's eyes was a Sabbath.
So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. He told them, "He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and now I can see."
Some of the Pharisees said, "This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath." But others asked, "How can a sinner do such miraculous signs?" So they were divided.
Then they turned to the blind man again and asked, "What do you say about him? It was your eyes he opened." The man replied, "He is a prophet."
The Jewish leaders still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight. So they sent for his parents.
They asked them, "Is this your son? Is he the one you say was born blind? How is it that he can see now?"
His parents answered, "We know that he is our son, and we know that he was born blind.
But we do not know how he can see now, or who opened his eyes. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself."
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders. The leaders had already agreed that anyone who said Jesus was the Christ would be thrown out of the synagogue.
That is why his parents said, "He is old enough. Ask him."
So for a second time they called the man who had been blind. They said to him, "Give glory to God by telling the truth. We know that this man is a sinner."
He replied, "I do not know whether he is a sinner or not. But one thing I do know: I was blind, and now I can see!"
Then they asked him, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
He answered, "I have told you already, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you want to become his followers too?"
Then they insulted him and said, "You are this man's follower! We are followers of Moses!
We know that God spoke to Moses. But as for this man, we do not even know where he comes from."
The man answered, "Now that is amazing! You do not know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
We know that God does not listen to sinners. But he does listen to anyone who worships him and does what he wants.
Since the world began, no one has ever heard of anyone opening the eyes of a person who was born blind.
If this man were not from God, he could do nothing."
They replied, "You were born completely in sin! How dare you try to teach us!" And they threw him out.
Jesus heard that they had thrown him out. When he found him, he asked, "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
The man answered, "Who is he, sir? Tell me, so that I can believe in him."
Jesus said, "You have now seen him. In fact, he is the one speaking with you."
Then the man said, "Lord, I believe," and he worshipped him.
Jesus said, "I came into this world to bring judgement, so that the blind will see, and those who think they see will become blind."
Some Pharisees who were with him heard him say this. They asked, "What? Are we blind too?"
Jesus said, "If you were blind, you would not be guilty of sin. But now that you claim you can see, your guilt remains."
"I tell you for certain, anyone who does not enter the sheep pen through the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
The one who comes in through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought out all his own sheep, he walks ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
They will never follow a stranger. In fact, they will run away from him, because they do not know a stranger's voice."
Jesus told them this picture story, but they did not understand what he was telling them.
So Jesus spoke again: "I tell you for certain, I am the gate for the sheep.
All who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. Whoever comes in through me will be saved. They will come in and go out and find good pasture.
The thief comes only to steal, kill and destroy. I have come so that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives up his life for the sheep.
A hired worker is not the shepherd, and the sheep do not belong to him. So when he sees a wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf attacks the flock and scatters it.
The man runs away because he is only working for money and does not really care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own sheep, and my own sheep know me,
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. And I give up my life for the sheep.
I have other sheep too, which are not in this sheep pen. I must bring them also. They too will listen to my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The Father loves me because I give up my life, so that I may take it back again.
No one takes it from me. I give it up of my own free will. I have the authority to give it up, and I have the authority to take it back again. This is what my Father has commanded me to do."
Once again the Jewish people were divided because of what Jesus said.
Many of them said, "He has a demon and is out of his mind. Why listen to him?"
But others said, "These are not the words of a man who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?"
Then came the Festival of Dedication in Jerusalem. It was winter,
and Jesus was walking in the temple courts, in the covered walkway called Solomon's Porch.
The Jewish leaders gathered round him and said, "How long will you keep us guessing? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered, "I did tell you, but you do not believe. The works I do in my Father's name speak for me.
But you do not believe, because you are not my sheep.
My sheep listen to my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
I give them eternal life, and they will never be lost. No one can snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of my Father's hand.
I and the Father are one."
Again the Jewish leaders picked up stones to stone him.
But Jesus said to them, "I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these are you going to stone me?"
They replied, "We are not stoning you for any good work, but for insulting God. You are only a man, but you are claiming to be God."
Jesus answered them, "Is it not written in your own law that God said, 'I have said that you are gods'?
God called them 'gods', those people to whom his message came, and the Scriptures cannot be set aside.
Then what about the one whom the Father set apart as his own and sent into the world? Why do you accuse me of insulting God because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
Do not believe me unless I do the works of my Father.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works. Then you will know and understand that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father."
Again they tried to arrest him, but he escaped from their hands.
Then Jesus went back across the Jordan River to the place where John had first been baptising, and he stayed there.
Many people came to him. They said, "John never did a miraculous sign, but everything John said about this man was true."
And in that place many people believed in Jesus.
A man named Lazarus was ill. He lived in Bethany, the village where Mary and her sister Martha lived.
This Mary was the one who later poured perfume on the Lord and wiped his feet with her hair. It was her brother Lazarus who was ill.
So the sisters sent a message to Jesus: "Lord, the one you love is ill."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "This illness will not end in death. It has happened for the glory of God, so that the Son of God will be honoured through it."
Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
Yet when he heard that Lazarus was ill, he stayed where he was for two more days.
Then he said to his followers, "Let us go back to Judea."
"But Rabbi," they said, "only a short time ago the Jewish leaders there tried to stone you. Are you going back there?"
Jesus answered, "Are there not twelve hours of daylight? Anyone who walks during the day will not stumble, because they can see by the light of this world.
But anyone who walks at night will stumble, because they have no light."
After he had said this, he went on to tell them, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up."
His followers replied, "Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better."
Jesus had been speaking about his death, but they thought he meant ordinary sleep.
So then he told them plainly, "Lazarus is dead.
For your sake I am glad that I was not there, because now you will believe. But let us go to him."
Then Thomas (also called the Twin) said to the other followers, "Let us go too, so that we may die with him."
When Jesus arrived, he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days.
Bethany was less than three kilometres from Jerusalem,
and many Jewish people had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them about the death of their brother.
When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him, but Mary stayed at home.
Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But I know that even now God will give you whatever you ask."
Jesus told her, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha answered, "I know he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day."
Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even though they die.
And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?"
"Yes, Lord," she replied. "I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one who was to come into the world."
After she had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside. "The Teacher is here," she said, "and he is asking for you."
When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to him.
Jesus had not yet come into the village. He was still at the place where Martha had met him.
The Jewish people who had been with Mary in the house, comforting her, saw how quickly she got up and went out. So they followed her, thinking she was going to the tomb to cry there.
When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet. She said, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
When Jesus saw her crying, and saw the people who had come with her crying too, he was deeply moved in his spirit and greatly troubled.
"Where have you laid him?" he asked. "Come and see, Lord," they replied.
Jesus wept.
Then the people said, "See how much he loved him!"
But some of them said, "He opened the eyes of the blind man. Could he not have kept this man from dying?"
Jesus, once more deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone placed across the entrance.
"Take away the stone," he said. Martha, the sister of the dead man, said, "But Lord, by now there will be a bad smell. He has been dead for four days."
Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"
So they took away the stone. Then Jesus looked up and said, "Father, thank you for hearing me.
I know that you always hear me. But I said this for the sake of the people standing here, so that they will believe that you sent me."
After he had said this, Jesus called out in a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!"
The dead man came out. His hands and feet were wrapped with strips of cloth, and a cloth was wrapped around his face. Jesus said to them, "Unwrap him and let him go."
Many of the Jewish people who had come to visit Mary saw what Jesus did, and they believed in him.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
Then the chief priests and the Pharisees called a meeting of the council. "What are we going to do?" they asked. "This man is doing many miraculous signs.
If we let him carry on like this, everyone will believe in him. Then the Romans will come and take away both our temple and our nation."
One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, spoke up. "You know nothing at all!" he said.
"You do not realise that it is better for you that one man should die for the people than for the whole nation to be destroyed."
He did not say this on his own. As high priest that year, he was speaking God's message without knowing it: Jesus would die for the Jewish nation,
and not only for that nation, but also to bring together all of God's children who were scattered everywhere, and make them one.
So from that day on they made plans to kill Jesus.
For this reason Jesus no longer moved about openly among the Jewish people. Instead, he went to a region near the desert, to a village called Ephraim, and stayed there with his followers.
It was nearly time for the Jewish Passover festival. Many people went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover to make themselves ceremonially clean.
They kept looking for Jesus. As they stood in the temple courts, they asked one another, "What do you think? Is he coming to the festival at all?"
But the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that anyone who found out where Jesus was must report it, so that they could arrest him.
Six days before the Passover festival, Jesus came to Bethany. Lazarus lived there, the man Jesus had raised from the dead.
A dinner was given there in honour of Jesus. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those eating at the table with him.

Then Mary took about half a litre of very expensive perfume made from pure nard. She poured it on Jesus' feet and wiped his feet with her hair. The whole house was filled with the sweet smell of the perfume.
But Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, one of Jesus' followers, who was later going to betray him, objected.
"Why was this perfume not sold?" he asked. "It was worth a whole year's wages. The money could have been given to the poor."
He did not say this because he cared about the poor. He said it because he was a thief. He looked after the money bag, and he used to help himself to what was put in it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She has kept this perfume for the day of my burial.
You will always have poor people with you, but you will not always have me."
A large crowd of Jewish people found out that Jesus was there. They came, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
because on account of him many of the Jewish people were leaving them and believing in Jesus.
The next day the large crowd that had come for the festival heard that Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem.
They took branches from palm trees and went out to meet him, shouting, "Hosanna! Praise God! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the King of Israel!"
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as the Scriptures say:
"Do not be afraid, people of Zion. Look, your King is coming, sitting on a donkey's colt."

At first his followers did not understand these things. But after Jesus had been raised to glory, they remembered that these things had been written about him, and that people had done these things to him.
The crowd that had been with Jesus when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept telling others what they had seen.
That is why so many people went out to meet him. They had heard that he had done this miraculous sign.
So the Pharisees said to one another, "You can see that we are getting nowhere. Look, the whole world is following him!"
There were some Greeks among the people who went up to worship at the festival.
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, with a request. "Sir," they said, "we would like to see Jesus."
Philip went to tell Andrew. Then Andrew and Philip went together to tell Jesus.
Jesus replied, "The time has come for the Son of Man to be given glory.
I tell you for certain, unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays just one seed. But if it dies, it produces many seeds.
Anyone who loves their life will lose it. But anyone who hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
Whoever serves me must follow me. Where I am, my servant will also be. My Father will honour the one who serves me.
Now my heart is troubled. What shall I say? 'Father, save me from this hour'? No, it was for this very reason that I came to this hour.
Father, bring glory to your name!" Then a voice came from heaven: "I have brought glory to it, and I will bring glory to it again."
The crowd standing there heard it and said it was thunder. Others said, "An angel spoke to him."
Jesus said, "This voice was for your benefit, not mine.
Now is the time for this world to be judged. Now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.
And when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself."
He said this to show what kind of death he was going to die.
The crowd answered, "We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain for ever. So how can you say, 'The Son of Man must be lifted up'? Who is this 'Son of Man'?"

Then Jesus told them, "The light will be with you for only a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, before darkness overtakes you. Whoever walks in the dark does not know where they are going.
Believe in the light while you have the light, so that you may become children of light." When he had finished speaking, Jesus went away and hid from them.
Even though Jesus had done so many miraculous signs in front of them, they still did not believe in him.
This happened so that the words of the prophet Isaiah would come true: "Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the power of the Lord been shown?"
That is why they could not believe. As Isaiah also said:
"He has blinded their eyes and made their hearts hard, so that they cannot see with their eyes or understand with their hearts, and turn to me, so that I could heal them."
Isaiah said this because he saw Jesus' glory, and he spoke about him.
Yet even among the leaders, many believed in him. But because of the Pharisees they would not say so openly, for fear that they would be thrown out of the synagogue.
They loved praise from people more than praise from God.
Then Jesus called out, "Whoever believes in me does not believe in me only, but also in the one who sent me.
Whoever looks at me is seeing the one who sent me.
I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in me should stay in darkness.
If anyone hears my words but does not obey them, I do not judge that person. I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
There is a judge for anyone who rejects me and does not accept my words. The very message I have spoken will judge them on the last day.
I have not spoken on my own. The Father who sent me commanded me what to say and how to say it.
I know that his command leads to eternal life. So whatever I say is just what the Father has told me to say."

It was just before the Passover festival. Jesus knew that the time had come for him to leave this world and go to the Father. He had always loved his own people who were in the world, and now he showed them the full extent of his love.
The evening meal was being served. The devil had already put the idea of betraying Jesus into the heart of Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
Jesus knew that the Father had put everything under his power. He knew that he had come from God and was going back to God.
So he got up from the meal, took off his outer clothing and wrapped a towel around his waist.
Then he poured water into a bowl and began to wash his followers' feet, drying them with the towel that was wrapped around him.
He came to Simon Peter, who said to him, "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
Jesus replied, "You do not understand now what I am doing, but later you will understand."
"No," said Peter, "you will never wash my feet!" Jesus answered, "Unless I wash you, you have no part with me."
"Then, Lord," Simon Peter replied, "do not wash only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!"
Jesus answered, "A person who has had a bath only needs to wash their feet. The rest of their body is clean. And you are clean, though not every one of you."
He knew who was going to betray him. That is why he said that not every one of them was clean.
When he had finished washing their feet, he put his clothes back on and took his place at the table again. "Do you understand what I have done for you?" he asked them.
"You call me 'Teacher' and 'Lord', and you are right, because that is what I am.
Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another's feet.
I have given you an example, so that you will do for others what I have done for you.
I tell you for certain, a servant is not greater than his master, and a messenger is not greater than the one who sent him.
Now that you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them.
I am not talking about all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But this has to happen so that the Scripture will come true: 'The one who eats bread with me has turned against me.'
I am telling you this now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you will believe that I am who I say I am.
I tell you for certain, whoever welcomes anyone I send welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me."
After Jesus had said this, he was deeply troubled in his spirit. He said openly, "I tell you for certain, one of you is going to betray me."
His followers looked at one another. They had no idea which of them he meant.
One of them, the follower whom Jesus loved, was reclining next to him at the table.
Simon Peter signalled to this follower and said, "Ask him which one he means."
So the follower leaned back against Jesus and asked him, "Lord, who is it?"
Jesus answered, "It is the one I will give this piece of bread to after I have dipped it in the dish." Then he dipped the piece of bread and gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
As soon as Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him. Jesus said to him, "What you are going to do, do it quickly."
But no one at the table understood why Jesus said this to him.
Judas looked after the money, so some of them thought Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the festival, or to give something to the poor.
As soon as Judas had taken the bread, he went out. And it was night.
When Judas had gone, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is given glory, and God is given glory through him.
If God is given glory through him, God will give glory to the Son in himself, and he will do it very soon.
My dear children, I will be with you only a little longer. You will look for me, but as I told the Jewish leaders, so I tell you now: where I am going, you cannot come.
I am giving you a new command: love one another. Just as I have loved you, you must love one another.
If you love one another, everyone will know that you are my followers."
Simon Peter asked him, "Lord, where are you going?" Jesus replied, "Where I am going, you cannot follow me now. But you will follow me later."
Peter asked, "Lord, why can I not follow you now? I am ready to give my life for you!"
Jesus answered, "Will you really give your life for me? I tell you for certain, before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know me."
"Do not let your hearts be troubled. Trust in God, and trust also in me.
My Father's house has many rooms. If that were not so, I would have told you. I am going there to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me, so that you may be where I am.
You know the way to the place where I am going."
Thomas said to him, "Lord, we do not know where you are going, so how can we know the way?"
Jesus answered, "I am the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
If you really knew me, you would know my Father as well. From now on, you do know him, and you have seen him."
Philip said, "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us."
Jesus answered, "Philip, I have been with all of you for such a long time. Do you still not know me? Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. So how can you say, 'Show us the Father'?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you are not just my own. It is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work.
Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me. Or at least believe because of the works you have seen me do.
I tell you for certain, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing. They will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Son may bring glory to the Father.
You may ask me for anything in my name, and I will do it.
If you love me, you will obey my commands.
And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Helper to be with you for ever.
He is the Spirit of truth. The world cannot accept him, because it does not see him or know him. But you know him, because he lives with you, and he will be in you.
I will not leave you all alone like orphans. I will come to you.
In a little while the world will not see me any more, but you will see me. Because I live, you will live too.
On that day you will realise that I am in my Father, and that you are in me, and I am in you.
Whoever knows my commands and obeys them is the one who loves me. My Father will love the one who loves me. I too will love them and show myself to them."
Then Judas (not Judas Iscariot) said, "But Lord, why do you plan to show yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered, "Anyone who loves me will obey my teaching. My Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.
Anyone who does not love me will not obey my teaching. The message you hear from me is not my own. It belongs to the Father who sent me.
I have told you all this while I am still with you.
But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything. He will remind you of everything I have said to you.
I am leaving you with peace. I am giving you my own peace. I do not give it the way the world gives. So do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not be afraid.
You heard me say, 'I am going away, and I am coming back to you.' If you loved me, you would be glad that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I am.
I have told you this now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you will believe.
I will not say much more to you, because the ruler of this world is coming. He has no power over me.
But I do exactly what my Father has commanded me, so that the world may learn that I love the Father. Come now, let us leave this place."
"I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
He cuts off every branch in me that does not produce fruit. And he trims every branch that does produce fruit, so that it will produce even more fruit.
You are already clean because of the message I have spoken to you.
Stay joined to me, and I will stay joined to you. A branch cannot produce fruit by itself. It must stay joined to the vine. In the same way, you cannot produce fruit unless you stay joined to me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. If you stay joined to me and I to you, you will produce a lot of fruit. Without me you can do nothing.
Anyone who does not stay joined to me is like a branch that is thrown away and dries up. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire and burned.
If you stay joined to me and my words stay in you, ask for whatever you want, and it will be done for you.
My Father is given glory when you produce a lot of fruit. This shows that you are my followers.
I have loved you just as the Father has loved me. Stay in my love.
If you obey my commands, you will stay in my love, just as I have obeyed my Father's commands and stay in his love.
I have told you this so that my joy may be in you, and so that your joy may be complete.
This is my command: love one another, just as I have loved you.
The greatest love a person can show is to give up their life for their friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing. Instead, I call you friends, because I have told you everything I have heard from my Father.
You did not choose me. I chose you, and I appointed you to go and produce fruit that will last. Then the Father will give you whatever you ask in my name.
This is my command: love one another.
If the world hates you, remember that it hated me first.
If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But you do not belong to the world. I have chosen you out of the world, and that is why the world hates you.
Remember what I told you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If people persecuted me, they will persecute you too. If they obeyed my teaching, they will obey yours too.
They will treat you like this because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me hates my Father as well.
If I had not done among them the works that no one else has ever done, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have seen these works, and still they have hated both me and my Father.
This has happened so that what is written in their Law would come true: 'They hated me for no reason.'
I will send you the Helper from the Father. He is the Spirit of truth who comes from the Father. When he comes, he will tell you about me.
And you also must tell others about me, because you have been with me from the beginning."
"I have told you all this so that you will not give up your faith.
They will throw you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think they are serving God.
They will do these things because they have not known the Father or me.
I have told you this so that when the time comes, you will remember that I warned you. I did not tell you this at the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me. Yet none of you asks me, 'Where are you going?'
Instead, your hearts are full of sadness because I have told you these things.
But I am telling you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. If I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
When he comes, he will show the people of the world how wrong they are about sin, about what is right, and about judgement.
About sin, because people do not believe in me.
About what is right, because I am going to the Father, where you cannot see me any more.
And about judgement, because the ruler of this world has already been judged.
I still have many things to tell you, but they would be too much for you to bear right now.
But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth. He will not speak on his own. He will speak only what he hears, and he will tell you what is still going to happen.
He will bring glory to me, because he will take what is mine and make it known to you.
Everything that belongs to the Father is mine. That is why I said the Spirit will take what is mine and make it known to you.
In a little while you will not see me any more. Then after a little while you will see me again, because I am going to the Father."

Some of his followers said to one another, "What does he mean by saying, 'In a little while you will not see me, and then after a little while you will see me'? And what does he mean by 'because I am going to the Father'?"
They kept asking, "What does he mean by 'a little while'? We do not understand what he is talking about."

Jesus saw that they wanted to ask him about this. So he said to them, "Are you asking one another what I meant when I said, 'In a little while you will not see me, and then after a little while you will see me'?
I tell you for certain, you will cry and mourn while the world celebrates. You will be sad, but your sadness will turn into joy.
A woman giving birth to a baby has pain, because her time has come. But when her baby is born, she forgets the pain because she is so happy that a child has been born into the world.
It is the same with you. Now you are sad, but I will see you again. Then your hearts will be full of joy, and no one will take that joy away from you.
On that day you will not need to ask me anything. I tell you for certain, my Father will give you whatever you ask him for in my name.
Until now you have not asked for anything in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy will be complete.
I have been speaking to you in picture language. But a time is coming when I will no longer speak like this. I will tell you plainly about my Father.
On that day you will ask in my name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father for you,
because the Father himself loves you. He loves you because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father and entered the world. Now I am leaving the world and going back to the Father."
Then his followers said, "Now you are speaking plainly and not using picture language.
Now we can see that you know everything, and you do not even need anyone to ask you questions. This makes us believe that you came from God."
Jesus answered, "So now you believe?

But a time is coming, and in fact it has already come, when you will be scattered. Each of you will go to your own home, and you will leave me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
I have told you these things so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will face hardship. But be encouraged! I have overcome the world."
After Jesus had said this, he looked up towards heaven and prayed: "Father, the time has come. Bring glory to your Son, so that your Son may bring glory to you.
You gave him authority over all people, so that he might give eternal life to all those you have given him.
And this is eternal life: to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.
I have brought you glory on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do.
And now, Father, give me glory in your presence, the glory I had with you before the world began.
I have shown what you are like to the people you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have obeyed your word.
Now they know that everything you have given me comes from you.
I gave them the message you gave me, and they accepted it. They know for certain that I came from you, and they believe that you sent me.
I am praying for them. I am not praying for the world, but for those you have given me, because they are yours.
All I have is yours, and all you have is mine. And glory has come to me through them.

I will not stay in the world any longer, but they are still in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them safe by the power of your name, the name you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one.

While I was with them, I kept them safe by the power of your name, the name you gave me. I guarded them, and not one of them was lost except the one who was headed for destruction, so that the Scripture would come true.
Now I am coming to you. But I am saying these things while I am still in the world, so that they may have my joy completely in their hearts.
I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world.
I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but to protect them from the evil one.
They do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to it.
Make them holy by your truth. Your word is truth.
Just as you sent me into the world, I have sent them into the world.
For their sake I give myself completely to you, so that they too may be made holy by the truth.
I am not praying only for them. I am also praying for everyone who will believe in me because of their message.
I pray that all of them may be one, Father, just as you are in me and I am in you. May they also be in us, so that the world will believe that you sent me.
I have given them the glory that you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one:
I in them and you in me. May they be brought into perfect unity. Then the world will know that you sent me, and that you have loved them just as you have loved me.
Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am. I want them to see my glory, the glory you gave me because you loved me before the world was made.
Righteous Father, the world does not know you, but I know you, and these people know that you sent me.
I have made you known to them, and I will keep on making you known. Then the love you have for me will be in them, and I myself will be in them."
When Jesus had finished praying, he went out with his followers and crossed the Kidron Valley. On the other side there was a garden, and he and his followers went into it.
Judas, who was betraying him, knew the place too, because Jesus had often met there with his followers.
So Judas came to the garden, leading a group of soldiers and some guards sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees. They were carrying lanterns, torches and weapons.
Jesus knew everything that was going to happen to him. So he went out and asked them, "Who are you looking for?"
"Jesus of Nazareth," they replied. "I am he," Jesus said. Judas, the one who was betraying him, was standing there with them.
When Jesus said, "I am he," they stepped back and fell to the ground.
Again he asked them, "Who are you looking for?" They said, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus answered, "I have told you that I am he. If you are looking for me, then let these men go."
This happened so that the words he had spoken would come true: "I have not lost one of those you gave me."
Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, pulled it out and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
Jesus told Peter, "Put your sword away! Shall I not drink the cup of suffering that the Father has given me?"
Then the group of soldiers, with their commander and the Jewish guards, arrested Jesus. They tied him up
and took him first to Annas. Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jewish leaders that it would be better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter and another follower were following Jesus. Because this other follower was known to the high priest, he went with Jesus into the high priest's courtyard.
But Peter had to wait outside at the gate. So the other follower, who was known to the high priest, came back. He spoke to the young woman on duty at the gate and brought Peter in.
The young woman at the gate asked Peter, "You are not one of this man's followers too, are you?" He replied, "No, I am not."
It was cold, so the servants and guards had made a charcoal fire and were standing around it to warm themselves. Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about his followers and his teaching.
Jesus answered, "I have spoken openly for the world to hear. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all the Jewish people come together. I have said nothing in secret.
Why are you questioning me? Ask the people who heard me. They know what I said."
When Jesus said this, one of the guards standing nearby slapped him across the face. "Is that how you answer the high priest?" he demanded.
Jesus replied, "If I said something wrong, tell everyone what was wrong. But if I spoke the truth, why did you hit me?"
Then Annas sent him, still tied up, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Meanwhile, Simon Peter was still standing there warming himself. So they asked him, "You are not one of his followers too, are you?" He denied it, saying, "No, I am not."
One of the high priest's servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, "Did I not see you with him in the garden?"
Again Peter denied it, and at that moment a rooster began to crow.

Then the Jewish leaders took Jesus from Caiaphas to the palace of the Roman governor. It was early in the morning. They did not go into the palace themselves, because they did not want to become ceremonially unclean. They wanted to be able to eat the Passover meal.
So Pilate came out to them and asked, "What charge are you bringing against this man?"
They answered, "If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you."
Pilate said, "Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law." The Jewish leaders objected, "But we do not have the right to put anyone to death."
This happened so that what Jesus had said about the kind of death he would die would come true.
Then Pilate went back inside the palace. He called Jesus and asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus asked, "Is that your own idea, or did others tell you about me?"
Pilate replied, "Do you think I am a Jew? It was your own people and your chief priests who handed you over to me. What have you done?"
Jesus said, "My kingdom does not belong to this world. If it did, my servants would fight to stop me being handed over to the Jewish leaders. But my kingdom is not from here."

"So you are a king, then!" said Pilate. Jesus answered, "You are right to say that I am a king. In fact, the reason I was born and came into the world is to tell people the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to me."
"What is truth?" Pilate asked. Then he went out again to the Jewish leaders and said, "I find no reason at all to charge him with a crime.
But you have a custom that I set one prisoner free for you at Passover time. Do you want me to set free 'the king of the Jews'?"
They shouted back, "No, not him! Give us Barabbas!" Barabbas was a robber.
Then Pilate took Jesus and had him whipped.
The soldiers twisted thorny branches together to make a crown, and they put it on his head. They dressed him in a purple robe.
They kept coming up to him and saying, "Hail, king of the Jews!" And they struck him in the face again and again.
Once more Pilate came out and said to the crowd, "Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you will know that I find no reason to charge him with a crime."
So Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. Pilate said to them, "Look at the man!"
As soon as the chief priests and their guards saw him, they shouted, "Crucify him! Crucify him!" But Pilate told them, "You take him and crucify him. As for me, I find no reason to charge him."
The Jewish leaders answered, "We have a law, and according to that law he must die, because he claimed to be the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid.
He went back inside the palace and asked Jesus, "Where do you come from?" But Jesus gave him no answer.
"Do you refuse to speak to me?" Pilate said. "Do you not realise that I have the power to set you free or to crucify you?"
Jesus answered, "You would have no power over me at all if it had not been given to you from above. That is why the one who handed me over to you is guilty of a greater sin."
From then on, Pilate tried to set Jesus free. But the Jewish leaders kept shouting, "If you let this man go, you are no friend of Caesar! Anyone who claims to be a king is against Caesar!"
When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judge's seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in the Hebrew language is Gabbatha.
It was the day of preparation for the Passover, about twelve o'clock, midday. Pilate said to the Jewish people, "Here is your king!"
But they shouted, "Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him!" Pilate asked, "Shall I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king except Caesar!"
Finally Pilate handed him over to them to be crucified. So the soldiers took charge of Jesus and led him away.
