Carrying his own cross, he went out to the place called the Place of the Skull, which in the Hebrew language is Golgotha.
There they crucified him, and with him two other men, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
Pilate had a notice written and fastened to the cross. It said: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Many of the Jewish people read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. The notice was written in Hebrew, Greek and Latin.
The chief priests of the Jewish people said to Pilate, "Do not write 'The King of the Jews'. Write that this man claimed to be king of the Jews."
Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."

When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and divided them into four shares, one for each soldier. They also took his long shirt. It had no seam, but was woven in one piece from top to bottom.

So they said to one another, "Let us not tear it. Let us throw dice to see who will get it." This happened so that the Scripture would come true: "They divided my clothes among them and threw dice for my clothing." So that is what the soldiers did.
Standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother there, and the follower whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, "Dear woman, here is your son."
Then he said to the follower, "Here is your mother." From that time on, this follower took her into his home.
After this, Jesus knew that everything had now been completed. So that the Scripture would come true, he said, "I am thirsty."
A jar of sour wine was standing there. So they soaked a sponge in it, put the sponge on a stalk of the hyssop plant, and lifted it to his lips.
When Jesus had received the drink, he said, "It is finished." Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

It was the day of preparation, and the next day was a special Sabbath. The Jewish leaders did not want the bodies left on the crosses during the Sabbath. So they asked Pilate to have the legs of the men broken, so that their bodies could be taken down.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and then those of the other.
But when they came to Jesus, they saw that he was already dead, so they did not break his legs.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced Jesus' side with a spear, and at once blood and water flowed out.
The man who saw this has told us about it, and what he says is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, and he tells it so that you also may believe.
These things happened so that the Scripture would come true: "Not one of his bones will be broken."
And another Scripture says, "They will look at the one they have pierced."

Later, Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate for permission to take away the body of Jesus. Joseph was a follower of Jesus, but secretly, because he was afraid of the Jewish leaders. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and took the body away.
Nicodemus, the man who had earlier come to Jesus at night, went with Joseph. He brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, weighing about thirty-four kilograms.
The two men took the body of Jesus and wrapped it, together with the spices, in strips of linen cloth. This was the Jewish custom for burying the dead.
At the place where Jesus was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb, where no one had ever been buried.
Because it was the Jewish day of preparation, and because the tomb was close by, they laid Jesus there.
Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb. She saw that the stone had been rolled away from the entrance.
So she ran to Simon Peter and the other follower, the one Jesus loved. She told them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have put him!"
So Peter and the other follower set out for the tomb.
Both of them were running, but the other follower ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
He bent down and looked in at the strips of linen cloth lying there, but he did not go in.
Then Simon Peter came along behind him and went straight into the tomb. He saw the strips of linen lying there.
He also saw the cloth that had been wrapped around Jesus' head. It was not lying with the strips of linen, but was folded up in a place by itself.
Then the other follower, who had reached the tomb first, also went inside. He saw, and he believed.
They still did not understand from the Scriptures that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
Then the followers went back to their homes.
But Mary stood outside the tomb, crying. As she cried, she bent down to look into the tomb.
She saw two angels dressed in white, sitting where the body of Jesus had been lying, one at the head and the other at the feet.
They asked her, "Woman, why are you crying?" She answered, "They have taken my Lord away, and I do not know where they have put him."
After saying this, she turned round and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not realise that it was Jesus.

He asked her, "Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?" She thought he was the gardener, so she said, "Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have put him, and I will go and get him."
Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned towards him and cried out, "Rabboni!" (which means Teacher).
Jesus told her, "Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet gone up to the Father. Instead, go to my brothers and tell them, 'I am going up to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.'"
Mary Magdalene went to the followers with the news: "I have seen the Lord!" And she told them what he had said to her.

On the evening of that first day of the week, the followers were together with the doors locked, because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders. Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you!"
After he said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The followers were filled with joy when they saw the Lord.
Again Jesus said, "Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, so I am sending you."
Then he breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven. If you do not forgive them, they are not forgiven."
Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called the Twin, was not with the others when Jesus came.

So the other followers told him, "We have seen the Lord!" But he said to them, "Unless I see the nail marks in his hands, and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe."
A week later his followers were in the house again, and Thomas was with them. Even though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you!"
Then he said to Thomas, "Put your finger here, and look at my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Stop doubting, and believe."
Thomas said to him, "My Lord and my God!"
Then Jesus told him, "You believe because you have seen me. Blessed are those who have not seen me and yet have believed."
Jesus did many other miraculous signs in front of his followers, which are not written down in this book.
But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life through his name.
Some time later, Jesus showed himself again to his followers, beside the Sea of Tiberias. This is how it happened.
Simon Peter, Thomas (called the Twin), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other followers were together.
Simon Peter told them, "I am going out to fish." They said, "We will come with you." So they went out and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing.
Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the followers did not realise that it was Jesus.
He called out to them, "Friends, have you caught any fish?" "No," they answered.
He said, "Throw your net on the right-hand side of the boat, and you will find some." When they did, they could not pull the net back in because there were so many fish.

Then the follower whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord!" As soon as Simon Peter heard him say, "It is the Lord," he wrapped his outer coat around him (for he had taken it off) and jumped into the water.
The other followers came in the boat, towing the net full of fish. They were not far from the shore, only about ninety metres.
When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish you have just caught."
So Simon Peter climbed back into the boat and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three of them. Even with so many, the net was not torn.
Jesus said to them, "Come and have breakfast." None of the followers dared to ask him, "Who are you?" They knew it was the Lord.
Jesus came, took the bread and gave it to them, and he did the same with the fish.
This was now the third time Jesus showed himself to his followers after he was raised from the dead.
When they had finished eating, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."
Again Jesus asked, "Simon son of Jonah, do you love me?" He answered, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Take care of my sheep."

The third time he said to him, "Simon son of Jonah, do you love me?" Peter was hurt because Jesus asked him the third time, "Do you love me?" He said, "Lord, you know everything. You know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my sheep.

I tell you for certain, when you were younger, you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you do not want to go."
Jesus said this to show the kind of death by which Peter would bring glory to God. Then he said to him, "Follow me!"
Peter turned and saw that the follower whom Jesus loved was following them. This was the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper and asked, "Lord, who is going to betray you?"
When Peter saw him, he asked, "Lord, what about him?"
Jesus answered, "If I want him to remain alive until I come back, what does that matter to you? You must follow me."

Because of this, a rumour spread among the believers that this follower would not die. But Jesus did not say that he would not die. He only said, "If I want him to remain alive until I come back, what does that matter to you?"
This is the follower who is telling about these things and who wrote them down. We know that what he says is true.
Jesus also did many other things. If every one of them were written down, I suppose that the whole world would not have room for all the books that would be written. Amen.
Acts: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,
until the day he was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, he gave orders to the apostles he had chosen.
After he suffered, he showed himself to them alive, and gave many proofs. He appeared to them over forty days and spoke about God's Kingdom.
While he was with them, he gave them this order: "Do not leave Jerusalem. Wait for what the Father promised, which you heard about from me.
John baptised with water, but in a few days you will be baptised with the Holy Spirit."
When they had come together, they asked him, "Lord, is this the time you will give the kingdom back to Israel?"
He said to them, "It is not for you to know the times or dates that the Father has set by his own authority.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you. You will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth."
After he said this, he was taken up while they watched, and a cloud hid him from their sight.
They were still staring into the sky as he went, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.
They said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you saw him go."
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the hill called the Mount of Olives. It is near Jerusalem, about a kilometre away.

When they arrived, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying. Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James were there.
They all kept praying together with one mind. The women were with them, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the believers, a group of about one hundred and twenty people, and said,
"Brothers, the Scripture had to come true which the Holy Spirit spoke long ago through David. It was about Judas, who led the men who arrested Jesus.
He was one of us, and he had a share in this work."
Judas bought a field with the money he was paid for his evil act. There he fell head first, his body burst open, and all his insides poured out.
Everyone living in Jerusalem heard about this. So in their language they called that field Akeldama, which means Field of Blood.
Peter said, "It is written in the book of Psalms, 'Let his home become empty. Let no one live in it.' And also, 'Let someone else take his place of leadership.'
"So we must choose one of the men who have been with us the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among us,
from the time John baptised him until the day he was taken up from us. One of these must join us as a witness that Jesus rose from the dead."
They put forward two men: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also known as Justus, and Matthias.
Then they prayed, "Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which of these two you have chosen
to take over this work as an apostle, which Judas left to go where he belongs."
Then they drew lots, and the lot fell to Matthias. So he was added to the eleven apostles.
When the day of Pentecost came, the believers were all together in one place.
Suddenly a sound like a strong rushing wind came from the sky, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability.
At that time there were Jews staying in Jerusalem, God-fearing men from every nation on earth.
When they heard this sound, a crowd came together. They were confused, because each one heard the believers speaking in his own language.
They were amazed and said to one another, "Look, are not all these men who are speaking from Galilee?
Then how is it that each of us hears them in our own native language?
We are Parthians, Medes, and Elamites. We come from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
from Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene. Some of us are visitors from Rome, both Jews and people who have turned to the Jewish faith.
Some are from Crete and Arabia. Yet we hear them telling about the great things God has done, in our own languages!"
They were all amazed and puzzled, and they asked one another, "What does this mean?"
But others laughed at them and said, "They have had too much wine."
Then Peter stood up with the eleven apostles and spoke loudly to the crowd: "Men of Judea and all of you living in Jerusalem, let me explain this to you. Listen to what I say.
These people are not drunk, as you think. It is only nine o'clock in the morning.
No, this is what the prophet Joel spoke about:
'God says, In the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
In those days I will pour out my Spirit even on my servants, both men and women, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
The sun will turn dark and the moon will turn red as blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
"Men of Israel, listen to this! Jesus of Nazareth was a man God showed to you as his own. God did great works, wonders, and signs through him among you, as you yourselves know.
God planned and knew ahead of time that Jesus would be handed over to you. And with the help of wicked men, you killed him by nailing him to a cross.
But God raised him from the dead and set him free from the pain of death, because death could not keep its hold on him.
David said this about him: 'I always saw the Lord in front of me. He is at my right side, so I will not be shaken.
That is why my heart is glad and my tongue is full of joy. My body also will rest in hope,
because you will not leave my soul in the place of the dead. You will not let your Holy One rot away.
You have shown me the ways of life. You will fill me with joy in your presence.'
"Brothers, I can tell you plainly that our ancestor David died and was buried, and his tomb is still here with us today.
But he was a prophet. He knew that God had promised him with an oath that one of his descendants would sit on his throne.
So David saw ahead and spoke about the Christ rising from the dead. He said that the Christ was not left in the place of the dead, and his body did not rot away.
God raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it.
Now he has been lifted up to the right side of God. He has received from the Father the Holy Spirit he promised, and he has poured out what you now see and hear.
David himself did not go up to heaven, but he said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
"So let all Israel know for certain this: God has made this Jesus, whom you nailed to a cross, both Lord and Christ."
When the people heard this, they were deeply troubled. They said to Peter and the other apostles, "Brothers, what should we do?"
Peter answered, "Turn away from your sins and be baptised, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ, so that your sins will be forgiven. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
This promise is for you and your children, and for all who are far away, for everyone the Lord our God calls to himself."
Peter warned them with many other words and begged them, "Save yourselves from these twisted people!"
Those who accepted his message were baptised, and about three thousand people were added to the believers that day.
They kept on learning from the apostles' teaching. They shared their lives together, broke bread together, and prayed.
Everyone was filled with awe, and the apostles did many wonders and signs.
All the believers stayed together and shared everything they had.
They sold their land and the things they owned, and gave the money to anyone who was in need.
Every day they kept meeting together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts.
They praised God and were liked by all the people. And every day the Lord added to their group those who were being saved.
One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at three in the afternoon, the time for prayer.
A man who had been lame from birth was being carried there. Every day people put him by the temple gate called Beautiful, so he could beg from those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to go in, he asked them for money.
Peter looked straight at him, and so did John. Then Peter said, "Look at us."
So the man looked at them, hoping to get something from them.
But Peter said, "I have no silver or gold, but I will give you what I do have. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!"
Peter took him by the right hand and helped him up. At once the man's feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped up, stood, and began to walk. Then he went into the temple with them, walking, jumping, and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They knew he was the man who used to sit and beg at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. They were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
The man held on to Peter and John, and all the people ran to them in the place called Solomon's Porch. They were greatly amazed.
When Peter saw this, he said to them, "Men of Israel, why are you surprised at this? Why do you stare at us, as if we made this man walk by our own power or goodness?

The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our ancestors, has given glory to his servant Jesus. You handed him over and rejected him in front of Pilate, even when Pilate had decided to let him go.
You rejected the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer to be set free instead.
You killed the one who gives life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
It is by faith in the name of Jesus that this man you see and know has been made strong. Faith that comes through Jesus has made him completely well, as you can all see.
"Now, brothers, I know that you did this without understanding, and so did your leaders.
But this is how God made happen what he had told through all his prophets: that his Christ would suffer.
"So turn away from your sins and turn back to God, so that your sins may be wiped away. Then times of refreshing will come from the Lord,
and he will send Jesus, the Christ he chose for you.
Jesus must stay in heaven until the time comes for God to make all things new, as he promised long ago through his holy prophets.
Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people. You must listen to everything he tells you.
Anyone who does not listen to that prophet will be completely cut off from God's people.'
"Yes, all the prophets from Samuel on, all who have spoken, also told about these days.
You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your ancestors. He said to Abraham, 'Through your descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
God raised up his servant and sent him first to you, to bless you by turning each of you away from your evil ways."
While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees came up to them.
They were very upset because the apostles were teaching the people and saying that through Jesus the dead will rise.
They arrested Peter and John and, because it was already evening, they kept them in jail until the next day.
But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men who believed grew to about five thousand.
The next day the rulers, the elders, and the teachers of the law met in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there, and so were Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and the other men of the high priest's family.
They had Peter and John stand in front of them and asked, "By what power or in what name did you do this?"
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers and elders of the people,
today you are asking us about a kind thing we did for a man who could not walk. You want to know how he was healed.
Then all of you and all the people of Israel should know this: this man stands before you healed by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. You nailed him to a cross, but God raised him from the dead.
Jesus is 'the stone you builders rejected, which has become the most important stone of the building.'
Salvation is found in no one else. There is no other name under heaven given to people by which we must be saved."
The leaders saw how bold Peter and John were, and they knew they were ordinary men with no schooling. They were amazed, and they realised that these men had been with Jesus.
They could also see the man who had been healed standing there with them, so there was nothing they could say against it.
So they ordered them to leave the council room, and then talked it over among themselves.
They said, "What should we do with these men? Everyone living in Jerusalem knows they have done an amazing miracle, and we cannot deny it.
But to stop this from spreading any further among the people, we must warn them not to speak to anyone in this name again."
So they called them back in and ordered them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered, "You decide which is right in God's eyes: to obey you, or to obey God.
We cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard."
After more threats, they let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, because all the people were praising God for what had happened.
The man who had been healed by this miracle was more than forty years old.
After they were set free, Peter and John went back to their own people and told them everything the chief priests and elders had said.
When they heard it, they all prayed to God together: "Lord, you made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
By the Holy Spirit you spoke through our ancestor David, your servant: 'Why do the nations rage? Why do the peoples make useless plans?
The kings of the earth get ready to fight, and the rulers come together against the Lord and against his Christ.'
"It is true. Herod and Pontius Pilate met together in this city with the Gentiles and the people of Israel. They came together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you chose.
They did what your power and your plan had already decided should happen.
Now, Lord, see how they threaten us. Help your servants to speak your word very boldly.
Stretch out your hand to heal, and let signs and wonders be done through the name of your holy servant Jesus."
After they prayed, the place where they were meeting shook. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God's word boldly.
All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one said that anything they owned was their own. They shared everything they had.
With great power the apostles kept telling people that the Lord Jesus had risen from the dead. And God's grace was on all of them.
There was no one in need among them. From time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money,
and put it at the apostles' feet. Then it was given to anyone who had need.
Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, was called Barnabas by the apostles. That name means Son of Encouragement.
He sold a field he owned, brought the money, and put it at the apostles' feet.
But a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold some land.
With his wife's full knowledge, he kept back part of the money for himself. He brought the rest and put it at the apostles' feet.
Then Peter said, "Ananias, why did you let Satan fill your heart? You have lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back some of the money you got for the land.
Did the land not belong to you before you sold it? And after it was sold, was the money not yours to use? Why did you think of doing such a thing? You have not lied to people, but to God."
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. And great fear came on everyone who heard what had happened.
Some young men came, wrapped up his body, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later his wife came in. She did not know what had happened.
Peter asked her, "Tell me, is this the price you and Ananias got for the land?" She said, "Yes, that was the price."
Peter said to her, "Why did you both agree to test the Spirit of the Lord? Listen! The men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out too."
At once she fell down at his feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came on the whole church and on everyone who heard about these things.
The apostles did many signs and wonders among the people. All the believers used to meet together in Solomon's Porch.
No one else dared to join them, but the people thought very highly of them.
More and more men and women believed in the Lord and were added to their number.
People even carried the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, so that at least Peter's shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
Crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem. They brought their sick and those troubled by evil spirits, and all of them were healed.
Then the high priest and all his friends, who belonged to the group of the Sadducees, became very jealous.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the jail doors and brought them out. He said,
"Go, stand in the temple courts, and tell the people all about this new life."

So at daybreak they went into the temple courts and began to teach. When the high priest and his friends arrived, they called together the council, all the elders of Israel. Then they sent to the jail for the apostles.
But when the officers got there, they did not find them in the jail. So they went back and reported,
"We found the jail locked up tight, with the guards standing at the doors. But when we opened them, there was no one inside!"
When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this, they were puzzled and wondered what would come of it.
Then someone came and said, "Look! The men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people."
So the captain went with his officers and brought the apostles back. They did not use force, because they were afraid the people would throw stones at them.
They brought the apostles in and made them stand before the council. The high priest questioned them.
He said, "We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name. But you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to blame us for this man's death."
Peter and the other apostles answered, "We must obey God rather than people.
The God of our ancestors raised Jesus from the dead. You killed him by hanging him on a cross.
God lifted him up to his own right side as Prince and Saviour, so that Israel could turn away from sin and be forgiven.
We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When the council heard this, they were furious and wanted to kill them.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up in the council. He was a teacher of the law, respected by all the people. He ordered the apostles to be taken outside for a short time.
Then he said to the council, "Men of Israel, be careful what you plan to do to these men.
Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be someone important, and about four hundred men followed him. He was killed, and all his followers were scattered, and it all came to nothing.
After him, Judas from Galilee appeared in the days of the count of the people. He got people to follow him. He also was killed, and all his followers were scattered.
So in this case I tell you, leave these men alone. Let them go. If their plan or work comes from people, it will fail.
But if it comes from God, you will not be able to stop them. You might even find yourselves fighting against God."
The council agreed with him. They called the apostles in and had them beaten. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
The apostles left the council full of joy, because God had counted them worthy to suffer shame for the name of Jesus.
Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they never stopped teaching and telling the good news that Jesus is the Christ.

In those days the number of followers was growing fast. The Greek-speaking Jews began to complain about the Hebrew-speaking Jews, because their widows were being left out when food was handed out each day.
So the twelve apostles called all the followers together and said, "It would not be right for us to stop preaching God's word in order to serve food at tables.
So, brothers, choose seven men from among you who are well respected and full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will put them in charge of this work.
Then we can keep giving our time to prayer and to teaching the word."

Everyone liked this idea. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit. They also chose Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus from Antioch, who had turned to the Jewish faith.
They brought these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
So God's word kept spreading. The number of followers in Jerusalem grew very large, and many priests also came to believe.
Stephen was full of God's grace and power, and he did great wonders and signs among the people.
But some men began to argue with Stephen. They were from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, and some were from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia.
But they could not stand up against the wisdom the Spirit gave him when he spoke.
So they secretly talked some men into saying, "We heard Stephen speak evil words against Moses and against God."
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the teachers of the law. They grabbed Stephen and brought him before the council.
They brought in false witnesses, who said, "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
We heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses gave us."
Everyone sitting in the council stared at Stephen, and they saw that his face looked like the face of an angel.
Then the high priest asked Stephen, "Are these things true?"
Stephen answered, "Brothers and fathers, listen to me. The God of glory appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran.
God said to him, 'Leave your country and your relatives, and go to the land I will show you.'
So he left the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. After his father died, God sent him to this land where you now live.
God gave him no land here, not even enough to put his foot on. But even though Abraham had no child yet, God promised that he and his descendants after him would own this land.
God told him this: 'Your descendants will live as strangers in a land that is not theirs. They will be made slaves and treated badly for four hundred years.
But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves,' God said, 'and after that they will come out and worship me in this place.'

Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. So when Abraham became the father of Isaac, he circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of the twelve fathers of our nation.
"Those fathers were jealous of Joseph, so they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him.
He rescued him from all his troubles. He gave Joseph wisdom and made Pharaoh, king of Egypt, like him. So Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over Egypt and over all his palace.
Then there was a famine in all of Egypt and Canaan, and people suffered greatly. Our ancestors could not find food.
When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
On their second visit, Joseph told his brothers who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.
Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five people in all.
So Jacob went down to Egypt, and there he and our ancestors died.
Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and buried in the tomb Abraham had bought with silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
"As the time came near for God to keep his promise to Abraham, the number of our people in Egypt grew and grew.
Then a new king who knew nothing about Joseph came to rule Egypt.
He was cruel to our people and treated our ancestors badly. He forced them to leave their babies outside so that they would die.
At that time Moses was born, and he was a very beautiful child in God's eyes. For three months he was cared for in his father's house.
When he was put outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
Moses was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in what he said and did.
"When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his own people, the people of Israel.
He saw one of them being treated badly by an Egyptian, so he went to help him. He struck the Egyptian and killed him to defend the man.
Moses thought his own people would understand that God was using him to save them, but they did not understand.
The next day Moses saw two of them fighting, and he tried to make peace between them. He said, 'Men, you are brothers. Why do you hurt each other?'
But the man who was hurting the other pushed Moses aside and said, 'Who made you our ruler and judge?
Do you want to kill me like you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
When Moses heard this, he ran away to the land of Midian. He lived there as a foreigner and had two sons.
"After forty years, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
When Moses saw it, he was amazed. As he went closer to look, he heard the voice of the Lord:
'I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Moses shook with fear and did not dare to look.
Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off your sandals, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have seen how badly my people are treated in Egypt. I have heard their groans, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.'
"This is the same Moses the people had rejected when they said, 'Who made you our ruler and judge?' God sent him to be their ruler and rescuer, through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He led them out of Egypt and did wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the desert for forty years.
This is the Moses who told the people of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people.'
He was with the people in the desert, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our ancestors. He received living words from God to pass on to us.
"But our ancestors refused to obey him. They pushed him aside, and in their hearts they wanted to go back to Egypt.
They said to Aaron, 'Make us gods who will lead us. As for this Moses who brought us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
That was when they made an idol shaped like a calf. They brought sacrifices to it and held a party to celebrate what they had made with their own hands.

But God turned away from them and let them worship the stars in the sky. This agrees with what is written in the book of the prophets: 'People of Israel, did you bring me animals to kill and sacrifices for forty years in the desert?
No, you carried the tent of the god Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, idols you made to worship. So I will send you away beyond Babylon.'
"Our ancestors had the tent of meeting with them in the desert. It was made just as God told Moses, following the pattern he had seen.

Later our ancestors who received the tent brought it with them when they went with Joshua into this land. They took the land from the nations God drove out ahead of them. The tent stayed here until the time of David.
David found favour with God and asked if he could build a house for the God of Jacob.
But it was Solomon who built the house for God.
"But the Most High does not live in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says,
'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me? says the Lord. Where is the place I will rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?'
"You stubborn people! Your hearts and ears are closed to God. You always fight against the Holy Spirit, just as your ancestors did.
Was there ever a prophet your ancestors did not attack? They even killed those who told ahead of time about the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him.
You received the law that was given through angels, but you have not obeyed it."
When the members of the council heard this, they were furious and ground their teeth at him.
But Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit. He looked up to heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at God's right side.
He said, "Look! I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right side of God!"
Then they shouted loudly and covered their ears. They all rushed at him together,
dragged him out of the city, and began to throw stones at him. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
Then he fell on his knees and cried out, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." When he had said this, he fell asleep in death.

Saul agreed that Stephen should be killed. On that day a great attack began against the church in Jerusalem. All the believers except the apostles were scattered through the lands of Judea and Samaria.
Some godly men buried Stephen and cried loudly over him.
But Saul was trying to destroy the church. He went from house to house, dragged off men and women, and threw them into prison.
Those who had been scattered went everywhere, preaching the word.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and told the people about the Christ.
When the crowds heard Philip and saw the signs he did, they all listened closely to what he said.
Evil spirits came out of many people, screaming loudly. And many who could not move or could not walk were healed.
So there was great joy in that city.
Now a man named Simon had been practising magic in that city for some time. He amazed the people of Samaria and claimed to be someone great.
Everyone, from the least to the greatest, listened to him and said, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
They followed him because he had amazed them with his magic for a long time.
But Philip told them the good news about God's Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ. They believed him, and both men and women were baptised.
Simon himself also believed and was baptised. He followed Philip everywhere, amazed by the great signs and miracles he saw.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that the people of Samaria had accepted God's word, they sent Peter and John to them.
When Peter and John arrived, they prayed for the new believers to receive the Holy Spirit.
The Holy Spirit had not yet come on any of them. They had only been baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John placed their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given when the apostles placed their hands on people, he offered them money.
He said, "Give me this power too, so that anyone I place my hands on will receive the Holy Spirit."
Peter answered, "May your money be destroyed with you, because you thought you could buy God's gift with money!
You have no part or share in this work, because your heart is not right with God.
Turn away from this evil and pray to the Lord. Perhaps he will forgive you for having such a thought in your heart.
I can see that you are full of bitter jealousy and are a prisoner of sin."
Then Simon answered, "Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said will happen to me."
After Peter and John had told what they knew and preached the word of the Lord, they went back to Jerusalem. On the way they preached the good news in many villages of Samaria.
Then an angel of the Lord said to Philip, "Get up and go south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is a desert road.
So he got up and went. On the way he met a man from Ethiopia, an important official in charge of all the money of Candace, queen of Ethiopia. He was a eunuch, and he had gone to Jerusalem to worship.
Now he was on his way home, sitting in his chariot and reading the book of the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit told Philip, "Go to that chariot and stay near it."
So Philip ran up to the chariot and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. Philip asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
The man said, "How can I, unless someone explains it to me?" So he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
This is the part of Scripture he was reading: "He was led like a sheep to be killed. Like a lamb is silent while its wool is cut, he did not open his mouth.
When he was put to shame, he was not treated fairly. Who can speak of his descendants? For his life was taken from the earth."
The official asked Philip, "Please tell me, who is the prophet talking about? Himself or someone else?"
Then Philip began with that same Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
As they travelled along the road, they came to some water. The official said, "Look, here is water. What is stopping me from being baptised?"
He ordered the chariot to stop. Then both Philip and the official went down into the water, and Philip baptised him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away. The official did not see him again, but he went on his way full of joy.
Philip appeared at Azotus. He travelled through all the towns, preaching the good news, until he came to Caesarea.
Meanwhile, Saul was still making threats to kill the Lord's followers. He went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. He wanted to find any people who belonged to the Way, men or women, tie them up, and bring them back to Jerusalem.
As Saul came near Damascus on his journey, a light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me?"
Saul asked, "Who are you, Lord?" He answered, "I am Jesus, the one you are attacking.
Now get up and go into the city. There you will be told what you must do."
The men travelling with Saul stood there unable to speak. They heard the sound, but they did not see anyone.
Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes, he could not see anything. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he was blind, and he did not eat or drink anything.
In Damascus there was a follower named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision: "Ananias!" He answered, "Yes, Lord, here I am."
The Lord told him, "Get up and go to the house of Judas on Straight Street. Ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying right now.
In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and place his hands on him so that he can see again."
Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard many reports about this man and all the harm he has done to your people in Jerusalem.
And he has come here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on your name."
But the Lord said to him, "Go! I have chosen this man to carry my name to the Gentiles and their kings, and to the people of Israel.
I will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

So Ananias went to the house and placed his hands on Saul. He said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
At once something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptised.
Then he ate some food and got his strength back. Saul spent several days with the followers in Damascus.
Right away he began to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

All who heard him were amazed. They asked, "Is this not the man who caused so much harm in Jerusalem to those who call on this name? Did he not come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?"
But Saul grew more and more powerful. He confused the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
After many days had gone by, the Jews made a plan to kill Saul.
But Saul learned about their plan. Day and night they watched the city gates closely so that they could kill him.
But his followers took him one night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall.
When Saul came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the followers, but they were all afraid of him. They did not believe he was really a follower.

But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road and how the Lord had spoken to him. He also told them how boldly Saul had preached in the name of Jesus in Damascus.
So Saul stayed with them and went freely all around Jerusalem,
speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He talked and argued with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they tried to kill him.
When the believers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

Then the church all through Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had a time of peace and grew strong. It kept growing in number as the believers lived in the fear of the Lord and were comforted by the Holy Spirit.
As Peter travelled around the country, he went to visit God's people who lived in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who could not move and had been lying in bed for eight years.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." At once Aeneas got up.
Everyone who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a follower named Tabitha. In Greek her name is Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping the poor.
About that time she became sick and died. Her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa. So when the followers heard that Peter was in Lydda, they sent two men to him. They begged him, "Please come at once!"

Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, he was taken upstairs. All the widows stood around him, crying. They showed him the coats and other clothes Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
Peter sent them all out of the room. Then he got down on his knees and prayed. He turned towards the dead woman and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called the believers and the widows and showed them that she was alive.
This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for some time with a man named Simon, who made leather.
In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius. He was a Roman army officer in what was called the Italian Regiment.
He and all his family were godly and feared God. He gave freely to people in need and prayed to God all the time.
One day at about three in the afternoon, he had a vision. He clearly saw an angel of God come to him and say, "Cornelius!"
Cornelius stared at him in fear. "What is it, Lord?" he asked. The angel answered, "Your prayers and your gifts to the poor have gone up to God, and he has remembered you.
Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon, who is also called Peter.
He is staying with Simon the leather maker, whose house is by the sea."
When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a godly soldier who was one of his helpers.
He told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.
The next day, as they were on their way and coming near the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray. It was about noon.
He became hungry and wanted something to eat. While the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
In it were all kinds of four-footed animals, as well as reptiles and birds.
Then a voice told him, "Get up, Peter. Kill and eat."
But Peter said, "Surely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything that is impure or unclean."
The voice spoke to him a second time: "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean."
This happened three times, and then the sheet was taken back up to heaven at once.
While Peter was wondering what the vision could mean, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon's house and stood at the gate.
They called out, asking if Simon, who was called Peter, was staying there.
While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Simon, three men are looking for you.
So get up and go downstairs. Do not doubt, but go with them, because I have sent them."
Peter went down and said to the men, "I am the one you are looking for. Why have you come?"

The men answered, "We have come from Cornelius, an army officer. He is a good man who fears God, and all the Jewish people respect him. A holy angel told him to invite you to his house so that he could hear what you have to say."
Then Peter invited the men in to be his guests. The next day Peter went with them, and some of the believers from Joppa went along.
The following day he arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, and he had invited his relatives and close friends.
As Peter came into the house, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.
But Peter made him get up. "Stand up," he said. "I am only a man myself."
While talking with him, Peter went inside and found a large group of people gathered.
He said to them, "You know that it is against our law for a Jew to visit or spend time with a Gentile. But God has shown me that I should not call anyone impure or unclean.
So when I was sent for, I came without asking any questions. May I ask why you sent for me?"
Cornelius answered, "Four days ago I was fasting and praying in my house at this same time, three in the afternoon. Suddenly a man in shining clothes stood in front of me.
He said, 'Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and has remembered your gifts to the poor.
Send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is staying in the house of Simon the leather maker, by the sea. When he comes, he will speak to you.'
So I sent for you right away, and it was good of you to come. Now we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has told you to say."
Then Peter began to speak: "Now I truly understand that God does not treat people differently.
He accepts people from every nation who fear him and do what is right.
You know the message God sent to the people of Israel. It is the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
You know what happened all through Judea, starting in Galilee after John preached about baptism.
You know how God poured out the Holy Spirit and power on Jesus of Nazareth. He went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil, because God was with him.
"We are witnesses of everything he did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a cross.
But God raised him from the dead on the third day and let him be seen.
He was not seen by all the people, but by us, the witnesses God had already chosen. We ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
He told us to preach to the people and to tell them that he is the one God has chosen to judge the living and the dead.
All the prophets speak about him. They say that everyone who believes in him will have their sins forgiven through his name."
While Peter was still saying these things, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message.
The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.
They heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Then Peter said,
"Surely no one can stop these people from being baptised with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have."
So he ordered that they be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.
The apostles and the believers all through Judea heard that the Gentiles had also accepted God's word.
So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the Jewish believers who held to circumcision argued with him.
They said, "You went into the house of men who are not circumcised, and you ate with them!"
So Peter began to explain to them step by step what had happened.
He said, "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision. Something like a large sheet was being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came down to where I was.
I looked closely at it and saw four-footed animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
Then I heard a voice telling me, 'Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.'
I answered, 'Surely not, Lord! Nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
The voice spoke from heaven a second time: 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'
This happened three times, and then it was all pulled back up to heaven.
Right then three men who had been sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
The Spirit told me to go with them and not to think of them as different. These six brothers also went with me, and we went into the man's house.
He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house. The angel said, 'Send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter.
He will bring you a message through which you and all your family will be saved.'
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came on them, just as he came on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered what the Lord had said: 'John baptised with water, but you will be baptised with the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stand in God's way?"
When they heard this, they had nothing more to say. They praised God and said, "So then, God has given even the Gentiles the chance to turn from sin and receive life."
The believers who had been scattered by the attacks that began when Stephen was killed travelled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They told the message only to Jews.
But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began to speak to Greeks too, telling them the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord's power was with them, and a large number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
News of this reached the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw what God's grace had done, he was glad. He encouraged them all to stay true to the Lord with all their hearts.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.

When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year Barnabas and Saul met with the church and taught large numbers of people. It was in Antioch that the followers were first called Christians.
During this time some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and through the Spirit said that a great famine would spread over the whole world. This happened while Claudius was emperor.
The followers decided that each of them would send help to the believers living in Judea, as much as each one was able.
They did this, sending their gift to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
About this time King Herod began to arrest some who belonged to the church, to hurt them.
He had James, the brother of John, killed with a sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he arrested Peter too. This happened during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting Peter, Herod put him in prison, with four groups of four soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
So Peter was kept in prison, but the church kept praying hard to God for him.
The night before Herod was going to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, tied with two chains. Guards stood at the door watching the prison.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up. "Quick, get up!" he said. And the chains fell off Peter's wrists.
Then the angel said to him, "Get dressed and put on your sandals." Peter did so. "Put your coat on and follow me," the angel told him.
Peter followed him out of the prison, but he did not know that what the angel was doing was really happening. He thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened for them by itself, and they went through it. They walked the length of one street, and suddenly the angel left him.
Then Peter came to himself and said, "Now I know for certain that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod's power, and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen."
When he understood this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John, who was also called Mark. Many people had gathered there and were praying.
Peter knocked at the outer door, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
When she knew Peter's voice, she was so happy that she ran back without opening the door. She told them, "Peter is at the door!"
They said to her, "You are out of your mind." But she kept saying it was true. So they said, "It must be his angel."
But Peter kept on knocking. When they opened the door and saw him, they were amazed.
Peter waved his hand to tell them to be quiet. He told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. "Tell James and the other brothers about this," he said. Then he left for another place.
In the morning there was a great fuss among the soldiers about what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched for him but could not find him. So he questioned the guards and ordered them to be put to death. Then Herod went from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Herod had been very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him together, after winning over Blastus, a trusted servant of the king. They asked for peace, because their country got its food from the king's country.
On the chosen day Herod put on his royal robes, sat on his throne, and gave a speech to the people.
The people shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not of a man!"
At once an angel of the Lord struck Herod down, because he did not give glory to God. He was eaten by worms and died.
But God's word kept spreading, and more and more people believed.
When Barnabas and Saul had finished their work, they went back from Jerusalem, taking with them John, who was also called Mark.
In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the ruler, and Saul.
While they were worshipping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work I have called them to do."
So after they had fasted and prayed, they placed their hands on them and sent them off.
The Holy Spirit sent Barnabas and Saul on their way. They went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
When they arrived at Salamis, they preached God's word in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their helper.
They travelled through the whole island until they came to Paphos. There they met a Jewish magician, a false prophet named Bar-Jesus.
He was a friend of the governor, Sergius Paulus, who was a wise man. The governor sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God's word.
But Elymas the magician, which is what his name means, tried to stop them. He tried to turn the governor away from the faith.
Then Saul, who was also called Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
and said, "You child of the devil! You are full of every kind of lie and trick, and you are an enemy of everything that is right. Will you never stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord?

Now the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind and will not see the light of the sun for a while." At once a dark mist came over him, and he went around looking for someone to lead him by the hand.
When the governor saw what had happened, he believed. He was amazed at the teaching about the Lord.
From Paphos, Paul and his friends sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. There John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
From Perga they went on to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the leaders of the synagogue sent them a message: "Brothers, if you have a message of encouragement for the people, please speak."
Paul stood up, waved his hand, and said, "Men of Israel, and you Gentiles who worship God, listen to me.
The God of the people of Israel chose our ancestors. He made the people great while they lived as strangers in Egypt, and with his mighty power he led them out of that country.
For about forty years he put up with them in the desert.
He destroyed seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to his people as their own.
All this took about four hundred and fifty years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled for forty years.
After removing Saul, God made David their king. God said about him, 'I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart. He will do everything I want him to do.'
From David's descendants God has brought to Israel the Saviour Jesus, as he promised.
Before Jesus came, John preached to all the people of Israel that they should turn from their sins and be baptised.
As John was finishing his work, he said, 'Who do you think I am? I am not the one you are waiting for. But someone is coming after me, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.'
"Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who worship God, this message of salvation has been sent to us.

The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not know who Jesus was. They did not understand the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath. But by condemning him, they made those words come true.
Even though they found no good reason to put him to death, they asked Pilate to have him killed.
When they had done everything that was written about him, they took him down from the cross and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead.
For many days he was seen by those who had travelled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to our people.
"We are telling you the good news: what God promised our ancestors
he has done for us, their children, by raising Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm, 'You are my Son. Today I have become your Father.'
God raised him from the dead, never to rot away. He said, 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.'
So he also says in another Psalm, 'You will not let your Holy One rot away.'
"David served God's purpose in his own time. Then he died, was buried with his ancestors, and his body rotted away.
But the one God raised from the dead did not rot away.
"So, brothers, I want you to know that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is told to you.
Through him everyone who believes is set free from every sin, something the law of Moses could never do for you.
Be careful, so that what the prophets said does not happen to you:
'Look, you who mock! Wonder and die! For I am doing something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.'"
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to speak about these things again on the next Sabbath.
When the meeting ended, many Jews and godly people who had turned to the Jewish faith followed Paul and Barnabas. They talked with them and urged them to keep living in the grace of God.
On the next Sabbath almost the whole city came to hear the word of the Lord.
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy. They spoke against what Paul was saying and insulted him.
Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: "We had to speak God's word to you first. But since you reject it and do not think you are worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
This is what the Lord has commanded us: 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'"
When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the word of the Lord. All who were chosen for eternal life believed.
The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.
But the Jews stirred up the important God-fearing women and the leading men of the city. They started an attack against Paul and Barnabas and threw them out of their area.
So Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet as a warning to them and went on to Iconium.
And the followers were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went together into the Jewish synagogue. They spoke so well that a large number of Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and turned their minds against the believers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord. The Lord showed that their message about his grace was true by letting them do signs and wonders.
The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
Then some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, made a plan to hurt them and kill them with stones.
But the apostles found out about it and escaped to Lystra and Derbe, cities in Lycaonia, and to the area around them.
There they kept on preaching the good news.
In Lystra there sat a man whose feet were crippled. He had been lame from birth and had never walked.
He listened as Paul was speaking. Paul looked straight at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
So Paul called out loudly, "Stand up on your feet!" At that, the man jumped up and began to walk.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us in human form!"
They called Barnabas Zeus, and they called Paul Hermes, because he was the main speaker.
The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and flowers to the city gates. He and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to the apostles.
But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard about this, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting,

"Friends, why are you doing this? We are only human, just like you. We are bringing you good news, telling you to turn away from these useless things to the living God. He made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
In the past, he let all the nations go their own way.
But he has always given proof of who he is by the good things he does. He gives you rain from the sky and crops in their seasons. He gives you plenty of food and fills your hearts with joy."
Even with these words, they could hardly stop the crowd from offering sacrifices to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and won the crowd over to their side. They threw stones at Paul and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
But after the followers had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas left for Derbe.
They preached the good news in that city and made many followers. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
There they made the followers stronger and encouraged them to stay true to the faith. They said, "We must go through many hard times to enter God's Kingdom."
Paul and Barnabas chose elders for them in each church. With prayer and fasting, they put them in the care of the Lord, in whom they had put their trust.
After going through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
They preached the word in Perga and then went down to Attalia.
From Attalia they sailed back to Antioch. That was where they had been put into God's care for the work they had now finished.
When they arrived, they gathered the church together. They told everything God had done through them, and how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
And they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
Some men came down from Judea to Antioch and were teaching the believers: "Unless you are circumcised as Moses taught, you cannot be saved."
Paul and Barnabas strongly disagreed with them and argued with them. So Paul, Barnabas, and some other believers were chosen to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
The church sent them on their way. As they went through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made all the believers very happy.
When they came to Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, the apostles, and the elders. They reported everything God had done through them.
Then some of the believers who belonged to the group of the Pharisees stood up and said, "The Gentiles must be circumcised and told to obey the law of Moses."
The apostles and elders met together to think about this question.
After much talk, Peter stood up and said to them, "Brothers, you know that some time ago God chose me from among you, so that the Gentiles would hear the message of the good news from me and believe.
God knows the heart, and he showed that he accepted them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us.
He made no difference between us and them, for he made their hearts clean by faith.
So why are you testing God now? Why are you putting a heavy load on the necks of the followers, a load that neither we nor our ancestors were able to carry?
No! We believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are."
The whole group became quiet as they listened to Barnabas and Paul. They told about the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
When they finished speaking, James said, "Brothers, listen to me.
Simon Peter has told us how God first showed his care for the Gentiles by choosing from them a people for himself.
The words of the prophets agree with this. As it is written,
'After this I will return and build again David's fallen tent. I will rebuild what was ruined, and I will set it up again,
so that the rest of humanity may look for the Lord, including all the Gentiles who are called by my name. This is what the Lord says, who does these things.'
These things have been known from long ago.
"So my decision is that we should not make it hard for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
Instead, we should write to them, telling them to stay away from food made unclean by idols, from sexual sin, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
The law of Moses has been preached in every city from long ago, and it is read in the synagogues every Sabbath."

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to choose some of their own men and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, called Barsabbas, and Silas, two men who were leaders among the believers.
They sent this letter with them: "From the apostles and elders, your brothers, to the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
We have heard that some men went out from us without our permission and troubled you with what they said, upsetting your minds.
So we all agreed to choose some men and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul.
They have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we are sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things we are writing.
It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to put any more weight on you than these necessary rules:
Stay away from food offered to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual sin. You will do well to keep away from these things. Goodbye."
So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch. There they gathered the church together and gave them the letter.
The people read it and were glad for its encouraging message.
Judas and Silas, who were prophets themselves, said many things to encourage the believers and make them stronger.
After spending some time there, they were sent off in peace by the believers to go back to those who had sent them.
But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. There they and many others taught and preached the word of the Lord.
Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us go back and visit the believers in all the towns where we preached the word of the Lord, and see how they are doing."
Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, with them.
But Paul did not think it was wise to take him, because he had left them in Pamphylia and had not kept on with them in the work.
They had such a sharp argument that they went their separate ways. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
but Paul chose Silas and left, after the believers put him into the care of the Lord's grace.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches stronger.
Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra. A follower named Timothy lived there. His mother was a Jewish believer, but his father was a Greek.
The believers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
Paul wanted to take Timothy with him on the journey. So he circumcised him because of the Jews who lived in that area, since they all knew that his father was a Greek.
As they travelled from town to town, they gave the believers the rules decided by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, and told them to obey them.
So the churches were made stronger in the faith and grew in number every day.
Paul and his friends travelled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, because the Holy Spirit had stopped them from preaching the word in Asia.
When they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
During the night Paul had a vision. A man from Macedonia was standing there, begging him, "Come over to Macedonia and help us."
After Paul had seen the vision, we got ready at once to leave for Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news to the people there.
From Troas we sailed straight to Samothrace, and the next day on to Neapolis.
From there we travelled to Philippi, a Roman colony and the leading city of that part of Macedonia. We stayed there several days.
On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to the river, where we expected to find a place of prayer. We sat down and began to speak to the women who had gathered there.
One of those listening was a woman named Lydia, from the city of Thyatira. She sold expensive purple cloth, and she worshipped God. The Lord opened her heart to accept Paul's message.
She and the people of her house were baptised. Then she invited us to her home. "If you agree that I truly believe in the Lord," she said, "come and stay at my house." And she made us come.
One day, as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl who had a spirit that told the future. She earned a lot of money for her owners by telling fortunes.
She followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God. They are telling you the way to be saved."

She kept doing this for many days. Finally Paul became so troubled that he turned around and said to the spirit, "In the name of Jesus Christ I order you to come out of her!" At that very moment the spirit left her.
When her owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into the market place to face the authorities.
They brought them to the city officials and said, "These men are Jews, and they are making trouble in our city.
They are teaching customs that we Romans are not allowed to accept or practise."
The crowd joined the attack against Paul and Silas. The officials ordered them to be stripped and beaten with rods.
After they had been beaten many times, they were thrown into prison. The jailer was ordered to guard them carefully.
Because of this order, he put them in the inner cell and locked their feet between heavy blocks of wood.
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
