So what can we say about all this? If God is on our side, who can be against us?
God did not hold back even his own Son, but gave him up for all of us. Since he did that, will he not also freely give us everything else, together with Christ?
Who can bring any charge against the people God has chosen? It is God himself who declares them not guilty.
Who then can condemn them? Christ Jesus died for us. More than that, he was raised to life. He is at the right hand of God, and he is praying for us.
Who can separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, hardship, persecution, hunger, poverty, danger or violent death?
As the Scriptures say, "Because of you we face death all day long. We are treated like sheep that are led to be killed."
No! In all these things we win an overwhelming victory through Christ, who loved us.
I am fully convinced that nothing can separate us from God's love. Not death or life, not angels or ruling spirits, not anything now or anything in the future, not any powers,
not anything high above or deep below, nor anything else in all creation. Nothing can separate us from the love of God that is ours in Christ Jesus our Lord.
I speak the truth in Christ. I am not lying. My conscience confirms it in the Holy Spirit.
I have great sorrow and unending pain in my heart.
I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my people, my own flesh and blood.
They are Israelites. Theirs is the adoption as sons. Theirs is the divine glory, the covenants, the receiving of the law, the temple worship and the promises.
Theirs are the fathers, and from them, according to the flesh, is the Christ, who is God over all, forever praised! Amen.
It is not as though God's word had failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are truly Israel.
Nor because they are his descendants are they all Abraham's children. On the contrary, "It is through Isaac that your offspring will be counted."
In other words, it is not the children by physical descent who are God's children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as Abraham's offspring.
For this was how the promise was stated: "At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son."
Not only that, but Rebekah's children were conceived at the same time by our father Isaac.
Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God's purpose in election might stand,
not by works but by him who calls, she was told, "The older will serve the younger."
Just as it is written: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."
What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Not at all!
For he says to Moses, "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."
It does not, therefore, depend on human desire or effort, but on God's mercy.
For Scripture says to Pharaoh: "I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth."
Therefore God has mercy on whom he wants to have mercy, and he hardens whom he wants to harden.
One of you will say to me: "Then why does God still blame us? For who is able to resist his will?"
But who are you, a human being, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?"
Does not the potter have the right to make out of the same lump of clay some pottery for special purposes and some for common use?
What if God, although choosing to show his wrath and make his power known, bore with great patience the objects of his wrath, prepared for destruction?
What if he did this to make the riches of his glory known to the objects of his mercy, whom he prepared in advance for glory?
Even us, whom he also called, not only from the Jews but also from the nations?
As he says in Hosea: "I will call them 'my people' who are not my people; and I will call her 'my loved one' who is not my loved one."
And, "In the very place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called 'children of the living God.'"
Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the Israelites be like the sand by the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
For the Lord will carry out his sentence on earth with speed and finality."
It is just as Isaiah said earlier: "Unless the Lord Almighty had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah."
What then shall we say? That the nations, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith.
But the people of Israel, who pursued the law as the way of righteousness, have not attained their goal.
Why not? Because they pursued it not by faith but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone.
As it is written: "See, I lay in Zion a stone that causes people to stumble and a rock that makes them fall, and the one who believes in him will never be put to shame."
Brothers and sisters, my heart's desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is that they may be saved.
For I can testify about them that they are zealous for God, but their zeal is not based on knowledge.
Since they did not know the righteousness of God and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God's righteousness.
Christ is the culmination of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.
Moses writes this about the righteousness that is by the law: "The person who does these things will live by them."
But the righteousness that is by faith says: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?'" that is, to bring Christ down,
or "Who will descend into the deep?" that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
But what does it say? "The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart," that is, the message concerning faith that we proclaim:
If you declare with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
For it is with your heart that you believe and are made right with God, and it is with your mouth that you profess your faith and are saved.
As Scripture says, "Anyone who believes in him will never be put to shame."
For there is no difference between Jew and Greek. The same Lord is Lord of all and richly blesses all who call on him.
For, "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved."
How, then, can they call on the one they have not believed in? And how can they believe in the one of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone preaching to them?
And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? As it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!"
But not all the Israelites accepted the good news. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our message?"
Consequently, faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the word about Christ.
But I ask: Did they not hear? Of course they did. "Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world."
Again I ask: Did Israel not understand? First, Moses says, "I will make you envious by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation that has no understanding."
And Isaiah boldly says, "I was found by those who did not seek me; I revealed myself to those who did not ask for me."
But concerning Israel he says, "All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and obstinate people."
I ask then: Did God reject his people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
God did not reject his people, whom he foreknew. Don't you know what Scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel?
"Lord, they have killed your prophets and torn down your altars. I am the only one left, and they are trying to kill me."
And what was God's answer to him? "I have reserved for myself seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal."
So too, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
And if by grace, then it cannot be based on works. If it were, grace would no longer be grace.
What then? What the people of Israel sought so earnestly they did not obtain. The elect among them did, but the others were hardened,
as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear, to this very day."
And David says: "May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution for them.
May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent for ever."
Again I ask: Did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Not at all! Rather, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the nations to make Israel envious.
But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the nations, how much greater riches will their full inclusion bring!
I am talking to you who are of the nations. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the nations, I take pride in my ministry
in the hope that I may somehow arouse my own people to envy and save some of them.
For if their rejection brought friendship with God to the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
If the part of the dough offered as firstfruits is holy, then the whole batch is holy. If the root is holy, so are the branches.
If some of the branches have been broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others and now share in the nourishing sap from the olive root,
do not consider yourself to be superior to those other branches. If you do, consider this: you do not support the root, but the root supports you.
You will say then, "Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in."
Granted. But they were broken off because of unbelief, and you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but tremble.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, he will not spare you either.
Consider therefore the kindness and sternness of God: sternness to those who fell, but kindness to you, provided that you continue in his kindness. Otherwise, you also will be cut off.
And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

After all, if you were cut out of an olive tree that is wild by nature, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you may not be conceited: Israel has experienced a hardening in part until the full number of the nations has come in,
and in this way all Israel will be saved. As it is written: "The deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn godlessness away from Jacob.
And this is my covenant with them when I take away their sins."
As far as the good news is concerned, they are enemies for your sake. But as far as election is concerned, they are loved on account of the patriarchs,
for God's gifts and his call are irrevocable.
Just as you who were at one time disobedient to God have now received mercy as a result of their disobedience,
so they too have now become disobedient in order that they too may now receive mercy as a result of God's mercy to you.
For God has bound everyone over to disobedience so that he may have mercy on them all.
Oh, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgements, and his paths beyond tracing out!
"Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counsellor?"
"Who has ever given to God, that God should repay them?"
For from him and through him and for him are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.
Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God. This is your true and proper worship.
Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God's will is, his good, pleasing and perfect will.

For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but rather think of yourself with sober judgement, in accordance with the faith God has distributed to each of you.
For just as each of us has one body with many members, and these members do not all have the same function,
so in Christ we, though many, form one body, and each member belongs to all the others.
We have different gifts, according to the grace given to each of us. If your gift is prophesying, then prophesy in accordance with your faith.
If it is serving, then serve. If it is teaching, then teach.
If it is to encourage, then give encouragement. If it is giving, then give generously. If it is to lead, do it diligently. If it is to show mercy, do it cheerfully.
Love must be sincere. Hate what is evil. Cling to what is good.
Be devoted to one another in love. Honour one another above yourselves.
Never be lacking in zeal, but keep your spiritual fervour, serving the Lord.
Be joyful in hope, patient in trouble, faithful in prayer.
Share with the Lord's people who are in need. Practise hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice. Mourn with those who mourn.
Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but be willing to associate with people of low position. Do not be conceited.
Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Be careful to do what is right in the eyes of everyone.
If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God's anger, for it is written: "It is mine to avenge; I will repay," says the Lord.
On the contrary: "If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him something to drink. In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head."
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established. The authorities that exist have been established by God.
Consequently, whoever rebels against the authority is rebelling against what God has instituted, and those who do so will bring judgement on themselves.
For rulers hold no terror for those who do right, but for those who do wrong. Do you want to be free from fear of the one in authority? Then do what is right and you will be commended.

For the one in authority is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for rulers do not bear the sword for no reason. They are God's servants, agents of wrath to bring punishment on the wrongdoer.
Therefore, it is necessary to submit to the authorities, not only because of possible punishment but also as a matter of conscience.
This is also why you pay taxes, for the authorities are God's servants, who give their full time to governing.
Give to everyone what you owe them. If you owe taxes, pay taxes. If revenue, then revenue. If respect, then respect. If honour, then honour.
Let no debt remain outstanding, except the continuing debt to love one another, for whoever loves others has fulfilled the law.

The commandments, "You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not murder," "You shall not steal," "You shall not covet," and whatever other command there may be, are summed up in this one command: "Love your neighbour as yourself."
Love does no harm to a neighbour. Therefore love is the fulfilment of the law.
And do this, understanding the present time: the hour has already come for you to wake up from your slumber, because our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
The night is nearly over. The day is almost here. So let us put aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armour of light.
Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
Rather, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not think about how to gratify the desires of the sinful nature.
Accept the one whose faith is weak, without quarrelling over disputable matters.
One person's faith allows them to eat anything, but another, whose faith is weak, eats only vegetables.
The one who eats everything must not treat with contempt the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted them.
Who are you to judge someone else's servant? To their own master, servants stand or fall. And they will stand, for the Lord is able to make them stand.
One person considers one day more sacred than another. Another considers every day alike. Each of them should be fully convinced in their own mind.
Whoever regards one day as special does so to the Lord. Whoever eats meat does so to the Lord, for they give thanks to God. And whoever abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
For none of us lives for ourselves alone, and none of us dies for ourselves alone.
If we live, we live for the Lord. And if we die, we die for the Lord. So, whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For this very reason, Christ died and returned to life so that he might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
You, then, why do you judge your brother or sister? Or why do you treat them with contempt? For we will all stand before God's judgement seat.
It is written: "'As surely as I live,' says the Lord, 'every knee will bow before me; every tongue will acknowledge God.'"
So then, each of us will give an account of ourselves to God.
Therefore let us stop passing judgement on one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in the way of a brother or sister.
I am convinced, being fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for that person it is unclean.
If your brother or sister is distressed because of what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy someone for whom Christ died.
Therefore do not let what you know is good be spoken of as evil.
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Because anyone who serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and receives human approval.
Let us therefore make every effort to do what leads to peace and to mutual building up.
Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a person to eat anything that causes someone else to stumble.
It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything else that will cause your brother or sister to fall.
So whatever you believe about these things keep between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
But whoever has doubts is condemned if they eat, because their eating is not from faith. And everything that does not come from faith is sin.
Now to him who is able to establish you in accordance with my good news, the message I proclaim about Jesus Christ, in keeping with the revelation of the mystery hidden for long ages past,
but now revealed and made known through the prophetic writings by the command of the eternal God, so that all the nations might come to the obedience that comes from faith,
to the only wise God be glory for ever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
We who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
Each of us should please our neighbours for their good, to build them up.
For even Christ did not please himself but, as it is written: "The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me."
For everything that was written in the past was written to teach us, so that through the endurance taught in the Scriptures and the encouragement they provide we might have hope.
May the God who gives endurance and encouragement give you the same attitude of mind toward each other that Christ Jesus had,
so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring praise to God.
For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the Jews on behalf of God's truth, so that the promises made to the patriarchs might be confirmed
and, moreover, that the nations might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written: "Therefore I will praise you among the nations; I will sing the praises of your name."
Again, it says, "Rejoice, you nations, with his people."
And again, "Praise the Lord, all you nations; let all the peoples extol him."
And again, Isaiah says, "The Root of Jesse will spring up, one who will arise to rule over the nations; in him the nations will hope."
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
I myself am convinced, my brothers and sisters, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with knowledge and competent to instruct one another.
Yet I have written to you quite boldly on some points to remind you of them again, because of the grace God gave me

to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the nations. He gave me the priestly duty of proclaiming the good news of God, so that the nations might become an offering acceptable to God, made holy by the Holy Spirit.
Therefore I glory in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
I will not venture to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the nations to obey God by what I have said and done,
by the power of signs and wonders, through the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the good news of Christ.
It has always been my ambition to preach the good news where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else's foundation.
Rather, as it is written: "Those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand."
This is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
But now that there is no more place for me to work in these regions, and since I have been longing for many years to visit you,
I plan to do so when I go to Spain. I hope to see you while passing through and to have you assist me on my journey there, after I have enjoyed your company for a while.
Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem in the service of the Lord's people there.
For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the Lord's people in Jerusalem.
They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the nations have shared in the Jews' spiritual blessings, they owe it to the Jews to share with them their material blessings.
So after I have completed this task and have made sure that they have received this contribution, I will go to Spain and visit you on the way.
I know that when I come to you, I will come in the full measure of the blessing of Christ.
I urge you, brothers and sisters, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
Pray that I may be kept safe from the unbelievers in Judea and that the contribution I take to Jerusalem may be favourably received by the Lord's people there,
so that I may come to you with joy, by God's will, and in your company be refreshed.
The God of peace be with you all. Amen.
I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchreae.
I ask you to receive her in the Lord in a way worthy of his people and to give her any help she may need from you, for she has been the benefactor of many people, including me.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.
They risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the nations are grateful to them.
Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my dear friend Epaenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
Greet Mary, who worked very hard for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow Jews who have been in prison with me. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
Greet Ampliatus, my dear friend in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my dear friend Stachys.
Greet Apelles, whose fidelity to Christ has stood the test. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my fellow Jew. Greet those in the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, those women who work hard in the Lord. Greet my dear friend Persis, another woman who has worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me, too.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas and the other brothers and sisters with them.
Greet Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the Lord's people who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send greetings.
I urge you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who cause divisions and put obstacles in your way that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Keep away from them.
For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the minds of naive people.
Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice because of you. But I want you to be wise about what is good, and innocent about what is evil.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
Timothy, my co-worker, sends his greetings to you, as do Lucius, Jason and Sosipater, my fellow Jews.
I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, whose hospitality I and the whole church here enjoy, sends you his greetings. Erastus, who is the city's director of public works, and our brother Quartus send you their greetings.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
1Cor: From Paul, called by God's will to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and from our brother Sosthenes.

I write to God's church in Corinth. You have been made holy in Christ Jesus and called to be his holy people. I write also to everyone everywhere who calls on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God for you, because of the grace he has given you in Christ Jesus.
In him you have been made rich in every way, in all your speaking and in all your knowledge.
This shows that what we told you about Christ has been made firm in you.
So you do not lack any gift as you wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be shown to the world.
He will keep you strong to the end, so that no one can blame you on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful. He called you to share life with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
Brothers and sisters, I beg you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to agree with each other. Do not split into groups. Be joined together, with the same mind and the same way of thinking.
My brothers and sisters, some people from Chloe's household have told me that you are quarrelling.
This is what I mean. One of you says, "I follow Paul." Another says, "I follow Apollos." Another says, "I follow Cephas." And another says, "I follow Christ."
Has Christ been divided? Was Paul nailed to a cross for you? Were you baptised in the name of Paul?
I thank God that I did not baptise any of you except Crispus and Gaius.
So no one can say that you were baptised in my name.
Oh yes, I also baptised the household of Stephanas. Apart from them, I do not remember baptising anyone else.
Christ did not send me to baptise, but to tell the good news. And I do not tell it with clever words, so that the cross of Christ does not lose its power.
The message of the cross seems foolish to those who are being lost. But to us who are being saved, it is the power of God.
The Scriptures say, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. I will make the cleverness of clever people come to nothing."
So where is the wise person? Where is the teacher of the law? Where is the great debater of this world? God has shown that the wisdom of this world is foolish.
In his wisdom, God made sure the world could not know him through its own wisdom. Instead, God was pleased to save those who believe through the message we preach, which seems foolish.
Jews ask for signs, and Greeks look for wisdom.
But we preach Christ nailed to a cross. This is a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to non-Jews.
But to those whom God has called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength.
Brothers and sisters, think about what you were when God called you. Not many of you were wise by human standards. Not many were powerful. Not many came from important families.
But God chose what the world thinks is foolish to put the wise to shame. God chose what the world thinks is weak to put the strong to shame.
God chose what the world thinks is low and looked down on, and what counts for nothing, to bring to nothing what the world thinks is important.
So no one can boast before God.
It is because of God that you are in Christ Jesus. Christ has become wisdom from God for us. He makes us right with God, holy and free.
So, as the Scriptures say, "Whoever boasts should boast about the Lord."
Brothers and sisters, when I came to you, I did not come with fine speeches or great wisdom as I told you God's message.
I decided that while I was with you, I would think about nothing except Jesus Christ and his death on the cross.
I came to you weak, afraid and trembling.
My words and my preaching did not use clever human wisdom to win you over. Instead, they showed the power of the Spirit.
I did this so that your faith would not rest on human wisdom, but on the power of God.
But we do speak wisdom among those who are grown up in faith. It is not the wisdom of this world, or of the rulers of this world, who are coming to nothing.
We speak God's hidden wisdom, his secret plan. Before time began, God planned it for our glory.
None of the rulers of this world understood it. If they had, they would not have nailed the glorious Lord to a cross.
But as the Scriptures say, "No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no mind has imagined what God has prepared for those who love him."
But God has shown these things to us through his Spirit. The Spirit searches everything, even the deep things of God.
Who can know a person's thoughts except that person's own spirit inside them? In the same way, no one knows God's thoughts except God's Spirit.
We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who comes from God. So we can understand what God has freely given us.
We speak about these things with words taught by the Spirit, not by human wisdom. We explain spiritual truths with spiritual words.
A person without the Spirit does not accept the things that come from God's Spirit. They seem foolish to them. They cannot understand them, because only the Spirit can help us understand them.
The person who has the Spirit can judge all things, but no one can judge that person.
The Scriptures ask, "Who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to teach him?" But we have the mind of Christ.
Brothers and sisters, I could not speak to you as people who live by the Spirit. I had to speak to you as people who still follow their human nature, like babies in Christ.
I fed you with milk, not solid food, because you were not ready for it. And you are still not ready.
You still follow your human nature. There is jealousy and quarrelling among you. Does this not show that you are living like people of the world?
One of you says, "I follow Paul," and another says, "I follow Apollos." Are you not acting like people of the world?
Who is Apollos? And who is Paul? We are only servants who helped you to believe. Each of us did the work the Lord gave us.
I planted the seed, and Apollos watered it. But God made it grow.
So the one who plants is not important, and neither is the one who waters. Only God, who makes things grow, is important.
The one who plants and the one who waters have the same goal. Each will be rewarded for their own work.
We work together for God. You are God's field. You are God's building.
By the grace God gave me, I laid a foundation like a wise master builder. Now someone else is building on it. But each person must be careful how they build.
No one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
People may build on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay or straw.
But the quality of each person's work will be seen on the day of judgement. That day will come with fire, and the fire will test what kind of work each person has done.
If what someone has built lasts, they will receive a reward.
If it is burned up, they will lose their reward. But they themselves will be saved, like someone escaping through a fire.
Do you not know that you yourselves are God's temple, and that God's Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person. For God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.
Do not fool yourselves. If any of you think you are wise by the standards of this world, you should become foolish, so that you can become truly wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness to God. The Scriptures say, "He catches the wise in their own clever tricks."
And again, "The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are worthless."
So do not boast about human leaders. Everything belongs to you.
Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, the present and the future, all of it belongs to you.
And you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
So think of us as servants of Christ, trusted with the secret truths of God.
Those who are trusted with something must prove to be faithful.
It matters very little to me if I am judged by you or by any human court. I do not even judge myself.
My conscience is clear, but that does not make me right. It is the Lord who judges me.

So do not judge anything before the right time. Wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness, and he will show the secret aims of people's hearts. Then each person will receive their praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I have used Apollos and myself as examples to help you. I want you to learn the meaning of the saying, "Do not go beyond what is written." Then you will not be proud of one person and look down on another.
What makes you better than anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if you did not?
You already have all you want! You are already rich! You have become kings without us! I wish you really were kings, so that we could be kings with you!
It seems to me that God has put us apostles last in line, like people sentenced to die. We have become a show for the whole world, for angels and for people.
We are fools for Christ, but you are so wise in Christ! We are weak, but you are strong! You are honoured, but we are looked down on!
Right up to this hour we are hungry and thirsty. We do not have enough clothes. We are beaten, and we have no home.
We work hard with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless them. When we are attacked, we put up with it.
When people say bad things about us, we answer kindly. Even now, we are treated like the rubbish of the world, the dirt everyone scrapes off.
I am not writing this to shame you. I am warning you as my own dear children.
You may have ten thousand teachers in Christ, but you do not have many fathers. I became your father in Christ Jesus when I brought you the good news.
So I beg you, follow my example.
That is why I am sending Timothy to you. He is my dear and faithful son in the Lord. He will remind you of the way I live in Christ Jesus, which is what I teach in every church everywhere.
Some of you have become proud, as if I were not coming to you.
But I will come to you very soon, if the Lord wants me to. Then I will find out not just what these proud people are saying, but what power they have.
For God's kingdom is not a matter of talk, but of power.
Which do you want? Shall I come to you with a stick, or with love and a gentle spirit?
People are actually saying that there is sexual sin among you, a kind that even people who do not know God would not allow. A man is living with his father's wife.
And you are proud! You should be full of sorrow instead. The man who did this should be put out of your group.
Even though I am not with you in body, I am with you in spirit. And as if I were there, I have already judged the man who did this.
When you meet together in the name of our Lord Jesus, I will be with you in spirit, and the power of our Lord Jesus will be there.
Then hand this man over to Satan, so that his sinful nature may be destroyed and his spirit saved on the day of the Lord.
Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little yeast spreads through the whole batch of dough?
Get rid of the old yeast, so that you can be a new batch of dough without yeast, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed for us.
So let us keep the festival, not with the old yeast of hatred and evil, but with the bread without yeast, which is honesty and truth.
In my letter I wrote to you not to mix with people who commit sexual sin.
I did not mean the people of this world who commit sexual sin, or who are greedy, or who cheat, or who worship idols. To avoid them, you would have to leave this world.

What I meant is that you must not mix with anyone who calls themselves a believer but commits sexual sin, or is greedy, or worships idols, or speaks evil of others, or gets drunk, or cheats. Do not even eat with such a person.
It is not my job to judge people outside the church. But you should judge those inside it.
God will judge those outside. As the Scriptures say, "Remove the evil person from among you."
If one of you has a complaint against another believer, how dare you take it to court before people who do not know God, instead of before God's people?
Do you not know that God's people will judge the world? And if you will judge the world, can you not settle even small matters?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? So surely we can judge the things of this life!
So if you have such cases, why do you ask people who count for nothing in the church to judge them?
I say this to shame you. Is there no one among you wise enough to settle a quarrel between believers?
Instead, one believer takes another to court, and in front of unbelievers!
Having court cases against each other already means you have failed. Why not rather be treated wrongly? Why not rather be cheated?
Instead, you yourselves do wrong and cheat, and you do it to your own brothers and sisters.

Do you not know that people who do wrong will not receive God's kingdom? Do not be fooled. People who commit sexual sin, who worship idols, who are unfaithful in marriage, or men who have sex with men,
thieves, greedy people, drunkards, people who speak evil of others, and cheats will not receive God's kingdom.
Some of you used to be like that. But you were washed clean. You were made holy. You were made right with God in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
You say, "I am allowed to do anything." But not everything is good for you. "I am allowed to do anything," but I will not let anything control me.
You say, "Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food." But God will destroy them both. The body is not for sexual sin. It is for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
God raised the Lord from the dead, and he will raise us too by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are parts of Christ's body? So should I take parts of Christ's body and join them to a prostitute? Never!
Do you not know that a man who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her? For the Scriptures say, "The two will become one."
But whoever joins himself to the Lord becomes one with him in spirit.
Run away from sexual sin! Every other sin a person commits is outside the body. But whoever commits sexual sin sins against their own body.
Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who lives in you and was given to you by God? You do not belong to yourselves.
God bought you at a high price. So honour God with your body.
Now about the things you wrote to me. You say, "It is good for a man not to have sex with a woman."
But because there is so much sexual sin, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
A husband should give his wife what she needs as his wife, and a wife should do the same for her husband.
The wife's body does not belong only to her, but also to her husband. In the same way, the husband's body does not belong only to him, but also to his wife.
Do not refuse each other, unless you both agree to stop for a short time to give yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan cannot tempt you because you lack self-control.
I say this as a suggestion, not as a command.
I wish everyone were single like me. But each person has their own gift from God. One has one gift, and another has a different one.
To those who are not married and to widows I say this. It is good for them to stay single, as I am.
But if they cannot control themselves, they should marry. It is better to marry than to burn with desire.
To those who are married I give this command, which comes not from me but from the Lord. A wife must not leave her husband.
But if she does leave him, she must stay single or else make peace with her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
To the rest I say this, and it is from me, not the Lord. If a believing man has a wife who is not a believer, and she is happy to live with him, he must not divorce her.
And if a woman has a husband who is not a believer, and he is happy to live with her, she must not divorce him.

For the husband who does not believe is made holy through his wife, and the wife who does not believe is made holy through her husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but as it is, they are holy.
But if the one who does not believe wants to leave, let them go. In such cases the believing man or woman is not bound. God has called us to live in peace.
Wife, how do you know whether you will save your husband? Husband, how do you know whether you will save your wife?
But each of you should live the life the Lord has given you, the life you had when God called you. This is the rule I give in all the churches.
Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not try to undo it. Was a man not circumcised when he was called? He should not be circumcised.
Being circumcised means nothing, and not being circumcised means nothing. What matters is keeping God's commands.
Each person should stay as they were when God called them.
Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it trouble you. But if you can gain your freedom, take the chance.
For a slave who was called by the Lord is the Lord's free person. In the same way, a free person who was called is Christ's slave.
God bought you at a high price. Do not become slaves of people.
Brothers and sisters, each of you should stay with God in the situation you were in when he called you.
Now about those who have never married. I have no command from the Lord. But I give my opinion as one who, by the Lord's mercy, can be trusted.
Because of the trouble of these present times, I think it is good for a person to stay as they are.
Are you married? Do not try to get out of it. Are you single? Do not look for a wife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a young woman marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will have troubles in this life, and I want to spare you from them.
Brothers and sisters, what I mean is that the time is short. From now on, those who have wives should live as if they had none.
Those who weep should live as if they were not weeping. Those who are happy should live as if they were not happy. Those who buy things should live as if they owned nothing.
Those who use the things of the world should not become wrapped up in them. For this world as we know it is passing away.
I want you to be free from worry. A man who is not married cares about the Lord's work and how to please the Lord.
But a married man cares about the things of this world and how to please his wife.

So his interests are divided. In the same way, a woman who is not married cares about the Lord's work. She wants to be holy in body and spirit. But a married woman cares about the things of this world and how to please her husband.
I am saying this for your own good, not to hold you back. I want you to live in the right way and give yourselves fully to the Lord without other things pulling at you.

If a man thinks he is not treating the young woman he is engaged to in the right way, and his feelings are strong, and he thinks they should marry, he should do as he wants. It is not a sin. They should get married.
But if a man has firmly decided in his heart not to marry, and he is under no pressure, and he has control over his desires, he also does the right thing by not marrying her.
So the man who marries his young woman does well, and the man who does not marry does even better.
A wife is joined to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wants, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
But in my opinion she will be happier if she stays single. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
Now about food offered to idols. We know that "we all have knowledge." But knowledge makes people proud, while love builds people up.
Anyone who thinks they know something does not yet know as they should.
But whoever loves God is known by God.
So about eating food offered to idols: we know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is only one God.
There may be so-called gods in heaven or on earth. In fact, there are many "gods" and many "lords".
But for us there is only one God, the Father. All things come from him, and we live for him. And there is only one Lord, Jesus Christ. All things were made through him, and we live through him.
But not everyone knows this. Some people are still so used to idols that when they eat this food, they think of it as offered to an idol. Their conscience is weak, so they feel unclean.
Food does not bring us closer to God. We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
But be careful that your freedom does not cause someone with a weaker faith to fall.
Suppose someone with a weak conscience sees you, who know better, eating in an idol's temple. Will they not be encouraged to eat food offered to idols?
So this weak believer, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
When you sin against your brothers and sisters like this and hurt their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
So if what I eat causes a believer to fall into sin, I will never eat meat again. I do not want to cause them to fall.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not the result of my work in the Lord?
Others may not think of me as an apostle, but surely you do. You yourselves are the proof that I am the Lord's apostle.
This is my answer to those who question me.
Do we not have the right to food and drink?
Do we not have the right to take a believing wife with us, as the other apostles do, and the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who must work for a living?
What soldier pays his own costs? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its grapes? Who looks after a flock and does not drink its milk?
Is this just human thinking? Does the law not say the same thing?
For it is written in the law of Moses, "Do not tie up the mouth of an ox while it is treading out the grain." Is it oxen that God is worried about?
Is he not really speaking for our sake? Yes, this was written for us. The one who ploughs and the one who threshes should both work in the hope of sharing in the harvest.
We planted spiritual seed among you. Is it too much to ask for a harvest of material help from you?
If others have this right, surely we have it even more. But we did not use this right. We put up with anything rather than get in the way of the good news about Christ.
Do you not know that those who work in the temple get their food from the temple? Those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar.
In the same way, the Lord has commanded that those who preach the good news should get their living from the good news.
But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this so that you will do these things for me. I would rather die than let anyone take away my reason to boast.
Preaching the good news gives me no reason to boast, because I must do it. How terrible it would be for me if I did not preach the good news!
If I did it because I chose to, I would have a reward. But I do not do it by my own choice. I have been trusted with this work.
So what is my reward? It is this: that I can preach the good news free of charge, and not use my right to be paid for it.
I am free and belong to no one. But I have made myself a slave to everyone, to win as many people as possible.
With Jews, I became like a Jew, to win Jews. With those under the law, I became like someone under the law, though I myself am not under the law, to win those under the law.
With those who do not have the law, I became like someone without the law, to win them. This does not mean I am free from God's law. I am under Christ's law.
With the weak, I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by every possible way I might save some.
I do all this for the sake of the good news, so that I can share in its blessings.
Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? So run in a way that will win the prize.
Everyone who competes in the games trains hard and controls themselves. They do it to win a crown that will not last. But we do it to win a crown that will last for ever.
So I do not run without a goal. I do not fight like a boxer hitting the air.
No, I train my body hard and make it obey me. Then, after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to remember what happened to our ancestors. They were all led by the cloud, and they all passed safely through the sea.
They were all baptised into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food,
and they all drank the same spiritual drink. They drank from the spiritual rock that went with them, and that rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, and their bodies were left in the desert.
These things happened as examples for us, so that we will not want evil things as they did.
Do not worship idols, as some of them did. As the Scriptures say, "The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to dance and party."
We must not commit sexual sin, as some of them did. In one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
We must not test Christ, as some of them did. They were killed by snakes.
Do not grumble, as some of them did. They were killed by the destroying angel.
These things happened to them as examples. They were written down to warn us, who are living near the end of the ages.
So if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you do not fall.

No temptation has come to you except what everyone faces. God is faithful. He will not let you be tempted more than you can bear. When you are tempted, he will also give you a way out, so that you can stand up under it.
So, my dear friends, run away from idol worship.
I am speaking to sensible people. Judge for yourselves what I say.
When we give thanks for the cup at the Lord's Supper, are we not sharing in the blood of Christ? When we break the bread, are we not sharing in the body of Christ?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body, for we all share the one loaf.
Think about the people of Israel. Those who eat the sacrifices share in the altar.
What do I mean? That food offered to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
No. I mean that what people who do not know God sacrifice is offered to demons, not to God. I do not want you to share with demons.
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too. You cannot eat at the Lord's table and at the table of demons too.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than he is?
You say, "I am allowed to do anything." But not everything is helpful. "I am allowed to do anything," but not everything builds people up.
No one should look out only for themselves. Look out for the good of others.
Eat anything sold in the meat market without asking questions to ease your conscience.
For the Scriptures say, "The earth and everything in it belong to the Lord."
If someone who does not believe invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat whatever is put in front of you without asking questions to ease your conscience.
But if someone tells you, "This was offered to an idol," then do not eat it. Do this for the sake of the person who told you, and for the sake of conscience.
I mean their conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I eat with thanks to God, why should I be blamed for eating food I have thanked God for?
So whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God.
Do not cause anyone to fall into sin, whether Jews, Greeks or God's church.
I try to please everyone in every way. I am not looking for what is good for me, but for what is good for many people, so that they may be saved.
Follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
I praise you for remembering me in everything, and for holding on to the teachings I passed on to you.
But I want you to understand that Christ is the head of every man, the man is the head of the woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Every man who prays or speaks God's message with his head covered brings shame on his head.
But every woman who prays or speaks God's message with her head uncovered brings shame on her head. It is the same as having her head shaved.
If a woman will not cover her head, she should cut her hair short. But if it is shameful for a woman to cut her hair or shave her head, she should cover her head.
A man should not cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man.
For man did not come from woman, but woman came from man.
And man was not created for woman, but woman for man.
That is why a woman should have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
But in the Lord, woman needs man and man needs woman.
For as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. And everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves. Is it right for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does nature itself not teach you that long hair is a shame for a man?
But long hair is a woman's glory. Her hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we have no other practice, and neither do the churches of God.
In the following things I do not praise you. When you meet together, you do more harm than good.
First, I hear that when you meet as a church, there are divisions among you, and I believe some of it.
No doubt there have to be differences among you, to show which of you have God's approval.
When you meet together, it is not really the Lord's Supper you eat.
For as you eat, some of you go ahead with your own meal. One person stays hungry, and another gets drunk.
Do you not have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you look down on God's church and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? No, I will not praise you for this!
For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you. On the night he was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread.
He gave thanks, broke it and said, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this to remember me."
In the same way, after supper he took the cup and said, "This cup is the new covenant made in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this to remember me."
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you are telling about the Lord's death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in a wrong way will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
Everyone should look closely at themselves before they eat the bread and drink from the cup.
For anyone who eats and drinks without seeing the meaning of the Lord's body eats and drinks judgement on themselves.
That is why many of you are weak and sick, and some of you have died.
But if we judged ourselves rightly, we would not come under judgement.
When the Lord judges us, he is correcting us, so that we will not be condemned with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you meet to eat, wait for each other.
If anyone is hungry, they should eat at home, so that your meetings do not bring judgement on you. I will give more instructions about the other things when I come.
Now, brothers and sisters, I want you to understand about the gifts of the Spirit.
You know that before you believed, you were led astray and carried away to worship idols that cannot speak.
So I want you to know that no one speaking by God's Spirit says, "Jesus is cursed." And no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit gives them.
There are different ways to serve, but we serve the same Lord.
There are different kinds of work, but the same God does all the work in all people.
The Spirit shows himself in each person for the good of everyone.
To one person the Spirit gives a message of wisdom. To another, the same Spirit gives a message of knowledge.
To another, the same Spirit gives faith. To another, the one Spirit gives gifts of healing.

To another he gives power to do miracles, and to another the gift of speaking God's message. To another he gives the ability to tell which spirits are from God. To another he gives the ability to speak in different kinds of languages, and to another the ability to explain what those languages mean.
All these are the work of one and the same Spirit. He gives them to each person as he chooses.
A body is one, even though it has many parts. All its many parts make up one body. It is the same with Christ.
For we were all baptised by one Spirit into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free. And we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
The body is not made up of one part, but of many.
If the foot said, "I am not a hand, so I am not part of the body," that would not stop it being part of the body.
And if the ear said, "I am not an eye, so I am not part of the body," that would not stop it being part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, how could it hear? If the whole body were an ear, how could it smell?
But God has put each part in the body just as he wanted.
If they were all one part, there would be no body.
As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I do not need you." And the head cannot say to the feet, "I do not need you."
In fact, the parts of the body that seem weaker are the ones we cannot do without.
The parts we think are less honourable, we treat with special honour. The private parts we cover with special care,
while the parts that can be seen need no special care. But God has put the body together and given more honour to the parts that lacked it.
So there should be no division in the body. Instead, all its parts should care for each other equally.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it. If one part is honoured, every part is happy with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

In the church God has given first apostles, second prophets, third teachers. Then there are those who do miracles, those with gifts of healing, those who help others, those who lead, and those who speak in different kinds of languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all do miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in other languages? Do all explain what they mean?
But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the best way of all.
If I speak in the languages of people and of angels, but do not have love, I am only a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of speaking God's message, and understand all secrets and all knowledge, and if I have enough faith to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give away everything I own to feed the poor, and even give up my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love is patient. Love is kind. Love is not jealous. It does not boast. It is not proud.
It is not rude. It does not look out only for itself. It is not easily angered. It does not keep a record of wrongs.
Love is not happy with evil, but is happy with the truth.
Love always protects, always trusts, always hopes, and always keeps going.
Love never ends. But the gift of speaking God's message will come to an end. The gift of speaking in other languages will stop. Knowledge will pass away.
For now we know only in part, and we speak God's message only in part.
But when what is complete comes, what is only in part will pass away.
When I was a child, I talked like a child. I felt like a child, and I thought like a child. When I became a man, I put childish ways behind me.
Now we see only a dim picture, as in a mirror. But then we will see face to face. Now I know only in part. Then I will know fully, just as God knows me fully.
So now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.
Make love your aim, and eagerly desire the gifts of the Spirit, most of all the gift of speaking God's message.
Anyone who speaks in another language is not speaking to people but to God. No one understands them. They are speaking secret things by the Spirit.
But anyone who speaks God's message speaks to people to build them up, encourage them and comfort them.
Anyone who speaks in another language builds up only themselves. But anyone who speaks God's message builds up the church.

I would like all of you to speak in other languages, but I would much rather you spoke God's message. The one who speaks God's message is greater than the one who speaks in other languages, unless someone explains what they say, so that the church may be built up.
Brothers and sisters, if I come to you and speak in other languages, how will I help you? Only if I bring you something God has shown me, or some knowledge, or God's message, or teaching.
Even things without life that make sounds, like a flute or a harp, must play clear notes. Otherwise, how will anyone know what tune is being played?
And if the trumpet does not give a clear call, who will get ready for battle?
It is the same with you. If you do not speak words people can understand, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
There are many different languages in the world, and every one of them has meaning.
But if I do not understand someone's language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker is a foreigner to me.
It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have the gifts of the Spirit, try to have plenty of the gifts that build up the church.
So anyone who speaks in another language should pray for the ability to explain what they say.
For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my mind does not understand.
So what shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
If you praise God only with your spirit, how can someone who does not understand say "Amen" to your prayer of thanks? They do not know what you are saying.
You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not built up.
I thank God that I speak in other languages more than all of you.
But in church I would rather speak five words that people can understand, to teach them, than ten thousand words in another language.
Brothers and sisters, stop thinking like children. Be like babies when it comes to evil, but in your thinking be grown up.
In the law it is written, "The Lord says, I will speak to this people through people of other languages and through the lips of foreigners. But even then they will not listen to me."
So speaking in other languages is a sign, not for believers but for unbelievers. But speaking God's message is a sign, not for unbelievers but for believers.
So if the whole church meets and everyone speaks in other languages, and some outsiders or unbelievers come in, will they not say you are out of your minds?
But if everyone speaks God's message, and an unbeliever or outsider comes in, they will be shown their sin by all, and judged by all.
The secrets of their heart will be brought into the open. Then they will fall down and worship God, saying, "God is really here among you!"

So what should we do, brothers and sisters? When you meet together, one of you has a song, another a teaching, another something God has shown them, another a message in another language, and another an explanation of it. Everything must be done to build up the church.
If anyone speaks in another language, two or at most three should speak, one at a time. And someone must explain what they say.
If there is no one to explain, the speaker should keep quiet in church and speak only to themselves and to God.
Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should think carefully about what is said.
If God shows something to another person who is sitting there, the first speaker should stop.
For you can all speak God's message one by one, so that everyone may learn and be encouraged.
Prophets can control their own spirits.
For God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of God's people.
Women should keep quiet in the churches. They are not allowed to speak, but must be under authority, as the law says.
If they want to ask about something, they should ask their own husbands at home. For it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
Did the word of God begin with you? Or are you the only people it has reached?
If anyone thinks they are a prophet or have gifts of the Spirit, let them accept that what I am writing to you is the Lord's command.
If anyone ignores this, they themselves will be ignored.
So, my brothers and sisters, be eager to speak God's message, and do not stop people from speaking in other languages.
But everything should be done in a proper and orderly way.
Brothers and sisters, I want to remind you of the good news I preached to you. You received it, and you stand firm in it.
By this good news you are saved, if you hold on to the message I preached to you. Otherwise you have believed for nothing.
What I received, I passed on to you as most important: Christ died for our sins, as the Scriptures said.
He was buried, and he was raised to life on the third day, as the Scriptures said.
He appeared to Cephas, and then to the twelve apostles.
After that, he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at the same time. Most of them are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles.
Last of all he appeared to me too, as to someone born at the wrong time.
For I am the least of the apostles. I do not even deserve to be called an apostle, because I attacked God's church.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace to me was not wasted. I worked harder than all of them. Yet it was not really me, but God's grace that was with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
If we preach that Christ was raised from the dead, how can some of you say that the dead are not raised to life?
If the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.
More than that, we would be lying about God. We have said that God raised Christ from the dead. But he did not raise him if the dead are not raised.
For if the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is worthless, and you are still in your sins.
Then those who have died believing in Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we should be pitied more than anyone else.
But Christ really has been raised from the dead. He is the first of the great harvest of all who have died.
Death came through a man, and rising from the dead also comes through a man.
For as everyone dies because of Adam, so everyone who belongs to Christ will be made alive.
But each in the right order: Christ first, and then, when he comes, those who belong to him.
Then the end will come. Christ will destroy every ruler, every authority and every power, and hand over the kingdom to God the Father.
For Christ must rule until God has put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For the Scriptures say, "God has put everything under his feet." But when it says everything has been put under him, it clearly does not include God himself, who put everything under Christ.
When all this is done, the Son himself will be made subject to God, who put everything under him. Then God will be everything to everyone.
If there is no rising from the dead, what will people do who are baptised for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptised for them?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
Brothers and sisters, I face death every day. That is as sure as my pride in you, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus only for human reasons, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, then "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
Do not be fooled: "Bad company ruins good character."
Come back to your senses as you should, and stop sinning. Some of you do not know God. I say this to shame you.
But someone may ask, "How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?"
How foolish! What you plant does not come to life unless it dies first.
When you plant, you do not plant the whole plant that will grow. You plant only a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.
But God gives it the body he has chosen, and to each kind of seed he gives its own body.
Not all flesh is the same. People have one kind of flesh, animals another, birds another and fish another.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. The glory of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and the glory of the earthly bodies is another.
The sun has one kind of glory, the moon another and the stars another. And each star is different from the others in its glory.
It will be the same when the dead are raised. The body that is buried will decay, but the body that is raised will never decay.
It is buried in shame, but raised in glory. It is buried in weakness, but raised in power.
It is buried as a natural body, but raised as a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
The Scriptures say, "The first man, Adam, became a living person." But the last Adam, Christ, became a spirit who gives life.
The spiritual did not come first. The natural came first, and then the spiritual.
The first man was made from the dust of the earth. The second man came from heaven.
Those who belong to the earth are like the man made of dust. And those who belong to heaven are like the man from heaven.
Just as we have been like the man made of dust, we will also be like the man from heaven.
Brothers and sisters, I tell you this: flesh and blood cannot receive God's kingdom. What decays cannot receive what never decays.
Listen, I tell you a secret. We will not all die, but we will all be changed.
It will happen in a moment, in the blink of an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised never to decay, and we will be changed.
For our bodies that decay must be clothed with what never decays. Our bodies that die must be clothed with what never dies.
When this happens, the Scriptures will come true: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
"Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?"
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the Lord's work, because you know that your work in the Lord is never wasted.
Now about the money being collected for God's people. Do what I told the churches in Galatia to do.
On the first day of every week, each of you should put aside some money, as much as you can afford. Then there will be no need to collect money when I come.
When I arrive, I will send the people you choose with letters, to take your gift to Jerusalem.
If it seems right for me to go too, they can travel with me.
I will come to you after I go through Macedonia, because I am planning to travel through Macedonia.
I may stay with you for a while, perhaps even for the whole winter. Then you can help me on my way, wherever I go next.
I do not want to see you now just in passing. I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord allows.
But I will stay in Ephesus until the festival of Pentecost,
because a wide door for great work has opened for me, even though many people are against me.
If Timothy comes, make sure he has nothing to fear while he is with you. He is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
So no one should look down on him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he can come back to me. I am expecting him with the other believers.
Now about our brother Apollos. I strongly urged him to visit you with the other believers. He did not want to go now, but he will go when he has the chance.
Be alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be brave. Be strong.
Do everything in love.
You know that the household of Stephanas were the first believers in Achaia. They have given themselves to serving God's people. Brothers and sisters, I beg you,
follow the lead of people like them, and of everyone who works hard with them.
I was glad when Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus arrived. They have made up for your not being here.
They cheered me up, and they cheered you up too. People like this deserve to be honoured.
The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters here send you greetings. Greet each other with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.
If anyone does not love the Lord, let that person be cursed. Come, Lord!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
2Cor: From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and from our brother Timothy. I write to God's church in Corinth, and to all God's holy people everywhere in Achaia.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. He is the Father who shows mercy, and the God who gives all comfort.
He comforts us in all our troubles. Then we can comfort others in any trouble, with the same comfort God has given us.
We share a lot in the sufferings of Christ. In the same way, we also share a lot of comfort through Christ.
If we have trouble, it is for your comfort and for your saving. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort too. It helps you to bear patiently the same sufferings that we bear.
Our hope for you is firm. We know that as you share in our sufferings, you also share in our comfort.
Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the trouble we had in the province of Asia. The load on us was far too heavy for our strength, so that we even gave up hope of staying alive.
In our hearts we felt we had been sentenced to death. But this happened so that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
He saved us from such a terrible danger of death, and he will save us again. We have put our hope in him, that he will keep on saving us.
You help us too by praying for us. Then many people will thank God for the kindness he shows us because so many prayed.

This is what we are proud of. Our conscience tells us that we have lived in the world, and even more with you, in a holy and honest way that comes from God. We did not live by worldly wisdom, but by God's grace.
We write to you only what you can read and understand. And I hope you will understand fully,
as you have already understood us in part. Then on the day of our Lord Jesus you will be proud of us, just as we will be proud of you.
Because I was sure of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you would be blessed twice.
I planned to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and again on my way back from Macedonia. Then you could send me on my way to Judea.
When I made this plan, did I change my mind too easily? Do I make my plans the way worldly people do, ready to say "Yes, yes" and "No, no" at the same time?
As surely as God is faithful, what we told you was not "Yes" and "No" at the same time.
Jesus Christ, the Son of God, whom Silas, Timothy and I preached to you, was not "Yes" and "No." In him it has always been "Yes."
However many promises God has made, they are all "Yes" in Christ. That is why we say "Amen" through him, to bring glory to God.
It is God who makes both us and you stand firm in Christ. He has anointed us.
He has put his mark of ownership on us, and he has put his Spirit in our hearts as a first payment of what is to come.
I call on God as my witness that I did not come back to Corinth because I wanted to spare you.
We are not trying to rule over your faith. We are working with you for your joy, because you stand firm in your faith.
So I made up my mind that I would not make another painful visit to you.
If I make you sad, who will make me glad? Only you, the ones I made sad.
I wrote to you as I did so that when I came, I would not be made sad by the very people who should make me happy. I was sure that all of you would share my joy.
I wrote to you with a very troubled and aching heart, and with many tears. I did not want to make you sad, but to let you know how deeply I love you.
If anyone has caused sadness, he has not so much made me sad as all of you, at least in part. I do not want to say it too strongly.
The punishment that most of you gave this man is enough for him.
So now you should forgive him and comfort him instead. If you do not, he may be crushed by too much sadness.
So I beg you to show him again that you love him.
I wrote to you to test you, to see if you would obey in everything.
Anyone you forgive, I forgive too. And what I have forgiven, if there was anything to forgive, I have forgiven for your sake in front of Christ.
We do this so that Satan will not get the better of us. We know his tricks very well.
When I came to Troas to preach the good news of Christ, the Lord opened a door for me.
But I still had no peace of mind, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to the people there and went on to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us like a winning army in Christ. Through us he spreads the knowledge of Christ everywhere, like a sweet smell.
