To God we are the sweet smell of Christ among those who are being saved and among those who are dying.
To those who are dying, we are a smell of death that brings death. To those who are being saved, we are a smell of life that brings life. And who is able for such a task?
We are not like so many people who sell God's message to make money. No, we speak honestly in Christ, as people sent from God, standing in front of God.
Are we starting to praise ourselves again? Do we need letters to recommend us to you or from you, as some people do?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts. Everyone can know it and read it.
You show that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our work. It is not written with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God. It is not written on tablets of stone, but on human hearts.
We can be this sure because of Christ, in front of God.
We are not able to do anything by ourselves. Our ability comes from God.
He has made us able to serve a new covenant. It is not a covenant of written law, but of the Spirit. The written law brings death, but the Spirit gives life.

The old way that brought death was carved in letters on stone, and yet it came with glory. The people of Israel could not even look at Moses' face because of its glory, even though that glory was fading.
So the work of the Spirit will have even greater glory.
The old way that brought blame had glory. So the way that makes people right with God has much more glory.
What once had glory now has no glory at all, next to the far greater glory.
If what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of what lasts for ever!
Since we have such a hope, we speak very boldly.
We are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so that the people of Israel would not see the end of the glory that was fading away.
But their minds were closed. Even to this day the same veil stays there when the old covenant is read. It is taken away only in Christ.
Even today, when the books of Moses are read, a veil covers their hearts.
But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And all of us, with faces not covered, see the glory of the Lord as in a mirror. We are being changed to become more like him, with more and more glory. This comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
God in his mercy has given us this work to do, so we do not give up.

We have turned away from secret and shameful ways. We do not use tricks, and we do not twist God's message. Instead, we tell the truth plainly, and so we show everyone's conscience in front of God what kind of people we are.
If the good news we preach is covered by a veil, it is covered only for those who are dying.
The god of this world has blinded the minds of those who do not believe. So they cannot see the light of the good news about the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
We do not preach about ourselves. We preach that Jesus Christ is Lord, and that we are your servants for Jesus' sake.
God said, "Let light shine out of darkness." He is the one who has made his light shine in our hearts. He lets us know the glory of God that we see in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we have this treasure in jars made of clay. This shows that the great power comes from God, and not from us.
We have troubles on every side, but we are not crushed. We are confused, but we do not give up hope.
People attack us, but God does not leave us. We are knocked down, but we are not destroyed.
We always carry in our bodies the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus can also be seen in our bodies.
While we live, we are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that his life can be seen in our bodies that die.
So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
It is written, "I believed, so I spoke." We have the same spirit of faith. We also believe, and so we speak.
We know that God, who raised the Lord Jesus from death, will also raise us with Jesus. He will bring us, together with you, to stand in front of him.
All this is for your good. As God's grace reaches more and more people, more and more people will thank God, and that brings him glory.
So we do not give up. Our bodies are wearing out, but inside we are being made new day by day.
Our troubles are small, and they last only a short time. But they are bringing us a glory that lasts for ever, a glory far greater than all our troubles.
So we do not look at what can be seen, but at what cannot be seen. What can be seen lasts only a short time, but what cannot be seen lasts for ever.
We know that our body here on earth is like a tent. If this tent is taken down, we have a building from God in heaven. It is a home not made by human hands, and it lasts for ever.
While we live in this tent, we groan, because we long to put on our home from heaven like clothes.
When we put it on, we will not be found without clothes.
While we are in this tent, we groan under its weight. We do not want to take off our clothes. We want to put on our new clothes, so that what dies will be swallowed up by life.
God made us for this very thing. And he has given us his Spirit as a first payment of what is to come.
So we are always full of courage. We know that while we are at home in this body, we are away from the Lord.
We live by faith, not by what we see.
We are full of courage. We would rather be away from this body and at home with the Lord.
So whether we are at home in the body or away from it, our goal is to please him.
All of us must stand in front of Christ to be judged. Each one will receive what he deserves for what he did while in the body, whether good or bad.
Since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to win people over. God knows us fully, and I hope you also know us fully in your hearts.
We are not praising ourselves to you again. We are giving you a reason to be proud of us. Then you can answer those who are proud of how things look on the outside, and not of what is in the heart.
If we seem to be out of our minds, it is for God. If we are in our right minds, it is for you.
Christ's love pushes us on. We are sure of this: one man died for everyone, so everyone has died.
He died for everyone, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves. They should live for Christ, who died for them and was raised to life again.
So from now on we do not judge anyone in a worldly way. Once we thought of Christ in a worldly way, but we do not do that any more.
So if anyone belongs to Christ, he is a new person. The old has gone. Look, the new has come!
All this comes from God. Through Christ he made us his friends again, and he gave us the work of bringing others back to him.
This is the message: God was in Christ, making the world his friend again. He did not hold people's sins against them. And he has given us this message of bringing people back to him.
So we speak for Christ, as if God were calling to you through us. We beg you, for Christ's sake: be friends with God again.
Christ had no sin, but God made him become sin for us. So in Christ we can become right with God.
As God's fellow workers, we beg you: do not let the grace you received from God be wasted.
God says, "At the right time I listened to you. On the day of saving I helped you." Listen! Now is the right time. Today is the day of saving.
We try not to put anything in anyone's way, so that no one can find fault with our work.
Instead, in everything we show that we are God's servants. We keep going through troubles, hard times and suffering.
We have been beaten and put in prison. We have faced angry crowds. We have worked hard, gone without sleep and gone without food.
We show it by being pure, by knowing the truth, by being patient and kind, by the Holy Spirit, and by real love.
We show it by speaking the truth and by God's power. We use right living as our weapons, in the right hand and in the left.
Sometimes people honour us, and sometimes they shame us. Sometimes they speak badly of us, and sometimes well. They call us liars, but we tell the truth.
They treat us as unknown, but we are well known. We seem to be dying, but look, we live on. We are beaten, but not killed.
We are sad, but always full of joy. We are poor, but we make many people rich. We have nothing, but we own everything.
People of Corinth, we have spoken openly to you. Our hearts are wide open to you.
We are not holding back our love from you, but you are holding back your love from us.
I speak to you as my children. Open your hearts wide to us in return.
Do not join yourselves with people who do not believe. What do right and wrong have in common? Can light and darkness share anything?
How can Christ agree with the devil? What does a believer share with someone who does not believe?
How can God's temple agree with idols? We are the temple of the living God. As God has said, "I will live with them and walk among them. I will be their God, and they will be my people."
So the Lord says, "Come out from among them and be separate. Touch nothing unclean, and I will welcome you.
I will be your Father, and you will be my sons and daughters, says the Lord All-Powerful."
Dear friends, since we have these promises, let us make ourselves clean from everything that makes body or spirit dirty. Let us become completely holy, because we fear God.
Make room for us in your hearts. We have not wronged anyone. We have not led anyone astray. We have not cheated anyone.
I do not say this to blame you. I have told you before that you are so dear to our hearts that we would die with you or live with you.
I speak to you very openly, and I am very proud of you. I am full of comfort. In all our troubles, my joy is overflowing.
When we came to Macedonia, our bodies had no rest. We met trouble on every side. There were fights all around us, and fears inside us.
But God, who comforts those who are low, comforted us when Titus arrived.

It was not only his coming that comforted us, but also the comfort you had given him. He told us how much you long to see me, how sorry you are, and how much you care for me. So my joy was even greater.
Even if my letter made you sad, I am not sorry I sent it. At first I was sorry, because I see that the letter made you sad, but only for a short time.
Now I am happy. I am not happy that you were made sad, but that your sadness made you turn back to God. You were sad in the way God wants, so we did not harm you in any way.
Sadness of the kind God wants makes people turn away from sin. This leads to being saved, and there is nothing to be sorry about. But the world's kind of sadness brings death.

See what this sadness of God's kind has done in you! It has made you so eager to put things right. It has made you want to clear yourselves. It has made you angry at the wrong, afraid, longing to see me, caring deeply, and ready to see justice done. In every way you have shown that you are innocent in this matter.
So when I wrote to you, it was not because of the one who did wrong, or the one who was wronged. I wrote so that you could see for yourselves, in front of God, how much you care about us.
That is why we have been comforted. And besides our own comfort, we were even happier to see how happy Titus was. All of you gave his spirit new strength.
I had told him how proud I was of you, and you did not let me down. Everything we said to you was true. In the same way, what we told Titus about being proud of you has also turned out to be true.
His love for you grows even more when he remembers how all of you obeyed. You welcomed him with fear and trembling.
I am glad that I can be completely sure of you.
Now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace God has given to the churches in Macedonia.
They have been tested by many troubles, and they are very poor. But their great joy has overflowed into rich giving.
I can tell you that they gave as much as they were able, and even more than they were able. They did it all by their own choice.
They begged us again and again for the joy of sharing in this gift for God's people.
They did more than we expected. First they gave themselves to the Lord, and then to us, as God wanted.
So we asked Titus to finish this kind work of giving among you, since he was the one who started it.
You do well in everything: in faith, in speaking, in knowledge, in eagerness to help, and in your love for us. So make sure you also do well in this kind work of giving.
I am not ordering you to do this. I want to test how real your love is, by comparing it with how eager others are.
You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. He was rich, but for your sake he became poor, so that by his being poor you could become rich.
This is my advice about what is best for you. Last year you were the first not only to give, but also to want to give.
So now finish the work. Be as eager to finish it as you were to start it, and give from what you have.
If you are willing to give, God accepts your gift by what you have, not by what you do not have.
We do not want others to have an easy time while you have a hard time. We want things to be equal.
Right now you have plenty, and that can help those who are in need. Then, when they have plenty, they can help you when you are in need. In this way things will be equal.
As it is written, "The one who gathered a lot did not have too much, and the one who gathered a little did not have too little."
I thank God that he has put in the heart of Titus the same care for you that I have.
Titus welcomed our request, but he was so eager that he is coming to you by his own choice.
We are sending with him the brother whom all the churches praise for his work in preaching the good news.
And the churches also chose him to travel with us as we carry this gift. We do this to honour the Lord himself and to show how eager we are to help.
We want to be careful so that no one can find fault with how we handle this large gift.
We are trying to do what is right, not only in the Lord's eyes, but also in the eyes of people.
We are also sending with them our brother who has often shown us in many ways that he is eager to help. Now he is even more eager, because he trusts you so much.
As for Titus, he is my partner, and he works with me to help you. As for the brothers, they are sent by the churches, and they bring honour to Christ.
So show these men your love, and show them why we are proud of you, so that the churches can see it.
I do not really need to write to you about this gift for God's people.

I know how eager you are to help. I have been telling the people in Macedonia how proud I am of you. I told them that you in Achaia have been ready to give since last year. Your eagerness has stirred most of them to act.
But I am sending the brothers so that our pride in you will not turn out to be empty. I want you to be ready, as I said you would be.
If some people from Macedonia come with me and find that you are not ready, we would be ashamed of being so sure of you, not to mention how ashamed you would be.
So I thought I should ask the brothers to visit you before I come. They will make sure the gift you promised is ready ahead of time. Then it will be a gift given freely, not one forced out of you.
Remember this: whoever plants only a few seeds will harvest only a little. Whoever plants many seeds will harvest a lot.
Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give. Do not give unwillingly or because you feel forced. God loves a person who gives gladly.
And God is able to give you more than enough of every blessing. Then you will always have everything you need, and plenty left over for every good work.
As it is written, "He gives freely to the poor. His goodness lasts for ever."
God gives seed to the farmer and bread to eat. He will also give you plenty of seed and make it grow, so that your good deeds will bring a large harvest.
He will make you rich in every way, so that you can always give freely. And when we take your gifts to those in need, they will thank God.
This work of giving does more than meet the needs of God's people. It also overflows in many thanks to God.

Your giving proves what you are. People will praise God because you obey the good news of Christ that you say you believe. They will praise him because you share so freely with them and with everyone.
And they will pray for you with deep love, because of the great grace God has given you.
Thanks be to God for his gift, which is too wonderful for words!
I, Paul, beg you by the gentleness and kindness of Christ. Some say that I am shy when I am with you, but bold towards you when I am away.
I beg you, do not make me be bold when I come. I expect I will have to be bold with some people who think we live in a worldly way.
We do live in the world, but we do not fight our battles the way the world does.
The weapons we fight with are not the world's weapons. They have God's power to pull down strong places.
We pull down every argument and every proud idea that stands against knowing God. We take every thought captive and make it obey Christ.
And once you have fully obeyed, we will be ready to punish every act of not obeying.
You are looking only at what is in front of your eyes. If anyone is sure that he belongs to Christ, he should think again. We belong to Christ just as much as he does.
Even if I boast a little too much about the authority the Lord gave us, I am not ashamed. He gave it to us to build you up, not to tear you down.
I do not want it to seem that I am trying to frighten you with my letters.
Some people say, "His letters are strong and powerful, but in person he is weak, and his speaking is nothing special."
Such people should know this: what we say in our letters when we are away, we will do when we are there.

We do not dare to put ourselves in the same group as some who praise themselves, or to compare ourselves with them. They measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves. That shows they do not understand.
But we will not boast beyond the limits. We will keep within the area of work God gave us, and that area reaches all the way to you.
We are not going too far by boasting about you, as if we had not reached you. We were the first to come all the way to you with the good news of Christ.
We do not boast about work done by others, beyond our limits. We hope that as your faith grows, our area of work among you will grow much bigger.
Then we can preach the good news in places beyond you. We do not want to boast about work already done in someone else's area.
But, "Whoever boasts should boast about the Lord."
It is not the one who praises himself who is approved. It is the one whom the Lord praises.
I hope you will put up with me while I act a little foolish. Please put up with me!
I am jealous for you with a jealousy that comes from God. I promised you to one husband, to Christ. I want to give you to him like a pure young bride.
But I am afraid that your minds may be led away from your simple and pure love for Christ, just as Eve was tricked by the snake's cunning.

If someone comes and preaches a different Jesus from the one we preached, you put up with it easily enough. You do the same if you receive a different spirit from the one you received, or a different good news from the one you accepted.
I do not think I am in any way less than those "super apostles."
I may not be a trained speaker, but I do have knowledge. We have made this very clear to you in every way.
Was it wrong for me to make myself low so that you could be lifted up? I preached God's good news to you without asking for any pay.
I took money from other churches, as if I were robbing them, so that I could serve you.

When I was with you and needed something, I did not make myself a load for anyone. The brothers who came from Macedonia gave me what I needed. I have kept myself from being a load to you in any way, and I will keep on doing so.
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, no one in all of Achaia will stop me from boasting about this.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
And I will keep on doing what I am doing. Then those people who want a chance to boast that they work just like us will have no chance to do it.
Such men are false apostles. They are workers who lie, pretending to be apostles of Christ.
That is not surprising, because even Satan pretends to be an angel of light.
So it is not surprising if his servants pretend to be servants of what is right. In the end they will get what their actions deserve.
I say again, no one should think I am a fool. But if you do, then accept me as a fool, so that I can boast a little too.
When I boast like this, I am not talking as the Lord would. I am talking like a fool.
Many people boast in a worldly way, so I will boast too.
You think you are so wise, yet you gladly put up with fools!
You even put up with anyone who makes you slaves, or takes everything you have, or takes advantage of you, or acts proud, or slaps you in the face.
I am ashamed to say that we were too weak to do that! But if anyone else dares to boast about something, I am talking like a fool now, I dare to boast about it too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they from Israel? So am I. Are they from Abraham's family? So am I.

Are they servants of Christ? I am out of my mind to talk like this, but I am more of one. I have worked much harder. I have been in prison more often. I have been whipped more times than I can count, and I have faced death again and again.
Five times the Jews gave me thirty-nine lashes.
Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was in a shipwreck. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

I have been on many long journeys. I have been in danger from rivers and from robbers. I have been in danger from my own people and from people who are not Jews. I have been in danger in the city, in the desert and at sea, and in danger from false believers.
I have worked hard and long. Often I have gone without sleep. I have been hungry and thirsty, and often gone without food. I have been cold and without enough clothes.
And besides everything else, every day I carry the worry of caring for all the churches.
If anyone is weak, I feel weak too. If anyone is led into sin, I burn inside.
If I must boast, I will boast about the things that show how weak I am.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is to be praised for ever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas had guards watching the city so that he could arrest me.
But I was let down in a basket through a window in the city wall, and I got away from him.
I must keep on boasting. It does not help, but I will go on to tell about visions and things the Lord has shown me.
I know a man who belongs to Christ. Fourteen years ago he was taken up to the third heaven. I do not know if he was in his body or out of it. Only God knows.
And I know that this man was taken up, whether in his body or out of it I do not know. God knows.
He was taken up to Paradise. There he heard things too wonderful to tell, things no person is allowed to speak.
I will boast about a man like that, but I will not boast about myself, except about my weaknesses.
Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be telling the truth. But I hold back, so that no one will think more of me than what they see me do or hear me say.
God showed me many great things. So to keep me from becoming proud, I was given a thorn in my body. It is a messenger from Satan that hurts me and keeps me from becoming proud.
Three times I begged the Lord to take it away from me.
But he said to me, "My grace is all you need. My power is strongest when you are weak." So I will gladly boast all the more about my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ can rest on me.
That is why, for Christ's sake, I am glad in weaknesses, insults, hard times, attacks and troubles. When I am weak, then I am strong.
I have made a fool of myself, but you made me do it. You should have been praising me. Even though I am nothing, I am not in any way less than those "super apostles."
When I was with you, I patiently did the things that show a true apostle: signs, wonders and mighty works.
How were you treated worse than the other churches? Only in that I never made myself a load for you. Forgive me for this wrong!

Now I am ready to visit you for the third time, and I will not be a load for you. I do not want what you own. I want you. Children should not have to save up for their parents. Parents should save up for their children.
I will very gladly spend everything I have for you, and even spend myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?
Well then, I was not a load for you. But some say I was cunning and caught you with a trick.
Did I cheat you through any of the men I sent to you?
I asked Titus to visit you, and I sent the brother with him. Titus did not cheat you, did he? Did we not act in the same spirit and walk in the same way?
Have you been thinking all this time that we are defending ourselves to you? No, we speak in front of God, as people who belong to Christ. Dear friends, everything we do is to build you up.

I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I want you to be, and you may not find me as you want me to be. I am afraid I may find fighting, jealousy, angry tempers, people taking sides, slander, gossip, pride and disorder.

I am afraid that when I come again, my God will make me feel small in front of you. I may have to cry over many who have sinned before and have not turned away from their dirty ways, their sexual sins and their wild living.
This will be my third visit to you. The Scriptures say, "Every matter must be proved by two or three witnesses."
I already warned you when I was with you the second time. Now I warn you again while I am away. When I come back, I will not spare those who sinned before, or any of the others.
You want proof that Christ speaks through me. He is not weak in dealing with you. He is powerful among you.
It is true that he was weak when he was nailed to the cross, but now he lives by God's power. We too are weak in him, but by God's power we will live with him to deal with you.
Look closely at yourselves to see if you are living in the faith. Test yourselves. Do you not know that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless, of course, you fail the test.
And I hope you will see that we have not failed the test.

We pray to God that you will not do anything wrong. We do not pray this so that people will see we have passed the test. We pray it so that you will do what is right, even if it looks as though we have failed.
We cannot do anything against the truth. We can only work for the truth.
We are glad when we are weak and you are strong. And we pray that you will become complete.
That is why I write these things while I am away. Then when I come, I will not have to be hard on you when I use my authority. The Lord gave me this authority to build you up, not to tear you down.
Finally, brothers and sisters, be full of joy. Work to be complete. Take comfort. Agree with each other. Live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet each other with a holy kiss.
All God's holy people here send you their greetings.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the friendship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you. Amen.
Gal: From Paul, an apostle. I was not sent by people, or through any person. I was sent by Jesus Christ, and by God the Father, who raised him from the dead.
All the brothers and sisters with me join me. I write to the churches in Galatia.
Grace and peace to you from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
He gave himself for our sins, to rescue us from this present evil age. This was the will of our God and Father.
To him be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I am amazed that you are so quickly turning away from God, who called you by the grace of Christ. You are turning to a different "good news".
But there is no other good news. Some people are troubling you. They want to twist the Good News of Christ.
But if we, or even an angel from heaven, preach to you a good news different from the one we preached, let him be cursed.
We said it before, and now I say it again. If anyone preaches to you a good news different from the one you received, let him be cursed.
Am I now trying to win the approval of people, or of God? Am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that the Good News I preached did not come from people.
I did not receive it from any person, and no one taught it to me. Jesus Christ showed it to me.
You have heard how I used to live in the Jewish religion. I attacked God's church terribly and tried to destroy it.
I was going further in the Jewish religion than many people of my own age. I was very keen on the traditions of my ancestors.
But God chose me before I was born, and called me by his grace. When it pleased him,
he showed his Son to me, so that I would preach him among the Gentiles. I did not rush to ask any person for advice.
I did not go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went away into Arabia, and later I returned to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter. I stayed with him for fifteen days.
I saw none of the other apostles, except James, the Lord's brother.
I tell you before God that what I write to you is not a lie.
Then I went to the areas of Syria and Cilicia.
The churches of Christ in Judea did not know me by face.
They only heard people say, "The man who once attacked us now preaches the faith he once tried to destroy."
And they praised God because of me.
Then fourteen years later I went up to Jerusalem again with Barnabas. I took Titus with me too.
I went because God showed me I should. I explained to them the Good News I preach among the Gentiles. I did this in private with the leaders, so that my work would not be wasted, now or before.
Titus was with me. He was a Greek, but even he was not forced to be circumcised.
This matter came up because of some false believers. They had sneaked in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus. They wanted to make us slaves again.
We did not give in to them, not even for a moment. We wanted the truth of the Good News to stay with you.
Those who seemed to be important added nothing to my message. What they once were makes no difference to me. God does not judge by how people look.
Instead, they saw that God had trusted me with the Good News for the Gentiles, just as he had trusted Peter with it for the Jews.
God was at work in Peter as an apostle to the Jews. He was also at work in me as an apostle to the Gentiles.

James, Peter and John were seen as pillars of the church. They saw the grace God had given me. So they shook hands with Barnabas and me as partners. They agreed that we should go to the Gentiles, and they would go to the Jews.
They only asked us to keep remembering the poor. That was the very thing I was keen to do.
But when Peter came to Antioch, I stood up to him face to face, because he was clearly wrong.
Before some men came from James, Peter used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and kept apart. He was afraid of those who wanted Gentiles to be circumcised.
The other Jewish believers joined him in this pretending. Even Barnabas was led astray by it.

I saw that they were not living by the truth of the Good News. So I said to Peter in front of them all, "You are a Jew, yet you live like a Gentile and not like a Jew. So how can you force Gentiles to live like Jews?
"We were born Jews, and not Gentile sinners.

Yet we know that a person is not made right with God by keeping the law. It is through faith in Jesus Christ. So we too put our faith in Christ Jesus, to be made right with God by faith in Christ, and not by keeping the law. No one will be made right with God by keeping the law.
We look to Christ to make us right with God. But what if we are then found to be sinners? Does that mean Christ helps us to sin? Certainly not!
If I build again what I tore down, I show that I am a law-breaker.
Through the law I died to the law, so that I can live for God.
I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in this body, I live by faith in the Son of God. He loved me and gave himself for me.
I do not set aside the grace of God. If we could be made right with God through the law, then Christ died for nothing!"
Foolish Galatians! Who has put a spell on you? Jesus Christ was clearly shown to you as crucified.
I just want to ask you one thing. Did you receive the Spirit by keeping the law, or by hearing and believing?
Are you so foolish? You began with the Spirit. Are you now trying to finish by your own human effort?
Did you suffer so much for nothing? Surely it was not for nothing!
God gives you his Spirit and does miracles among you. Does he do it because you keep the law, or because you hear and believe?
It is just like Abraham. "He believed God, and God counted it to him as being right with him."
So you can see that those who have faith are the children of Abraham.
The Scriptures saw ahead that God would make the Gentiles right with him by faith. So they told the Good News to Abraham beforehand: "All nations will be blessed through you."
So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
All who depend on keeping the law are under a curse. It is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not keep on doing everything written in the book of the law."
It is clear that no one is made right with God by the law, because "The righteous will live by faith."
The law is not based on faith. Instead, it says, "The person who does these things will live by them."
Christ set us free from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. It is written, "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree."
He did this so that the blessing given to Abraham would come to the Gentiles through Christ Jesus. Then by faith we could receive the Spirit God promised.
Brothers and sisters, let me give an example from everyday life. When a person's agreement has been made firm, no one can cancel it or add to it.
God made his promises to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say "to offsprings", meaning many people. It says "to your offspring", meaning one person, who is Christ.
This is what I mean. God first made a firm agreement. The law came four hundred and thirty years later. It cannot cancel the agreement and so do away with the promise.
If the inheritance comes from the law, then it no longer comes from the promise. But God gave it freely to Abraham through a promise.
Then why was the law given? It was added because of wrongdoing, until the offspring came to whom the promise was made. It was put in place through angels, by a go-between.
A go-between is needed when there is more than one side. But God is one.
So is the law against God's promises? Certainly not! If a law had been given that could give life, then we could be made right with God by the law.
But the Scriptures show that the whole world is held prisoner by sin. So the promise is given through faith in Jesus Christ to those who believe.
Before this faith came, we were held under the law like prisoners. We were locked up until the faith that was coming would be shown.
So the law was our guardian to lead us to Christ, so that we could be made right with God by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
You are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
All of you who were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
There is no Jew or Greek, no slave or free person, no male or female. You are all one in Christ Jesus.
If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring. You will receive what God promised.
Think about it this way. While an heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, even though he owns everything.
He is under guardians and managers until the time his father has set.
It was the same for us. When we were children, we were slaves to the basic powers of this world.
But when the right time came, God sent his Son. He was born of a woman and born under the law.
He came to set free those under the law, so that we could be adopted as God's children.
Because you are his children, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts. The Spirit calls out, "Abba, Father!"
So you are no longer a slave, but a child. And if you are his child, God has also made you an heir through Christ.
In the past you did not know God. You were slaves to things that are not really gods.
But now you know God, or rather, God knows you. So why do you turn back to those weak and worthless basic powers? Do you want to be their slaves all over again?
You keep special days, months, seasons and years!
I am afraid for you. Maybe all my hard work for you was wasted.
Brothers and sisters, I beg you, become like me, for I became like you. You did me no wrong.
You know that I first preached the Good News to you because I was ill.
My illness was a trial to you, but you did not look down on me or turn me away. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, or even Christ Jesus himself.
What happened to your joy? I can tell you, if you could have, you would have torn out your own eyes and given them to me.
So have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
Those people are very keen to win you over, but not for good. They want to cut you off from us, so that you will be keen on them.
It is always good to be keen for a good purpose, and not only when I am with you.
My dear children, I am again in pain for you, like a woman giving birth, until Christ is formed in you.
I wish I could be with you now and speak in a different way, because I am very worried about you.
Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not listen to what the law says?
It is written that Abraham had two sons. One was by the slave woman, and the other by the free woman.
The son of the slave woman was born in the normal human way. But the son of the free woman was born because of God's promise.
These things are a picture. The two women stand for two agreements. One agreement is from Mount Sinai, and its children are born to be slaves. This is Hagar.
Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia. She is like the Jerusalem of today, because she and her children are slaves.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
It is written, "Be glad, woman who could not have children. Shout for joy, you who never felt the pain of giving birth. The lonely woman will have more children than the woman who has a husband."
Now you, brothers and sisters, are children of the promise, just like Isaac.
At that time, the son born in the normal human way attacked the son born by the power of the Spirit. It is the same now.
But what do the Scriptures say? "Send away the slave woman and her son. The slave woman's son will never share the inheritance with the free woman's son."
So, brothers and sisters, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
Christ has set us free so that we can live in freedom. So stand firm, and do not let yourselves be tied up again under the load of slavery.
Listen! I, Paul, tell you this. If you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no use to you at all.
I say it again to every man who lets himself be circumcised. He must then keep the whole law.
You who are trying to be made right with God by the law have cut yourselves off from Christ. You have fallen away from grace.
But through the Spirit, and by faith, we wait eagerly for the hope of being right with God.
In Christ Jesus, being circumcised or not being circumcised means nothing. What matters is faith working through love.
You were running a good race. Who stopped you from obeying the truth?
That kind of persuasion does not come from God, who calls you.
A little yeast spreads through the whole batch of dough.
In the Lord, I am sure you will not think any other way. The person who is troubling you will be judged, whoever he is.
Brothers and sisters, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still being attacked? If that were so, the cross would no longer offend anyone.
I wish those who are upsetting you would go all the way and cut themselves off!
You, my brothers and sisters, were called to be free. But do not use your freedom as an excuse to do what your sinful nature wants. Instead, serve one another in love.
The whole law is summed up in one command: "Love your neighbour as yourself."
But if you keep biting and tearing at each other, watch out, or you will destroy each other.
So I say, live by the Spirit, and you will not do what your sinful nature wants.
The sinful nature wants what is against the Spirit. The Spirit wants what is against the sinful nature. They fight each other, so you do not do what you want to do.
But if the Spirit leads you, you are not under the law.
The things the sinful nature does are clear. They are adultery, sexual sin, impure living, and wild desires,
worshipping idols, witchcraft, hatred, fighting, jealousy, fits of anger, selfish ambition, splits, groups that take sides,
envy, murders, getting drunk, wild parties, and things like these. I warn you, as I did before, that people who live like this will not inherit God's Kingdom.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness and self-control. There is no law against such things.
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the sinful nature, with its passions and desires.
Since we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
Let us not be proud, or annoy one another, or be jealous of one another.
Brothers and sisters, if someone is caught in a sin, you who live by the Spirit should gently help that person back. But watch yourselves, or you may also be tempted.
Carry each other's heavy loads. In this way you will obey the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks he is important when he is not, he is fooling himself.
Each person should test his own actions. Then he can be proud of himself, without comparing himself with someone else.
Each person must carry his own load.
Those who are taught God's word should share all good things with their teacher.
Do not be fooled. No one can make a fool of God. A person reaps whatever he sows.
Whoever sows to please his sinful nature will reap ruin from it. But whoever sows to please the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Let us not get tired of doing good. If we do not give up, we will reap a harvest at the right time.
So whenever we have the chance, let us do good to everyone, and most of all to the family of believers.
See what large letters I use as I write to you with my own hand!
Those who want to look good to others are trying to force you to be circumcised. They only do it so that they will not be attacked for the cross of Christ.
Even those who are circumcised do not keep the law themselves. They want you to be circumcised so that they can boast about it.
But I will never boast about anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through the cross, the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
Being circumcised or not means nothing. What matters is being made a new creation.
Peace and mercy to all who follow this rule, and to God's Israel.
From now on, let no one cause me trouble. I carry on my body the scars that show I belong to Jesus.
Brothers and sisters, may the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
Eph: From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will. I write to God's holy people in Ephesus, who are faithful in Christ Jesus.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. He has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.
Even before he made the world, God chose us in Christ to be holy and without fault in his sight. In love
he decided long ago to adopt us as his children through Jesus Christ. This was what he wanted, and it gave him pleasure.
So we praise God for his glorious grace, which he freely gave us in the Son he loves.
In Christ we are set free through his blood, and our sins are forgiven. This shows how rich God's grace is.
He poured out his grace on us, with all wisdom and understanding.
He let us know the secret of his plan. It was his good purpose, which he planned in Christ.
When the right time comes, he will bring everything together under Christ, everything in heaven and on earth.
In Christ we were also chosen to receive an inheritance. God planned this long ago. He makes everything work out the way he decides.
He did this so that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, would bring praise to his glory.
You too heard the message of truth, the Good News that saves you. When you believed in Christ, God marked you with his seal, the Holy Spirit he promised.
The Spirit is the guarantee of what we will receive, until God sets free those who belong to him. This brings praise to his glory.
That is why I keep thinking of you. I have heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all God's people.
I never stop thanking God for you, and I remember you in my prayers.
I keep asking the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, to give you the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, so that you know him better.
I pray that the eyes of your heart may be opened. Then you will know the hope he has called you to. You will know how rich and glorious his inheritance is among his holy people.
And you will know his great power, which is far beyond anything, for us who believe. It is the same mighty strength
that he used when he raised Christ from the dead. God seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places.
Christ is far above every ruler, authority, power and lord, and above every name that can be named, not only in this age but also in the age to come.
God put everything under his feet. He made him head over everything for the church.
The church is his body. It is filled by Christ, who fills everything in every way.
Once you were dead because of your wrongdoing and sins.
You used to live in them, following the ways of this world. You obeyed the ruler of the powers of the air. He is the spirit now at work in those who disobey God.
All of us once lived like them. We followed the desires of our sinful nature and our thoughts. Like everyone else, we deserved God's anger.
But God is rich in mercy, and he loves us with a great love.
Even when we were dead in our sins, he made us alive with Christ. It is by grace you have been saved.
God raised us up with Christ and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
He did this so that in the ages to come he could show how great his grace is. He shows it through his kindness to us in Christ Jesus.
It is by grace you have been saved, through faith. It does not come from you. It is God's gift.
It does not come from what you do, so no one can boast.
We are God's handiwork. He created us in Christ Jesus to do good works, which he prepared long ago for us to do.
So remember what you were before. You were born Gentiles. The Jews, who are circumcised in the body by human hands, called you "the uncircumcised".
At that time you were without Christ. You were not part of the people of Israel. You were outsiders to the agreements of God's promise. You had no hope, and you were without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus, you who were once far away have been brought near through the blood of Christ.
Christ himself is our peace. He made the two groups one. He broke down the wall of hatred that divided us.
In his own body he set aside the law with its commands and rules. He did this to make one new people out of the two, and so make peace.
Through the cross he brought both of them back to God in one body. On the cross he put an end to the hatred.
He came and preached peace to you who were far away, and peace to those who were near.
Through him we both can come to the Father by one Spirit.
So you are no longer strangers and outsiders. You are citizens together with God's people, and members of God's family.
You are built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets. Christ Jesus himself is the main cornerstone.
In him the whole building is joined together. It grows into a holy temple in the Lord.
In him you too are being built together into a home where God lives by his Spirit.
For this reason I, Paul, am a prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles.
Surely you have heard that God gave me his grace to share with you.
God showed me his secret plan, as I have already written in a few words.
When you read this, you will understand what I know about the secret plan of Christ.
It was not made known to people in earlier times. But now the Spirit has shown it to God's holy apostles and prophets.
This is the secret. Through the Good News, the Gentiles share the inheritance with Israel. They are members of the same body. They share in the promise in Christ Jesus.
I became a servant of this Good News by the gift of God's grace, given to me through his mighty power.
I am less than the least of all God's people. Yet God gave me this grace, to preach to the Gentiles the endless riches of Christ.
He gave me the task of helping everyone see how God's secret plan works. It was hidden for ages in God, who created all things.
God wanted the church to show his wisdom in all its many forms to the rulers and powers in the heavenly places.
This was his eternal purpose, which he carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord.
In Christ, and through faith in him, we can come to God boldly and with confidence.
So I ask you not to lose heart because I am suffering for you. My suffering is for your glory.
For this reason I kneel before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
from whom every family in heaven and on earth gets its name.
I pray that from his glorious riches he will make you strong in your inner being, with power through his Spirit.
I pray that Christ will live in your hearts through faith. I pray that you will be rooted and built up in love.
Then together with all God's holy people you will have power to understand how wide and long and high and deep it is,
the love of Christ. It is greater than anyone can know. And you will be filled with all the fullness of God.
God can do far more than all we ask or imagine, by his power that is at work in us.
To him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus, through all generations, for ever and ever. Amen.
So I, a prisoner for the Lord, beg you to live a life worthy of the calling you have received.
Be humble and gentle in every way. Be patient, and put up with one another in love.
Try hard to keep the unity of the Spirit, joined together by peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope.
There is one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
and one God and Father of all. He is over all, through all, and in all.
But each one of us has been given grace, as Christ chose to give it.
That is why the Scripture says, "When he went up on high, he led captives with him, and gave gifts to people."
What does "he went up" mean? It means he also first came down to the lower parts of the earth.
The one who came down is the same one who went up far above all the heavens, so that he could fill everything.
He gave some people to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be preachers of the Good News, and some to be pastors and teachers.
Their task is to prepare God's people for works of service, so that the body of Christ is built up.
This goes on until we all come to unity in the faith and in knowing the Son of God. Then we will be mature, and reach the full measure of Christ.
Then we will no longer be like children, thrown back and forth by every wind of teaching. We will not be fooled by people's tricks and clever lies.
Instead, we will speak the truth in love. We will grow up in every way into Christ, who is the head.
From him the whole body is joined and held together by every part. As each part does its work, the body grows and builds itself up in love.
So I tell you this, and I insist on it in the Lord. You must no longer live like the Gentiles, whose thinking is empty.
Their understanding is darkened. They are cut off from the life of God, because they do not know him and their hearts are hard.
They have lost all feeling. They have given themselves over to wild living. They are greedy to do every kind of impure thing.
But that is not the way you learnt about Christ.
You heard about him and were taught in him, and the truth is in Jesus.
You were taught to put off your old self and your old way of life. The old self is ruined by its lying desires.
You were taught to be made new in the attitude of your minds,
and to put on the new self. It is created to be like God, truly right and holy.
So stop telling lies. Each of you must speak the truth to your neighbour, because we all belong to one body.
"When you are angry, do not sin." Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry,
and do not give the devil a chance.
Anyone who has been stealing must stop. Instead, he must work, doing something useful with his own hands. Then he will have something to share with those in need.
Do not let any bad talk come out of your mouths. Only say what helps build others up, as they need it. Then your words will do good to those who hear.
Do not make the Holy Spirit of God sad. He is the seal that marks you for the day you will be set free.
Get rid of all bitterness, rage, anger, shouting and evil talk, along with every kind of spite.
Be kind to one another and tender-hearted. Forgive each other, just as God forgave you in Christ.
So copy God, as children he loves.
Live a life of love, just as Christ loved us. He gave himself up for us as an offering and sacrifice to God, like a sweet smell.
There must not even be a hint of sexual sin among you, or any kind of impure living, or greed. These are not right for God's holy people.
There must be no dirty talk, foolish talk, or crude jokes. They are out of place. Instead, give thanks to God.
You can be sure of this. No one who lives in sexual sin, or is impure, or greedy, will have any share in the Kingdom of Christ and of God. A greedy person is really worshipping an idol.
Do not let anyone fool you with empty words. Because of such things, God's anger comes on those who disobey him.
So do not join in with them.
Once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light.
The fruit of the light is found in all that is good, right and true.
Find out what pleases the Lord.
Have nothing to do with the useless deeds of darkness. Instead, show them up for what they are.
It is shameful even to talk about what they do in secret.
But when the light shows things up as wrong, they become clear, because whatever makes things clear is light.
and everything made clear becomes light. That is why it is said, "Wake up, sleeper, rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you."
So be very careful how you live. Do not live like foolish people, but like wise people.
Make the most of every chance, because the days are evil.
So do not be foolish. Understand what the Lord wants.
Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to wild living. Instead, be filled with the Spirit.
Speak to one another with psalms, hymns and songs from the Spirit. Sing and make music to the Lord from your heart.
Always give thanks to God the Father for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Put others first, out of respect for Christ.
Wives, put your husbands first, as you do the Lord.
The husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the church. Christ is the Saviour of the church, which is his body.
As the church follows Christ, so wives should follow their husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.
He did this to make her holy, cleansing her by the washing with water through the word.
He wanted to bring the church to himself in all its beauty, with no stain or wrinkle or any other fault, but holy and without blame.
In the same way, husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. A man who loves his wife loves himself.
No one ever hated his own body. Instead, he feeds it and cares for it, just as Christ does for the church.
We are parts of his body, of his flesh and of his bones.
"That is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one body."
This is a deep secret, but I am talking about Christ and the church.
Still, each one of you must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must respect her husband.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, because this is right.
"Honour your father and mother." This is the first command with a promise:
"so that it may go well with you, and you may live a long life on the earth."
Fathers, do not make your children angry. Instead, bring them up with the training and teaching of the Lord.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters with respect and fear, and with an honest heart, just as you would obey Christ.
Do not obey them only when they are watching, to win their favour. Obey them as slaves of Christ, doing what God wants from your heart.
Serve them gladly, as if you were serving the Lord, not people.
You know that the Lord will reward each person for whatever good he does, whether he is a slave or free.
Masters, treat your slaves in the same way. Do not threaten them. You know that both they and you have the same Master in heaven, and he treats everyone the same.
Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power.
Put on the full armour of God, so that you can stand against the devil's tricks.
Our fight is not against human beings. It is against the rulers, the authorities, the powers of this dark world, and the evil spiritual forces in the heavenly places.
So put on the full armour of God. Then when the day of evil comes, you will be able to stand your ground. And after you have done everything, you will still be standing.
So stand firm. Wear the belt of truth around your waist, and the breastplate of being right with God.
For shoes, put on the readiness that comes from the Good News of peace.
Above all, take up the shield of faith. With it you can put out all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
Take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
Pray in the Spirit at all times, with all kinds of prayers and requests. Stay alert, and keep on praying for all God's people.
Pray for me too. Pray that God will give me the right words when I speak, so that I can boldly make known the secret of the Good News.
I am an ambassador for it, in chains. Pray that I will speak about it boldly, as I should.
Tychicus, our dear brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you all my news, so that you know how I am.
I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you know how we are, and so that he can encourage you.
Peace to the brothers and sisters, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace to all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with a love that never dies. Amen.
Phil: From Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus. We write to all God's holy people in Christ Jesus at Philippi, and to the church leaders and helpers.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God every time I remember you.
Whenever I pray for all of you, I always pray with joy,
because you have shared with me in spreading the Good News, from the first day until now.
I am sure of this. God began a good work in you, and he will carry it on until it is finished on the day of Christ Jesus.
It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, because you are in my heart. Whether I am in chains or defending the Good News and proving it true, you all share in God's grace with me.
God knows how much I long for all of you, with the tender love of Christ Jesus.
This is my prayer. I pray that your love will grow more and more, with knowledge and good judgement.
Then you will be able to choose what is best. You will be pure and without blame for the day of Christ.
You will be filled with the good fruit of being right with God, which comes through Jesus Christ. This brings glory and praise to God.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that what has happened to me has actually helped the Good News to spread.
The whole palace guard and everyone else here know that I am in chains for Christ.
And because I am in chains, most of the believers have become more confident in the Lord. They dare to speak God's word more boldly and without fear.
It is true that some preach Christ because they are jealous and want to fight. But others preach him with good hearts.
The first group preach Christ out of selfish ambition, not honestly. They think they can add to my troubles while I am in chains.
The others do it out of love. They know that God has put me here to defend the Good News.
But what does it matter? What matters is that Christ is preached in every way, whether for wrong reasons or true ones. I am glad about that. Yes, and I will keep on being glad,
because I know that this will turn out for my good. It will happen through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
I eagerly hope that I will not be ashamed in any way. I hope to be very bold, so that now as always Christ will be honoured in my body, whether I live or die.
For me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
If I go on living in this body, it will mean fruitful work for me. Yet I do not know which to choose.
I am torn between the two. I long to leave this life and be with Christ, which is far better.
But it is more important for you that I stay in the body.
Since I am sure of this, I know that I will stay. I will stay with all of you, to help you grow and have joy in the faith.
Then when I come to you again, you will have even more reason to boast in Christ Jesus because of me.

Whatever happens, live in a way that is worthy of the Good News of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you, I will know this. You stand firm in one spirit, fighting side by side, with one mind, for the faith of the Good News.
Do not be frightened in any way by those who are against you. This is a sign to them that they will be destroyed, but that you will be saved, and that by God.
God has given you the gift, for Christ's sake, not only of believing in him but also of suffering for him.
You are going through the same struggle you saw me have, and now hear that I still have.
Does being one with Christ encourage you? Does his love comfort you? Do you share in the Spirit? Do you have tender kindness and care?
Then make my joy complete by agreeing with each other. Have the same love. Be united in spirit and in purpose.
Do nothing out of selfish ambition or pride. Instead, be humble, and think of others as better than yourselves.
Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Have the same attitude that Christ Jesus had.
He was God by nature, yet he did not think being equal with God was something to hold on to.
Instead, he gave up everything and took the nature of a servant. He was born as a human being.
And when he appeared as a man, he humbled himself. He obeyed God even to the point of death, yes, death on a cross!
So God raised him to the highest place. He gave him the name that is above every name.
So at the name of Jesus every knee will bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth.
And every tongue will say that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So, my dear friends, you have always obeyed, not only when I was with you. Now that I am away, obey even more. Keep working out your salvation with respect and trembling.
It is God who works in you, to make you want and do what pleases him.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing.
Then you will be pure and without blame, children of God without fault, in a crooked and twisted world. You will shine among them like stars in the sky,
as you hold firmly to the word of life. Then I can be proud on the day of Christ that I did not run my race or work hard for nothing.
Your faith is like an offering to God. Even if my life is poured out like a drink offering on it, I am glad. I share my joy with all of you.
In the same way, you too should be glad and share your joy with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon. Then I too will be cheered when I hear news about you.
I have no one else like him, who truly cares about how you are.
All the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know that Timothy has proved himself. He has worked with me for the Good News, like a son with his father.
So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me.
And I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon too.
But I think I must send Epaphroditus back to you. He is my brother, my co-worker and fellow soldier. You sent him to help me in my need.
He longs for all of you, and he is upset because you heard he was ill.
He was indeed ill, and he nearly died. But God had mercy on him, and on me too, so that I would not have sorrow on top of sorrow.
So I am all the more eager to send him. Then when you see him again you will be glad, and I will worry less.
Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honour people like him.
He almost died for the work of Christ. He risked his life to give me the help that you could not give.
Finally, my brothers and sisters, be glad in the Lord! It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again, and it keeps you safe.
Watch out for those dogs, those people who do evil. They insist on cutting the body.
It is we who are truly circumcised. We worship God by his Spirit. We boast in Christ Jesus, and put no trust in human things.
I could have reasons to trust in such things. If anyone else thinks he has reasons, I have more.
I was circumcised on the eighth day. I was born an Israelite, from the tribe of Benjamin, a true Hebrew. As for the law, I was a Pharisee.
As for being keen, I attacked the church. As for being right by keeping the law, no one could find fault with me.
But whatever was a gain to me, I now count as loss for the sake of Christ.
More than that, I count everything as loss compared with how great it is to know Christ Jesus my Lord. For him I have lost everything. I count it all as rubbish, so that I may gain Christ
and be found in him. I do not have my own rightness that comes from the law. I have the rightness that comes through faith in Christ. It comes from God and is received by faith.
I want to know Christ and the power of his rising from the dead. I want to share in his sufferings and become like him in his death.
Then somehow I too will rise from the dead.
I do not mean that I have already reached this, or that I am already perfect. But I keep pressing on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of me.
Brothers and sisters, I do not think I have taken hold of it yet. But I do one thing. I forget what is behind me and reach out for what is ahead.
I press on towards the finish line, to win the prize. God has called me to it in Christ Jesus, to the life above.
All of us who are mature should think this way. If you think differently about something, God will make that clear to you too.
But let us live up to what we have already reached, following the same rule. Let us think the same way.
Brothers and sisters, join together in following my example. Pay attention to those who live as we showed you.
As I have often told you before, and now tell you again with tears, many people live as enemies of the cross of Christ.
Their end is ruin. Their stomach is their god. They are proud of things they should be ashamed of. Their minds are on earthly things.
But we are citizens of heaven. And we eagerly wait for a Saviour from there, the Lord Jesus Christ.
By the power that lets him rule over everything, he will change our weak bodies to be like his glorious body.
So, my brothers and sisters, whom I love and long for, my joy and my crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, dear friends!
I beg Euodia and I beg Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.
Yes, and I ask you too, my true partner, to help these women. They worked hard with me to spread the Good News, along with Clement and my other co-workers. Their names are in the book of life.
Always be glad in the Lord. I will say it again: be glad!
Let everyone see how gentle you are. The Lord is near.
Do not worry about anything. Instead, in every situation, pray and ask God, and thank him, and tell him what you need.
Then God's peace, which is greater than we can understand, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers and sisters, think about whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, and whatever is worth admiring. If anything is excellent or worthy of praise, think about such things.
Keep doing what you have learnt and received from me, and what you heard from me and saw in me. And the God of peace will be with you.
I am very glad in the Lord that at last you have shown your care for me again. You did care, but you had no chance to show it.
I am not saying this because I am in need. I have learnt to be content whatever my situation.

I know what it is to have little, and I know what it is to have plenty. I have learnt the secret of being content in any and every situation, whether well fed or hungry, whether I have plenty or not enough.
I can do all this through Christ, who gives me strength.
Yet it was good of you to share in my troubles.
And you Philippians know this. In the early days of the Good News, when I left Macedonia, not one church shared with me in giving and receiving, except you.
Even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent me help more than once when I was in need.
It is not that I want your gift. I want more fruit to be added to your account.

I have received everything in full, and even more. I am well supplied, now that Epaphroditus has brought me the gifts you sent. They are a sweet-smelling offering, a sacrifice that God accepts and is pleased with.
And my God will meet all your needs from his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
Glory to our God and Father for ever and ever. Amen.
Greet all God's people in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters with me send greetings.
All God's people here send you greetings, especially those in Caesar's household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
Col: From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and from our brother Timothy.
We write to God's holy people in Colossae, the faithful brothers and sisters in Christ. Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you.
We have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love you have for all God's people.
Your faith and love come from the hope that is kept safe for you in heaven. You first heard about this hope in the true message, the Good News
that came to you. All over the world this Good News is bearing fruit and growing. It has been doing the same among you, since the day you heard it and truly understood God's grace.
You learnt it from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant. He is a faithful servant of Christ for your sake.
He also told us about your love in the Spirit.
So since the day we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you. We ask God to fill you with the knowledge of what he wants, with all the wisdom and understanding the Spirit gives.
Then you will live a life worthy of the Lord and please him in every way. You will bear fruit in every good work, and grow in knowing God.
We pray that you will be made strong with all power, by his glorious might. Then you will keep going and be patient with joy.
And you will give thanks to the Father. He has made you fit to share in the inheritance of his holy people in the kingdom of light.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness. He has brought us into the Kingdom of the Son he loves.
In his Son we are set free, and our sins are forgiven.
The Son is the image of the God we cannot see. He is first and above all creation.
Everything was created by him, in heaven and on earth, things we can see and things we cannot see, whether thrones or powers or rulers or authorities. Everything was created through him and for him.
He existed before everything, and in him everything holds together.
He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, and the first to rise from the dead, so that he would be first in everything.
God was pleased to have all his fullness live in him.
Through him God was pleased to bring everything back to himself, things on earth and things in heaven. He made peace through Christ's blood, shed on the cross.
Once you were far from God. You were his enemies in your minds, because of the evil things you did.
But now he has brought you back to himself through Christ's death in his human body. He did this to bring you before him holy, without fault, and free from blame.

But you must keep going in your faith, firm and steady. Do not move away from the hope of the Good News you heard. It has been preached to every creature under heaven, and I, Paul, have become its servant.
Now I am glad to suffer for you. In my own body I am adding to what is still lacking in Christ's sufferings, for the sake of his body, the church.
I became the church's servant by the task God gave me, to tell you the whole message of God.
It is the secret that was hidden for ages and generations. But now God has shown it to his holy people.
God chose to make known to them the glorious riches of this secret among the Gentiles. The secret is this: Christ in you, the hope of glory.
We preach about Christ. We warn and teach everyone with all wisdom, so that we can bring everyone to God, mature in Christ.
To do this I work hard and struggle, with all the energy that Christ so powerfully gives me.
I want you to know how hard I am struggling for you, for those at Laodicea, and for all who have not met me in person.
I want their hearts to be encouraged and joined together in love. I want them to have the full riches of complete understanding. Then they will know God's secret, which is Christ himself.
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in him.
I tell you this so that no one will fool you with clever-sounding talk.
Even though I am away from you in body, I am with you in spirit. I am glad to see how well you are doing and how firm your faith in Christ is.
So then, just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, keep on living in him.
Be rooted and built up in him. Be strong in the faith, as you were taught, and overflow with thanks.
Make sure no one captures you with empty and false ideas. Such ideas come from human tradition and the basic powers of this world, not from Christ.
All the fullness of God lives in Christ in a human body.
And you have been given full life in Christ. He is the head over every power and authority.
In him you were also circumcised, but not by human hands. Your sinful nature was cut away, by the circumcision that Christ gives.
You were buried with him in baptism. And you were raised with him through your faith in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.
You were dead in your sins, and your sinful nature was not yet cut away. But God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our sins.
He cancelled the written record of what we owed, with its rules that were against us. He took it away and nailed it to the cross.
He took away the power of the rulers and authorities. He made a public show of them, and won the victory over them by the cross.
So do not let anyone judge you by what you eat or drink, or about a festival, a New Moon celebration or a Sabbath day.
These are a shadow of the things that were coming. The real thing is found in Christ.

Do not let anyone rob you of your prize. Some people delight in false humility and in worshipping angels. They go into great detail about what they have seen. Their sinful minds puff them up with empty pride.
They have lost touch with the head, Christ. From him the whole body is fed and held together by its joints and muscles. And it grows as God makes it grow.
You died with Christ to the basic powers of this world. So why do you still live as if you belonged to the world? Why do you follow its rules?
"Do not hold! Do not taste! Do not touch!"
These rules are about things that are all used up and gone. They are only human commands and teachings.
Such rules may seem wise, with their self-made worship, false humility and harsh treatment of the body. But they are no use at all in stopping the desires of the sinful nature.
Since you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
You died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you too will appear with him in glory.
So put to death whatever belongs to your earthly nature: sexual sin, impure living, lust, evil desires and greed. Greed is the same as worshipping idols.
Because of these things, God's anger is coming on those who disobey him.
You used to live that way, in the life you once lived.
But now you must get rid of all these things: anger, rage, spite, evil talk, and dirty language from your lips.
Do not lie to each other. You have taken off your old self with its ways,
and you have put on the new self. It is being made new in knowledge, to be like its Creator.
Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, foreigner, wild outsider, slave or free. But Christ is all, and he is in all.
You are God's chosen people, holy and dearly loved. So clothe yourselves with tender care, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.
Put up with each other. If any of you has a complaint against someone, forgive them. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
Above all these, put on love. It binds everything together perfectly.
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts. You were called to peace as members of one body. And be thankful.
Let the message of Christ live in you richly. Teach and warn one another with all wisdom. Sing psalms, hymns and songs from the Spirit, with thanks to God in your hearts.
Whatever you do, in word or action, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus. Give thanks to God the Father through him.
Wives, put your husbands first, as is right in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, and do not be harsh with them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, because this pleases the Lord.
Fathers, do not make your children bitter, or they will lose heart.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything. Do it not only when they are watching, to win their favour. Do it with an honest heart, out of respect for the Lord.
Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as if working for the Lord, not for people.
You know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as a reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
Anyone who does wrong will be paid back for the wrong he has done. God treats everyone the same.
Masters, give your slaves what is right and fair. You know that you also have a Master in heaven.
Keep on praying. Stay alert as you pray, and be thankful.
