Pray for us too, that God will open a door for our message. Then we can preach the secret of Christ, which is why I am in chains.
Pray that I will make it clear, as I should.
Be wise in the way you act towards outsiders. Make the most of every chance.
Let your talk always be full of grace and tasty, as if seasoned with salt. Then you will know how to answer everyone.
Tychicus will tell you all my news. He is a dear brother, a faithful helper and a fellow servant in the Lord.
I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you know how we are, and so that he can encourage your hearts.
He is coming with Onesimus, our faithful and dear brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything that is happening here.
Aristarchus, who is in prison with me, sends greetings. So does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas. You have been told about him: if he comes to you, welcome him.
Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jewish believers among my co-workers for God's Kingdom. They have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends greetings. He is always praying hard for you. He prays that you will stand firm, mature and fully sure of all that God wants.
I can tell you that he is working very hard for you, and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Our dear friend Luke, the doctor, and Demas send greetings.
Give my greetings to the brothers and sisters at Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church that meets in her house.
After this letter has been read to you, make sure it is also read in the church at Laodicea. And you must read the letter from Laodicea too.
Tell Archippus, "Make sure you finish the work the Lord gave you."
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
1Thess: From Paul, Silas and Timothy, to the church of the people of Thessalonica, who belong to God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always thank God for all of you, and we mention you in our prayers.
Before our God and Father we never stop remembering the work your faith does, the hard work your love does, and how your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ keeps you going.
Brothers and sisters loved by God, we know that he has chosen you.
Our Good News came to you not just in words, but also with power, with the Holy Spirit, and with deep certainty. You know how we lived among you for your good.
You followed our example and the Lord's. Even though you suffered a lot, you received the message with the joy the Holy Spirit gives.
So you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.
The Lord's message has spread out from you, not only in Macedonia and Achaia. Your faith in God has become known everywhere, so we do not need to say anything about it.
People everywhere tell how you welcomed us. They tell how you turned away from idols to God, to serve the living and true God,
and to wait for his Son to come from heaven. God raised him from the dead. He is Jesus, who saves us from the anger that is coming.
Brothers and sisters, you know yourselves that our visit to you was not wasted.

Before that, as you know, we had suffered and been treated shamefully in Philippi. But with the help of our God we were brave enough to tell you God's Good News, even though many people were against us.
What we urged you to believe did not come from mistakes, or from impure reasons, and we were not trying to trick you.
Instead, God tested us and trusted us with the Good News, so that is how we speak. We are not trying to please people, but God, who tests our hearts.
As you know, we never used flattering words. We never used a false face to hide greed. God is our witness.
We were not looking for praise from people, not from you or from anyone else. As apostles of Christ we could have demanded things from you.
But we were gentle among you, like a mother caring for her own little children.
We cared so much for you that we were happy to share with you not only God's Good News, but our own lives too, because you had become very dear to us.
Brothers and sisters, you remember how hard we worked and struggled. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you while we preached God's Good News to you.
You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy, right and without blame we were towards you who believe.
You know that we treated each of you as a father treats his own children. We urged you, comforted you and begged you
to live in a way that is worthy of God, who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.

And we also thank God all the time for this: when you received God's message from us, you accepted it not as a human message, but as what it truly is, God's word. And it is at work in you who believe.
Brothers and sisters, you followed the example of God's churches in Judea that belong to Christ Jesus. You suffered the same things from your own people as those churches suffered from the Jews.
Those Jews killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, and they drove us out. They do not please God, and they are against all people.
They try to stop us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they can be saved. In this way they keep adding to their sins. But in the end God's anger has come on them.
Brothers and sisters, we were taken away from you for a short time, in body but not in heart. We wanted so much to see you face to face that we tried all the harder.
We wanted to come to you. I, Paul, tried again and again, but Satan stopped us.
What is our hope, our joy, the crown we will be proud of in front of our Lord Jesus when he comes? Is it not you?
Yes, you are our glory and our joy.
So when we could not bear it any longer, we decided it was good to be left alone in Athens.
We sent Timothy, our brother and God's servant in the Good News of Christ, to make you strong and to encourage you in your faith,
so that no one would be shaken by these troubles. You know yourselves that we are meant to face such things.
In fact, when we were with you, we kept telling you that we were going to suffer troubles. And it happened that way, as you know.
That is why, when I could not bear it any longer, I sent Timothy to find out about your faith. I was afraid that the tempter had tempted you in some way, and that all our hard work had been wasted.

But Timothy has just come back to us from you. He has brought good news about your faith and love. He says you always have good memories of us, and that you long to see us, just as we long to see you.
So, brothers and sisters, in all our distress and trouble, your faith has comforted us about you.
Now we really live, since you are standing firm in the Lord.
How can we thank God enough for you, for all the joy we have in front of our God because of you?
Night and day we pray very hard that we may see you again face to face, and give you what is still missing in your faith.
Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus Christ, make a way for us to come to you.
May the Lord make your love for each other and for everyone grow and overflow, just as our love for you does.
May he make your hearts strong, holy and without blame in front of our God and Father when our Lord Jesus comes with all his holy ones.
Finally, brothers and sisters, we ask you and urge you in the Lord Jesus: we taught you how to live in order to please God. Keep doing this more and more.
You know what instructions we gave you by the authority of the Lord Jesus.
God wants you to be holy. He wants you to keep away from sexual sin.
Each of you should learn to control his own body in a way that is holy and honourable,
not with selfish desire, like the Gentiles who do not know God.
In this matter no one should wrong a brother or sister or take advantage of them. The Lord will punish people for all these things, as we told you and warned you before.
God did not call us to live impure lives, but holy lives.
So anyone who rejects this teaching is not rejecting a human being, but God, who gives you his Holy Spirit.
You do not need anyone to write to you about loving your brothers and sisters, because God himself has taught you to love each other.
And you do love all the brothers and sisters all over Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers and sisters, to do it more and more.
Make it your aim to live a quiet life, to mind your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we told you.
Then outsiders will respect the way you live, and you will not need to depend on anyone.
Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about those who have died, so that you do not grieve like other people who have no hope.
We believe that Jesus died and rose again. So we believe that God will bring with Jesus those who have died believing in him.
Here is what the Lord's own message tells us: we who are still alive when the Lord comes will certainly not go before those who have died.
The Lord himself will come down from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of the archangel and with the sound of God's trumpet. And those who died believing in Christ will rise first.
After that, we who are still alive will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will be with the Lord for ever.
So comfort each other with these words.
Now, brothers and sisters, we do not need to write to you about times and dates.
You know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
While people are saying, "All is peaceful and safe," sudden ruin will come on them, like labour pains on a pregnant woman. And they will not escape.
But you, brothers and sisters, are not in the dark, so that day should not surprise you like a thief.
You all belong to the light and to the day. We do not belong to the night or to the darkness.
So let us not sleep like others do. Let us stay awake and keep a clear head.
People who sleep, sleep at night, and people who get drunk, get drunk at night.
But we belong to the day, so let us keep a clear head. Let us put on faith and love to protect our chests like armour, and the hope of being saved like a helmet.
God did not choose us to suffer his anger, but to be saved through our Lord Jesus Christ.
He died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with him.
So encourage each other and build each other up, just as you are doing.
Brothers and sisters, we ask you to respect those who work hard among you, who lead you in the Lord and warn you.
Respect them very highly and love them because of the work they do. Live in peace with each other.
We urge you, brothers and sisters: warn those who are lazy and disorderly, encourage those who are afraid, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Make sure that no one pays back wrong for wrong. Instead, always try to do what is good for each other and for everyone.
Always be joyful.
Never stop praying.
Give thanks in every situation, because this is what God wants for you in Christ Jesus.
Do not put out the Spirit's fire.
Do not look down on prophecies.
Test everything. Hold on to what is good.
Keep away from every kind of evil.
May God himself, the God of peace, make you completely holy. May your whole spirit, soul and body be kept without blame when our Lord Jesus Christ comes.
The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do it.
Brothers and sisters, pray for us.
Greet all the brothers and sisters with a holy kiss.
I command you by the Lord to read this letter to all the brothers and sisters.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
2Thess: From Paul, Silas and Timothy, to the church of the people of Thessalonica, who belong to God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers and sisters, we must always thank God for you, and it is right to do so. Your faith is growing more and more, and the love every one of you has for each other is overflowing.
So we ourselves boast about you among God's churches. We tell them how you keep going and keep your faith through all the attacks and troubles you are suffering.
All this clearly shows that God judges rightly. Because of it you will be counted worthy of God's kingdom, which you are suffering for.
God is fair. He will pay back trouble to those who trouble you,
and he will give rest to you who are troubled, and to us as well. This will happen when the Lord Jesus comes from heaven in blazing fire with his mighty angels.
He will punish those who do not know God and those who do not obey the Good News of our Lord Jesus.
They will be punished with ruin that lasts for ever. They will be shut out from the Lord's presence and from his glorious power.
This will happen on the day he comes to receive glory among his holy people, and to be praised by all who have believed. And that includes you, because you believed what we told you.

With this in mind, we always pray for you. We pray that our God will make you worthy of the life he called you to. We pray that by his power he will help you do every good thing you want to do, and every work that comes from your faith.
Then the name of our Lord Jesus will be honoured because of you, and you will be honoured because of him. This all comes from the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers and sisters, now we want to talk about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and how we will be gathered together to meet him. We ask you

not to be quickly upset in your minds or alarmed. Some may say that the day of the Lord has already come. They may claim it came from a spirit, or a spoken message, or a letter that seems to be from us.
Do not let anyone trick you in any way. That day will not come until the great turning away from God happens first, and the man of sin is shown for who he is, the one who is doomed to be destroyed.
He will oppose and set himself above everything that is called God or is worshipped. He will even sit in God's temple and claim that he himself is God.
Do you not remember that I told you these things when I was still with you?
And you know what is holding him back now, so that he will be shown only at the right time.
The secret power of lawlessness is already at work. But the one who holds it back will keep doing so until he is taken out of the way.
Then the lawless one will be shown. The Lord Jesus will kill him with the breath of his mouth, and destroy him by the brightness of his coming.
The lawless one will come by Satan's work. He will use all kinds of power and signs and false wonders.
He will use every kind of evil trick on those who are being lost. They are lost because they refused to love the truth that would save them.
Because of this, God sends them a powerful lie to fool them, so that they will believe what is false.
So all who have not believed the truth, but have enjoyed doing wrong, will be judged.
But we must always thank God for you, brothers and sisters loved by the Lord. From the beginning God chose you to be saved, through the Spirit making you holy and through your belief in the truth.
He called you to this through the Good News we preached, so that you would share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm. Hold on to the teachings we passed on to you, whether by what we said or by our letter.
Our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father loved us. By his grace he gave us comfort that lasts for ever and a good hope.
May they comfort your hearts and make you strong in every good thing you do and say.
Finally, brothers and sisters, pray for us. Pray that the Lord's message will spread quickly and be honoured, just as it was with you.
And pray that we will be rescued from wicked and evil people, because not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He will make you strong and protect you from the evil one.
The Lord gives us confidence about you. We are sure that you are doing what we tell you, and that you will keep on doing it.
May the Lord lead your hearts into God's love and into the patient strength that Christ gives.
Brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ we command you: keep away from any believer who lives a lazy and disorderly life, and does not follow the teaching we passed on to you.
You know yourselves that you should follow our example. We were not lazy or disorderly when we were with you.
We did not eat anyone's food without paying for it. Instead, we worked hard and struggled night and day, so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
We did this, not because we do not have the right to your help, but to give you an example to follow.
Even when we were with you, we gave you this rule: "Anyone who is not willing to work should not eat."
We hear that some among you are lazy and disorderly. They do not work at all. Instead, they are busy in other people's business.
We command such people, and urge them in the Lord Jesus Christ, to settle down, work quietly and earn their own food.
And as for you, brothers and sisters, never get tired of doing what is right.
If anyone does not obey what we say in this letter, take note of that person. Do not mix with him, so that he will feel ashamed.
But do not treat him as an enemy. Warn him as you would a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. This is the mark in all my letters. This is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
1Tim: From Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our Saviour and of the Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope.
To Timothy, my true son in the faith. Grace, mercy and peace to you from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
When I was leaving for Macedonia, I urged you to stay in Ephesus. Stay there so that you can order certain people to stop teaching wrong ideas.
Tell them not to give their attention to myths and to endless lists of ancestors. These things cause arguments. They do not help God's plan, which works through faith.
The goal of this order is love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience and a faith that is real.
Some people have missed this goal. They have turned away to talk that is empty.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying, or the things they are so sure about.
We know that the law is good if people use it in the right way.

We also know that the law is not made for people who do right. It is for people who break the law and refuse to obey, for those who do not respect God and for sinners, for those who are unholy and do not care about God. It is for people who kill their fathers or mothers, and for murderers,

for people who commit sexual sin, for men who have sex with men, for people who buy and sell slaves, for liars, for those who lie under oath, and for anything else that goes against true and healthy teaching.
This teaching agrees with the glorious Good News of the blessed God, which he trusted me with.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has given me strength. I thank him because he thought I could be trusted, and he chose me to serve him.
Once I spoke against God, attacked his people, and was cruel and proud. But God showed me mercy, because I did not know what I was doing. I did not believe.
The grace of our Lord was poured out on me in great measure, together with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Here is a saying you can trust, which everyone should accept: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and I am the worst of them.

But that is why God showed me mercy. Christ Jesus wanted to use me, the worst sinner, to show how very patient he is. I am an example for those who would later believe in him and receive life that lasts for ever.
Now to the King who rules for ever, who never dies and cannot be seen, the only God who is wise, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.
My son Timothy, I give you this instruction. It agrees with the prophecies that were spoken about you before. By following them you can fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a clear conscience. Some people have pushed their conscience away, and so their faith has been wrecked like a ship.
Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander. I have handed them over to Satan, so that they will learn not to speak against God.
So first of all, I urge you to pray for everyone. Ask God for what they need, pray for them, speak to God for them, and give thanks for them.
Pray for kings and for all who are in power, so that we can live calm and quiet lives, serving God and living in a way that is respectful.
This is good, and it pleases God our Saviour.
He wants all people to be saved and to know the truth fully.
There is one God. And there is one go-between for God and people, the man Christ Jesus.
He gave himself to pay the price to set all people free. This was the message God gave at the right time.
That is why I was chosen to preach it and to be an apostle. I am telling the truth in Christ, I am not lying. I was chosen to teach the Gentiles about faith and truth.
So I want men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or arguing.
In the same way, I want women to dress modestly and decently, with good sense. They should not make themselves beautiful with fancy braided hair, gold, pearls or expensive clothes.
Instead, they should make themselves beautiful by doing good things. That is right for women who say they worship God.
A woman should learn quietly and fully accept what she is taught.
I do not allow a woman to teach a man or to have authority over him. She should be quiet.
For Adam was made first, and then Eve.
And Adam was not the one who was tricked. It was the woman who was tricked and fell into sin.
But women will be saved through having children, if they keep on in faith, love and holiness, with good sense.
Here is a saying you can trust: if anyone wants to be a church leader, he wants to do a good work.

So a church leader must be someone no one can find fault with. He must have only one wife. He must control himself, think clearly, and behave well. He must welcome guests into his home and be good at teaching.
He must not drink too much or be violent. He must be gentle, not quick to argue, and he must not love money.
He must manage his own family well, and see that his children obey him and respect him fully.
If someone does not know how to manage his own family, how can he take care of God's church?
He must not be a new believer, or he may become proud and fall under the same judgment as the devil.
People outside the church must also speak well of him, so that he will not fall into shame and into the devil's trap.
In the same way, church helpers must be worthy of respect, and must mean what they say. They must not drink too much wine or be greedy for money.
With a clear conscience they must hold on to the deep truths of the faith.
They must first be tested. Then, if no one can find fault with them, let them serve.
In the same way, their wives must be worthy of respect. They must not spread lies about others. They must control themselves and be faithful in everything.
A church helper must have only one wife, and he must manage his children and his family well.
Those who serve well earn a good name for themselves, and great confidence in their faith in Christ Jesus.
I hope to come to you soon, but I am writing these things to you
so that, if I am delayed, you will know how people should behave in God's family. That family is the church of the living God, which holds up the truth like a pillar and a strong base.

No one can deny how great the secret of our faith is: God came as a human being. He was proved right by the Spirit. He was seen by angels. He was preached among the nations. People in the world believed in him. He was taken up to heaven in glory.
The Spirit clearly says that in later times some people will turn away from the faith. They will listen to spirits that lead people astray, and to things taught by demons.
These teachings come through liars who pretend to be good. Their consciences have been burnt dead, as if with a hot iron.
They forbid people to marry. They order them not to eat certain foods. But God made these foods to be eaten with thanks by those who believe and know the truth.
Everything God made is good. Nothing should be refused if it is received with thanks,
because it is made holy by God's word and by prayer.
If you teach these things to the brothers and sisters, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus. You will be fed by the words of the faith and the good teaching you have followed.
Have nothing to do with ungodly myths and old wives' tales. Instead, train yourself to live for God.
Training the body has some value, but living for God has value in every way. It holds a promise for the life we live now and for the life to come.
This is a saying you can trust, which everyone should accept.
That is why we work hard and put up with insults. We have put our hope in the living God, who is the Saviour of all people, and most of all of those who believe.
Command and teach these things.
Do not let anyone look down on you because you are young. Instead, be an example to the believers in what you say, in how you live, in love, in spirit, in faith and in purity.
Until I come, give your attention to reading the Scriptures aloud, to encouraging people, and to teaching.
Do not neglect the gift God gave you. It was given to you through a prophecy, when the church leaders laid their hands on you.
Work hard at these things. Give yourself fully to them, so that everyone can see how you are growing.
Watch your life and your teaching closely. Keep on doing these things. If you do, you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
Do not speak harshly to an older man. Instead, encourage him as you would your father. Treat younger men like brothers,
older women like mothers, and younger women like sisters, with complete purity.
Honour and care for widows who really are alone.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to serve God by caring for their own family, and so pay back their parents. This pleases God.
A widow who is really alone, with no one to help her, puts her hope in God. Night and day she keeps on praying and asking God for help.
But a widow who lives just for pleasure is dead even while she is alive.
Give the people these instructions too, so that no one can find fault with them.
Anyone who does not take care of his relatives, and most of all his own family, has denied the faith. He is worse than someone who does not believe.
To be put on the list of widows, a widow must be at least sixty years old. She must have been faithful to her husband.

She must be well known for her good deeds, such as bringing up children, welcoming strangers into her home, washing the feet of God's people, helping those in trouble, and giving herself to every kind of good work.
But do not put younger widows on the list. When their own desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry again.
Then they are judged for breaking the first promise they made.
Besides, they get into the habit of being lazy and going from house to house. And not only lazy, but they also gossip and get busy in other people's business, saying things they should not say.
So I want the younger widows to marry, to have children, and to manage their homes. Then the enemy will have no chance to speak badly of us.
Some have already turned away to follow Satan.
If any believing man or woman has widows in the family, they should help them, so that the church is not burdened. Then the church can help the widows who are really alone.
Church leaders who lead well should be counted worthy of double honour and pay, most of all those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
For the Scripture says, "Do not tie up the mouth of an ox while it is treading out the grain." And, "The worker deserves his pay."
Do not accept a charge against a church leader unless it is backed by two or three witnesses.
Correct those who keep on sinning in front of everyone, so that the others will be afraid to sin.
In front of God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels, I command you to keep these rules without taking sides. Do nothing out of favouritism.
Do not be in a hurry to lay hands on anyone to appoint them. Do not share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
Stop drinking only water. Use a little wine for your stomach, because you are often ill.
Some people's sins are clear to see. They go ahead of them to judgment. But the sins of others only show up later.
In the same way, good deeds are clear to see. And even those that are not clear cannot stay hidden for ever.
All who are slaves should treat their masters as worthy of full respect. Then no one will speak against God's name and our teaching.

Slaves whose masters are believers should not respect them less because they are brothers. Instead, they should serve them even better, because those who benefit from their work are believers whom they love. Teach these things and urge people to do them.
Someone may teach different ideas and not agree with the true and healthy words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and with the teaching that leads to living for God.
That person is proud and understands nothing. He has an unhealthy love of arguing and fighting about words. This leads to jealousy, quarrels, insults, evil suspicions,
and constant fights between people whose minds are rotten and who have lost hold of the truth. They think that serving God is a way to get rich. Keep away from such people.
But living for God, and being content with what you have, is a great gain.
We brought nothing into the world, and we certainly cannot take anything out of it.
So if we have food and clothes, we will be content with that.
People who want to get rich fall into temptation and a trap. They fall into many foolish and harmful desires that drag people down to ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some people, eager for money, have wandered away from the faith and stabbed themselves with many sorrows.
But you, man of God, run away from all this. Chase after what is right, living for God, faith, love, patience and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the life that lasts for ever. God called you to it when you spoke up well about your faith in front of many witnesses.
In front of God, who gives life to everything, and of Christ Jesus, who spoke up well when he stood before Pontius Pilate, I command you:
keep this command without stain or fault until our Lord Jesus Christ appears.
God will make that happen at the right time. He is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
He alone can never die. He lives in light that no one can come near. No one has ever seen him, and no one can see him. To him be honour and power for ever. Amen.

Command those who are rich in this world not to be proud. Tell them not to put their hope in riches, which are so uncertain. They should put their hope in the living God, who richly gives us everything to enjoy.
Command them to do good, to be rich in good deeds, and to be generous and willing to share.
In this way they will store up treasure for themselves, a strong base for the time to come. Then they will take hold of the life that is truly life for ever.
Timothy, guard what has been trusted to you. Turn away from godless empty talk, and from the opposing ideas of what is falsely called knowledge.
Some people have claimed to have this knowledge, and so they have wandered away from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
2Tim: From Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, sent to tell about the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus.
To Timothy, my dear son. Grace, mercy and peace to you from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience, as my ancestors did. Night and day I keep remembering you in my prayers.
I remember your tears, and I long to see you, so that I may be filled with joy.
I remember your faith that is real. It lived first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and I am sure it lives in you too.
That is why I remind you to stir up God's gift, like a fire, the gift that is in you since I laid my hands on you.
For God did not give us a spirit that makes us afraid. He gave us a spirit of power, love and self-control.
So do not be ashamed to speak about our Lord, or ashamed of me, his prisoner. Instead, share with me in suffering for the Good News, by the power of God.
God saved us and called us to a holy life. He did this not because of anything we had done, but because of his own plan and grace. He gave us this grace in Christ Jesus before time began.
But now he has made it known through the coming of our Saviour, Christ Jesus. Christ has destroyed death, and through the Good News he has brought life that never dies into the light.
For this Good News I was chosen to be a preacher, an apostle and a teacher of the Gentiles.
That is why I am suffering these things. But I am not ashamed, because I know the one I have believed. I am sure he is able to guard what I have trusted to him until that day.
Keep the pattern of healthy teaching that you heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good thing that was trusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
You know that everyone in the province of Asia has turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord show mercy to the family of Onesiphorus. He often cheered me up, and he was not ashamed that I was in chains.
Instead, when he was in Rome, he searched hard for me until he found me.
May the Lord let him find mercy from the Lord on that day! And you know very well how many ways he helped me in Ephesus.
So you, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
You heard me teach many things in front of many witnesses. Pass these things on to people you can trust, who will be able to teach others too.
Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No soldier on duty gets mixed up in everyday business. He wants to please the officer who chose him.
In the same way, an athlete does not win the prize unless he keeps the rules.
The farmer who works hard should be the first to get a share of the crops.
Think about what I am saying. The Lord will help you understand all these things.
Remember Jesus Christ, who was raised from the dead and came from the family of David. This is the Good News I preach.
For this Good News I am suffering, even to the point of being chained like a criminal. But God's word is not chained.
So I put up with everything for the sake of God's chosen people, so that they too may be saved in Christ Jesus and have glory that lasts for ever.
Here is a saying you can trust: "If we died with him, we will also live with him.
If we keep going, we will also rule with him. If we say we do not know him, he will also say he does not know us.
If we are not faithful, he stays faithful, because he cannot go against who he is."
Keep reminding God's people of these things. Warn them in front of God not to argue about words. Such arguing does no good. It only ruins those who listen.
Do your best to present yourself to God as one he approves, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, who handles the true message correctly.
Keep away from godless empty talk, because people who do that will become more and more ungodly.
Their teaching will spread like a disease that eats away the body. Hymenaeus and Philetus are among them.
They have wandered away from the truth. They say that the rising from the dead has already happened, and they are destroying the faith of some people.
But God's strong foundation stands firm, and it is sealed with these words: "The Lord knows those who are his," and, "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from what is wrong."
In a large house there are not only things made of gold and silver, but also things made of wood and clay. Some are for special use and some for ordinary use.
If anyone makes himself clean from these wrong things, he will be like a special dish. He will be made holy, useful to the Master, and ready for every good work.
Run away from the evil desires of youth. Chase after what is right, and after faith, love and peace, together with those who call on the Lord with a pure heart.
Have nothing to do with foolish and stupid arguments, because you know they lead to fights.
The Lord's servant must not fight. Instead, he must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and patient.
He must gently correct those who oppose him. Maybe God will help them turn from their sins and come to know the truth fully.
Then they will come to their senses and escape from the devil's trap. He has caught them to make them do what he wants.
But know this: in the last days there will be terrible times.
People will love only themselves and money. They will boast and be proud. They will speak against God and will not obey their parents. They will not be thankful or holy.
They will have no natural love for others, and they will not forgive. They will spread lies about others. They will have no self-control. They will be cruel, and they will not love what is good.
They will betray their friends, act without thinking, and be full of pride. They will love pleasure more than they love God.
They will look as if they serve God, but they will deny the power that makes this real. Stay away from people like that.
Some of them sneak into homes and take control of weak women. These women are weighed down with sins, and led by all kinds of evil desires.
They are always learning, but they can never come to know the truth.
Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses. In the same way these teachers oppose the truth. Their minds are twisted, and God has rejected their faith.
But they will not get very far. Everyone will see how foolish they are, just as people saw it with Jannes and Jambres.
But you have followed my teaching, the way I live, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love and how I keep going.
You know the attacks and the suffering I went through in Antioch, Iconium and Lystra. I put up with those attacks, and the Lord rescued me from all of them.
In fact, everyone who wants to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be attacked.
But evil people and those who pretend to be what they are not will get worse and worse. They will fool others and be fooled themselves.
But as for you, keep on in the things you have learnt and are sure of. You know the people who taught you.
Since you were a small child, you have known the holy Scriptures. They can make you wise so that you are saved through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is breathed out by God. It is useful for teaching, for showing people what is wrong, for correcting them, and for training them in doing right.
So each person who belongs to God can be complete, fully ready for every good work.
In front of God and Christ Jesus, I give you this command. Christ Jesus will judge the living and the dead when he appears and his kingdom comes.
Preach the message. Be ready at all times, whether it is easy or not. Correct people, warn them and encourage them, with great patience and careful teaching.
The time will come when people will not listen to healthy teaching. Instead, they will gather many teachers around them to say what their itching ears want to hear, to suit their own desires.
They will stop listening to the truth and turn to myths.
But you, keep a clear head in every situation. Put up with hardship. Do the work of telling the Good News, and do all the work God has given you.
As for me, my life is already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time for me to leave this life has come.
I have fought the good fight. I have finished the race. I have kept the faith.

Now the crown for doing right is waiting for me. The Lord, the judge who is always fair, will give it to me on that day. And he will give it not only to me, but also to all who have longed for him to appear.
Do your best to come to me soon.
Demas has left me, because he loved this world. He has gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is a help to me in my work.
I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the coat I left with Carpus in Troas. Bring my scrolls too, and most of all the parchments.
Alexander the metalworker did me a lot of harm. The Lord will pay him back for what he has done.
You too should watch out for him, because he strongly opposed our message.
The first time I had to defend myself in court, no one came to help me. Everyone left me. May it not be held against them.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message could be fully preached and all the Gentiles could hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Greet Priscilla and Aquila, and the family of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth. I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
Do your best to get here before winter. Eubulus greets you, and so do Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the brothers and sisters.
The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
Titus: From Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ. I was sent to help God's chosen people to believe, and to know the truth that leads to living for God.
This faith and knowledge rest on the hope of life that lasts for ever. God, who never lies, promised this life before time began.
And at the right time he made his message known through the preaching he trusted me with, by the command of God our Saviour.
To Titus, my true son in the faith we share. Grace, mercy and peace to you from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
I left you in Crete so that you could put in order what was still not done, and appoint church leaders in every town, as I told you.
A leader must be someone no one can find fault with. He must have only one wife. His children must be believers, and no one must be able to accuse them of wild living or of not obeying.

A church leader takes care of God's work, so he must be someone no one can find fault with. He must not be proud or quick to get angry. He must not drink too much, or be violent, or chase after money in dishonest ways.
Instead, he must welcome guests into his home and love what is good. He must think clearly, be fair and holy, and control himself.
He must hold firmly to the message we can trust, as it was taught. Then he can encourage others with healthy teaching, and show those who oppose it where they are wrong.
For there are many people who refuse to obey. They talk nonsense and fool others, most of all those who insist on circumcision.
They must be stopped from talking. They are upsetting whole families by teaching things they should not teach, just to make money in a shameful way.
Even one of their own prophets said, "People from Crete are always liars, evil animals and lazy people who eat too much."
What he said is true. So correct them strongly, so that they will be healthy in the faith.
Then they will stop listening to Jewish myths and to the commands of people who turn away from the truth.
To those who are pure, everything is pure. But to those who are unclean and do not believe, nothing is pure. Both their minds and their consciences are unclean.
They say they know God, but what they do shows that they deny him. They are hateful and disobedient, and no use for any good work.
But you must teach what agrees with healthy teaching.
Teach the older men to control themselves, to be worthy of respect, and to think clearly. Teach them to be strong in faith, in love and in keeping going.
In the same way, teach the older women to live in a way that honours God. They must not spread lies about others or be slaves to much wine. They must teach what is good.
Then they can train the younger women to love their husbands and their children,
to think clearly and be pure, to work well at home, to be kind, and to accept the leadership of their own husbands. Then no one will speak badly of God's word.
In the same way, encourage the young men to think clearly and control themselves.
In everything, set them an example by doing what is good. When you teach, be honest and serious, and keep your teaching pure.
Speak in a healthy way that no one can criticise. Then anyone who opposes you will be ashamed, because they will have nothing bad to say about us.
Teach slaves to obey their own masters and to please them in everything. They must not talk back to them,
or steal from them. Instead, they must show that they can be fully trusted. Then in every way they will make the teaching about God our Saviour attractive.
For the grace of God has appeared, and it brings salvation to all people.
It teaches us to say "No" to ungodly living and to worldly desires. It teaches us to live in this world with self-control, doing what is right and living for God.
We do this while we wait for the blessed hope, when the glory of our great God and Saviour, Jesus Christ, will appear.
He gave himself for us to set us free from all evil, and to make us pure, a people who belong to him alone and who are eager to do good.
Teach these things. Encourage people and correct them with full authority. Do not let anyone look down on you.
Remind God's people to accept the authority of rulers and leaders, to obey them, and to be ready to do every good thing.
Remind them not to speak evil of anyone, and not to start fights. They should be gentle and always humble towards everyone.
At one time we too were foolish and did not obey. We were fooled and were slaves to all kinds of desires and pleasures. We lived with spite and jealousy. People hated us, and we hated each other.
But then the kindness and love of God our Saviour for people appeared.
He saved us, not because of good things we had done, but because of his mercy. He saved us by washing us, so that we were born again and made new by the Holy Spirit.
God poured out the Spirit on us richly through Jesus Christ our Saviour.
He did this so that, made right with God by his grace, we would receive what he promised, with the hope of life that lasts for ever.
This is a saying you can trust. I want you to stress these things, so that those who believe in God will be careful to keep doing good. These things are good and helpful for everyone.
But keep away from foolish arguments, lists of ancestors, quarrels and fights about the law. They are useless and worth nothing.
Warn a person who causes divisions once, and then a second time. After that, have nothing more to do with him.
You can be sure that such a person has turned from the right way and is sinning. He judges himself by what he does.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to spend the winter there.
Do all you can to help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way. Make sure they have everything they need.
Our people must learn to keep doing good, to meet real needs. Then their lives will not be wasted.
Everyone who is with me greets you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
Phlm: From Paul, a prisoner for Christ Jesus, and from our brother Timothy. To Philemon, our dear friend who works with us,
to our dear sister Apphia, to Archippus who fights alongside us, and to the church that meets in your home.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God when I mention you in my prayers,
because I hear about your love for all God's people, and your faith in the Lord Jesus.
I pray that as you share your faith with others, it will work powerfully, as you come to know every good thing we have in Christ Jesus.
Your love has given me great joy and comfort, my brother, because you have cheered the hearts of God's people.
So in Christ I could be bold and order you to do what you ought to do.
But because of love, I would rather ask you. I, Paul, am now an old man, and a prisoner for Christ Jesus too.
I am asking you for my son Onesimus. He became my son in the faith while I was in chains.
Once he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
I am sending him back to you. Welcome him, because he is very dear to my heart.
I would have liked to keep him with me, so that he could help me in your place while I am in chains for the Good News.
But I did not want to do anything without your agreement. I wanted any kindness you show to be something you choose to do, not something you are forced to do.
Maybe the reason he was away from you for a short time was so that you could have him back for ever,
no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a dear brother. He is very dear to me, and even dearer to you, both as a person and as a brother in the Lord.
So if you think of me as your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
If he has done you any wrong or owes you anything, charge it to me.
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I will pay it back. And I will not even mention that you owe me your very self.
Yes, my brother, let me have this joy from you in the Lord. Cheer my heart in Christ.
I am sure you will obey, so I am writing to you. I know you will do even more than I ask.
And one more thing: get a guest room ready for me, because I hope God will answer your prayers and let me come back to you.
Epaphras, who is in prison with me for Christ Jesus, greets you.
So do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, who work with me.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
Heb: Long ago God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets, many times and in many different ways.
But in these last days he has spoken to us through his Son. God chose him to own all things, and through him God made the universe.

The Son shows God's glory and is the exact picture of who God is. He holds all things together by his powerful word. After he made us clean from our sins, he sat down at the right hand of God, the Majesty in heaven.
So he became much greater than the angels, just as the name God gave him is far greater than theirs.
God never said to any angel, "You are my Son. Today I have become your Father." Or again, "I will be his Father, and he will be my Son."
And when God brings his firstborn Son into the world, he says, "Let all of God's angels worship him."
About the angels God says, "He makes his angels like winds, and his servants like flames of fire."
But about the Son he says, "Your throne, O God, lasts forever and ever. You rule your kingdom with what is right.
You have loved what is right and hated what is evil. That is why God, your God, has chosen you and poured the oil of joy on you, more than on anyone else."
He also says, "Lord, in the beginning you laid the foundations of the earth. The heavens are the work of your hands.
They will pass away, but you will remain. They will all wear out like old clothes.
You will roll them up like a coat, and they will be changed like clothes. But you stay the same, and your years will never end."
God never said to any angel, "Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet."
Angels are all spirits who serve God. He sends them to help those who will receive salvation.
So we must pay even more attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away from it.
The message God gave through angels was firm, and everyone who broke it or disobeyed it was fairly punished.
So how can we escape if we ignore such a great salvation? The Lord himself first told us about it, and those who heard him proved to us that it is true.
God also showed it was true by signs, wonders and many kinds of miracles, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit that he gave as he wanted.
God did not put angels in charge of the world to come, the world we are talking about.
Somewhere in the Scriptures someone says, "What are people, that you think about them? What is a son of man, that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels for a while. You crowned him with glory and honour.
You put everything under his feet." When God put everything under him, he left nothing that is not under him. But right now we do not yet see everything under him.
But we do see Jesus. For a little while he was made lower than the angels, and now he is crowned with glory and honour because he suffered death. By God's kindness, he died for everyone.
God made all things, and all things exist for him. He wanted to bring many children to share his glory. So it was right for him to make Jesus, who leads them to salvation, perfect through suffering.
Jesus makes people holy, and those he makes holy belong to the same family. So he is not ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters.
He says, "I will tell my brothers and sisters about your name. I will sing your praise among your people."
He also says, "I will trust in him." And again, "Here I am, with the children God has given me."
Since the children are people of flesh and blood, Jesus also became flesh and blood like them. He did this so that by his death he could destroy the devil, who has the power of death,
and set free all those who were slaves all their lives because they were afraid of dying.
It is clear that he does not come to help angels. He comes to help the children of Abraham.
So he had to become like his brothers and sisters in every way. Then he could be a high priest who is kind and faithful in serving God, and he could take away the sins of the people.
Because he himself suffered when he was tempted, he is able to help those who are being tempted.
So, holy brothers and sisters, you who share in God's call from heaven, think carefully about Jesus. He is the one God sent, and the High Priest of the faith we believe.
He was faithful to God, who chose him, just as Moses was faithful in all God's house.
But Jesus deserves more glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honour than the house itself.
Every house is built by someone, but God is the one who built everything.
Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant. He told the people about things God would say in the future.
But Christ is faithful as the Son in charge of God's house. And we are his house, if we hold on firmly to our courage and to the hope we are proud of, right to the end.
That is why the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear his voice,
do not make your hearts stubborn, as your people did when they rebelled, on the day they tested God in the desert.
There your ancestors tested me and tried me, even though they saw what I did for forty years.
That is why I was angry with that generation. I said, 'Their hearts always go the wrong way. They have not known my ways.'
So in my anger I made a promise: 'They will never enter my place of rest.'"
Brothers and sisters, be careful that none of you has an evil heart that does not believe, and turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage each other every day, while it is still called "today", so that none of you is fooled by sin and becomes stubborn.
We share in Christ, if we hold on firmly to the trust we had at the beginning, right to the end.
As the Scripture says, "Today, if you hear his voice, do not make your hearts stubborn, as your people did when they rebelled."
Who heard God's voice and still rebelled? It was all those whom Moses led out of Egypt.
Who was God angry with for forty years? It was with those who sinned, and they died in the desert.
Who did God promise would never enter his place of rest? It was those who disobeyed him.
So we see that they could not enter because they did not believe.
God's promise that we can enter his rest still stands. So let us be careful that none of you fails to enter it.
We have heard the good news, just as they did. But the message they heard did not help them, because they did not join it with faith.
We who believe are the ones who enter that rest. As God said, "So in my anger I made a promise: 'They will never enter my place of rest.'" Yet God's work was finished when he made the world.
Somewhere in the Scriptures he says this about the seventh day: "On the seventh day God rested from all his work."
And in the place we just read he says again, "They will never enter my place of rest."
So some people will still enter that rest. But those who first heard the good news did not enter, because they disobeyed.
So God set another day and called it "today". Much later he spoke about it through David, in the words we already read: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not make your hearts stubborn."
If Joshua had given them that rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
So there is still a special Sabbath rest waiting for God's people.
Whoever enters God's rest also rests from their own work, just as God rested from his.
So let us work hard to enter that rest, so that no one falls by disobeying, as they did.
God's word is alive and powerful. It is sharper than any sword with two edges. It cuts deep enough to divide soul and spirit, joints and bone marrow. It judges the thoughts and plans of our hearts.
Nothing in all creation is hidden from God. Everything is uncovered and open before his eyes, and we must all explain ourselves to him.
We have a great High Priest who has gone up into heaven: Jesus, the Son of God. So let us hold on firmly to the faith we say we believe.
Our High Priest understands how weak we are. He was tempted in every way, just as we are, yet he never sinned.
So let us come boldly to God's throne, where his kindness is found. There we will receive mercy, and find his kindness to help us when we need it.
Every high priest is chosen from among the people. He is given the job of serving God for them, offering gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can be gentle with people who do not know better and who go the wrong way, because he himself is weak too.
That is why he must offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.
No one takes this honour for himself. God must call him, just as he called Aaron.
In the same way, Christ did not give himself the glory of becoming High Priest. God said to him, "You are my Son. Today I have become your Father."
And in another place God says, "You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek."
While Jesus lived on earth, he prayed and begged God with loud cries and tears. God was able to save him from death, and God heard him because he honoured God so deeply.
Even though he was God's Son, he learned to obey through what he suffered.
After he was made perfect, he became the source of salvation that lasts forever for everyone who obeys him.
And God named him a High Priest in the line of Melchizedek.
We have a lot to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you have become slow to listen.
By now you should be teachers. Instead, you need someone to teach you the very first lessons about God's message again. You need milk, not solid food.
Anyone who lives on milk is still a baby, and does not yet understand the teaching about what is right.
But solid food is for people who are grown up. They have trained themselves by practice to know the difference between good and evil.
So let us move on from the first lessons about Christ and grow up. We do not need to lay the foundation again: turning away from actions that lead to death, and trusting God,
teaching about baptisms, laying hands on people, the dead rising to life, and God's judgment that lasts forever.
And we will move on, if God allows it.
Some people once had their eyes opened to the truth. They tasted the gift from heaven and shared in the Holy Spirit.
They tasted how good God's word is, and the powers of the world to come.
If they then turn away, it is impossible to bring them back to turning from sin. They are nailing the Son of God to the cross again for themselves, and shaming him in front of everyone.
Land that drinks in the rain that often falls on it, and grows a good crop for the people who farm it, receives a blessing from God.
But if it grows only thorns and weeds, it is worthless and close to being cursed. In the end it will be burned.
Dear friends, even though we talk like this, we are sure that better things are true of you, things that come with salvation.
God is fair. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown him by helping God's people, and by still helping them.
We want each of you to keep working just as hard to the very end, so that what you hope for will surely happen.
We do not want you to become lazy. Instead, copy those who receive what God promised because of their faith and patience.
When God made his promise to Abraham, there was no one greater for him to swear by, so he swore by himself.
He said, "I will surely bless you, and I will give you many, many descendants."
So Abraham waited patiently, and he received what God promised.
People swear by someone greater than themselves. Their oath proves what they say and ends every argument.
God wanted to show very clearly to those who would receive his promise that his plan would never change. So he backed his promise with an oath.
God cannot lie, and these two things, his promise and his oath, can never change. So we who have run to God for safety can be greatly encouraged to hold on to the hope set in front of us.
This hope is like an anchor for our souls, firm and safe. It goes behind the curtain into the most holy place in heaven,
where Jesus has already gone ahead of us, for us. He has become a High Priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek.
This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham, who was coming back after defeating the kings, and he blessed him.
Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had won. First, the name Melchizedek means "king of what is right". Also, king of Salem means "king of peace".
Nothing is written about his father, his mother or his family. There is no record of when he was born or when he died. Like the Son of God, he stays a priest forever.
Think how great this man was! Even Abraham, the father of our nation, gave him a tenth of the best things he had won in battle.
The law says the priests from the family of Levi must collect a tenth from the people, that is, from their own relatives, even though they all come from Abraham.
But Melchizedek did not come from Levi's family, yet he collected a tenth from Abraham. And he blessed Abraham, the one who had God's promises.
Everyone agrees that the person who blesses is greater than the one who is blessed.
The priests who collect a tenth are people who die. But Scripture says that Melchizedek lives on.
We could even say that Levi, whose family collects the tenth, paid a tenth through Abraham.
Levi was not born yet. He was still in the body of his ancestor Abraham when Melchizedek met him.

The people were given the law under the priests from Levi's family. If those priests could have made people perfect, why was another priest needed, one in the line of Melchizedek and not in the line of Aaron?
When the priesthood changes, the law must change too.
The one we are talking about belongs to a different tribe. No one from that tribe has ever served as a priest at the altar.
It is clear that our Lord came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests from that tribe.
This becomes even clearer when another priest appears who is like Melchizedek.
He became a priest, not because of a law about his family line, but because of the power of a life that cannot be destroyed.
For Scripture says, "You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek."
So the old rule has been set aside, because it was weak and useless.
The law never made anything perfect. But now a better hope has been given, and through it we come close to God.
And God made Jesus a priest with an oath.

Other priests became priests without an oath, but Jesus became a priest with an oath, when God said to him, "The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: 'You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek.'"
Because of this oath, Jesus is our guarantee of a better covenant.
There were many of those other priests, because death stopped each of them from continuing.
But Jesus lives forever, so his priesthood never ends.
That is why he can save completely those who come to God through him. He lives forever to speak to God for them.
Jesus is the High Priest we need. He is holy, without blame and pure. He is set apart from sinners and raised higher than the heavens.

He does not need to offer sacrifices every day like the other high priests, first for their own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all time, when he offered himself.
The law chooses high priests who are weak men. But God's oath, which came after the law, chose the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
Here is the main point of what we are saying: we have a High Priest like this. He sat down at the right hand of the throne of God, the Majesty in heaven.
He serves in the holy place, the true tent of worship, which was set up by the Lord, not by people.
Every high priest is chosen to offer gifts and sacrifices. So our High Priest also had to have something to offer.
If he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because there are already priests who offer the gifts the law asks for.

They serve in a place that is only a copy and a shadow of what is in heaven. That is why God warned Moses when he was about to build the tent of worship: "Make sure you make everything like the pattern I showed you on the mountain."
But the work Jesus has been given is much better than theirs. In the same way, the covenant he brings between God and people is better, because it is built on better promises.
If the first covenant had been perfect, there would have been no need for a second one.
But God found fault with the people. He said, "The days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors, when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. They did not stay faithful to my covenant, so I turned away from them, says the Lord.

This is the covenant I will make with the people of Israel after that time, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
They will no longer need to teach their neighbours or their brothers, saying, 'Get to know the Lord.' Everyone will know me, from the least important to the most important.
I will forgive the wrong things they have done, and I will never again remember their sins."
By calling this covenant "new", God has made the first one old. And whatever is old and getting older will soon disappear.
The first covenant had rules for worship and a holy place here on earth.
A tent was set up. Its first room was called the Holy Place. In it were the lampstand, the table and the special bread offered to God.
Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place.

It had a gold altar for burning incense, and the covenant box, which was covered with gold on every side. Inside the box was a gold jar holding manna, Aaron's walking stick that had grown buds, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
Above the box were the glorious cherubim, spreading their wings over the cover where sins were forgiven. But we cannot talk about all these things in detail now.
When everything was set up like this, the priests went into the first room every day to do their work.
But only the high priest went into the second room, and only once a year. He always took blood with him, which he offered for his own sins and for the sins the people had done without knowing.
By this the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place was not yet open while the first tent was still standing.
This is a picture for the present time. It shows that the gifts and sacrifices offered there could not make the worshipper's conscience clean and perfect.
They were only about food, drink and different kinds of washing. They were rules for the body, which lasted until the time God would set things right.
But Christ has come as the High Priest of the good things that are now here. He went through a greater and more perfect tent, not made by human hands, not part of this created world.
He did not take the blood of goats and calves. He took his own blood, and he went into the Most Holy Place once for all time. So he set us free forever.
The blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a young cow sprinkled on people who were unclean, made their bodies clean.

So the blood of Christ will do so much more! Through the Spirit that lives forever, he offered himself to God as a perfect sacrifice. His blood will clean our consciences from actions that lead to death, so that we can serve the living God.

That is why Christ brings a new covenant between God and people. His death sets people free from the sins they did under the first covenant. So those whom God has called can receive what he promised: a gift that lasts forever.
When someone leaves a will, it must be proved that the person who made it has died.
A will only takes effect after a death. It never works while the person who made it is still alive.
That is why even the first covenant was not started without blood.
Moses told all the people every command in the law. Then he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, red wool and branches of hyssop, and sprinkled the book of the law and all the people.
He said, "This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded you to keep."
In the same way, he sprinkled blood on the tent of worship and on everything used in worship.
The law says that almost everything must be made clean with blood. And without blood being poured out, sins cannot be forgiven.
So the copies of the things in heaven had to be made clean by these sacrifices. But the things in heaven needed much better sacrifices.
Christ did not go into a holy place made by human hands, which was only a copy of the real one. He went into heaven itself, and now he stands before God for us.
He did not go in to offer himself again and again, like the high priest who goes into the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.
If that were so, Christ would have had to suffer many times since the world was made. But now, at the end of the ages, he has come once for all time to take away sin by sacrificing himself.
Everyone must die once, and after that comes judgment.
In the same way, Christ was offered once to take away the sins of many people. He will come a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.
The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming, not the real things themselves. So the same sacrifices, offered year after year, can never make perfect those who come to worship.
If they could, people would have stopped offering them. The worshippers would have been made clean once, and would no longer feel guilty for their sins.
Instead, those sacrifices remind people of their sins every year.
The blood of bulls and goats can never take away sins.
That is why, when Christ came into the world, he said to God, "You did not want sacrifices and offerings, but you prepared a body for me.
You were not pleased with burnt offerings or sacrifices for sin.
Then I said, 'Here I am, O God. I have come to do what you want, just as the scroll says about me.'"
First he said, "You did not want sacrifices, offerings, burnt offerings or sacrifices for sin, and you were not pleased with them," even though the law asks for them.
Then he said, "Here I am. I have come to do what you want." So he takes away the first way to set up the second.
Because Jesus Christ did what God wanted, and offered his body once for all time, we have been made holy.
Every priest stands day after day doing his work, offering the same sacrifices again and again. But they can never take away sins.
But Christ offered one sacrifice for sins, for all time. Then he sat down at the right hand of God.
Now he is waiting until God puts his enemies under his feet.
By that one offering, he has made perfect forever those who are being made holy.
The Holy Spirit also tells us this. First he says,
"This is the covenant I will make with them after that time, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts, and write them on their minds."
Then he says, "I will never again remember their sins and the wrong things they have done."
When sins have been forgiven, there is no more need for an offering for sin.
So, brothers and sisters, because of the blood of Jesus, we can now go boldly into the Most Holy Place.
Jesus opened a new way for us, a way that gives life. He opened it through the curtain, that is, through his own body.
And we have a great Priest who is in charge of God's house.
So let us come close to God with an honest heart and full faith. Our hearts have been sprinkled clean from a guilty conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us hold on firmly to the hope we say we have, without doubting, because God can be trusted to keep his promise.
Let us think about how we can encourage each other to love and to do good things.
Let us not stop meeting together, as some people have done. Instead, let us encourage each other, and do it even more as you see the Day of the Lord coming closer.
If we keep on sinning on purpose after we have learned the truth, there is no other sacrifice left to take away sins.
All that is left is a terrible fear of judgment, and of the raging fire that will destroy God's enemies.
Anyone who refused to obey the law of Moses was put to death without mercy, if two or three witnesses spoke against them.

So think how much worse the punishment will be for those who walk all over the Son of God! They treat the blood of the covenant, which made them holy, as if it were worthless, and they insult the Spirit who gives God's kindness.
We know God, who said, "I will punish people. I will pay them back." He also said, "The Lord will judge his people."
It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember the early days, after you first came to know the truth. You stayed strong through a hard fight and much suffering.
Sometimes you were insulted and treated badly in front of everyone. At other times you stood beside others who were treated like that.
You felt for those who were in prison, and you were glad when your things were taken from you, because you knew you had something better that will last forever.
So do not throw away your courage. It will bring you a great reward.
You need to keep going, so that after you have done what God wants, you will receive what he promised.
For the Scripture says, "In just a little while, the one who is coming will come. He will not wait.
My people who do what is right will live by faith. But if they turn back, I will not be pleased with them."
But we are not people who turn back and are destroyed. We are people who have faith and are saved.
Faith means being sure of what we hope for, and certain of what we cannot see.
It was because of their faith that God was pleased with people long ago.
By faith we understand that God made the universe by his word. So what we see was not made out of things that can be seen.

By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. Because of his faith, God said he was a good man, and God accepted his gifts. Even though Abel is dead, he still speaks to us through his faith.
By faith Enoch was taken up to God without dying. No one could find him, because God had taken him away. Before he was taken, Scripture says that he pleased God.
Without faith, no one can please God. Anyone who comes to God must believe that he is real, and that he rewards those who look for him.

By faith Noah built a big boat to save his family. God warned him about things that had not yet happened, and he honoured God and obeyed. By his faith he showed the world was wrong, and he became one of those whom God accepts because of their faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed when God called him to go to a land he would later receive as his own. He left, even though he did not know where he was going.
By faith he lived like a foreigner in the land God had promised him. He lived in tents, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who received the same promise.
Abraham was waiting for the city with lasting foundations, the city planned and built by God.
By faith even Sarah was able to have a child, though she was too old. She trusted that God would keep his promise.
So from one man, who was as good as dead, came a family as many as the stars in the sky, and as many as the grains of sand on the seashore, which no one can count.

All these people were still living by faith when they died. They did not receive what God had promised, but they saw it coming from far away and welcomed it. They said that they were only strangers and visitors on earth.
People who say things like that show that they are looking for a home of their own.
If they had been thinking about the country they had left, they could have gone back.
Instead, they wanted a better country, a home in heaven. So God is not ashamed to be called their God, because he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham offered Isaac as a sacrifice when God tested him. Abraham had received God's promises, yet he was ready to offer his only son.
God had told him, "Your family line will come through Isaac."
Abraham believed that God could even raise the dead. And in a way, he did get Isaac back from death.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, speaking about their future.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons. He worshipped God as he leaned on the top of his walking stick.
By faith Joseph, when he was about to die, spoke about the people of Israel leaving Egypt. He told them what to do with his bones.
By faith Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born. They saw he was a special child, and they were not afraid of the king's order.
By faith Moses, when he grew up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
He chose to suffer with God's people rather than enjoy the pleasures of sin for a short time.
He thought that being insulted for the sake of Christ was worth more than all the treasures of Egypt, because he was looking ahead to his reward.
By faith Moses left Egypt, and he was not afraid of the king's anger. He kept going because he saw God, who cannot be seen.
By faith Moses kept the Passover, and had blood sprinkled on the doorposts, so that the angel who killed the firstborn would not touch the firstborn of Israel.
By faith the people walked through the Red Sea as if on dry land. When the Egyptians tried to follow, they drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
By faith Rahab, the prostitute, was not killed with those who disobeyed God, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
What more can I say? I do not have time to tell you about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets.
Through faith they defeated kingdoms, did what was right, and received what God promised. They shut the mouths of lions,
put out raging fires, and escaped being killed by the sword. They were weak, but they were made strong. They became powerful in battle and chased away foreign armies.
